{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:46:09.858752+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_068d0203f92520322e4cf3001bf6e90b2a7b0ef327e2b07ec8f62ca5aef9da21","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.21155, 'Asymptotic Probabilities of Attaining the Maximum in Heterogeneous Gaussian Samples'] For $\sigma>1$,  the sequence
  $\mathbb P (M^{(1)}_{n_1}>M^{(2)}_{n_2} )$
converges to a limit in $(0,1)$ if and only if \eqref{eq:N1N2} holds for some $C\in(0,\infty)$.  Moreover, in this case,
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P\!\left(M^{(1)}_{n_1}>M^{(2)}_{n_2}\right)
=
\mathbb P\!\left(\Lambda_1>\sigma^2(\Lambda_2-\kappa(C,\sigma))\right)
=
\int_0^\infty \exp\left(-y - e^{-\kappa(C,\sigma)} y^{1/\sigma^2}\right) \mathrm dy,
\end{equation}
where $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ are independent Gumbel random variables, and
\begin{align}
 
 \kappa(C,\sigma)
=
\frac{1}{\sigma^2}\log\frac{C}{\sigma}
+\frac12\left(1-\frac{1}{\sigma^2}\right)\log(4\pi).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["M(t) finite at the value of t used","independence is needed only for the product form of M"],"created_at":"2026-08-29T02:26:24.137772+00:00","domain":"probability / concentration","id":"claim_068e40c4c7d310aba3587dba7663e41d10e88d8e2188f2b3d971854d15ff2ab6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a real random variable and let M(t) = E[e^{tX}] be its moment generating function. For every real a and every t > 0 with M(t) < infinity, P(X >= a) <= e^{-ta} M(t); hence P(X >= a) <= inf_{t > 0} e^{-ta} M(t). Likewise for every t < 0 with M(t) < infinity, P(X <= a) <= e^{-ta} M(t). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:25:35.795985+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_069062865cd41854571b7310e54ed0ad2e9a988e34329fa47aab309296228884","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem.proj_coeffs of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] For any integer $d$, $d \ge 2$ 
    and a positive $\gamma$
    
    
    
    there
    are positive reals $\delta_0 =\delta_0(d, \gamma)$,
    $R_1=R_1(d,\gamma)$
    and an integer 
    $L_0 = L_0(d, \gamma)$
    such that the following holds.

    Let ${\bf X}$ be a random vector in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and let $\round{{\bf X}}$ 

    be
    obtained by rounding each component of ${\bf X}$ to the nearest integer. 
    

    Let $q = \sup_{e: \|e\|=1} \mathcal{Q}(\langle e, {\bf X} \rangle, 1)$, that is $q$ is
    the supremum of the mass of ${\bf X}$ concentrated (strictly) between any two hyperplanes at distance one from each other.

    
    

    Let $R_0 >0$ and suppose that in the open ball $\{x: \|x\| < R_0\}$ the random vector ${\bf X}$ has
    a positive and differentiable density $f$ (that is $\mathbb P({\bf X} \in A) = \int_{A} f(x) d x_1 \dots d x_d > 0$ for any Borel set $A \subseteq \{x: \|x\| < R_0\}$) such that

    
    \begin{equation}
        \sup_{ \|x\| < R_0 } \|\nabla \ln f(x) \| \le \delta_0
        
    \end{equation}
    Then for any vector $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$ either
    \begin{equation}
        \mathcal{Q}(\langle a, \round{{\bf X}} \rangle) = \max_{x \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathbb P(\langle a, \round{{\bf X}} \rangle = x) \le \gamma q + \mathbb P\left(\|{\bf X}\| \ge R_0 - R_1\right)
    \end{equation}
    or there is $\kappa \in \mathbb{R}$, $\kappa \ne 0$ such that $\kappa a \in \{-L_0, \dots, L_0\}^d$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.497777+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_06b72d9378526bd49ed16a833192ec61fd4fb5f76632dba9b821ea6be694fcf0","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 (Completely monotone, Bernstein, and Stieltjes classes) of arXiv:2607.04467, 'Bernstein Functions at Work:\\ Coalescents, Copulas, and Subordination'] Let all functions below be defined on \((0,\infty)\) and take values in
\([0,\infty)\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.3em]
\item A function \(f\) is \emph{completely monotone}, written \(f\in\CM\), if
\(f\in C^\infty\) and
\((-1)^n f^{(n)}(x)\ge0\) for every \(n\ge0\) and \(x>0\). It is
\emph{strictly completely monotone} if all these inequalities are strict.

\item A function \(g\) is a \emph{Bernstein function}, written \(g\in\BF\), if
\(g\in C^\infty\) and \(g'\in\CM\).

\item A Bernstein function \(g\) is a \emph{special Bernstein function}, written
\(g\in\SBF\), if \(x/g(x)\in\BF\).

\item A Bernstein function \(g\) is a \emph{complete Bernstein function}, written
\(g\in\CBF\), if its L\'evy measure has a completely monotone density.

\item A function \(h\) is a \emph{Stieltjes function} if
\begin{equation}
h(x)=\frac{a}{x}+b+\int_{(0,\infty)}\frac{1}{x+t}\,\sigma(dt),\qquad x>0,
\end{equation}
where \(a,b\ge0\) and
\(\int_{(0,\infty)}(1+t)^{-1}\,\sigma(dt)<\infty\).
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.177505+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_06bcc8c744c35f9e53258930c2a42e4230c2963bfb9ddbaddd3c27b6b7d32b10","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 77 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\gamma:[q_0,1]\to[q_0,1]$ be a monotone and absolutely continuous function, and define its generalized inverse
	\[
	\lambda:[q_0,\gamma(1)]\to[q_0,1]\,,\quad
	\lambda(s)
	\equiv\inf\Big\{
	t : \gamma(t)>s
	\Big\}\,.
	\]
Then the set $\{s : \gamma'(\lambda(s))=0 \}$ has zero Lebesgue measure.

\begin{proof}
It is straightforward to verify that $\lambda$ is a right-continuous function with $\gamma(\lambda(s))=s$ for all $s$. For any measurable set $A\subseteq\R$, consider the preimage $\lambda^{-1}(A)$: we have $s\in \lambda^{-1}(A)$ if and only if $\lambda(s)\in A$, which implies $s=\gamma(\lambda(s)) \in \gamma(A)$. This proves that 
	\[\lambda^{-1}(A)
	\subseteq \gamma(A)\]
(the converse need not hold). Let $A=\{t\in[q_0,1] : \gamma'(t)=0\}$: by absolute continuity of $\gamma$, we have
	\[|\gamma(A)|
	= \int_{q_0}^1 \gamma'(t)
	\ind\{t\in A\}
	\,dt = 0\,.\]
Since $\lambda^{-1}(A)\subseteq \gamma(A)$, it follows that
	\[
	|\lambda^{-1}(A)|
	=\bigg| \Big\{s : \gamma'(\lambda(s))=0
	\Big\}\bigg|=0\,,
	\]
as claimed.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:38:58.683023+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_06d33a069c6151dab2253c61a92e30547b9d5481c5bbc8307bf1a1d01726dc1a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma of arXiv:2510.18792, 'The frog model with death revisited'] \thlabel{lem:biased-walk-bounds}
Let $(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a nearest-neighbor random walk on $\mathbb Z$ with $X_0=n> 0$ that moves left with probability $0<p<1/2$ and right with probability $1-p$ at each step. Let $\rho = p/(1-p)$. We let $\Geo(r)$ denote the geometric distribution supported on the nonnnegative integers. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item
For $\tau_{n-1}=\inf\{t\ge1: X_t=n-1\}$, it holds that
$$\frac{\tau_n-1}{2} \preceq \Geo\left(r\right) \quad 
\text{ with } \quad r = \exp\left(-\frac{3(1 - 2p)^2}{2(1 + 4p)} \right).$$

\item Let $T_n = \max \{t \colon X_t =n\}$ be the time of the last visit to $n$. It holds that 
    $$\frac{T_n}{2}\ \preceq \Geo(s) \quad \text{ with } \quad s=(1-2p)r.$$
\item
Suppose the walk is conditioned to never go left of $n$ i.e.\ conditioned on the event $A=\{X_t \geq n \text{ for all $t \geq 0$}\}$. 
Let $T_n'$ denote the time of its last return to $n$. Then $T_n' \preceq T_n$. 

\end{enumerate}
It follows that the length of each excursion between steps taken by the recursive frog model on $\mathbb T_d$ is stochastically dominated by the $2\Geo((1-p)(1-\rho)r) +1$ distribution. Moreover, these excursion lengths are independent between non-backtracking steps by the strong Markov property of random walk.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:49:05.383923+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_06d9d97a8f7ace8381c9ca7666373734ca68f8db35c96e7764a55d7235631646","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:one_arm_decomposition_lemma of arXiv:2601.07808, 'Supercritical long-range percolation on graphs of polynomial growth: the truncated one-arm'] \label[lemma]{lem:one_arm_decomp}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:25:49.848163+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_06e3e3886aae71981bf48a96b99d8f66a0769f097737e8b80f342ad532f7e826","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2609.01996, 'Baumslag--Solitar Subgroups Obstruct Model Companions for Fields with Group Actions'] For every integer \(\nu\geq1\), put
  \[
    H_\nu:=\langle\sigma,\tau^\nu\rangle\leq\BS(m,n).
  \]
  Then
  \[
    \tau^\nu\sigma^{m^\nu}=\sigma^{n^\nu}\tau^\nu,
  \]
  and hence there is a surjective homomorphism
  \[
    \varphi_\nu:\BS(m^\nu,n^\nu)\twoheadrightarrow H_\nu.
  \]
  If \(\sigma_\nu,\tau_\nu\) denote the standard generators of the source, then
  \[
    \varphi_\nu(\sigma_\nu)=\sigma,\quad \varphi_\nu(\tau_\nu)=\tau^\nu.
  \]
  Let \(\beta_\nu\) be the intrinsic 1-cocycle and \(\ell_\nu\) the \(\tau_\nu\)-exponent-sum homomorphism of \(\BS(m^\nu,n^\nu)\).
  Identifying
  \[
    \Z\left[\frac1{m^\nu n^\nu}\right]=\Z\left[\frac1{mn}\right],
  \]
  one has
  \[
    \beta\circ\varphi_\nu=\beta_\nu,\quad \ell\circ\varphi_\nu=\nu\ell_\nu.
  \]
  Consequently,
  \[
    \ker\varphi_\nu\subseteq\ker\beta_\nu\cap\ker\ell_\nu.
  \]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.952064+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_06e59369e21e8b9751742db14876319e58b2670cbda83547a825586651b3823e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 4 (Bessel Kernel) of arXiv:2608.07365, 'A pathwise Ito formula \\for weakly differentiable functions'] The Bessel kernel $g_{\alpha}\colon \Rr^d\to \Rr,\, \alpha>0$ is defined by its Fourier transform

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:44:27.938469+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_06f3b7ee754004da9680c7b6281f9221ab8588b88700161032fb7a2bc9777a24","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 10 (Uniform expansion for conditioned-Poisson kernels) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] There is an absolute constant $\gamma_*>0$ with the following property. Let
$\Lambda=\Lambda_N>0$ be arbitrary. Let $D_1,\ldots,D_N$ be independent with
law $\Poi(\Lambda)$ conditioned on being at least three, condition further on
$\sum_iD_i$ being even, and let $\Kernel_N$ be the corresponding
configuration-model multigraph. If $P_{\Kernel_N}$ is the simple-random-walk
transition kernel on $\Kernel_N$, then
\[
        \Pbb\bigl(\lambda_2(I-P_{\Kernel_N})\ge\gamma_*\bigr)\longrightarrow1
\]
as $N\to\infty$, uniformly in the choice of the parameter sequence
$\Lambda_N>0$. Consequently, on the same event,
\begin{equation}
        \Reff^{\Kernel_N}(x,y)
        \le \gamma_*^{-1}\left(\frac1{d_{\Kernel_N}(x)}+
             \frac1{d_{\Kernel_N}(y)}\right)
        \qquad (x,y\in V(\Kernel_N)).
\end{equation}
In particular, let
\[
        \bar d_N:=\frac1N\sum_xd_{\Kernel_N}(x)
\]
and let $\widehat\pi$ be the degree-stationary law of simple random walk on the
kernel, namely
\[
        \widehat\pi(x)
        =\frac{d_{\Kernel_N}(x)}{\sum_zd_{\Kernel_N}(z)}
        =\frac{d_{\Kernel_N}(x)}{N\bar d_N}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{x,y}\widehat\pi(x)\widehat\pi(y)\Reff^{\Kernel_N}(x,y)
        \le \frac{2}{\gamma_*\bar d_N}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["All three hypotheses are needed.","Property (N) alone does not imply bounded variation, and bounded variation alone does not imply (N)."],"created_at":"2026-09-12T14:01:51.298668+00:00","domain":"real analysis, absolute continuity","id":"claim_06f4b839744b0627c4df8416fbfacc62a3acab1ee1f4e93cd0eb0dafd6002f88","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"A function f : [a,b] -> R is absolutely continuous if and only if it satisfies all three of the following: f is continuous on [a,b], f is of bounded variation on [a,b], and f has Lusin's property (N), that is, f maps every Lebesgue null subset of [a,b] to a null set. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:53:39.146807+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_06f7432d524b71ac0dfa225933e83fc4430d92fc3a47111f3069874190036fdc","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 11 of arXiv:2608.26953, '2608.26953'] A differential graded algebra \(\Omega^\bullet\) is \emph{graded commutative} if \(\alpha\wedge \beta =\ (-1)^{\lvert \alpha\lvert \lvert \beta\lvert }\beta\wedge \alpha, \text{ for all homogeneous } \alpha, \beta \in \Omega^\bullet\). It is \emph{exterior} if \(\Omega^1\) satisfies the surjectivity condition, and the iterated wedge 
\[\wedge\colon (\Omega^1)^{\otimes_An}
\rightarrow \Omega^n \] is surjective for each \(n\ge1\). 
For \((\Omega^\bullet, \wedge,d)\) a DGA, a \emph{differential graded ideal} \(I^\bullet \subseteq\Omega^\bullet\) is a graded two-sided ideal such that \[
\Omega^p \wedge I^q \subseteq I^{p+q},\quad
I^p \wedge \Omega^q \subseteq I^{p+q},\quad
d(I^q)\subseteq I^{q+1}\quad\text{for all }p,q\ge 0.
\]
A \emph{differential graded left $\Omega^\bullet$-module} (DG-module) is a graded left $\Omega^\bullet$-module \((M^\bullet, \cdot, d_M )\), where \(d_M: M^\bullet \rightarrow M^{\bullet+1}\) is a degree one \(\Bbbk\)-linear map satisfying \(d_M^2=0\), as well as \(d_M(\alpha\cdot m)= d(\alpha)\cdot m + (-1)^{\lvert \alpha\lvert } \alpha\cdot d_M(m), \ \text{for all homogeneous } \alpha\in \Omega^\bullet,\ m \in M^\bullet.\)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:58:40.869237+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_06f94410906d4c0e4a64c5a77ea82f46ec5a22acb099a1c305304865aef95c6a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem cor:stability of arXiv:2605.10491, 'Zero-couplings of infinite measures with cyclically monotone support and multivariate regu'] Let $\mu_n,\nu_n\in\mathrm{M}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:56:25.277151+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_071e014e17c1f646373fb7b265f61fe2e28e9a7489d930bdba1ffcbda23d9ccd","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi 3 (\Adam\ vector field) of arXiv:2606.21433, 'Central limit theorem for\\ the averaged Adam optimizer'] For a triple $(\alpha,\beta,\epsilon)$ of damping factors with $ \alpha<\sqrt\beta$ and an innovation $(X,U)$ we call the function
$
  f = ( f^{ (1) }, \dots, f^{ (d) } ) \colon \R^d \to \R^d
$
satisfying for all $ \theta \in \R^d $ that
\bas{
\textstyle
  f^{ (i) }( \theta )
  =
  ( 1 - \alpha ) \,
  \E\Bigl[
    \Bigl(
      \epsilon +

        ( 1 - \beta )
        \sum_{ k = - \infty }^0

        | X^{(i)}(  \theta, U_k ) |^2
      }
    \Bigr)^{ - 1 }
    \sum_{k=-\infty}^{0} \alpha^{-k} X^{(i)}(\theta,U_k)
  \Bigr]
}
with $ ( U_k )_{ k \in - \N_0 } $
being a family of independent copies of $ U $,
the \emph{\Adam\ vector field of the innovation $ ( X, U ) $
for the damping factors $ ( \alpha, \beta, \epsilon ) $}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the counterexample is a 2-dimensional real l^p computation (the ratio at (1, 1/2) is 1.7268 and the maximum over x = (1,t) is attained near t = 0.62 at about 1.7320)","complexification bound: ||T_C f||_q <= ||T u||_q + ||T v||_q for f = u + i v"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:36.553381+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis, interpolation of operators","id":"claim_0730394901107dee5537f5da05c6f3480958fb025978d553df02c49ce8dba25d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Two hypotheses of the Riesz-Thorin theorem are load-bearing and are routinely dropped in write-ups. (1) COMPLEX SCALARS. The proof interpolates through an analytic family f_z, so the conclusion ||T||_{p_theta -> q_theta} <= M_0^{1-theta} M_1^{theta} is a theorem about complex L^p spaces. Counterexample for real scalars: on R^2 with the l^p norms let T(x_1, x_2) = (x_1 - x_2, x_1 + x_2). Over the REALS, ||T||_{l^infinity -> l^1} = 2 (the maximum of |x_1-x_2| + |x_1+x_2| = 2 max(|x_1|,|x_2|) over the unit cube) and ||T||_{l^2 -> l^2} = sqrt(2) (T is sqrt(2) times a rotation). Interpolating the endpoints (p_0,q_0) = (infinity,1) and (p_1,q_1) = (2,2) at theta = 1/2 gives (p,q) = (4, 4/3) and the putative bound 2^{1/2} (sqrt 2)^{1/2} = 2^{3/4} = 1.6818...; but the real operator norm from l^4 to l^{4/3} is about 1.7320 (already the vector (1, 1/2) gives the ratio 1.7268 > 1.6818). No contradiction with the complex theorem: over C the norm ||T||_{l^infinity -> l^1} is 2 sqrt 2 (take (1, i)), and the complex bound becomes (2 sqrt 2)^{1/2} (sqrt 2)^{1/2} = 2, which is consistent. Remedy: for a real-linear T, complexification costs at most a factor 2, so the real conclusion holds with constant 2 M_0^{1-theta} M_1^{theta}. (2) LINEARITY. Riesz-Thorin is false as stated for merely sublinear operators, and it also requires STRONG endpoint bounds; an operator with only weak endpoint bounds, or one that is sublinear (such as a maximal operator), must be interpolated with the Marcinkiewicz theorem instead, whose constant is not M_0^{1-theta} M_1^{theta} and blows up at the endpoints.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:01:25.576764+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_073e4f43dfa5e735f34a2fd9ca11318bd612bccb735f219284a6c65b5d1998b9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:E-DFS of arXiv:2605.16086, 'Loop pruning and downward deviations for maximum local time of discrete-time simple random'] Let $T^*=(T,\sigma)\in \mathbf{T}^*$ be an $E$-segmented marked tree with root $\rho$.  
We define the \textit{$E$-depth-first traversal} of $T^*$ as a finite sequence 
\[
f=f_{T^*}:\{0,1,\ldots,M\}\longrightarrow V(T),
\]
constructed recursively as follows.

\begin{enumerate}
    \item The sequence starts at the root:
    \[
    f(0)=\rho.
    \]
    \item Suppose $f(0),\ldots,f(m)$ have already been defined for some $m\in \mathbb{N}$. We then determine $f(m+1)$ according to the position of $f(m)$ in the tree:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[(i)] If $f(m)$ has at least one child not contained in $\{f(0),\ldots,f(m)\}$, then $f(m+1)$ is the leftmost such child with respect to the ordering of $T$.
        \item[(ii)] If all children of $f(m)$ have already appeared in the sequence and $f(m)\neq \rho$, let $u_1<u_2<\cdots <u_L$ denote $f(m)$ and all its siblings (i.e. the children of the parent of $f(m)$). Assume $f(m)=u_j$ and that the labels of $u_1,\ldots, u_L$ decompose into a concatenation of elementary sequences
        \[
        (\sigma(u_1),\ldots, \sigma(u_L))=K_1\circ K_2\circ \cdots \circ K_P.
        \]
        If the $j$-th element of this concatenation belongs to $K_\ell$, then
        \begin{itemize}
            \item if it is not the last element of $K_\ell$, we define $f(m+1)=u_{j+1}$, the next sibling of $f(m)$;
            \item if it is the last element of $K_\ell$, we define $f(m+1)$ as the parent of $f(m)$.
        \end{itemize}
    \end{itemize}
    \item The recursion terminates once the root $\rho$ is reached and all children of $\rho$ have appeared in the sequence.
\end{enumerate}

Figure~(fig:tree1 of the paper) illustrates this construction. The red contour line is drawn in analogy with the usual contour of a depth-first traversal: it starts from the root and follows the edges of the tree along the traversal. The only difference is that, when encountering a family of vertices corresponding to an elementary sequence, the contour does not immediately return to their parent after each visit; instead, it keeps moving through the sequence until the traversal has completely finished with the last vertex of this family (i.e., after its entire subtree has been explored), only then does it return to the parent. 

The order in which the vertices are visited along this contour line coincides with the $E$-depth-first traversal defined above.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:43:44.238676+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_074b9292bead897b5af1e067e80d991612cb97f8564f955d8b61f9cdb6559d14","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 15 of arXiv:2604.14427, 'A criterion for proving entropy chaos on path space'] Let $\PP$, a probability measure on the probability space $\Omega=C([0,T];\RR^d),$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.357926+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_074da0e685fb432dc28bacba60057e21af057b6ad4f19b226aa9d9ae921892d7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 245 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Assume that $L\ge1$ and that condition \eqref{e:deriv.p.bound} holds. Let $\vX\equiv \vX^N$ be the process defined by \eqref{e:X.decomp} and \eqref{e:Delta.X.Ising}. Then the process $X^\RomI$ satisfies the estimate
	\[ \max_{a\in[M]}
	\E\bigg[ \max_{0\le d\le\dmax}
	 \Big(X^\RomI(q_d,a)
	 -\E X^\RomI(q_d,a)\Big)
	 ^8\bigg] \le L^{O(1)}\,,\]
with the estimate holding uniformly in $N$.
\begin{proof} Similarly as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:martingale.sup.bound.X.II.III.Ising}, let us abbreviate
	\[
	\frac{\Delta X^{\RomI}(q_d,a)}{\delta_d p'(q_d)^{1/2}}
	\equiv \mathfrak{y}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)
	\equiv \frac{(\bmeta^a(q_{d+1}),\by(q_{d+1}))}{N^{1/2}}\,.
	\]
Define truncated $\tilde{\bmeta}$ and $\tilde{\by}$ similarly as
in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:martingale.sup.bound.X.II.III.Ising}, and define
	\[
	\frac{\Delta \tilde{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)}{\delta_d p'(q_d)^{1/2}}
	\equiv \tilde{\mathfrak{y}}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)
	\equiv \frac{(\tilde{\bmeta}^a(q_{d+1}),
		\tilde{\by}(q_{d+1}))}{N^{1/2}}\,.
	\]
By the same argument as for \eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.l4.step2} or for \eqref{e:RomII.tilde.discrepancy.second.mmt.bound}, we have
	\beq
	\bigg|\E\bigg[
	\Big(
	\mathfrak{y}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)
	- \tilde{\mathfrak{y}}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)
	\Big)^8
	\bigg]\bigg|
	\le e^{-cN}\,.
	\eeq
Let $\tilde{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)$ be the process started from zero with increments
$\Delta \tilde{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)$. (As before, we regard this as a process indexed by time $q_d$, for fixed $a\in[M]$.) Applying \eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.l4.step2.RomI} gives
	\beq
	\E\bigg[ \max_{0\le d \le \dmax}\Big(
	X^{\RomI}(q_d,a)- \tilde{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)\Big)^8\bigg]
	\le o_N(1)\,.
	\eeq
Then consider the centered increments
	\begin{align*}
	\frac{\Delta \bar{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)}{\delta_d p'(q_d)^{1/2}}
	&\equiv
	\frac{\Delta \tilde{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)}{\delta_d p'(q_d)^{1/2}}
	-\E\bigg[
	\frac{\Delta \tilde{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)}{\delta_d p'(q_d)^{1/2}}
		\,\bigg|\, \cG(q_d)
		\bigg]\\
	&= \tilde{\mathfrak{y}}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)
	- \E\Big[\tilde{\mathfrak{y}}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)
		\,\Big|\,\cG(q_d)\Big]\,.
	\end{align*}
Each increment above is a Lipschitz function of the gaussian noise, with Lipschitz constant $L^{O(1)}\delta_d$, and has mean zero conditional on $\cG(q_d)$.
Let $\bar{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)$ be the process started from zero with increments
$\Delta \bar{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)$. (Again, we regard this as a process indexed by time $q_d$, for fixed $a\in[M]$.)
Then $\bar{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)$ is a \emph{martingale}, whose increments are subgaussian with variance proxy $L^{O(1)} (\delta_d)^2$. Similar arguments as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:martingale.sup.bound.X.II.III.Ising} give (cf.\ \eqref{e:bar.X.II.martingale.exponential.concentration})
	\[
	\E \Big[\exp\{ \theta \bar{X}^{\RomI}(1,a)\}\Big]
	\le \exp( \theta^2 L^{O(1)} \delta)\,,\]
and combining with Doob's $L^p$ martingale inequality gives (cf.\ \eqref{e:martingale.bar.X.II.application.of.Doob})
	\beq
	\E\Big[ \max_{0\le d\le \dmax}
	\bar{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)^8\Big] 
	\le L^{O(1)} \delta^4\,.
	\eeq
It remains to address the discrepancy between $X^{\RomI}$ and $\bar{X}^{\RomI}$. Since $\tilde{X}^{\RomI}$ has subgaussian increments, we have
	\[
	\E\bigg[
	\Big( \Delta \tilde{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a) - \E \Delta \tilde{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)
	\Big)^8\bigg] \le  L^{O(1)}\delta^8\,,
	\]
and summing over increments gives
	\beq
	\E\bigg[ \max_{0\le d\le \dmax}
	\Big(
	 \tilde{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a) - \E \tilde{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)\Big)^8\bigg]
	 \le L^{O(1)}\,.
	\eeq
It also follows from  
\eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.l4.step2.RomI}
or \eqref{e:martingale.X.I.to.tilde.X.I.error}
that
 \beq
 \max_{0\le d\le \dmax}
 \bigg|\E \Big[ \tilde{X}^{\RomI}(q_d,a)
 - X^{\RomI}(q_d,a) \Big] \bigg| \le o_N(1)
 \eeq
 where we recall $\E X^{\RomI}(q_d,a)
 = \E X(q_d,a)$.  Combining \eqref{e:martingale.X.I.to.tilde.X.I.error}, \eqref{e:martingale.tilde.X.I.close.to.mean}, and \eqref{e:martingale.tilde.X.I.close.to.X.I} gives the conclusion.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:13:21.347448+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_076c452da6e3a6921118bb3dd9dd2e08a5a7381d939d26c5fbfcab5c89fb9e5c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 7 (Insensitivity for $M/G/k/k$ with Charging) of arXiv:2609.01559, 'Erlang Loss Model with Energy Constrained Servers'] Consider an $M/G/k/k$ loss system with Poisson arrivals of rate $\lambda$. Each admitted customer undergoes a service time $S \sim F$ followed immediately by a charging time $ R \sim G$, where $F$ and $G$ are arbitrary nonnegative distributions with finite means $\mathbb{E}[S]$ and $\mathbb{E}[R]$.  Then the steady-state blocking probability is
\begin{align}
B &= \frac{\frac{\rho^k}{k!}}{\displaystyle \sum_{j=0}^{k} \frac{\rho^j}{j!}},
\end{align}
where
\begin{align}
\rho = \lambda \big(\mathbb{E}[S] + \mathbb{E}[R]\big),
\end{align}
and hence depends only on the means of $S$ and $R$, not on their full distributions.

\begin{proof}
Let $S$ and $R$ be nonnegative random variables with distributions $F$ and $G$ and finite means. Let $B$ denote the steady-state blocking probability in the $M/G/k/k$ loss system with i.i.d.\ service times $S$ and charging times $R$, and arrival rate $\lambda$.  We first approximate $S$ and $R$ by phase-type (PH) distributions. It is well known that PH distributions are dense in the set of probability measures on $[0,\infty)$ with respect to weak convergence, and moreover can be chosen to approximate first moments. Hence, there exist sequences $\{S^{(n)}\}$ and $\{R^{(n)}\}$ such that
\[
S^{(n)} \Rightarrow S, \qquad R^{(n)} \Rightarrow R, \qquad 
\mathbb{E}[S^{(n)}] \to \mathbb{E}[S], \qquad \mathbb{E}[R^{(n)}] \to \mathbb{E}[R],
\]
where each $S^{(n)}$ and $R^{(n)}$ is phase-type.

For each $n$, consider the $M/PH/k/k$ system with service times $S^{(n)}$ and charging times $R^{(n)}$. Since phase-type distributions are closed under convolution, the total time $T^{(n)} := S^{(n)} + R^{(n)}$ is also phase-type. Thus, the system is an $M/PH/k/k$ loss system with i.i.d.\ holding times $T^{(n)}$.  It is a classical result for $M/PH/k/k$ systems that the stationary distribution is insensitive to the specific phase-type representation and depends only on the mean holding time. In particular, the blocking probability is given by the Erlang loss formula
\[
B^{(n)} = E_k(\rho_n), \qquad 
\rho_n := \lambda \, \mathbb{E}[T^{(n)}] = \lambda \big(\mathbb{E}[S^{(n)}] + \mathbb{E}[R^{(n)}]\big),
\]
where
\[
E_k(\rho) := \frac{\frac{\rho^k}{k!}}{\displaystyle \sum_{j=0}^{k} \frac{\rho^j}{j!}}.
\]

By convergence of expectations, we have
\[
\rho_n \to \rho := \lambda \big(\mathbb{E}[S] + \mathbb{E}[R]\big).
\]
Since $E_k(\cdot)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty)$, it follows that
\[
B^{(n)} = E_k(\rho_n) \to E_k(\rho).
\]

It remains to show that $B^{(n)} \to B$. To this end, note that the $M/G/k/k$ system can be described as a Markov process on the finite state space $\{0,1,\dots,k\}$ augmented with residual service times. The corresponding sequence of processes associated with $T^{(n)}$ converges weakly to that associated with $T = S+R$ under the assumed weak convergence and convergence of first moments. 

Moreover, since the state space of the occupancy process is finite, the stationary distribution is uniquely determined and depends continuously on the underlying holding-time distribution through the associated Markov renewal kernel. This continuity follows from standard perturbation results for regenerative processes with finite state space and uniformly integrable cycle lengths, see for example \citet{asmussen2003applied, resnick2013adventures}. Consequently, the stationary blocking probabilities satisfy
\[
B^{(n)} \to B.
\]

Combining the above limits yields
\[
B = \lim_{n\to\infty} B^{(n)} = \lim_{n\to\infty} E_k(\rho_n) = E_k(\rho),
\]
that is,
\[
B = \frac{\frac{\rho^k}{k!}}{\displaystyle \sum_{j=0}^{k} \frac{\rho^j}{j!}},
\qquad 
\rho = \lambda \big(\mathbb{E}[S] + \mathbb{E}[R]\big).
\]

This establishes that the blocking probability is insensitive to the full distributions $F$ and $G$, depending only on their means.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:59:45.013029+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0791c09fd4c7bb033b963786f6e0e92eb00b855772e07909a73e07efe1114eca","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defin def:backward of arXiv:2605.13519, 'Perfect simulation for interacting Hawkes processes with reset-induced variable length mem'] Set
\[
C_0=\{i\},\qquad T_0=t,
\]
and let $\mathscr J_0=\varnothing$. Suppose $(C_n,T_n,\mathscr J_n)$ has been constructed and $C_n\neq\varnothing$. Define
\[
S_n:=S(C_n).
\]
Let $T_{n+1}$ be the largest time $r<T_n$ at which at least one point of the environment occurs at a site in $S_n$. Almost surely this point is unique; write it as
\[
(J_{n+1},T_{n+1},\tau_{n+1},U_{n+1}),
\]
where $J_{n+1}\in S_n$, $\tau_{n+1}\in\{s,c\}$ and $U_{n+1}\in[0,1]$.

Set
\[
\mathscr J_{n+1}:=\mathscr J_n\cup\{(J_{n+1},T_{n+1},\tau_{n+1},U_{n+1})\}.
\]
The active set is updated by
\begin{equation}
C_{n+1}:=
\begin{cases}
C_n\setminus\{J_{n+1}\}, & \tau_{n+1}=s,\ J_{n+1}\in C_n,\\
C_n\cup\{J_{n+1}\}, & \tau_{n+1}=c,\ J_{n+1}\in \partial C_n,\\
C_n, & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
The exploration stops at
\[
N_{\rm ext}:=\inf\{n\geq 0:C_n=\varnothing\}.
\]
The clan of ancestors of $(i,t)$ is the stopped random object
\[
\mathcal A(i,t):=\mathscr J_{N_{\rm ext}}
\]
when $N_{\rm ext}<\infty$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:57:59.865459+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_079b3568943c34ff7886a38189a3165973231e85bcd46d14037b710f4593649c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:rooted-matching-tree of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Let $G=(I,J,M)$ be a weighted bipartite graph. Fix a right vertex $j_\star\in J$, 
and set
\[
I_\star:=N_G(j_\star).
\]
We say that $G$ contains an $m$-matching rooted tree at $j_\star$ if, for each $i\in I_\star$, there is a set
\[
\mathcal K_i\subseteq N_G(i)\setminus\{j_\star\},
\qquad
|\mathcal K_i|=m,
\]
such that
\[
N_G(j)\cap I_\star=\{i\}
\qquad
\forall i\in I_\star,\ \forall j\in\mathcal K_i,
\]
the sets $\mathcal K_i$, $i\in I_\star$, are pairwise disjoint, and the outer left neighborhoods
\[
N_G(j)\setminus I_\star,
\qquad
j\in\bigcup_{i\in I_\star}\mathcal K_i,
\]
are pairwise disjoint. Indeed, these vertices form a three-layer rooted tree in the support graph, including all neighbors of the right vertices in the tree:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $j_\star$ is the root,
  \item $I_\star$ is the first left layer, 
  \item the vertices in $\bigcup_i\mathcal K_i$ are the second right layer, and 
  \item the sets $N_G(j)\setminus I_\star$ for $j \in \bigcup_{i\in I_\star}\mathcal K_i$ form the third left layer.
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["G is finite, connected, simple, distance-regular, and n>=2."],"created_at":"2026-10-10T06:51:51.364496+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_07e8c48717f2e4462cbff10644f98ed2bdee48e66a11c8ccf4e48c023be5f089","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked against a direct linear-algebra solve on twelve graphs, with the complete graph and the cycle as independent controls at the two extremes.] This is the proved identity behind the campaign reduction of Open Problem 7.31 in David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html). Let G be a finite connected simple distance-regular graph with n>=2 vertices, valency k, and diameter d: for vertices at distance i, the numbers of neighbors one step closer to or farther from the target are constants c_i and b_i depending only on i. Use c_1=1, b_0=k, b_d=0. Let k_i be the number of vertices at distance i from a fixed vertex, so k_0=1, k_1=k, k_{i+1} c_{i+1}=k_i b_i, and n=sum_{i=0}^d k_i. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:22:59.736176+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_081bc520f5c04681d2a67fc5e5350a4d0185883ecbaf6eb2bedad5a4fc85ce68","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn Coarse slope of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\mathcal{G}$ be an oriented foliation on $\mathbb{T}^2$ and $\ell$ is a leaf of $\mathcal{G}$ not lying in the interior of a Reeb annulus, we define its $\textbf{(coarse) slope}$, $\slope(\ell)$ which is an element of $(\mathbb{R}^2\setminus \{0\})/\mathbb{R}_{>0} \cong S^1$, where $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ acts on $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus \{0\}$ by scaling. It is defined as 
$$\slope(\ell) \coloneqq \left[ \lim_{t\to +\infty} \frac{\varphi_t(x)-x}{t} \right],$$ 
where $\varphi_t$ denotes a flow directing the universal cover $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $x\in \ell$; up to positive scalars, the limit does not depend on these choices. We are usually concerned with slopes having non-negative $x$-coordinate; we call these the \textbf{admissible} slopes. The admissible slopes can be identified with $\mathbb{R} \cup \{\pm \infty\}$ via $(1,x) \mapsto x$.

If $\mathcal{G}$ has no Reeb annuli, all of its leaves have the same (coarse) slope which we denote by $\slope(\mathcal{G})$. If $\mathcal{G}$ has Reeb annuli, $\slope(\mathcal{G})$ is not well-defined.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:01:56.364803+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_08404f6e59878a825820ca327edb10eee2cc843aed665463efecc18e44df0221","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:slopestability of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] A \textbf{central charge}, also known as a \textit{stability function}, on an abelian category $\cA$ is an additive map $Z\colon K_0(\cA)\to\bC$ such that $Z(E)\in\bR_{>0}e^{\sqrt{-1}(0,\pi]}$ for $0\neq E\in\cA$, i.e.\ $Z(E)$ lies in the upper half-plane or negative real axis.
The \textbf{phase} of a non-zero object $E$ is defined to be $\phi(E)=\arg(Z(E))/\pi\in(0,1]$.
An object $E\in\cA$ is said to be
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{semistable} if $0\neq A\subseteq E\implies \phi(A)\leq \phi(E)$,
    \item \textbf{stable} if $E\neq 0$ and $0\neq A\subsetneq E\implies \phi(A)< \phi(E)$,
    \item \textbf{polystable} if $E$ is a finite direct sum of stable objects of equal phase.
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:33:21.485041+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0876afd796b8bfc599511bd3570d193cd72d6d77550ca9a72b7c7e3cb84d32e2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem Sharp small-hole eigenvalue asymptotic, \(d = 2\) of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] Let \(d = 2\) and \(\partial M\)
uniformly of class \(C^{1,1}\), and write
\(\delta_{\varepsilon} = \operatorname{dist}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\partial M \right)\).
The planar boundary layer has three regimes:

(i) boundary-scale centers,
\(\delta_{\varepsilon}/\varepsilon = O(1)\) (including
\(\delta_{\varepsilon} = 0\)):

\[\lambda\left( B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right) \right) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\pi}{|M|\,\log(1/\varepsilon)}\,\left( 1 + o(1) \right);\]

(ii) intermediate centers,
\(\varepsilon \ll \delta_{\varepsilon} \ll 1\) with
\(\theta: = limlog\left( 1/\delta_{\varepsilon} \right)/\log(1/\varepsilon) \in (0,1)\)
(equivalently
\(\delta_{\varepsilon} = \varepsilon^{\theta + o(1)}\)):

\[\lambda\left( B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right) \right) = B(\theta) \cdot \frac{\pi}{|M|\,\log(1/\varepsilon)}\,\left( 1 + o(1) \right),\quad\quad B(\theta) = \frac{1}{1 + \theta};\]

(iii) macroscopically interior centers, \(\delta_{\varepsilon}\)
bounded below:

\[\lambda\left( B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right) \right) = \frac{\pi}{|M|\,\log(1/\varepsilon)}\,\left( 1 + o(1) \right).\]

Here \(\theta \in \lbrack 0,1\rbrack\) is the logarithmic
boundary-layer parameter, with \(\theta = 0\) for macroscopically
interior centers (iii) and \(\theta = 1\) for boundary-scale
centers (i); the three regimes are the single asymptotic
\(\lambda\left( B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right) \right) = B(\theta)\,\pi/\left( |M|\log(1/\varepsilon) \right)\,\left( 1 + o(1) \right)\)
with \(B(\theta) = 1/(1 + \theta)\). The profile \(B\)
acts on the eigenvalue --- and, by Proposition D.5, on the Neumann
capacity --- decreasing from the interior value \(B(0) = 1\) to
the boundary value \(B(1) = \frac{1}{2}\); the associated
hitting-time constant of Corollary D.9 is the reciprocal
\(1/B(\theta) = 1 + \theta\), increasing from \(1\) to
\(2\). Thus a boundary-scale target has half the eigenvalue, and
twice the hitting time, of a macroscopically interior one. In contrast
to \(d \geq 3\), every fixed rescaled distance
\(\delta_{\varepsilon}/\varepsilon\) corresponds to
\(\theta = 1\) and hence to the same boundary value; the
nontrivial planar transition occurs only on the logarithmic scale
\(\theta\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:39:11.687973+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0876bc6fc82f75867d902c73386a0d5804e1f7618b5cc82c1998c0420fd51066","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 97 (Compact perfection under uniform spatial trace tightness) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $\mathcal P_{\rm sp}\subset\mathfrak S_{\Lambda,0}^{0,T}(H)$ have a

 \omega_{\boldsymbol\vartheta}(\delta_j)
 +\delta_j^\kappa+\delta_j^{2\beta}\le2^{-8j}.
\]
Put
\[
 \mathfrak T_{\boldsymbol\vartheta}(x)
 :=\sup_{m\ge0}2^m\|(I-P_m)x\|_{\infty;H},
\]
let $a_n,b_n,c_j$ be the finite-scale increments in

on the locus where the finite-scale limits exist,

 \qquad \Tr Q_{s,t}\le\Lambda(t-s),
 \qquad \Tr(R_mQ_{s,t}R_m)\le\vartheta_m(t-s)

Set $\mathfrak R_{\boldsymbol\vartheta}=\infty$ off this locus and let
$\mathcal C_R^{\boldsymbol\vartheta}$ be its sublevels.  Then there are
constants $C,c,C_*>0$, depending only on the fixed parameters and the spatial
profile, such that the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.5em]
\item For every $R\ge1$, $\mathcal C_R^{\boldsymbol\vartheta}$ is compact in

\[
 c_{\mathcal P_{\rm sp}}
 \bigl((\mathcal C_R^{\boldsymbol\vartheta})^c\bigr)

\]
\item On every $\mathcal C_R^{\boldsymbol\vartheta}$ and for every

\item With $\Gamma_*(R,S)=1+C_*(1+R+S)^2$, uniformly in the seam $s$,
\[

 $$

The hypothesis is that the LIMIT avoids the discontinuity set almost surely, not that g is continuous everywhere - which is what makes the theorem usable for maps such as x -> 1/x when the limit is almost surely nonzero, or x -> 1_{(a, infinity)}(x) when P(X = a) = 0. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.453874+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_08cb2cce823e3ef90c0d4d8176c14e9e2ecaded0819ca030e68b0f0abce94635","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma eq:coord_redn_r_ineq1 of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:calYr_min_M2s}
Let $f \in \Sym^r$. 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item[(i)] If $r=0$, then $M_2(f) \ge 2$, with equality if and only if $f = \hat{f}_1^0$. 
\item[(ii)] If $r\in(0,1)$, then $M_2(f) \ge 2-2r+r^2 > 1$, with equality if and only if $f = \hat{f}_0^r$. 
\item[(iii)] If $r=1$, then $M_2(f) \ge 1$, with equality if and only if $f = \hat{f}_0^1$. 
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
First consider $r=0$. We compute
\begin{align}
M_2(f) 

= \sum_{\substack{z \in 2\mathbb{Z} \\ z \ne 0}} z^2 f(z)
&\ge \sum_{\substack{z \in 2\mathbb{Z} \\ z \ne 0}} 2^2 f(z)  \\
&= 4(1-f(0)) \nonumber \\

&= 4\bigg(1-\frac{1-\sum_{k \ge 2}\alpha_k^0}{2}\bigg) \\
&\ge 4\bigg(1-\frac{1}{2}\bigg) 
= 2 
= M_2(\hat{f}_1^0) .  
\end{align}
where we have used 
(thm:Bernoulli_calY_representation of the paper) in 
(equation eq:coord_redn_r_eq2 of the paper),
and (lem:calY_negative_coefficient_control of the paper) in (equation eq:coord_redn_r_ineq2 of the paper).
Equality is attained in (equation eq:coord_redn_r_ineq1 of the paper) only if $\supp(f) \subseteq \{0, \pm 2\}$; 
which forces $f = \hat{f}_1^0$ by 
(thm:Bernoulli_calY_representation of the paper).

Now consider $r \in (0,1)$. 

Noting that the four smallest elements in magnitude of $S^r = 2\mathbb{Z} + \{\pm r\}$ are $\{\pm r, \pm(2-r)\}$, we compute
\begin{align*}
M_2(f) 
&= \sum_{z \in S^r} z^2 f(z) \\

&\ge 

r^2(f(r)+f(-r)) + \sum_{\substack{z \in S^r \\ z \ne \pm r}} (2-r)^2 f(z) \\
&= r^2(f(r)+f(-r)) + (2-r)^2(1-f(r)-f(-r)) \\

&= 4(1-r)(1 - f(r) - f(-r)) + r^2 .
\end{align*}
By (lem:calY_negative_coefficient_control of the paper), 

\( 
\alpha_0^r +\alpha_1^r 
= 1-\sum_{\substack{k \in \mathbb{Z} \\ k \ne 0,1}} \alpha_k^r
\le 1,
\)
and 
$$f(r) 
= \alpha_0^r \hat{f}_0^r(r) + \alpha_1^r \hat{f}_1^r(r) 
= \alpha_0^r (\frac{q}{2}) + \alpha_1^r (\frac{p}{2})$$
and similarly 
$$f(-r) 
= \alpha_0^r \hat{f}_0^r(-r) + \alpha_1^r \hat{f}_1^r(-r) 
= \alpha_0^r (\frac{p}{2}) + \alpha_1^r (\frac{q}{2})$$
so that 
$f(r) + f(-r) 

= \frac{1}{2}(\alpha_0^r + \alpha_1^r)
\le \frac{1}{2}
$. 
Therefore
\begin{align*}
M_2(f) 
&\ge 4(1-r)(1-\frac{1}{2}) + r^2 
= 2(1-r) + r^2 

= M_2(\hat{f}_0^r) . 
\end{align*}
Equality is attained only if $\supp(f) \subseteq \{\pm r, \pm(2-r)\}$, which forces $f = \hat{f}_0^r$ by (thm:Bernoulli_calY_representation of the paper). 

Finally consider $r=1$. 
In this case $\supp(f) = 2\mathbb{Z}+\{1\}$, so 
\[ 
M_2(f) = \sum_{z \in \supp(f)} z^2 f(z) 
\ge \sum_{z \in \supp(f)} f(z) = 1 = M_2(\hat{f}_0^1). 
\]
In order to attain equality we need $z^2 = 1$ for every $z \in \supp(f)$; in this case $\supp(f) \subseteq \{\pm 1\}$ and $f = \hat{f}_0^1$ by (lem:support_size_one_or_two of the paper). 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:49:15.416016+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_08e731367b202eb8720e9876e297021caa7de2fe4ced011afeb645d84a309278","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2608.27904, 'Instantons, indefinite 4-manifolds, and Dehn surgery'] A \textit{stratified-smooth space} $(P,\Delta)$ (or simply $P$) of dimension $n$ is the following data: 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item a partially ordered set $\Delta$ equipped with a dimension function $d: \Delta \to \mathbb N$ with maximum value $n$, 
		\item a compact topological space $P$ equipped with a partition into locally-closed subsets $P_\sigma$ for $\sigma \in \Delta$, satisfying $\overline P_\sigma = \bigcup_{\tau \le \sigma} P_\tau$, 
		\item the structure on each stratum $P_\sigma$ of a smooth manifold of dimension $d(\sigma)$.
	\end{itemize}
	We demand that the following {\it locally standard} hypothesis holds: for each $p \in P_\sigma$, there are non-negative integers $k$, $l$, an isomorphism of posets 
	$\bar \phi: \Delta_{\ge \sigma} \cong \{0,1\}^k$, an open neighborhood $U$ of $p$ in $P$, an open neighborhood $V$ of the origin in $[0,\infty)^k \times \mathbb R^{n+l-k}$, 
	a smooth map $\psi: V\to \mathbb R^l$, and a homeomorphism $\phi:U\to \psi^{-1}(0)$ with the following properties. For any stratum $Q_\sigma$ of $[0,\infty)^k \times \mathbb R^{n+l-k}$,
	the restriction of the map $\psi$ to $V\cap Q_\sigma$ is smooth and transverse to $0$. Furthermore, $\phi$ restricted to $P_\sigma$ takes values in 
	$V\cap Q_{\overline \phi(\sigma)}$ and this restriction is a diffeomorphism.
	
	A \textit{stratified-smooth $SO(3)$-space} is a stratified-smooth space $P$ equipped with a continuous $SO(3)$-action, for which each $P_\sigma$ is $SO(3)$-invariant, and the action is smooth on each stratum.

	A \textit{diffeomorphism} of stratified-smooth spaces $(\phi,\bar \phi): (P,\Delta)\to (P',\Delta')$  is the pair of an isomorphism of partially-ordered sets 
	$\bar \phi:\Delta \to \Delta'$ and a homeomorphism $\phi:P\to P'$ that restricts to a diffeomorphism from $P_\sigma$ to $P'_{\bar \phi(\sigma)}$ for each 
	$\sigma\in \Delta$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:47:07.717619+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_08e88cf174ac5237af95ebd6cac52a7a117f8694ab18c38326f2d4d4d0a8a556","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 16 (Uniform scalar state estimate) of arXiv:2608.06393, 'Intrinsic Tangential Hadamard Differentiability of Rough-BSDE Solution Maps'] Suppose \eqref{eq:local-quadratic-growth} holds and
\(\|\zeta\|_\infty\leq M_\zeta\).  Every bounded solution of
\eqref{eq:transformed-local-bsde} satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|\widetilde Y\|_{\mathbb S^\infty(I)}
 \leq e^{a_1|I|}\bigl(M_\zeta+\bar a_0|I|\bigr),
 \qquad
 \bar a_0:=a_0+\frac{a_2^2}{2},
 \quad \bar\gamma:=\gamma+1.
 
\end{equation}
To initialize the construction, fix a preliminary deterministic reset
partition
\[
 \Pi^{\mathrm{ex}}
 =\{0=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_{N_{\mathrm{ex}}}=T\}
\]
using only the deterministic rough-flow estimates.  It may be chosen
uniformly over the fixed rough, tangent, and realization budgets, after
shrinking the perturbation radius if necessary.  Let \(D_{\mathrm{ex}}\)
be a deterministic bound such that
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{I_j=[s_j,s_{j+1}]\in\Pi^{\mathrm{ex}}\\
        \text{base or admissible perturbed flow}}}
 \ \sup_{t\in I_j,\,y\in\mathbb R}
 |\phi_t^{I_j}(y)-y|
 \leq D_{\mathrm{ex}}.
 
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{align}
 \widetilde M_{\mathrm{ex}}
 &:=e^{a_1T}\left(
      \|\xi\|_\infty+\bar a_0T
      +N_{\mathrm{ex}}D_{\mathrm{ex}}\right),
 \\
 M_Y&:=\widetilde M_{\mathrm{ex}}+D_{\mathrm{ex}},
 \qquad
 M_*:=e^{a_1T}\bigl(M_Y+\bar a_0T\bigr).
 
\end{align}
Backward construction on \(\Pi^{\mathrm{ex}}\) then gives
\(\|\widetilde Y\|_{\mathbb S^\infty(I_j)}
\leq\widetilde M_{\mathrm{ex}}\) and
\(\|Y\|_{\mathbb S^\infty([0,T])}\leq M_Y\).
On every later deterministic refinement, any bounded local transformed
solution whose terminal value is the already constructed original-coordinate
solution at the right endpoint satisfies
\(\|\widetilde Y\|_{\mathbb S^\infty(I)}\leq M_*\).
In particular, \(M_*\) is fixed before the critical BMO partition is chosen
and does not depend on the number of intervals in that later refinement.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:15:54.967076+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_08f51bd59b2085f4fc56baa910537b5f4f46c2747f470e6bb8e64be46ba42c6b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:preservativity-logics of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] {litak_lewis_2018}}] 
  Consider the following axiom schemes:
  \begin{align*}
    \textsf{L}_a &: \quad (\Box \varphi \to \varphi) \lewis \varphi, \\
    \textsf{W}_a &: \quad ((\varphi \land \Box \psi) \lewis \psi) \to (\varphi \lewis \psi), \\

  \end{align*}
  We define:
  \begin{align*}
    \textbf{iGL}_a^\flat   &\coloneq \textbf{HLC}^\flat + \textsf{L}_a, &
    \textbf{iGL}_a^\sharp  &\coloneq \textbf{HLC}^\sharp + \textsf{L}_a, \\
    \textbf{iGW}_a^\flat   &\coloneq \textbf{HLC}^\flat + \textsf{W}_a, &
    \textbf{iGW}_a^\sharp  &\coloneq \textbf{HLC}^\sharp + \textsf{W}_a, \\
    \textbf{iPreL}^\flat   &\coloneq \textbf{iGW}_a^\flat + \textsf{M}_a, &
    \textbf{iPreL}^\sharp  &\coloneq \textbf{iGW}_a^\sharp + \textsf{M}_a.
  \end{align*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:35:19.876445+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_090d912884e7a1330f71e1dd6bc9f6160829acd76b3c364aade7532218444c85","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem defect of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] There is a ``defect" function
\[
        \delta:\mathcal P\times\mathcal P
        \longrightarrow\mathbb R_{\geq 0}
\]
with the following property. For $A,B\in\mathcal P$, $x\in A$,
and $y\in B$, if $x'=\Psi(x)$ and $y'=\Psi(y)$ then
\begin{equation}
        d_{\mathbb{H}^3}(x',y')
        \leq
        d_{\mathbb{H}^2}(x,y)-\delta(A,B).
\end{equation}
Moreover:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $\delta(A,A)=0$ for every $A\in\mathcal P$;

\item[(ii)] if $B$ lies between $A$ and $C$, then
\[
        \delta(A,C)

        \delta(A,B)+\delta(B,C);
\]

\item[(iii)] for every $\gamma\in\pi_1(S)$,
\[
        \delta(\gamma\cdot A,\gamma\cdot B)
        =
        \delta(A,B).
\]
\end{itemize}
In addition, $\delta(A,B)>0$ whenever $A$ and $B$ are contained
in distinct plaques of
$\mathbb{H}^2\setminus\widetilde\lambda$. If they are contained in the
same plaque, then $\delta(A,B)=0$.","status":"unverified"}

Then: (E1) for every $k > 0$, $\\alpha\\int_\\Omega|\\nabla T_k(u)|^p\\,dx \\leq k\\,\\|f\\|_{L^1}$; (E2) for every $k > 0$, $|\\{|u| \\geq k\\}| \\leq (S^p\\|f\\|_{L^1}/\\alpha)^{N/(N-p)}\\,k^{-N(p-1)/(N-p)}$, where $S$ is the Sobolev constant of $W_0^{1,p} \\hookrightarrow L^{p^*}$, $p^* = Np/(N-p)$; i.e. $u$ is bounded in the Marcinkiewicz space $M^{N(p-1)/(N-p)}(\\Omega)$; (E3) for every $h > 0$, $|\\{|\\nabla u| \\geq h\\}| \\leq C\\,h^{-N(p-1)/(N-1)}$, i.e. $|\\nabla u|$ is bounded in $M^{N(p-1)/(N-1)}(\\Omega)$; hence, $\\Omega$ being bounded, $u$ is bounded in $W_0^{1,q}(\\Omega)$ for every $q < N(p-1)/(N-1)$. EXISTENCE. If moreover $p > 2 - 1/N$ (equivalently $N(p-1)/(N-1) > 1$), there exists $u \\in W_0^{1,q}(\\Omega)$ for every $q < N(p-1)/(N-1)$, with $T_k(u) \\in W_0^{1,p}(\\Omega)$ for every $k$, $a(x,u,\\nabla u) \\in L^{r}(\\Omega)$ for some $r > 1$, and $\\int_\\Omega a(x,u,\\nabla u)\\cdot\\nabla\\varphi\\,dx = \\int_\\Omega f\\varphi\\,dx$ for all $\\varphi \\in C_c^\\infty(\\Omega)$ (a distributional solution). For $p = 2$ this is exactly Stampacchia's $q < N/(N-1)$. Sharp edges: (a) $q = N(p-1)/(N-1)$ is not attained - the fundamental solution of the $p$-Laplacian with $f = \\delta_0$ has $|\\nabla u| \\sim |x|^{-(N-1)/(p-1)}$, in $L^q$ iff $q < N(p-1)/(N-1)$; (b) for $1 < p \\leq 2 - 1/N$ the gradient of the solution is in general NOT in $L^1$, $u \\notin W^{1,1}$, and the distributional formulation is meaningless - one must use entropy or renormalized solutions defined through the truncations $T_k(u) \\in W_0^{1,p}$ and a generalized gradient; (c) existence is asserted, uniqueness is NOT: distributional $W^{1,q}$ solutions need not be unique (Serrin's pathological solutions of $\\operatorname{div}(A\\nabla u) = 0$ with $u \\in W^{1,q}$, $q < 2$, $u \\notin H^1_{loc}$, already for $p = 2$ and measurable coefficients); uniqueness holds in the entropy-solution class (Benilan, Boccardo, Gallouet, Gariepy, Pierre, Vazquez 1995) for $L^1$ data; (d) the estimates (E1)-(E3) require $T_k(u)$ to be an admissible test function, which is why they are proved on the approximations; (e) for measure data one gets the same $W_0^{1,q}$ bounds, but for a measure concentrated on a set of zero $p$-capacity the entropy uniqueness theory does not apply.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:38:11.735717+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_092f647668962c58af82e5e5f77ed3d543aea8d38795a25920ac1a86802cdd53","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:complex_cumu of arXiv:2504.00512, 'Localization-delocalization transition for a random block matrix model at the edge'] (Complex cumulant expansion) 
		Let $h$ be a complex random variable all of whose moments exist. The $(p,q)$-cumulant of $h$ is defined as
		$$
		\mathcal{C}^{(p,q)}(h)\mathrel{\vcenter{\baselineskip0.65ex \lineskiplimit0pt \hbox{.}\hbox{.}}}= (-\mathrm{i})^{p+q} \cdot \left(\frac{\partial^{p+q}}{\partial {s^p} \partial {t^q}} \log \mathbb{E} e^{\mathrm{i}sh+\mathrm{i}t\overline{h}}\right) \bigg{|}_{s=t=0}\,.
		$$
		Let $f:\mathbb C^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ be a smooth function, and we denote its holomorphic  derivatives by
		$$
		f^{(p,q)}(z_1,z_2)\mathrel{\vcenter{\baselineskip0.65ex \lineskiplimit0pt \hbox{.}\hbox{.}}}= \frac{\partial^{p+q}}{\partial z_1^p \partial z_2^q} f(z_1,z_2)\,.
		$$ Then, for any fixed $l \in \mathbb{N}$, we have
		\begin{equation} 
		\mathbb{E} f(h,\overline{h})\overline{h}=\sum\limits_{p+q=0}^l \frac{1}{p!\,q!}\mathcal{C}^{(p,q+1)}(h)\mathbb{E} f^{(p,q)}(h,\overline{h}) + R_{l+1}\,,
		\end{equation}
		given all integrals in ((5.16 of the paper)) exist. Here, $R_{l+1}$ is the remainder term depending on $f$ and $h$, and for any $\tau>0$, we have the estimate
		$$
			\begin{aligned}
			R_{l+1}=&\, \mathrm{O}(1)\cdot \mathbb{E} \big|h^{l+2}\mathbf{1}_{\{|h|>N^{\tau-1/2}\}}\big|\cdot \max\limits_{p+q=l+1}\big\| f^{(p,q)}(z,\overline{z})\big\|_{\infty} \\
			+&\,\mathrm{O}(1) \cdot \mathbb{E} |h|^{l+2} \cdot \max\limits_{p+q=l+1}\big\| f^{(p,q)}(z,\overline{z})\cdot \mathbf{1}_{\{|z|\le N^{\tau-1/2}\}}\big\|_{\infty}\,.
			\end{aligned}
		$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:09:59.188980+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0935d8c0dfb8300de8ce81d192e6cb1afc0aca7c9668dc92e877c9391089a3a4","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:Qh-monotonicity of arXiv:2608.05262, 'The law of $(1+1)$D SOS with an area tilt in a wedge'] {HKS25}}]
    
    Consider laws $\mathbb Q^\uparrow,\mathbb Q^\downarrow$
    on 
    
    ordered random walk curves $X_1 \ge \cdots \ge X_K$ on interval $I\subset \mathbb Z$, 
    parametrized by curves $g(x) \ge h(x)$ on $I$,  
    boundary values $\underline{u}, \underline{v} \in \mathbb Z^K$ and 
    area-tilt $\underline{b}=\{b_i(x),  x \in I,  1 \le i \le K\}$,  such that:
    \begin{itemize}
    \item The ordered curves $X_1(x)\geq \cdots \geq X_K(x)$ for all $x\in I$ have a global ceiling 
    $g(\cdot) \le \infty$ and floor $h(\cdot) \ge - \infty$ (i.e.,  $X_1 \leq g$ and $X_K \geq h$).
    \item The curves have boundary conditions $\underline{u},\underline{v}$, each of which is either ordered (e.g., $\underline{u}=(u_1,\ldots,u_K)$ where $u_i\geq u_{i+1}$) or free.
    \item The law of the increment $\mathfrak{X}\in \mathbb Z$ for curve $1\leq i\leq K$ at location $x\in I$ may depend on $i,x$ as long as it is of the form $\mathbb P(\mathfrak X_{i,x}=k) = \exp(-f_{i,x}(k))$ for a convex function $f_{i,x}$ which is finite at
 least when $k \in \pm 1$.
    \item The area tilt of curve $1\leq i\leq K$ at location $x\in I$ may depend on $i,x$,  of the form $\exp(-b_{i}(x) X_i(x))$.
    \end{itemize} 
    If the parameters of $\mathbb Q^\uparrow,\mathbb Q^\downarrow$ are such that
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
    \item the ceilings and floors are ordered: $g^\uparrow\geq g^\downarrow$ and $h^\uparrow\geq h^\downarrow$ coordinate-wise; \item the boundary conditions are ordered: $\underline{u}^\uparrow\geq \underline{u}^\downarrow$ coordinate-wise or both are free, the same applies to $\underline{v}$;
    \item the area tilts are reversely-ordered:  $b_i^\uparrow(x) \leq b_i^\downarrow(x)$ for all $i,x$;
    \end{enumerate} 
    then there is a coupling of $\mathbb Q^\uparrow,\mathbb Q^\downarrow$  so that $X_i^\uparrow(x)\geq X_i^\downarrow(x)$ for all $1\leq i\leq K$ and $x\in I$.","status":"unverified"}

\begin{proof} Consider any $\YY$ belonging to the set on the left-hand side of the above display. By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality,
    \[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:00:15.234645+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0962ae962adc0e44a788c0597106273429c8b88cbc5975f0fc4225bf1c976ec4","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 6 (Exponential convergence under partial terminal observation) of arXiv:2607.19176, 'Exponential Convergence of the Sinkhorn Algorithm for the Schrödinger Bridge with Regime S'] Let Assumptions~  \ref{assum:reference_marginals_partial}, \ref{assum:po_measures} and~\ref{assum:po_map_c2} hold. Let $\gamma^{\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p}}$ be the optimal coupling of the projected static EOT problem, and let $\gamma^{n+1,n}$ and $\gamma^{n+1,n+1}$ be the half-step and full-step couplings generated by \eqref{eq:partial_sinkhorn_update}. Assume that $ H(\gamma^{\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p}} \mid \gamma^{1,0}) < \infty$, $H(\gamma^{\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p}} \mid \gamma^{1,1}) < \infty$. Then there exist constants $A>0$ and $\theta\in(0,1)$ such that, for all $n\ge0$,
\[
H(\gamma^{\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p}}\mid\gamma^{n+1,n})

Consequently,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:04:30.575900+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_09a72eea6ebad9dde546093f4b6f106f59358bcb315f671cb06597c4f6c9fa26","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn of arXiv:2411.10318, 'Polynomial Mixing of the critical Glauber Dynamics for the Ising Model'] Let $f:\{-1,1\}^V\to[0,\infty)$ be a function on the possible configurations. We define the \textbf{entropy} of $f$ to be
$$\text{Ent}_{\mu_\beta}(f):=\mathbb{E}_{\mu_\beta}(f\log(f))-\mathbb{E}_{\mu_\beta}(f)\log\mathbb{E}_{\mu_\beta}(f),$$
where we set $0\log0=0$.
Also, for a function $f:\{-1,1\}^V\to\mathbb{R}$, we define the Dirichlet forms $\mathcal{E}_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2$ as follows:
$$\mathcal{E}_1(f,f):=\sum\limits_{i=1}^n\mathbb{E}_\beta\left[(f(\sigma)-f(\sigma^i))^2\right],\ \ \text{and}\ \ \mathcal{E}_2(f,f):=\dfrac{1}{2}\sum\limits_{\sigma,\tau}\mu_\beta(\sigma)P_\beta(\sigma,\tau)(f(\sigma)-f(\tau))^2.$$
Also, let $\gamma_\beta$ and $\alpha_\beta$ be the respective log-Sobolev constants, i.e.
$$\gamma_\beta=\inf\left\{\dfrac{\mathcal{E}_1(f,f)}{\text{Ent}_{\mu_\beta}(f^2)}:\text{Ent}_{\mu_\beta}(f^2)\neq0\right\}\ \ \text{and}\ \ \alpha_\beta=\inf\left\{\dfrac{\mathcal{E}_2(f,f)}{\text{Ent}_{\mu_\beta}(f^2)}:\text{Ent}_{\mu_\beta}(f^2)\neq0\right\}.$$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:38:13.643319+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_09c19db6313e2731b46f8072455ad61247a140f68cb112e8b2bc4ecf69db94d1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 17 of arXiv:2609.00702, 'On the Set-Valued Katugampola Fractional Integral: Properties and Regular Selections'] Let the set-valued mapping $F:\mathcal{I} \rightrightarrows \mathbb{R}$ be nonempty compact values with $\rho \neq -1, \nu > 0.$ Then for each $t \in \mathcal{I},$ let $H(t)= _a^\rho\mathfrak{D}^\nu F(t).$ By Theorem \ref{bounded}, for each $t \in \mathcal{I}$ the $H(t)$ is a non empty compact subset of $\mathbb{R}.$ Consider the extremal selections

Given two vertices in $a_i,a_j \\in S$ with $i < j$, a \\emph{triangular gap}, or gap for short, occurs between them if the triangle adjacent to $a_i$ branching to $a_j$ does not contain any points in $S$, while the succeeding triangle branching to $a_j$ contains $a_j$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:48:00.292571+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_09c7fc3ea2bc45cd77593f7d755908336a3cf3b38488acef779f1d96b946cd65","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition lem:GWDerivative of arXiv:2609.03094, 'Discrete Gromov--Wasserstein Duality: Algorithms and Isomorphism Testing'] Let $(\nu_0,\nu_1)\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X_0)\times \mathcal P(\mathcal X_1)$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:30:50.719350+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_09c883292bff63b5ad43c130ce968f4b05de90a8850f25712bb3f80ede4acad7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:ordinal of arXiv:2609.02155, 'Exact Limits of Random Projections for Preserving Geometry:\\ Distance Recovery, Nearest-N'] \begin{romannum}
\item The sign-pattern bounds of Warren [warren1968lower] and Milnor
[milnor1964betti] give
\[
\abs{\mathcal O_{n,m}}\le\exp(O(mn\log n)).
\]
\item Almendra-Hern{\'a}ndez and Mart{\'\i}nez-Sandoval
[almendra2022prescribing] proved that every strict total ordering of the
$N$ pairwise distances is realizable in $\mathbb{R}^{n-2}$. Their February 2026
correction, prompted by a construction of Maldonado, Raggi P\'erez, and
Rold\'an-Pensado [maldonado2026total], leaves open whether every ordering
is realizable in $\mathbb{R}^{n-3}$.
We call the minimum dimension realizing a specified $n$-point ordering its
\emph{Almendra-Hern{\'a}ndez--Mart{\'\i}nez-Sandoval (AHMS) dimension}.

\item Consequently, a uniformly random abstract ordering satisfies
\[
\Pr(\text{realizable in }\mathbb{R}^m)
\le\exp[-\Theta(n^2\log n)+O(mn\log n)],
\]
which is superexponentially small when $m=o(n)$.
\end{romannum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X is a compact metric space and T is continuous","the metric is fixed, but the notions defined are independent of the choice of a compatible metric on a compact space","Gamma_eps(x) is taken with forward iterates for a general continuous map and with two-sided iterates for a homeomorphism","Bowen's entropy h(T,Y) is used for arbitrary, possibly non-invariant, subsets Y"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.090635+00:00","domain":"topological dynamics, entropy","id":"claim_09ce2d5bcd2dcfca590ed7dbdf3202b050716fcf7e9c95e3a6d615cdc80401f0","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X, d) be a compact metric space and T : X -> X continuous. For a subset Y of X (not assumed invariant or closed) Bowen's entropy of T on Y is h(T, Y) = lim as delta -> 0 of limsup_n (1/n) log r_n(delta, Y), where r_n(delta, Y) is the least cardinality of a set S that (n, delta)-spans Y, that is such that every y in Y admits s in S with d(T^i y, T^i s) <= delta for all 0 <= i < n. For eps > 0 and x in X put Gamma_eps(x) = { y in X : d(T^i x, T^i y) <= eps for all i >= 0 }, the set of points whose forward orbit shadows that of x at scale eps (for a homeomorphism one lets i range over all integers). DEFINITIONS: T is h-EXPANSIVE (Bowen) if there exists eps > 0 with h(T, Gamma_eps(x)) = 0 for every x in X. The TAIL ENTROPY of T is h*(T) = lim as eps -> 0 of sup over x in X of h(T, Gamma_eps(x)); the limit exists because the supremum is nondecreasing in eps. T is ASYMPTOTICALLY h-EXPANSIVE (Misiurewicz) if h*(T) = 0. Relations and cautions: expansive implies h-expansive (for small eps the sets Gamma_eps(x) are singletons, with the one- or two-sided convention matching the map), and h-expansive implies asymptotically h-expansive; neither implication reverses. Subshifts and expanding maps are expansive, hence h-expansive; every C^infinity diffeomorphism of a compact manifold is asymptotically h-expansive (Newhouse), while for finite smoothness this can fail. The quantity h*(T) measures the entropy invisible at any finite scale - the entropy 'in the tail' - and it is zero exactly when the system admits a principal symbolic extension (Boyle-Downarowicz theory); it is not the same as the topological entropy and carries no information about it.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.476862+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_09ef64e39f8041b11f5d7d5d89986a034f527c9a0cf757fad1cde849f5115bd2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem eq:symm_4q_special of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] In $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{4q}$ with $2 \nmid q$, there exist symmetrization resistant random variables for which the minimum-entropy independent symmetrizer is not unique. 

\begin{proof}
In $\mathbb{Z}_3$, writing PMFs as $z = (z(-1),z(0),z(1))$, we see that $f = \frac{1}{3}(1,2,0)$ (which is symmetrization resistant by (thm:Z3 of the paper)) has $\frac{1}{3}(2,0,1)$ and $\frac{1}{3}(0,2,1)$ as symmetrizers. 

In $\mathbb{Z}_{4q}$,
$f = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{0} + \mathbb{1}_{q})$ 
has equal-entropy symmetrizers 
$f_{-} = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{0} + \mathbb{1}_{3q})$
and
$g = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{0} + \mathbb{1}_{2q})$. 

Note that $h \in \Sym(f)$ if and only if for all $s \in [4q]$
\begin{equation}
h(s) + h(s-q) = h(-s) + h(-s-q) 
\end{equation}
so that if $h(s) > \frac{1}{2}$ for some $s$, we have 
\[ \frac{1}{2} < h(s) \le h(-s) + h(-s-q) \]
and therefore 
\[ 1 < h(s) + h(-s) + h(-s-q) \]
so that either $s = -s$ (so $s = 0$) or $s = -s-q$ (so $2s = q$). 
Since $2$ does not divide $q$, the latter cannot happen and we need only consider $s=0$.
Evaluating (equation eq:symm_4q_special of the paper) at $s=q$ yields
\[ h(q) + h(0) = h(-q) + h(-2q) \]
so that 
\[ \frac{1}{2} < h(0) \le h(-q) + h(-2q) \]
and since $0$, $-q$, and $-2q$ are distinct modulo $4q$, we obtain 
\[ 1 < h(0) + h(-q) + h(-2q) \le \sum_x h(x) = 1 , \]
a contradiction. 
Thus $h \le \frac{1}{2}$ everywhere and
\[ H(h) = \sum_{x}h(x) \log_2\bigg(\frac{1}{h(x)}\bigg) \ge \sum_{x} h(x) = 1 = H(f), \]
so our $f$ is symmetrization resistant. 

\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:09:34.497230+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0a13feb8b6c2da5875bf465be8e3a647d826169e7400caa42c4687fc7952300e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm commutation_relation_u of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] In the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, let $n$ radial SLEs start at $e^{i\theta_1}, e^{i\theta_2}, \ldots, e^{i\theta_n} \in \partial \mathbb{D}$, with a marked interior point \( u \neq 0 \).

\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] For \( u = e^{i v} \), let the infinitesimal diffusion generators be
    \[
    \mathcal{M}_i = \frac{\kappa}{2} \partial_{ii} + b_i(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u) \partial_i + \sum_{j \neq i} \cot\left(\frac{\theta_j - \theta_i}{2}\right) \partial_j + \cot\left(\frac{v - \theta_i}{2}\right) \partial_v + \cot\left(\frac{\overline{v} - \theta_i}{2}\right) \overline{\partial}_v.
    \]
    If the $n$ SLEs locally commute, the generators satisfy:
    \[
    [\mathcal{M}_i, \mathcal{M}_j] = \frac{1}{\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta_j - \theta_i}{2}\right)} (\mathcal{M}_j - \mathcal{M}_i).
    \]
    There exists a partition function \(\psi(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u)\) such that the drift term \( b_i(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u) \) is given by
    \[
    b_i(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u) = \kappa \partial_i \log \psi,
    \]
    and \(\psi\) satisfies the null vector equations:
    \[
    \frac{\kappa}{2} \partial_{ii} \psi + \sum_{j \neq i} \frac{2}{\theta_j - \theta_i} \partial_i \psi + \frac{2}{v - \theta_i} \partial_v \psi + \frac{2}{\overline{v} - \theta_i} \overline{\partial}_v \psi + \left[\left(1 - \frac{6}{\kappa}\right) \sum_{j \neq i} \frac{1}{(\theta_j - \theta_i)^2} + h_i(\theta_i, u)\right] \psi = 0.
    \]

    \item[(ii)] By analyzing the asymptotics of adjacent points \( \theta_i \) and \( \theta_{i+1} \), we deduce that \( h_i(\theta, u) = h_{i+1}(\theta, u) \). If all points are consecutive, there exists a common function \( h(\theta, u) \) such that
    \[
    h(\theta, u) = h_1(\theta, u) = \cdots = h_n(\theta, u).
    \]

\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:37:51.440387+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0a3effbf05bb6faca0550adad52b0d29c2de1856ccf908dfd901d90c36156e5f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 9 (Existence and uniqueness of a BSPDE (general case)) of arXiv:2604.02998, 'Nonzero-Sum Stochastic Differential Games for Controlled Convection-Diffusion SPDEs'] Let $V$ and $\mathbb{H}$ be separable Hilbert spaces such that
\[
V \subset \mathbb{H} \simeq \mathbb{H}^* \subset V^*
\]
with continuous and dense embeddings, and let $\mathcal L_{\rho,a,b}:V\to V^*$ be a linear operator.
Let $\phi\in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F_T;\mathbb{H})$ and consider the BSPDE
\begin{equation}
\left\{
\begin{aligned}
-dP(t) &= \big[\mathcal L_{\rho,a,b} P(t) + b(t,P(t),Q(t))\big]\,dt - Q(t)\,dB(t),
\qquad t\in[0,T],\\
P(T) &= \phi,
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation}
understood in the variational sense in $V^*$.

Assume that $b:\Omega\times[0,T]\times \mathbb{H}\times \mathbb{H}\to \mathbb{H}$ is progressively measurable and that
there exists a constant $c>0$ such that for all $t\in[0,T]$ and all
$(p_1,q_1),(p_2,q_2)\in \mathbb{H}\times \mathbb{H}$,
\begin{equation}
\|b(t,p_1,q_1)-b(t,p_2,q_2)\|_\mathbb{H}
\le c\big(\|p_1-p_2\|_\mathbb{H}+\|q_1-q_2\|_\mathbb{H}\big),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\!\left[\int_0^T \|b(t,0,0)\|_\mathbb{H}^2\,dt\right]<\infty.
\end{equation}

Then there exists a unique adapted solution $(P,Q)$ to \eqref{eq:bspde-general} such that
\[
P\in L^2(\Omega;C([0,T];\mathbb{H}))\cap L^2(\Omega\times(0,T);V),
\qquad
Q\in L^2(\Omega\times(0,T);\mathbb{H}),
\]
and for all $t\in[0,T]$ the following identity holds $\mathbb P$-a.s.:
\[
P(t)=\phi+\int_t^T \big(\mathcal L_{\rho,a,b} P(s)+b(s,P(s),Q(s))\big)\,ds-\int_t^T Q(s)\,dB(s).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f_n -> f in measure or mu-almost everywhere","uniform integrability of {f_n}","uniform tightness of {f_n}: on an infinite measure space this is an independent hypothesis"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.751693+00:00","domain":"measure theory","id":"claim_0a5d28e3a2f0563534ddca90e6e5c1998a87b5c53300e2cd9dcf829e15f851d8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"On a FINITE measure space, uniform integrability plus convergence in measure gives L^1 convergence. On a general (for instance sigma-finite but infinite) measure space this is FALSE and a third hypothesis is needed. The correct statement: let (Omega, F, mu) be a measure space and f_n in L^1(mu) with f_n -> f in measure (or mu-a.e.). Then f_n -> f in L^1(mu) if and only if (i) {f_n} is uniformly integrable, meaning sup_n integral_{|f_n| > K} |f_n| dmu -> 0 as K -> infinity, AND (ii) {f_n} is uniformly tight, meaning for every eps > 0 there is a set A with mu(A) < infinity and sup_n integral_{Omega \\ A} |f_n| dmu < eps. Counterexample showing (ii) is not implied by (i): on R with Lebesgue measure take f_n = 1_{[n, n+1]}. Then |f_n| <= 1 so the family is uniformly integrable and dominated, f_n -> 0 pointwise everywhere, yet ||f_n||_1 = 1 for every n. Mass escapes to infinity; on a finite measure space it has nowhere to go, which is exactly why the finite-measure statement can omit (ii). [standard; e.g. Bogachev, Measure Theory, Vol. I, Section 4.5]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:07:17.256291+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0a60fd160e84429e26bd981f1133f3bc1725ae3b7b6dab59d1a3e3e6350bed50","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem ASASiid of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] There exists a sequence of deterministic values, called {Lyapunov exponents}
	\[
	\lambda_k < \cdots < \lambda_1, \qquad \lambda_i \in [-\infty, \infty),
	\]
	and a set of full measure $\tilde{\Omega} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathcal{B} \times \mathcal{B}$ with respect to $\mu \times \mathbf{P}$ such that 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The set $\tilde{\Omega}$ is $\Theta_t$-invariant for every $t \ge 0$.  
		For each $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$, define
		\[
		G_\lambda(\omega,x) := \left\{ z \in \mathbb{R}^d : 
		\limsup_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log \big| \mathrm{D}_x \Phi^t_\omega(z) \big| \le \lambda \right\}.
		\]
		Then $G_{\lambda_1}(\omega, x) = \mathbb{R}^d$, and for every $1 \le i < k$,
		\[
		z \in G_{\lambda_i}(\omega,x) \setminus G_{\lambda_{i+1}}(\omega,x)
		\quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad
		\lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log \big| \mathrm{D}_x \Phi^t_\omega(z) \big| = \lambda_i.
		\]
		Moreover, for all $z \in G_{\lambda_k}(\omega,x) \setminus \{0\}$,
		\[
		\lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log \big| \mathrm{D}_x \Phi^t_\omega(z) \big| = \lambda_k.
		\]
		\item Suppose $\lambda_1 < 0$ and that for some $r \in (0,1]$ and all $y,z \in \mathbb{R}^d$ there exist constants $\overline{C}_F > 0$ and $p_1 \ge 1$ such that
		\begin{equation}
			\| \mathrm{D}_y F - \mathrm{D}_z F \|_{L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)}
			\le \overline{C}_F (1 + |y| + |z|)^{p_1} |y-z|^r.
		\end{equation}
		Then there exists a full-measure set $\mathcal{M} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d \times \Omega$ such that, for every $0 < \nu < -\lambda_1$, there exists a positive random variable
		\begin{align}

		with the property that for all $(x,\omega) \in \mathcal{M}$ and all $y \in \mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying $|y| \le R^\nu(x,\omega)$,
		\[
		\sup_{t \ge 0} \exp(t\nu) \, \big| \Phi^t_\omega(x+y) - \Phi^t_\omega(x) \big| < \infty.
		\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. rows C^{1/2} z with z having i.i.d. mean-zero unit-variance entries and finite twelfth moment","p/n -> q_0 in (0, infinity)","the population spectral distribution converges to a limit with bounded support","the formula is used inside the bulk; isolated spikes are handled by the BBP correction"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T05:50:37.943602+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory","id":"claim_0a70bf7dec2d4a8e97f8b3a3a903aaf467d73a6d689fe2fb896f6788c775985a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $E = \\frac{1}{n} X^T X$ be the sample covariance of $n$ i.i.d. rows in $\\mathbb{R}^p$ with population covariance $C$ (rows $C^{1/2} z_i$ with $z_i$ having i.i.d. entries of mean zero, variance one and finite twelfth moment), in the regime $p, n \\to \\infty$ with $q = p/n \\to q_0 \\in (0, \\infty)$, and assume the spectral distribution of $C$ converges to a limit with bounded support. Let $\\lambda_k, u_k$ be the sample eigenvalues and eigenvectors and let $g_E(z) = \\frac{1}{p}\\operatorname{tr}(z I - E)^{-1}$ be the Stieltjes transform of the sample spectrum, with $g(\\lambda - i0) := \\lim_{\\eta \\downarrow 0} g_E(\\lambda - i\\eta)$ inside the bulk. THEOREM (Ledoit and Peche, 2011, Theorem 4; in the form of Bun, Bouchaud and Potters 2017). The oracle eigenvalues $\\xi_k^{\\mathrm{or}} = u_k^T C u_k$ converge, uniformly in $k$ inside the bulk, to $$\\xi(\\lambda_k) = \\frac{\\lambda_k}{\\big|\\, 1 - q + q\\, \\lambda_k\\, g_E(\\lambda_k - i0) \\,\\big|^2}.$$ This limit depends on the population covariance $C$ only through the observable sample spectrum, so it is a consistent, computable estimator (the rotationally invariant estimator, RIE, or nonlinear shrinkage): replace each sample eigenvalue by $\\xi(\\lambda_k)$, keep the sample eigenvectors. In practice $g_E$ is evaluated at $\\lambda_k - i\\eta$ with a small $\\eta$ of order $n^{-1/2}$ times the eigenvalue scale, and the result is floored at a small positive fraction of the bulk level. When $C = \\sigma^2 I$ the formula returns $\\sigma^2$ for every eigenvalue (the Marchenko-Pastur spread is entirely removed); for a spike above the bulk it returns approximately the debiased population spike. Applying the formula to a matrix whose largest eigenvalue is a signal one is trying to keep, and flooring relative to that top eigenvalue, destroys the small eigenvalues that the inverse depends on.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:43:45.379287+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0aa26f24c4760e3f56c26efc76ce5f53a34c26fbb62df233133ab251c052775b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2609.03993, 'The Endpoint Fractional Riesz Estimate on the Hamming Cube'] Let $0<\theta<1$.

{"assumptions":["Zero-mean fixed finite-rank GP, supplied feature norms <=R, independent Gaussian noise variance s>0","At most n context labels; all input locations and context length jointly independent of latent GP and noises; iid tasks","Full original posterior is the target; only the predictor clips context labels at the explicit deterministic B"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T16:46:14.074691+00:00","domain":"Gaussian process predictive approximation; context truncation","id":"claim_0aac28c997e413b6e870c7d366e02430c9ded09828abe71420cb34a1f75fae4a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"OWNER RESULT DRAFT, proof (unaudited), C007 v1; no novelty claim.
Let a fixed zero-mean finite-rank Gaussian process have a supplied feature map phi with ||phi(x)||<=R, independent Gaussian observation noise of variance s>0, and at most n context observations. All context/query input locations and context length are jointly independent of the GP and all noises. Context labels may be correlated and are not bounded or conditioned. Put V=s+R^2. Given the full original context W, let P_W=N(m,v) be the exact noisy posterior predictive. Clip each context label to [-B,B], B>0, and recompute the mean m_B with the same design; v is unchanged. Suppose a Gaussian predictor h_B=N(mhat,vhat), depending only on clipped context and supplied features, has vhat>=s and KL(N(m_B,v)||h_B)<=eps_c for every possible context and design. Then on the ORIGINAL unconditioned task law,
E_W KL(P_W||h_B) <= 2 eps_c + (2 sqrt(2) n^2 R^4 V/s^3) exp(-B^2/(4V)).
In particular, for eps>0, eps_c=eps/4 and B=sqrt(4V log(max(e,4 sqrt(2) n^2 R^4 V/(s^3 eps)))) make the expected KL at most eps. If nR=0 the bias is zero. This does not assert that N(m_B,v) is the conditional law given clipped labels. The supplied-feature comparator exists by the separately audited C002 construction; this clipping lemma itself awaits independent review.","status":"unverified"}
