{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:27:14.911750+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0aaecc49d44d87907f247a5d4649f0d44cb4b47482a6a7ec68426e9191e0ff9a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 1 (Criterion for $\Xstar_T$ {\cite[Lemma~4.1) of arXiv:2608.24294, 'Existence of densities and atoms for the running maximum of time-inhomogeneous jump diffus'] {NakagawaSuzuki2024}}]
Fix $p>1$ and $\Theta=(h,v)\in \Hb_{\infty-}\times \Vb_{\infty-}$.
For each $n\ge1$, let $\{X^{(n)}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a right-continuous real-valued process, and let $\{X_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a right-continuous real-valued process.
Write
\[
\Xstarn_T:=\sup_{0\le s\le T}X^{(n)}_s,
\qquad
\Xstar_T:=\sup_{0\le s\le T}X_s.
\]

Assume that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item $\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\E[|\Xstarn_T|^p]<\infty$, and for every $t\in[0,T]$ we have $X^{(n)}_t\in W^{1,p}_\Theta$ with
\[
\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\E\Big[\sup_{0\le s\le T}|D_\Theta X^{(n)}_s|^p\Big]<\infty;
\]
\item for each $n\ge1$, the process $\{D_\Theta X^{(n)}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ admits a right-continuous version;
\item $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty}\E\Big[\sup_{0\le s\le T}|X^{(n)}_s-X_s|^p\Big]=0$.
\end{enumerate}
Assume moreover that $D_\Theta X$ admits a right-continuous version and satisfies
\[
\Pbb\big(D_\Theta X_t\neq 0 \text{ on }\{t\in(0,T]: X_t=\Xstar_T\}\big)=1.
\]
Then the law of $\Xstar_T$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\R$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:33:43.752806+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0aaf0eeda49a148795c8062a1dac9b7fc0ce6d7bb1e6216fd9b2d6af9307a1f4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def_pointwise_multiplier of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] Fix $\eta\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\alpha\in[0,1)$ such that $\alpha=0$ if

and

{"assumptions":["Finite-dimensional Euclidean space; n>=2 components and K>=2 epochs","Convex C1 f_i with globally L_i-Lipschitz gradients, L_i>0","Proper closed convex psi and an attained finite minimum of F=f+psi","x_1 is in dom psi; eta is constant, positive, and satisfies the displayed K-dependent cap","For the expected random-reshuffling bound, use fresh independent uniform permutations","For the optimized-rate corollaries assume D>0; the fixed-step inequalities do not require D>0"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T15:34:11.132651+00:00","domain":"Liu Zhou; proximal shuffling; random reshuffling; last iterate; convex optimization","id":"claim_0ab04f1d8562a58b42caeb8c92cdff50dfe5a30627a7b67abd496813c58be7c6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let n>=2, K>=2 and d>=1. Let each f_i:R^d->R be convex C1 with globally L_i-Lipschitz gradient, L_i>0. Let psi:R^d->R union {+infinity} be proper closed convex. Set f=(1/n)sum_i f_i, F=f+psi, and suppose x* minimizes F with F(x*) finite. Start at x_1 in dom psi. Write D=||x_1-x*||, Lbar=(1/n)sum_i L_i, Lmax=max_i L_i, s=1+log K, sigma_any^2=(1/n)sum_i ||grad f_i(x*)||^2 and sigma_rand^2=sigma_any^2+n||grad f(x*)||^2. Use a fixed positive step eta<=1/[4n sqrt(2 Lbar Lmax s)]. In epoch k, set z_0=x_k, take z_i=z_(i-1)-eta grad f_(sigma_i)(z_(i-1)) for i=1,...,n along a permutation sigma, and set x_(k+1)=prox_(n eta psi)(z_n), where prox_(n eta psi)(z) minimizes psi(x)+||x-z||^2/(2n eta). There is an absolute constant C such that, for every sequence of permutations, F(x_(K+1))-F(x*)<=C[D^2/(n eta K)+(n eta)^2 Lbar sigma_any^2 s]. If fresh independent uniform permutations are used in each epoch, E[F(x_(K+1))-F(x*)]<=C[D^2/(n eta K)+n eta^2 Lbar sigma_rand^2 s]. These are bounds for the last epoch iterate, with no strong-convexity assumption. For D>0, balancing eta under the stated cap gives respectively O(D^2 sqrt(Lbar Lmax s)/K+D^(4/3)(Lbar sigma_any^2 s)^(1/3)/K^(2/3)) and O(D^2 sqrt(Lbar Lmax s)/K+D^(4/3)(Lbar sigma_rand^2 s)^(1/3)/(n^(1/3) K^(2/3))). The fixed-step bounds also cover D=0. All norms are Euclidean. Source: Zijian Liu and Zhengyuan Zhou, On the Last-Iterate Convergence of Shuffling Gradient Methods, Theorem 4.4 and its full version Theorem C.1.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T11:58:53.978374+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ab65f335e4846d89753e7dca87d1223","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Exact rank three for the bounded-density conjecture: what is proved and what is open. (1) The step 'a rank-three coarea bound ||p_S||_inf <= K ||rho||_inf^{2/3} for S = sum_{j<=3} lambda_j Y_j^2' is false for general bounded densities rho on R^3: a density rho <= B that puts mass 2hB A(s) on the shell {|S - s| < h} gives p_S about B A(s) near s, where A(s) = d/ds vol{S <= s} = 2 pi s^{1/2}/sqrt(lambda_1 lambda_2 lambda_3) for a definite form, unbounded as s grows; a bound needs regularity of rho beyond its supremum. (2) Orthonormal 3D projections of product densities have that regularity on spheres: their spherical means satisfy M_{y0}(r) <= 6/(pi r) uniformly in the centre, and definite rank-three forms have density <= 82 for every linear term. (3) The marginal bound is sharp and law-free: the projection onto a k-dimensional subspace of a vector with independent coordinates of densities <= 1 has density <= min{(n/(n-k))^{(n-k)/2}, 2^{k/2}} (Livshyts, Paouris and Pivovarov 2016); Ball's cube slicing is the uniform case and Rudelson-Vershynin give (CK)^d with an unspecified absolute C. (4) Indefinite exact rank three is bounded with any c-pivot, when every leverage is at most 1/2 (<= 12), for a leak-free hub with the linear term in the range (<= 278), and for a leaking hub with a spread light frame up to a factor log(1/eps); the no-pivot indefinite case with a hub (a hub plus a small cross term) is open and is the single-hub core of the general conjecture.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.211852+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ac6c86f902d62b5037f21bb5d2b9e94b3dc420f9686cffab5c2fcd0a8d5005a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] Fix constants $C',c', K>0$. 
Let $X$ be a nonnegative random variable such that $\E X \leq r$ and, for some $\sigma \in (0,K]$, 
\[
\P(X>u ) \leq C' e^{- c' u^2/\sigma^2}\,.
\]
Then for each $\lambda>0$, there exist constants $C_\lambda, c_\lambda>0$ (depending also on $c',C'$, and $K$) such that
\[
  \E e^{\lambda X}-1 \leq C_\lambda r + C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma}\,.
\]
\begin{proof}
On the event $\{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}\}$, the mean value theorem yields
\[
  \E[(e^{\lambda X} - 1) \ind{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq \E[\lambda e^{\lambda \sigma^{1/2}} X \ind{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda r\,,
\]
where the $\sigma$ independence in the last bound comes from $\sigma\leq K$.
On  $\{X > \sigma^{1/2}\}$, we write
\begin{multline}
  \E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] - (e^{\lambda \sigma^{1/2}}-1)\P(X>\sigma^{1/2})
  \\
  = \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} \int_0^x \partial_u (e^{\lambda u}) \d u ~\d \P_X(x)  
  = \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} \P(X>u) \lambda e^{\lambda u} \d  u  \leq C_\lambda \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} e^{-c'\frac{u^2}{\sigma^2} + \lambda u} \d u\,.
\end{multline}
Now, for $u\geq \sigma^{1/2}$ and $\lambda>0$, there exists $\sigma_\lambda>0$ such that for all $\sigma \in (0,\sigma_\lambda]$, we have 
$
  \lambda u \leq \tfrac{c' u^2}{2\sigma^2}$.
For such $\sigma$, it follows from \eqref{eq:layer-cake} that
$
  \E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma}\,.
$
For $\sigma >\sigma_\lambda$, note that the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:layer-cake} can be bounded by a constant $C_\lambda'>0$ times the Laplace transform of a Gaussian with variance $K^2/2c'$
to get 
$\E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda$,
possibly enlarging $C_\lambda$ from before.
We finish by multiplying by $e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma} e^{c_\lambda/\sigma_\lambda}$, which is larger than $1$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f is continuous on a closed cylinder around (t_0,y_0)","f is Lipschitz in y, uniformly in t, on that cylinder"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T14:20:41.451641+00:00","domain":"ordinary differential equations","id":"claim_0ad98344cc4c4b7f94070b09639fced6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f: [t_0-a,t_0+a] x B(y_0,b) -> R^n be continuous, where B(y_0,b) subset R^n is the closed ball of radius b around y_0, and suppose f is Lipschitz in its second argument uniformly in the first: there is L >= 0 with |f(t,y_1)-f(t,y_2)| <= L|y_1-y_2| for all t in the interval and y_1,y_2 in B(y_0,b). Let M = max|f(t,y)| over this compact domain and h = min(a, b/M). Then the initial value problem y'(t) = f(t,y(t)), y(t_0)=y_0, has a unique solution y on [t_0-h, t_0+h]. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:38:04.525682+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ae1b4267139277f9deeb412aaabc6ee6c548ef0d00de6bde7b964ee7ab405b2","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition eq:third_renormalisation of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] For $i \geq 0$ and for $c_{\mathrm{vor}}{}$ as in \thref{prop:tile_and_cell_volume_bounds}, we let 
    
    \begin{equation}
        
        \rho_i 
        = 
       
            1 - (i+s)^{-3/2}/2
      
        ,

        \quad
        \text{and}
        \quad
        C_i
        =
        c_{\mathrm{vor}}{}
        (m_i/2)^d.
    \end{equation}
    
    We say that a level-$0$ tile $\Tile{0}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if it contains a cluster $\mathcal{C}_{0,j}$ satisfying
    
    \begin{equation}
        \# 
        \left(
            \mathcal{C}_{0,j}
            \cap

        \right)
        \geq 
        \nu 
        \# B(r_0/2),
    \end{equation}
    
    where $\nu$ is as in \thref{prop:biskup}.
    
    For a good level-$0$ tile $\Tile{0}{j}$, the \textbf{good part} is $\mathcal{C}_{0,j}
            \cap
            B(x_{0,j},r_0/4)$.
    
    We say that a level-$1$ tile $\Tile{1}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if at least a $\rho_1$ proportion of its level-$0$ subtiles are good, and their good parts are connected to each other inside $\Tile{1}{j}$.

    For a good level-$i$ tile $\Tile{i}{j}$, we choose $C_i$ of its good level-$i-1$ subtiles and the \textbf{good part} of $\Tile{i}{j}$ is the union of the good parts of these subtiles, denoted by $\mathcal{C}_{i,j}$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:06:18.018139+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0aef0141d919e0e19efdf652be1d05369f7101a8b0e2efebee9eed78a173f38b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 13 (Two-level kernel for fixed-orientation nested rectangles) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Let $(m_0,n_0)$ and $(m_1,n_1)$ satisfy
\[
 m_0\leq m_1,\qquad n_0\leq n_1,
\]
and assume the same physical side is weakly larger at both endpoints. If
\[
 m_0\geq n_0,\qquad m_1\geq n_1,
\]
put
\[
 (p,q,P,Q)=(n_0,m_0,n_1,m_1).
\]
If
\[
 n_0\geq m_0,\qquad n_1\geq m_1,
\]
put
\[
 (p,q,P,Q)=(m_0,n_0,m_1,n_1).
\]
Set
\[
 A=P-p,\quad B=Q-q,\quad r_0=q-p,\quad r=Q-P,
\]
and assume $A+B\geq1$. Put
\[
 \mathcal L_{d,\alpha}(x,y)
 =
 \sum_{k=0}^{d-1}
 \frac{k!}{(k+\alpha)!}
 L_k^{(\alpha)}(x)L_k^{(\alpha)}(y).
\]

Define $W(x,z)=0$ unless $z>x$. If $A=0$, set
\begin{equation}
 W(x,z)=\ee^{-z}\frac{(z-x)^{B-1}}{(B-1)!}.
\end{equation}
If $B=0$, set
\begin{equation}
 W(x,z)=
 \ee^{-z}z^r\frac{(z-x)^{A-1}}{(A-1)!}.
\end{equation}
If $A,B\geq1$, set
\begin{equation}
 W(x,z)
 =
 \ee^{-z}z^r
 \int_x^z
 \frac{(u-x)^{B-1}u^{-(r+A)}(z-u)^{A-1}}
 {(B-1)!(A-1)!}\,\dd u.
\end{equation}

The two-level positive squared-singular-value process is determinantal. With the earlier level indexed by zero and the later level by one, one exact kernel has blocks
\begin{equation}
 K_{11}(x,y)
 =
 \ee^{-y}y^r\mathcal L_{P,r}(x,y),
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 K_{00}(x,y)
 =
 \ee^{-x}y^{r_0}\mathcal L_{p,r_0}(x,y)
 \qquad(B\geq1),
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 K_{00}(x,y)
 =
 \ee^{-x}x^{r_0}\mathcal L_{p,r_0}(x,y)
 \qquad(B=0),
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 K_{10}(x,y)
 =
 \left(\frac{\dd}{\dd y}\right)^B
 (E_y-rI)^{\mathrm{fall}\,A}
 [y^r\mathcal L_{P,r}(x,y)]
 \qquad(B\geq1),
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 K_{10}(x,y)
 =
 \left(\frac{\dd}{\dd y}\right)^A
 \mathcal L_{P,r}(x,y)
 \qquad(B=0),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 K_{01}(x,y)
 =
 -W(x,y)
 +
 \int_0^\infty W(x,z)K_{11}(z,y)\,\dd z.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:47:53.348324+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0af011f94e62f7ccab35fbda2461902128b8787a5db6a09c81fbf3d6dbdbfcb3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 10 ($n$-atomic $q$-Bass map) of arXiv:2607.15872, 'Existence of $q$-Bass martingales in the semidiscrete setting'] Let $\nu \in \Prob_1(\RR), q \in \Prob(\RR)$ such that $q \ll \lambda$, and define the function $g:\RR^{n-1}_{\geq 0}\times\RR\to\RR$ by
\[
g(h,z)=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j F_q\left(z-\sum_{k=1}^{j-1}h_k\right),
\qquad h=(h_1,\dots,h_{n-1})\in\RR^{n-1}_{\geq 0},\ z\in\RR.
\]
The map $f:\RR^{n-1}_{\geq 0}\to\RR^{n-1}$ defined componentwise by
\begin{equation}

	f_i(h_1, \dots, h_{n-1})
	=
	\int_\RR Q_\nu \big(g(h,z)\big)\,
	\sum_{j=1}^{i} p_j \rho_q \left( z - \sum_{k=1}^{j-1} h_k \right)\, dz,
	\qquad i\in\{1,\dots,n-1\},
\end{equation}
is called the \emph{$n$-atomic $q$-Bass map} with respect to the weights $p_1,\dots,p_n$ and terminal distribution $\nu$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:38:17.819804+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0afc50d0d9eebc04f3bcc2f47f01177c1d0dc7f3736bbf43f1b5e87583714390","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition p.sfacts of arXiv:2510.07682, 'From tug-of-war to Brownian Boost: \\ explicit ODE solutions for player-funded stochastic-'] Let $\rho,\xi \in (0,\infty)$ and $u \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$.
\begin{enumerate}

 $S_\rho(1,-u) = S_\rho(1,u)^{-1}$.
\item Now let $v = v(\xi)$ denote the unique real number such that $8 \rho v = 2\log \xi + \rho^{-1} \big( \xi^\rho - \xi^{-\rho} \big)$.

$$

$$
\item $f_\rho(1,u) = g_\rho(1,-u)$.
\item $f_\rho(1,u)$ and $g_\rho(1,u)$ are bounded above by $e^{-2 \vert u \vert+o(\vert u \vert)}$ as $\vert u \vert  \to \infty$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:13:18.501965+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0afdafd4b352c5fcad844d588f8048f7a3634622f9b8b5964f08fe8ff6f0d068","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theo 22 (Explicit threshold, compact-support branch and onset amplitude) of arXiv:2608.30578, 'Compactly Supported Solutions near a Nehari Critical Value'] Let $0<\alpha<1$ and $n\ge2$. Consider the problem
\[
\begin{cases}
	-u''=\lambda u+m_n(x)u^\alpha,& -1<x<1,\\
	u(-1)=u(1)=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Define
\[
\lambda_{c,n}:=
\frac{\pi^2}
{\left((1-\alpha)+\dfrac{1+\alpha}{n}\right)^2}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{\pi^2}{4}
<
\lambda_{c,n}
<
\lambda_n^*.
\]
At $\lambda=\lambda_{c,n}$ there exists an even positive flat solution
$u_{c,n}$ satisfying $u_{c,n}(\pm1)=u_{c,n}'(\pm1)=0$. For every
$\lambda\in(\lambda_{c,n},\lambda_n^*)$ there exists a unique even
non-negative solution in the above class whose connected support is
\[
\operatorname{supp}u_{\lambda,n}
=
[-b_{\lambda,n},b_{\lambda,n}]
\Subset(-1,1),
\]
where
\[
b_{\lambda,n}
=
\frac{1}{1-\alpha}
\left(
\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{\lambda}}
-\frac{1+\alpha}{n}
\right).
\]
For $x\ge0$ the solution is
\[
u_{\lambda,n}(x)
=
\begin{cases}
	A_{\lambda,n}\cos(\sqrt{\lambda}\,x),
	& 0\le x\le\dfrac1n,\\[2mm]
	\displaystyle
	\left(
	\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\lambda}
	\right)^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
	\sin^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}}
	\left[
	\frac{1-\alpha}{2}\sqrt{\lambda}\,
	(b_{\lambda,n}-x)
	\right],
	& \dfrac1n\le x\le b_{\lambda,n},\\[3mm]
	0,
	& b_{\lambda,n}\le x\le1,
\end{cases}
\]
and it is extended evenly to $(-1,0)$. Moreover,
\[
A_{\lambda,n}
=
\|u_{\lambda,n}\|_{L^\infty(-1,1)}
=
\left(
\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\lambda}
\right)^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
\cos^{\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}}
\left(\frac{\sqrt{\lambda}}{n}\right).
\]
For each fixed $n$, the mapping $\lambda\longmapsto A_{\lambda,n}$
is strictly decreasing on $(\lambda_{c,n},\lambda_n^*)$, and
$A_{\lambda,n}\longrightarrow0\hbox{ as }\lambda\uparrow\lambda_n^*$. If
\[
A_n:=\|u_{c,n}\|_{L^\infty(-1,1)},
\]
then
\[
A_n=
\left[
\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\pi^2}
\left(
(1-\alpha)+\frac{1+\alpha}{n}
\right)^2
\right]^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
\cos^{\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}}
\left(
\frac{\pi}{n(1-\alpha)+(1+\alpha)}
\right),
\]
and
\[
\lambda_{c,n}\uparrow
\lambda_{c,\infty}:=
\frac{\pi^2}{(1-\alpha)^2},
\]
while
\[
A_n\longrightarrow
A_\infty:=
\left[
\frac{2(1-\alpha)^2}
{(1+\alpha)\pi^2}
\right]^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
>0.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
\frac{\lambda_{c,n}}{\lambda_n^*}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover, $H_\lambda(u_{\lambda,n})=M_n(u_{\lambda,n})<0$, and therefore
$E_\lambda(u_{\lambda,n})>0,\ E_\lambda''(u_{\lambda,n})<0$. Thus, these
explicit solutions have the variational character of the
branch $u_{\lambda,n}^-$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.219598+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0afdbdc971c547695c9e078780fb9154254908c50aad10fa4c595f8a18883c32","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 2 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Let $B$ be a ball in $\sX$ with  $\overline B\subsetneq \sX.$
 For an open subset $U\subset B,$
  we say $G^B_U(x, y)$ is
the Green function of $X^B$ in $U$ (or equivalently $X^U$)  with respect to the measure $m_B$ if it is  not identically infinite and is  the potential kernel of $X^B$ in $U$. That is, the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item[\rm (i)]
 For any Borel bounded function  $f\geq 0$ on $U$,
$$
\E_x \int_0^{\tau_U} f(X_s) ds=\E_x \int_0^{\tau_U} f(X^B_s) ds = \int_U G^B_U (x, y) f(y) m_B(dy), \quad \hbox{for} \quad x\in U.

\item[\rm (ii)]
For each fixed $y\in U,$ $x\mapsto G^B_U(x, y)$ is excessive with respect to $X^B$ in $U.$ For each fixed $x\in U,$  $y\mapsto G^B_U(x, y)$ is excessive with respect to $\wh X^{B, U}.$

 \end{enumerate}

  When   $U=B$,  we denote the Green function $G^B_U(x, y)$ by $G^B(x, y)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X compact, T continuous.","The two limits in eps are monotone so they exist in [0, infinity];","separated and spanning counts interleave by r(n,eps) <= s(n,eps) <= r(n, eps/2), which is why the two definitions agree."],"created_at":"2026-09-12T14:04:29.025418+00:00","domain":"dynamical systems, entropy","id":"claim_0b2a19515f9b50a6070dee1dd7534cd4a246344088b2dfd716b30980eb13ccc5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X,d) be a compact metric space and T : X -> X continuous. Define the Bowen metric d_n(x,y) = max over 0 <= k < n of d(T^k x, T^k y). A set E is (n, eps)-SEPARATED if distinct points of E are at d_n-distance greater than eps; a set F is (n, eps)-SPANNING if every point of X is within d_n-distance eps of some point of F. Let s(n,eps) be the largest cardinality of an (n,eps)-separated set and r(n,eps) the smallest cardinality of an (n,eps)-spanning set. Then the topological entropy is h_top(T) = lim as eps -> 0 of limsup_n (1/n) log s(n,eps) = lim as eps -> 0 of limsup_n (1/n) log r(n,eps), and this agrees with the open-cover definition of Adler, Konheim and McAndrew. The quantity does not depend on the metric, only on the topology, and is invariant under topological conjugacy.","status":"unverified"}

    For $i \in [\max \left( d_1 , d_2 \right)]$,
    set

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-11-02T23:06:16.394829+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_0b55c2d88e03d2f8000ab6cf220ac242624096435ae66578a4f66109c1b2ba36","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Publication record. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:01:25.646081+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b600bdd255e11fc7c6c972317800c314127899fe0b9377f9b5f18986b1b3020","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:exceptional-boundary-pairs of arXiv:2605.16086, 'Loop pruning and downward deviations for maximum local time of discrete-time simple random'] For each pair \((i,v)\in [0,u_n]\times \mathcal{U}\) with \(v\in V^{\partial}(W_i)\), called a boundary pair, define
\[
\eta^{(i,v)}
:=\bigl(S[0,N^{-1}(i)]\circ_t \eta_{\mathrm{exp}}^{v,W_i}\bigr)\circ_d S'[i,u_n],
\]
Equivalently, in the loop-pruned decomposition notation,
\[
\eta^{(i,v)}
=S'[0,u_n]\oplus(\xi_k^{(i,v)})_{0\le k\le u_n},
\qquad
\xi_k^{(i,v)}
=
\begin{cases}
\xi_k, & 0\le k<i,\\
\eta_{\mathrm{exp}}^{v,W_i}, & k=i,\\
(0), & i<k\le u_n.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus \(\eta^{(i,v)}\) is obtained from the pruned path \(S'[0,u_n]\) by adding back the pruned loops in their canonical order, stopping at the time corresponding to the boundary address \(v\) in the \(i\)-th erased segment.

For \(x\in\mathbb Z^d\), we say that \(x\) is \textit{critical for the boundary pair \((i,v)\)} if
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\ell_x\bigl(\eta^{(i,v)}\bigr)\ge \Lambda_n
\quad\text{and}\quad
\exists\,e\in E\ \text{such that }
\ell_x\bigl(\eta^{(i,v)}\triangleleft_j e\bigr)
>\ell_x\bigl(\eta^{(i,v)}\bigr),\\
&\text{with }j=N^{-1}(i)+\tau_{\mathrm{exp}}^{v,W_i}.
\end{aligned}
\]

We then define the exceptional boundary-pair set
\[
\mathsf{Exc}_n
:=
\Bigl\{
\text{boundary pairs }(i,v):
\exists\,x\in\mathbb Z^d
\text{ that is critical for }(i,v)
\Bigr\}.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0064-infrared-bound-for-nearest-neighbour-percolation-in-every-dimension-d","No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:26:45.042777+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b65f9440e44a1939a7c37c4a3d79566b822d1d97ca4449343b4b1d8ecf71796","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine the small parameter of the lace expansion and whether a different expansion parameter exists for d in {7,...,10}. Result: The lace expansion converges when the triangle diagram at p_c is small, which for nearest-neighbour percolation is controlled by the random-walk quantities: the triangle at p_c is bounded by a constant times (2d)^{-1} times sum over n of the return probabilities, i.e. by beta_d = O(1/d); the NoBLE refinement replaces 1/d by a numerically computed constant and the bootstrap closes for d >= 11 because the computed bound on the triangle at d = 10 exceeds the threshold. Below d = 11 there is no small parameter: the triangle diagram is of order 1 but finite for d > 6, and finiteness alone does not make the expansion converge; convergence needs smallness. An alternative is to bootstrap from d = 11 downward using a continuous interpolation in the dimension (long-range or spread-out interpolation), but the interpolated models at d = 10 are spread-out models, whose infrared bound is already known, and the interpolation does not return to the nearest-neighbour model at d = 10 without passing through a non-small regime. So the obstruction is structural: the method requires a small parameter and there is none for nearest-neighbour d in {7,...,10}. A rigorous partial statement: the infrared bound holds for the nearest-neighbour model in d in {7,...,10} on any lattice whose triangle diagram at p_c is below the NoBLE threshold, which fails for Z^d but holds for some non-Z^d lattices of higher coordination number (e.g. the body-centred or the D_d-type lattices in d = 7, 8 where the coordination number is larger); I did not verify the threshold numerically for those lattices. Obstruction: No small parameter for nearest-neighbour Z^d with 7 <= d <= 10.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:18:27.580584+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b8185d657d046e082a7b6c18e617f82ef2c43b55fb618f9ff5d5ee03cb237cf","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 20 (Girsanov is not tight) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Let $\Prob_{\mathrm{true}}$ and $\Prob_{\mathrm{dir}}$ be the laws of the full and the directed (single-parent-conditioned) systems on a time interval $[0,\tau]$. The Radon--Nikodym density is
\[
\log\frac{d\Prob_{\mathrm{true}}}{d\Prob_{\mathrm{dir}}}=\int_0^\tau\langle b^{-1}\Delta_t,dW_t\rangle-\frac12\int_0^\tau\|b^{-1}\Delta_t\|^2\,dt,
\]
where $\Delta_t=\gamma\,\sigma\big(s^{(v)}_t-\theta_{vu}\big)$ is the back-reaction drift. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:57:30.960954+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b8f18fe327e34760324678511b662199c5eee8dc7271fd991035361750bc333","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 8 (Connection splitting of higher-order tangent vectors) of arXiv:2608.12225, 'Higher-order variation and\\ pathwise It\^o calculus on manifolds'] Let $M$ be a smooth manifold equipped with an affine connection
$\nabla$, and let $p\geq1$. Then the map
\[

    \longrightarrow

    \oplus

    \qquad
    j_x^p f
    \longmapsto
    \bigl(
        f(x),\nabla f(x),\ldots,\nabla^{(p)}f(x)
    \bigr),
\]
is a linear isomorphism. Consequently, dualizing and removing the
zeroth-order component yields a connection-dependent bundle
isomorphism
\[
    S_p^\nabla:
    \tau^{(p)}M
    \longrightarrow
    \bigoplus_{k=1}^p\Sym^k(TM).
\]
Thus every $L\in\tau_x^{(p)}M$ is represented uniquely by tensors
$    A_k\in\Sym^k(T_xM), 1\leq k\leq p,$
such that
\begin{equation}
    Lf
    =
    \sum_{k=1}^p
    \frac1{k!}
    \left\langle
        \nabla^{(k)}f(x),A_k
    \right\rangle.
    
\end{equation}
Moreover, this splitting is compatible with the filtration
\[
    0\longrightarrow\tau^{(p-1)}M
    \longrightarrow\tau^{(p)}M
    \longrightarrow\Sym^p(TM)
    \longrightarrow0.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:32:56.096630+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b8f3e049cc44d3d26af803befac5668dd0d79ddd52f4782d563350cc0edd79a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Def:limit_shape of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'] For $G\neq \delta_0$ and $0\le \theta \le \frac \pi 2$, we define the curve

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:54:12.530658+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b97a085ebb8eb2a53f1e99830513c8ea60dabfabe9709d7d7c3a39babfd941a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:coupr of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $I=\llbracket a,b\rrbracket$ for some $-\infty \le a < b \le \infty$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:36:44.527213+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0bb8e071126343b77b34535612ee300a284954dd91f4b90b2d41362908fc0d9e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 5 of arXiv:2604.01748, 'Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$'] Let $\lambda = [\lambda(0), \lambda(1), \cdots, \lambda(m)]$ be a path of length $m$ in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$. 
    \begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] Define
    $$ l_{1} = \max \big\{ k -j \ : \ 0 \le j \le k \le m, \ \lambda (j) = \lambda (k) \big\}. $$
This is the maximum length of loops in $\lambda$. Among the pairs $(j,k)$ that attain the maximum on the right-hand side of the definition of $l_{1}$ above, let $(j_{1},k_{1})$ be the one with the smallest $j$:
\begin{itemize}
\item let 
$$\Lambda (1) = \Big\{ (j, k) \, : \, 0 \le j \le k \le m, \ \ \lambda (j) = \lambda (k), \ \ k-j = l_{1} \Big\},$$
\item set 
$$ j_{1} = \min \big\{ 0 \le  j \le m \, : \, \exists k \in [j, m] \, \text{ such that } \, (j,k) \in \Lambda (1) \big\},$$
\item choose $k_{1}$ so that 
$(j_{1}, k_{1}) \in \Lambda (1). $
\end{itemize}
That is, $(j_{1},k_{1})$ is the leftmost pair $(j,k)$ such that $\lambda(j)=\lambda(k)$ and $k-j=l_{1}$.

\item[(ii)]
 We define $\lambda_{1}$ to be the path obtained from $\lambda$ by removing this maximal loop. That is, $\lambda_{1}$ is a path of length $m - k_{1} + j_{1}$ defined by 
$$ \lambda_{1} = [\lambda (0), \cdots, \lambda (j_{1}), \lambda (k_{1} +1), \cdots \lambda (m) ] = \lambda [0, j_{1}] \oplus \lambda [k_{1}, m]. $$
Note that $\lambda = \lambda_{1}$ if and only if $\lambda$ is a simple path. For notational convenience, we abbreviate $\lambda$ as $\lambda_0$.

\item[(iii)] Apply the procedures (i) and (ii) above to $\lambda_{1}$ in the same way. Denote the resulting path by $\lambda_{2}$. Repeating the same procedure, $\lambda_{3}, \lambda_{4}, \cdots$ are obtained.

\item[(iv)] Define $q$ by
$$ q = \min \Big\{ l \ge 0 \ : \ \text{ $\lambda_{l}$ is a simple path} \Big\}.$$
 The largest-loop-first (LLF) loop-erasure of $\lambda$ is given by 
 $$ \text{LE}^{\ast} (\lambda) = \lambda_{q}. $$

\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:02:34.830532+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0bbb7013515d9200ad03b39966477906154d5f6ff3db149169d3a5bb1e6f889b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 24 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Assume that the action of $G$ on $\wt B$ satisfies the moment condition \eqref{moment-assumption-01},
the action of $G$ on $B$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B},

Suppose that, for every $\wt b \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b) \in \supp \nu$,  we have $\wt b M \subset \overline{\Gamma_{\mu} \wt b}$. 
Fix $\wt b_0 \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b_0) \in \supp \nu$. 
Then, for every character $(\chi, t)$ of the group $(M \times \bb R)/ M_1^{\mu}$, the operator $P_{\mu, \chi, it}$ 
has a unique eigenvalue $\lambda_{\chi, t}$ of modulus one in the space $W_{\chi}^{0}$. 

Moreover, there exists a unique associated eigenvector $\varphi_{\chi, t} \in W_{\chi}^{0}$
such that $\varphi_{\chi, t}(\wt b_0) = 1$ and $\varphi_{\chi, t}$ is H\"older continuous on $\wt B$.  
Also, the generalized eigenspace associated with the eigenvalue $\lambda_{\chi, t}$ for the operator $P_{\mu, \chi, it}$ acting on the space $W_{\chi}^0$ 
is equal to $\bb C \varphi_{\chi, t}$, that is, this eigenvalue is multiplicity free. 

Finally, the restriction $\varphi_{\chi, t}|_{\eta^{-1}(\supp \nu)}$ is the unique continuous function on $\eta^{-1}(\supp \nu)$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:40:22.370540+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0bc3473a9b51457a5a282678cc515903150f642ab5ad1c64b8556284c1a1b53d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm thm-cont-time-walk of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] There exists a function $\mathfrak w_* : \mathcal V\mathcal G \to (0,\infty)$ such that for each function $\mathfrak w : \mathcal V\mathcal G \to (0,\infty)$ with $\mathfrak w(x) \geq \mathfrak w_*(x) ,\, \forall x\in\mathcal V\mathcal G$ and for each possible starting point $z \in \mathcal V\mathcal G$, the following is true. There is a unique (in law) continuous-time stochastic process $X : [0,\infty) \to \mathcal V\mathcal G \cup \{\infty\}$ with $X_0 = z$, called the \textbf{continuous time random walk on $\mathcal G$ reflected off of infinity}, which satisfies the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[($i$)]
\item  \textit{(Almost everywhere defined).} For each $t\geq0$, a.s.\ $X_t \in \mathcal V\mathcal G$ and there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $X_s = X_t$ for each $s\in (t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon)$. 
\item  \textit{(Right continuity).} Almost surely, for every $t\geq 0$ such that $X_t\in\mathcal V\mathcal G$, there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $X_s = X_t$ for each $s\in [t,t+\varepsilon]$. 
\item  \textit{(Continuous time random walk).} If we let $\tau := \min\{t > 0:  X_t \not= z \}$, then $\tau$ and $X_\tau$ are independent, $\tau$ has the exponential distribution with rate $\mathfrak w(z)$, and $X_\tau$ has the law of a step of the random walk on $\mathcal G$ started at $z$ (i.e., for each $x \sim z$, $\mathbbm P[X_\tau = x] = \mathfrak c(z,x) / \pi(z)$). 
\item  \textit{(Markov property).} For every $t\geq 0$ and $x\in\mathcal V\mathcal G$, on the event $\{X_t = x\}$, the conditional law of $\{X_{s+t} \}_{s\geq 0}$ given $\{X_s\}_{s\leq t}$ is the same as the law of $\{X_s\}_{s\geq 0}$ started from $X_0=x$.  
\item  \textit{(Recurrence).} Almost surely, there exist arbitrarily large values of $t\geq 0$ for which $X_t = z$. 
\item  \textit{(Relation to harmonic functions).} Let $\mathcal A\subset \mathcal V\mathcal G$ be a non-empty finite set and let $\phi : \mathcal A\to\mathbbm R$. Let $h^\phi : \mathcal V\mathcal G\to\mathbbm R$ be the energy-minimizing discrete harmonic function as in Proposition~(prop-min-harmonic of the paper). If we let $\tau := \min\{t\geq 0 : X_t \in\mathcal A\}$, then for each choice of starting point $z\in\mathcal V\mathcal G$, 
\begin{equation*}
h^\phi(z) = \mathbbm E_z\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft[ \phi(X_\tau) \aftergroup\egroup\originalright] .
\end{equation*}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.160341+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0bce53c2a54a877341b0ab6914a27bb4ca63a6faae2fb61944aae563360a55f7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 4 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any constant $\delta > 0$, there exists $c = c(\alpha, L, \delta) > 0$ such that with probability $1-e^{-cN}$,
    \begin{align}
        
        \bigg|\frac{\|\bar{\bx}\|^2}{N} - 1\bigg| &\le \delta\,,\\
    
        \bigg|\frac{\E[ \|\hat{\by}\|^2 | \bG]}{N} - 1\bigg| &\le
        \frac{\delta}{2}\,.
    \end{align} 
Moreover, conditional on any realization of $\bG$ satisfying \eqref{e:fp-y-cond-conc} the following holds. Let $\hat{\bx} = N^{1/2} \bar{\bx}  / \|\bar{\bx}\|$ (we set this arbitrarily to $\bone \in \R^N$ if $\bar{\bx} = \bzero$). Let $\bXi'$ be an independent copy of $\bXi$ and $\hat{\by}' = \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi')$. Then
    \beq
        
        \lt|\frac{\|\hat{\by}\|^2}{N} - 1\rt|\,,
        \frac{|(\hat{\bx},\hat{\by})|}{N},
        \frac{|(\hat{\by},\hat{\by}')|}{N} \le \delta
    \eeq
   with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$.

\begin{proof}
    Since $\bG \mapsto \|\bar{\bx}\|$ is $L$-Lipschitz, $\|\bar{\bx}\|$ is $O(1)$-subgaussian by gaussian concentration of measure.
    Combined with $\E \|\bar{\bx}\|^2 = N$ this implies \eqref{e:fp-x-conc}.
    We next argue that the function
    \[
        f(\bG) = \E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}
    \]
    is also $L$-Lipschitz. Indeed,
    \[
        \nabla f(\bG)
        = \frac{\E[ (\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi))(\bG,\bXi) \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi) | \bG]}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}}\,,
    \]
    and thus
    \[
        \|\nabla f(\bG)\|^2
        = \frac{\|\E[ (\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)) \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi) | \bG]\|^2}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}
        \le \frac{\E[ \|\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|_\op^2 \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}
        \le L^2\,.
    \]
    Thus $\E[ \|\hat{\by}\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}$ is also $O(1)$-subgaussian.
    Combined with $\E \|\hat{\by}\|^2 = N$ this proves \eqref{e:fp-y-cond-conc}. 
    The first inequality of \eqref{e:fp-y-conc} follows similarly to \eqref{e:fp-x-conc}, applying gaussian concentration on $\bXi$ conditional on $\bG$.

    The third inequality of \eqref{e:fp-y-conc} follows similarly, conditioning further on a realization of $\hat{\by}$ such that $\|\hat{\by}\| \le 2N^{1/2}$ (which holds with probability $1-e^{-cN}$).
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:04:07.031757+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0bd972b23ea9d4d9bac50a2f8de700e903f9daf0083c5cf3bb9e0d3e871209d6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:one-point-conditional-hessian of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] Let \(f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)\) be regular, let \(\zeta=\zeta_f\), and let

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:29:28.004370+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0be3138574ffaada721bb9e1ba66473c719d7e17a3eee97388a92c6a47fcaa1c","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 3 (Radial order-statistic representation) of arXiv:2608.24964, 'Common-Center Geometry and Certified Radial Reconstruction for Energy-Form Full Conformal '] Assume $I_1,\ldots,I_m$ are each star-shaped about the same point $c$.  For
\[

\]
define
\[
R_j(u)=\sup\{r\ge0:c+ru\in I_j\}\in[0,\infty].
\]
Let
\[
R_{(1)}(u)\le\cdots\le R_{(m)}(u)
\]
be the ascending order statistics.  For $0\le\varepsilon<1$ and
\[
1\le k=\lfloor(m+1)\varepsilon\rfloor\le m,
\]

\[
R_\varepsilon(u)

\]
Thus finite power-distance radial reconstruction begins at $m\ge2$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["product measure on a finite product of totally ordered two-point spaces (or a measure satisfying the FKG lattice condition)","both functions increasing, or both decreasing","square integrability"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.542860+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0bf9a3e418fbc58529078909919960e7533413ef78f5b985e45f4917e302a72f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let P be a PRODUCT probability measure on {0,1}^E with E finite (the infinite case follows by approximation). Call f : {0,1}^E -> R increasing if f(omega) <= f(omega') whenever omega_e <= omega'_e for every e. Then for increasing f and g in L^2(P), E[f g] >= E[f] E[g]. In particular, for INCREASING events A and B, P(A and B) >= P(A) P(B), and for two DECREASING events the same inequality holds. For one increasing and one decreasing event the inequality REVERSES: P(A and B) <= P(A) P(B). The hypothesis that both functions are monotone IN THE SAME DIRECTION is the whole content; nothing is claimed for events of mixed or no monotonicity. The result extends beyond product measures to any measure satisfying the FKG LATTICE CONDITION mu(x or y) mu(x and y) >= mu(x) mu(y), which covers the random-cluster and ferromagnetic Ising measures; that extension is the FKG inequality proper, Harris's version being the product case. [Harris (1960); Fortuin, Kasteleyn and Ginibre (1971); see Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Theorem 2.4]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:29:21.917044+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c01392a1bd9c746e686d9a5483d0fcac5dfd5992ca13f504729f5d405f12239","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 (Extended mapping) of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$, let $d\in\mathbb N$,
and let
$f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\colon \mathbb R^n\to \mathbb R^k$ be a measurable mapping
such that
\[
0<\sigma_{f_j}^2:=\operatorname{Var}_\mu(f_j)<\infty
\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}.
\]
Let
\[
\hat f_j
=
\sigma_{f_j}^{-1}
\biggl(f_j-\int_{\mathbb R^n} f_j\,d\mu\biggr)
\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\},
\]
and set
$\hat f:=(\hat f_1,\ldots,\hat f_k)$.
Assume also that
\[
\hat f^{\mathbf m}:=\hat f_1^{m_1}\ldots \hat f_k^{m_k}\in L^2(\mu)
\quad \forall \mathbf m=(m_1,\ldots,m_k)\in\mathbb Z_+^k
\quad\text{with}\quad
1\le |\mathbf m|\le d^{k-1}.
\]
We define the \emph{extended mapping} of order $d$ by
\[
F_\mu^d(f)
=
\bigl(\hat f^{\mathbf m}\bigr)_{1\le |\mathbf m|\le d^{k-1}},
\]
and set
\[
\Sigma_\mu^d(f):=\operatorname{Cov}_\mu \bigl(F_\mu^d(f)\bigr).
\]
In other words, $\Sigma_\mu^d(f)$ is the matrix, in the monomial basis, of the quadratic form
\[
Q\mapsto \operatorname{Var}_\mu\bigl(Q(\hat f)\bigr),\quad Q\in\mathcal P_{d^{k-1}}(\mathbb R^k),\quad
Q(0)=0.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f in L^1(mu); the conclusion fails for f merely locally integrable with a non-integrable singularity"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.751760+00:00","domain":"measure theory","id":"claim_0c039b146bde482b5bfdfebdcb4b9034381228ac2f84c60709b2e4ec59f3f350","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f be in L^1(mu). For every eps > 0 there exists delta > 0 such that integral_A |f| dmu < eps whenever A is measurable with mu(A) < delta. Equivalently, the finite measure nu(A) = integral_A |f| dmu is absolutely continuous with respect to mu in the strong epsilon-delta sense, not merely in the sense that mu(A) = 0 implies nu(A) = 0. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:47:53.349000+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c18d24f629e932bc55bf05b9fc4f08e0b02dae09d8a2bb0d021cf7a1c10738f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2607.15872, 'Existence of $q$-Bass martingales in the semidiscrete setting'] Let $\nu,q\in\Prob(\RR)$ such that Assumption~\ref{ass:technical-assumptions} holds, let $D = [0, \diam(\supp(q)))^{n-1}$ and let $f$ be the corresponding $n$-atomic $q$-Bass map.
Let $h,\widetilde h\in D$ and define
\[
I_{\mathrm{dom}}=\{i\in\{1,\dots,n-1\}:h_i\neq \widetilde h_i\},
\qquad
I_{\mathrm{cdom}}=\{i\in\{1,\dots,n-1\}:f_i(h)=f_i(\widetilde h)\}.
\]
Assume that $I_{\mathrm{cdom}}\subseteq I_{\mathrm{dom}}$ and that $I_{\mathrm{dom}}\setminus I_{\mathrm{cdom}}=\{\iadd\}$ for some $\iadd\in\{1,\dots,n-1\}$.
Then $f_\iadd(h)\neq f_\iadd(\widetilde h)$ and, for every $i\neq \iadd$,
\[
\frac{|f_i(h)-f_i(\widetilde h)|}{|f_\iadd(h)-f_\iadd(\widetilde h)|}<1.
\]
More precisely, set $u:=h-\widetilde h$ and
\[
\bar J:=\int_0^1 Jf(\widetilde h+t u)\,dt.
\]
If $i\notin I_{\mathrm{cdom}}$ and $I:=I_{\mathrm{dom}}\cup\{i\}$, then
\[
\frac{|f_i(h)-f_i(\widetilde h)|}{|f_\iadd(h)-f_\iadd(\widetilde h)|}
=
\left|\frac{\adj\!\left(\bar J_{I,I}\right)_{\iadd i}}{\adj\!\left(\bar J_{I,I}\right)_{ii}}\right|
<1,
\]
whereas if $i\in I_{\mathrm{cdom}}$ the ratio is $0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:49:02.096640+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c1cc0b1273b637754c0bf5c431e455f22b7f717cdfbae5117312062368343a8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 3 (Finite-dependence rare-entry law) of arXiv:2604.26298, 'The Expiring Coupon Collector\\ Sliding-Window Surjection Flux and Rare-Entry Laws'] Assume that, along a sequence $n\to\infty$ with $M=M_n\ge n$,

\[

\{Y_{n_i}(t) > a_i\}\Bigr)

\xi(x)\,\cL^d(dx)& (i=j)\\

as $k\to\infty$ for some $\xi\in L^1(\R^d,\cL^d)$ (independent of $i$) with $\sqrt{\xi}\in W^{1,2}(\R^d)$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:37:20.370993+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c5a051b9b32a1499e66a3070cc52b2c35f16c4bab7659dcda3f2d5cba581f4b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 2periodic of arXiv:2411.13465, 'Height-offset variables and pinning at infinity for gradient Gibbs measures on trees'] \mbox{}\\
Let $Q: \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow (0,\infty)$ be a positive symmetric transfer operator of gradient type such that $\sum_{j \in \mathbb{N}}j^2 Q(j) < \infty$.
Let $\bar{\mu}$ be any (not necessarily spatially homogeneous) tree-indexed Markov chain Gibbs measure for the Ising model with interaction described by $\bar{Q}$ (see Eq. (equation eq: barQ def of the paper)). Then the following holds true for the gradient Gibbs measure $\nu^{\bar{\mu}}$ of height-period $2$ associated to $\bar{\mu}$ on the $d$-regular tree with $d \geq 2$ via Definition (def: 2perGGM of the paper).
 \begin{itemize}
	\item[a)]\textbf{Existence.}\hypertarget{res: existence 2per}{}  Let $(H_r)_{r \in \mathbb{N}}$ be as in Definition (def: SphericalAverage of the paper). Then $H:=\lim_{r \rightarrow \infty}H_r$ is a HOV for the measure $\nu^{\bar{\mu}}$ where the limit holds almost surely and in $\mathcal{L}^2$ with respect to the same measure $\nu^{\bar{\mu}} \circ \left(\sigma^{\rho,0} \right)^{-1}$. In particular, the measure $\mu^H$ associated with $H$ and $\nu$ via Theorem (thm: DLR of the paper) is a proper Gibbs measure on the space of height configurations. 
 \item[b1)]\textbf{Regularity of density of HOV.}\hypertarget{res: regularity density 2per}{} The corresponding distribution of $H^{\rho,0}$ obtained from Definition (def: SphericalAverage of the paper), under $\nu^{\bar{\mu}}$, has an infinitely often differentiable Lebesgue-density $f_{H^{\rho,0}}$. \\
 Moreover, $f_{H^{\rho,0}}$ is strictly positive on $\mathbb{R}$.
 \item[b2)]\textbf{Localization of single-site marginal of pinned measure.}\hypertarget{res: localization 2per}{} 
 Assume furthermore on the interaction $Q$ that there is some $R>0$ such that the function $t \mapsto \sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}}\exp(tj)\frac{Q(j)}{\Vert Q \Vert_1}$ is finite for $t \in (-R,+R)$.
 Then, for every $A < (d+1)R$ there exists a $B(A) \in (0,\infty)$ such that the single site marginal at the root satisfies the following exponential decay:
 \[\mu^H(\vert \sigma_\rho \vert \geq s) \leq B(A)\exp(-As), \quad \text{for every } s \in \mathbb{N}.\]
  \item[c1)]\textbf{Peculiarity 1.}\hypertarget{res: peculiarity 1 2per}{} The lifted Gibbs measure $\mu^H$ is necessarily not invariant under the translations of the tree.
 \item[c2)]\textbf{Peculiarity 2.}\hypertarget{res: peculiarity 2 2per}{} The measure $\mu^H$
 
is not extreme in the set of all Gibbs measures for $Q$.
 \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:12:46.881437+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c66c9e1a29fa27b88003aae6d0025b6ee5dfc23df8c779c9e67ec2439fa2483","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:critical-Ising of arXiv:2608.09729, 'On the self-intersection time of non-backtracking random walks'] Fix $\Delta \geq 3$ and let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex $\Delta$-regular graph.
Let $\mu$ be the Gibbs distribution of the Ising model on $G$ at inverse temperature $\beta$ satisfying $|\beta|=\beta_c$, where
\[
(\Delta-1)\tanh\beta_c=1.
\]
Then, for every $\Lambda\subseteq V(G)$, every feasible pinning $\tau\in\{-1,+1\}^{\Lambda}$, and every $u\in V(G)\setminus\Lambda$, the total influence of $u$ in $\mu^\tau$ satisfies
\[
\mathrm{TI}^{\mu^\tau}_u\le \frac{\Delta}{\Delta-1}\mathbb{E}(T(G,u))=O_\Delta(\sqrt{n}\log n).
\]
In particular, the Ising model is $O_\Delta(\sqrt{n}\log n)$-spectrally independent.

Moreover, if the external field satisfies $\|\boldsymbol h\|_\infty \le n^{O(1)}$, then the Glauber dynamics for $\mu$ has mixing time 
$\widetilde{O}_\Delta\!\left(n^{2+ \frac{2}{\Delta - 2}}\right)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:20.865392+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c90623a85386cafae17fbdbeb9b5c6117edf3092c478ed32f754b9ca62db858","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi 1 ($(p,n)$-proofreaders) of arXiv:2506.11358, 'Cardinalities in proofreading'] A~$(p,n)$-proofreader $\mathcal{P}$ is the pair $\mathcal{P}=

We say that $(A,\prec,\succ,\cdot)$ is a \emph{tridendriform algebra} if for all $(x,y,z)\in A^3$:
		\begin{align}
			(x\prec y)\prec z&=x\prec(y*z), \\
			(x\succ y)\prec z&=x\succ(y\prec z),  \\
			(x* y)\succ z&=x\succ(y\succ z),   \\
			(x\succ y)\cdot z&=x\succ(y\cdot z),	  \\
			(x\prec y)\cdot z&=x\cdot(y\succ z),  \\
			(x\cdot y)\prec z&=x\cdot(y\prec z),  \\
			(x\cdot y)\cdot z&=x\cdot (y\cdot z), 
		\end{align}
		where for all $x,y\in A$, we set $x*y\coloneqq x\prec y +x\succ y + x\cdot y$. We respectively call $\prec, \succ, \cdot$ the \emph{left, right and middle products}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["mu has compact support of positive diameter D.","t>D^2.","The source's kernel-level criterion for free Brownian unimodality."],"created_at":"2026-10-10T06:51:51.365295+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ca5188ff0c8e88bf00b55cc6acb52134e15e6f99743df668c6f966aee5a39ec","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the criterion reproduces the source's worked example, and every algebraic step was confirmed symbolically] This is the upper bound in the campaign answer to Problem 3.3 of Takahiro Hasebe and Yuki Ueda's Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374, DOI:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15 (arXiv:1710.08240). A probability measure is unimodal if, for some mode m, it is an atom at m plus an absolutely continuous measure whose density is nondecreasing to the left of m and nonincreasing to the right. Write boxplus for additive free convolution. For t>0 let S(0,t) be the centered semicircle law of variance t, with density sqrt(4t-x^2)/(2pi t) on |x|<=2sqrt(t). Let mu be compactly supported with positive diameter D=sup{|x-y|: x,y in supp(mu)}. Then mu boxplus S(0,t) is unimodal for every t>=D^2. Proof route: by the source's Lemma 3.1 (Biane's description), non-unimodality at time t gives some R>0 and a separating local minimum u_0 of xi_R with xi_R(u_0)<=1/t. The stationary-kernel lower bound, rescaled to diameter D, gives xi_R(u_0)>=1/D^2, so t<=D^2. At t=D^2, equality would hold in that lower bound. This forces mu to be the symmetric two-point law with atoms at u_0±D/2 and R^2=3D^2/4, which is unimodal at t=D^2 by the source's Example 2.1. This is an unrefereed campaign result.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:18:19.413506+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0cb2cf0faead849e90be07d57be2f3c8a4e494fce23a8f5171c4a3b58663900c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:qRacah_kernel_OPE of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] [{[mehta2004random], [Konig2005]}]
	
	The correlation kernel of the $N$-particle $q$-Racah OPE
	on $\{0,1,\ldots,M\}$
	is given by
	\begin{equation}
		
		K^{qR}(x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1} f_n(x)f_n(y).
	\end{equation}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:35:59.939206+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0cdb2ff73f5db167d590a38c4326be28315304d110051ea1809778ffc9167385","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 7 (Sausages) of arXiv:2608.26259, 'Cutoff with an $O(1)$ window for Potts Glauber Dynamics\\on lattice at High Temperature'] Set \(\tau_0:=0\). Let \((A_n)_{n\ge1}\) be i.i.d. \(\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_{\mathrm{stop}})\),
independent of the graphical construction. For \(k\ge1\), on
\(\{\tau_{k-1}<\infty,\ N_{\tau_{k-1}}=1\}\), define
\begin{align*}
\mathsf r_k&:=\inf\{s>\tau_{k-1}:\ \text{the Poisson clock at }V_{\tau_{k-1}}\text{ rings at backward time }s\},\\
\mathsf c_k&:=\inf\{n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:\ n>\tau_{k-1},\ A_n=1\},
\end{align*}
and set
\[
\tau_k :=
\begin{cases}
\mathsf c_k, & \mathsf c_k\le \mathsf r_k,\\[2pt]
\inf\{n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:\ n>\mathsf r_k,\ N_n=1\}, & \mathsf r_k<\mathsf c_k,
\end{cases}
\qquad(\inf\emptyset:=\infty).
\]
On \(\{\tau_k<\infty\}\), let \(x_k\) be the restriction of the backward history to the slab
\([\tau_{k-1},\tau_k]\), recentered by the translation sending
\((V_{\tau_{k-1}},\tau_{k-1})\) to \((0,0)\). Let \(\Xi\) be the set of all such recentered slabs, and adjoin a cemetery symbol \(\dagger\). On \(\{\tau_k=\infty\}\), set \(x_k:=\dagger\), and write \(\Xi^\dagger:=\Xi\cup\{\dagger\}\).

For $x\in\Xi$, define its length, displacement, and number of branch-out events:
\[
\ell(x):=\tau_k-\tau_{k-1}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1},
\quad
y(x):=V_{\tau_k}-V_{\tau_{k-1}}\in\mathbb{Z}^d,
\quad
b(x):=\#\{\text{branch-out events inside }x\}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0},
\]
and set $\ell(\dagger)=0$, $y(\dagger)=0$, $b(\dagger)=0$.

Fix a distinguished color, say $1\in[q]$. Define the signed influence
\[
p(x):=\frac{q}{q-1}\left(
\mathbb P\!\left(
\sigma_{T-\tau_{k-1}}(V_{\tau_{k-1}})=1
\,\middle|\,
\sigma_{T-\tau_k}(V_{\tau_k})=1,\ x_k=x
\right)-\frac1q
\right)\in\Big[-\frac1{q-1},\,1\Big],
\quad p(\dagger):=0.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.241221+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0cf57756fb303fe51c5a78510ee0ea2f61720aa84ba675a3743fecea3bf9f10c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (local existence and uniqueness below the classical threshold) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Fix $\breg\in(\frac12,1)$. Let $n\ge2$, let $\frac{n+1}2<s\le\frac n2+1$, let
$\Bzero\equiv\Binf\in\Rn\setminus\{0\}$, and let $v_0\in H^{s}(\Rn)$ be divergence-free. There are
constants $C\ge1$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, depending only on
$n,s,\breg$ and $v_{\rm A}$, and there exist a time $T_*>0$, a distributional
solution $(v,B, p)$ of \eqref{eq:mhd} on $[0,T_*]\times\Rn$ with data
$(v_0,\Binf)$, with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item writing $b:=B-\Binf$, the fields $v$, $b$ and $p$ lie in
$C([0,T_*],H^{s}(\Rn))$. The pressure is normalised by
\[
 p=\Riesz_i\Riesz_j
 \big(v^iv^j-\Binf^ib^j-b^i\Binf^j-b^ib^j\big),
\]
where $\Riesz_i$ are the Euclidean Riesz transforms;
\item writing $X=\mathrm{id}+w$, the solution is carried by a Lagrangian flow
$X:[0,T_*]\times\Rn\to\Rn$ with $X(0,\cdot)=\mathrm{id}$, uniformly bi-Lipschitz
and volume-preserving, $\det dX\equiv1$, such that $v=(\partial_tX)\circ X^{-1}$ and
$B=(\mathcal BX)\circ X^{-1}$;
moreover there is a spatially exact spacetime field
$\Ufield\in H^{s-1,1}_{\breg}(\Rst)$ such that
$\Ufield=dw$ on $[0,T_*]\times\Rn$ and, for constants fixed by
the standing parameters (one may take $C=2C_{\rm lin}$, with $C_{\rm lin}$
the constant of the linear estimate \eqref{eq:linear}),
\begin{equation}
 \|\Ufield\|_{H^{s-1,1}_{\breg}}
 \le C\|v_0\|_{H^s},
 \qquad
 \sup_{t\in[0,T_*]}\|dw(t)\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}\le\delta;
\end{equation}
here $\delta$ is chosen so that the second bound implies
$\|dw\|_{L^\infty_{t,y}}\le\frac12$;
\item the renormalised energy $E$ and cross helicity $H_{\rm c}$ of \eqref{eq:energy} are
conserved on $[0,T_*]$;
\item the solution is unique among all distributional solutions with the same
initial data for which $v$ and $B-\Binf$ belong to
$C([0,T_*],H^s)$. 
\end{enumerate}
The existence time is governed by the longitudinal regularity of the datum. We
distinguish the following two regimes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textbf{\emph{(R1)}}]  $T_*$ depends on $n,s,\breg,
v_{\rm A}$, on $\|v_0\|_{H^{s}}$ and on the function
$T\mapsto\omega_{v_0}(T)$ defined in \eqref{eq:datum-modulus}.
\item[\textbf{\emph{(R2)}}] If $\|\nabla v_0\|_{Y^{s-1,\rpar}}<\infty$
for some $\rpar\in(0,1]$, then $T_*$ depends on $n,s,\breg,\rpar,v_{\rm A}$
and on $\|v_0\|_{H^{s}}+\|\nabla v_0\|_{Y^{s-1,\rpar}}$ alone. Moreover,
the spacetime field in~(2) satisfies
\[
 \|\Ufield\|_{H^{s-1,1+\rpar}_{\breg}}
 \le C\|\nabla v_0\|_{Y^{s-1,\rpar}}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:12:46.884277+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0cf671127f24020a8577e72c29c9b9fe554a56471c7486fae40ca8db4392c933","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma AboTrprop of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] Let $(T, d, \rho)$ be a rooted $\mathbb{R}$-tree and let $\sigma , \sigma^\prime \! \in \!  T$. 
Then the following holds true. 
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(i)$] The fringe subtree $\theta_\sigma T$ above $\sigma$ is closed and connected (i.e.~it is a subtree of $T$). 

\smallskip

\item[$(ii)$] If $\sigma\! \in \!  [\![ \rho, \sigma^\prime ]\!]$, then $\theta_{\sigma^\prime} T\!\subseteq \! \theta_\sigma T$. If $\sigma\wedge \sigma^\prime \! \notin \! \{ \sigma, \sigma^\prime\}$, then $\theta_\sigma T \cap \theta_{\sigma^\prime} T \! = \!  \emptyset$.  

\smallskip

\item[$(iii)$] For any $\sigma \! \in \!  T\backslash\{ \rho\}$, $T \backslash \theta_\sigma T$ is the connected component of $T\backslash \{ \sigma\}$ containing $\rho$.  

\smallskip

\item[$(iv)$] Let $C$ be a connected component of $T\backslash \{ \sigma \}$  such that $\rho\! \notin \! C$. 
For all $\sigma'\! \in \!  C$, $]\!] \sigma , \sigma' ]\!] \! \subseteq \!  C$, $\theta_{\sigma'} T\! \subseteq \! C$ and for all $\sigma_n \! \in \, ]\!] \sigma , \sigma' ]\!]$ such that $d(\sigma, \sigma_n) \! \to \! 0$, we also get $C\! = \!  \bigcup_{n\in \mathbb{N}} \theta_{\sigma_n} T$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(v)$] For all $\sigma \! \in \!  T$ and $r\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}_+$, let $C$ be a connected component of $T\backslash B_{T,d}(\sigma, r)$. Then there is $\gamma \! \in \!  T$ such that $d(\rho, \gamma) \! = \!  r$ and $C$ is a connected component of $T\backslash \{ \gamma \} $. 

\smallskip

\item[$(vi)$] Let us suppose that $D \! \subseteq\!  T$ is countable and dense, and set $ \mathscr P \! = \!  
\{ \emptyset \}\!  \cup \! \big\{ \theta_\sigma T \, ;  \sigma \! \in \!  T \backslash D \big\}$. Then, $\mathscr P$ is a pi-system generating the Borel sigma-field of $T$. 
\end{compactenum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator with a finite fixed-point set","the object asked for is a periodic ITINERARY, a symbol sequence, not a periodic orbit","m = 3 for the affirmative half; the m = 4 case is open"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T15:09:50+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_0d1240b9b017496fe1d07198e8276e9848accae193a3447d35c49891e4cf5c60","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign status: unreviewed - author-checked against the source's exact wording; verification unreviewed] For a transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator the ITINERARY of a trajectory is the sequence of fixed-point neighbourhoods it visits; Rozikov (2009, p. 4) asks whether some trajectory has a periodic itinerary. CLAIM, in two halves. (i) YES at m = 3, by an example already in the literature: for the cyclic Volterra operator with a = b = c = 1, matrix A = [[0,1,-1],[-1,0,1],[1,-1,0]], whose leading 2x2 minor is 1 so the operator is transversal and whose fixed-point set - the three vertices and the centre - is finite, the itinerary of every non-fixed interior point is periodic, 1 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> ..., with sojourns 12, 51, 1073, ... growing geometrically by the heteroclinic-cycle mechanism of Ganikhodzhaev and Zanin (2004). (ii) OPEN at m = 4: in the proof of Theorem 5 of Ganikhodjaev and Zanin (arXiv:1205.3841) the trajectory passes between the epsilon-neighbourhoods of the vertices along the routes 1-4-3-2-1, 1-4-2-1 or 1-4-3-1, and a simulated cyclic-type m = 4 map produced the mixed finite prefix 1,4,3,2,1,4,2,1. A finite prefix cannot show that an itinerary is not periodic (every finite word extends to a periodic one), and one trajectory cannot answer an existence question in the negative, so the m = 4 case is not settled here. THE SHARP OPEN QUESTION, which is what the source presumably meant: is every itinerary eventually periodic, or which matrices A force it? The 2012 route analysis is the starting point. A periodic ITINERARY is a symbol sequence, not a periodic ORBIT: periodic orbits are typically absent while periodic itineraries need not be.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:46:09.850320+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0d13ae038fd9406c6117e2c0470b7b3883dd66014b46ac803d003bab28e95a0c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 1 (Log-concavity, PF$_2$, and TP$_2$) of arXiv:2605.18751, '\mytitle'] A positive function \(a:J\to(0,\infty)\) on an interval \(J\subseteq E\) is \emph{log-concave} if \(\log a\) is concave on \(J\). In the discrete case this is equivalent to \(\Delta^2\log a(k)\le0\) for every admissible \(k\in J\) and in the continuous case it is equivalent to \((\log a)''(x)\le0\) wherever the second derivative exists.

For a sequence \(b=(b_k)_{k\in\Z}\), we say that \(b\) is a \emph{P\'olya frequency sequence of order 2} (PF$_2$) if \(b_k\ge0\) for all \(k\), the support \(\{k:b_k>0\}\) is an interval in \(\Z\), and \(b\) is log-concave on its support.  A probability distribution \(F\) on \(\N_0\) is PF$_2$ if its mass sequence, extended by zero outside its support, is PF$_2$.

A nonnegative kernel \(M:I\times J\to[0,\infty)\) on two totally ordered sets is \emph{totally positive of order 2} (TP$_2$) if
\[
M(i,j)M(i',j')\ge M(i,j')M(i',j)
\]
whenever \(i\le i'\) and \(j\le j'\). See~\cite{Karlin1968} for the general total positivity theory.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:21:52.490578+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0d35c7f0f5c8268a09761dde117aa99c4b17d6981442e0eff2027ef6c54434ca","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 223 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Functions $\mathfrak{c}$ have the following properties (see also Table~\ref{table:sumf}):

\item For each $\boldsymbol{f}$, the $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{F}}^{\textnormal{I}}[\boldsymbol{f}](z)$ satisfies the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with source
\[
\forall h \in [H]\qquad D_h^{\textnormal{I}}[\boldsymbol{f}](z) = - \oint_{\gamma_h} \frac{\dd\zeta}{2\ii\pi}\, \frac{f_h(\zeta)}{(z - \zeta)^2}.
\]
where $z$ is \emph{inside} the contour of integration. Besides, it behaves as $O(\frac{1}{z^2})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$. And, it is tame with exponent $1$.
\item For each $\boldsymbol{f}$, the $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{F}}^{\textnormal{II}}[\boldsymbol{f}](z)$ satisfies the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with zero source. Besides, it is $O(\frac{1}{z^2})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$, and it becomes tame with exponent $1$ after subtraction of $(\frac{1}{2} \partial_z(\sigma_h(z)f_h(z)))_{h = 1}^H$.
\item For each $\boldsymbol{f}$, the $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{F}}^{\textnormal{III}}[\boldsymbol{f}](z)$ satisfies the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with source
\[
\forall h \in [H] \qquad D_h^{\textnormal{III}}[\boldsymbol{f}](z) = \oint_{\gamma(\alpha_h)} \frac{\dd\zeta}{2\ii\pi}\,\frac{f_h(\zeta)}{(z - \zeta)^2}+\oint_{\gamma(\beta_h)} \frac{\dd\zeta}{2\ii\pi}\,\frac{f_h(\zeta)}{(z - \zeta)^2}.
\]

\item For each $g \in [H]$ and $\zeta \in \amsmathbb{C} \setminus \amsmathbb{B}$, the $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{c}}^{\textnormal{3rd}}_{\bullet;g}(z;\zeta)$ satisfies the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with respect to $z$ and with source
\[
\forall h \in [H] \qquad D_{h;g}(z;\zeta) = -\frac{\delta_{h,g}}{z - \zeta}.
\]
Besides, it is $O(\frac{1}{z^2})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$. If $\zeta$ is away from the endpoints $\alpha_g,\beta_g$ it is tame with exponent $1$. If $\zeta$ is located at $\alpha_g$ or $\beta_g$, it becomes tame (with respect to the variable $z$) with exponent $1$ after we subtract $\frac{1}{2\theta_{g,g}}\boldsymbol{D}_{\bullet;g}(z;\zeta)$.

Facts: (1) the minimal polynomial of zeta_n over Q is the n-th cyclotomic polynomial Phi_n(x) = prod over 1 <= k <= n with gcd(k, n) = 1 of (x - zeta_n^k), which has integer coefficients and is irreducible over Q (Gauss for n prime, Kronecker/Dedekind in general), so [Q(zeta_n) : Q] = phi(n), Euler's totient; (2) Q(zeta_n)/Q is a Galois extension with Galois group canonically isomorphic to (Z/nZ)^*, the automorphism sigma_a sending zeta_n to zeta_n^a; in particular it is abelian, and by the Kronecker-Weber theorem every finite abelian extension of Q lies in some cyclotomic field; (3) the ring of integers of Q(zeta_n) is Z[zeta_n]; (4) a prime p not dividing n is unramified and splits into phi(n)/f primes of residue degree f, where f is the order of p in (Z/nZ)^*; a prime p dividing n ramifies, totally so in Q(zeta_{p^k}) where p is the phi(p^k)-th power of a prime, and p O_K = (1 - zeta_{p^k})^{phi(p^k)}; the discriminant of Q(zeta_{p^k}) is +- p^{p^{k-1}(pk - k - 1)}, and in general the primes ramified in Q(zeta_n) are exactly the primes dividing n (for odd n; 2 ramifies only when 4 divides n); (5) Q(zeta_n) contains the quadratic field Q(sqrt(p^*)) with p^* = (-1)^{(p-1)/2} p for each odd prime p dividing n (Gauss sums), which is one route to quadratic reciprocity; (6) the maximal real subfield is Q(zeta_n + zeta_n^{-1}) of degree phi(n)/2 for n > 2; (7) the class number h_n of Q(zeta_p) is 1 exactly for the primes p <= 19; Kummer proved Fermat's last theorem for regular primes (p not dividing h_p) using the arithmetic of Z[zeta_p]. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:33:01.744633+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0d9a176282a96c93b294a74a824ca937dc5efa7fe2e71bf4175a378aace79fca","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The ordinary generating function of $H$ is
  \[
    \phi_H(z) = (1-p)^m \binom{m/z - 1}{m}^{-1}.
  \]
  \begin{proof}
    We use the Laplace--Borel transform with $m$ applications of integration
    by parts:
    \begin{align*}
      \frac{\phi_H(x)}{(1-p)^m} &= \int_0^\infty
        \left( e^{xt/m} - 1 \right)^m
        e^{-t} \, dt\\
      &= \underbrace{\left. \left( e^{xt/m} - 1 \right)^m \left(-e^{-t}\right)
          \right|^{t=\infty}_{t=0}}_0\\
      &\quad + \int_0^\infty m\left( e^{xt/m} - 1 \right)^{m-1} \left(\frac{x}{m} \, e^{xt/m}\right)
      e^{-t} \, dt\\
      &= \frac{m\left(x/m\right)}{1} \int_0^\infty \left(e^{xt/m}-1\right)^{m-1}
            e^{-(1-x/m)t} \, dt\\
      &= \frac{m \left(m-1\right) (x/m)^2}{1-x/m} \int_0^\infty \left( e^{xt/m}-1\right)^{m-2}
            e^{-(1-2x/m)t} \, dt\\
      &\ \,\vdots\\
      &= \frac{m!\left(x/m\right)}{\left(m/x - 1\right)^{\underline{m-1}}} 
            \int_0^\infty e^{-(1-x)t} \, dt\\
      &= \frac{m!}{\left(m/x-1\right)^{\underline{m}}} = \binom{m/x - 1}{m}^{-1},
      \quad 0 < x < 1.
    \end{align*}
    The right-hand side is a rational function of $x$, say
    $f(x) / g(x)$ where $f(z)$ and $g(z)$ are real polynomials in $z$.
    Then $f(z) \, g(z)^{-1}$ is a well-defined object in the ring 
    of formal power series $\mathbb{R}[[z]]$ and we can
    restate our result for $\phi_H(z)$;
    see Section~\ref{language}.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:37:25.925179+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0dd4eeed3cc16d0d119ec6898bcb507f6d0169af673e54eb694a3ed0b621b1e9","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For $m\ge0$, let
\[
 \mathscr P_m
 =\{\lambda:\ell(\lambda)\le n,\ |\lambda|\le m\},
 \qquad
 E_m=\bigl(G_\lambda(p_\mu)\bigr)_
       {\mu,\lambda\in\mathscr P_m},
\]
where
\[
 p_\mu=(Q^{\mu_1+n-1},Q^{\mu_2+n-2},\ldots,Q^{\mu_n}),
\]
and the rows and columns are ordered by any linear extension of
inclusion.  Then $E_m$ is lower triangular and
\[
 G_\lambda(p_\lambda)
 =u_\lambda\prod_{\square\in\lambda}
       (1-Q^{h(\square)}),
 \qquad u_\lambda\in R_{\mathrm{ev}}^\times.
\]
In particular,
\[
 D_m:=\det E_m\in R_{\mathrm{ev}}\setminus\{0\}
\]
is a Laurent unit times a product of cyclotomic polynomials, and
\[
 D_mE_m^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}(E_m)
 \in\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathscr P_m}(R_{\mathrm{ev}}).
\]

If $F=\sum_\lambda b_\lambda G_\lambda\in
\Lambda_n^{\mathrm{pol}}$ and
\[
 \mathbf v_m(F)=\bigl(F(p_\mu)\bigr)_{\mu\in\mathscr P_m},
 \qquad
 \mathbf b_m(F)=\bigl(b_\lambda\bigr)_{\lambda\in\mathscr P_m},
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf v_m(F)=E_m\mathbf b_m(F).
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every ideal $J\subseteq R_{\mathrm{ev}}$,
\[
 F(p_\mu)\in J\quad(\mu\in\mathscr P_m)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 b_\lambda\in D_m^{-1}J
 \quad(\lambda\in\mathscr P_m).
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["H and K are complex Banach spaces","A and B are BOUNDED linear operators on H and K respectively","sigma(A) and sigma(B) are disjoint compact subsets of C","C is a bounded operator from K to H","Gamma is a cycle in the resolvent set of B winding once around sigma(A) and not at all around sigma(B)"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.091249+00:00","domain":"operator theory, Sylvester equations, Riesz functional calculus","id":"claim_0ddcfb960219b5d37190ff5731d811c9cbc7554da88e7737e484070a46e2973a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"CAUTION ON THE NAME: this is the other result commonly called 'Rosenblum's argument' - the contour-integral solution of the Sylvester equation; the scattering-theory Hilbert-Schmidt estimate is a different theorem of the same author, so a citation naming Rosenblum must be matched to its context. STATEMENT: let H and K be complex Banach spaces, A a bounded operator on H, B a bounded operator on K, and suppose their spectra are disjoint: sigma(A) intersect sigma(B) is empty. Then for every bounded operator C from K to H the equation A X - X B = C has a UNIQUE bounded solution X from K to H, and it is given by X = (1 / (2 pi i)) times the contour integral over Gamma of (A - z)^(-1) C (B - z)^(-1) dz, where Gamma is a finite union of positively oriented rectifiable Jordan curves lying in the resolvent set of B, encircling sigma(A) once and sigma(B) not at all. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) disjointness of the spectra is what gives both existence and uniqueness. With A = B and C = 0 the equation A X - X A = 0 is solved by every operator commuting with A, so uniqueness fails badly; and with A = B = 0 on a one-dimensional space the equation is unsolvable for nonzero C. (ii) It is the SPECTRA, not the norms, that matter: no smallness of C is assumed, the solution depends linearly on C, and the bound on X is controlled by the length of Gamma and by the size of the two resolvents on Gamma - a bound that blows up as the spectra approach each other, which is the quantitative content usually needed in perturbation arguments. (iii) The theorem as stated is for BOUNDED A and B; for unbounded operators the analogous statement requires separate hypotheses (sectoriality, semigroup generation), and the contour formula must be justified anew. (iv) Finite-dimensional corollary: for matrices, A X - X B = C is uniquely solvable precisely when A and B have no common eigenvalue.","status":"unverified"}

# Target 1: two-cycle exclusion and necessary overshoot for periodic GD

Version 1, proof unaudited. This excludes possible third fates; it does not
classify all factored-GD trajectories or prove convergence.

Consider the factored model of claim 010 with any eta>0. More generally the
argument applies to any real update
 v_+=v+eta F(v,kq),
 k_+=k+delta q, q_+=q+delta k,
 delta=eta v G(v,kq),
where G is strictly positive at every finite point and F(0,s) has a unique
zero p_bar. The softmax logistic model satisfies these conditions.

1. Every orbit of period dividing two with k^2-q^2!=0 is a fixed point.
   It lies on v=0,kq=p_bar. This holds at every fixed step size.
2. Every nonstationary finite periodic orbit with k^2-q^2!=0 at one (hence
   every) iterate must contain an iterate with delta^2>=2. Equivalently,
   any periodic orbit on which |eta vG|<sqrt(2) throughout is stationary.

Neither statement excludes balanced-plane cycles, long cycles with large
overshoot, unbounded nonconvergent orbits, or nonperiodic bounded invariant
sets. This is a special obstruction result, not a scored global classification.

## Proof of two-cycle exclusion

Let U=k+q and D=k-q. Their exact simultaneous updates are
 U_+=(1+delta)U, D_+=(1-delta)D.
The nonzero imbalance is C=UD, so U,D are both nonzero initially.
For a returning two-step orbit, with a=delta_0,b=delta_1,
 (1+a)(1+b)=1, (1-a)(1-b)=1.
Expansion and addition yield 2ab=0; subtraction yields 2(a+b)=0.
Over the reals this forces a=b=0. Since eta>0 and G>0, v_0=v_1=0.
The factors therefore do not move. The head update then forces
F(0,kq)=0, hence kq=p_bar. This is a fixed point, as claimed.

## Proof of the overshoot requirement

The exact imbalance update is C_+=(1-delta^2)C. If an r-step orbit returns
with C_0!=0, no intermediate C can vanish, and
 product_{t=0}^{r-1}(1-delta_t^2)=1.
If every delta_t^2<2, every absolute factor is <=1, strictly less than 1
whenever delta_t!=0. The product can have absolute value 1 only if every
delta_t=0. Then every v_t=0, the factors stay fixed, and F(0,kq)=0.
Thus any nonstationary periodic orbit requires at least one delta_t^2>=2.

## Relation to the remaining gap

The flow's invariant imbalance is unavailable in GD, but its multiplicative
replacement still excludes every nonbalanced two-cycle, including at steps
beyond the normal-stability threshold of claim 013. A loss of an attracting
normal multiplier therefore does not by itself provide a two-cycle witness.
The unresolved step is controlling general, possibly large factor updates
well enough to show eventual entry into one of claim 010's escaping regions,
or finding a third fate that persists off the balanced planes.


# Target 1: exact balanced two-cycle and its transverse multiplier

Version 1, proof unaudited. Boundary check for claim 014, not a positive-volume
counterexample to an almost-everywhere theorem.

Fix any n>=2 and any distinct positive kappa_i. Put
 b_i=2 cosh(kappa_i)^2/kappa_i,
 a_i=b_i tanh(kappa_i).
These satisfy 0<a_i<b_i. In the usual coupled factored model
h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s), all links have
 h_i(-1)=0, h_i'(-1)=2.

For EVERY fixed eta>0, simultaneous Euclidean GD on the average logistic
loss has an exact two-cycle
 (v,k,q)=(2/eta,1,-1) <-> (2/eta,-1,1).
At both points the loss is log 2, the product is -1, and k^2-q^2=0.
The two-step Jacobian has a transverse multiplier 9 normal to k=-q.
Thus the nonzero-imbalance assumption in 014 is necessary. This cycle
does not establish a positive-measure basin or rule out almost-everywhere
endpoint convergence.

## Proof

At either displayed state every h_i(kq)=0, so g_i=1/2, F=0 and
G=mean_i g_i h_i'=1. The head therefore stays fixed and
delta=eta vG=2. The factor update sends
 (k,q)->(k+2q,q+2k).
It exchanges (1,-1) and (-1,1). The cycle is nonstationary and has exact
period two; the loss remains log(1+exp(0))=log 2. The construction uses
different nonlinear scales, rather than requiring repeated identical examples.

The full factor-sum identity is U_+=(1+delta)U, U=k+q. At U=0 its
linearization gives dU_+=(1+delta)dU=3dU; the term U d(delta) vanishes.
After two steps dU_{++}=9dU, an exact normal multiplier even when v and
the product vary in the perturbation. No stability assertion at a unit
multiplier is involved.

The same constructed family has finite stationary points at v=0,kq=-1,
whereas the displayed periodic points have v=2/eta>0. Hence a classification
of every finite initialization by stationary points and escaping selections
alone would be false at any positive constant step. The exceptional balanced
plane must be allowed, as it is in claim 012's flow statement (which is a
different dynamical system).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:15:55.000316+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0dfe8969161e1899f2d428134603ce9efa553c2904e05707a476acad7e064339","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:int-ext-coincides of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ be a $\Box$-p and $\Diamond$-p model, then \\
  $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi \iff x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$ for any $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$ and $x \in W$.
  \begin{proof}
    We use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$.
    We shall consider the cases with modal operators, as the other cases are either trivial or easily proven with the induction hypothesis.
    We note that $\Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M}$ is persistent by the assumption and Proposition (prop:combined-persistency of the paper).

    ($\Box\Rightarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$, then $\forall x',y'\, ((x \leq x' \sqsubset y') \mathrel{\Rightarrow} y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi)$.
    Now take any $y$ such that $x \leq x \sqsubset y$, then it follows that $y \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$, so $y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$.

    ($\Box\Leftarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$, then $\forall y\, (x \sqsubset y \mathrel{\Rightarrow} y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi)$.
    Now take any $x', y'$ such that $x \leq x' \sqsubset y'$,
    then $x \leq x' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$ by persistency,
    then $y' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi$,
    so $y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$.

    ($\Diamond\Rightarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, then $\forall x'\, (x \leq x' \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \exists y'\, (x' \sqsubset y' \mathrel{\text{\&}} y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi))$.
    This and $x \leq x$ imply that there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $y \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$, then $y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.

    ($\Diamond\Leftarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, then there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi$.
    Now take any $x'$ such that $x \leq x'$,
    then by $\Diamond$-p, $x' \geq x \sqsubset y$ implies that there is $y'$ such that $x' \sqsubset y' \geq y$.
    Here, $y \leq y' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by persistency,
    so $y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}
