{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:11:35.835003+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0dff93f836167272c94a9a19759dd320c50182ba2f54a788c18cb387e37cb350","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm-omni-BM24 of arXiv:2607.25567, 'Random Trees in Hyperbolic FPP'] The following hold for both forward and backward random trees for FPP on a hyperbolic group. 

	\begin{enumerate}
		\item If $G$ is not free (up to finite index), almost surely exceptional directions in ${\partial G}$ exist and are dense in ${\partial G}$.
		\item If ${\partial G}$ has topological dimension $\dim_t {\partial G}$ greater than 1, then almost surely there are 
		\emph{uncountably many} exceptional directions.
		\item If $G$ is a cocompact lattice in the hyperbolic plane, and the Cayley graph $\Gamma$ is planar, then  almost surely there are \emph{countably many} exceptional directions. 
		\item Let $G$ be a  hyperbolic group such that $\dim_t {\partial G} = n-1$. Then
		there exists an exceptional direction $z \in {\partial G}$ with multiplicity \emph{at least $n$}. Thus there exist hyperbolic groups with arbitrarily large
		multiplicity of an exceptional direction.
		\item Exceptional directions have measure zero with respect to the Patterson-Sullivan measure. In fact the set of exceptional directions has Hausdorff dimension (almost surely uniformly) smaller than that of ${\partial G}$.
		\item For any (fixed) $\Gamma$, there exists an almost sure uniform upper bound 
		on the  multiplicity of an exceptional direction.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:59:53.355646+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0e454a2fdf0e2142f16a538a5000da87c0d04288a9b5e2145910ecaf5a2d7a3f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:depinning of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Along the phase family, the reaction

{"assumptions":["rows independent and identically distributed (the pairs bootstrap resamples rows, not residuals, so heteroscedasticity is allowed)","finite fourth moments and a converging empirical second-moment matrix (Freedman 1981); the predictor is a fixed measurable map of the sample, applied identically to every resample"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T12:03:52.456149+00:00","domain":"regression / resampling","id":"claim_0e4e01deefe6a25c51c622bfa99085bafd98403f8cc1a516a140a42803b61b73","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a least-squares predictor yhat(x) = x' beta_hat fitted on n rows, the textbook variance at a new point x is sigma^2 x'(X'SX)^(-1) x (sigma^2 times the leverage), and the hat matrix H = X(X'SX)^(-1)X'S has trace equal to the number of parameters. Both statements require X'SX to be invertible. On a design that is rank-deficient - here, an ensemble whose members include exact duplicates, so the member-prediction Gram of every output is singular by the number of duplicates - the leverage is undefined: the trace of the hat matrix drops to the rank (21 instead of 24 on the s104 Y1 cell of the EMIT pool), and inverting through a tiny ridge assigns any new point that leaves the duplicates' span an arbitrarily large leverage (a load 11.8 times the whole prediction error on that cell), which is a property of the ridge, not of the predictor actually used. The pairs bootstrap sidesteps this: resample the n rows with replacement B times, refit the predictor exactly as it is fitted in production (with its own ridge or pseudo-inverse and its own constraints), and take the empirical variance of the B predictions at x. Under Freedman's (1981) conditions for the pairs (correlation-model) bootstrap - independent rows, finite fourth moments of the regressors and errors, and a design whose empirical second-moment matrix converges - the bootstrap variance of a linear predictor is consistent for its sampling variance, and it remains well defined on a singular design because every resample is fitted by the same regularised map as the original. It is the right variance estimator when the estimator's regularisation, rather than an invertible Gram, determines its behaviour; it also applies unchanged to a constrained estimator (a long-only stack) for which no closed form exists. Cost: B refits per cell; B = 8 was enough to rank rows and cells in the RMT ensemble program (the ranking, not the level, was used).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:38:04.508989+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0e5f961a58377d7f217e3c5df5c78c2eb827d28358baf6714f59590983a52753","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:fast of arXiv:2607.14266, 'The Swapping Mechanism for Interacting Diffusions: Framework, Comparison with Switching, a'] Let $p_0(x,y,t)$ denote the product density appearing in
		Proposition~(prop:slow of the paper). As $st\to\infty$,
		$p(x,y,t)$ converges in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ to the symmetrised mixture
		\[
		p_\infty(x,y,t)=\frac12\bigl[p_0(x,y,t)+p_0(y,x,t)\bigr].
		\]
		Thus the rapid swapping makes the two configurations
		$(x,y)$ and $(y,x)$ equally probable, but the system still
		remembers the two possible initial assignments. Moreover, for all
		$st\ge 1$,
		\begin{equation}
			\|p(\,\cdot\,,\cdot\,,t)-p_\infty(\,\cdot\,,\cdot\,,t)\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)}
			\le C(t)(st)^{-1/2},
		\end{equation}
		where $C(t)>0$ depends continuously on $t$. The $O((st)^{-1/2})$ rate
		is dictated by the $z\to0$ edge of the Bessel integrals, where
		$I_\nu(u)\sim e^u/\sqrt{2\pi u}$, and is a signature of the underlying
		telegraph-type structure
		[goldstein1951,kac1974,tailleur2008,cates2012]. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Finite public Gaussian family with common positive spherical variance; d>=1","Finite prescribed set of nonnegative OU time-point pairs; epsilon>0","No prescribed Lipschitz constant, gradient constraint, or OU-consistency assumption for estimated fields","Adaptive application assumes identical public input, uniform finite query cap, and a finite selected set of query-randomness seeds","Finite-seed masking does not establish continuously randomized query hardness"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T17:55:25.688168+00:00","domain":"diffusion score-oracle models and adaptive query lower bounds","id":"claim_0e651190fbfa6f03b770cb3ff6afd9c955530ace92f76294c324253c623d80f8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own-work draft; C18 v1 status SKETCH, independent audit pending, no novelty claim; not a certified theorem. Each field has some finite global spatial Lipschitz constant uniform over t; no prescribed, polynomial, or efficient-computability bound is supplied. For a sampler with a uniform finite query cap Q and a selected finite set S of query-randomness seeds, form at most Q|S| query pairs from all-zero-reply adaptive paths. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.454072+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0e8b7c6ee0d52d7623ece31112df7ff29419743b0b431fb70e169c0294a62f03","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:VarY_exceeds_VarX of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] Let $X \sim \Bern(p,a,b)$ for some $p \ne \frac{1}{2}$. 
Then, any independent symmetrizer $Y$ of $X$ satisfies $\Var(Y) \ge \Var(X)$, with equality if and only if $f_Y = f_{-X}$. 

\begin{proof}
By (lem:affine_invariance of the paper) we may take $X \sim \Bern(p,-1,1)$. 

Let $f \in \Sym$, 
define $R_f$ as in (thm:Bernoulli_calY_representation of the paper),

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:27:14.948752+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0e9f64994f3645ba4c9e217d69839dd8fa8a987b221afb7a810cea98888cf9a1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.24352, 'Second moments associated with finite free multiplicative convolution'] Let $d\geq 1$ be a positive integer and $A,B \in \mathcal{M}_{d,d}(\mathbb{C})$ two complex Hermitian matrices with positive eigenvalues. Denote by $a = (a_1,\ldots,a_d)$, $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_d)$ their eigenvalues. Let $U$ be a Haar-distributed random unitary matrix. Let $1 \leq k\leq l \leq d$ be two integers such that $d \geq k+l$. Then,
\begin{align*}
	 & \mathbb{E}[e_k(AUBU^{\star})e_l(AUBU^{\star})]                      \\
	 & \hspace{1cm}=\frac{1}{l!k!}\sum_{y,m = 0}^{k} \tilde{M}_m(a)\tilde{M}_y(b)  \\
	 & \hspace{0.5cm}\sum_{\substack{\sK_1, \sK_2\in \partitionskl                              \\ {t({\sK}_1)}=(2^m,1^{k+l-2m}) \\ {t({\sf K}_2)}=(2^y,1^{k+l-2y})}}\hspace{-0.5cm}{2^{{\sf C}(\sK_1,\sK_2)}}\sum_{h = 0}^{(\sK_1,\sK_2 )[k]}\tilde{B}((\sK_1,\sK_2)[k+l]-h,h) \frac{1}{(d+1)_{h+ {\tilde{\sf S}}(\sK_1,\sK_2)}(d)_{k+l-h-{\tilde{\sf S}}(\sK_1,\sK_2)}}
\end{align*}
with
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $
\tilde{B}((\sK_1,\sK_2)[k+l]-h,h)=\frac{B((\sK_1,\sK_2)[k+l]-h,h)}{\binom{(\sK_1,\sK_2)[k+l]}{(\sK_1,\sK_2)[k]}}=\frac{\binom{(\sK_1,\sK_2)[k+l]}{h}-\binom{(\sK_1,\sK_2)[k+l]}{h-1}}{\binom{(\sK_1,\sK_2)[k+l]}{(\sK_1,\sK_2)[k]}},
$
where the ${B}(p,q),\, p \geq q $, are the \emph{weak ballot numbers}:
$$
B(p,q) = \binom{p+q}{q}-\binom{p+q}{q-1}.
$$ 
The numbers $B(p,q)$ count the number of lattice paths from  $(0,0)$ to $(p+q,p-q)$ with steps $(1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$ that never dip below the $x$-axis. When $p=q$ this is exactly a Dyck path, and $B(p,p)$ coincides with the $p$-th Catalan number.
\item $\tilde{M}_r(a) = r!(k+l-2r)! M_r(a)$, where $M_r(a)$ is the monomial symmetric polynomial associated to the partition $(2^r, 1^{k+l-2r})$ in the variables $a = (a_1,...,a_d)$.
\item For positive integers $d \geq n \geq 1$, the quantity $(d)_n = d(d-1)...(d-n+1)$ is the \emph{falling factorial} (or \emph{Pochhammer symbol}).

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:18:56.348883+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ea39677b012bc3adafc64b9260457d4d5cd919dbab54d8162588ce7d371e9f0","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 23 of arXiv:2603.13798, 'Iterated Graph Systems (I): random walks and diffusion limits'] A sequence $(r_n)_{n\ge k}$ is called admissible for $v$ if $r_n\to\infty$ and there exist integers $m_n$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$,
\[
c_0\le m_n\le n-k-c_0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
c_{\dist}\rho_{\min}(\mathcal D)^{m_n}\le r_n\le C_{\dist}\rho_{\min}(\mathcal D)^{m_n}.
\]
For every $v\in V(G^\infty)$ and every admissible sequence $(r_n)$ for $v$, define
\[
\dimwalk(G^\infty:v)
:=
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\log \mathbb E^v\big[\tau_{B_{G^n}(v,r_n)^{\mathrm c}}^{G^n}\big]}{\log r_n}.
\]
If all vertices in $G^\infty$ share the same walk dimension, then we say that $G^\infty$ possesses walk dimension $\dimwalk(G^\infty)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-06T07:26:44.650115+00:00","domain":"matrix analysis, Schatten norms and singular values","id":"claim_0eb30ff7577661040f84ccd987fc3f1b12ba0d9cd878123591ce0282549634d9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a complex m by n matrix A, s_1(A) >= s_2(A) >= ... >= 0 are its singular values (padded with zeros to min(m, n) entries). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:47.651197+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ecba4327d83e6bcf5f0e9ab526d9f8854fb6f5e939a15167f6eb56dad9c0344","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 1 of arXiv:2605.07050, 'Universality of the fluctuations of the free energy in generalized Sherrington--Kirkpatric'] Suppose that $\sqrt{N} W_{ij}$ $(1 \leq i<j \leq N)$ are i.i.d., symmetric, and strictly sub-Gaussian random variables with variance $1$. Suppose that $\sqrt{N} x_k$ $(1 \leq k \leq N)$ are i.i.d., symmetric, and strictly sub-Gaussian random variables with variance $1$, independent of $\sqrt{N} W_{ij}$. Let
\beq 
	Z_N \equiv Z_N(\beta) = \E_{\caX} \left[ \exp \left( \beta N \sum_{i<j} W_{ij} \frac{x_i x_j}{\| \bsx \|^2} \right) \right], \qquad F_N \equiv F_N(\beta) = \frac{1}{N} \log Z_N.
\eeq
(When $\| \bsx \| = 0$, we define $x_i x_j / \| \bsx \|^2 = 0$ for all $i, j$.) Then, for any $\beta \in (0, 1)$,
\[
	F_N(\beta) \to F(\beta) := \beta^2 /4
\]
and
\[
	N(F_N(\beta) - F(\beta) ) \Rightarrow \caN(m_F, V_F),
\]
as $N \to \infty$, i.e., $N(F_N(\beta) - F(\beta) )$ converges in distribution to the Gaussian with mean $m_F$ and the variance $V_F$ as $N \to \infty$. Here,
\[
	m_F = \frac{1}{4} \log (1- \beta^2) + \frac{\beta^2 (1-m_4)}{4} + \frac{\beta^4 (w_4-3)(m_4^2 -3)}{48}
\]
and
\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:36.747527+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0eec9bc2ba12b01ed70b8ab77b27cc7f369474d35ef4de5f878d559bc3499995","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi 1 of arXiv:2511.20322, 'Dissertation'] A stochastic process $X : \Om \times [0,\infty) \to \R^d$ is called an \emph{epoched Brownian bridge} if there exists a jointly Gaussian\footnote{Jointly Gaussian family means $(B^{j_1}_{t_1}, \dots, B^{j_m}_{t_m})$ is Gaussian for all $j_1,\dots, j_m \in \N_0$ and $t_1,\dots, t_m \in [0,1]$.} family $(B^j : \Om \times [0,1] \to \R^d)_{j \in \N_0}$ of Brownian bridges from $0$ to $0$, such that
	\[X_t = B^{\floor t}_{\frk t}, \quad t\geq 0.\]
	A stochastic process $\hat W : \Om \times [0,\infty) \to \R^d$ is called an \emph{epoched Brownian motion} of period $T > 0$ if there exists an epoched Brownian bridge $X$ and a random variable $V\sim \cN(0, 1_{d\times d})$ independent of $X$, such that

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:58:38.108456+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ef573b6bff47de3ac458a2ca1c3a5d6bde0823367933384eece17a6942106b5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:strong-solution of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Let \((\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})\) be a complete probability space supporting a family of \(d\)-dimensional Wiener processes \((W(\cdot,\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) and a family of initial random variables \((X_0(\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) , along with a deterministic initial fibered probability-graphon \(q_0 \in \mathcal{P}_{\nu\otimes \nu}([-W,W]\times [0,1]^2)\). We shall say that a pair \((X(\cdot,\xi),q_\gamma^{\xi,\xi'})_{\xi,\xi'\in [0,1]}\) is a \emph{strong solution} of (equation eq:multi-agent-macroscopic-SDE of the paper) if the family of continuous stochastic processes \(X=(X(\cdot,\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) and the map \(q:[0,1]^2\times [0,T]\times \mathcal{C}_T^d\times \Omega \to \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})\) verify:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item For almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\), the pathwise law of the state process satisfies \(\mu^{\xi} = \mathrm{Law}(X(\cdot,\xi)) \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_T^d)\), and the map \(\xi \mapsto \mu^{\xi}\) is measurable.
		\item For almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\), the process \(X(\cdot,\xi)\) is adapted to the filtration generated by the Wiener process \(W(\cdot,\xi)\) and the initial condition \(X_0(\xi)\), and satisfies the following integral equation \(\mathbb{P}\)-a.s.:
		\[
			\begin{aligned}
            &\quad X(t,\xi) = X_0(\xi)\\
            &\qquad+ \int_{0}^{t} \int_0^1\int_{\mathcal{C}^d_s} \int_{\mathbb{R}} w \,q^{\xi,\xi'}_\gamma(s,dw)\,K(X(s,\xi),\gamma(s))\,d\mu_{[0,s]}^{\xi'}(\gamma)\,d\xi' \,ds + \sqrt{2\nu}W(t,\xi), \quad t \in [0,T].
            \end{aligned}
		\]
		\item \(\mathbb{P}\)-a.s. and for almost every \(\xi,\xi' \in [0,1]\), the map 
		\[
		(t,\gamma) \in [0,T]\times \mathcal{C}_T^d \mapsto q^{\xi,\xi'}_\gamma(t) \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})
		\]
		is narrowly continuous. Moreover, for any fixed path \(\gamma \in \mathcal{C}_T^d\), the time-dependent measure \(t \in [0,T] \mapsto q^{\xi,\xi'}_\gamma(t) \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})\) solves the transport equation \((equation eq:multi-agent-macroscopic-SDE of the paper)_2\) in the distributional sense, with initial condition \(q^{\xi,\xi'}_{\gamma}(0) = q_0^{\xi,\xi'}\).
		\item \(\mathbb{P}\)-a.s., for every \(t\in [0,T]\) and every \(\gamma\in \mathcal{C}_T^d\), the map \((\xi,\xi') \in [0,1]^2 \mapsto q^{\xi,\xi'}_\gamma(t) \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})\) is measurable.
	\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:04:39.773972+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0f22a9cbc5f0fcf5d3cf93befa811dcda34f6b05effd61604d8a9aa3348900b9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition eqn:SplittingMap of arXiv:2609.01464, 'Removability of non-isolated singularities for Einstein metrics and RCD spaces'] Let $n\geqslant 2$ be an integer. Let $(X,\mathrm{d},\mathcal{H}^n)$ be an $\mathrm{RCD}(-1,n)$ metric measure space, and let $1\leqslant k\leqslant n$. Let $\delta>0$, $r>0$. We say that $u=(u_1,\ldots,u_k):B_r(x)\to \mathbb R^k$ is a {\rm $\delta$-splitting map} if there is a constant $C=C(n)$ such that the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $u_i$ is harmonic on $B_r(x)$ for every $i=1,\ldots,k$.
        \item $|\nabla u_i|\leqslant C$ for every $i=1,\ldots,k$.
        \item We have, for every $i,j=1,\ldots,k$,
        \[
        \fint_{B_r(x)} |\nabla u_i\cdot \nabla u_j-\delta_{ij}|\ensuremath{\mathrm d}\mathcal{H}^n \leqslant \delta.
        \]
        \item We have, for every $i=1,\ldots,k$ 
        \[
        r^2\fint_{B_r(x)} |\operatorname{Hess} u_i|^2\ensuremath{\mathrm d}\mathcal{H}^n \leqslant \delta
        \]
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

\(c_0\in\C\) with \(\left|c_0\right|\leq s\).  Put \(c_1=su^2\).
Let \(\mathbf{A}_N=\mathbf{A}_N^*\) be deterministic and satisfy
\[
 \sup_N\left\|\mathbf{A}_N\right\|<\infty,
 \qquad
 L_{\mathbf{A}_N}\overset{\mathrm{w}}{\longrightarrow}\mu_0,
\]
and let \((b_N)\) be a deterministic scalar sequence with
\(b_N\to b\in\C\).  Let
all the matrices \(\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j)\), \(N\geq1\), \(j=0,1\), be
defined on a common probability space.  Assume that, for each \(N\) and
\(j\), the entries of \(\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j)\) are centred and jointly
real-Gaussian, and satisfy
\[
 \E[(\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j))_{ab}
       \overline{(\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j))_{kl}}]
 =\frac{s}{N}\delta_{ak}\delta_{bl},
 \qquad
 \E[(\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j))_{ab}
       (\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j))_{kl}]
 =\frac{c_j}{N}\delta_{al}\delta_{bk}.
\]
The matrices may be coupled arbitrarily with each other and across \(N\).

\[
 p_N(z)=\det\!\left(z\mathbf{I}-b_N\mathbf{I}

 \begin{aligned}
 \nu_{q_N}

 (x\mapsto b+ux)_*(\mu_0\boxplus\mathfrak{sc}_s),\\
 L_{\,b_N\mathbf{I}+u\mathbf{A}_N+\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_1)}
 &\overset{\mathrm{w}}{\longrightarrow}
 (x\mapsto b+ux)_*(\mu_0\boxplus\mathfrak{sc}_s).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

	\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T01:37:28.983850+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0f39ca00997d214612de86fe4c3bf3e91b63a999cb61d00167cf22b324047249","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm prop.convipvt of arXiv:2412.00822, '\textsc{Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations \\ beyond hyperbolic spaces}'] Let $\mathbf{X}^{(\lambda)}=(X_i^{(\lambda)} \, \,;\; \, i\geq 1 )$ be a PPP of intensity measure $\lambda \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_{ \mathcal{M}}$, where the points of $\mathbf{X}^{(\lambda)}$ are ranked by increasing values of $d(X_i^{(\lambda)},\mathbf{o})$. We call $\mathrm{Vor}( \boldsymbol{\Theta}, \boldsymbol{\Phi}, \mathbf{D})$ the \textbf{\textit{ideal Poisson–Voronoi tessellation}} of $\mathcal{M}$ and denote it by $\text{\rm IPVT}(\mathcal{M})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

Let $\vec{x}, \vec{y} \in W_k^{\circ}$, $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and $f: [a,b] \rightarrow (-\infty, \infty]$ and $g: [-\infty, \infty)$ be two continuous functions. With the above data we define the $(f,g)$-avoiding Brownian line ensemble on the interval $[a,b]$ with entrance data $\vec{x}$ and exit data $\vec{y}$ to be the $\llbracket 1 , k \rrbracket$-indexed line ensemble $\mathcal{Q}$ on $\Lambda = [a,b]$ whose law is the same as that of $\{B_i\}_{i = 1}^k$ (with law $\mathbb{P}_{\operatorname{free}}^{a,b, \vec{x}, \vec{y}}$), conditioned on the event

We denote the law of $\mathcal{Q}$ by $\mathbb{P}_{\operatorname{avoid}}^{a,b,\vec{x},\vec{y},f,g}$, and expectations with respect to this measure by $\mathbb{E}_{\operatorname{avoid}}^{a,b,\vec{x},\vec{y},f,g}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:15:34.489842+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0f8bcd06d0913ff173db1b842c50fe9f2abb64cf2287332684be00475e067a93","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 22 (Type I and Type II) of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] A Ricci flow $g(t)$ on a compact manifold with finite maximal existence time $T < \infty$ develops a \emph{Type I} singularity if

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:43:53.603564+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0f95ed68a6db7e889dbf4acde0dfd6d922559bc7d74287e5a5fcee5efa91b867","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:active/passive marks process of arXiv:2512.12902, 'Non-equilibrium fluctuations for the \\stirring process with births and deaths'] [   The active/passive marks process]
\quad

$\bullet$\; The active/passive marks process is realized in a probability space denoted by $(\Omega,\mathbf{P}_\epsilon)$.
It is a product of Poisson processes indexed by $\{x,x+1\}$, $x\in \mathbb Z$: for each pair $\{x,x+1\}$
we have a Poisson point process of intensity $\epsilon^{-2}$, its events are called ``marks'' and each mark
is independently given the attribute ``active'' or ``passive'' with probability $1/2$. The processes
relative to different pairs are mutually independent and their common law is $\mathbf{P}_\epsilon$, its expectation
being also denoted by $\mathbf{E}_\epsilon$.

$\bullet$\;  For any $\omega\in \Omega$ we  define the following particle
evolution in $\Lambda_N$: a particle at $x\in \Lambda_N$ moves as soon as an
active mark appears at a pair $x,y$ with $y\in \Lambda_N$. The particle
then moves to $y$ (note that if another particle was at $y$ then it
would simultaneously move to $x$). Passive marks do not play any
role so far as well as all marks  $\{x,x+1\}$ with either $x$ or
$x+1$ not in $\Lambda_N$; they will be used later to construct
couplings. We denote by $X(t)\subset \Lambda_N$ the set of all sites
occupied by the particles at time $t$, so that $\eta(x,t)=1$ iff
$x\in X(t)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T01:10:08.702656+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0f980a52dfe6247b6bc2261ba9c9e494e18cc720cb420148c1b2409d44312c48","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2411.17524, 'Stationary measures for the Porous Medium Model'] Let $\Lambda$ be an interval of $\mathbb Z$. 
 \begin{enumerate}
  \item  For $\eta\in\Omega$, the transformation $\eta\mapsto\eta^{x,x+1}$ is an \emph{allowed jump} if $c_x(\eta)>0$.
  \item For $\{x,x+1\}\subset\Lambda$, $\sigma\in\Omega_\Lambda$, $\sigma\mapsto\sigma^{x,x+1}$ is an \emph{allowed jump inside $\Lambda$} if $c_x(0\cdot\sigma)>0$, where $0\cdot\sigma$ is the configuration equal to $0$ on $\Lambda^c$ and to $\sigma$ on $\Lambda$.
  \item For $\eta\in\Omega$, $x\in\mathbb Z$ such that $\eta(x)=1$, the particle at $x$ is \emph{active} if $c_x(\eta)+c_{x-1}(\eta)>0$ (equivalently, if there is another particle within distance $2$ of $x$).
  \item A pair of particles within distance $2$ of each other an \emph{mobile cluster}.
  \item A configuration without active particles is called \emph{frozen}.
 \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["each F_n nondecreasing, right-continuous, with values in [0,1]","no tightness is assumed, and without it the limit can be defective"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.752559+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0fba1416669badf1de8ab735445eeb6c5d50526da69885c6f0c2f43871a867fd","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (F_n) be a sequence of distribution functions on R, that is nondecreasing right-continuous functions with values in [0,1]. Then there exist a subsequence (F_{n_k}) and a nondecreasing right-continuous F : R -> [0,1] such that F_{n_k}(x) -> F(x) at every continuity point x of F. The limit F need NOT be a distribution function: mass can escape to plus or minus infinity, and with F_n the distribution function of the point mass at n one gets F identically 0. This is exactly the gap that tightness closes: the family is tight, meaning sup_n (1 - F_n(M) + F_n(-M)) -> 0 as M -> infinity, if and only if every such subsequential limit is a proper distribution function, which is Prokhorov's theorem on R. Nothing is assumed about the F_n beyond monotonicity, right-continuity and the range [0,1] - no continuity, no tightness, no common support. [standard; e.g. Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Theorem 3.2.6]","status":"unverified"}

A \emph{facet surface} \(F(z)\) for \(z\) is the union of a maximal collection of disjoint, non-parallel, properly norm-minimizing surfaces \(S_{1},\ldots ,S_{k}\) in \(M\) such that

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T17:15:45.375658+00:00","domain":"general topology","id":"claim_0fc6ca3efccfbfb81740d50ff4b42e6d92b545e1d6116f465b8a720d7d0ba797","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"A topological space X is compact if every open cover of X has a finite subcover: whenever X is the union of a family of open sets {U_i : i in I}, there are finitely many indices i_1, ..., i_n such that X is the union of U_(i_1), ..., U_(i_n). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:41:28.175431+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0fe92c2c3a66065cf6b5bdef344e3592858a429adda497c795705a803f8618aa","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition $(r-2)_*$-BP of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] Let $T$ be a $K_r$-tree
and $S\subset V(T)$ a set of {\it seeds}, 
which we consider to be initially {\it infected}. 
Then, in each step of the process, either 
\begin{itemize}
\item {\it (usual step)} some vertex $v$ with at least $r-2$ 
infected neighbors becomes infected; or else
\item {\it (special step)} if no such $v$ exists, but 
for some internal edge $e$, there are two cliques $H_i\neq H_j$ 
containing $e$ such that $H_i$ has $r-4$ infected vertices 
and $H_j$ has $1$ infected vertex,  
and all $r-3$ of these vertices are not in $e$, 
then  we infect an arbitrarily chosen vertex $u\in e$; and 
otherwise, 
\item {\it (terminal step)} if neither type of step is possible, 
then the process terminates. 
\end{itemize}
We call this process {\it $(r-2)_*$-BP} 
on $T$, 
and let $\langle S;T\rangle_*$ denote the set of 
eventually infected vertices in $T$ started with 
the seed set $S$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-07T05:37:57.011652+00:00","domain":"harvested statement (arXiv 2602.20111, 2026): owner_math","id":"claim_1005a2114ea14d5489e831f30d8a4622","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 4.3 of arXiv:2602.20111, 'Reliable Abstention under Adversarial Injections: Tight Lower Bounds and New Upper Bounds'] Algorithm 2, when run in the adversarial injection setting with an $(m,c,k)$ -resilient function $f$ and threshold $\\alpha>0$, satisfies: $\\displaystyle err_{\\mathrm{mis}}\\leq\\frac{c}{k!\\alpha}T^{k}\\qquad\\text{and}\\qquad\\mathbb{E}[err_{\\mathrm{abs}}]\\leq em\\bigl(\\alpha+cT^{k-1}\\bigr)^{1/k}\\log T$ We can asymptotically bound the combined error by choosing the optimal $\\alpha$, giving $\\displaystyle\\mathbb{E}[err_{\\mathrm{mis}}+err_{\\mathrm{abs}}]=\\tilde{\\mathcal{O}}\\left(\\frac{c^{\\frac{1}{k+1}}}{k}\\left(mT\\right)^{1-\\frac{1}{k+1}}\\right)$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:27:56.777577+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_100732cc4807bc604438dca980aa18a0120a4302ad213ce88ab9f754e0e957fb","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 9 of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Let \(\mathscr E\subseteq\Sym^2T^*\Mcal\) be a relaxation bundle and let \(\mathscr F\subset\mathscr E\) be an open fiber domain containing its zero section. A \textbf{Navier--Stokes potential} is a smooth scalar function
\be
\chi=\chi(\beta,\zeta),
\qquad
\beta\ \text{future timelike},
\qquad
\zeta\in\mathscr F,
\ee
satisfying the following conditions.
\bei

\item \emph{Euler equilibrium.} For every future timelike~\(\beta\), one has
\be
\chi(\beta,0)=\chi_{\rm E}(\beta).
\ee

\item \emph{Dominant energy condition.} The potential-generated stress-energy tensor satisfies
\be 
T_\chi^{\alpha\beta}(\beta, \zeta) X_\alpha Y_\beta
=
\frac{\del^2\chi}{\del\beta_\alpha\del\beta_\beta}(\beta, \zeta)
X_\alpha Y_\beta
\geq0
\ee
for all future-directed causal vectors~\(X,Y\), all future timelike~$\beta$ and all $\zeta\in\mathscr F$. 

\item \emph{Causal hyperbolicity.}  With \(\Xi=(\beta,\zeta)\), define the symmetric principal matrices
\bel{eq:pot-principal}
K^{\alpha AB}(\Xi)
\coloneqq
\frac{\del^3\chi}
{\del\beta_\alpha\del\Xi_A\del\Xi_B}(\Xi).
\ee
For every future-directed timelike vector~\(n\), the quadratic form
\be
-n_\alpha K^{\alpha AB}(\Xi)Z_AZ_B
\ee
is positive for every non-zero variation~\(Z\) of\/~\(\Xi\) and every state \((\beta,\zeta)\) in the constitutive domain.
\eei","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:32:35.558668+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1008395ce24656b441e3898f56666d94f9fb8e5d5cff32bc3269c0cacbaccf28","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop I-prop of arXiv:2605.21366, 'The Martin boundary of the Directed Landscape'] The following holds on a full probability event.

 (W^{\theta-}(x,s;x_0,s_0)+a_-)\vee(W^{\theta+}(x,s;x_0,s_0)+a_+),\quad x,s\in\mathbb{R}.\]
Let $a=a_+-a_-$ and take $s\in\mathbb{R}$.
\begin{enumerate} [label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}] \itemsep=1pt

{"assumptions":["1 <= p < infinity","for p = 1: mu sigma-finite (or localizable)","no hypothesis on mu for 1 < p < infinity"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.752289+00:00","domain":"functional analysis","id":"claim_100fb934fa9d5d9538b1e3ae23bbcd65c2cf4181580ee3941350c3dff3f9394b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (Omega, F, mu) be a measure space and 1 <= p < infinity with conjugate exponent q = p/(p-1) (q = infinity when p = 1). For 1 < p < infinity the map g -> (f -> integral f g dmu) is an isometric isomorphism from L^q(mu) onto the dual space L^p(mu)^*, for ANY measure space. For p = 1 the same map from L^infinity(mu) onto L^1(mu)^* is an isometric isomorphism provided mu is sigma-finite (or, more generally, localizable); without such a hypothesis it can fail to be surjective. The dual of L^infinity is strictly larger than L^1 whenever L^infinity is infinite-dimensional: on ([0,1], Lebesgue) a Banach limit or a Hahn-Banach extension of the functional f -> lim_{x -> 0} f(x) from C[0,1] gives an element of (L^infinity)^* not represented by any L^1 function. So the duality chain (L^1)^* = L^infinity does NOT continue to (L^infinity)^* = L^1, and L^1 is not reflexive; L^p is reflexive exactly for 1 < p < infinity. [standard; e.g. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorem 6.15]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:55:37.368878+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_101ffb92aa1710fdc766771588065123d2203bfc1e6dd9e5742efc214a6d5c9a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 8 (Generalized Gaussian product factorization) of arXiv:2606.18458, 'Stable size-biasing and the positive scale-mixture order of generalized Gaussian laws'] Let $p,q>0$, and let $X_p\sim N_p(0,1)$ and $X_q\sim N_q(0,1)$. Then
\[
X_p\scle X_q\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p\le q.
\]
Equivalently, there exists a strictly positive random variable $V$, independent of $X_q$, such that
\[
X_p\stackrel{d}{=}VX_q
\]
if and only if $p\le q$. When such $V$ exists, its law is unique.

More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $p=q$, one may take $V=1$.
\item If $p<q$, put $a=1/p$, $b=1/q$, $\alpha=b/a=p/q$, let $S_\alpha$ be positive $\alpha$-stable, put $W_0=S_\alpha^{-b}$, let $W$ be the $W_0$-size-biased version of $W_0$, chosen independent of $X_q$, and define
\[
V=2^{a-b}W.
\]
Then $V>0$ almost surely, $V\perp X_q$, and $VX_q\stackrel{d}{=}X_p$.
\item If $p>q$, no such strictly positive independent factor exists.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

The data are $n$ independent rows $x_i \\in \\mathbb{R}^p$ with covariance $\\Sigma$ (Gaussian in the sharpest results; finite fourth moments suffice for the eigenvalue statements), and the object studied is the sample covariance $S = \\frac{1}{n} \\sum_i x_i x_i^T$ in the proportional regime $p, n \\to \\infty$ with $p/n \\to \\gamma \\in (0, \\infty)$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:33.544132+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_102b0c94f0a077a9bc16e235659cb9aebd39afc61d193efcf1bc836f9ab10399","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 33 (Monotonicity of the edges) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix a finite graph $G$ and some $\beta\in[0,\infty)$.

{"assumptions":["U and V are open subsets of R^n of the same dimension n","phi : U -> V is a bijection, continuously differentiable, with continuously differentiable inverse (equivalently injective C^1 with nonvanishing Jacobian determinant and image V)","Lebesgue measure and Lebesgue measurable functions are used on both sides","f is measurable and either nonnegative or integrable"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.090563+00:00","domain":"real analysis, measure theory, integration in R^n","id":"claim_1047e7e34c38c2168c64f635d6e025f096e2d64b3ad9dc9fbd5d8a3856bb2cb5","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let U and V be open subsets of R^n and let phi : U -> V be a C^1 DIFFEOMORPHISM: phi is a bijection of U onto V, phi is continuously differentiable, and its inverse is continuously differentiable. (By the inverse function theorem it is equivalent to assume phi is injective, C^1, onto V, with det Dphi(x) nonzero for every x in U.) Let Dphi(x) denote the Jacobian matrix. Then for every Lebesgue measurable f : V -> [0, +infinity], the integral of f(y) dy over V equals the integral of f(phi(x)) |det Dphi(x)| dx over U, both sides being simultaneously finite or infinite; the same identity holds for complex-valued f, with f integrable over V if and only if (f composed with phi) times |det Dphi| is integrable over U. Taking f an indicator gives the measure statement: the Lebesgue measure of phi(E) equals the integral of |det Dphi| over E, for every measurable E contained in U. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) the ABSOLUTE VALUE of the determinant is required. The density is |det Dphi|; the sign records orientation and belongs to the theory of differential forms, not to Lebesgue integration. (ii) Injectivity cannot be dropped without paying for multiplicity: for a general C^1 map the correct statement is the area formula, the integral of f(phi(x)) |det Dphi(x)| dx over U equals the integral over V of f(y) N(y) dy, where N(y) is the number of preimages of y in U; N identically 1 is exactly injectivity. (iii) Smoothness cannot be relaxed to 'differentiable almost everywhere'. One needs the Luzin (N) property, that null sets map to null sets, which C^1 and Lipschitz maps have: in dimension one the Cantor function is continuous and nondecreasing with derivative 0 almost everywhere, yet it maps a null set onto a set of measure 1, and the naive substitution formula is false for it. (iv) The hypothesis is a diffeomorphism between OPEN sets; for maps defined on closed or lower-dimensional sets the statement must be routed through the area or coarea formula.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:41:28.165285+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_10481ef2ca34f8c3e5d918c755a8fb020f38f279aafadc53589ce33814706e5b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Order of TWGs of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] The {\it order} $\vartheta(T)$ of a TWG

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:02:11.260184+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1048ad50eb1acdbd71eb1f4162d74647667f635eadfb382d6eccd887c15bc60e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:majorant of arXiv:2509.08430, 'One-dimensional particle clouds with elastic collisions'] \begin{myenumi}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item
Given $M_0, \ldots, M_N$ and $U_0, \ldots, U_M$,
a continuous, concave function $u: [0,M_N] \to {\mathbb R}$ is a 
\emph{concave majorant} if $U_k \leq u(M_k)$ for every $k \in \{0,1,\ldots,N\}$. 
The (unique) \emph{least concave majorant} $\overline{u} : [0,M_N] \to {\mathbb R}$ is a concave majorant  
such that $\overline{u} (x) \leq u(x)$ for all $x \in [0,M_N]$ and every concave majorant~$u$. See Figure~(fig:elastic_stable_m of the paper) for a picture.

\item
It is not hard to see that $\overline{u}$ is piecewise linear. Denote
\begin{equation}

V := \bigl\{ k \in \{0,1,\ldots, N\} : U_k = \overline{u}(M_k) \bigr\},
\end{equation}
the 
set of \emph{boundary} indices for  $\overline{u}$; note
that it is always the case that $\{0, N\} \subseteq V$. In other words, $V = \{ k_0, k_1, \ldots, k_\nu \}$ ($\nu \in [N]$)
is the unique set with $0 = k_0 < \cdots < k_\nu = N$, 
\begin{align}
    
    \frac{U_{k_{j-1},k_{j}}}{M_{k_{j-1},k_{j}}} & \geq  \frac{U_{k_j,k_{j+1}}}{M_{k_j,k_{j+1}}} , 
     \text{ for all } j \in [\nu-1], 
    \text{ and } \\
    
          \frac{U_{k_j,m}}{M_{k_j,m}} & < \frac{U_{k_j,k_{j+1}}}{M_{k_j,k_{j+1}}} \text{ for all } 0 \leq j < \nu \text{ and all } k_j < m < k_{j+1} ,
\end{align}
where the convention is $U_0/M_0 := \infty$.

\item
Given boundary indices $V = \{ k_0, k_1, \ldots, k_{\nu} \}$, denote the sequence of \emph{slopes} of successive boundary segments by
\begin{equation}
    
    v_j :=  \frac{U_{k_{j-1},k_{j}}}{M_{k_{j-1},k_{j}}} , \text{ for } j \in [\nu];
\end{equation}
then~(equation eq:boundary-1 of the paper) says that $v_{j} \geq v_{j+1}$ for all $j \in [\nu-1]$.
\end{myenumi}","status":"unverified"}

 I=\{i:p_i>0\},\qquad J=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus I,
 \qquad  
 \qquad \boldsymbol\theta=\Sigma_{II}^{-1}\boldsymbol1_I.
\]
Then
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta=\frac{\boldsymbol p_I}{\sigma_*^2}>0,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol r_J=\Sigma_{JI}\Sigma_{II}^{-1}\boldsymbol1_I\geq\boldsymbol1_J,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol1_I^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\theta=\frac1{\sigma_*^2}.
\]
Write $r_j$ for the $j$th component of $\boldsymbol r_J$.
Let
\[
 P=\{j\in J:r_j=1\},\qquad N=\{j\in J:r_j>1\},
\]
and let $G_P$ be centred Gaussian with covariance matrix
\[
 \Gamma_P=\Sigma_{PP}-\Sigma_{PI}\Sigma_{II}^{-1}\Sigma_{IP}.
\]
Set $c_P=\Pp\{G_P>0\}$, with $c_P=1$ when $P$ is empty.  If
$M=\min_{1\leq i\leq n}X_i$, then, as $u\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \Pp\{M>u\}\sim
 \frac{c_P}{(2\pi)^{|I|/2}\det(\Sigma_{II})^{1/2}
                  \prod_{i\in I}\theta_i}
 u^{-|I|}\exp\left\{-\frac{u^2}{2\sigma_*^2}\right\}.
 
\end{equation}
Let $(\xi_i)_{i\geq1}$ be independent unit exponential random variables.
If $P$ is nonempty, let $G_P^+$ have law
$\mathcal L(G_P\mid G_P>0)$ and be independent of $(\xi_i)_{i\geq1}$.
Furthermore, as $u\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal L\left(
 \left(
   (u(X_i-u))_{i\in I},
   (X_j-u)_{j\in P},
   \frac{\boldsymbol X_N}{u}
 \right)
   \ \middle|\ M>u\right)
 \Longrightarrow
 \mathcal L\left(
   (\xi_i/\theta_i)_{i\in I},
   G_P^+,
   \boldsymbol r_N
 \right).
 
\end{equation}
The $G_P^+$ and $\boldsymbol r_N$ blocks are omitted
when $P$ and $N$, respectively, are empty. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.199654+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1071a2338358110494cec48ce2da366826450939e1b46a3f99b8559e9fb42441","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 133 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $t\notin \oJ$ (recall Lemma~\ref{l:bad.J}) and parameters as in \eqref{eq:order-of-limits}: 
    \[\bE\Big[|tp'(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
    \leq  
    o_{\trK}(1)
    \]
for $ \trrr_t\equiv \trrr(t,X^\plus(t))$. 

\begin{proof}
Let $\bar{P}(t)$ be the temporal smoothing of $tp'(t)$. Then for $t\notin\bar{J}$ we have
	\[
    \bE\Big[|tp'(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
    =
    \bE\Big[|tp'(t) - \bar P(t)|\Big]
    +\bE\Big[|\bar P(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
    = O(\lambda)
    +\bE\Big[|\bar P(t) - \trrr_t|
    \Big]\,.
    \]
Let $\bar{P}^N$ be the temporal smoothing of $t(p^N)'(t)$. It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:limit.coefs} that $\bar{P}^N$ converges pointwise to $\bar{P}$, and $\trrr^N$ converges pointwise to $\trrr$. It follows by the bounded convergence theorem that we also have convergence in expectation, so
	\[
	\bE\Big[|\bar P(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
	=\bE\Big[|\bar P^N(t) - (\trrr^N)_t|\Big] + o_N(1)\,.
	\] 
We then note that $\bar{P}^N-\trrr^N$ is the smoothing (via Definitions~\ref{d:sp.smooth} and \ref{d:t.smooth}) of 
	\begin{align} \nonumber
	A^N(t,\vy)
	&\equiv t(p^N)'(t)-\rrr^{\plus,N}(t,\vy)
	= t(p^N)'(t)-\sum_{B^\frozen \subseteq B^{\frozen,\coarse}}
    \frac{|B|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}
    \rrr^{\trunc,N}(t,B) 
    \\
	&\qquad= \bigg(
	1-\frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse} \cap [M]|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|} 
	\bigg)
	t(p^N)'(t)
	+ \sum_{B^\frozen \subseteq B^{\frozen,\coarse}} \frac{|B|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}
	\bigg(
	t(p^N)'(t) -
	\rrr^{\trunc,N}(t,B)\bigg)\,,
	
	 \end{align}
where the correspondence between $\vy$ and $B^{\frozen,\coarse}$ is as described around \eqref{e:review.P}. For the first term in
\eqref{e:P.N.r.frozen.twoterms}, at any fixed time $t$, we have
\[\bE\bigg[ 1-\frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse} \cap [M]|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|} \bigg]
    = 1 - \sum_{B^{\frozen,\coarse}}
    \frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}{M^\frozen}
    \frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse} \cap [M]|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}
    = 1 - \frac{M}{M^\frozen}
    = o_{\trK}(1)\,,
\]
by recalling the choice of $M^\frozen$ from Definition~\ref{d:froze}. For the second term in \eqref{e:P.N.r.frozen.twoterms},  we argued in the proof of Proposition~\ref{p:budget-constraints-without-frozen}\ref{it:Ising-budget-constraint} that the total fraction of particles ever frozen is with high probability at most $o_{\trK}(1)$, so this term is also small on average at any fixed time for the process $Y$. Altogether this shows
	\beq
	\bE\Big[ |A^N(t,\vY^{\frozen,N,\RomI:\RomIII}(t)) |\Big]
	= \int_{\R^3} |A^N(t,\vy)| \varrho_{N,t}(d\vy)
	\le o_{\trK}(1)\,.
	\eeq
Let $\tilde{A}^N$ be the spatial smoothing of $A^N$, via Definition~\ref{d:sp.smooth}. Let $\tvY^{\frozen,N}(t)\equiv \vY^{\frozen,N}(t)+\xxx$, and denote the projection onto the sum of the first three coordinates as

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:06:06.299765+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1078611bccc031a28b58a0008adc81dceb3a33555eeca0c8a88acf99100cfb16","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:Buse_basic_properties of arXiv:2605.26048, 'Classification of the eternal solutions and multiple coalescing shocks in the KPZ fixed po'] [Busa-Sepp-Sore-22a] 
On the space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb P)$, there exists a process
\[
\Bigl(W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t): \xi \in \mathfrak{X}, (x,s;y,t) \in \mathbb{R}^4\Bigr)
\]
such that for each fixed $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$, $\xi \in \Xi^c$, and $x \mapsto W^\xi(0,t;x,t)$ is a Brownian motion with diffusion coefficient $\sqrt 2$ and drift $2\mathcal P(\xi)$. Furthermore, the process satisfies the following properties on a single event of probability one:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont]
\item{\rm(Continuity)}  The $\mathbb{R}^4 \times \mathfrak{X} \to \mathbb{R}$ function  $(x,s;y,t;\xi) \mapsto W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t)$ is  continuous. Furthermore, if $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^4$ is a compact set, then for all $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$ and sequences $\xi_n \to \xi$, there exists $N \in \mathbb{N}$ so that for all $n \ge N$, we have 
\[
W^{\xi_n}(x,s;y,t) = W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t),\quad \text{for all }(x,s;y,t) \in K.
\]
 \item {\rm(Additivity)}  For all $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$ and $p,q,r \in \mathbb{R}^2$, 
    $W^{\xi}(p;q) + W^{\xi}(q;r) = W^{\xi}(p;r)$.   In particular, \\ $W^{\xi}(p;q) = -W^{\xi}(q;p)$ and $W^{\xi}(p;p) = 0$.
    \item {\rm(Monotonicity along a horizontal line)}
     Whenever $\xi_1< \xi_2$ in $\mathfrak{X}$, $x < y$, and $t \in \mathbb{R}$,
    \[
  W^{\xi_1}(x,t;y,t) \le W^{\xi_2}(x,t;y,t).
    \]
    \item \rm{(Divergence to $\pm \infty$)} 
    For all $\xi_1 < \xi_2$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$,
    \[
\lim_{x \to \pm \infty} W^{\xi_2} (0,0;x,t) -W^{\xi_1}(0,0;x,t) = \pm \infty.
\]
    \item {\rm(Eternal solution)} For 
    all $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$, $x,y \in \mathbb{R}$, and $s < t$,
    \begin{equation}
    W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t) = \sup_{z \in \mathbb{R}}\{W^{\xi}(x,s;z,s) +
 \mathcal{L}(z,s;y,t)\}.
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["d>=2 integer; real harmonics orthonormal for probability surface measure","P_l(1)=1; fixed dimension throughout","polynomials have finitely many coefficients"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T15:42:45.052423+00:00","domain":"Hermite interpolation; positive zonal kernels; spherical universal optimality","id":"claim_109875adfd105aaef59be23afb39e3a4e35c93b1540b5f44db1f9edd648408b7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Fix an integer d>=2 and normalized uniform surface measure sigma on S^(d-1). Let H_l be the real degree-l spherical harmonics, h_l=dim H_l, and Y_(l,1),...,Y_(l,h_l) any orthonormal basis in L2(sigma). Let P_l be the degree-l polynomial orthogonal to lower-degree polynomials for weight (1-t^2)^((d-3)/2) on [-1,1], normalized by P_l(1)=1. Then sum_(j=1)^(h_l) Y_(l,j)(x)Y_(l,j)(y)=h_l P_l(<x,y>). In particular P_l(<x,y>) is a positive semidefinite kernel: for any finite x_i on the sphere and real c_i, sum_(i,j)c_i c_j P_l(<x_i,x_j>)>=0. For a real polynomial u=sum_l a_l P_l, its zonal kernel u(<x,y>) is positive semidefinite if and only if every a_l>=0. The product of two such polynomials again has nonnegative P_l coefficients. If every coefficient through the respective degrees is strictly positive, the product also has every coefficient through its degree strictly positive. Here d=2 uses the normalized Chebyshev polynomials, and d>=3 the Gegenbauer polynomials rescaled to value 1 at 1. Positive semidefinite kernels allow zero quadratic forms; strictly positive coefficients do not mean strict positivity of every finite Gram matrix.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:11:09.319730+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_10ae89aad78e0fc69097f30e9fe9c191ff493e03ff3e432047db1bff53018b87","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:subdivided-graph of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] For $r\in{\mathbb N}_0$, the \emph{$2^r$-subdivision}
$G_r=(\Lambda_r,E_r)$ of $G$ is obtained by replacing every edge by a series
of $2^r$ edges as follows.
\begin{itemize}
\item $\Lambda_r$ is obtained from $\Lambda$ by adding $2^r-1$ new vertices $v_{e,2^{-r}j}$,
  $j=1,\ldots,2^r-1$ for
  any edge $e\in E$. We say that these new vertices are located on the edge $e$. 
  In particular, $\Lambda\subseteq \Lambda_r$. 
\item Every edge $e\in E$ is replaced by a series of $2^r$ edges $e_{1,r},\ldots,e_{2^r,r}$ as follows.
  For bookkeeping purposes only, we endow $e$ with a direction, and 
  call $v_{e,0}$ and $v_{e,1}$ the two vertices it consists of. Then, $e$ is
  replaced by the new edges $e_{j,r}=\{v_{e,2^{-r}(j-1)},v_{e,2^{-r}j}\}$, $1\le j\le 2^r$,
  which we view as being located on the edge $e$. Thus, 
  $E_r=\{e_{j,r}:e\in E, 1\le j\le 2^r\}$.
\end{itemize}
Note that $\Lambda_0=\Lambda$ and $\Lambda_r\subseteq\Lambda_{r+1}$. 
For technical convenience, we introduce also the set of
direct self-loops $\Delta_r:=\{\{i,i\}:i\in\Lambda_r\}$.","status":"unverified"}

        \[
            V_{\infty}(t) \leq (1+\eta)\frac{2C_{\alpha}}{\sigma^2}\frac{t^{-\alpha}}{\ell(t)}, \qquad t \in (0,t_0),
        \]
        where the constant is given by
        \[

        \]
        Moreover, the function $V_{\infty}$ satisfies the fractional Riccati differential equation

        \item[(b)] For the pure fractional kernel $K(t) = \frac{t^{\alpha-1}}{\Gamma(\alpha)}$, we obtain

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:18:54.371986+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_10cefe5b37cf18d47df9a0a64154be5a5a4b64ac1cecfb2540514c8833698c22","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The orthonormal polynomials for $L^2[-1,1]$, subject to
$$\int_{-1}^1P_k(x)P_l(x)\,dx=\delta_{kl}$$
and called Legendre polynomials, satisfy the following differential equation,
$$(1-x^2)P_k''(x)-2xP_k'(x)+k(k+1)P_k(x)=0$$
which is the Legendre equation from physics. Moreover, we have the formula
$$(k+1)P_{k+1}(x)=(2k+1)xP_k(x)-kP_{k-1}(x)$$
called Bonnet recurrence formula, as well as the formula
$$P_k(x)=\frac{1}{2^kk!}\cdot\frac{d^k}{dx^k}\left(1-x^2\right)^k$$
called Rodrigues formula for the Legendre polynomials.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:37:15.397228+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_10e6b2d7c70b79b3e462d15cd26bd3fed6252a89d509048fe7f1a36c085cd652","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 9 (Feller boundary classification) of arXiv:2607.12365, 'Bernoulli--Doob representation, asymptotic limits and boundary behavior of bounded homogen'] Consider $dZ_t=\sigma(Z_t)\,dW_t$ on $[a,b]$ with $Z_0=z\in(a,b)$,
$\sigma\in C^2([a,b])$, $\sigma>0$ on $(a,b)$,
$\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=0$. Since the drift is zero, the diffusion is
in natural scale $s(x)=x$ with speed measure density
$m(x)=2/\sigma^2(x)$. Fix an interior reference point $z\in(a,b)$
and define
\[
N_a := \int_a^z(z-x)\sigma^{-2}(x)\,dx\,,\qquad
\Sigma_a := \int_a^z(x-a)\sigma^{-2}(x)\,dx\,,
\]
and analogously $N_b$, $\Sigma_b$ at the right boundary $b$. The
boundary type is determined by the following table.
\[
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.4}
\begin{array}{c|c|l}
N_a & \Sigma_a & \text{Boundary type of }a \\ \hline
<\infty & <\infty & \text{Regular: attainable and startable} \\
<\infty & =\infty & \text{Exit: attainable, not startable} \\
=\infty & <\infty & \text{Entrance: not attainable, startable} \\
=\infty & =\infty & \text{Natural: not attainable, not startable}
\end{array}
\]
Here $N_a<\infty$ means $\Pr_x(\tau_a<\infty)>0$ for all
$x\in(a,b)$; $N_a=\infty$ means $\tau_a=\infty$ a.s.
$\Sigma_a<\infty$ means $a$ is an admissible starting point in the
diffusion sense; $\Sigma_a=\infty$ means it is not. The same table
applies to the right boundary $b$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:54:18.239674+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_10f0dbad1eaf8af2c306fe342b19bc0c5c230c06db91a298f11f1c48bd16b0f6","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:upper-box-to-requests of arXiv:2608.29561, 'Ball codes: A coding characterization of Hausdorff and packing dimensions'] Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and bounded, and let \(q>0\) satisfy
\[
\overline{\dim}_{\mathrm B}(F)<q.
\]
For every \(\eta>0\), there are \(r_0\in\omega\), closed balls
\(B_{r,i}\ (r\ge r_0, i<m_r)\), and natural numbers
\(\ell_{r,i}\ (r\ge r_0, i<m_r)\) such that, for every \(r\ge r_0\),
\[
F\subseteq\bigcup_{i<m_r}B_{r,i},
\qquad
\diam(B_{r,i})\le2^{-r},
\]
and, in total,
\[
\sum_{r\ge r_0}\sum_{i<m_r}2^{-\ell_{r,i}}<\eta,
\]
and
\[
\ell_{r,i}\le qr+2\log_2(r+1)+O(1)
\]
where the constant in \(O(1)\) may depend on \(F,q,\eta\), but not on
\(r\) or \(i\).  Thus a bounded set of upper box-counting dimension \(<q\) admits
descriptions at \emph{every sufficiently large scale} with rate \(q\), up to a
logarithmic overhead, and with arbitrarily small total Kraft weight.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:55:56.998160+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_10fdc9a64162ef67cc4ba64daacd55f877a428f93b25a2e283c970959146d568","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2609.02785, 'Characterization of Stanley-Reisner varieties by their automorphism group'] Let $\Delta$ be a simplicial complex on $[n]$ and let $\partial\neq0$ be a $\ZZ^n$-homogeneous
derivation of $\KK[\Delta]$ of degree $\alpha\in\ZZ^n$. Define $c_1,\dots,c_n\in\KK$ by

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:10:05.675939+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_11000472bd74a779265b6835e9c550245fffe4f84bed98dcd2568da600171155","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 6 (Wendel's formula: Probabilistic version) of arXiv:2608.16752, 'Absorption Probabilities for Random Convex Hulls: Distribution-Freeness via the Wall-Cross'] Let $\xi_1, \dots, \xi_n$ be random vectors in $\R^d$ whose joint distribution is invariant under sign flips, that is,
$$

\qquad \text{for every } \eps \in \{\pm 1\}^n.
$$
Suppose additionally that the configuration $X := (\xi_1 \,|\, \dots \,|\, \xi_n)$ is regular almost surely, i.e.\ $\pr(X \in \mathcal D) = 0$. Then
\begin{align*}

    = \frac{1}{2^{\,n-1}} \sum_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{n-1}{j}.
\end{align*}
Note that neither independence nor exchangeability of $\xi_1, \dots, \xi_n$ is assumed.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(X_n) a submartingale for a filtration (F_n)","sup_n E[X_n^+] < infinity (for a martingale: sup_n E|X_n| < infinity)","no uniform integrability is assumed, and without it convergence is only almost sure"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.627158+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_111070f1050f003220fb4766d3ba4d411602ec9050d0c6e450a5eeb448ccb643","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X_n) be a submartingale with sup_n E[X_n^+] < infinity. Then X_n converges almost surely to a limit X_infinity with E|X_infinity| < infinity. For a MARTINGALE the hypothesis is equivalent to sup_n E|X_n| < infinity, since E[X_n] is constant and E|X_n| = 2E[X_n^+] - E[X_n]. Convergence is ONLY almost sure: it need not hold in L^1, and E[X_infinity] need not equal E[X_0]. Standard failure: let (X_n) be the product of independent nonnegative mean-one factors, for instance X_n = prod_{k <= n} (1 + eps_k) with eps_k = +1 or -1 with probability 1/2 each - equivalently X_n = 2^n on the event that all signs were +1 and 0 otherwise. Then X_n is a nonnegative martingale with E X_n = 1 for every n, so it is L^1-bounded and converges a.s., but the limit is 0 almost surely and E X_infinity = 0 != 1 = E X_0. Nonnegative supermartingales always converge a.s. because X_n^+ = X_n has bounded expectation; upgrading to L^1 convergence is exactly what uniform integrability supplies. [standard; e.g. Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Theorem 4.2.11]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:46:55.640920+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_11177de8223e6dede0a9be910763cb7f635c599eece988a1fe104aa5e1f8e643","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 23 (Skorokhod representation and generalized weak limit) of arXiv:2605.23529, 'Generalized Bessel-Dunkl diffusions'] Assume \ref{ass:cont}-\ref{ass:sigma}, and let $X^{(n)}$ be the approximating
sequence. Then, after passing to a subsequence, there exist a probability space, a
continuous $\Cc$-valued process $X$, a continuous local martingale
$M=(M_1,\ldots,M_N)$, and, for every $\alpha\in R_+$, a continuous increasing
process $A^\alpha$ on $[0,\zeta)$ with $A^\alpha(0)=0$, such that, for
\begin{equation*}
    \zeta
    :=
    \lim_{r\to\infty}
    \inf\{t\ge0:\ |X(t)|\ge r\},
\end{equation*}
we have, for every $t<\zeta$,
\begin{equation}
    
    X(t)
    =
    x_0
    +
    M(t)
    +
    \int_0^t b(s,X(s))\,ds
    +
    \sum_{\alpha\in R_+}\alpha\,A^\alpha(t),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}

\end{equation}

$N$-dimensional Brownian motion $B$ such that
\begin{equation*}
    M(t)

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:28:08.660922+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_111e04d7407e518dbc2b8eb97fe19053a3cddf9ce81b560743bede5f72906e9d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 4 (See, e.g., {\cite[Fact~3.5) of arXiv:2607.29495, 'Fast Mixing for Low-Temperature Potts Models via Poisson Trees'] {CLV21a}}]
Let $\nu$ be a Gibbs distribution over $[q]^{V}$ and $P$ denote the Glauber dynamics for $\nu$. Let $\nu_{\mathrm{min}}=\min_{\sigma: \nu(\sigma)>0} \nu(\sigma)$. Then the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item $T_{\mathrm{mix}}(\epsilon)\leq \frac{1}{\gamma}\log \frac{1}{\epsilon\nu_{\mathrm{min}}}$ where $\gamma$ is the spectral gap of $P$.
    \item $T_{\mathrm{mix}}(\epsilon)\leq \frac{1}{\alpha}\big(\log\log \frac{1}{\nu_{\mathrm{min}}}+\log \frac{1}{2\epsilon^2}\big)$ where $\alpha$ is the log-Sobolev constant of $P$
    \item $T_{\mathrm{mix}}(\epsilon)\leq \frac{1}{\hat\alpha}\big(\log\log \frac{1}{\nu_{\mathrm{min}}}+\log \frac{1}{2\epsilon^2}\big)$ where $\hat\alpha$ is the modified log-Sobolev constant of $P$.    
\end{enumerate}
It holds that $\alpha\leq \hat\alpha\leq 2\gamma$. Moreover, with $K(r)=\frac{1-2r}{\log (\frac{1}{r}-1)}$, it holds that $\alpha\geq K(\nu_{\mathrm{min}})\gamma$; for $\nu$ that is $b$-marginally bounded, it holds that $\alpha\geq K(b) \hat\alpha$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:38:17.813274+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1121eb0608246f8d6c834b00350f834e462f30a837726b65b6cf8f9de7ab00b6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma l.boostdrag of arXiv:2510.07682, 'From tug-of-war to Brownian Boost: \\ explicit ODE solutions for player-funded stochastic-'] Let $(S_-,S_+) \in \mathcal{S}_0^2$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item Suppose that the quantities $\textrm{Right}(S_-)$ and $\textrm{Right}(S_+)$ are finite. Let $i \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ exceed both, and let $\psi \in \big( \tfrac{1-\kappa}{1+\kappa},1 \big)$. 
Choose $k \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$ so that
\begin{equation}
 \Big( \frac{1-\kappa}{1+\kappa} \Big)^{k+1} \big( m_\infty - m_* \big)
 + \bigg( \psi^k +  \Big( \frac{1-\kappa}{1+\kappa} \Big)^{k+1} \bigg)  \kappa^{-1} \bigg( \frac{\psi}{1 - \psi} + \frac{1-\kappa}{(1+\kappa)\big(1 - \frac{1-\kappa}{(1+\kappa)\psi}\big)} \bigg)
\end{equation}
 is strictly less than $m_{-\infty,\infty}$.
Then $\egameplay{S_-}{\textrm{Rocket}_\psi^{i\rightarrow}}{i+k}[P_+] > \egameplay{S_-}{S_+}{i+k}[P_+]$. 
\item  Suppose that $\textrm{Right}(S_+) = \infty$ and $\textrm{Right}(S_-) < \infty$. Let $i \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ satisfy  $i > \textrm{Right}(S_-)$ and  $S_+(i,1) > 0$. Then  $\egameplay{S_-}{\textrm{Drag}^{i\rightarrow}(S_+)}{i}[P_+] > \egameplay{S_-}{S_+}{i}[P_+]$.
\item  If $\textrm{Left}(S_-)$ and $\textrm{Left}(S_+)$ exceed $-\infty$ and $i \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ is less than their minimum, then, provided that the quantity given by replacing $m_\infty - m_*$ by $n_{-\infty} - n_*$ in~((e.kappahyp of the paper)) is strictly less than $n_{\infty,-\infty}$, we have that $\egameplay{\textrm{Rocket}_\psi^{\leftarrow i}(S_-)}{S_+}{i-k}[P_-] > \egameplay{S_-}{S_+}{i-k}[P_-]$.
\item  If $\textrm{Left}(S_-) = -\infty$, $\textrm{Left}(S_+) > - \infty$ and $i \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ is such that $i < \textrm{Left}(S_+)$ and $S_-(i,1) > 0$, then  $\egameplay{\textrm{Drag}^{\leftarrow i}(S_-)}{S_+}{i}[P_-] > \egameplay{S_-}{S_+}{i}[P_-]$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-06T03:36:16.690087+00:00","domain":"harvested statement (arXiv 2512.18592, 2025): mathematics","id":"claim_115c89f8a67d4fce88f37c87ae749bc1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2.4 (Erdős–Rényi, SBMs and logistic RDPGs) in the first version of arXiv:2512.18592, 'Wavelet Latent Position Exponential Random Graphs'] Fix $c\\in\\mathbb{R}$ and a real symmetric Hilbert–Schmidt matrix $S=(s_{rs})_{r,s\\geq 0}$, and let $G_{n}\\sim\\mathrm{WL\\mbox{-}ERG}(c,S)$ be generated as in Definitions 2.1 – 2.3. 1. (Erdős–Rényi.) If $s_{rs}=0$ for all $(r,s)\\neq(0,0)$, then $G_{n}$ is Erdős–Rényi $G(n,p)$ with $p=\\sigma(c+s_{00})$. 2. (Haar/SBM special case.) Assume the underlying wavelet system is the Haar system and fix an integer $J\\geq 0$. Let $\\{I_{\\ell,J}\\}_{\\ell=0}^{2^{J}-1}$ be the dyadic partition of $(0,1)$, define $\\phi_{\\ell,J}(x):=2^{J/2}\\mathbf{1}_{I_{\\ell,J}}(x)$, and let $V_{J}:=\\mathrm{span}\\{\\phi_{\\ell,J}:0\\leq\\ell\\leq 2^{J}-1\\}\\subset L^{2}(0,1)$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.978268+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_115f29b1d1046ab98502656faec2c385f358491dda3e3bd5f862b169731712f7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 58 (Universal critical endpoint and its sharp boundary) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Suppose \(H\) is infinite dimensional.  Then, for every \(K,T>0\),
\begin{equation}
 p_{\mathrm{univ}}(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{cont}}(K,T);H)=1.
 
\end{equation}
The exponent-one upper bound is dimension free and is quantified by
\eqref{cc:eq-universal-weak-area-bound}.  It is sharp in all of the
following distinct senses.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item No \(\mathcal S_{p,\infty}\) with \(p<1\) contains all terminal
areas in \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{cont}}(K,T)\).
\item No finite critical Lorentz ideal \(\mathcal S_{1,\rho}\),
\(0<\rho<\infty\), is universal.
\item Given any deterministic positive sequence
\(\varepsilon_n\downarrow0\), there is one
martingale in \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{cont}}(K,T)\) such that, almost surely,
\begin{equation}
 A_{0,T}\in\mathcal S^0_{1,\infty}(H),\qquad
 \sup_n\frac{n s_n(A_{0,T})}{\varepsilon_n}=\infty,
 \qquad
 A_{0,T}\notin\bigcup_{0<\rho<\infty}\mathcal S_{1,\rho}(H).
 
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Thus there is no conflict between
\eqref{cc:eq-individual-little-weak} and universal sharpness: each fixed
martingale area has \(ns_n(A)\to0\), while dimension-varying Brownian
blocks make that convergence arbitrarily slow and destroy every fixed

{"assumptions":["A a square complex matrix; eigenvalues counted with algebraic multiplicity in the refinement","the discs are closed; a point of the union may fail to be an eigenvalue (the theorem localises, it does not characterise)"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:31:12.479038+00:00","domain":"linear algebra","id":"claim_118eb1edbdd586661b78b6b8a406c50d9aa31e793c06b918802f39726a6468d2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let A = (a_ij) be a complex n x n matrix and for each i let R_i = sum_{j != i} |a_ij| be the i-th deleted absolute row sum and D_i = { z in C : |z - a_ii| <= R_i } the i-th Gershgorin disc. Then every eigenvalue of A lies in the union of the discs D_1, ..., D_n. Applying the theorem to the transpose, every eigenvalue also lies in the union of the column discs (radii the deleted column sums), so the spectrum lies in the intersection of the two unions. Refinement: if a union of k of the discs is disjoint from the union of the other n - k, then exactly k eigenvalues (counted with algebraic multiplicity) lie in the union of those k discs. Consequences: a strictly diagonally dominant matrix (|a_ii| > R_i for all i) is invertible, since 0 lies in no disc; a Hermitian strictly diagonally dominant matrix with positive diagonal is positive definite; and the discs can be shrunk by a diagonal similarity D^{-1} A D, which changes the radii to sum_{j != i} |a_ij| d_j / d_i.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:17:10.016420+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_119d43813e76545de1e2529f61bcbe76b0041d46bdb7534e3ff8a898685af7f1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 52 (No universal bound below the first moment) of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] Let $d\ge1$. \[
\Psi:\ \{ \text{nonnegative integer-valued random variables} \}

\]
with the following \emph{universality property}:

For every finitary coding $\varphi$, every i.i.d.\ input $X$, every local observable $f$, and every $n\in\mathbb N$,
\[

\]
and letting $n\to\infty$,
\[

\ \le\ K\, \liminf_{n\to\infty}\Psi\big(r_\varphi^{(n)}(X)\big).

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.476988+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_11b452e7f62e7bd5150fe2be71047976f821de421d83b02882c1e20f2cc19c08","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition eq:entropy limit property of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] For all odd $k \ge 3$ and any distinct $i,j \in [k]$, there exist asymmetric two-point distributions supported on $\{i,j\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_k$ which are not symmetrization resistant. 

\begin{proof}
By affine invariance ((lem:affine_invariance of the paper)), we may take $p > 1/2$, and we may take our two-point PMF $f = f_k$ on $\mathbb{Z}_k$ to be such that $f_k(-1) = 1-p$ and $f_k(1) = p$ and zero elsewhere. 
We will construct a PMF $g = g_k$ for each $k$ such that $f * g$ is symmetric and 
\begin{equation} \lim_{p \downarrow \frac{1}{2}} H(g_k) = 0 . \end{equation}

We begin by writing $k = 2l + 1$ and $\delta = \frac{2p-1}{kp-l} = \frac{2p-1}{2lp+p-l}$. 
Define $g(0) = 1-l\delta$; the values of $g$ at the $2l$ remaining elements of $\mathbb{Z}_k = \mathbb{Z}_{2l+1}$ will be $\delta$ ($l$ times) and $0$ ($l$ times), according to the following pattern:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item If $k \equiv_4 1$, 
 $g_k(1) \coloneqq g_k(2) \coloneqq 0$ 
and $g_k(3) \coloneqq g_k(4) \coloneqq \delta$. 
\item If $k \equiv_4 3$, 
 $g_k(1) \coloneqq \delta$,
 $g_k(2) \coloneqq 0$;
and when $k > 3$, 
 $g_k(3) \coloneqq 0$ and 
 $g_k(4) \coloneqq \delta$. 
\item For all $k \ge 11$, for all integers $r \in [5,l]$, $g_k(r) \coloneqq g_k(r-4)$. 

\item Finally, for all $r \in [l]$, $g(-r) \coloneqq 0$ iff $g(r)=\delta$ and $g(-r)\coloneqq \delta$ iff $g(r)=0$. 
\end{enumerate}
Intuitively, $g$ consists of one large mass at the origin, and alternating pairs of zeros and $\delta$s on the rest of $\mathbb{Z}_k$. 

Note that $\lim_{p \downarrow \frac{1}{2}} \delta = 0$, so that
$\lim_{p \downarrow \frac{1}{2}} g_k = \mathds{1}_{0}$ and therefore $g_k$ satisfies (equation eq:entropy limit property of the paper). 
It remains to show that $g_k$ is a symmetrizer of $f_k$, i.e., that $(g_k * f_k)(r) = (g_k * f_k)(-r)$ for all $r \in [l]$. 

For $r \ge 2$, noting that $g(\pm(r-1)), g(\pm(r+1)) \in \{0, \delta\}$ with $g(-(r-1)) = \delta$ iff $g(r-1) = 0$ iff $g(r+1) = \delta$ iff $g(-(r+1))=0$, 
we have $g(-(r-1)) = g(r+1)$ and $g(-(r+1)) = g(r-1)$, so that
\[
(f * g)(r) 
= pg(r-1) + (1-p)g(r+1)
= pg(-r-1) + (1-p)g(-r+1) 
= (f * g)(-r) .
\]
Finally, noting that the values of $g_k(2) = 0$ and $g_k(-2) = \delta$ for all $k$, we compute
\begin{align*}
(f* g)(1) 
&= pg(0) + (1-p)g(2) \\

&= \frac{p^2}{2lp + p -l} \\
&= \frac{p^2 - (1-p)p + (1-p)p}{2lp + p -l} \\
&= \frac{p(2p - 1)}{2lp + p -l} + (1-p)g(0) \\
&= p \delta + (1-p)g(0) \\

&= (f* g)(-1). \qedhere
\end{align*}
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:48:00.295619+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_11cf28bf71a3b09320896cdd4391626cba4513a1bcd90bba63371a94269408b3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Entropy number of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $(X,\rho)$ be a metric space, and $\mathcal{M}\subseteq X$ be compact. For every fixed $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the entropy number $\varepsilon_n(\mathcal{M})_X$ is the infimum of all $\varepsilon > 0$ for which $2^n$ balls with centers from $X$ and radius $\varepsilon$ cover $\mathcal{M}$. Formally, we write
    \[
        \varepsilon_n(\mathcal{M})_X
        =
        \inf\left\{
            \varepsilon > 0 :
            \exists
            g_1,\cdots,g_{2^n} \in X,
            \
            \mathcal{M}
            \subseteq
            \bigcup_{j=1}^{2^n} B(g_j,\varepsilon)
        \right\}.
    \]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:53:10.159922+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_11dba8d96b3ee019c555414aab40d141b426fbd14ec02e18a2e6efe002943189","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm MO-as-colim of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The cocone $\sigma_{[0]}$ exhibits $\textbf{\textup{MO}}=\smash{\textbf{\textup{MOP}}^{[0]}}$ as the global colimit of $\smash{{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak J}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{gl}|_{\ul\textup{VRep}_{[0]}}}$.
    \begin{proof}
        We will more generally prove this for any $d\in{\mathbb{Z}}$, and similarly to before it will suffice to show that $\tilde\sigma_{[d]}$ exhibits $\textbf{\textup{BOP}}^{[d]}\hookrightarrow\textbf{\textup{BOP}}$ as a colimit.

        As $\ul\textup{VRep}=\coprod_{d\in{\mathbb{Z}}}\smash{\ul\textup{VRep}_{[d]}}$, we get an equivalence
        \[
            \mathop{\textup{colim}}_{\ul\textup{VRep}}\bar y_{\textup{top}} \simeq \coprod_{d\in{\mathbb{Z}}}\,\mathop{\textup{colim}}_{\ul\textup{VRep}_{[d]}}\,\bar y_{\textup{top}}|_{\ul\textup{VRep}_{[d]}}
        \]
        in ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}[\textbf{\textup{BOP}}]$. As the left-hand side is terminal by Proposition~(prop:MOP-as-colim of the paper), so is the coproduct on the right-hand side. Thus, the coproduct of the maps 
        \[
            \mathop{\textup{colim}}\bar y_{\textup{top}}|_{\ul\textup{VRep}_{[d]}}\to\big(\textbf{\textup{BOP}}^{[d]}\hookrightarrow\textbf{\textup{BOP}}\big)
        \]
        induced by $\tilde\sigma_{[d]}$ for all $d\in{\mathbb{Z}}$ is a map between terminal objects and hence an equivalence in ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}[\textbf{\textup{BOP}}]$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:03:59.343356+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_11f2164fdf0cb4847c636b8d0698ad9b63dfdf120cc4e2333fe53967dafefdfa","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Satz thm:HigherOrderLSq of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on ${\mathbb R}^n$ which satisfies an $\mathrm{LS}_q$-inequality with constant $\sigma^q > 0$, and let $f\colon {\mathbb R}^n \to {\mathbb R}$ be a $\mathcal{C}^d$-smooth function with ${\mathbb E} f = 0$.
	\begin{enumerate}

		\[

{"assumptions":["Discrete Gaussian free field on a two-dimensional lattice domain with Dirichlet boundary conditions","Gibbs-Markov (domain Markov) property and lattice Green function asymptotics","Random-walk-below-a-barrier (ballot) estimates for the scale walk"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.987849+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_11fcc5b0b92d4300329a446dd3a28c80e7535335cb27eaecb364b7fce9c12206","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). The concentric decomposition (Biskup-Louidor) describes the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field h in a box of side N as seen from a point x where the field is near its maximum. Around x one takes nested dyadic annuli; conditioning on the values of h on the boundaries of the concentric boxes, the Gibbs-Markov property splits h into (i) a random walk S_k along the scales, whose increments are the Gaussian binding fields' values at x, with variance of order g log 2 per scale, with the maximum constraint acting as a barrier the walk must stay below (entropic repulsion), (ii) independent zero-boundary fields in the annuli, and (iii) explicit bounded error terms from the non-exact scale invariance of the lattice Green function. The maximum-at-x event becomes a ballot-type event for the walk S_k, handled by random-walk-below-a-barrier estimates, which yield tightness of the centred maximum, the local limit law of the maximum, and the description of the cluster of near-maximal points around x (the cluster law nu). It is the tool behind the full extremal process of the DGFF (Biskup-Louidor 2016, 2018) and the intermediate level sets. It does not by itself give universality for other log-correlated fields: the binding-field structure uses the DGFF's exact Gibbs-Markov property. Typical failure: Treating the annulus fields phi_k as exactly independent rather than approximately so, and carrying a multiscale second-moment computation through without tracking the coupling error terms; because the GFF is only log-correlated rather than an exact branching random walk, the independence used in the concentric decomposition is an approximation that must be explicitly controlled, and skipping this step is a common source of unjustified exponent claims for GFF level-set percolation. Canonical reference: Biskup and Louidor, 2016, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Biskup and Louidor, 2018, Advances in Mathematics; Biskup, Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field, PIMS-CRM lecture notes, 2020, Springer.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.355487+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_120844a9e4d83f44ff30daf26d429f2a5182a56faf96997588561c50bbb77eb5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 223 (relaxed domains) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\dist(\cdot,\cdot)$ denote the Euclidean distance in $\R^N$, and define
\beq
\begin{aligned}
    S_N(\iota)
    &\equiv\bigg\{\bx\in\R^N :
    \frac{\dist(\bx,S_N)}{N^{1/2}} \le \iota
    \bigg\}\,, &
    \Sigma_N(\iota)
    &\equiv\bigg\{\bx\in\R^N :
    \frac{\dist(\bx,\Sigma_N)}{N^{1/2}} \le \iota
    \bigg\}\,.
\end{aligned}\eeq
We call $S_N(\iota)$ the \textbf{$\iota$-relaxed spherical domain},
and $\Sigma_N(\iota)$  the \textbf{$\iota$-relaxed Ising domain}.\footnote{While these relaxed domains are needed in the Ising setting for the notion of a Lipschitz algorithm to make sense, any point in $S_N(\iota)$ or $\Sigma_N(\iota)$ can be rounded to a point in $S_N$ or $\Sigma_N$ with nearly the same performance; see Remark~\ref{r:relaxed-wlog}.}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["G finite, connected, undirected, without isolated vertices (weighted graphs work verbatim with weighted degrees and volumes)","the spectral gap is that of the NORMALISED Laplacian; for regular graphs it is (d - mu_2)/d, and the unnormalised version scales by d","conductance is measured against volume; the vertex-count edge expansion h(G) is the same quantity only for regular graphs"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:49:11.846189+00:00","domain":"spectral graph theory","id":"claim_123dda5b10ef9e8af280ba37a63254fd3b1973ad6a342a5785086a24af3d21fc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let G = (V, E) be a finite connected graph with vertex degrees d(v), volume vol(S) = sum_{v in S} d(v), and for a vertex set S with 0 < vol(S) <= vol(V)/2 let phi(S) = e(S, V - S) / vol(S) be its conductance, where e(S, V - S) counts the edges leaving S. The conductance (Cheeger constant) of G is phi(G) = min over such S of phi(S). Let 0 = lambda_1 < lambda_2 <= ... <= lambda_n <= 2 be the eigenvalues of the normalised Laplacian L = I - D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2}. CHEEGER'S INEQUALITY (Alon-Milman, Sinclair-Jerrum, Dodziuk; the graph form of Cheeger's 1970 Riemannian inequality): lambda_2 / 2 <= phi(G) <= sqrt(2 lambda_2). For a d-regular graph with adjacency eigenvalues d = mu_1 >= mu_2 >= ..., lambda_2 = (d - mu_2)/d and the edge expansion h(G) = min e(S, V-S)/|S| (over |S| <= n/2) satisfies (d - mu_2)/2 <= h(G) <= sqrt(2 d (d - mu_2)). Both sides are sharp up to constants: the cycle C_n has phi of order 1/n and lambda_2 of order 1/n^2 (so the square root is needed), while the hypercube and expanders have phi and lambda_2 of the same order. Consequences: a graph is an expander (phi bounded below) if and only if it has a spectral gap bounded below; the mixing time of the random walk is O(log(n) / lambda_2) and at least of order 1/phi; the sweep cut of the second eigenvector (the proof of the upper bound) is the spectral partitioning algorithm, with the guarantee phi(S) <= sqrt(2 lambda_2) for the set it returns; higher-order Cheeger inequalities (Lee-Oveis Gharan-Trevisan) relate lambda_k to k-way partitions, and the improved Cheeger inequality bounds phi by lambda_2 / sqrt(lambda_3).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:51:11.463204+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_124528d929f6d734b3af9da0d623a149f8e9b2fbbd826f9c30808973fd01d0e6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 20 ({\cite[Definition~6.2, 6.9, and Proposition~6.10) of arXiv:2609.02561, 'NON-NEF LOCI IN MIXED CHARACTERISTIC'] {MS}}]
With notation as above,
set $d:=\dim R$.
Let $(R,\Delta)$ be a log $\Q$-Gorenstein pair, and let $E_R(k)$ be the injective hull of $k$ as an $R$-module.
Fix a canonical divisor $K_R \geq 0$.
Write
$K_R +\Delta=\frac{1}{m}\divi(f)$ for some $0\neq f\in R$ and some $m\in\Z_{>0}$.
Take a representing element $f^{\frac{1}{m}}\in R^+$.
Let $B$ be a perfectoid big Cohen-Macaulay $R^{+}$-algebra and
let $\phi:H_{\m}^{d}(R(K_R)) \rightarrow H_{\m}^{d}(B)$ denote the morphism such that
the composition of the natural morphism $H_{\m}^{d}(R) \rightarrow H_{\m}^{d}(R(K_R))$ and $\phi$ is identical to the morphism induced by the multiplication by $f^{\frac{1}{m}}$.

The BCM-test ideal of $(R,\Delta)$ with respect to $B$ is defined as
\[ \tau_{B}(R,\Delta) 
:= {\Image( E_R(k) \cong H_{\m}^{d}(R(K_R)) \xrightarrow{\phi} H_{\m}^{d}(B))}^{\vee} \subset R, \]
where ${(-)}^{\vee}$ denotes Matlis duality.
The BCM-test ideal of $(R,\Delta)$ is defined as
\[ \taubcm(R,\Delta) := \bigcap_{B} \tau_B (R,\Delta) \subset R.\]
We say
that $(R,\Delta)$ is $\BCM_B$-regular if $\tau_B (R,\Delta)=R$
and
that $(R,\Delta)$ is BCM-regular if $\taubcm(R,\Delta)=R$.
These definitions are independent of the choices of $K_R$ and $f^\frac{1}{m}\in R^+$.","status":"unverified"}
