{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:58:53.185383+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_124638bc797a9a4572624a22ce91ae82e81cd300580d95579507cac5f603d60d","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2606.30349, 'Attenuated Poisson Dirichlet approximations for divisibility configurations'] Let \(X,Y,Z\) be \(\mathbf N(\mathbbm X)\)-valued random variables defined on a common probability space, and let \(B\subset \mathbf N(\mathbbm X)\) be measurable. Suppose that

\begin{align*}
p
:=
\Pb[Z\in B]\wedge \Pb[Y\in B]
>
0.
\end{align*}

Assume moreover that \(X\in B\) on the event \(\{Z\in B\}\), and that \(B\) has finite diameter with respect to \(\mathfrak d\), namely

\begin{align*}
D_B
:=
\sup_{\eta,\zeta\in B}\mathfrak d(\eta,\zeta)
<

\end{align*}
Then
\begin{align*}

\mathcal L(Y\mid Y\in B)
\right)
\le

\Pb\big[\{Z\in B\}\Delta\{Y\in B\}\big].
\end{align*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["mu is a product measure on {0,1}^n, or satisfies the FKG lattice condition (log-supermodular)","A and B are both increasing (or both decreasing) events; f and g both monotone in the same direction","the reversed inequality needs one increasing and one decreasing event","no conclusion for events that are not monotone, and none for a non-FKG measure"],"created_at":"2026-09-02T07:51:33.048644+00:00","domain":"percolation and correlation inequalities (hand-authored statement with hypotheses, 2026-09-02)","id":"claim_12642faa7ec3d8f83d07d4fc84666d17c25bf65b9cb7021607d2e1967b320070","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let mu be a product probability measure on {0,1}^n (Harris 1960), or more generally a measure on a finite distributive lattice satisfying the FKG lattice condition mu(x v y) mu(x ^ y) >= mu(x) mu(y) (Fortuin, Kasteleyn, Ginibre 1971). If A and B are both increasing events, then mu(A and B) >= mu(A) mu(B); equivalently, for increasing functions f and g, E[f g] >= E[f] E[g]. The same holds when both are decreasing. If one event is increasing and the other decreasing, the inequality reverses: mu(A and B) <= mu(A) mu(B). The inequality says nothing about a pair of events that are neither increasing nor decreasing, and it fails for a general (non-FKG) measure.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.095753+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_126a5230d73954e91a0788ca6a1a8b548482fd7a6f3c0aa23b352d79980695a6","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:fold of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $\mathcal F$ be an enterable distance-hereditary one-front fold with
ordered formal ports $x_1,\ldots,x_p$ on its carrier arcs.  For an incoming
two-front state $\Xi$, its open tensor has an identity
\[
 \mathcal F(x_1,\ldots,x_p)[\Xi]
 =\sum_\nu a_\nu
 u_\nu(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\,\Xi\,
 v_\nu(x_1,\ldots,x_p),
\tag{2.4.3}
\]
where every port variable occurs exactly once, every fixed letter in
$u_\nu,v_\nu$ is a safe gate or signed isometry, and
$\sum_\nu|a_\nu|\le A^s$ for a fold with $s$ coefficient occurrences.
After substituting safe words $X_i$ for the ports,
\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:47.659256+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_126e4f1a177aa826fa23e4d73aebf2fc9d6ea0efe3bf8b478348f4cac9e263a3","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2605.08844, 'Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential '] Let $S$ be a finite-dimensional Banach space. Let $\mathbf{X}\in \Omega G_p([a,b],V)$ and $\mathbf{Y}\in \Omega G_q([c,d],W)$, and set $\kappa=\lfloor p\rfloor$ and $\lambda=\lfloor q\rfloor$. Let $g\colon F\to S$ be Fr\'echet smooth, and let $Z$ be a two-parameter $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$-controlled path.
Then the composition $g(Z)$ defines a two-parameter controlled path
\[
g(Z) \in \mathcal{D}^{p,q}_{\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y}}([a,b]\times[c,d], S).
\]
Moreover, $g(Z)$ is characterized by the identity
\[
g(Z)_{t,v}[\eta,\xi] = g\left(Z^{(0,0)}_{t,v}\right)[\eta,\xi],
\qquad
\text{for all } \eta \in V^{\otimes 0},\ \xi \in W^{\otimes 0}.
\]

The higher level components of $g(Z)$ are given as follows. For
$\xi_j \in V^{\otimes j}$ and $\eta_k \in W^{\otimes k}$, define
\[
g(Z_{t,v})[\xi_j,\eta_k] :=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\displaystyle
\sum_{m=1}^{\kappa-1} \frac{1}{m!}
D^m g\left(Z^{(0,0)}_{t,v}\right) \circ Z_{t,v}^{\otimes m}
\circ \left(\tilde{\Delta}^m \boxtimes \mathrm{id}_{T^{<\lambda(W)}}\right)
[\xi_j,\eta_k],
& j>0,\ k=0, \\[2ex]
\displaystyle
\sum_{n=1}^{\lambda-1} \frac{1}{n!}
D^n g\left(Z^{(0,0)}_{t,v}\right) \circ Z_{t,v}^{\otimes n}
\circ \left(\mathrm{id}_{T^{<\kappa(V)}} \boxtimes \tilde{\Delta}^n\right)
[\xi_j,\eta_k],
& j=0,\ k>0, \\[2ex]
\displaystyle
\sum_{\ell=1}^{\lambda+\kappa-2} \frac{1}{\ell!}
D^\ell g\left(Z^{(0,0)}_{t,v}\right) \circ Z_{t,v}^{\otimes \ell}
\circ \widetilde{(\Delta \boxtimes \Delta)}^{\ell}
[\xi_j,\eta_k],
& j>0,\ k>0 .
\end{cases}
\]
Here, $\Delta$ denotes the shuffle coproduct, $\tilde{\Delta}$
denotes the restriction $\pi_{\geq 1} \circ \Delta$ and $\Delta^m$ denotes the $m$-fold iterate of $\Delta$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. observations with finite variance (Andrews states the result under moment conditions for the CLT)","the constraint is active at the true parameter (theta = 0); for theta > 0 the bootstrap is consistent"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T09:23:59.828365+00:00","domain":"resampling / constrained estimation","id":"claim_128317036fe4b38de221748567b9dd5e4b220bf4b14f749dabab4f8dd0bb0ff4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $X_1, \\dots, X_n$ be i.i.d. with mean $\\theta \\ge 0$ and variance $\\sigma^2$, and let the estimator respect the constraint: $\\hat\\theta_n = \\max(0, \\bar X_n)$. When the true parameter is interior ($\\theta > 0$) the nonparametric bootstrap is consistent: the conditional law of $\\sqrt n(\\hat\\theta_n^* - \\hat\\theta_n)$ converges to $N(0, \\sigma^2)$, the law of $\\sqrt n(\\hat\\theta_n - \\theta)$. When the true parameter is on the boundary ($\\theta = 0$) it is not: $\\sqrt n(\\hat\\theta_n - \\theta) \\Rightarrow \\max(0, Z)$ with $Z \\sim N(0, \\sigma^2)$, a law with an atom of mass $1/2$ at zero, whereas the bootstrap law of $\\sqrt n(\\hat\\theta_n^* - \\hat\\theta_n)$ converges, conditionally on the data, to the law of $\\max(0, Z + \\zeta) - \\max(0, \\zeta)$ with $\\zeta \\sim N(0, \\sigma^2)$ a random shift that does not vanish - so the bootstrap distribution is random in the limit and does not equal the sampling distribution (Andrews 2000, Theorem 1). The same failure holds for maximum-likelihood and least-squares estimators under inequality constraints whenever the true parameter has an active constraint, in particular for nonnegatively constrained regression and portfolio weights with coordinates at zero: the bootstrap replicates flip the constrained coordinates between zero and positive values, and the spread of the replicates is not the spread of the estimator. Consistent alternatives: the $m$-out-of-$n$ bootstrap with $m \\to \\infty$, $m/n \\to 0$, and subsampling, both of which recover the limit law at the boundary.","status":"unverified"}

T is ergodic if every T-invariant measurable set has measure 0 or 1: whenever A in Sigma satisfies T^{-1}A = A up to a mu-null set, mu(A) is 0 or 1. {"assumptions":["H is a finite bipartite graph with specified parts L and R","the network is layered s -> L -> R -> t, terminal capacities are 1, middle capacities are positive integers","the flow is integral"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T02:29:07.665547+00:00","domain":"finite bipartite graphs and their flow networks","id":"claim_129bed04f6bb1485d3e8c8182389b81f3a48db36763f86564b6ce5e5ab32147c","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let H = (L, R, E) be a finite bipartite graph and take the network with a source s, a sink t, arcs s->u of capacity 1 for u in L, arcs u->v for each edge uv, and arcs v->t of capacity 1 for v in R, the middle arcs carrying positive integer capacities. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:33:01.740854+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_12b24723aa93f050871e7949f914605cbec33b4efdc7c35f81ec8af464b9628e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] Let $\{ C_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be uniformly random elements of $[m]\coloneqq\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$, and let
$\{ U_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be uniformly random elements of $(0, 1)$.
Assume the family $\{ U_n, C_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is independent.
The random variable $C_n$ denotes the coupon type
obtained on day $n$.
Define the random variables
\[
  L(i, n) \coloneqq \sup\{ k \leqslant n \mid C_k = i \}, \quad i \in [m], \quad n > 0.
\]
Then $L(i, n)$ is the most recent day no later than $n$ that coupon
type $i$ was issued.
For clumsiness probability $p \in [0, 1)$, the 
clumsy coupon collection time can be defined by
\[
  T_{m, p} \coloneqq \inf \{ n > 0 \mid L(i, n) > 0 \ \text{and} \ U_{L(i, n)} \leq 1 - p \ 
    \text{for all $i \in [m]$} \},
\]
the first day that every coupon type has been updated, their most
recent updates all having been non-clumsy.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:10:07.530380+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_12cada61a0fe3477c1bfafbdeb2ef3132076cda06b26983b5dd3acb4db76c1c9","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition eq:residual-mixed-set of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[proposition]{prop:bulk-sparse-reduction}
Let \(V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be Borel measurable and bounded below, and let
\(0<r_N\le1\) and \(1\le k_N\le N\) be arbitrary deterministic
sequences.  Write
\[
 D_{N,r_N}
 =\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):\left\lVertx\right\rVert_\infty\le r_N\}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal A_N(k_N,\rho)
 =\left\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):
 \text{some \(S\subset[N]\), \(\left\lvertS\right\rvert\le k_N\), satisfies }
 \norm{x_{S^c}}_2\le\rho\right\}.
\]
For \(\rho>0\), define the residual mixed-profile set
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R_N(r_N,k_N,\rho)
 :=
 \left\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):
 \left\lVertx\right\rVert_\infty>r_N,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{S\subset[N]\\|S|\le k_N}}
 \norm{x_{S^c}}_2>\rho\right\}.
\end{equation}
Then the disjoint decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb S^{N-1}(1)
 =D_{N,r_N}\,\dot\cup\,
  \bigl(\mathcal A_N(k_N,\rho)\setminus D_{N,r_N}\bigr)
  \,\dot\cup\,\mathcal R_N(r_N,k_N,\rho)
\end{equation}
holds.  Suppose only that the exact bulk slice satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
 \log\mathscr C_N^J(V;D_{N,r_N})
 =:\Phi\in\mathbb R.
\end{equation}
No independence, moment matching, tail, density, or nondegeneracy
condition is needed for the decomposition itself.
For \(\rho>0\), set
\begin{align*}
 \mathscr S_N(\rho)
 &:=
 \mathscr C_N^J\bigl(
 V;\mathcal A_N(k_N,\rho)\setminus D_{N,r_N}\bigr),\\
 \mathscr R_N(\rho)
 &:=
 \mathscr C_N^J\bigl(
 V;\mathcal R_N(r_N,k_N,\rho)\bigr),
\end{align*}
and define
\begin{align}
 \overline\Phi_{\rm sp}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 &:=
 \lim_{\rho\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
 \frac1N\log\mathscr S_N(\rho),
 \\
 \overline\Phi_{\rm mix}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 &:=
 \lim_{\rho\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
 \frac1N\log\mathscr R_N(\rho).
 
\end{align}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathscr C_N^J(V)
 =
 \max\left\{
 \Phi,\,
 \overline\Phi_{\rm sp}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet),\,
 \overline\Phi_{\rm mix}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 \right\}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, exact universality holds if and only if both nonbulk
upper exponents are at most \(\Phi\).

If \(k_N=o(N)\), \(({\rm PT})_p\), and
(equation eq:critical-count-ceiling of the paper) also hold, then
\begin{equation}
 \overline\Phi_{\rm sp}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 \le\Xi_p^{\rm sp}(V).
\end{equation}
In particular, whenever the explicit sparse-rate compatibility condition
\begin{equation}
 \Xi_p^{\rm sp}(V)\le\Phi
\end{equation}
holds, exact universality is equivalent to the single residual condition
\begin{equation}
 \overline\Phi_{\rm mix}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 \le\Phi.
\end{equation}
When the disorder and \(V\) satisfy the hypotheses of
(thm:growing-point-cutoff of the paper), and
(equation eq:growing-Haar-zero-cost-condition of the paper) and
\(q_N^{\rm gr}\to0\) hold, that theorem supplies the corresponding
universal regularized bulk pressure.  Controlling its one-sided
de-regularization defects is one sufficient route to
(equation eq:exact-growing-bulk-slice of the paper), with
\(\Phi=\Phi_p^{\rm bulk}(V)\).","status":"unverified"}

\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:57:30.977815+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_12dde8600a7cd77087c4f47bf8b0a8c4c1cbc0690096feda3968f025a0dffa4f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 20 (\textsf{Exact four-moment counterexample}) of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Let $\eps_1, \eps_2, \eps_3$, $\eps_a$, $\eps_b$, $\eps_c$, and
$\eps_d$   be i.i.d. symmetric
Rademacher random variables. 
Define
\[
 Q_\triangle
 :=\eps_1\eps_2
 +\eps_1\eps_3
 +\eps_2\eps_3
 \AND
  Q_\square
 :=\eps_a\eps_b
 +\eps_b\eps_c
 +\eps_c\eps_d
 +\eps_d\eps_a.
\]
Take four independent copies of $Q_\triangle$ and three independent
copies of $Q_\square$, and set their independent sums to be
\noi
\begin{align}
 F:=\sum_{j=1}^4Q_{\triangle,j}
   +\sum_{j=1}^3Q_{\square,j}.
 \notag
\end{align}
Then, $F$ belongs to the second Rademacher chaos
and satisfies 

 
\noi
\begin{align}
 \frac{F+24}{2}\in\N_0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \E[(F+24)^k]=\E[P_{24}^k],
 \qquad 1\leq k\leq4,
  \notag
\end{align}
where $P_{24}\sim\Pois(24)$.  Moreover,

\noi
\begin{align}
 \dTV\bigl(\cL(F+24),\Pois(24)\bigr)
 \geq\frac{1-e^{-48}}2.
 \notag
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:45:05.414944+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_12f8694c347adefbcbc66df0eeb77a1945bae752dbb884acdf3a98d0cd7314b4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 135 (Backward-compatible continuation interface) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] A \emph{backward-compatible continuation interface} on the selected state
consists of the law family $\cP$ together with causal conditional response
operators $\mathcal E_{s,t}$ on a declared bounded operational class,
$0\le s\le t\le T$, such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(B\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item $\mathcal E_{s,t}$ is monotone, constant preserving and local at the
information available at time $s$;
\item the exact tower
\[
 \mathcal E_{r,s}\mathcal E_{s,t}=\mathcal E_{r,t},\qquad r\le s\le t,
\]
holds on the declared operational class and is compatible with deterministic
restart of the selected state;
\item under the usual right-continuous $P$-augmentation, every
$R$ in the declared response-supermartingale class is a square-integrable
continuous special semimartingale with normalized Doob--Meyer decomposition
\[
 R_t=R_0+M_t^{R,P}-K_t^{R,P},
 \qquad M_0^{R,P}=K_0^{R,P}=0.
\]
$K^{R,P}$ is predictable and nondecreasing.
\item for every declared $R$, the interface supplies a common upper-energy
class $Z^R\in\mathbb H_{\cP}^2$ such that
\[
 \pi_P\bigl(I(Z^R)\bigr)=M^{R,P}
 \qquad\text{in }\mathbb S^2(P),\qquad P\in\cP.
\]
Consequently the modelwise Galtchouk--Kunita--Watanabe component orthogonal to
the closed $X$-integral range vanishes, and $j_P(Z^R)$ is the modelwise GKW
energy class.  Whenever $R$ is supplied together with a declared first-jet
coordinate $Z$, compatibility of that declaration means $Z^R=Z$ in
$\mathbb H_{\cP}^2$.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses~\textup{(B1)}--\textup{(B2)} specify deterministic-time continuation
and restart compatibility, clause~\textup{(B3)} gives lawwise semimartingale
semantics, and clause~\textup{(B4)} supplies the common martingale channel.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.165902+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_130d0fcbcdcd0f683c879543b2a120aa210cf6d3b05371410eae4b6a1bca7cc8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Ppn 44 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any fixed $C_9$, and any fixed $\gamma \in [1/C_9,C_9]$, we have
    \[
        \sup \Big\{ V_\gamma(\by) :\|\by\|^2=N\Big\}
         \le g(\gamma) + \frac{\epsilon'}{20}\,.
    \]
with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$, where $c$ depends on $C_9$ and the parameters in Remark~\ref{r:fp-rpr}. 

\begin{proof}In this proof, we will set constants $\upsilon, \upsilon_1, \delta > 0$, where $\upsilon$ is sufficiently small depending on $C_9$, $\upsilon_1$ sufficiently small depending on $\upsilon,C_9$, and $\delta$ sufficiently small depending on $\upsilon_1,\upsilon,C_9$. That is,
\beq
    \delta \ll \upsilon_1 \ll \upsilon \ll \frac1{C_9}\,.
\eeq
Note that $C_9, \upsilon, \upsilon_1, \delta$ nonetheless depend on only the parameters in Remark~\ref{r:fp-rpr}.

Consider any local maximizer $\by$, and recall that $\dbA_\beta \equiv (\beta I_N-\dbD)^{-1}$.
By Lemma~\ref{l:fp-g-prep2}, $\by$ is of the form \eqref{e:fp-g-prep2-stationarity}, which we expand as
    \[
    \by
    =\dbA_\beta\bigg(\gamma^{1/2}\dbg
        +\sum_{j=1}^{r'}
        \frac{\hx_j}{M}(\tbmeta^j,\by)
        \tbmeta^j
        \bigg)
    =\dbA_\beta\sum_{j=0}^{r'} c_j \tbmeta^j\,.
    \]
For the last equality, we have defined $c_0\equiv \gamma^{1/2}$, $\tbmeta^0\equiv\dbg$, and 
    \[c_j\equiv \frac{\hx_j(\tbmeta^j, \by)}{M}\]
    for $1\le j\le r'$. With probability at least  $1-e^{-cN}$ (with $c$ an absolute constant), we have $\|\tbmeta^j\| \le 2\sqrt{N}$ for all $j \in 1[r']$, which implies 
        \[|c_j| \le \frac{2 |\hx_j|}{\alpha}
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:reduced-normalization}}{\le} \frac{4\alpha}{\iota}
        \]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.178381+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_131ae949172d86ae168b2e818eabd79a5838d7728d49005f103c10b7e9b9c37a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 84 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\acute{Y}$ be a continuous local martingale started from $\acute{Y}(0)=1$, and let $\theta$ be a stopping time with $\E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta<\infty$. If $\E [(|{{\acute{Y}}}_\theta|-1)^2] \le\epsilon$, then $\E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta \le 4\epsilon^{1/2}$.

\begin{proof}
The process
$\acute{M}(t)\equiv \acute{Y}^2(t)-\langle\acute{Y} \rangle_t$ is a continuous local martingale. It follows from e.g.\ \cite[Thm.~4.13]{MR3497465} that the stopped process $\acute{M}(t\wedge\theta)$ is a uniformly integrable true martingale, so the optional stopping theorem gives
    \[
    \E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta
    = \E\Big[ (\acute{Y}_\theta)^2-1\Big]\,.
    \]
Combining with Lemma~\ref{l:quadratic.ineq} and the hypothesis gives
    \[
    \E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta
    \le 2\epsilon^{1/2}
    + \frac{2\E[(|\acute{Y}_\theta|-1)^2]}{\epsilon^{1/2}}
    \le 4\epsilon^{1/2}\,,
    \]
as claimed.
\end{proof}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:39:12.432703+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_13279b84b29dd341ec4ea79e17486be448a9a1e1f755f1def7f857a636231449","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 3. dfn: effective resistance between sets of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Effective resistance between sets}]  
  Fix a resistance form $(\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{F})$ on $F$
  and write $R$ for the corresponding resistance metric.
  For sets $A, B \subseteq F$,
  we define
  \begin{equation}
    R(A,B)
    \coloneqq
    \left(
    \inf\{
    \mathcal{E}(f,f):
    f \in \mathcal{F},\
    f|_{A} \equiv 1,\
    f|_{B} \equiv 0
    \}
    \right)^{-1},
  \end{equation}
  which is defined to be zero if the infimum is taken over the empty set.
  Note that by (4. dfn cond: resistance forms condition 4 of the paper) 
  we clearly have $R( \{x\}, \{y\}) = R(x,y)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:26:17.750915+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_132da43bc91cf7eb9797b0900a3ac3ae5a6835c63beb20a2ab0734ae45ff71b5","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2511.02725, 'Mixing of general biased adjacent transposition chains'] Let $A=[i+1,n-j]$ and $A^c=[n]\setminus A = [i]\cup[n-j+1,n] $. 
    Let $\vell$ be $n$-admissible.
            For $b:A^c\to [n]$ that is $\vell$-localized, define the relabeling map $r_{b}:[n-i-j]\to [n]\bs b(A^c)$ as the unique strictly increasing (one-to-one) map between those sets.
    Given $\si:A\to [n]$ (such that $\si\opl b\in S_n$\footnote{$\si\opl b$ denotes the function that takes values $\si(x)$ when $x\in A$ and $b(x)$ when $x\in A^c$.}), define the restriction $R_{b}\si\in S_{n-i-j}$ by
    \[
R_b\si(x) = r_b^{-1}(\si(i+x)) \qquad \text{for $x\in [n-i-j]$}\,.
    \]
    Then the following hold.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item 
        (Labels preserved (up to translation) away from boundary)
        Let $\si\in S_n$ and $b=\si(A^c)$. Then 
        $r_{b}(k) = k+i$ for $k\in [1+\ell_{\max}^-, n-i-j-\ell_{\max}^+]$.
                \item 
        (Locality maintained)
        Let $\si\in S_n$. 
        $\si\in \vloc$ if and only if letting $b=\si(A^c)$, $b$ is $\vell$-localized and  
        $R_b\si\in \vell'\loc$, where $\vec{\ell}'=R_b\vell$ is defined by 
        \begin{align*}
        \ell_{k}^{\prime-} &= 
                \min\{\ell_{r_b(k)}^- +k+i - r_b(k), k-1\}
        \\ 
        \ell_{k}^{\prime+} &=
        \min\{\ell_{r_b(k)}^+ + r_b(k)-k-i, n-i-j-k\}
        .
        \end{align*}
        Moreover, 
        $\vell'$ is $n-i-j$-admissible with $\ell_{\max}^{\prime\pm}\le \ell_{\max}^{\pm}$, respectively.
        \item (Measure on restriction)
        Let $\mu$ be the probability measure on $S_n$ given by $p_{k,k'}$, and let $\mu_{|b}$ be the measure conditioned on $\set{\si\in S_n}{\si({A^c})=b}$. 
        Then $(R_b)_* \mu_{|b}$\footnote{We use the notation $f_*\mu$ to denote the pushforward of the measure $\mu$ by the function $f$.} is the probability measure on $S_{n-i-j}$ given by~\eqref{eq:stationary-distribution} with $\vec{q}$ given by $q_{k,k'} = p_{r_b(k),r_b(k')}$. If $\vec{p}$ satisfies $\ep$-positive bias, then $\vec{q}$ satisfies $\ep$-positive bias. 
            \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:47.658524+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_135d76fe090d841832a9d1ccd3f68ba7e306916f708faaae3d0d4db304d2c130","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 (Control and $\omega$-$p$-variation) of arXiv:2605.08844, 'Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential '] A control on $[a,b]$ is a continuous, super-additive map
$\omega:\Delta_{[a,b]}\to[0,\infty)$ vanishing on the diagonal.

Given $p\ge 1$ and $f:\Delta_{[a,b]}\to F$ set
\[
\|f\|_{p,\omega}
:=
\inf\Big\{C>0:\ \|f_{s,t}\|_F\le C\,\omega(s,t)^{1/p}
\ \text{for all }(s,t)\in\Delta_{[a,b]}\Big\},
\]
with the convention $\inf\varnothing=\infty$, and define
\[
C_\omega^p(\Delta_{[a,b]},F)
:=
\{f:\Delta_{[a,b]}\to F:\ \|f\|_{p,\omega}<\infty\}.
\]

For a path $g:[a,b]\to F$, we write $g\in C_\omega^p([a,b],F)$ if its increment map
\(
(s,t)\mapsto g_{s,t}
\)
belongs to $C_\omega^p(\Delta_{[a,b]},F)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:48:24.296466+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1385f546816d7b24554a5fa481bfafe95d74b0d238d9843baffed62269a94a4a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem q>1 of arXiv:2605.10452, 'A secretary for Messrs. Luce and Mallows'] Consider the secretary problem for a Mallows distribution with $q=q_n>1$ in the case that the largest number is  of highest rank.

\noindent i. Let $q_n=1+\frac cn$, where $c>0$. Then the asymptotically optimal strategy is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
\begin{equation}
M_n^*\sim n\Big(\frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{1-e^{-c}}{e-1+e^{-c}}\big)\Big),
\end{equation}
 and the corresponding  limiting probability of success
is $\frac1e$:
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q_n}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$
Also, $\lim_{c\to\infty} \frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{1-e^{-c}}{e-1+e^{-c}}\big)=0$ and $\lim_{c\to0} \frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{1-e^{-c}}{e-1+e^{-c}}\big)=\frac1e$.

\noindent ii.
Let $q_n=1+\frac c{n^\alpha}$, where $c>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Then the asymptotically optimal strategy  is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
$$
M_n^*\sim\frac1c\left(1-\log(e-1)\right)n^\alpha\approx0.459\frac{n^\alpha}c,
$$
 and the corresponding limiting probability of success
is $\frac1e$:
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q_n}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$
\noindent iii. Let $q>1$.  Then the asymptotically optimal strategy  is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M^*)$, where
$$
M^*=\begin{cases}&\max\left\{M\ge1: \sum_{j=M}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}\ge\frac q{q-1}\right\}, \ \text{if}\ \sum_{j=1}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}\ge \frac q{q-1};\\
&0,\ \text{if}\ \sum_{j=1}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}<\frac q{q-1}.\end{cases}
$$
(If  $\sum_{j=M^*}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}=\frac q{q-1}$, then $M^*-1$ is also optimal.)

\noindent The corresponding limiting probability of success is given by
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q}(\mathcal{S}^\downarrow(n,M^*))=\begin{cases}&\frac{q-1}q(1-q^{-M^*})\sum_{j=M^*}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}\ge\\
&(1-q^{-M^*}),\ \text{if}\ M^*\ge1;\\
&\frac{q-1}q>,\ \text{if}\ M^*=0.\end{cases}
\end{equation}
The limiting probability in (equation SuccessProbup of the paper) is always greater or equal to $\frac1e$ and is strictly greater than $\frac1e$ for all but at most a countable number of $q$ with no accumulation points in $(0,\infty)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:48:45.323301+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_13bc000e6b45d98e783a33edd9380fc69e016f142640c420c1076f7c9720307a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary c:PpaisoPolish of arXiv:2411.14936, 'Massive Particle Systems,\\Wasserstein Brownian Motions,\\ and the Dean--Kawasaki Equation'] $(\msP^\pa_\iso,\tau_\mrma)$ is a Polish space.
\begin{proof}
Since~$(M,\tau)$ is Polish by assumption (cf.~\S(ss:Rescaling of the paper)), its countable product~$(\mbfM,\tau_\mrmp)$ is Polish as well.
The space~$(\mbfT,\tau_\mrmp)$ too is Polish since it is a closed subset of the infinite cube~$\mbfI$.
In light of the above lemma, it suffices to show that~$(\widehat\mbfM_\circ,\widehat\tau_\mrmp)$ is a Polish space.
In turn, since the product of two Polish spaces is Polish, the conclusion follows if we show that~$(\mbfM_\circ,\tau_\mrmp)$ and~$(\mbfT_\circ,\tau_\mrmp)$ are both Polish.
Since they are clearly~$G_\delta$ sets in~$\mbfM$ and~$\mbfT$ respectively, the fact that they are Polish follows from the latter spaces being Polish, by Alexandrov's Theorem, e.g.~[Kec95].

{"assumptions":["d-regular graphs on n vertices; tau_2 = the relaxation time (inverse spectral gap) of the natural random walk, maximised over all d-regular graphs on n vertices for fixed n","the d=3 (cubic) enumerations used are COMPLETE for n<=12 (counts 1,2,5,19,85 match the known sequence); the d>=4 enumerations are RANDOM SAMPLES (isomorphism-deduplicated, stopped after 4000 consecutive repeats) and are NOT certified complete, especially at n=12"],"created_at":"2026-09-24T23:46:59.998009+00:00","domain":"probability/Markov chains","id":"claim_13c3a894a23e44b0acdc4d79135f18d9","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"The paper proving the Aldous-Fill spectral gap conjecture leaves conditional the claim that for every sufficiently large even order n, the slowest d-regular graph (maximising relaxation time tau_2) is cubic (d=3); the finite crossover point is n=8. The 2-regular cycle has tau_2 = 1/(1-cos(2 pi/n)) ~ n^2/(2 pi^2), one third of the cubic asymptotic 3n^2/(2 pi^2), so cubic graphs must eventually overtake the cycle but do not lead at first: the slowest-known regular graph by order is 2-regular (the cycle) at n=4 (tau_2=1.0000) and n=6 (2.0000), then becomes 3-regular at n=8 (3.9271, versus the cycle's 3.4142), n=10 (13.5414, cycle 5.2361), and n=12 (17.8846, cycle 7.4641). Separately, the extremal cubic maxima (0.75, 1.50, 3.93, 13.54, 17.88 for n=4,6,8,10,12) jump by a factor of 3.5 from n=8 to n=10, out of line with the surrounding steps; this is because the extremal cubic graph acquires a BRIDGE at n=10 and CANNOT do so at any earlier order. Proof that a bridged cubic graph needs n>=10: if a cubic graph has a bridge uv, deleting it leaves a component A containing u where every vertex has degree 3 except u (degree 2), so the degree sum 3|A|-1 must be even, forcing |A| odd; |A|=1 would need a loop and |A|=3 would need four edges among three vertices (both impossible for a simple cubic graph), so both sides of any bridge are odd and at least 5, giving n>=10. This matches exact enumeration: no bridged cubic graph exists at n=4, 6, or 8; at n=10 there is exactly one bridged cubic graph and it IS the extremal one (tau_2=13.5414, versus 6.8423 for the best bridgeless cubic graph on 10 vertices); at n=12 there are four bridged cubic graphs and the extremal one among them is a 5|7 split (17.8846, versus 10.3190 for the best bridgeless cubic graph), a 6|6 split being impossible by the same parity argument. So the crossover at n=8 (cubic first overtakes the cycle, still bridgeless there, via a narrow 2-edge 4|4 cut) and the jump at n=10 (the bridge becomes possible) are two DIFFERENT events. NOT CERTIFIED: whether any regular graph of degree d>=4 ever competes with the cubic extremal graphs at these orders - only suggested: a 4-regular graph would need a second eigenvalue of 0.944 to compete, and the best 4-regular graph seen has 0.890; and a parity fact (a d-regular graph has a cut of size c across a vertex subset A only if c = d|A| mod 2, checked on 8400 random cuts with zero violations) shows a bridge is impossible outright for any EVEN degree d, which is suggestive but not a proof that odd degrees d>=5 cannot compete either.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:30:36.767363+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_13d24f2d223b8ec4a2b83478bf5e28a469964840c9d34d6c23849f0754743ff0","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2607.10102, 'Dynamical mean-field limit and replica-symmetric free energy for the orthogonally-invarian'] Suppose the conditions of Theorem \ref{thm:replica} hold.
Fix any sufficiently large $T_0,T>0$ and sufficiently small $\eps>0$.
Let $(\tilde c_g,\tilde r_g) \equiv (\tilde c_g^m,\tilde r_g^m)$ be
the kernels of Corollary \ref{cor:semigroupapprox} for this $\eps$. Let
$\{\tilde g^t\}_{t \in \R},\{\tilde b^t\}_{t \geq T_0},z$
be mutually independent such that
$\{\tilde g^t\}_{t \in \R} \sim \GP(0,\tilde c_g)$,
$\{\tilde b^t\}_{t \geq T_0}$ is a standard Brownian motion with $\tilde b^{T_0}=0$, and $z \sim \cN(0,q_*\cR_\Lambda'(v_*-q_*))$.

Then there is a coupling of
$(\{\tilde g^t\}_{t \in \R},\{\tilde b^t\}_{t \geq T_0},z)$
with the process $\{\theta^t\}_{t \geq 0}$ in \eqref{eq:dmft-theta} of
Definition \ref{def:DMFT} such that the following holds: Define the process
$\{\tilde \theta^t\}_{t \geq 0}$ by
\begin{align*}
\tilde\theta^t&=\theta^t \text{ for all } t \in [0,T_0],\\
\d\tilde \theta^t&=
\left[-U'(\tilde \theta^t)+\int_0^t \tilde r_g(t-s)
\tilde \theta^s ds+\tilde g^t+z\right]
\d t+\sqrt{2}\,\d \tilde b^t \text{ for } t \geq T_0.
\end{align*}
Then for some constants $C,c>0$ not depending on $T_0,T,\eps$,
\begin{equation}
\sup_{t \geq 0} \E(\theta^t)^4<C,
\qquad \sup_{t \geq 0} \E(\tilde \theta^t)^4<C,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\sup_{t \in [T_0,T_0+T]} \E(\tilde \theta^t-\theta^t)^2
<C(\eps+T^{1/4}e^{-cT_0})^{2/3}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["S is a finite subset of R^d","for the final claim: N <= d and x_1,...,x_N are linearly independent"],"created_at":"2026-08-20T03:43:30.215738+00:00","domain":"convex geometry","id":"claim_13f960d12d7361f53f8b9649a3a09792dc53550f7d06e91b0c0b658011ff3912","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $S=\\{x_1,\\dots,x_N\\}$ be a finite subset of $\\mathbb{R}^d$. The following are equivalent: (i) there is $y$ with $\\langle y,x_i\\rangle>0$ for every $i$; (ii) $0 \\notin \\operatorname{conv}(S)$. The frequently attempted substitute is FALSE: the condition that $\\operatorname{conv}(S)$ have empty interior does NOT imply (i). Counterexample in $\\mathbb{R}^2$ with $N=2$: take $x_1=e_1$ and $x_2=-e_1$. Their convex hull is a segment, which has empty interior, yet $0$ lies in it and no $y$ satisfies both inequalities. In particular, the observation that $N$ points in $\\mathbb{R}^N$ span an affine hull of dimension at most $N-1$, and so have a hull with empty interior, proves nothing about separation. What does suffice is linear independence: if $N \\le d$ and $x_1,\\dots,x_N$ are linearly independent then (i) holds, and an explicit witness solves $\\langle y,x_i\\rangle = 1$ for every $i$.","status":"unverified"}

Burdzy-Scheutzow (2014), Problem 7.5 asks whether a process with law equivalent to Wiener measure can receive a random finite prefix to become Brownian motion. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:27:56.773082+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1447ac7edeb187e1982ff160bc578d85fb9b1cf07f7630c9907d6544d4217793","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (The \JKL{} formulation of Einstein areal flows) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Consider four-dimensional spacetimes $(\Mcal,\guntrois)$ with spatial topology $\Tbb^3$ and two commuting spacelike Killing fields with closed orbits, admitting a foliation by the area~$|t|$ of the symmetry orbits. Consider a constitutive law $p=p(\mu)$ (pressure vs.\ mass-energy density) satisfying hyperbolicity and asymptotic conditions (stated in~\eqref{hyperbolic-eos-zero}, below). Then the following properties hold.
\bei

\item \textbf{Perfect-fluid matter model.} In the class of regular flows, the Einstein--Euler system 
\bel{equa-49F}
G^{\alpha\beta} = T^{\alpha\beta},
\qquad
\nabla_\alpha T^{\alpha\beta}=0
\ee
is equivalent to an \emph{evolution--constraint, first-order differential system} in terms of the variables \eqref{equa-phipsi}, as  given in \eqref{eq:T2-1234-def}--\eqref{equa-9385}, below, and referred to as the \JKL{} system. Its evolution subsystem has essentially \emph{quadratic nonlinearities} with a partial \emph{null structure} and, away from vacuum, is strongly hyperbolic.   All differential operators in the formulation 
remain defined on the full (closed) state space, including cavitation and near-light speed fluid propagation, although the hyperbolicity degenerates at non-zero null states.  

\item \textbf{Particle-production dissipative model.} Analogous properties hold for the following class of Einstein--Navier--Stokes systems
\bel{eq:pot-production-system0}
G^{\alpha\beta}=T_\chi^{\alpha\beta},
\qquad
\nabla_\alpha T_\chi^{\alpha\beta}=0,
\qquad
\nabla_\alpha A_\chi^{\alpha\beta\gamma}
=-\mathscr B^{\beta\gamma}, 
\ee
namely an extension of the Einstein--Euler system by adjoining to the fluid variables a symmetric two-tensor relaxation field~$\zeta$. The tensors $T_\chi$ and $A_\chi$ are defined from second-order derivatives
of a \emph{Navier--Stokes potential} denoted by~$\chi$, which is assumed to satisfy suitable equilibrium, dominant-energy, and causal-hyperbolicity conditions in \autoref{def-pot-hyperbolic}. The relaxation rate tensor~$\mathscr B$ is prescribed and satisfies suitable stable-equilibrium and positivity conditions in \autoref{def-pot-source}. In particular, the coupled evolution equations are symmetric hyperbolic in the interior of the state space, and both Einstein equations and Bianchi equations are satisfied.  The associated particle-number current~$\vNumb_\chi$ satisfies $\nabla_\alpha \vNumb_\chi^\alpha = \zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}\geq 0$.

\item \textbf{Dissipated-energy dissipative model.} 
Analogous properties also hold for the following class of Einstein--Navier--Stokes systems
\bel{eq:pot-dissipated-system0}
\begin{aligned}
G^{\alpha\beta}
&=T_\chi^{\alpha\beta}+T_{\rm aux}^{\alpha\beta}, \quad
&
\nabla_\alpha T_\chi^{\alpha\beta}
&=-\sigma n^\beta, \quad
&
\nabla_\alpha A_\chi^{\alpha\beta\gamma}
&=-\mathscr B^{\beta\gamma},
\end{aligned}
\ee 
with 
\be
\begin{aligned}
T_{\rm aux}^{\alpha\beta}
&=\sigma \underline\pi^{\alpha\beta},
&
\sigma & \coloneqq \frac{\zeta_{\alpha\beta} \mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}}{-n_\alpha\beta^\alpha} \geq 0. 
\end{aligned}
\ee 
Here $\underline\pi^{\alpha\beta}$ is the (rescaled) projection onto the symmetry orbits, $n_\alpha$ is the future-directed normal to the areal foliation, and $\beta$ is the rescaled fluid momentum.
The model includes an auxiliary stress tensor~$T_{\rm aux}$ (\autoref{def-diss-en}), which compensates the mass-energy dissipated by~$T_\chi$. In particular, the coupled evolution equations are symmetric hyperbolic in the interior of the state space, and both Einstein equations and Bianchi equations are satisfied.
The associated particle-number current~$\vNumb_\chi$ is divergence-free.
\eei
\noindent For all three systems, the Einstein constraints propagate from one areal hypersurface, and the metric variables are reconstructed from the transport, constraint, and periodicity equations. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:10:05.811459+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1462b8573927d96c3abdc0fc68aaa22bdd65445bc1765e17ae60ad6e20faa327","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 27 (Widom {\cite[Theorem~3) of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] {Widom1982}}]

Let \(\sigma\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})\), and let \(W_L(\sigma)\) be the truncated Wiener--Hopf operator on \(L^2(0,L)\). Suppose that there exists a bounded determination \(\psi\) of \(\log\sigma\) whose inverse Fourier transform \(\check{\psi}\) satisfies
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}}|x|\,|\check{\psi}(x)|^2\,\mathrm{d}x<\infty.
\]
Then \(W_L(\sigma)\exp(-W_L(\psi))\) is of determinant class, and
\[
\det\bigl(W_L(\sigma)\exp(-W_L(\psi))\bigr)
\to
\exp\left(
\int_0^{\infty}x\check{\psi}(x)\check{\psi}(-x)\,\mathrm{d}x
\right)
\]
as \(L\to\infty\). If, in addition, \(\psi\in L^1(\mathbb{R})\), then
\[
\det W_L(\sigma)

\right)
\to
\exp\left(
\int_0^{\infty}x\check{\psi}(x)\check{\psi}(-x)\,\mathrm{d}x
\right),
\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:04:59.433586+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1463d037402008beca2be5c9f6f935be95dc80b0c5c4e7d5d348d243c016c4d8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:raw-velocity-decay of arXiv:2605.20697, 'Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for \\ Second-Order Consensus-Based Optimization'] Under the assumptions of (thm:exp-decay-centered-moments of the paper) for \(p\geqslant 2\), 
    assume in addition that \(\mathbf{E}|V_0^j|^p<\infty\).

    Then there exists a constant \(C_V>0\) such that, for all \(t\geqslant 0\),
    \[
        \mathbf{E}|V_t^j|^p
        \leqslant
        \begin{cases}
            C_V \e^{-\lambda_{p} t},
            & \text{if } \lambda_{p} < \eta_p, \\[0.4em]
            C_V(1+t)\e^{-\eta_p t},

    \]

    \[

        \min\left\{\lambda_{p},\frac{p\gamma}{2m}\right\}.
    \]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:30.021103+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1487be506026583512ad9cff1734a471905cad89116737eaeff491ee3b251e1c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 19 of arXiv:2605.06556, 'Probability of Quota Violations in Divisor Apportionment Methods with Nonzero Allocations'] (Asymptotic Quota Stabilization) Let $\bm\tau$ be a nonexceptional parameter vector for which Theorem~\ref{lim_1_nstates} holds. Then there exists $x_{\bm{\tau}}$ such that for all $x\ge x_{\bm\tau}$

$$
A(1,x,y_1(x,\tau_1),\dots,y_{n-2}(x,\tau_{n-2}))
= \tilde A_1(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n).
$$

Consequently the quota behavior stabilizes: for sufficiently large $x$, the apportionment is always either quota compliant, a quota violation caused by nonzero allocation, a quota violation worsened by nonzero allocation, or an upper quota violation. Moreover, this behavior depends only on $\bm{\tau}$. If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)=(\tilde a_2,\dots,\tilde a_n)$ is the apportionment of $M$ seats among states $2,\dots,n$ and state $i$ receive the last seat then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)$ is not a quota violation and $\tilde a_i=\lfloor\tilde q_i\rfloor$, then the asymptotic apportionment is a quota violation caused by nonzero allocation.
\item If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)$ is not a quota violation and $\tilde a_i=\lceil\tilde q_i\rceil$, then the asymptotic apportionment is not a quota violation.
\item If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)$ is an upper quota violation where state $i$ is the only state assigned more than its upper quota and $\tilde{a}_i = \lceil\tilde q_i\rceil +1$, then the asymptotic apportionment is not a quota violation.
\item If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)$ is an upper quota violation and case (3) does not apply, then the asymptotic apportionment is an upper quota violation.
\item If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)$ is a lower quota violation, then the asymptotic apportionment is a quota violation worsened by nonzero allocation.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:12:13.423548+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_14bb85308e22a638539c8f646770d358f7cfd504e96a7286f3ca74115b032c30","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 101 of arXiv:2608.28200, '\textbf On the Formality of Configuration Spaces of $\aka$'] An $(n',n)$-vertex algebra consists of the data $(V, Y, \TT, \VAvacuum)$ with
\begin{itemize}
\item (space of states) a $\Z$-graded $\C$-vector space $V=\oplus_{r\in \Z} V^r$.
\item (vacuum vector) a degree $0$ element $\VAvacuum\in V^0$.
\item (translation operator) a vector $\TT=(T_1,\cdots,T_n)$, where $T_i\in \End V$ are degree $0$ endomorphisms of $V$. 
\item (vertex operators) a degree $0$ $\C$-linear map 
\ali{
Y: V &\lra \Kdisk \otimes \End V \\
   a &\lmt Y(a,\zz) = \sum_{\kk \ge \bs{0}} \zz^{\kk} a_{(-\bs{1}-\kk)} + \Omegaz^\kk a_{(\kk)} 
}
which assigns a field $Y(a,\zz)$ to $a$. 

The condition that $Y(a,\zz)$ is a field means that for every $v\in V$, there exists a vector $\jj \ge \bs0$ such that $a_{(\kk)}v=0$ whenever $\kk>\jj$. 
$Y$ has degree $0$  means 
$$
\deg a_{(-\bs{1}-\kk)}=\deg a, \qquad \deg a_{(\kk)} = \deg a -(n'+n-1).
$$
\end{itemize}
The data must satisfy the following axioms:
\begin{itemize}
\item (vacuum axiom) $Y(\VAvacuum,\zz) = \Id_V$. Furthermore, for any $a\in V$ we have 
$$
Y(a,\zz) \VAvacuum \in \C[[z^1,\cdots,z^n]] \otimes V,
$$
and 
$$
Y(a,\zz) \VAvacuum |_{\zz=0}= a.
$$
\item (translation axiom) For any $a\in V$, 
$$
[T_i,Y(a,\zz)] = \partial_{z^i} Y(a,\zz),
$$
and for every $i$, we have
$$T_i \VAvacuum =0.
$$
\item (locality axiom) All fields $Y(a,\zz)$ are mutually local in the sense of \cites{Cohomological-VA}. 
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.165090+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_14c12419e48d441dc5aa5a7d5a0e080939ec89667ae7347c2f8743f09e0c5653","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 38 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] There exists a constant $C_8=C_8(\alpha,\iota)$ such that the following holds with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$ over $\dot{\bg}_+, \hat{\bg}_+$, where $c$ is an absolute constant. 
    For any $\|\by\|^2=N$, the function
    \[
        \btheta_+ \mapsto
        \frac{2(\hbg_+,\btheta_+)}{M}
        + \frac{2\|\btheta_+\|(\dbg_+,\by)}{M\sqrt{N}}
        - \frac{((\hbD_+)^{-1} \btheta_+, \btheta_+)}{M}
    \]
    attains its supremum over $\R^{B_+}$ at some $\btheta_+$ satisfying
    $\|\btheta_+\| \le C_8N^{1/2}$.
    (We take the assertion to be vacuously true if $B_+ = \emptyset$.)

\begin{proof}
    Since the function tends to $-\infty$ as $\|\btheta_+\| \to +\infty$, the supremum is attained at a local maximizer $\btheta_+$.
    The function is differentiable everywhere except possibly at $\btheta_+=\bzero$, so the only possible local maximizer are $\btheta_+=\bzero$ and stationary points $\btheta_+$. 
    The stationarity condition gives
    \[
      \btheta_+
     =\hbD_+\bigg(   \hbg_+
        + \frac{(\dbg_+,\by) \btheta_+}{N^{1/2} \|\btheta_+\|}
        \bigg) \,.
    \]
With probability $1-e^{-cN}$, we have $\|\hbg_+\| \le 2 M^{1/2}$, $\|\dbg_+\| \le 2 N^{1/2}$, and consequently $|(\dbg_+,\by)| \le 2N$. Since the operator norm of $\hbD_+$ is at most $\hv_1$, it follows that any stationary point $\btheta_+$ must satisfy
    \[
        \|\btheta_+\|
        \le\hv_1 \bigg(
            \|\hbg_+\|
            + \bigg|
            \frac{(\dbg_+,\by) }{N^{1/2} }
            \bigg|
        \bigg)
        \le
        2\hv_1\Big( M^{1/2} + N^{1/2}
         \Big)
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:reduced-normalization}}{\le}
        \frac{4(\alpha^{1/2}+1)}{\iota} N^{1/2}\,.
    \]
This proves the claim.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:06:18.036932+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1502859edd23c606034c4c629462768805a76a0f98526e9b71543466e5051ab9","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 18 ($\Sigma$ is a reflective submanifold) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] \begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] $R_L$ restricts to an isometric involution of
$S^{m-1}(2)$ whose fixed-point set is exactly
$L\cap S^{m-1}(2)$; thus $\Phi(\Sigma)$ is a \emph{reflective
submanifold} of the round sphere.
\item[\textup{(ii)}] The map
$\iota:=\Phi^{-1}\circ R_L\circ\Phi$ is defined on the open set
\[
U=\bigl\{\pi\in\Delta^\circ_{m-1}:\
2P_L\sqrt\pi-\sqrt\pi>0\ \text{componentwise}\bigr\},
\]
an open neighbourhood of $\Sigma^\circ$, on which
it is an involutive isometry of the Fisher--Rao metric with
$\operatorname{Fix}(\iota)=\Sigma\cap U$.
\item[\textup{(iii)}] $R_L$ reverses every transverse functional:
writing $\ell_O(x)=\kappa(z)^{1/4}x_z-\kappa(\sigma(z))^{1/4}
x_{\sigma(z)}$ for the linear form cutting out the orbit
hyperplane,
\[
\ell_O(R_Lx)=-\ell_O(x)\qquad\text{for every orbit }O.
\]
In particular the differential of $\iota$ along $\Sigma$ is $+1$
on $T\Sigma$ and $-1$ on the normal bundle, and for $r=1$ the
reflection exchanges the two connected components of
$S^{m-1}(2)\setminus\bigl(L\cap S^{m-1}(2)\bigr)$ --- a statement
about the \emph{full} sphere. Nothing is claimed about the number of
components of $S^{m-1}_+(2)\setminus\Phi(\Sigma^\circ)$: the octant
is not $R_L$-invariant, as Remark~\ref{rem:iota-domain} records. On
the octant one has only that, wherever both sides meet the domain,
the two sides are the sign regions of the orbit functional
$\ell_O$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:17:42.300829+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_150695aae1416938622114b2c4a679692c1815cb8ead848472a4025947266e99","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 6 (Main result in spatial dimension $d=1$) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Let $\{K_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ denote an environment satisfying Assumption \ref{a1}, and let $\mathfrak H^N$ be as in \eqref{hn}. There is an explicit Banach space $X$ of distributions on $\mathbb R$, which is continuously embedded in $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R)$, such that the rescaled and recentered collection $\{ \mathfrak F^N\}_{N \ge 1}$ is tight with respect to the topology of $C([0,T], X)$. Furthermore any limit point as $N\to \infty$ is as follows. 
\begin{itemize} 
\item (Bulk fluctuations in $d=1$) If $N^{1/2}\varsigma_N \to \boldsymbol{\varsigma} \text{ as } N\to\infty$, then the limit point is unique and coincides with the law of $(t,x)\mapsto e^{\varsigma\bullet x +\frac12 |\varsigma|^2 t} \mathcal U(t,x+\varsigma t)$ where $\mathcal U$ is the solution of the additive-noise SPDE \begin{equation}\partial_t \mathcal U(t, x) = \frac12\partial_x^2 \mathcal U(t, x) + \gamma_{\mathrm{ext}}\cdot \partial_x^p \big((\mathfrak H_0 *G_t)(x)\;\xi(t, x)\big),
\end{equation}started with initial data $\mathcal U(0, x)=0$. 

\item (Extremal fluctuations up to location scale $N^{1-\frac1{4p}}$ in $d=1$) If $N^{-1/2}\ll  |\varsigma_N|\ll  N^{-1/4p} \text{ as } N\to \infty,$ then the limit point is unique and coincides with the law of the solution of the additive-noise SPDE \begin{equation}\partial_t \mathcal U(t, x) = \frac12\partial_x^2  \mathcal U(t, x) + \gamma_{\mathrm{ext}}\cdot   (\mathfrak H_0 *G_t)(x)\; \xi(t, x),
\end{equation}started with initial data $\mathcal U(0, x)=0$. 
\end{itemize} Here $G_t(x) = G(t,x)= (2\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2t}$ is the standard heat kernel, $*$ denotes spatial convolution, and $ \xi$ is a standard space-time white noise defined on $\mathbb R_+\times \mathbb R.$ Furthermore in either case we have the noise coefficient $$\gamma_{\mathrm{ext}}^2:=  \frac1{(2p)!}\int_{I} \bigg[ \int_{I^2}( x- y)^{2p}\mu(\mathrm d x)\mu(\mathrm d y)-\int_I ( a- z)^{2p} \pdif( z,\mathrm d a)\bigg]
\pi^{\mathrm{inv}}(\mathrm d z).

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:45:05.471965+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_15126f178600d332706e30e01df7115827c94b0bad41e7b5ee9bc3b33e40bf8e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 157 (Hilbertian response differential) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Suppose a linear tangent block is generated by a real vector space $V$ with a
positive semidefinite bilinear form $g_z$.  Let
\[
 N_z:=\{v:g_z(v,v)=0\},\qquad
 \mathscr H_z:=\overline{V/N_z}^{\,\|\cdot\|_{g_z}},\qquad
 \|[v]\|_{g_z}^2=g_z(v,v).
\]
If a scalar linear cotangent response $\lambda_z$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 |\lambda_z(v)|\le C_z\|[v]\|_{g_z},
\end{equation}
then there is a unique $\nabla_g^{\rm resp}F(z)\in\mathscr H_z$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_z(v)
 =\langle\nabla_g^{\rm resp}F(z),[v]\rangle_{\mathscr H_z}.
\end{equation}
Thus $\lambda_z$ is the cotangent datum, whereas
$\nabla_g^{\rm resp}F(z)$ is its Riesz representative relative to $g_z$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:43:16.147899+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_152e9d0887a2f78df9360571f2c0f23619c3d18a8967063893b64c203888da26","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lema 4 ({\cite[Lemma~3.2) of arXiv:2604.13387, 'Multiradial Schramm-Loewner evolution: \\ Infinite-time large deviations and transience'] {Healey-Lawler:N_sided_radial_SLE}}] 

Let $g_t \colon \bD \smallsetminus \bgamma[0,t] \to \bD$ be the Loewner chain of $\bgamma \in \commonpaths[T]$, and denote by 
$g_t^j \colon \bD \smallsetminus \gamma^j[0,t] \to \bD$ the mapping-out function of each $\gamma^j[0, t]$. 
Then, $g_{t, j} := g_t \circ (g^j_t)^{-1} \colon \bD \smallsetminus \hat{K}^j_t \to \bD$, 
where $\hat{K}^j_t := g^j_t \big(\bigcup_{i \neq j} \gamma^i[0,t]\big)$,
is a conformal bijection such that $g_{t, j}(0)=0$ and $g_{t, j}'(0)>0$.
Write $g^j_t(\gamma^j(t)) = \exp({\ii \xi^j_t})$, and $g_{t, j}(e^{\ii z}) =: e^{\ii h_{t, j}(z)}$ 
Then, we have
\begin{align}
\partial_t \indeptime_\bgamma^j(t) = \frac{1}{\big( h'_{t, j}(\xi^j_t) \big)^{2} }, \qquad  j \in \{1,\ldots,n\} , \; t \in [0,T] .
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:15:34.382632+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_152f9442b41c3e62365b779600bd288e06091404d967ae50cd4d9aa2bf8311c2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 6 (Theorem A in \cite{GSZ2025}) of arXiv:2609.03243, 'Weighted Ces\`aro type operators on the weighted Bergman spaces in the unit ball'] Let $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ be two positive measures on the space $X$ and let $K(x,y)$ be a nonnegative measurable function on $X\times X$. Let $T$ be the integral operator defined with kernel $K$ as follows:
\[
    Tf(x)=\int_{X}K(x,y)f(y){\rm d}\mu_1(y).
\]
Suppose $1<p\leq q<\infty$ and $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{p'}=1$. Let $\gamma_1, \gamma_2>0$ with $\gamma_1+\gamma_2=1$. Assume that there exist two positive functions $h_1, h_2$ and positive constants $C_1, C_2$ such that
\[
    \int_{X}h_1(y)^{p'}K(x,y)^{\gamma_1 p'}{\rm d}\mu_1(y)\leq C_1h_2(x)^{p'}
\]
for almost all $x\in X$, and 
\[
    \int_{X}h_2(x)^qK(x,y)^{\gamma_2 q}{\rm d}\mu_2(x)\leq C_2h_1(y)^q
\]
for almost all $y\in X$. Then the operator $T: L^p(X,{\rm d}\mu_1)\to L^q(X, {\rm d}\mu_2)$ is bounded. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["sub-Gaussian increments with respect to the metric d","separability of the process, so that the supremum is measurable and the chaining series converges","convergence of the entropy integral"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.628694+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_15319d42d2a2e77a7eb628a9a06e56b61b321dba9d4e5dfffbd869a984b61dbb","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X_t)_{t in T} be a stochastic process on a metric space (T, d) with SUB-GAUSSIAN INCREMENTS, meaning P( |X_s - X_t| > u ) <= 2 exp( - u^2 / (2 d(s,t)^2) ) for all s, t and u > 0. Then there is an absolute constant C with E sup_{t in T} X_t <= C integral_0^{diam(T)} sqrt( log N(T, d, u) ) du, where N(T, d, u) is the covering number, the smallest number of d-balls of radius u needed to cover T. If the process is not centred one should read the statement for X_t - X_{t_0} with a fixed base point. Two standard cautions: the bound can be LOOSE - for a centred Gaussian process the sharp answer is Talagrand's generic chaining and the majorizing measure theorem, and Dudley's integral can overshoot by an unbounded factor; and the integral must converge, so a class with covering numbers growing faster than exp(u^{-2}) is not handled. Sudakov's minoration provides the matching lower bound E sup_t X_t >= c sup_{u > 0} u sqrt( log N(T, d, u) ) for centred GAUSSIAN processes, so the two differ exactly by the integral versus the supremum. [Dudley (1967); see Vershynin, High-Dimensional Probability, Theorem 8.1.6]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:13:18.530012+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_15432adff4f8ab0df6ac9b5c3446f4e5fd251373fd7556ef6a6ca078d087c632","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 1 (Dichotomy recurrence/transience for $\Tree_{\infty}$-walk) of arXiv:2608.30668, 'Recurrence and capacity of stable branching random walks'] Assume that \(\theta\) is not supported by a strict subgroup of \(\Z^d\). Consider the \emph{total escape} event
\(\esc= \bigl(W_{\Tree_{\infty}}(u) \neq 0\ \forall u \in \Tree_{\infty}\!\setminus\! \{ c_0 \} \bigr)\).

\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item
  If \(\P(\esc)=0\) then almost surely, for every \(x \in \Z^d\),
  \(\sum_{u \in \Tree_{\infty}} \1_{W_{\Tree_{\infty}}(u)=x} = +\infty\)
  \emph{i.e.} \(x\) is visited infinitely often by
  \(W_{\Tree_{\infty}}\).
\item
  If \(\P(\esc)>0\) then almost surely, for every \(x \in \Z^d\),
  \(\sum_{u \in \Tree_{\infty}} \1_{W_{\Tree_{\infty}}(u)=x} < +\infty\).
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, \[\P(\esc)=0 \text{ if and only if } \P(\esc_{+})=0,\] where
\(\esc_{+}= \bigl(W_{\Tree_{\infty}}(u) \neq 0\ \forall u \in \Tree_{+} \bigr)\)
as in \eqref{eq:LinkFiniteInfinite}, and in the recurrent case we actually have that almost surely, for every \(x \in \Z^d\),
  \(\sum_{u \in \Tree_{+}} \1_{W_{\Tree_{\infty}}(u)=x} = +\infty\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:58:01.576896+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_15465d1124e7798ba9a6e60f375cd927a8d35bb367121cb87cabb7c34f1d303c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 15 (Barrier-regularized universality) of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Fix $N,n\ge1$, $K_{\rm feat}>0$, and $\beta,\gamma>0$.
	Let $W\in\R^N$ be a $(K_{\rm feat},\tau)$-regular feature with
		covariance matrix $\Sigma$, and set
		$\lambda_{\Sigma}=\|\Sigma\|_{\op}>0$.  Let $G$ be the centered Gaussian
	feature with covariance $\Sigma$, and let
	$W_1,\ldots,W_n$ and $G_1,\ldots,G_n$ be independent arrays of i.i.d.
	copies of $W$ and $G$, respectively.

	There are constants $C,n_0<\infty$, depending only on
	$K_{\rm feat}$, with the following property.  Let
	$\mathcal D\subset\R^N$ be nonempty, bounded, convex, and relatively
	open in its affine hull, and let
	$\mathcal B:\mathcal D\to[0,\infty)$ be a
	$\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier for some $\vartheta\ge1$.
	Define the reference scale
	\begin{equation}
		
		\Lambda_{\rm ref}
		:=\left(1+\frac{1}{\beta}\right)
		\left(
		1+\inf_{\theta\in\mathcal D}
		\{\lambda_{\Sigma}\|\theta\|_2^2+\gamma\mathcal B(\theta)\}
		\right).
	\end{equation}
	If $n\gamma\ge n_0$, then
		\begin{equation}
			
			\left|
			\E\Phi_W(\mathcal D,\mathcal B;\beta,\gamma)
			-
			\E\Phi_G(\mathcal D,\mathcal B;\beta,\gamma)
			\right|
			\le
			C\Lambda_{\rm ref}^2\left(
			\frac1{\sqrt{n\gamma}}
			+\frac{\sqrt{\dim\mathsf V_{\mathcal D}}(\tau/\lambda_{\Sigma}+1)}{n}
			\right).
		\end{equation}
	Moreover,
		\begin{equation}
			
			\Var\!\left(\Phi_W(\mathcal D,\mathcal B;\beta,\gamma)\right)
			+
			\Var\!\left(\Phi_G(\mathcal D,\mathcal B;\beta,\gamma)\right)
			\le C\frac{\Lambda_{\rm ref}^2}{n},
		\end{equation}
	and hence, for every $t>0$,
		\begin{equation}
			
			\P\left(
			\left|\Phi_W(\mathcal D,\mathcal B;\beta,\gamma)
			-\Phi_G(\mathcal D,\mathcal B;\beta,\gamma)\right|
			>C\Lambda_{\rm ref}^2\left(
			\frac1{\sqrt{n\gamma}}
			+
			\frac{\sqrt{\dim\mathsf V_{\mathcal D}}(\tau/\lambda_{\Sigma}+1)}{n}
			\right)+t
			\right)
			\le \frac{C\Lambda_{\rm ref}^2}{nt^2}.
		\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:45:05.473551+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_155cab74a5c4c7ddc91543d2267c40d113873e75f78a07160955b3ad1325a52b","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 168 (Dense-skeleton one-set perfection) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $(\Theta,d_\Theta)$ be a separable metric space, let $(E,d_E)$ be a
metric space, and let $F,G:\Omega\times\Theta\to E$ be jointly Borel fields.
Suppose there is a Borel $\cP$-full set $G_0$ on which the two parameter
sections are continuous.  If, for one countable dense set
$D\subset\Theta$,
\[
 F(\cdot,\theta)=G(\cdot,\theta)
 \quad\cP\text{-quasi surely},\qquad \theta\in D,
\]
then there is one Borel $\cP$-polar set $N$, independent of $\theta$, such
that
\[
 F(x,\theta)=G(x,\theta),
 \qquad x\in G_0\setminus N,\quad \theta\in\Theta.
\]
The same conclusion holds for a jointly Borel residual
$\mathfrak R:\Omega\times\Theta\to E$ whose parameter sections are
continuous on $G_0$: if $\mathfrak R(\cdot,\theta)=e_0$ quasi surely on
$D$, then it equals $e_0$ on $(G_0\setminus N)\times\Theta$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:47:21.707303+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_155e2995071bbcb67564993fea5d7fd4aad7d1e54e77fe15466f977823f5edb0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem intro-th:sec-order-main of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] (Theorem (th:sec-order-main of the paper))

  Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$ and assume that for every
  finite $r$ one has
  \begin{equation} 
  \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N^2 \left( \frac{1}{N} \log \mathbb{E}[H
     \text{} C (x_1, \ldots, x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A), \ldots, \lambda_N
     (A))] - \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (x_i) - \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i = 1}^r \Phi (x_i)
     \right) = \sum_{i = 1}^r \mathrm{T} (x_i), 
     \end{equation} 
  where $\Psi, \Phi, \mathrm{T}$ are smooth functions in a complex neighborhood of $0$ and
  the above convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$. Then the $1 /
  N^2$ correction of the average empirical distribution of $N^{- 1} A$
  is given by
  \[ \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N^2 \left( \frac{1}{N^{k + 1}}
     \mathbb{E}[\ensuremath{\operatorname{Tr}} (A^k)] -\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_k - \frac{1}{N}
     \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}'_k \right) =\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}''_k
     +\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\nu}}''_k, \]
  where $(\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}, (\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}'_k)_{k \in
  \mathbb{N}}$ are given by ((intro-topg of the paper)),((intro-G of the paper)) respectively. The sequences
  $(\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}''_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}, (\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\nu}}''_k)_{k \in
  \mathbb{N}}$ are given by
  \[ \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}''_k = \sum_{m = 0}^{k - 1} \frac{k!}{m! (m + 1) ! (k -
     m - 1) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi' (x))^{k - m - 1}
     \mathrm{T}' (x)) \right|_{x = 0} \]
  \begin{equation}
    \text{{\hspace{10em}}} + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{m = 0}^{k - 2} \frac{k!}{m! (m
    + 1) ! (k - m - 2) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi'
    (x))^{k - m - 2} (\Phi' (x))^2) \right|_{x = 0} 
  \end{equation}
  and
  \[ \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\nu}}''_k = \frac{1}{24} \sum_{m = 0}^{k - 3} \frac{k!}{m! (m
     + 1) ! (k - m - 3) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi'
     (x))^{k - m - 3} \Psi''' (x)) \right|_{x = 0} \]
  \[ \text{{\hspace{4em}}} + \frac{1}{12} \sum_{m = 0}^{k - 3} \frac{k!}{m! (m
     + 2) ! (k - m - 3) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi'
     (x))^{k - m - 3} \Psi''' (x)) \right|_{x = 0} \]
  \begin{equation}
    \text{{\hspace{10em}}} + \frac{1}{12} \sum_{m = 0}^{k - 4} \frac{k!}{m! (m
    + 2) ! (k - m - 4) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi'
    (x))^{k - m - 4} (\Psi'' (x))^2) \right|_{x = 0} . 
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(a) f absolutely continuous with E|f'(Z)| finite","(c) the characterisation quantifies over a rich enough class of test functions","(d) the Gaussian vector must be CENTRED"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543764+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1564c803ed1f4f740d9c5f603549c04916aaed26f09262fdb378ee739b59ba18","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"(a) Let Z be standard Gaussian on R and f absolutely continuous with E|f'(Z)| < infinity. Then E[ Z f(Z) ] = E[ f'(Z) ]. (b) Multivariate: if X is centred Gaussian on R^n with covariance Sigma and f is differentiable with the appropriate integrability, then E[ X_i f(X) ] = sum_j Sigma_{ij} E[ d f / d x_j (X) ]. (c) STEIN'S CHARACTERISATION: a real random variable Z is standard Gaussian IF AND ONLY IF E[ Z f(Z) ] = E[ f'(Z) ] for every bounded, continuously differentiable f with bounded derivative. This is the identity that makes Stein's method work: to show a law is close to Gaussian, one bounds E[ Z f(Z) - f'(Z) ] over a class of test functions f solving Stein's equation. (d) ISSERLIS-WICK FORMULA: for a centred Gaussian vector, E[ X_1 X_2 ... X_{2m} ] = sum over all PERFECT MATCHINGS of {1, ..., 2m} of the product of the covariances of the matched pairs, and any odd moment vanishes. For 2m = 4 this reads E[X_1X_2X_3X_4] = Sigma_{12}Sigma_{34} + Sigma_{13}Sigma_{24} + Sigma_{14}Sigma_{23}, and in particular E[Z^4] = 3 for a standard Gaussian, which is the '3' that the fourth moment theorem tests against. Centring is essential in (d); for a non-centred Gaussian one must first subtract the means. [standard; Isserlis (1918), Stein (1972); see Nourdin and Peccati, Normal Approximations with Malliavin Calculus, Chapter 3]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:26:20.445387+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_15760300cd965d69d348d8a143d29826ff8e5c226be9884c43d220e996706c12","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn of arXiv:2411.11676, 'Surface sums for lattice Yang--Mills in the large-$N$ limit'] A \\textbf{surface sum} is a sum of the form $\\sum_{M\\in\\mathcal{M}}w(M)$ where $\\mathcal{M}$ denotes a  collection of planar or high genus maps,\\footnote{See Section~(sect:embedded-maps of the paper) for further details on maps.} sometimes referred to as \\textbf{surfaces}, and $w(M)\\in\\mathbb{R}$ represents a \\textbf{weight} associated with $M$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:32:34.753737+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1577b48896d345baa3b86028c9328bba2b01c07c693b123097d223c496a8ed0e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:lpp of arXiv:2411.08018, 'Last passage percolation in hierarchical environments'] Let $(X(v))_{v\in \mathbb{Z}^2}$ be a collection of random variables indexed by the vertices of the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$.
    We refer to the individual variables $X(v)$ as \emph{weights}.
    For $n\ge1$, let $L_n$ be the \emph{last passage time} from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$:
\begin{equation}
        L_n \coloneqq \max_{\pi} \sum_{v\in\pi} X(v),
\end{equation}
    where the maximum is taken over up-right directed lattice paths that start
    at $(0,0)$ and end at $(n,n)$.
    A \emph{geodesic} is a path achieving the above maximum.
    We write $\Gamma_n$ to denote such a maximizer (one may fix a deterministic 
    rule to break ties in the case there are multiple geodesics).
    
    Note that the definition of last passage time naturally extends to any pair of ordered points (in the coordinate-wise ordering) $u\preceq v \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ by defining $L(u;v)$ as in (equation LPPdef of the paper) but with the maximum over up-right directed paths from $u$ to $v$ (so $L_n=L((0,0);(n,n))$).
    Thus LPP can be thought of as a model of a random metric space where the last passage time is the distance between points 
    (strictly speaking, it is not a metric as it satisfies the reverse triangle inequality on account of the maximization in (equation LPPdef of the paper)).
    \footnote{The related model of \emph{first passage percolation} is where the weights are positive and one minimizes the passage time over all paths (including non-directed paths), thereby obtaining a genuine metric space.}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:33:17.680604+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_157acc903534612097a8eb48b465184203989d35d4019d10add649e0a3d9a78a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 14 (Maximal common Gaussian factor) of arXiv:2607.10769, '\fontsize{14}{17}\selectfont\bfseries Sharp Poincar\'e interpolation along Wasserstein geo'] Let $\mu_i$ be $\kappa_i$-strongly log-concave probability measures
on $\R^n$, let $m_i=\int x\,\d\mu_i$, and define
\begin{equation}
	E=\left\{v\in\R^n:
		\int v\cdot\nabla\psi\,\d\mu_i
		=\kappa_i\int v\cdot(x-m_i)\psi\,\d\mu_i,\quad \forall\,\psi\in C_c^\infty(\R^n),\quad i=0,1\right\}.
\end{equation}
Then $E$ is a linear subspace. Moreover, under the orthogonal identification
$\R^n=E\oplus E^\perp$, there exist $\nu_i\in\mathcal P(E^\perp)$ such
that
\begin{equation}
 \mu_i=N_E(P_E m_i,\kappa_i^{-1}I_E)\otimes\nu_i,
 \qquad i=0,1.
\end{equation}
Here $N_E$ denotes a Gaussian law on $E$.  If a subspace $F\subseteq
\R^n$ admits such a factorization for both endpoints, with respective
covariances $\kappa_i^{-1}I_F$, then $F\subseteq E$.  Thus $E$ is the
unique maximal common Gaussian subspace.  Moreover, equality in
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} at one (equivalently, every) time
$t\in(0,1)$ holds if and only if $E\neq\{0\}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.357294+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1594701927aa6e86d36b76834ad067d19846f3f6e390572f70d1e106f8d7846f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 240 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\alpha,L,\epsilon,\delta>0$, and $\fq\in [1,2)$, there exists $c = c(\alpha,L,\delta) > 0$ such that the following holds for sufficiently large $N$. For any $L$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA_N$, we have
	\[
		\P\bigg(
			\bbW_\fq\Big(\mu_\bG(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)), \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)
			\Big) \le \delta
		\bigg) \ge 1 - e^{-cN}\,,
	\]
for $\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)$ as defined by \eqref{e:cM.Lip.union.L}. The analogous estimate holds likewise for $\bbW_\fq(\mu_{\bG,\sym}(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux))$ and $\cM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha;\epsilon))$, where the latter is defined by \eqref{e:cM.Lip.union.L.SYM}. 

\begin{proof}
	Throughout this proof, $c$ denotes a constant that depends on $\alpha,L,\delta$, which can change line by line.
	By \eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.tail} from Lemma~\ref{l:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound}, for $C = C(\alpha)$ as defined therein, we have
	\beq
		\P\bigg(
			\mu_\bG(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)) \in \cP_2(\R,C)
		\bigg) \ge 1 - e^{-cN}\,.
	\eeq
We now define
	\[
		S_\delta \equiv
		\Big\{ \mu \in \cP_2(\R,C) : \bbW_\fq(\mu, \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)) \ge \delta \Big\}
	\]
(note this differs slightly from the set $S_\delta$ defined in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:confinement.lip.trunc.to.ideal}). 
	By Lemma~\ref{l:confinement.cPp.compact.Wq}, the space $\cP_2(\R,C)$ endowed with the $\bbW_\fq$ metric is compact.
	The set $S_\delta$ is closed with respect to the $\bbW_\fq$ metric, and therefore also compact. We may thus cover $S_\delta$ with finitely many $\bbW_\fq$-balls,
	\[S_\delta = \bigcup_{\mu \in T_\delta} \cB_{\fq,\delta/5}(\mu)
		\,,\]
	where $T_\delta \subseteq S_\delta$ is a finite set depending on only $\fq, \delta$, and
		\[\cB_{q,\delta/5}(\mu) 
		\equiv\bigg\{
			\mu' \in S_\delta : \bbW_\fq(\mu,\mu') \le 
			\frac{\delta}{5}
		\bigg\}\,.\]
	Note that for each $\mu \in S_\delta$, we have
	\begin{align*}
		\bbW_\fq(\mu(\cA_N),\mu) 
		&\ge \bbW_\fq(\mu,\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon))
		- \bbW_\fq(\mu(\cA_N),\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)) \\
		&\ge \delta - \bbW_\fq(\mu(\cA_N),\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon))\,,
	\end{align*}
where the last term on the right-hand side above does not depend on $
\mu$, and is $o_N(1)$ by
	Proposition~\ref{p:confinement}. It follows that for $N$ large enough, we have
	\[
		\inf_{\mu \in S_\delta} \bbW_\fq(\mu(\cA_N),\mu) \ge 
		\frac{4\delta}{5}\,.
	\]
	For each $\mu \in T_\delta$,  Lemma~\ref{l:confinement.consequence.of.variance.bound} implies
	\[
		\E \bbW_\fq\Big(\mu_\bG(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)),\mu\Big)
		\stackrel{\eqref{e:confinement.consequence.of.variance.bound}}{\ge} \bigg(\Big[\bbW_\fq(\mu(\cA_N),\mu)^2 - o_N(1)\Big]_+\bigg)^{1/2}
		\ge \frac{3\delta}{5}
	\]
	for sufficiently large $N$.
	Note that the $o_N(1)$ term above may depend on $\mu$; however, as $T_\delta$ is a finite set independent of $N$, the above estimate can be taken to hold simultaneously for all $\mu \in T_\delta$. By Lemma~\ref{l:Wq.lip.to.fixed.msr.conc} combined with a union bound over
$\mu \in T_\delta$, we obtain
	\[
		\P\bigg(
			\min_{\mu \in T_\delta} \bbW_\fq\Big(\mu_\bG(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux),\mu\Big)
			\ge \frac{2\delta}{5}
		\bigg)
		\stackrel{\eqref{e:Wq.lip.to.fixed.msr.conc.tail}}{=} 1 - e^{-cN}\,.
	\]
	(This $c$ depends on $\alpha,L,\delta$ only, as $\epsilon,\fq$ affect only the $N$-independent number of terms $|T_\delta|$ in the union bound.)
	On this event, we further have
	\[\bbW_\fq\Big(\mu_\bG(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)), S_\delta\Big)
		\ge \min_{\mu \in T_\delta} \bbW_\fq\Big(\mu_\bG(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)),\mu\Big) - \frac{\delta}{5}
		\ge 
		\frac{\delta}{5}\,,\]
	and therefore $\mu_\bG(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)) \not\in S_\delta$.
	Combining with \eqref{e:confinement.mu.bG.to.P2} shows that 
	\[
		\mu_\bG(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)) \in \cP_2(\R,C) \setminus S_\delta
	\]
with probability $1-e^{-cN}$ (again adjusting $c$ appropriately). 
	On this event, we obtain the desired estimate
	\[
		\bbW_\fq\Big(\mu_\bG(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)), \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)
		\Big) \le \delta\,.
	\]

{"assumptions":["All hypotheses, dimensions, step restrictions and observable norms in the statement; no independent audit."],"created_at":"2026-10-21T19:50:21.974827+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_15ae575f5cdf6ffb959dcd4d6db118bd84cd72568d605a4fd10d69cb34b06ab0","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own work draft; proof (unaudited), claim w730-T355-C009 v1; novelty unestablished.

Let d,q be finite positive integers. Let H be constant SPD with eigenvalues
in [m,M], m>0, and let sigma,D,kappa>=0. Let 0<rho<2 and

    0<eta<=rho/M, gamma=min(m,M(2-rho)/rho),
    eta kappa^2 <= gamma/2, B=I-eta H.

An adapted recursion starts from deterministic u0,v0 and satisfies

    u_{k+1}=u_k-eta xi_k^u,  v_{k+1}=B v_k-eta xi_k^v,
    E[xi_k^u | F_k]=0, E[xi_k^v | F_k]=0,
    E[|xi_k^v|^2 | F_k] <= sigma^2 tr H + kappa^2 |v_k|^2,
    E[|xi_k^u|^2 | F_k] <= sigma^2 D^2 |v_k|^2.           (1)

The filtration contains the state before the kth increment. No iid,
symmetry or moments beyond these conditional second moments are required
for the oracle estimate. If the target's on-manifold covariance identity
is desired, additionally impose Cov(xi^v | state (u,0))=sigma^2 H.
The tangent condition then forces tangent and cross covariance to vanish
there, giving sigma^2 diag(0,H), proportional to the population Hessian.

Define V=|v0|, alpha=sigma^2 tr H, and

    c_V=2(alpha+kappa^2 V^2)/gamma,
    R_T=sigma^2 D^2 (V^2/gamma+T c_V).

For F in C_b^2(R^{d+q}), let F_uu,F_uv,F_vv be the global operator-norm
bounds of its second derivative blocks. For every T>=0,

    sup_{integer 0<=K<=floor(T/eta^2)}
      |E F(u_K,v_K)-F(u0,B^K v0)| <= eta C(T,V),
    C(T,V)=F_uu R_T/2+F_uv sqrt(c_V R_T)+F_vv c_V/2.    (2)

Thus a=1, with explicit constants, in a larger normal-noise class than
C007's uniformly bounded conditional covariance class. This is not a
claim that the new constants improve those of C007 when kappa=0.

When v0=0, (2) compares against the constant slow limit (u0,0) at every
index. For general fixed v0 and F_v=sup ||D_v F||, comparison against
(u0,0) has bound eta(C(T,V)+F_v) at every integer

    ceil(log(max(1,V/eta))/(eta gamma))<=K<=floor(T/eta^2).

An empty interval covers no indices. The initial-layer cutoff is the
same deterministic contraction argument as C008; it is not a logarithm
in the weak-error constant. No comparison against (u0,0) is asserted at
K=0 from nonzero v0 for arbitrary ambient observables.","status":"unverified"}
