{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:17:04.322392+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_285a62c00817a0f33025b8ff1c05b23babc90cc138d8df542b70852feac71128","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma main invertible lemma of arXiv:2606.01683, 'Singular-value gap of nonreversible Markov processes'] Let $(S,\mu)$ be a probability space.
    Let $L$ be the generator on $L^2(\mu)$, either of a strongly continuous Markov semigroup $(P_t)_{t \geq 0}$, or of the form $L = P - I$ for a discrete-time Markov chain 
    with Markov transition kernel $P$.
    Let $K \subset L^2_0(\mu)$ be a closed subspace such that 
    $P_t(K) \subset K$ for all $t \geq 0$ in continuous time, or
    \(P(K)\subset K\) in discrete time. Let $L_K$ denote the 
    generator  restricted to $K$.
    Suppose that $L$ has a singular-value gap on $K$:
    \begin{align} 
    \gamma_K \coloneqq \inf_{f \in \operatorname{Dom}(L_K)\backslash\{0\}} 
    \frac{\|L_Kf\|}{\|f\|} > 0.
    \end{align} 
    Then $L_K$ is invertible with 
    \[
    \|L_K^{-1} \|_{K \to K} \leq \frac{1}{\gamma_K}.
    \]
    
    \begin{proof}
        Since $L_K$ is the generator of a contraction semigroup, the resolvent set of $L_K$
        contains the positive half-plane. Explicitly, in continuous time,
         the resolvent $R_\lambda$ of $L_K$ at $\lambda > 0$ is given by
        \[
        R_\lambda g:= (\lambda I - L_K)^{-1} g = \int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda s}P_s g\,ds,
        \quad g \in K;
        \]
        see Theorem II.1.10 in [engel_nagel_2000].
        In discrete time, for $\lambda > 0$,
        \[
            R_\lambda:= (\lambda I -L_K)^{-1} =  ((1+\lambda)I-P_K)^{-1},
        \]
        where $P_K$ is the restriction of the Markov kernel $P$ on $K$.
        Since
        $\|\frac{1}{1+\lambda}P_K \|\le \frac{1}{1+\lambda}<1$,
        the Neumann series gives
        \[
        R_\lambda
        =
        \frac{1}{1+\lambda}\sum_{n=0}^\infty \left( \frac{P_K}{1+\lambda} \right)^n.
        \]

        For $0<\lambda<\gamma_K$ and $f\in \operatorname{Dom}(L_K)$,
        \[
        \|(\lambda I-L_K)f\|
        \ge \|L_Kf\| -\lambda\|f\|
        \ge (\gamma_K-\lambda)\|f\|.
        \]
        Therefore,
        $\|R_\lambda\|
        \le \frac{1}{\gamma_K-\lambda}$.
        For $0<\lambda,\mu<\gamma_K$, the resolvent identity yields
        \[
        R_\lambda-R_\mu=(\mu-\lambda)R_\lambda R_\mu.
        \]
        Thus, $(R_\lambda)_{\lambda\downarrow 0}$ is Cauchy in operator norm. Let
        \[
        R_K:=\lim_{\lambda\downarrow 0}R_\lambda
        \qquad\text{in } \ \| \cdot \|_{K \to K}.
        \]
        We claim that $R_K=-L_K^{-1}$. Consider $g\in K$. Since for $\lambda > 0$  
        \[
            (\lambda I - L_K) R_\lambda =I,
        \]
        we have
        \[
        -L_KR_\lambda g=g - \lambda R_\lambda g \to g
        \qquad\text{as} \ \lambda \downarrow 0.
        \]
        Since $L_K$ is closed, it follows that $R_K \mkern1mu g\in \operatorname{Dom}(L_K)$ and
        \[
        -L_KR_K \mkern1mu g=g.
        \]
        Similarly, we deduce $-R_K L_K f = f$ for any $f \in \operatorname{Dom}(L_K)$, hence
        \[
        R_K=-L_K^{-1}.
        \]
        Finally, since $\|L_Kf\| \geq \gamma_K \|f\|$ for $f \in \operatorname{Dom}(L_K)$,
        we get $\|L_K^{-1}\| \leq \gamma_K^{-1}$.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:00:15.234424+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_285f77268eeea08fb2f4846741d13a50f37855a48f674a4e3386242477a3d2c2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 4 (Characterization of the optimal control under partial terminal observation) of arXiv:2607.19176, 'Exponential Convergence of the Sinkhorn Algorithm for the Schrödinger Bridge with Regime S'] Under Assumption \ref{assum:reference_marginals_partial} the partially observed static regime-switching Schr\"odinger bridge problem \eqref{eq:eot-partial} admits
a unique optimal solution $\pi^{\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p}}\ll P_{0, T}$, characterized as follows.
There exist nonnegative measurable functions $(\tilde f_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}$ and $\tilde g$, unique up to the transformation
\[
(\tilde f,\tilde g)
\sim
(\lambda\tilde f,\lambda^{-1}\tilde g),
\qquad
\lambda>0,
\]
such that
\begin{equation}

\frac{\mathrm d\pi^{\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p}}}{\mathrm dP_{0,T}}(z_0,z_T)
=
\tilde f_{i_0}(x_0)\tilde g(x_T) \quad \text{for }\pi^{\rho,\mu}\text{-a.e. } (z_0,z_T)=((x_0,i_0),(x_T,i_T)).
\end{equation}
Moreover, $(\tilde f_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}$ and $\tilde g$ solve the projected Schr\"odinger system
\begin{equation}

\left\{
\begin{aligned}
1
&=
\tilde f_i(x)
\int_{\mathbb R^d}
\bar p_i(x,y)\tilde g(y)\,\mu_{\mathrm p}(\mathrm dy),
&&
\rho_i\text{-a.e. }x,
\quad i\in\mathcal I,
\\
1
&=
\tilde g(y)
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
\int_{\mathbb R^d}
\bar p_i(x,y)\tilde f_i(x)\,\rho_i(\mathrm dx),
&&
\mu_{\mathrm p}\text{-a.e. }y.
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation}

Equivalently, the optimal projected endpoint coupling $\gamma^{\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p}}
:=
(\mathrm{id}_E \times \mathrm{pr}_{\mathbb{R}^d})_{\#} \pi^{\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p}}$, where $ \mathrm{pr}_{\mathbb{R}^d}(y, i) = y $, is given componentwise by
\[
\gamma_i^{\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p}}(\mathrm dx,\mathrm dy)
=
\tilde f_i(x)\bar p_i(x,y)\tilde g(y)\,
\rho_i(\mathrm dx)\mu_{\mathrm p}(\mathrm dy),
\qquad
i\in\mathcal I.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:47:53.350535+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_286f663404b83ddccf608e08b01ca7aa030e6c8089b61bfcc139b453132e04ac","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 26 (Minimal diagonal gap) of arXiv:2607.15872, 'Existence of $q$-Bass martingales in the semidiscrete setting'] Let $\Ccal \in \Lambda_\nu^{p_1,\dots,p_n}$. For every $i\in\{1,\dots,n-1\}$, define
\[
\delta_i:=\mathrm{dist}\Big((p_i^*,\Ccal_i),\,\big[(p_{i-1}^*,\Ccal_{i-1}),(p_{i+1}^*,\Ccal_{i+1})\big]\cap\{x=p_i^*\}\Big).
\]
The quantity
\[
\delta:=\min_{1\le i\le n-1}\delta_i
\]
is called the \emph{minimal diagonal gap} of $\Ccal$. An index $i_\delta\in\{1,\dots,n-1\}$ is called a \emph{minimal-gap index} with respect to $\Ccal$ if
\[
i_\delta\in\arg\min_{1\le j\le n-1}\delta_j.
\]","status":"unverified"}

An \emph{orbit} generated by $\rho$ from $\sigma$ over the index interval $[a{:}b] = \{a, a+1, \dots, b\} \subset \mathbb{Z}$, with $a \le b$, is the ordered collection
\[
\mathcal{O} = (\sigma_a, \sigma_{a+1}, \dots, \sigma_b),
\]
where each element is defined by
\[
\sigma_k = \sigma \circ \rho^k.
\]
Here, $\rho^k$ denotes the $k$-fold composition of $\rho$ with itself if $k \ge 0$, and the $|k|$-fold composition of $\rho^{-1}$ if $k < 0$. The \emph{length} of the orbit, denoted $|\mathcal{O}|$, is $b - a + 1$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:37:51.460987+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_28a54d38de63edbaee28410a1bfeebd8bfd513c6cf4da72421468853b211705a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 56 (Intermediate martingale problem) of arXiv:2604.03777, 'Equilibrium fluctuations for a multi-species particle system with long jumps'] We call an $\mathcal{S}' (\mathbb{R})$-valued
  stochastic process $(\mathcal{Z}_t)_{t \geqslant 0}$ on some complete
  probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$ a \textit{solution to the intermediate martingale
problem} for equation \eqref{spdefbe} if the following conditions are
  satisfied:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item Path regularity: For all $H \in \mathcal{S}$ the
    process $t \mapsto \mathcal{Z}_t (H)$ is continuous.
    
    \item Incompressibility: $\sup_{t \leqslant T} | \mathbb{E}
    [F (\mathcal{Z}_t)] | \lesssim \| F \|_{L^2 (\mu)}$ for all $T > 0$ and $F
    \in \mathcal{C}$.
    
    \item Non-linear energy estimate: For all $F \in
    \mathcal{C}$ and for all $T > 0$
    \begin{equation}
      \mathbb{E} \left[ \sup_{t \leqslant T} \left| \int_0^t F (\mathcal{Z}_s)
    \; \dd s \right| \right] \lesssim (T^{1 / 2} + T) \| F
      \|_{\mathcal{H}^{- 1}_0} . 
    \end{equation}
    In particular, there exists a unique continuous extension to
    $\mathcal{H}^{- 1}_0$ of the map
    \[ I : \mathcal{C} \rightarrow \bigcap_{T > 0} L^1 (\Omega, C ([0, T],
       \mathbb{R})), \qquad I (F)_t = \int_0^t F (\mathcal{Z}_s) \; \dd s . \]
    \item Weak solution: For $H \in \mathcal{S}$ the process
    \[ M^H_t = \mathcal{Z}_t (H) - \mathcal{Z}_0 (H) - \int_0^t \mathcal{Z}_s

       s - I_t (\langle B (\cdot, \cdot), H \rangle_{L^2 (\mathbb{R})})
       , \quad t \geqslant 0, \]
    where the last term is well-defined due to \eqref{BinHminusone} and $(\ref{propEEnl})$, is a martingale in the filtration generated by $\mathcal{Z}$ with
    quadratic variation $\langle M^H \rangle_t = 2 t \langle
    \mathbb{L}^{\gamma} H, H \rangle_{L^2 (\mathbb{R})}$. Moreover, there exist $p <
    2$ and for all $T > 0$ the following convergence holds in probability:
    \[ \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \left\| I (\langle B (\cdot, \cdot), H
       \rangle_{L^2 (\mathbb{R})}) - \int_0^{\cdot} \langle B
       (\vec{\iota}_{\varepsilon} \ast \mathcal{Z}_s,
       \vec{\iota}_{\varepsilon} \ast \mathcal{Z}_s), H \rangle_{L^2
       (\mathbb{R})} \; \dd s \right\|_{p \text{-var}} = 0, \]
    where $\| X \|_{p - \text{var}}^p = \sup \left\{ \sum_{k = 0}^{n - 1} |
    X_{t_{k + 1}} - X_{t_k} |^p : n \in \mathbb{N}_0, 0 = t_0 < \cdots < t_n =

{"assumptions":["delta > 0, started at x > 0","the diffusion is considered on (0, infinity) up to the hitting time of 0","the integer case delta = d transfers to Brownian motion in R^d through the radial part"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543969+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_28ae49b4849a217435a2f33e1bff7911ba62b44c71425000ee08e45fdab6ac40","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a Bessel process of dimension delta > 0 started at x > 0, solving dX_t = dW_t + ((delta - 1)/(2 X_t)) dt on (0, infinity). Its SCALE FUNCTION is s(x) = x^{2 - delta}/(2 - delta) for delta != 2 and s(x) = log x for delta = 2. Consequently: for delta > 2 the process is TRANSIENT, never hits 0 from x > 0, and X_t -> infinity almost surely; for delta = 2 it never hits 0 and is NEIGHBOURHOOD RECURRENT, visiting every interval (a,b) with 0 < a < b at arbitrarily large times almost surely, while X_t -> infinity fails and liminf X_t = 0 with limsup X_t = infinity; for 0 < delta < 2 the process reaches 0 almost surely in finite time. Specialising to integer delta = d and using that |B| is BES^d recovers the classical dichotomy for Brownian motion in R^d: recurrent for d = 1 (point recurrent) and d = 2 (neighbourhood recurrent, never hitting a fixed point), transient for d >= 3. The critical dimension is exactly 2 and the transition is driven by whether the integral of s' diverges at 0 and at infinity. [standard; e.g. Revuz and Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion, 3rd ed., Chapter XI, Proposition 1.5]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:36.746095+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_28cc758249dbc47793acae9ac6bdeda9f897700a60b12e072e99cc29aab64b8e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 2 (Classical history–dependent walk on $G$) of arXiv:2511.18216, 'Classical localization problem: a survey'] Fix a collection of node matrices $\{S^{(v)}\}_{v\in V}$ with $N_v=2$, and let
$G=(V,E)$ be a finite directed graph. A \emph{configuration} at time $n$ is a
pair $(\gamma_n,\eta_n)$, where
\begin{itemize}
  \item $\gamma_n=(e_0,\dots,e_n)$ is a directed path of length $n$ on $G$;
  \item $\eta_n$ records, for each node $v$, how many times each incident edge
        has been used by $\gamma_n$.
\end{itemize}
The process starts from some initial edge $e_0$ with configuration
$(\gamma_0,\eta_0)$. Given $(\gamma_n,\eta_n)$, let $v$ be the terminal vertex
of $e_n$, and let $j\in\{1,2\}$ be the label of the incoming channel at $v$
used by $e_n$. If $\gamma_n$ has never visited $v$ before, the walk chooses the
outgoing channel $i\in\{1,2\}$ with probability proportional to
$|S^{(v)}_{ij}|^2$, and sets $e_{n+1}$ to be the corresponding outgoing edge.
If $\gamma_n$ has already used some of the incident edges at $v$, the walk exits
along one of the remaining edges with probability~$1$ (if exactly one remains)
or according to the appropriate conditional weight derived from
\eqref{eq:node-weight}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:59:58.455270+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_291a0a75fff7f80bcf4331f3433d01af03bfb8fd1ae4afcd4b31e2c0e9287bc8","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Df associated of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] Let $w>0$.
  Associated with a configuration $\eta\in\Omega$ of the $k$-plaquette percolation model on $\mathbb{R}^d$, a directed graph $G_w=G_w(\eta)$ is defined as follows.
  The vertex set $V_w$ is given by
  \[
  V_w:=\{[\delta]\mid\text{$\delta$ is a $k$-collar based at some discrete $(k-1)$-sphere $S$ with $\diam(S)\le w$}\}.
  \]
  For distinct vertices $\Delta,\Delta'\in V_w$, we include the ordered pair $(\Delta,\Delta')$ as a directed edge in $E_w=E_w(\eta)$ if and only if there exist $k$-collars
  \[
  \delta\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times I_\varepsilon\to|\mathcal{K}_k^d|
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \delta'\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times I_\varepsilon\to|\mathcal{K}_k^d|
  \]
  representing the equivalence classes $\Delta$ and $\Delta'$, respectively, and an open $k$-tube
  \[
  \gamma\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}^d
  \quad\text{with $\width(\gamma)\le w$}
  \]
  such that the following conditions hold:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item (\emph{Initial compatibility}).
    For any $(p,h)\in\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[0,\varepsilon]$,
    \[
    \gamma(p,a+h)=\delta(p,h);
    \]
    \item (\emph{Terminal compatibility}).
    For any $(p,h)\in\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[-\varepsilon,0]$,
    \[
    \gamma(p,b+h)=\delta'(p,h);
    \]
    \item (\emph{Locality}).

    \[
    \diam(\im\gamma)\le2w+4.
    \]
  \end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:38:58.690712+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_291c93b8e53a60aa073b28a0abe83b0dc8dcd760f837b47f36ec6871d909d5fd","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:momentsP of arXiv:2510.21186, 'Weingarten Calculus with Virtual Isometries'] Let $m$, $l$ be nonnegative integers, and consider four sequences
\[
\bm{i}=(i_1,\dots, i_m), \qquad \bm{j} =(j_1,\dots, j_m), \qquad
\bm{i}'=(i_1',\dots, i_l'), \qquad \bm{j}' =(j_1',\dots, j_l').
\]
of positive integers in $\{1,\dots, n\}$.
Then the moment
\[
\mathbb{E} \bigl[ p_{i_1 j_1} \cdots p_{i_m j_m} \overline{p_{i_1' j_1'} \cdots p_{i_l' j_l'}} \bigr]
\]
vanishes unless $\bm{i} \sqcup \bm{j}'$ is a permutation of $\bm{j} \sqcup \bm{i}'$.
In this case, the moment is equal to
\[
\alpha_1! \cdots \alpha_{n-1}! \frac{n^{\uparrow \alpha_n}}{n^{\uparrow m}n^{\uparrow l}},
\]
where
\[
\alpha_k := \mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{i}\sqcup \bm{j}') = \mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{j} \sqcup \bm{i}'),
\qquad k=1,\dots,n.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:19:42.536838+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2921d0f70345bc7caac3fa8ccd7f728fc569a2e2da61d5f35cf88284964bfab7","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2609.03506, 'Divergence of decreasing rearranged Fourier series\\ on every infinite compact abelian gro'] Fix \(N\geq1\) and any bijection \(r:\T_N\to\{1,\ldots,L\}\).
There exist an integer \(D\geq1\), an integer \(C\),
sets \(E_v\subseteq\R_p^D\) for \(|v|\leq N\), a function
\(k:\R_p^D\to\{1,\omega,\ldots,\omega^{p-1}\}\), and functions
\(P_v:\R_p^D\to\mathbb C\) for \(v\in\T_N\), each a character polynomial, with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item \(E_\varnothing=\R_p^D\). For every \(v\in\T_N\), the \(p\) sets
       \(E_{va}\), \(0\leq a\leq p-1\), partition \(E_v\). Moreover,
       \(\mu_D(E_v)=p^{-|v|}\) for every \(v\) with \(|v|\leq N\).
 \item For \(v\in\T_N\), the function

       vanishes outside \(E_v\) and equals \(\zeta_a\) on \(E_{va}\);
       and \(P_v=k\,h_v\).
 \item The Fourier supports of the \(P_v\) are pairwise disjoint.
 \item The exponents \(C+r(v)\) are nonnegative, and, for

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:09:43.678722+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_292a85264fbf68b817c8f7ba65f0dc7b9f82cb4afbcff326a1b69f5a259c0083","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn def.Lp-stabilizing_marking-weak of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] In the setting of Definition~(def.Lp-stabilizing_marking of the paper), we say:

functions $\varphi_p: [0, \infty) \to [0,1]$,  $p \in \mathbb{N}$,

\bk{\xi^{\cup(r)}}{l+1}{p}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})
\bigr)
\Bigr)
\;\le\; 2\varphi_p(r), \qquad r  \geq 0.

\end{enumerate}

(ii)~\emph{\textnormal{BL}~cluster-localization on finite windows},

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:16:46.149134+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2932ec2a4bfc6fa17d04533ff139f07a2323c9aa626f4df89da669f048034b58","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:holder-bookkeeping of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] Fix a finite set of replica indices.

Then there is a self-adjoint extension T_F of T (the Friedrichs extension) with the same lower bound, ⟨T_F x, x⟩ ≥ c‖x‖² for all x ∈ D(T_F), given by the closed form obtained as the continuous extension of q to Q; its domain is D(T_F) = D(T*) ∩ Q and T_F = T* restricted to that domain. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:15:34.546453+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_295d3a7cb2eeda13702b82fd6afdd8e9db49b3b77c89a9437fc91387e0ddca09","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 40 (Borderline case) of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] Let $\widehat{M}$ be the compactification of $(0,\ell) \times P$ as in Theorem \ref{thm:contracting_Q0}. Suppose
$T = T_F' = \min_{k \geq 2}\big\{T_k^0, T_k^\ell\big\}$.

Let $\mathcal{I} := \big\{k \in \{2,\cdots,r\} : T_k^0 = T\big\} = \big\{k \in \{2,\cdots,r\} : T_k^\ell = T\big\}$, the two sets being equal by the Remark following \eqref{eq:T_max}. Let $E_{\mathcal{I}} = \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}}^{\oplus(m+1)}$ be the vector bundle obtained by restricting the normal bundle $\mathcal{N}_{Q_0}$ of $Q_0 \subset \widehat{M}$ to $\prod_{k \in \mathcal{I}} N_k$, as in Theorem \ref{thm:contracting_Q0}, so that $c_1(\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}}) = -\sum_{k \in \mathcal{I}} q_k a_k$, and let
\[\widehat{Z} \;:=\; \mathbb{P}\big(\mathcal{O} \oplus E_{\mathcal{I}}\big)\]
be the $\mathbb{CP}^{m+1}$-bundle over $\prod_{k \in \mathcal{I}} N_k$ obtained by projectivization. 

Let $K_j := (T-t_j)^{-1}$, and fix any $\bar{x} \in \widehat{M}$. Consider the rescaled and dilated sequence $g_j(t) = K_j g(t_j + K_j^{-1}t)$ defined on $t \in [-K_j t_j, K_j(T-t_j))$. Then, along a subsequence,
\begin{equation}
\big( \widehat{M}, \; g_j (t), \; \bar{x} \big) \;\longrightarrow\; \Big( \widehat{Z} \times \mathbb{C}^{n''} \,, \;\; g_{\widehat{Z}} (t) \oplus g_{\mathbb{C}^{n''}} \Big) \,, \qquad t \in \big( - \infty, 1 \big)\,,
\end{equation}
where $n'' = \sum_{k \geq 2, \, k \not\in \mathcal{I}} \dim_{\mathbb{C}} N_{k}$, and $g_{\widehat{Z}}(t)$ is the unique compact shrinking K\"ahler--Ricci soliton of ansatz form on $\widehat{Z}$ --- constructed by Koiso \cite{Koiso} and Cao \cite{Cao96} when the base is a single projective space, and by Dancer--Wang \cite{DW2011} in general, with uniqueness given by Tian--Zhu \cite{TZhu}.

In the extreme case $\mathcal{I} = \{2, \cdots, r\}$, we have $n'' = 0$ and $\widehat{Z} = \widehat{M}$: then $[\omega(t)] = 2(T-t)\,c_1(\widehat{M})$, which is the Fano canonical-class case, and the blow-up limit is $\widehat{M}$ itself equipped with its compact shrinking K\"ahler-Ricci soliton.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["fixed-event qualitative mixing is the only supplied dynamical hypothesis"],"created_at":"2026-10-10T09:09:48.564065+00:00","domain":"probability theory; planar point processes","id":"claim_297d85898ff92f5cf98f5d3f78dbb0c51cdc2d58340a72cd928a63f0feaff461","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"DRAFT; independent review pending.  -2 \le \delta_n(r,x) \le  r2^{r-1},

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:02:28.642016+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_29c8269c309626654685acea7a53fd0e3c71388e53363444090500b3c392a0f9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Def 8 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] Let $X$ be a closed subscheme of $\mbP$ defined by a homogeneous ideal $I \subset R$.
We set
\[
C_X \coloneq \Spec (R/I)
\]
and call it the \textit{affine cone} of $X$.
Let $\pi \colon \mbA^{N+1} \setminus \{O\} \to \mbP$ be the natural projection, where $O$ is the origin.
For a point $\msp \in X$, we say that $X$ is \textit{quasismooth at $\msp$} if $C_X$ is smooth along $\pi^{-1} (\msp)$.
We say that $X$ is \textit{quasismooth} if it is quasismooth at any point of $X$, that is, $C_X$ is smooth away from the origin.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:49.842276+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_29c9f5f7cf824673e8f97af440107e1226d2f6b7978e6b914f0dc504aa604c2e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2506.13913, '2506.13913'] {}{conexion-multi-dim}
Let \(\{W_t\}_{t \geq 0}\) be a \(d\)-dimensional Brownian motion starting at $x$ defined on a probability space \((\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})\), and and assume that \(f \in C(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L^{\infty}( \mathbb{R}^d)\). Furthermore, Consider the \(d\)-dimensional heat equation
\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \Delta u, \quad x \in \mathbb{R}^d, \, t > 0,
\]
with initial condition \(u(x, 0) = f(x)\), where \(\Delta = \sum_{i=1}^d \frac{\partial^2}{\partial x_i^2}\) is the Laplace operator. Then:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item There exists a classical solution \(u\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d\times(0,\infty))\) given by
    \[
    u(x, t) = \frac{1}{(4\pi t)^{d/2}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f(y) \exp\left(-\frac{\|x - y\|^2}{4t}\right) \, dy, \quad t > 0.
    \]

    \item The solution \(u(x, t)\) admits a stochastic representation in terms of \(d\)-dimensional Brownian motion
    \[
    u(x, t) = \mathbb{E}[f(W_t) \mid W_0 = x],
    \]
    where \(\mathbb{E}\) denotes expectation with respect to the probability measure induced by the Brownian motion \(\{W_t\}_{t \geq 0}\).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T07:57:26.282085+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_29ca853a7ea246539c6092053aa6abf5","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In geometric measure theory, Falconer's conjecture, named after Kenneth Falconer, is an unsolved problem concerning the sets of Euclidean distances between points in compact $d$ -dimensional spaces. Intuitively, it states that a set of points that is large in its Hausdorff dimension must determine a set of distances that is large in measure. More precisely, if $S$ is a compact set of points in $d$ -dimensional Euclidean space whose Hausdorff dimension is strictly greater than $d/2$, then the conjecture states that the set of distances between pairs of points in $S$ must have nonzero Lebesgue measure.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:23:05.285432+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_29cbfe58a1c48c4df7f48c04d5aed2c0f19ea3271ca9169c4e1acbea890e5726","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2608.21551, '\bf Sparse Separable Factor Analysis in the Complex Domain with an Application to Local Fi'] For $j=1,\ldots,d$, suppose that $\Sigmab_j\in\CC^{p_j\times p_j}$ is Hermitian positive definite with factor-analytic representation
\begin{align}
  \Sigmab_j
  &=
  \Lambdab_j\Lambdab_j^\star+\Psib_j,
  \qquad
  \Lambdab_j\in\CC^{p_j\times k_j},
  
\end{align}
where $\Psib_j$ is a real-valued diagonal matrix with positive diagonal entries. Let $(c_1,\ldots,c_d)$ be the rescaling constants in \eqref{eq:iden-c}, and define
\begin{align*}
  \widetilde{\Sigmab}_j
  &=
  c_j\Sigmab_j,
  \qquad
  j=1,\ldots,d.
\end{align*}
Each $\widetilde{\Sigmab}_j$ admits the factor-analytic representation
\begin{align}
  \widetilde{\Sigmab}_j
  &=
  \Lb_j\Lb_j^\star+\Db_j,
  \qquad
  \Lb_j
  =
  c_j^{1/2}\Lambdab_j,
  \qquad
  \Db_j
  =
  c_j\Psib_j,
  \qquad
  j=1,\ldots,d,
  
\end{align}
and the rescaled diagonal matrices satisfy
\begin{align}
  \min\left\{\diag(\Db_1)\right\}
  &=
  \cdots
  =
  \min\left\{\diag(\Db_d)\right\}.
  
\end{align}
Furthermore, $\widetilde{\Sigmab}_d \otimes\cdots\otimes \widetilde{\Sigmab}_1 = \Sigmab_d \otimes\cdots\otimes \Sigmab_1$. The tuple $(\widetilde{\Sigmab}_1,\ldots,\widetilde{\Sigmab}_d)$ is the unique admissible multiplicative rescaling of $(\Sigmab_1,\ldots,\Sigmab_d)$ for which the corresponding diagonal matrices $(\Db_1,\ldots,\Db_d)$ satisfy \eqref{eq:app-cor-3}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["entries independent and uniform on {-1, +1}","the statement is asymptotic, with an o(1) inside the base","it is NOT a statement about symmetric random sign matrices"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.544307+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_29dc17afa1384af10ab2de54ecf88bb013b8c4634cd8ecae367cf91b3e346b1c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For each n let M_n be an n by n random matrix with INDEPENDENT entries each uniform on {-1, +1}. Then P( M_n is singular ) = ( 1/2 + o_n(1) )^n. The matching lower bound is elementary: the probability that two rows are equal, or two rows are opposite, or two columns are equal, or two columns are opposite, is already of order n^2 2^{-n} = (1/2 + o(1))^n, and each such coincidence forces singularity. The content of the theorem is the UPPER bound, which settled a long-standing conjecture: Komlos (1967) proved the probability is o(1), Kahn, Komlos and Szemeredi (1995) obtained 0.999^n, and Tao-Vu and Bourgain-Vu-Wood improved the base to (1/sqrt(2) + o(1))^n before Tikhomirov reached the conjectured (1/2 + o(1))^n. Note precisely what is claimed: the ENTRIES are independent uniform signs, and the statement is asymptotic in n with an o(1) in the base, so it gives no numerical bound at any fixed n. The analogous question for a random symmetric sign matrix is a separate problem, resolved later and by different methods, and the result stated here must not be quoted for it. [Tikhomirov (2020), 'Singularity of random Bernoulli matrices', Ann. of Math. 191; arXiv:1812.09016]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.166814+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_29e7b5f9dc670b6497726a5cf51f0d035fa1cc54b03c5456cb9804140ab77be5","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:ExpIneq of arXiv:2608.30848, '\huge \bf Limit Laws of the Iterated Logarithm Under Sub-linear Expectations'] Let $\{X_1,\ldots, X_n\}$ be independent random variables on $(\Omega, \mathscr{H}, \widehat{\mathbb E})$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:25:41.600184+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_29e88081c4183425d97ec94e0c5d6a78419e3b867616b1c2c6934d173267c5e0","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:generalized-mass-characterization of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] Let $\phi\in\mathcal{I}$ with $\phi^{-1}(\mathbb R_+)\neq\emptyset.$
Assume that either
\begin{equation*}
    \mu(X)<\infty
    \qquad\text{or}\qquad
    \phi\text{ satisfies }\hyperref[eq:LG]{\textup{(LG)}}{}.
\end{equation*}
The following statements are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[\rm(i)]
    \(G\) satisfies \hyperref[def:SC-infinity]{\textup{{(SC\textsubscript{$\infty$})}}}{}.

    \item[\rm(ii)]
    For every \(T>0\), every bounded positive pointwise solution \(u\) of the (eq:GPME of the paper) with initial datum \(u_0 \in \mathcal D_+\) satisfies \hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{} on \([0,T]\).

    \item[\rm(iii)]
    There exist \(T_0>0\) and a nonzero positive finitely supported
    \(u_*\) such that every bounded positive pointwise solution on
    \([0,T_0]\times X\) with initial datum \(u_*\)
    satisfies~\hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{}.

    \item[\rm(iv)]
    For some \(T_0>0\), every bounded positive pointwise solution on
    \([0,T_0]\times X\) with zero initial datum
    satisfies~\hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{}.
\end{enumerate}

If these conditions hold, then, for every solution \(u\) as in
\textup{(ii)}, the total mass \(\mathsf M_u\) is absolutely continuous
on \([0,T]\) and satisfies~(equation eq:differential-mass-balance of the paper) for
almost every \(t\in(0,T)\).

If \(G\) is not stochastically complete at infinity, then, for every
\(T>0\) and every \(u_0\in\mathcal D_+\), at least one bounded
positive pointwise solution with initial datum \(u_0\)
violates~\hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{}.  For \(u_0=0\), every
nontrivial bounded positive solution violates \hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{}.

When \(\mu(X)<\infty\), statement \textup{(iii)} may equivalently be
replaced by a constant-data test: There exist \(T_0>0\) and \(c_0 \in \mathbb R_+\)
such that every bounded positive solution with \(u_0= c_0\)
satisfies \hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{}.  Moreover, in the incomplete case, the violating
solution may be chosen for every constant datum \(u_0= c\), for
\(c\ge0\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:56:03.900551+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2a382e8ac7a732cceb4b43f95328694990b05356400c5c992a89761c8c3352ae","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 14 (From \cite{AEK2017}) of arXiv:2606.20816, 'Spectral Properties of Dense Barab\'asi--Albert Graphs'] Let $H = H^{(N)}$ be a self-adjoint $N \times N$ random matrix with centered, independent entries (up to symmetry). Set
\[
s_{k j}
\ := \
\E[\abs{h_{k j}}^2],
\qquad
S
\ = \
\left(s_{k j}\right)_{k, j = 1}^N.
\]
Assume the variance matrices $S^{(N)}$ satisfy the following.
\begin{itemize}
\item(A) Flatness: $s_{k j} \le C / N$ for all $k, j$, with a constant $C > 0$ that is independent of $N$.
\item(B) Uniform primitivity: there exist $p > 0$ and $L \in \mathbb{N}$ with $\left(S^L\right)_{k j} \ge p / N$ for all $k, j$.
\item(C) Bounded solution: the solution below obeys $\abs{m_k \left(z\right)} \le P$ for all $z$ in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}$ and all $k$.
\item(D) Moment bounds: $\E[\abs{h_{k j}}^b] \le \mu_b s_{k j}^{b / 2}$ for all $b \in \mathbb{N}$, all $k, j$.
\end{itemize}

Define the quadratic vector equation (QVE): for each $z \in \mathbb{H}$ there is a unique vector $\mathbf{m} \left(z\right) = \left(m_1 \left(z\right), \dots, m_N \left(z\right)\right) \in \left(\mathbb{H}\right)^N$ solving
\begin{equation}
-\frac{1}{m_k \left(z\right)}
\ = \
z + \sum_{j = 1}^N s_{k j} m_j \left(z\right),
\qquad k = 1, \dots, N,
\end{equation}
and $\Im m_k \left(z\right) > 0$ for $\Im z > 0$.

Define
\[
\rho^{(N)} \left(\tau\right)
\ := \
\frac{1}{\pi N} \sum_{k = 1}^N \Im m_k \left(\tau + i 0\right).
\]

As $N \rightarrow \infty$, the empirical eigenvalue distribution of $H$ converges to the deterministic measure with density $\rho^{(N)}$.

Continuous version: if in addition
\[
s^{(N)}_{k j}
\ = \
\frac{1}{N} f \left(\frac{k}{N}, \frac{j}{N}\right)
\]
for a bounded, symmetric, nonnegative $f : \left[0, 1\right]^2 \to \R_+$, then as $N \to \infty$ the discrete system converges to the continuous QVE
\begin{equation}
-\frac{1}{m \left(x; z\right)}
\ = \
z + \int_0^1 f \left(x, y\right) m \left(y; z\right) \, d y,
\qquad x \in \left[0, 1\right],\ z \in \mathbb{H},
\end{equation}
and the limiting eigenvalue density is
\begin{equation}
\rho \left(\tau\right)
\ = \
\frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^1 \Im m \left(x; \tau + i 0\right) \, d x,
\qquad \tau \in \R.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

Roughly speaking, it asserts that if each boundary vertex is associated with a highly probable event that is increasing with respect to the percolation configuration, then, conditionally on the origin being connected to the boundary, the origin is likely to be connected to a boundary vertex whose associated event occurs. The conjecture implies $\\theta(p_c)=0$ for Bernoulli bond percolation on $\\mathbb Z^d$, for every $d\\geq2$. We prove the conjecture for finite planar graphs when the origin and the boundary vertices lie on the outer-face boundary, with the explicit bound $1-2\\sqrt{\\varepsilon}$. The proof combines a left-first depth-first exploration with a partial FKG inequality adapted to monotonicity up to a stopping time. A counterexample shows that the connectivity structure is essential: the analogous statement fails when the connectivity events are replaced by arbitrary increasing events.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:19:46.237067+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2a878f8cfa7e1b1cdb0c13c1eb670712600455677aca1edf3a9555723814c7f5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 102 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] If $\pi \in \rm{Hom}(\G,G)$ and $x \in X$, then the \textbf{orbit map at $x$} is

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:04:39.767634+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2a87e7c11cc68431be1695678b8aef96d13786da0ee7d413ce6364ef4529e137","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] A \textbf{curved $A_\infty$-category} over $\mathbf k[[t]]$, $\cA$, is given by 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item a collection of objects $\mathrm{Ob}(\cA)$,
    \item for each pair $X,Y\in \mathrm{Ob}(\cA)$ a $\bZ$-graded $\mathbf k[[t]]$-module $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)$ such that each $\operatorname{Hom}^i(X,Y)$ is topologically free,
    \item for each $n\geq 0$ and $X_0,\ldots,X_n\in \mathrm{Ob}(\cA)$ a map of $\mathbf k[[t]]$-modules
    \[
    \mathfrak m_n\colon \operatorname{Hom}(X_{n-1},X_n)\otimes\cdots\otimes \operatorname{Hom}(X_0,X_1)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(X_0,X_n)
    \]

    \[

    \]
    hold, where $\|a\|\coloneqq |a|-1$.
    Moreover, we require the existence of strict units $1_X\in\operatorname{Hom}^0(X,X)$, $X\in\mathrm{Ob}(\cA)$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.230762+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2aaecc5984372324c5b9da2d23a38e1385e7a9d04ad6a1e82b5a295e873bcf1f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 24 (Formal period of the Gaussian-origin branch) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] For every support \(S\subset K\), the critical point \(u=0\) of
\(G_{K\mid S}\) extends uniquely to a formal critical section
\[
 u_{\mathrm G}(\rho,\boldsymbol\lambda)
 \in\rho^{m-1}\C[\boldsymbol\lambda][[\rho]]^{N_K}.
\]
Its critical action has no negative power:
\begin{equation}
 \rho^{-2}\Psi_{K\mid S}
 \bigl(\rho,u_{\mathrm G}(\rho,\boldsymbol\lambda)\bigr)
 \in\rho^{m-2}\C[\boldsymbol\lambda][[\rho]].
 
\end{equation}
After Gaussian density normalisation, the formal period of this local branch
is
\begin{equation}
 \widehat\Phi^{\mathrm G}_{P,K,\Sigma_K}
 (\rho,\boldsymbol\lambda)
 =
 \left.
 \exp\!\left(\frac12\Delta_{\Sigma_K\otimes I_d}\right)
 \exp\!\left(
  i\rho^{m-2}\sum_{a\in K}\lambda_aP(x_a)
 \right)
 \right|_{\boldsymbol x=0}.
 
\end{equation}
More generally, if
\(f(\rho,\boldsymbol u)\in
\C[\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol\lambda][[\rho]]\), define
\begin{equation}
 \ell_{K,\rho}
 \bigl([f(\rho,\boldsymbol u)\operatorname{vol}_{\boldsymbol u}]\bigr)
 =
 \left.
 \exp\!\left(\frac12\Delta_{\Sigma_K\otimes I_d}\right)
 \left(
  f(\rho,\rho\boldsymbol x)
  \exp\!\left(
   i\rho^{m-2}\sum_{a\in K}\lambda_aP(x_a)
  \right)
 \right)
 \right|_{\boldsymbol x=0}.
 
\end{equation}
This functional is well defined on \(\mathcal L_{K\mid S}\) and is
horizontal for the dual of the Gaussian-normalised radial connection.  Its value on
the constant class is \eqref{eq:central-Gaussian-Wick-series}; in
particular that series begins with \(1\) and is compatible with all maps

\eqref{eq:central-Gaussian-Wick-series} is the asymptotic expansion of the

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:49:05.348624+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2af3a838f6fa434d9951d91c8ed562acb91fe9151e255e7d6ea4fec0007e5176","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition defn:concatenation of arXiv:2601.07045, 'From Continuous to Discrete: \\ a No-U-Turn Sampler for Permutations'] Let $a, b, c \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $a \le b < c$, and fix $\rho \in S_n$ and $\sigma \in S_n$.  
Define two consecutive orbits generated by $\rho$ from $\sigma$:
\[
\mathcal{O} = (\sigma_a, \sigma_{a+1}, \dots, \sigma_b) \quad \text{and} \quad \widetilde{\mathcal{O}} = (\sigma_{b+1}, \dots, \sigma_c),
\]
where $\sigma_k = \sigma \circ \rho^k$ for $k \in [a:c]$.   The \emph{concatenation} of these orbits, denoted $\mathcal{O} \odot \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}$, is the combined sequence
\[
\mathcal{O} \odot \widetilde{\mathcal{O}} = (\sigma_a, \sigma_{a+1}, \dots, \sigma_c),
\]
with length $|\mathcal{O} \odot \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}| = c - a + 1$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:32:23.712347+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2af3b2cf94f3f72c87d49d11a3bd3dbd2710f2385faacbe0ac4bbc3d13eb2cbd","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition gammadef of arXiv:2603.20078, '\bf \Large Gated Infinite Server Queues in Light Traffic'] Suppose that $\sigma_i$ are i.i.d.\ random variables with density 
$g$ and finite moments of all orders. Let $f$ denote the invariant density of the 
stationary stage length, and suppose that $\beta_k:=\int_0^\infty x^k f(x) dx$, 
$k=1,2,\ldots$, denote its moments (which exist as shown in Proposition (prop:pi-moments of the paper)). 
Define the quantities
 \begin{equation} 
\gamma_{m,k} \;:=\; \mathbb{E}[\min(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\ldots,\sigma_k)^m].
\end{equation}
Then the moments $\{\beta_i\}$, $i=2,3,\ldots,$ satisfy the infinite linear system
\begin{eqnarray}  \nonumber
\beta_i &=& \gamma_{i,1} + \frac{\lambda^2 \beta_2}{2!} \, \left( \gamma_{i,1}-\gamma_{i,2} \right) 
- \frac{\lambda^3 \beta_3}{3!} \, \left( \gamma_{i,1}-\gamma_{i,3} \right) +\cdots
+(-1)^j \frac{\lambda^j \beta_j}{j!} \, \left( \gamma_{i,1}-\gamma_{i,j} \right) +\cdots \\ 
&& \hspace{4.1in} i=2,3,4,\ldots \;\;
\end{eqnarray}
The invariant density $f$ of the stage length can be expressed in terms of the moments 
$\{\beta_i\}$, the density $g$, and complementary distribution function $\overline{G}$ 
of the service time by the series
\begin{eqnarray}  \nonumber
f(y) &=& g(y)\,
 \left[ 1+ \frac{\lambda^2 \beta_2}{2!} \left(1- 2\overline{G}(y) \right) - \frac{\lambda^3 \beta_3}{3!} 
 \left( 1 - 3\overline{G}(y)^2 \right) \right. \\  
&& \hspace{2.3in} \left. + \frac{\lambda^4 \beta_4}{4!} \left( 1 - 4\overline{G}(y)^3 \right) - \cdots \right].
\end{eqnarray}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.973484+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2af5c0e5d170ca0b4b567bd6ee07fbb568c761ddbc5dfc6c547c69b6084484c7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 36 (Reader symbols and Yoneda factorization) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let $\mathscr A_r$ be a class of allowed boundary readers
$A:\partial_r\mathcal Y\to Z_A$, and put
\[
 K_{r,A}:=(\operatorname{Id}\otimes A)\mathfrak K_r(\mathcal R)
 \in G_r\otimes Z_A,
 \qquad
 S_r(\mathscr A):=
 \sum_{A\in\mathscr A_r}\operatorname{supp}_L(K_{r,A}).
\]
The total allowed response on $G_r^*$ is injective if and only if
\begin{equation}
 S_r(\mathscr A)=G_r.
 
\end{equation}
If $Z_A$ contains a fixed nonzero line $\mathbf k\tau_{r,A}$ and
$K_{r,A}=\sigma_A\otimes\tau_{r,A}$, then
\begin{equation}
 A\,\operatorname{gr}_r\mathcal R(q)
 =q(\sigma_A)\tau_{r,A}.
 
\end{equation}

coordinate form of the canonical response kernel.  The reader symbols detect
order $r$ exactly when they span $G_r$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:38:13.633212+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2aff2e73a27227ae72a3ee9c4672134c44c4675e191e9f5a7a8e46e3f020c9b2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 8 (Complete phase characterization) of arXiv:2609.00673, '2609.00673'] Let $n\ge3$ and let
\[
0<\theta_i<\pi\quad(1\le i\le n-1),\qquad
\phi_i\in(-\pi,\pi]\quad(1\le i\le n-2)
\]
be discrete Frenet data. These data arise from a discrete general helix with non-orthogonal axis if and only if there exist
\[
\alpha\in(0,\pi/2),\qquad
\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_{n-1}\in(-\pi/2,\pi/2)
\]
such that
\begin{align}
\tan\frac{\theta_i}{2}&=\tan\alpha\,\cos\psi_i,
\qquad 1\le i\le n-1,\\
\phi_i&\equiv \pi-\psi_i-\psi_{i+1}\pmod{2\pi},
\qquad 1\le i\le n-2,
\end{align}
where $\phi_i$ is represented in $(-\pi,\pi]$. For each chosen oriented helical direction $U$ with $T_i\cdot U>0$, the corresponding parameters $\alpha$ and $\psi_i$ are uniquely determined by that direction. If at least one torsion angle is different from $\pi$, the Frenet data determine the non-orthogonal helical direction, and hence the phase parameters, uniquely. On the fully alternating locus $\phi_i=\pi$ for every $i$, helical data necessarily have a constant turning angle; for such data the same Frenet data admit a one-parameter family of helical directions (see Remark~\ref{rem:branch-overlap}).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.359699+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2b1f7ad1992e8fdd7dfed1f47b063f35a69389766d5a1dedb0b1e17f698c0673","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 248 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Assume that $L\ge1$ and that condition \eqref{e:deriv.p.bound} holds. Let $\vX\equiv \vX^N$ be the process defined by \eqref{e:X.decomp}
and \eqref{e:Delta.X.Ising}, and assume that condition~\eqref{e:w2.coupling.assumption} holds. Then the processes $\vX^\trstar$ and $\vX^\frstar$ of Definitions~\ref{d:trunc} and \ref{d:froze} can be coupled so that
	\[
	\E\Big[\|\vX^\trstar(1)
		-\vX^\frstar(1)\|^2\Big]
	\le o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\]
uniformly in $N$.

\begin{proof}
Consider $\sigma\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$. Abbreviate 
	\[\epsilon(\trK)\equiv 
		\frac{1/\trK^6}
		{1+1/\trK^6}\,.\]
If we let $U$ denote a random variable sampled uniformly at random from the interval $[0,1]$, then 
$X^{\frstar,\sigma}(1)$ is equidistributed as
	\[
	X^{\frstar,\sigma}(1,U)
	\equiv
	\begin{cases} \displaystyle
	X^{\trstar,\sigma}\bigg(1,
		\bigg\lceil
		\frac{M\cdot U}{1-\epsilon(\trK)}
		\bigg\rceil\bigg)
	& \textup{if }U\in[0,1-\epsilon(\trK)]\,,\\
	T(U) & 
		\textup{if }U\in(1-\epsilon(\trK),1]\,,
	\end{cases}
	\]	
where $T$ is a random variable confined to $[-2\trK,2\trK]$. On the other hand, $X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1)$ is equidistributed as
	\[
	X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1,U)
	\equiv 
	\begin{cases} \displaystyle
	X^{\trstar,\sigma}\bigg(1,
		\bigg\lceil
		\frac{M\cdot U}{1-\epsilon(\trK)}
		\bigg\rceil\bigg)
	& \textup{if }U\in[0,1-\epsilon(\trK)]\,,\\ \displaystyle
	X^{\trstar,\sigma}\bigg(1,
		\bigg\lceil
		\frac{M\cdot 
			[U-(1-\epsilon(\trK))]}{\epsilon(\trK)}
		\bigg\rceil\bigg)
	&\textup{if } U\in(1-\epsilon(\trK),1]
	\end{cases}\,.
	\]
Under this coupling, we have
	\[\E\Big[(
	X^{\frstar,\sigma}(1,U)
	-X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1,U))^2
	\Big]
	\le O(1) \epsilon(\trK)
	\E\Big[
	T(U)^2 + X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1)^2\Big]\,.
	\]
Since $T(U)$ is confined to $[-2\trK,2\trK]$, we clearly have $\E[T(U)^2] \le 4\trK^2$. It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:martingale.sup.bound.X.II.III.Ising} that $X^\sigma(1)$ has bounded second moment for $\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$. Under condition~\eqref{e:w2.coupling.assumption}, it follows from Lemma~\ref{l:martingale.sup.bound.X.I.minus.mean} combined with \eqref{e:X.I.squared.expectation.avg.bound} that  $X^\RomI(1)$ also has bounded second moment. Combining with
Corollary~\ref{c:X.versus.trstar.X.W2.error.estimate} gives that $\vX^\trstar(1)$ has bounded second moment. Substituting into the above bound, and recalling the definition of $\epsilon(\trK)$, we conclude
	\[\E\Big[(
	X^{\frstar,\sigma}(1,U)
	-X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1,U))^2
	\Big]
	\le O(1) 
	\frac{\trK^2 + O(1)}{\trK^6}
	\le o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\]
which proves the claim for $\sigma\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:56:03.900376+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2b3bdc8d9f51cf44ad613f1ac39be4e8d3428fbc36a144b0a0262b9221766d4b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 12 (Variance kernel for the independent centered matrix) of arXiv:2606.20816, 'Spectral Properties of Dense Barab\'asi--Albert Graphs'] Let $H$ be the independent Poisson matrix from Proposition~\ref{prop:independent-poisson-comparison}, with $m = c n$ and fixed $c \in \left(0, \frac12\right)$. For $k > t_0 := m + 1$ and $j < k$, set
\[
p_{k j}
\ := \
\frac{d_j \left(k - 1\right)}{D_{k - 1}},
\qquad
D_{k - 1}
\ := \
\sum_{v=1}^{k-1} d_v \left(k - 1\right).
\]
Then
\[
\Var \left(H_{k j}\right)
\ = \
\E[p_{k j}],
\qquad
n \Var \left(H_{k j}\right)
\ = \
n \E[p_{k j}].
\]
Consequently, if $j/n \to x$ and $k/n \to y$, then
\begin{equation}
\sigma^2 \left(x, y\right)
\ := \
\lim_{n \to \infty} n \Var \left(H_{k j}\right)
\ = \
\frac{1}{c} F \left(x, y\right).
\end{equation}
Equivalently, with $A = \left[0, c\right]$, $B = \left(c, 1\right]$, and $u \left(t\right) = \left(2 t - c\right)^{-1 / 2}$,
\begin{equation}
\sigma^2 \left(x, y\right)
\ = \
\begin{cases}
0, & x, y \in A,\\[4pt]
\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{c}} u \left(y\right), & x \in A,\ y \in B,\\[8pt]
\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{c}} u \left(x\right), & x \in B,\ y \in A,\\[8pt]
u \left(x\right) u \left(y\right), & x, y \in B,
\end{cases}
\qquad
u \left(t\right)
\ = \
\left(2 t - c\right)^{-1 / 2}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:02:28.645967+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2b6cd8c8b379f21c2a75308b1f7ca7d1031c5f517bfa309884745562894c8439","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Def 19 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] For a linear system $\mcM$ on $X$, we denote by $n (\mcM)$ the positive rational number such that $\mcM \sim_{\mbQ} - n (\mcM) K_X$.
Let $\varphi \colon Y \to X$ be an extremal divisorial contraction.
We say that $\varphi$ is a \textit{Sarkisov extraction} if there is a Sarkisov link (in the Mori category) initiated by $\varphi$.
We say that $\varphi$ is a \textit{maximal extraction} if there is a movable linear system $\mcM$ such that $\ord_E (\mcM) > n (\mcM) a_X (E)$.
We say that $\varphi$ is a \textit{strong maximal extraction} if there is a movable linear system $\mcM$ on $X$ such that 
\[
\frac{1}{n (\mcM)} > c (X, \mcM) = \frac{a_X (E)}{\ord_E (\mcM)},
\]
where $c (X, \mcM)$ is the canonical threshold of the pair $(X, \mcM)$.

A subvariety $\Gamma \subset X$ is said to be a \textit{Sarkisov center} (resp.\ \textit{maximal center}, resp.\ \textit{strong maximal center}) if there is a Sarkisov extraction (resp.\ maximal extraction, resp.\ strong maximal extraction) $\varphi \colon Y \to X$ whose center is $\Gamma$.
We say that a subvariety $\Gamma \subset X$ is a \textit{weak maximal center} if there is a movable linear system $\mcM$ on $X$ such that $\Gamma$ is a center of non-canonical singularities of the pair $(X, \frac{1}{n (\mcM)} \mcM)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:49.560670+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2b71eff3caa1ffbf59e93572f7f40ca3f12968a1d9f498d9805731a69bde3f27","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defs 55 of arXiv:2509.06869, 'Infinite Interacting Brownian Motions and EVI Gradient Flows'] Let $\QP$ be a Borel probability measure on~$(\U, \tau_\mrmv)$.
\begin{itemize}
\item A locally Lebesgue-integrable function $f_\QP^{(k)}: \R^k \to \R_+$ is called {\it $k$-point correlation function} of $\QP$ if for any $m \in \N$, any disjoint bounded Borel subsets $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_m \subset \R$  and any $k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_m \in \N$ with $k=\sum_{i=1}^m k_i$, we have 
$$\int_{\U}\prod_{i=1}^m\frac{\mssn_{A_i}(\gamma)!}{(\mssn_{A_i}(\gamma)-k_i)!}\diff \QP(\gamma) = \int_{A_1^{\times k_1}\times \cdots \times A_m^{\times k_m} }f_\QP^{(k)}(x_1, \ldots, x_k)\diff x_1 \cdots \diff x_k \fstop$$
\item $\QP$ is (the law of) {\it a determinantal point process with kernel $K: \R^2 \to \mathbb C$} if $\QP$ has the $k$-point correlation function given by
$$f_\QP^{(k)}(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_k)={\rm det}\bigl[K(x_i, x_j)\bigr]_{i, j=1}^k \cquad k \in \N \fstop$$

\item $\sine_2$ is the determinantal point process whose kernel is 
$$K(x, y)=\frac{\sin(\pi(x-y))}{\pi(x-y)} \fstop$$
\item $\Airy_2$ is the determinantal point process whose kernel is 
$$K(x, y)=\frac{{\rm Ai}(x){\rm Ai}'(y)-{\rm Ai}'(x){\rm Ai}(y)}{x-y} \comma$$
where ${\rm Ai}'(x)=\frac{\diff {\rm Ai}(x)}{\diff x}$ and 
$$\Ai(x)=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^\infty\cos\Bigl(\frac{t^3}{3}+xt\Bigr) \diff t \fstop$$
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0031-almost-sure-convergence-in-the-heavy-tailed-circular-law","No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:26:45.040072+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2baefc2c0406d6c3a48185f5ac0c2336fe99679e75e852b557161bfbf121d0d6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Borel-Cantelli over the Hermitisation: identify which estimate is only in probability. Result: The proof of Theorem 6.2 has three inputs: (i) convergence of the singular-value distributions of n^{-1/alpha}X - z for each z, which is almost sure by the objective method (the local weak convergence to the PWIT holds a.s.); (ii) uniform integrability of log at infinity, a.s. from moment bounds; (iii) uniform integrability of log near zero, i.e. a lower bound on the small singular values, which is where only an in-probability bound s_n(n^{-1/alpha}X - z) >= n^{-c} with probability 1 - o(1) is available. To make (iii) almost sure one needs the failure probability summable in n, i.e. a bound like P(s_n <= n^{-c}) <= n^{-1-eps}. For heavy tails the row norms are not concentrated and the Rudelson-Vershynin small-ball argument gives only polynomial failure probabilities with exponent that is not obviously above 1. If the failure probability were shown to be O(n^{-1-eps}) (for instance via an Esseen-type anti-concentration in the alpha-stable domain, which gives exponent depending on alpha), Borel-Cantelli finishes the a.s. statement. So the problem reduces to a quantitative smallest-singular-value bound for heavy-tailed matrices with summable failure probability; the bound is plausible but I did not prove it. Obstruction: Need P(s_n(n^{-1/alpha}X - z) <= n^{-c}) summable in n for heavy-tailed entries.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T16:46:51.521012+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_2bbafc7b207a545087acfe35261c4470845f24f76e02fee6b19717d0a135d093","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In mathematics, particularly in differential topology, there are two Whitney embedding theorems, named after Hassler Whitney:The strong Whitney embedding theorem states that any smooth real m-dimensional manifold can be smoothly embedded in the real 2m-space, ⁠⁠ if m > 0. This is the best linear bound on the smallest-dimensional Euclidean space that all m-dimensional manifolds embed in, as the real projective spaces of dimension m cannot be embedded into real (2m − 1)-space if m is a power of two. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:33:01.744824+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2bc8e1ca609c146347695642f5f8fdf9e6a29b12d32e5716fc39a59d793352a6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 12 (Probability-generating function) of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The \textsc{pgf} of $T_{m,p}$ is
  \[
    G_{T_{m,p}}(z)
    \coloneqq \sum_{n=0}^\infty \PP \left(T_{m,p} = n\right) z^n
    = \left[
        \sum_{\ell=0}^m
        \binom{m-m/z}{\ell}
        (-1)^\ell
        \left(\frac{1}{1-p}\right)^\ell
      \right]^{-1}.
  \]
  As an analytic expression,
  both sides agree on an open ball around the origin
  with radius (strictly) greater than $1$,
  upon defining $G_{T_{m,p}}(0)$ by its limit $0$.
  \begin{proof}
    By Proposition \ref{thm:concatenation}, Remark \ref{rem:lgf is pgf},
    Lemma \ref{thm:H ogf} and Lemma \ref{thm:G ogf},
    \begin{align*}
      G_{T_{m,p}}(z) =
      \phi_J(z) = \frac{\phi_H(z)}{\phi_G(z)}
      &= \left(1-p\right)^m \binom{m/z - 1}{m}^{-1}
        \left[\sum_{\ell=0}^m \binom{m}{\ell} 
        \binom{m/z-1}{\ell}^{-1} \left(1-p\right)^\ell\right]^{-1} \\
      &= \left(1-p\right)^m
        \left[ \sum_{\ell=0}^m
        \binom{m/z - 1}{m}
        \binom{m}{\ell} 
        \binom{m/z-1}{\ell}^{-1} \left(1-p\right)^\ell\right]^{-1} \\
      &= (1-p)^m
        \left[
        \sum_{\ell=0}^m
        \frac{\left(m/z-1\right)^{\underline{m}} m^{\underline{\ell}}
        }{
          m! \left(m/z-1\right)^{\underline{\ell}}}
          \left(1-p\right)^\ell\right]^{-1}\\
      &= (1-p)^m
        \left[
        \sum_{\ell=0}^m
        \binom{m/z - \ell - 1}{m - \ell}
        \left(1-p\right)^\ell\right]^{-1}.
    \end{align*}
    Reverse the summation order via $\ell \mapsto m - \ell$
    then use $\binom{-\nu}{\ell} = (-1)^\ell \binom{\nu + \ell - 1}{\ell}$.
    This concludes the formal result.

    Let $E_k$ be the event that coupons
    $1, 2, \dots, m$ are collected on
    the days $k\,m + 1, k\,m+ 2, \dots, k\,m + m$ respectively.
    Then $\{ E_k \}_{k \geqslant 0}$ is a collection of
    independent events, each with positive probability $q = ((1-p)/m)^m$.
    The random variable $G = \inf_{k \geqslant 0} \1_{E_k}$
    is geometric with parameter $q$ and thus
    \[
      \PP(T_{m, p} = n) \leq \PP(T_{m, p} \geq n)
      \leq \PP(m\,G + m \geq n)
      = (1-q)^{\left\lceil\frac{n-m}{m}\right\rceil}.
    \]
    The radius of convergence is no less than $(1-q)^{-1/m} > 1$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f integrable on the circle (or on R^d)","claims about rates require stated regularity of f"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.264433+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis, common errors","id":"claim_2be4b7e12c3e3f49eba47dda81e2c6f8756b4f804878db25d11f6a85781b81a8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"What the lemma says: $f\\in L^1$ implies $\\hat f(n)\\to0$ (on $\\mathbb T$) or $\\hat f(\\xi)\\to0$ as $|\\xi|\\to\\infty$ (on $\\mathbb R^d$), with $\\hat f$ continuous and bounded by $\\|f\\|_1$. What it does not say. (i) No rate is implied: for every even sequence $(a_n)$ of nonnegative reals with $a_n\\to0$ that is convex for $n\\ge1$ ($a_{n-1}+a_{n+1}-2a_n\\ge0$), there is a nonnegative $f\\in L^1(\\mathbb T)$ with $\\hat f(n)=a_n$ for all $n$; taking $a_n=1/\\log(|n|+e)$ shows the decay can be as slow as one likes. So an estimate like $|\\hat f(n)|\\le Cn^{-\\alpha}$ must come from extra regularity: e.g. $\\alpha$-Holder continuity gives $|\\hat f(n)|\\le\\frac{C}{2}(2|n|)^{-\\alpha}$ via $\\hat f(n)=\\frac12\\int(f(x)-f(x+\\tfrac1{2n}))e^{-2\\pi inx}dx$, and bounded variation gives $|\\hat f(n)|\\le V(f)/(2\\pi|n|)$. (ii) The converse fails: not every null sequence is the sequence of Fourier coefficients of an $L^1$ function. For odd $f\\in L^1(\\mathbb T)$ with sine coefficients $b_n$, the series $\\sum_nb_n/n$ must converge; since $\\sum_{n\\ge2}\\frac1{n\\log n}=\\infty$, the everywhere-convergent series $\\sum_{n\\ge2}\\frac{\\sin(2\\pi nx)}{\\log n}$ is not the Fourier series of any integrable function. (iii) Consequently 'the coefficients tend to 0' is never evidence that a given trigonometric series is a Fourier series, and never by itself a convergence statement.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:49:05.364017+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2beb6ccfc1d6c7240d3b7c48e7081027b73d52380af595b28741bb3328db57af","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:Omegai of arXiv:2601.07045, 'From Continuous to Discrete: \\ a No-U-Turn Sampler for Permutations'] For a transposition $\tau_{ij} = (i\,j)$ with $1 \le i < j \le n$, define the
associated direction set
\[
  \Omega_{ij}
  :=
  \Bigl\{
    \eta = \tau_{ij} h :
    h \in S_{[n]\setminus\{i,j\}},
    \text{ and every cycle of } h \text{ has odd length}
  \Bigr\},
\]
where
\[
  S_{[n]\setminus\{i,j\}}
  :=
  \bigl\{\, h \in S_n : h(i)=i,\ h(j)=j \,\bigr\}
  \cong S_{n-2}.
\]
A permutation $\eta \in S_n$ is called \emph{shiftable} if
$\eta \in \Omega_{ij}$ for some $1 \le i < j \le n$. A direction law $q$ on $S_n$
is called shiftable if its support is contained in
\[
  \Omega := \bigcup_{1 \le i < j \le n} \Omega_{ij}.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Fixed integer d>=3 or d>=4 as specified, t downarrow0, noiseless bilinear Gaussian classifiers; standard coordinate-plane generators with unit operator norm; no dimension-uniform remainder asserted.","For the exact d4 formula additionally 0<t<pi.","No independent reviewer PASS has been received."],"created_at":"2026-10-22T02:43:15.572586+00:00","domain":"statistical learning theory","id":"claim_2bfbe9f5ac9b892595ae02a14536ccf15fa76fa102dbfd11dc7f313f881c1c05","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Own-work draft: T407-WEDGE-008 v2, proof (unaudited); not independently checked; priority unestablished.] For independent Gaussian a,b in R^d and wedges where sign((exp(tG)a) dot b) differs from sign(a dot b), a coordinate-plane tangent has probability c_d t+o(t), c_d=Gamma(d/2)/(2sqrt(pi)Gamma((d+1)/2)). Define $\mathcal B$ to be the set of branching nodes, $\mathcal L$ the set of leaves, and $\mathfrak r$ the root. We also write $\mathcal L_\mathfrak n=\mathcal L\cap \mathcal T_\mathfrak n$ and $\mathcal B_\mathfrak n=\mathcal B\cap\mathcal T_\mathfrak n$ etc. 
\item For $\mathfrak n\in\mathcal B$, define $\gamma_\mathfrak n=|\mathcal C_\mathfrak n|$ to be the number of children of $\mathfrak n$ (leaves are counted \emph{without} multiplicity; later we also need to treat leaves \emph{with multiplicity}, which will be clearly indicated below).
\item Finally, for $\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m'\in\mathcal T$, define $\mathfrak m\vee\mathfrak m'$ to be the lowest common ancestor of $\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak m'$. Note that $\mathfrak m\vee\mathfrak m'\in\mathcal L$ if and only if $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m'\in\mathcal L$; otherwise $\mathfrak m\vee\mathfrak m'\in\mathcal B$.
\end{enumerate}

We usually denote $r$ to be the total number of leaves of $\mathcal T$ without multiplicity; it is easy to see that $\sum_{\mathfrak n\in\mathcal B}(\gamma_\mathfrak n-1)=r-1$. We may also denote by $m=\sum_{\mathfrak l\in\mathcal L}m_\mathfrak l$ the total number of leaves of $\mathcal T$ with multiplicity (each leaf $\mathfrak l$ counted $m_\mathfrak l$ times).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:06:55.284971+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2c0da39cfb62b7939ff19dea1f031c1d23688d4ce73f53742bb5764d4e62bf02","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:transform_BR of arXiv:2601.08184, 'Wasserstein-p Central Limit Theorem Rates: From Local Dependence to Markov Chains'] Under the assumptions and notation of Lemma~(lem:BR_Hilbert of the paper), let
\((a_k)_{k\ge 1}\) be a real-valued predictable sequence, i.e.,
\(a_k\) is \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\)-measurable for each \(k\ge 1\). Define
\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:35:57.404345+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2c1141712ed3d71842739d3d9b1f518bd18c5feef162f7acab1587c4ed13a37e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] Let $d, n$ be positive integers and $d\le n/2$.  
    Let $M$ be an $n\times n$ random matrix where each row is independently and uniformly chosen from all $n$-dimensional binary vectors $\{0,1\}^n$ with exactly $d$ ones. Let $X$ denote the number of zero columns in $M$. Then the following holds.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Assume that $d=\log n - g(n)$ for some non-negative function $g$ satisfying $g(n) \longrightarrow \infty$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. Then,
        \[
        \lim_{n\to \infty} \mathbb{P}(X\ge 1)=1.
        \]
        That is, asymptotically (in $n$) the matrix $M$ almost surely has at least one zero column. In particular, it holds for 
        $d\le (1-\varepsilon)\log n$ (for  any fixed $\varepsilon>0$). 
        \item For any fixed $d\geq 1$ and fixed $\theta \in (0,1)$,
        \[
         \liminf_{n\to \infty} \mathbb{P}(X > \theta \mathbb{E} X ) 
         \geq (1-\theta)^2.
        \]
        In particular, 
        \[
         \liminf_{n\to \infty}\mathbb{P}(X>\theta  e^{-d} n /2) 
         \geq (1-\theta)^2,
        \]
        that is, for large enough $n$, the nullity of the matrix $M$ is bounded from below by  a constant proportion of $n$ with a positive probability.
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. real observations","no assumption whatsoever on F","the uniformity is over half-lines; for a general class of sets a complexity condition is required"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:40.782115+00:00","domain":"statistics","id":"claim_2c322d793604c5ad716d92397e36484a3a1c70d121206cb63e12642f98799942","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X_1, X_2, ... be i.i.d. real random variables with distribution function F, and let F_n(x) = (1/n) sum_{i <= n} 1{X_i <= x} be the empirical distribution function. Then sup_{x in R} | F_n(x) - F(x) | -> 0 almost surely. NO regularity of F is assumed: F may have atoms, may be singular, may be anything. The strong law alone gives only F_n(x) -> F(x) almost surely for each FIXED x, with a null set depending on x, and the union over uncountably many x of those null sets need not be null; the content of the theorem is that monotonicity upgrades pointwise convergence to UNIFORM convergence with a single null set. The quantitative companion is the Dvoretzky-Kiefer-Wolfowitz inequality, P( sup_x |F_n(x) - F(x)| > t ) <= 2 exp(-2 n t^2) with Massart's sharp constant 2, valid for every n and t. The abstract generalisation replaces the class of half-lines by a general class of sets or functions, and then a combinatorial condition such as finite Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension is required - uniform convergence over an ARBITRARY class of sets is false. [Glivenko and Cantelli (1933); Massart (1990) for the sharp DKW constant; see van der Vaart, Asymptotic Statistics, Theorem 19.1]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-05T05:50:37.944175+00:00","domain":"hierarchical estimation","id":"claim_2c4ac5aa20827fd32b69fb4dd3efa5783003321360a715b05cdb388b2eb6b0e2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Consider $D$ related regressions whose coefficient vectors $w_d \\in \\mathbb{R}^p$ are modelled hierarchically, $w_d = w_0 + \\delta_d$ with $\\delta_d \\sim N(0, T)$ independent across $d$, observed through $\\hat w_d = w_d + z_d$ with known noise $z_d \\sim N(0, \\Sigma_d)$ (the sampling covariance of row $d$'s least-squares estimate). The posterior mean of $w_d$ given $\\hat w_d$ is the matrix shrinkage $$\\tilde w_d = w_0 + T\\,(T + \\Sigma_d)^{-1}(\\hat w_d - w_0),$$ which shrinks fully in the directions where the prior spread $T$ is small relative to the noise and not at all where it is large. Empirical Bayes estimates the unknowns from the rows themselves: $w_0$ by the row mean (or by a pooled fit such as the global convex weights of a stacking problem), and $T$ from the row covariance of the residuals $\\hat w_d - w_0$, whose expectation is $T + \\bar\\Sigma$: with a common noise covariance one whitens by $\\bar\\Sigma^{-1/2}$, forms the $p \\times p$ residual covariance $\\hat R = \\frac{1}{D}\\sum_d r_d r_d^T$ of the whitened rows, and takes $\\hat T = (\\hat R - I)_+$ (eigenvalues below one set to zero - the same 'subtract the noise level, keep the positive part' as the spiked-covariance debiasing, now at the aspect ratio $p/D$ of the row covariance, which is a random-matrix problem in its own right). The scalar positive-part James-Stein rule toward $w_0$ is the special case $T \\propto \\Sigma$. Two facts decide whether the construction helps in practice: the noise model $\\Sigma_d$ must be right (under heteroscedastic residuals the homoscedastic $\\sigma_d^2 (X_d^T X_d)^{-1}$ can understate the noise by a large factor in the ill-conditioned directions, making the estimated amount of shrinkage collapse to zero where cross-validation would shrink substantially - the sandwich covariance is the repair), and the gain is a variance reduction only, so it is largest when the rows are noisy relative to their spread, i.e. at small calibration sizes.","status":"unverified"}

For $n\in\mathbbm Z$, let $(\mathfrak{m}_{n,\infty},\lambda_n)$ be the rooted submap of the UIBOT obtained by applying, as detailed in  Remark~(remark-kmsw-infinite of the paper), the KMSW procedure to $\mathfrak Z|_{[n,\infty)}$. 

The boundary of $\mathfrak{m}_{n,\infty}$ is the union of the root edge $\lambda_n$, the rightmost directed path in $\mathfrak{m}_{-\infty,\infty}$ from the terminal vertex of $\lambda_n$ to $\infty$, and the leftmost directed path in $\mathfrak{m}_{-\infty,\infty}$ from $-\infty$ to the initial vertex of $\lambda_n$. The edge $\lambda_n$ and the edges on the rightmost directed path are part of $\mathfrak{m}_{n,\infty}$ and form the right boundary of $\mathfrak{m}_{n,\infty}$, whereas the edges of the leftmost directed path are not, i.e.\ are missing edges, and form the left boundary of $\mathfrak{m}_{n,\infty}$. 

Furthermore, every vertex on the left boundary of $\mathfrak{m}_{n,\infty}$, including the initial vertex of $\lambda_n$, has at least one outgoing edge but no incoming edges (recall that missing edges are not oriented), while every other vertex of $\mathfrak{m}_{n,\infty}$ has at least one incoming and one outgoing edge. Finally, every pair of rightmost directed paths $P_x$ and $P_{x'}$ started from a pair of boundary vertices $x$ and $x'$ of $\mathfrak{m}_{n,\infty}$ coalesce into each other, i.e.\ there is some $s,s'>0$ such that $P_x(s+t)=P_{x'}(s'+t)$ for all $t\geq 0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:31:14.338711+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2c6cc831c2dcf60376624aa66723075205997760eced18a0e5f3ef5d3cacbb2b","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma macro BBM, lower bound of arXiv:2606.19207, 'Extrema of cooling branching Brownian motion and related Gaussian fields'] Consider a BBM $\{Z_t^v\colon t\in[0,\mathbf{T}],\ v\in\mathcal{N}_t^Z\}$ with branching rate $1$, binary splitting, and variance profile
	\[
	\sigma(t)=\widetilde{\sigma}(t/\mathbf{T}),
	\qquad t\in[0,\mathbf{T}],
	\]
	where $\widetilde{\sigma}\in C^2([0,1];(0,\infty))$ is strictly decreasing and $\inf_{u\in[0,1]}\widetilde{\sigma}(u)>0$. Let
	\[
	\eta(t):=\alpha_1\lvert\sigma'(t)\rvert^{2/3}\sigma(t)^{1/3},
	\]
	where $\alpha_1$ is given in (equation eqA: Airy eigenvalues of the paper). Then, for any $\beta\in(0,1/3)$, there exists $c>0$ such that
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb{P}\Bigl(
		\max_{v\in\mathcal{N}_T}Z_{\mathbf{T}}^v
		\le \int_0^{\mathbf{T}}
		\Bigl(\sqrt{2}\,\sigma(s)-\frac{\eta(s)}{\sqrt{2}}\Bigr)\,\text{d} s
		-\mathbf{T}^\beta
		\Bigr)
		\le \exp\{-c\mathbf{T}^\beta\},
	\end{equation}
	for all $\mathbf{T}$ large enough.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:59:58.454184+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2c6f036c779033a31faee765d96996df1fba330b1a65493c877b504a011249c5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Df $k$-tube of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$.
  A continuous map $\gamma\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[a,b]\to X$~(with $-\infty<a<b<\infty$) is called a \emph{$k$-tube} in $X$ if $\gamma$ is \emph{locally self-avoiding}; that is, for every $t\in[a,b]$, there exists a neighborhood $U\subset[a,b]$ of $t$ such that the restriction $\gamma|_{\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times U}$ is injective.
  If $\gamma$ itself is injective, then $\gamma$ is said to be \emph{self-avoiding}.
  The topological $(k-1)$-spheres $S=\gamma(\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times\{a\})$ and $S'=\gamma(\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times\{b\})$ are called, respectively, the \emph{initial sphere} and the \emph{terminal sphere} of $\gamma$ (the \emph{initial loop} and the \emph{terminal loop} of $\gamma$ when $k=2$).
  In this case, we further say that $S$ and $S'$ are \emph{joined} in $X$, and denote this by $S\overset X{\approx}S'$.
  (See Figure~(fig:tube of the paper).)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:23:37.803288+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2c788fd27e5df15edc9139a3632eb0ad69bbf8af0f5bf46a98c4d9e5840a8b25","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (Main results) of arXiv:2609.03593, '\textbf{New Homogeneous Einstein Metrics from Detection}'] The following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let
\[
 H=\Sp(p+q),\qquad K=\Sp(p)\times\Sp(q),\qquad
 M_{p,q}=(H\times H)/\Delta K,
\]
with $1\le p<q$.  The asymmetric two-factor family obtained by allowing the two horizontal
scales to vary independently contains an Einstein metric if and only if
\[
 q\ge15\quad (p=1),\qquad
 q\ge8p^2+5p+1\quad (p\ge2).
\]
For every admissible pair it is unique in that branch up to homothety and
interchange of the two horizontal factors.

\item For every $n=3$ or $n\ge5$, the space
\[
 \SU(n)^3/\Delta\SO(n)
\]
has exactly two Einstein metrics in the detected asymmetric branch up to
homothety.  They are pairwise non-isometric; neither is naturally reductive
with respect to any connected transitive group of isometries.

\item For
\[
 \SU(2n)^3/\Delta\Sp(n),\qquad n\ge2,
\]
there is a sharp threshold at $n=22$: the detected asymmetric branch contains
no positive Einstein metric for $2\le n\le21$ and exactly two up to homothety
for $n\ge22$.  For $n\ge22$ the two metrics are pairwise non-isometric.

\item Each of
\[
 E_6^3/\Delta\Sp(4),\qquad
 E_7^3/\Delta\SU(8),\qquad
 E_8^3/\Delta\SO(16)
\]
has exactly two Einstein metrics in the detected asymmetric branch up to
homothety.  In each case the twto metrics are pairwise non-isometric and are
not naturally reductive with respect to any connected transitive group of
isometries.

\item On
\[
 M_9=\SU(18)^4/\Delta\Sp(9),
\]
the $3+1$ and $2+2$ fixed families studied in this paper contain, up to
homothety and their internal block permutations, exactly three asymmetric
Einstein metrics: two of type $3+1$ and one of type $2+2$.  The three metrics
are pairwise non-isometric under arbitrary Riemannian isometries, are
Riemannian irreducible, and are not naturally reductive with respect to any
connected transitive group of isometries.  The $2+2$ metric is globally
unique in the positive $2+2$ fixed family up to homothety and interchange of
the two blocks.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:19:00.888843+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2c7c5dabc4f2ab069043a623114d837eca7042d09aaa9bf347e78fbdaabb7665","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 48 (Per-step form of the multi-prior coincidence divergence) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] Let $\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_W$ be path priors on $\Omega_T$ (different models, time scales, or modalities), let $\rho$ be a posterior path measure, and let $\alpha \in \Delta([W])$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:multi-PAC} holds verbatim for these path measures, and its coincidence divergence resolves by time:
\begin{equation}
  \cC_\alpha(\pi_{1:W})
  = -\log \E_{Q^*}\!\Bigl[\,\prod_{t=1}^T z_t\,\Bigr]
  \;\le\; \sum_{t=1}^T \E_{Q^*}\!\left[
      \min_{\widetilde q_t}\sum_w \alpha_w\,\KL(\widetilde q_t\|\pi_{w,t})
    \right],
\end{equation}
where $\pi_{w,t}$ is the conditional of $\pi_w$ at time $t$,
$z_t(x_{1:t-1})=\int\prod_w\pi_{w,t}^{\alpha_w}$ is the local normalizer (so that the per-step minimum equals $-\log z_t$), and $Q^*=\prod_t\bigl(\prod_w\pi_{w,t}^{\alpha_w}/z_t\bigr)$ is the sequential geometric-mixture path measure.
The inequality is Jensen's, so it is tight exactly when $\prod_{t=1}^T z_t$ is $Q^*$-almost surely constant; it suffices that each $z_t$ be free of the history, which holds whenever every prior is a product measure over time, $\pi_w=\bigotimes_{t=1}^T \pi_{w,t}$ with $\pi_{w,t}$ not depending on $x_{1:t-1}$.
In that case $\cC_\alpha(\pi_{1:W})=\sum_{t=1}^T\cC_\alpha(\pi_{1:W,t})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.162577+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2cb88ae55b4b1978d381b4c799a79a9809cfd94fdb352ce7ad68c2052bd365fc","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 20 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $C$ be as in \eqref{e:wishart.bound.repeated}.
    Fix any realization of $\bG$ satisfying
    \beq
    
    \max\bigg\{
       \frac{ \|\bG\|_{\op}}{C},
       \frac{\|\bar{\bx}\|}{2}
      \bigg\} \le N^{1/2}\,.
    \eeq
For such $\bG$, we have the following:
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item  Under the additional constraint that $\bXi$ satisfies
        \beq
            
            \frac{\|\bXi\|_{\op}}{N^{1/2}}
             \le C\,,
        \eeq
        the function
$\by \mapsto F^{\ri}(\bG,\bXi,\by)$,
        restricted to the domain $\{\|\by\| \le 2 N^{1/2}\}$, is $O(N^{-1/2})$-Lipschitz.
        \item 
Restricted to the (convex) domain \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bXi-event},
the function
        \beq
        
            \bXi \mapsto F^{\ri}(\bG,\bXi,\ytrunc(\bG,\bXi))\,,
        \eeq
         is $O(N^{-1/2})$-Lipschitz.
    \end{enumerate}
Consequently, for any realization of $\bG$ satisfying \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bG-event}, there exists a function $\tilde{F}(\bXi;\bG)$ which is $O(N^{-1/2})$-Lipschitz in $\bXi$, and agrees with the function
\eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-fn-bXi} on the set of $\bXi$ satisfying \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bXi-event}.

\begin{proof}
Fix $\bG$, $\bXi$ satisfying \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bG-event}, \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bXi-event}. Recalling \eqref{e:F.B}--\eqref{e:F.w}, we calculate
    \begin{align*}
    \nabla_\by F_B(\bG,\bXi,\by)
    &=
    \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hB_j}{MN|B_j|}
        \bigg(\sum_{a\in B_j} \bmeta^a, \by \bigg)
        \bigg(\sum_{a\in B_j} \bmeta^a \bigg)\,,\\
            \nabla_\by F_v(\bG,\bXi,\by)
    &=\sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hv_j}{M}
        \sum_{a\in B_j}
        \frac{(\barbg^a,\by) \barbg^a}{N}
    \\
            \nabla_\by F_U(\bG,\bXi,\by)
    &=
    \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hU_j}{M|B_j|}
        \bigg(
            \sum_{a\in B_j}
            \frac{(\bmeta^a,\bar{\bx})(\barbg^a,\by)}{N}
        \bigg)\bigg(
            \sum_{a\in B_j}
            \frac{(\bmeta^a,\bar{\bx})\barbg^a}{N}
        \bigg)\\
            \nabla_\by F_w(\by)
    &=\sum_{j=1}^s\frac{2\hw_j}{N} \Pi_j \by\,.

{"assumptions":["(G_n) decreasing with intersection G_infinity","Y integrable, or (X_n) a backward martingale with X_0 integrable"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.627382+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_2cc2222ab16695a55dfeff86ffc172230befd9f45d112c7f7776ea4b190fd13c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (G_n)_{n >= 0} be a DECREASING family of sub-sigma-algebras, G_0 containing G_1 containing G_2 and so on, and let G_infinity be their intersection. For Y in L^1, E[Y | G_n] converges almost surely and in L^1 to E[Y | G_infinity]. More generally a BACKWARD MARTINGALE, a family (X_n) with X_n G_n-measurable and E[X_n | G_{n+1}] = X_{n+1}, converges almost surely and in L^1 - and unlike the forward case NO extra hypothesis is required, because a backward martingale is automatically uniformly integrable: X_n = E[X_0 | G_n] is a family of conditional expectations of one integrable variable. This asymmetry with the forward theorem is the point: forward martingales need an L^1 bound for almost sure convergence and uniform integrability for L^1 convergence, backward martingales need neither. The classical application is the strong law of large numbers: with S_n the partial sums of an i.i.d. integrable sequence and G_n the exchangeable sigma-algebra generated by S_n, S_{n+1}, ..., one has E[X_1 | G_n] = S_n/n, so S_n/n converges almost surely and in L^1, and the Hewitt-Savage 0-1 law identifies the limit as E[X_1]. [standard; e.g. Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Theorem 4.6.1]","status":"unverified"}
