\]
Let $D\in M_n(\mathbb R)$ be a deterministic diagonal matrix with $D\succeq I_n$ and let $A\in M_n(\mathbb R)$ be a normalized GOE matrix.

Let $\xi>1$ be fixed and let $L,C',c,C>0$ be the constants from \pref{cor:AIk+Bk-final-bound} (applied with this $\xi$).
Define deterministic sequences
\[
\eta_n \,:\, =C'(\log n)^{L}\,n^{-1/3},
\qquad
\delta_n \,:=\, \frac{1}{\log n},
\qquad
\theta_n \,:=\, 2+\eta_n+\delta_n.
\]
Let
\begin{equation}

\end{equation}
where $\zeta_A$ is as in \pref{cor:AIk+Bk-final-bound}. Then $\mathop{{}\mathbb{P}}\Omega_\gamma^c \;\leqslant\; C e^{-c(\log n)^\xi}$.
Assume that $n$ is large enough that $n^2\mathop{{}\mathbb{P}}\Omega_\gamma^c$ is bounded by some positive rational function of $\beta$ and $1/\gamma$ and also
\begin{equation}

\beta\bigl((\theta_n+\delta_n)-2\bigr) \;\leqslant\; \gamma.
\end{equation}

Let $F := F_{\beta,-D}$ be the complex analytic subordination function in \pref{lem:subordination-semicircular}.
Then $F$ extends analytically to $a$, and there exists a universal constant $C_0>0$ such that
\begin{equation}

\mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}_A\!\left[E_{\mathcal D_n}\bigl[D(aI_n-\beta A+D)^{-2}D\bigr]\,\mathds{1}_{\Omega_\gamma}\right]
\,-\,
F'(a)\,D\bigl(F(a)I_n+D\bigr)^{-2}D
}
 \leqslant\
\frac{C_0\,\beta^4}{n^{3/2}\gamma^6}
\;+\;
\frac{C_0\,\beta^2}{n\gamma^4}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:33:01.745954+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_34eded4e47fda8bfa953967f1708fed3055331411980a025ddafe2c472a1c787","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] Within our coupling of the collection times (Definition~\ref{def:coupling}),
  $T_{m,0}$ is independent of $T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}$ and this difference
  has \textsc{mgf}
  \[
    M_{T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}}(t) = I_{m, p}(t), \quad t \leqslant 0.
  \]
  \begin{proof}
    If $T_{m, 0} = k$, then the value of $T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}$
    is a deterministic function of the initial clumsiness $\{ U_{L(i,k)} \}_{i \in [m]}$,
    the future updates $\{ C_n \}_{n > k}$,
    and the future clumsiness $\{ U_n \}_{n > k}$. Call this function $f$.
    We will make $f$ explicit. Consider an initial clumsiness vector
    $\mathbf{x} = (x_1, \dots, x_m)^\top \in [0, 1]^m$,
    coupon updates $\mathbf{y} = (y_n)_{n > 0} \in [m]^\mathbb{N}$,
    and future clumsiness $\mathbf{z} = (z_n)_{n > 0} \in [0, 1]^\mathbb{N}$.
    Then define
    $L'(i, n; \mathbf{y})$ as the most recent update of coupon $i$
    no later than $n$,
    \[
      L'(i, n; \mathbf{y}) \coloneqq
      \sup\{ k \leqslant n \mid y_k = i \}, \quad
      i \in [m], \quad n \geqslant 0,
    \]
    where naturally $\sup\emptyset = -\infty$ and $L'(i, 0; \mathbf{y}) = -\infty$.
    Define
    \begin{align*}
      f(\mathbf{x}; \mathbf{y}; \mathbf{z})
      \coloneqq \inf \{ n \geqslant 0 \mid {} &\text{for all $i \in [m]$,}\\
          &\text{if $x_i > 1-p$ or $L'(i, n; \mathbf{y}) > 0$,}\\
          &\text{then $L'(i, n; \mathbf{y}) > 0$
          and $z_{L'(i, n; \mathbf{y})} \leq 1-p$}
          \}.
    \end{align*}
    Thus, for any integers $\ell \geqslant m$ and $x \geqslant 0$,
    \begin{align*}
      \PP\left( T_{m,p} - T_{m,0} = x \right)
      &= \sum_{k \geqslant m}
        \PP\left( T_{m,p} - T_{m,0} = x \mid T_{m,0} = k\right)
        \PP(T_{m,0} = k)\\
      &= \sum_{k \geqslant m} \PP\left(f(U_{L(1, k)}, \dots, U_{L(m, k)};
      C_{k+1}, C_{k+2}, \dots;
      U_{k+1}, U_{k+2}, \dots) = x\right)\\
      &\qquad \qquad \qquad \times \PP\left(T_{m,0} = k\right)\\
      &= \sum_{k \geqslant m} \PP\left(f(U_{L(1, \ell)}, \dots, U_{L(m, \ell)};
      C_{\ell+1}, C_{\ell+2}, \dots;
      U_{\ell+1}, U_{\ell+2}, \dots) = x\right)\\
      &\qquad \qquad \qquad \times \PP\left(T_{m,0} = k\right)\\
      &= \PP\left(f(U_{L(1, \ell)}, \dots, U_{L(m, \ell)};
      C_{\ell+1}, C_{\ell+2}, \dots;
      U_{\ell+1}, U_{\ell+2}, \dots) = x\right)\\
      &\qquad \qquad \qquad \times \underbrace{
        \sum_{k \geqslant m} \PP\left(T_{m,0} = k\right)
      }_1\\
      &= \PP\left(T_{m,p} - T_{m,0} = x \mid T_{m,0} = \ell\right).
    \end{align*}
    The third line uses our i.i.d.~assumptions from

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:45:01.844023+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_34fae5bbd6b1f32ae977dc738117c6c6ef5102386e59411bed35c851f3c25624","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2512.18435, 'Indistinguishability for recurrent clusters'] A \\textbf{tail component property} is a component property $\\mathscr A$ such that if $\\omega$ and $\\omega'$ are two percolation configurations with environments $\\eta$ and $\\eta'$ such that $\\eta$ and $\\eta'$ differ only at finitely many sites or edges, and the clusters of $o$ in $\\omega$ and $\\omega'$ are infinite and have a finite symmetric difference, then either $o$ has type $\\mathscr A$ in both $\\omega$ and $\\omega'$, or in neither.\n\n    We call a component property $\\mathscr A$ \\textbf{essentially tail} if there exists a tail component property $\\mathscr A'$ with $\\mathbb P(\\{(\\eta,x)\\in\\mathscr A\\}\\bigtriangleup\\{(\\eta,x)\\in\\mathscr A'\\})=0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:36:44.551748+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_34fd9fae7b41cda5283a1108094a574e2c1ee96b6cfe04afedd622806387eefe","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2604.01978, 'Homogenized Transformers'] Fix $i,j\in[n]^2$ and define
\(
R_{ij}(t)\coloneqq \langle x_i(t),x_j(t)\rangle.
\)
We have
\begin{equation}
\de R_{ij}(t)
=
\de M_{ij}(t)
+
\cD_{ij}(t)\,\de t,
\end{equation}
where the local martingale part is
\begin{equation}
\de M_{ij}(t)
=
\int_\Uptheta
\left(\langle G_i(t,\bm{\theta}),x_j(t)\rangle+\langle x_i(t),G_j(t,\bm{\theta})\rangle\right)
\,\mathsf{W}(\de\bm{\theta},\de t),
\end{equation}
and the drift is
\begin{align}
\cD_{ij}(t)
&=
\frac1d\left(d-2+R_{ij}(t)^2\right)\,s_{\mu(t)}(x_i(t),x_j(t))\nonumber\\
&-
\frac{(d-1)}{2d}\,R_{ij}(t)\left(s_{\mu(t)}(x_i(t))+s_{\mu(t)}(x_j(t))\right),
\end{align} 
where $\mu(t) = \mu_{X(t)}$ and 
\begin{align*}
s_\mu(x)&\coloneqq \E\left\|\mathsf{m}_{\upbeta,\bA}[\mu](x)\right\|^2,\nonumber\\
s_\mu(x,x')&\coloneqq \E\left\langle \mathsf{m}_{\upbeta,\bA}[\mu](x),\mathsf{m}_{\upbeta,\bA}[\mu](x')\right\rangle.
\end{align*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T01:47:04.949102+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_35140157bd19549c382ac82b71ad229e12a89dd84d8efcf51fb0b1de901dd797","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm-omni-intro of arXiv:2412.03067, 'Geodesic Trees and Exceptional Directions in FPP on Hyperbolic Groups'] $ $

\emph{uncountably many} exceptional directions (Theorem~(thm-uncountable of the paper)).

on the  multiplicity of an exceptional direction (in the sense of Question~(qn-exceptionaldirn of the paper)(3)) (Theorem~(t:finite of the paper)).

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:17:17.060981+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3515ce152b34b5963b7d05c50c165f2995ae5c14e1dc2fc693ff1e6b2b6c5437","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Let $X$ be an $\R^d$-valued conservative Markov process reversible with respect to a

observable.  Suppose that conditions \textbf{(I)}-\textbf{(V)} above

\[

    \lambda'(\beta_\theta)=\theta,

\[

    \qquad
    I_Q(\theta)
       =\lambda(\beta_\theta)-\beta_\theta\theta.

Then, for every fixed initial state $x$ and every fixed $z\in\mathbb R$,
\[

\]
in total variation.  The corresponding fixed-width conclusion of

 For arbitrary initial values $s_1,\hat{s}_1  \in \mathbb{R}$, consider the implicit stochastic approximations
$$\frac1n h(X_n - s_n) + s_{n-1} = s_n $$
and
$$
\frac1n h(X_n - \hat{s}_n) + h(\hat{s}_{n-1}-\hat{s}_n) = 0.
$$
The resulting sequences $\{s_n\}_{n \geq 1}$ and $\{\hat{s}\}_{n \geq 1}$ both converge to $0$ almost surely, given that in the case of the second iteration $\{\hat{s}\}_{n \geq 1}$, we additionally have that $h^{-1}$ exists and satisfies $$h^{-1}(x)=x+O(x^2)$$ in a neighborhood of $0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:00:46.830692+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_352bcb0176a874149a430827a3caaaa4e8a7b827381e3621add30a35fa673a9d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2608.13358, 'Extreme points of sets of probability measures and $\phi$-divergences'] Assume that $\cI=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ for some $n\in \N$. Then, for $p\in \cM$, the following statements are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $p$ is an extreme point of $\cM$.
    \item There exist $m\in \N$, coefficients $\alpha_1,\ldots, \alpha_m>0$, and pairwise disjoint $p$-atoms $A_1,\ldots, A_m\in \cF$ such that
    \[
    p=\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_j\, p_{A_j}
    \]
    and the matrix
    \[
    \left(\begin{matrix}
    1 & \dots & 1 \\
    f_1(A_1) & \dots & f_1(A_m) \\
    \vdots & & \vdots \\
    f_n(A_1) & \dots & f_n(A_m)
    \end{matrix}\right)
    \]
    has rank $m$, i.e., the vectors
    \[
    v_j:=\big(1,f_1(A_j),\ldots,f_n(A_j)\big)^\top\in\R^{n+1},
    \qquad j=1,\ldots,m,
    \]
    are linearly independent. In particular, extremality forces $m\leq n+1$.
    \item $p$ is $\ll$-minimal in $\cM$.
    \item For every $p'\in\cM\setminus\{p\}$, every $q\in\cM$ with $p\ll q$ and $p'\ll q$, and every convex function $\varphi\colon[0,\infty)\to\R$ satisfying \eqref{eq:phi:blowup},
    one has
    \[
    \lim_{\lambda\uparrow 1}\frac{\Div{\varphi}{\lambda p+(1-\lambda)p'}{q}-\Div{\varphi}{p}{q}}{1-\lambda}=-\infty.
    \]
    In particular, $\lambda=1$ is a strict local maximizer of the map
    \begin{equation*}
        [0,1]\to[0,\infty),\quad \lambda\mapsto\Div{\varphi}{\lambda p+(1-\lambda)p'}{q}.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:15:54.966277+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_35384028510594e8fbb549e1c83a1dfa39a340dc28bd2e477f393918a208f82c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:basic-lewis-logics of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] {litak_lewis_2018}}] 
  Consider the following rule and axiom schemes:
  \begin{align*}
    \textsf{N}_a  &: \quad \frac{\varphi \to \psi}{\varphi \lewis \psi}, \\
    \textsf{Tr}   &: \quad (\varphi \lewis \psi) \to ((\psi \lewis \chi) \to (\varphi \lewis \chi)), \\
    \textsf{K}_a  &: \quad (\varphi \lewis \psi) \to ((\varphi \lewis \chi) \to (\varphi \lewis (\psi \land \chi))), \\
    \textsf{Di}   &: \quad (\varphi \lewis \chi) \to ((\psi \lewis \chi) \to ((\varphi \lor \psi) \lewis \chi)), \\
    \textsf{Box}  &: \quad (\varphi \lewis \psi) \to \Box(\varphi \to \psi).
  \end{align*}
  We define:
  \begin{align*}
    \textbf{HLC}^\flat  &\coloneq \textbf{Int} + \textsf{N}_a + \textsf{Tr} + \textsf{K}_a, &
    \textbf{HLC}^\sharp &\coloneq \textbf{HLC}^\flat + \textsf{Di}, \quad \\
    \textbf{i-Box}      &\coloneq \textbf{HLC}^\sharp + \textsf{Box}.
  \end{align*}
  Following the notation in [visser_lewis_2024,groot_relational_2026],
  a $\textsf{Di}$-free logic is generally marked with a superscript $\flat$,
  and its extension by $\textsf{Di}$ with a superscript $\sharp$.\footnote{
    Litak and Visser [litak_lewis_2018] denote $\textbf{HLC}^\flat$ and $\textbf{HLC}^\sharp$
    by $\textbf{iA}^-$ and $\textbf{iA}$, respectively.
    Accordingly, their flat versions of the extensions below carry a superscript minus,
    while their sharp versions carry no superscript.}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.593854+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_353fc364bd67ffc2318ca26b389201b563c7c6cb4dbdc98ab902441c083a9b37","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.02682, 'LDP for tensor forms'] In this paper, we study the large deviation principle (LDP) for a tensor-weighted functional of i.i.d. random variables, when the sequence of tensors converges under a variant of the \\enquote{bad} cut norm. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:49.842503+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_353fce2171a8628b0af92a22f95bffdb556538eed95fac9c5e3bbcc4db6f6ba9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2506.13913, '2506.13913'] {Fundamental Properties of the Itô Integral}{}
Let \(f, g \in L^2([0, T] \times \Omega)\) be processes adapted to \(\mathcal{F}_t\), and let \(a, b \in \mathbb{R}\). Then

   \begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Linearity.} The Itô integral is linear, i.e., 
    \[
    \int_0^T \big(a f(t) + b g(t)\big) \, \mathrm{d}W_t = a \int_0^T f(t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t + b \int_0^T g(t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Isometry.} The Itô integral satisfies the isometry property, i.e., 
    \[
    \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_0^T f(t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t\right)^2\right] = \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^T f(t)^2 \, \mathrm{d}t\right].
    \]

    \item \textbf{Martingale Property.} The process
    \[
    M_t = \int_0^t f(s) \, \mathrm{d}W_s, \quad t \in [0, T],
    \]
    is a martingale with respect to the filtration \((\mathcal{F}_t)\).

    \item \textbf{Quadratic Variation.} The quadratic variation of the Itô integral is given by
    \[
    \left[\int_0^t f(s) \, \mathrm{d}W_s\right]_t = \int_0^t f(s)^2 \, \mathrm{d}s.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Zero-Mean Property.} The expectation of the Itô integral is zero, i.e., 
    \[
    \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^T f(t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t\right] = 0.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:06:39.270499+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_35531d9c88c835147c911c63490c4a99315674f3a15fa236c1333c03b1a50e7c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:density_profiles of arXiv:2607.08914, 'Linear spreading speed in non-monotone population models'] For given $\varepsilon, \delta  >0$ and $k_0 \in \mathbb{N}$, \emph{comparison

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:40:59.390819+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3566cfcea565dcc90c2ef3957ae194e5f79097f27f5814eeae0ec4f8cce61df4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 15 (Admissible Targeted Local-Time Markov Family) of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian burg'] The family of laws $(\Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_0})$ is \emph{regular} if it satisfies the following conditions :
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Stretching Covariance:} If $g$ is a stretching morphism from $\lambda$ to $g(\lambda)$, then $g$ pushes forward $\Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_0}$ to $\Pb^{g(\lambda)}_{g(x) \to g(x_0)}$, i.e.\ if $X\sim \Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_0}$, then $g(X)\sim \Pb^{g(\lambda)}_{g(x) \to g(x_0)}$.
\item \textbf{Symmetry:} If $X\sim \Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_0}$, then $-X\sim \Pb^{\tilde \lambda}_{-x \to -x_0}$, where $\tilde \lambda$ is the symmetric of the capacity $\lambda$ on the interval $I$, i.e.\ $\tilde \lambda(x) = \lambda(-x)$ for $x\in -I$.
\item \textbf{Local-Time Markov Property:} If $(X_t)_{0 \le t \le T(X)} \sim \Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_0}$, then for any finite stopping time $T$ for the filtration of $X$, conditionally on $X_T$ and $\lambda_T$, we have $(X_{T+t})_{0\le t \le T(X)-T}\sim\Pb^{\lambda_T}_{X_T \to x_0}$ independently on $\F_T$.
\item \textbf{Side-Locality:} If $X\sim \Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_1}$ and $X'\sim \Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_2}$ with $x<x_1<x_2$, then $X$ and $X'$ have same law until reaching $x_1$, i.e.\ in the same time-parametrization, $$\left( X_t \right)_{0 \le t \le \tau_{x_1}}  \overset{(d)}{=}  \left( X'_t \right)_{0 \le t \le \tau'_{x_1}}.$$

\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:05:28.080749+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_357284b985ff888d2c1c29af9510420130262d1665162bbe9a236df7a5cd3cbf","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem maintheorem2 of arXiv:2601.20502, 'Optimal matching under size priority'] Let $G_n=(V_n,E_n)$ be a sequence of random graphs and choose a root $\overset{\rightarrow}{o}_n$ uniformly among the vertices.
    Suppose that the sequence of rooted weighted random graphs $(G_n,o_n)$ converges locally to an (vertex-rooted) Unimodular Bienaymé-Galton-Watson (UBGW) tree $(\mathbb{T},o)$ with reproduction law $\pi$. Now assign i.i.d weights $(w_n(e))_{e \in E(G_n)}$ of distribution $\omega$ on the edges of $G_n$. We have
    \begin{enumerate}

         \[

        \item Reciprocally, for any sequence $(M_n)_n$ of matchings of $G_n$, take $(a,b)$ to be any subsequential limit of

        then we must have that

        \]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:27:56.768571+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3592f0d92e3023c80526b84d36186dc6b64b548b7964ed67597be9b5d67d3f94","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2608.31168, 'The anisotropic Michael-Simon inequality for surfaces in every codimension'] Given a unit direction $e \in \bS^{m-1}$, we consider the strip
\[
\cU^e_j := \{ x \in \bR^m : j \leq \la x, e \rg \leq j+1 \}.
\]
Let $\gamma : [a,b] \to \cU_j^e$ be a Lipschitz curve and write $\dot{\gamma}(t)^{\perp} := \dot{\gamma}(t) - \la \dot{\gamma}(t), e \rg e$.
Then it holds that
\[
\int_a^b ( \la \dot{\gamma}(t), e \rg - |\dot{\gamma}(t)^{\perp}| )_+ \, dt \leq 1 + \int_a^b ( \la \dot{\gamma}(t), e \rg - |\dot{\gamma}(t)^{\perp}|)_- \, dt.
\]
Moreover, if $\la \gamma(b) , e \rg \leq \la \gamma(a), e \rg$, and in particular if the curve is closed, we have
\[
\int_a^b ( \la \dot{\gamma}(t), e \rg - |\dot{\gamma}(t)^{\perp}| )_+ \, dt \leq \int_a^b ( \la \dot{\gamma}(t), e \rg - |\dot{\gamma}(t)^{\perp}|)_- \, dt.
\]
Finally, given any non-negative function $h \in W^{1,1}([a,b])$ with $\min h = 0$, we have
\[
\int_a^b h(t) \, ( \la \dot{\gamma}(t), e \rg - |\dot{\gamma}(t)^{\perp}|)_+ \, dt \leq \int_a^b |h'| \, dt + \int_a^b h(t) \, ( \la \dot{\gamma}(t), e \rg - |\dot{\gamma}(t)^{\perp}|)_- \, dt.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.493719+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_35a1649f0eed818661ecf26f6be089586b8e06b79355699ab61f4a8e20abb80a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 15 (Double hive) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{def:double-hive}
For \(\nu\in\Spec_n\), write
\[
\nu^\vee=(-\nu_n,\ldots,-\nu_1).
\]
A double hive with exterior boundary
\((\alpha,\beta,\eta,\phi)\) and middle side \(\nu\) is a pair of hives
\[
(h_1,h_2)\in
H_n(\alpha,\beta;\nu)\times H_n(\eta,\phi^\vee;\nu^\vee),
\qquad
\phi^\vee=(-\phi_n,\ldots,-\phi_1),
\]
viewed as glued along the common middle side, with opposite orientations on
the two copies of that side.  The corresponding double hive polytope is
\[
\mathcal D(\alpha,\beta,\eta,\phi^\vee)
:=
\bigcup_{\nu\in\Spec_n + \R \one}
H_n(\alpha,\beta;\nu)
\times
H_n(\eta,\phi^\vee;\nu^\vee).
\]
A quadruply augmented double hive is obtained by additionally choosing
Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns on the four exterior boundary components with matching spectra.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:30:28.841999+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_35a34d25938a93aa2bbe87d1006e637b0ff295ecdbcc146b23a282c3d9db5ec2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 3 of arXiv:2609.02173, 'Bounding Selmer Groups of Superelliptic Jacobians via Class Groups'] Every element of $J(F)$ admits a representative given by a degree-zero divisor defined over $F$ whose support contains neither the point at infinity $\infty$ nor any point with $y$-coordinate equal to $0$. 		\[
		D = {}^{\sigma_1}Q + \cdots + {}^{\sigma_m}Q - m\infty,

		$Q\in \mathcal C(\bar F)$ with $y(Q)\neq 0$. Then
		\[
		(x-T)([D]) \equiv \prod_{i=1}^m \bigl(x({}^{\sigma_i}Q)-T\bigr)

		\]

		\[
		D = (\alpha_1,0)+\cdots+(\alpha_r,0)-r\infty,

		\[

		\prod_{i=1}^r (\alpha_i-T)^{u_i}+

		\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.973830+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_35b671fa93579110d97793a9f55ecb766fd0e815ebc25c9a5b8c52d7f70ee466","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 37 (Naturality and base change of response kernels) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let $f:(M,F^\bullet)\to(M',F^\bullet)$ preserve the decreasing
filtrations, let
$B:(\mathcal Y,K_\bullet)\to(\mathcal Y',K_\bullet)$ preserve the
increasing filtrations, and let
$\mathcal R:M^*\to\mathcal Y$ and
$\mathcal R':(M')^*\to\mathcal Y'$ be filtered responses satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R'=B\circ\mathcal R\circ f^*.
 
\end{equation}
Write $f_r:G_r(M)\to G_r(M')$ and
$B_r:\partial_r\mathcal Y\to\partial_r\mathcal Y'$ for the induced
maps.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak K_r(\mathcal R')
 =(f_r\otimes B_r)\mathfrak K_r(\mathcal R).
 
\end{equation}
Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{supp}_L\mathfrak K_r(\mathcal R')
 \subseteq f_r\bigl(\operatorname{supp}_L\mathfrak K_r(\mathcal R)\bigr).
\]
If $\mathcal R$ has full support, $f_r$ is surjective, and $B_r$ is
injective on the image of
$\operatorname{gr}_r\mathcal R\circ f_r^*$, then $\mathcal R'$ has full
support on $G_r(M')$.  Thus a quotient observation recovers exactly its
observable ancestry layer.  In particular, spatial pushforwards,
exact-layer identifications, and native boundary readers act on one canonical
kernel rather than creating new detector data.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:33:21.475413+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_35bf47abec61f9db29b7eebf89e9a7c4afaff60e4f8c136040dff8c92d64a317","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:fixed-chaos-maximal-tail of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Let \(m\ge1\)
and  \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\) be random variables such that every interval sum
\[
    Z(I):=\sum_{j\in I}Z_j,
    \qquad I\subset\{1,\ldots,N\},
\]
belongs to the fixed \(m\)-th Wiener chaos. Assume that for some \(B>0\) and some \(q>1\),
\[
    \operatorname{Var}(Z(I))
    \le

\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:52:45.032349+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_35c0beb00f11d5ea3a5ad1aacac72aebde7f9d1c6be50402595304932b9dae4c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2606.07290, 'Boundary behaviour of the Volterra square-root process'] Suppose that $K \in C^1(\R_+)$. Then the following assertions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] The function $V_u$ satisfies the two-sided bounds
        \begin{equation}
            W_u(t) \leq V_u(t) \leq W_u(t) + K(0)L_0(0) \int_0^t W_u(s) \mathrm{e}^{\beta^+ K(0)(t-s)}\, \mathrm{d}s.
        \end{equation}
        where $\beta^+ = \max\{\beta, 0\}$. The function $W_u$ is for $\beta \neq L_0(0)$ given by
        \[
            W_u(t) = \frac{(\beta - L_0(0))K(0)u \mathrm{e}^{K(0)(\beta - L_0(0))t}}{\beta - L_0(0) + \frac{\sigma^2}{2}K(0)u \left( \mathrm{e}^{K(0)(\beta - L_0(0))t} - 1\right)} , \qquad t > 0,
        \]
        while for $\beta = L_0(0)$ it takes the form
        \[
            W_u(t) = \frac{K(0)u}{1 + \frac{\sigma^2 K(0)^2}{2}ut}, \qquad t > 0.
        \]
        \item[(b)] The function $R_u(t) := (L \ast V_u)(t)$ satisfies the upper bound 
        \begin{equation}
            R_u(t) \leq \frac{W_u(t)}{K(0)} + L_0(0)\int_0^t W_u(s) \mathrm{e}^{\beta^+ K(0)(t-s)}\, \mathrm{d}s.
        \end{equation}
        \item[(c)] For any $t>0$ such that $\beta < L_0(t)$, we have
        \[
            \int_0^t V_u(s)\, \mathrm{d}s \leq \frac{L_0(0) - \beta}{L_0(t) - \beta}\int_0^t W_u(s)\, \mathrm{d}s.
        \]
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.975577+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_35c47bbf1f7208df753d4015bf37b19f6e6b31c698c4c6227e79805fa5e46ac5","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 44 (Multiplicative exterior area reader) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] For every \(g,h\in\mathcal G_2(H)\),
\begin{equation}
 \Sigma_{\wedge}^{\lambda}(g\circ h)
 =\Sigma_{\wedge}^{\lambda}(g)\wedge
  \Sigma_{\wedge}^{\lambda}(h).
 
\end{equation}
If \(a_1(A)\geq a_2(A)\geq\cdots\) are the positive two--plane
singular values of \(A\), then
\begin{align}
 \mathfrak P_A(z)
 &:=\log\|\exp_{\wedge}(z\alpha_A)\|^2
   =\sum_{j\geq1}\log(1+z^2a_j(A)^2) \notag\\
 &=\frac12\log\det(I+z^2A^*A)
   =\mathfrak F_A(z).
 
\end{align}
Consequently, for every \(0<p<2\), the weak and little
\(\mathcal S_{p,\infty}\) scales are read directly from \(\mathfrak P_A\)
by \Cref{cc:prop:weak-detection}.  The full vector
\(\Sigma_{\wedge}^{\lambda}\) is faithful in \(A\) for
\(\lambda\ne0\), whereas the scalar profile remembers precisely the nonzero
singular spectrum, with multiplicity, and forgets the singular subspaces.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:20:30.573369+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_35e67fdb082f44f4a4efc7407262e727fa40df332c0dadb9c38dedf0a69d4e1c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 39 (Well-posedness of the nonlinear memory problem) of arXiv:2609.01826, 'An extension theory for fully fractional Schr\"odinger equations with memory'] Let $0<s<1$, set $a=1-2s$, let $\mu\in\C\setminus\{0\}$, and let
$u_0\in\mathcal H^s$ be a prescribed history.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{(i) The range $0\le a<1$.} Let
\[
p_c=1+\frac{2(1-a)}{d+a+1},
\]
suppose that $1<p\leq p_c$, set $r=p+1$, and let $q$ be determined by
\eqref{E:admissible-positive}. We note that $q>2$ is automatic: since
$2<r\le p_c+1=\frac{2(d+2)}{d+a+1}$, \eqref{E:admissible-positive} gives
$\frac2q\le\frac{d+a+1}{d+2}<1$, the last inequality because $a<1$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] If $p=p_c$, there exists
$\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_0(d,a,c_s\mu)>0$ such that
\[
\|u_0\|_{\mathcal H^s}\leq\varepsilon_0
\]
implies that, for every $T<\infty$, the problem has a unique mild solution on
$(0,T]$ with prescribed history $u_0$, in the sense of
Definition~\ref{D:memory-solution}.
\item[(b)] If $1<p<p_c$, there exists
$T=T\bigl(d,a,p,\mu,\|u_0\|_{\mathcal H^s}\bigr)>0$ such that the problem has a
unique mild solution on $(0,T]$ with prescribed history $u_0$. If, in addition,
$\operatorname{Im}(c_s\mu)=0$ --- equivalently, by
Remark~\ref{R:admissible-mu} below, if $\mu\in e^{i\frac{\pi s}{2}}\R$ --- then this
solution extends to a mild solution on $(0,T]$ for every $T<\infty$, by
\cite[Theorem~2.8(2)]{GS2}, applied with vanishing interior forcing and
boundary coefficient $-c_s\mu$.
\end{itemize}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{(ii) The range $-1<a<0$.} Let
\[
p_c=1+\frac{2}{d+1},
\]
suppose that $1<p\leq p_c$, set $r=p+1$, and let $q,q_\infty$ satisfy
\eqref{E:admissible-negative}.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] If $p=p_c$, then for every $T<\infty$ there exists
$\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_1(d,a,c_s\mu,T)>0$ such that
\[
\|u_0\|_{\mathcal H^s}\leq\varepsilon_1
\]
implies that the problem has a unique mild solution on $(0,T]$ with prescribed
history $u_0$. One may take

{"assumptions":["Primary-source scope record, not a new polynomial-gap theorem","Matrix sensing application assumes 1/20-RIP on all rank-at-most-2k matrices","The actual row has iid Gaussian rank-one measurements and m at least C d log^3 d"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T20:04:21.099115+00:00","domain":"sampling and nonconvex learning","id":"claim_35f9c193fc020fba4b06d0f0b693bea38742862f79e20a892b24d653fe16ba68","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"# Moitra-Risteski: relevant decomposition, uncovered phase-retrieval hypotheses

T321 Target 2. Literature applicability finding, not a new proof of Target 2.
Source: Fast Convergence for Langevin Diffusion with Manifold Structure,
arXiv:2002.05576, primary PDF saved under papers/.

Section 2, PDF page 3, requires the matrix-sensing operator to satisfy
(19/20)||M||_F^2 <= ||A(M)||_2^2 <= (21/20)||M||_F^2
for every matrix M of rank at most 2k. This is an operator-wide assumption,
not concentration for a fixed deterministic M.

For phase retrieval take k=1 and A_ph(M)_j=(a_j^T M a_j)/sqrt(m), so the
squared residual is precisely the normalized empirical quartic loss.
For every nonzero measurement a_i, set u=a_i/||a_i|| and M=uu^T. Then
rank(M)=1, ||M||_F=1 and

 ||A_ph(M)||_2^2=(1/m)sum_j(a_j.u)^4 >= ||a_i||^4/m.

Thus the upper RIP inequality would force
m >= (20/21)max_i||a_i||^4. The witness is allowed to depend on the sample,
because RIP quantifies over EVERY rank-one matrix. This is the exact
deterministic fourth-moment obstruction already relevant to this row,
applied to the paper's stated hypothesis; it is not presented as new.
For Gaussian measurements, ||a_1||^2/d tends to 1 in probability. Therefore
for m=C d log^3 d with fixed C, this necessary inequality fails with
probability tending to 1 as d grows. Multiplication by any fixed scalar
normalization of A_ph does not remove the growing d/log^3 d obstruction.
No claim is made here about operators obtained by data-dependent weighting,
truncation or a changed loss; those require their own arguments.

Section 4.1, Theorem 4, PDF page 7, is nevertheless a relevant generic
decomposition framework: along-level and across-level Poincare control,
control of changing conditional density/Jacobian, and finite-time retention
near the minimizer manifold combine into convergence to a restricted law.
These are hypotheses to establish, not consequences of benign landscape
alone. Our C007 is a different polar decomposition with the same unresolved
need for one conditional spectral-gap estimate.

Section 4.2, Theorem 5, PDF pages 7-8, assumes the matrix measurement
conditions above, a sufficiently large beta, and an absolutely continuous
initial law supported near one minimizer component. The target p_i is
defined just before the theorem as the Gibbs law restricted to points
closer to component E_i than the other component. The theorem's displayed
TV error includes an additive epsilon, as well as a decaying chi-square
term. It is not a statement of the full unrestricted even Poincare constant
for the empirical rank-one measurement model at beta~d/epsilon_loss.
The TV accuracy epsilon in the paper must not be identified silently with
the row's optimization/loss tolerance epsilon_loss.

The discussion on PDF page 9 explicitly leaves reaching the prescribed
initialization by unmodified Langevin for future work, while explaining
that optimization can supply such an initialization in the stated models.
Even if a warm-start sampling guarantee were imported, an additive-error
TV guarantee alone is not a variational Poincare inequality for the full law.

NEXT: adapt the near-well decomposition and retention estimates using the
actual rank-one measurement geometry, without imposing false global RIP;
then control the rest of the quotient to obtain the full polynomial gap.
No claim of a solved parameter range or a scored frontier move is made.
The rank-one diagnostic is analytic and unaudited, not a numerical bound
or a Lean-certified assertion.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:07:56.656926+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3602a942d36037448d060dcd4dbbb50334b9b3583ef08c8588a2ae0bde45bc33","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:BESQflow of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Let $\delta \in {\mathbb R}$.  We call ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow  driven by $\mathcal W$ a collection ${\mathcal S}$ of continuous processes $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)_{r\in {\mathbb R},a\ge 0}$ such that: 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item
for each $(a,r)\in {\mathbb R}_+\times {\mathbb R}$, the process $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)$ is almost surely the strong solution of the following SDE  
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a) = 
a + 2 \int_r^x  {\mathcal W}([0,{\mathcal S}_{r,s}(a)], \, \mathrm{d} s) + 
\delta (x-r) 
,\, x\ge r
\end{equation}
 and which, in the case $\delta<0$, is absorbed when hitting $0$.
 \item Almost surely,
 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
 \item for all $r\in {\mathbb R}$ and $a\ge 0$, $ {\mathcal S}_{r,r}(a)=a$,
 \item for all $r\le x$, $a\mapsto  {\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a)$ is c\`adl\`ag,
 \item (Perfect flow property) for any $r\le x \le y$ and $a\ge 0$, $\mathcal S_{r,y}(a)=\mathcal S_{x,y}\circ \mathcal S_{r,x}(a)$. 
\end{enumerate} 
\end{enumerate}

We call killed ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow driven by $\mathcal W$ the flow obtained from the ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow by absorbing at $0$ the flow line $\mathcal S_{r,\cdot}(a)$ at time $\inf\{x>r\,:\,\mathcal S_{r,x}(a)=0\}$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:27:14.894319+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_360caad4b046da3988a288efa0e7a656e7b5de7528d0f004fb1e444d3f2bf3a9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.23960, 'Learning from Uncertainty-dependent Missing Labels for Semi-supervised Classification'] Let \((Y,Z)\) have joint density \(p_\theta(Y,Z)\), and let
\(M\in\{0,1\}\) denote the label-missingness indicator, with \(M=1\) if the
label is missing and \(M=0\) if it is observed. Suppose that
\[
  M\perp Z\mid Y
\]
and that the missingness mechanism has the form
\[
  r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)
  =
  \Pr(M=1\mid Y;\theta,\boldsymbol\xi)
  =
  h\{\eta_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\},
\]
where \(h\) is a smooth inverse link function and
\(\eta_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\) may depend on \(\theta\). Then, for known
\(\boldsymbol\xi\), the observed-data Fisher information for \(\theta\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}(\theta)
  =
  \mathcal I_{CC}(\theta)
  -
  \mathcal I_{CC}^{(\mathrm{miss},r)}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi)
  +
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{mech}}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi).

\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}(\theta)
  =
  \mathcal I_{UC}(\theta)
  +
  E_\theta\!\left[
    \{1-r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\}
    \operatorname{Var}_\theta\{S_c(Y,Z;\theta)\mid Y\}
  \right]
  +
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{mech}}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi).

\end{equation}
The mechanism-curvature term is positive semidefinite. For the logistic inverse
link,
\[
  w_h\{\eta_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\}
  =
  r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)
  \{1-r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\}.
\]
If \(r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\equiv\gamma\), then
\[
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}(\theta)
  =
  \mathcal I_{CC}(\theta)
  -
  \gamma\,\mathcal I_{CC}^{(\mathrm{miss})}(\theta)
  +
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{mech}}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["entries of Z i.i.d., mean zero, variance one (finite second moment suffices for the almost-sure convergence in the Bai-Silverstein form)","the spectral distribution of Sigma converges weakly to H; p/n -> c in (0, infinity)","Sigma and Z independent (Sigma may be random)"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T16:00:40+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory","id":"claim_3625ab2a19639ec1e18b098bfb508774dc8680a3563d30345ceda3df84ad0c18","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $X = Z\\Sigma^{1/2}$ be $n \\times p$ with $Z$ having i.i.d. entries of mean $0$ and variance $1$, $\\Sigma$ positive semidefinite, and let $S = \\frac{1}{n}X^T X$. {"assumptions":["Ω ⊂ R^n open","u continuous on Ω","F continuous on Ω × R × R^n (for part (b))"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T10:04:12.416110+00:00","domain":"partial differential equations: viscosity solution theory","id":"claim_367dca126752a97158c2d321bbcf3990dfd46c533d360292e0deac44d1f630d1","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open and u ∈ C(Ω). For x0 ∈ Ω define the superdifferential D^+u(x0) = { p ∈ R^n : limsup_{x→x0} ( u(x) - u(x0) - p·(x-x0) ) / |x - x0| ≤ 0 } and the subdifferential D^-u(x0) = { p : liminf_{x→x0} ( u(x) - u(x0) - p·(x-x0) ) / |x-x0| ≥ 0 }. Then: (a) p ∈ D^+u(x0) if and only if there exists φ ∈ C^1(Ω) with Dφ(x0) = p such that u - φ has a local maximum at x0; symmetrically for D^-u(x0) and local minima. (b) Hence, for continuous F, u is a viscosity subsolution of F(x,u,Du) = 0 iff F(x, u(x), p) ≤ 0 for every x ∈ Ω and every p ∈ D^+u(x), and a viscosity supersolution iff F(x,u(x),p) ≥ 0 for every x ∈ Ω and every p ∈ D^-u(x). (c) u is differentiable at x0 if and only if D^+u(x0) and D^-u(x0) are both nonempty, and in that case D^+u(x0) = D^-u(x0) = {Du(x0)}.","status":"unverified"}

	\ce

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:09:49.789183+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3750e1b8ef87fa0ccb27d299955bf7024c26d314fb83caaa613edff78412dc95","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 12 of arXiv:2609.03061, '2609.03061'] \cite{GL} 
For $N$ a real $m \times m$ matrix with $det(N) \neq 0$.  Let
$$
N = P(N) \cdot Q(N)
$$
be the unique polar decomposition of $N$. That is, $Q(N) = \sqrt{N^t \cdot N}$, a real symmetric positive
definite matrix, and $P(N) = N \cdot Q(N)^{-1}$ which is a real orthogonal matrix, i.e.,
$P(N)^t  \cdot P(N) = Id[m]$.

\vspace{.1in} If $M(t) \in Sp(2n,\mathbb{R})$, then
$P(M(t))$ and $Q(M(t))$ are also symplectic. Indeed, for $K: U(n) \subset Sp(2n, \mathbb{R})$
the inclusion, $P(M(t)) = K( \Pi(M(t)))$ for unique $\Pi(M(t)) \in U(n)$ and $Q(M(t))$ is uniquely
expressed in the form
$$
Q(M(t)) = e^{A(M(t))} \ \ with \ \ A(M(t)) = \left( \begin{array}{cc} a_1(M(t)) & a_2(M(t)) \\ a_2(M(t)) & -a_1(M(t)) \end{array}
\right)
$$
for real symmetric $n \times n$ matrices $a_1(M(t)), \ a_2(M(t))$. Here \newline
 $ J \   \left( \begin{array}{cc} a_1(M(t)) & a_2(M(t)) \\ a_2(M(t)) & -a_1(M(t)) \end{array} \right)
=  - \ \left( \begin{array}{cc} a_1(M(t)) & a_2(M(t)) \\ a_2(M(t)) & -a_1(M(t)) \end{array} \right) \cdot J$
implies that $e^{A(M(t))} \in Sp(2n,\mathbb{R})$.

Additionally, under the standard identification \newline $C: \{n \times n \ real \  symmetric\} \cong \mathbb{R}^{n(n-1)/2}$
$$
M(t) \mapsto (\Pi(M(t)),  C(a_1(M(t))), C(a_2(M(t)))) \in U(n) \times  \mathbb{R}^{n(n-1)/2} \times \mathbb{R}^{n(n-1)/2}

is a smooth bijection. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:47:40.724355+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_375b2b51a05ee14834c28f13b0b6c3d12063d8b90da949dff2c7b81304ae6af6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:good_parameters of arXiv:2604.18558, 'Uniform analyticity of local observables in FK-percolation and analyticity of the Ising sp'] Define $\mathcal G_{\mathsf{FK}}$ to be the set of triplets $(d,p,q)$ such that the FK measures in finite volumes $\phi_{\Lambda_n, p, q}$ satisfy the following hypotheses. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Exponential weak mixing property}: for any $\alpha > 1$, there exists $c > 0$ such that for any $n \geq 0$ sufficiently large\footnote{$\mathrm{d}_{\mathsf{TV}}$ denotes the classical total variation distance between probability measures, and for any measure $\mu$, $\mu( \cdot_{|\Lambda_n})$ denotes the restriction of the measure $\mu$ to the box $\Lambda_n$.}, 
\[
\mathrm{d}_{\mathsf{TV}}( \phi^1_{\Lambda_{\alpha n}, p,q}( \cdot_{|\Lambda_n} ), \phi^0_{\Lambda_{\alpha n}, p,q}( \cdot_{|\Lambda_n} ) ) < \exp(-cn). 
\]
\item One of the two following conditions holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textit{Exponential decay}: for any $\alpha > 1$, there exists $c>0$ such that for any $n \geq 0$ large enough, 
\[
\phi^1_{\Lambda_{\alpha n, p ,q}}[A_n] < \exp(-cn),
\]
where $A_n$ is the event that $\Lambda_n$ contains a cluster of diameter greater than $n/100$.
\item \textit{Local uniqueness}: for any $\alpha > 1$, there exists $c>0$ such that for any $n \geq 0$ large enough, 
\[
\sup_\eta \phi^\eta_{\Lambda_{\alpha n, p ,q}}[U_n^c] < \exp(-cn),
\]
where the local uniqueness event $U_n$ is the event that $\Lambda_n $ contains a \emph{crossing} cluster and all the other clusters have diameter less than $n/100$, where a crossing cluster is a cluster that connects all the sides of the box $\Lambda_n$. The event $U_n^c$ is the complement of $U_n$.
In the last property, the supremum is taken over all the boundary conditions on the box $\Lambda_{\alpha n}$. 
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:50:30.562372+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_376f73ec0e4a8fa79094fd56bcc2e399117f8992563f9193bea8b6347e7d3bba","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2605.30560, 'Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport'] Let $p>d+2$, let $\P_0\in\Pc(\Xc\times\R^d)$, and let
\[
b:\R_+\times\Xc\times\R^d\longrightarrow\R^d
\]
be a Borel-measurable vector field. Assume that there exists a weak solution to
\[
dY_t
=
b(t,X,Y_t)\,dt+\sqrt{2} \,dB_t,
\qquad
(X,Y_0)\sim\P_0,
\qquad
(X, Y_0) \independent B,
\]
where $\independent$ denotes the indepenance. 
For $T>0$ and $R>0$, define
\begin{equation} 
C_1(R,T,b)
:=
\int_0^T
\left\{
\E\Big[
|b(t,X,Y_t)|^p\mathbf{1}_{\{|Y_t|\le R\}}
\Big]
+
\int_{\Xc} \int_{B(0,R)} |b(t,x,y)|^p\,dy\,\mu(dx)
\right\}
dt.
\end{equation}
Assume that $C_1(R,T,b)<\infty$ for every $R>0$. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)]
    \item 
    For every $t\in(0,T]$, the law
    \[
    \P_t:=\Lc(X,Y_t)
    \]
admits a density with respect to $\mu \otimes \mathrm{L}$,
    still denoted by $\tilde{\P}_{t,x}(y)$. 
    Moreover, for every $R>0$ and every
    $t\in(0,T]$, there exists a constant $K_{T,R}>0$ such that
    \begin{equation} 
    \big\|
    \tilde{\P}_t\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|y|\le R\}}
    \big\|_{\L^p(\mu\otimes \mathrm{L} ) }
    \le
    K_{T,R} \bigl(1+C_1(R,T,b)\bigr).
    \end{equation}

    \item 
    Assume furthermore that the second marginal of $\P_t$ is given by
    \[
    \Lc(Y_t)=\nu(dy)=e^{-V(y)} \,dy, \quad \forall \, t \in \R_+.
    \]
    For every bounded Borel function $\phi:\Xc\to\R$, define
    \[
    w_\phi(t,y):=\E[\phi(X)\mid Y_t=y].
    \]
    Equivalently, for $\nu$-a.e.\ $y$,
    \begin{equation} 
    w_\phi(t,y)
    =
    \int_{\Xc} \phi(x)\,\tilde{\P}_{t,x}(y)\,\mu(dx)\,e^{V(y)}.
    \end{equation}
    Then, for every $R>0$ and every $\delta>0$, there exist constants
    $\alpha,\beta,K>0$, depending only on $C_1(R,T,b)$, $R$, and $\delta$, such
    that for all $y,y'\in B(0,R)$ and all $t,t'\in[\delta,T]$ satisfying
    $|t-t'|\le1$,
    \begin{equation} 
    |w_\phi(t',y')-w_\phi(t,y)|
    \le
    K\|\phi\|_\infty
    \Big(
    |y-y'|^\alpha + |t-t'|^\beta
    \Big).
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. nonnegative edge weights on the nearest-neighbour edges of Z^d, d >= 2","E[min of 2d independent copies of tau_e] < infinity (implied by E[tau_e] < infinity); without it the limit exists only in probability","positivity of mu is NOT part of this theorem and holds exactly when F(0) < p_c"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.542493+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_377aff255f0c4f83a8772b658e8326b0c3e89f3f2873cda60908dbe935ed4d02","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Consider i.i.d. first-passage percolation on Z^d with edge-weight law F supported on [0, infinity). Let Y be the minimum of 2d independent copies of tau_e - the smallest weight among the edges at a vertex. If E[Y] < infinity then the limit mu(e_1) = lim_{n -> infinity} T(0, n e_1)/n exists almost surely and in L^1 and is a deterministic constant in [0, infinity), and the same holds along every lattice direction, defining mu on Z^d and by homogeneity and convexity on all of R^d, invariant under the symmetries of the lattice; mu is either identically 0 or a genuine norm. Three companion facts, each with its own status. (i) WITHOUT the moment condition the limit still exists IN PROBABILITY, by Kesten, Cox-Durrett and Wierman, and when the moment condition does hold the two limits agree. (ii) 0 <= mu(e_1) <= E[tau_e], the upper bound by taking the direct path and applying the law of large numbers - so the finiteness of E[tau_e] gives the bound but is NOT needed for existence. (iii) POSITIVITY is a separate theorem and is not part of this one: mu(e_1) > 0 IF AND ONLY IF F(0) < p_c(d), the bond percolation threshold, and mu(e_1) > 0 if and only if mu(x) > 0 for every nonzero x. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:45:01.871693+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_377b4f30f51792116fc6b95a20b722ce396b31cf32e9351c1aad545a0bcadfbb","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem eq:main of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'] Let $0<q<1$ and $x\in[0,1]$. Consider the Markov chain $\left(Q_i\right)_{i\ge1}$ on $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ with initial law
\[
\mathbb{P}\left(Q_1=k\right)=\pi_k=\frac{\left(q;q\right)_\infty}{\left(q;q\right)_k}q^k,
\]
and one-step transition probabilities (independent of $i$), for $k\ge0$,
    \[
    P\left(k,k+1\right)=x\left(1-x\right),\qquad
    P\left(k,k-1\right)=x\left(1-x\right)\left(1-q^k\right),\qquad
    P\left(k,k\right)=1-x\left(1-x\right)\bigl(2-q^k\bigr),
    \]
with the convention $P\left(0,-1\right)=0$. We write
    \[
    P\left(a,b\right):=\mathbb{P}\bigl(Q_{i+1}=b\big|Q_i=a\bigr)
    \]
    for the one-step transition probability, which does not depend on $i$. 
    Fix $n\ge1$ and a sequence $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and set $s:=\sum_{i=1}^n s_i$. Then
        \begin{equation}    \sum_{k\ge0}\mathbb{P}\left(Q_1=k,Q_2=k+s_1,\dots,Q_{n+1}=k+s\right) = q^{-s}\sum_{m\ge0}\mathbb{P}\left(Q_1=m,Q_2=m-s_n,\dots,Q_{n+1}=m-s\right).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:37:51.440784+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_37801bd1dbe4d694c4b16ca36c1325fe50c071e314df8709ca9dc7c4a20e1f8a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 1 of arXiv:2604.03206, 'The extreme statistics of some noncolliding Brownian processes'] Consider, for each $n$, the model \eqref{eqn:Hreg} and assume the eigenvalues of $H^{\mathrm{reg}} = H^{\mathrm{reg}}_n$ are
$\lambda^n_i = \lambda_1^n - \Delta \cdot (i-1)$ for $1 \leq i \leq n$ with a fixed $\Delta > 0$.
Define the rescaled random variable
$$ \lambda_{max}^n = \Delta \cdot (\lambda_{max}(H(1)) - \lambda_1^n) - \log(n-1).$$
Then, for each $a \in \R$,
$$ \lim_n \mathbf{Pr}(\lambda^n_{max} \leq a) = \dt{I - K_{\Delta}}_{L^2[a,\infty)}$$
where the integral kernel $K_{\Delta}$ is as follows.
$$K_{\Delta}(x,y) = \frac{1}{(2 \pi \mathbf{i})^2} \oint_{\gamma_{rec}}d\zeta \oint_{\gamma_{ver}} dz\,
    \frac{e^{\frac{\Delta^2}{2} z^2 -yz}}{e^{\frac{\Delta^2}{2}\zeta^2-x\zeta}} \cdot \frac{\Gamma(\zeta)}{\Gamma(z)}\cdot \frac{1}{z-\zeta}.$$
Here $\gamma_{ver}$ is the vertical contour $\{\Re(z) = 1\}$ oriented upwards, and $\gamma_{rec}$ is the counter clockwise oriented contour
$\{t \pm \mathbf{i}/2; t \leq 1/2\} \cup \{1/2 + \mathbf{i}t; |t| \leq 1/2\}$. Also, $\Gamma(z)$ is the Gamma function. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:11:09.317791+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_379223428004d7efd78d22695193deeb16dd036ad798e8757d892ce06ac2b383","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:restriction-to-a-subset of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] \mbox{}\\
  Let $(X_n,T_n)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$ be a continuous-time jump process on $G$.
  Recursively, we take $\sigma_0:=0$ and for $n\in{\mathbb N}$, on the event
  $\{\sigma_{n-1}<\infty\}$, we define 
  $\sigma_n:=\inf\{l>\sigma_{n-1}:X_l\neq X_{\sigma_{n-1}}\}$ to be the index
  of the next jump to a different location. 
  The process with self-loops removed is defined by 
  $(X^{\neq},T^{\neq})=(X^{\neq}_n,T^{\neq}_n)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}:=(X_{\sigma_n},\sum_{l=\sigma_n}^{\sigma_{n+1}-1}T_l)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$
  on the event $\{\sigma_n<\infty\text{ for all }n\in{\mathbb N}\}$.

  M}_1( D_+(\mathbb{T}))$, then there exists a unique measure  $\pi_\infty\in {\mathcal
  M}_1( D(\mathbb{T}))$  such that
\begin{equation}

    U}_t^VFd\mu= \int_{  D_+(\mathbb{T})}F d\pi_\infty .
\end{equation}
The measure $\pi_\infty$ is invariant under  $\big(\tilde
\mathcal{U}^V_t\big)$.

In addition,  for any $\delta>0$, $p\in[1,+\infty)$

  D_+(\mathbb{T})}\mathbf{E}\big\|\rho^V(t;\rho_1)-\rho^V(t;\rho_2)\big\|^p_\infty\leq

In  consequence, for any $p\ge1$,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:32:20.038036+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_37a53560003cf2dea62914756d09d4aab3a49eea5937c321b8579fd386c1cd85","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 44 (Convergence after $n(x)$ steps, stated with a reference measure) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $(\XX,\XXA)$ be a measurable space and $\lambda$ a $\sigma$-finite measure on
it. Let $p : \XX \to [0,\infty)$ be measurable with $\int_{\XX} p \dd\lambda = 1$, let
$\tau : \XX\times\XX \to [0,\infty)$ be $\XXA\otimes\XXA$-measurable with
$\int_{\XX} \tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) = 1$ for every $x \in \XX$, and define
\[
  \pi(A) := \int_{A} p \dd\lambda, \qquad T(A \mid x) := \int_{A}\tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y)
  \qquad (A \in \XXA,\ x \in \XX),
\]
and $\Xp := \{p > 0\} \in \XXA$. Let $\tau_{n} : \XX\times\XX \to [0,\infty)$ be given
by the Chapman--Kolmogorov recursion
\[
  \tau_{1} := \tau, \qquad
  \tau_{n+1}(y \mid x) := \int_{\XX} \tau_{n}(y \mid z)\,\tau(z \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd z)
  \qquad (n \in \N).
\]
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep,topsep=3pt]
  \item \emph{(invariance)} $\displaystyle\int_{\XX} \tau(y \mid x)\,p(x)\,\lambda(\dd x) = p(y)$ for $\lambda$-almost every $y \in \XX$;

        \[
          \lambda\bigl(\{ y \in \XX\setminus\Xp : \tau_{n}(y \mid x) > 0 \}\bigr) = 0
          \qquad\text{and}\qquad
          \lambda\bigl(\{ y \in \Xp : \tau_{n}(y \mid x) = 0 \}\bigr) = 0 .
        \]
\end{enumerate}
Then $\pi$ is the unique invariant probability measure of $T$, and

Assume that $F \in \bW^{\infty}$ and $\Delta_F^{-1} \in L^q(\Omega)$.
Then, for every $j \in \{0, \ldots, k\}$ and $a \in \R$, we have
\begin{align}
    \rho^{(j)}_{\cN}(a) - \rho^{(j)}_{F}(a)
    &= \sum_{i=0}^{M-1} \frac{\kappa_{i+1}(F)}{i!}\dpair{\bW^{-j-i, s_{j+i}}}{(\sD^{i}f_{a,j})(F)}{1}{\bW^{j+i, s_{j+i}'}}\\
    &\quad + \dpair{\bW^{-j-M, s_{j+M}}}{(\sD^{M}f_{a,j})(F)}{\Gamma_M(F)}{\bW^{j+M, s_{j+M}'}}\\
    &\quad - \dpair{\bW^{-j-1, s_{j+1}}}{(\sD f_{a,j})(F)}{1}{\bW^{j+1,s_{j+1}'}},
\end{align}
where $\dpair{\bW^{0, s_0}}{f_{a,0}(F)}{1}{\bW^{0,s_0'}}$ is understood as $\E[f_{a,0}(F)]$.
In particular, if in addition $\E[F] = 0$ and $\E[F^2] = 1$, then $\kappa_1(F) = 0$ and $\kappa_2(F) = 1$, and consequently  
\begin{align}
    \rho^{(j)}_{\cN}(a) - \rho^{(j)}_{F}(a) 
    &= \sum_{i=2}^{M-1} \frac{\kappa_{i+1}(F)}{i!}\dpair{\bW^{-j-i, s_{j+i}}}{(\sD^{i}f_{a,j})(F)}{1}{\bW^{j+i, s_{j+i}'}}\\
    &\quad + \dpair{\bW^{-j-M, s_{j+M}}}{(\sD^{M}f_{a,j})(F)}{\Gamma_M(F)}{\bW^{j+M, s_{j+M}'}}.
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:04:55.805932+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_37d957f301c34a6c3d7fdea04c3374d4bd25499549c2f122403005586520360c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop p:markov-property-CDRP of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] {AJRS22}}]
    Fix $(s,x;t,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{4}_{\uparrow}$ and fix $s',t'$ satisfying $s<s'<t'<t$.
    Define the following $\sigma$-algebras on path space $C([s,t])$:
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal{G}_{s,s'} \coloneqq  \sigma\left(
            X|_{[s,s']}:X\in C([s,t])
        \right),
        \qquad
        \mathcal{G}_{t',t} \coloneqq  \sigma\left(
            X|_{[t',t]}:X\in C([s,t])
        \right).
    \end{align*}
    Then almost surely,
    for all bounded  measurable functions $F:C([s',t'])\to\mathbb{R}$,  we have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}^\xi_{1,(s,x),(t,y)}\left[
            F(X|_{[s',t']})\,\middle|\,\mathcal{G}_{s,s'},\, \mathcal{G}_{t',t}
        \right]
        &=
        \mathbb{E}^\xi_{1,(s',X(s')), (t', X(t'))}\left[
            F(X)
        \right]
        \qquad\quad
        \textup{$\mathbb{P}^\xi_{1,(s,x),(t,y)}$-a.s.,}
    \end{align*} 
    where $\mathbb{E}^\xi_{1,(s,x),(t,y)}$ denotes expectation with respect to $\mathbb{P}^\xi_{1,(s,x),(t,y)}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:03:59.273118+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_37e5920d7fa3fb66da17b3eb4791e697f878442c193d1ef3afa97edca38b3674","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:Conc of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] \begin{enumerate}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:12:19.464074+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_37f9e23eb13e2294349f0aaf2da4b0ccc2ed76095064b4331de2e8d3720977fc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 12 (Consistency of the Lipschitz-case powers) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $p=\alpha-1\in(0,1)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \textup{Initial value perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=x_0+W_t+Z_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt x_0+W_t+Z_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p=|x_0-\wt x_0|^p.
\]
Thus the initial error exponent $p=\alpha-1$ is exact.

\item \textup{Drift perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=bt,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt b t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p=T^p|b-\wt b|^p.
\]
Since $B=T|b-\wt b|$, this is exactly $B^p$.

\item \textup{Brownian diffusion perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=aW_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt a W_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p
  =m_p T^{p/2}|a-\wt a|^p,
\]
where $m_p=\E|N(0,1)|^p$. Since $A=T^{1/2}|a-\wt a|$, this is $m_p A^p$.

\item \textup{Stable jump coefficient perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=\sigma Z_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt\sigma Z_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p
  =\E|Z_1|^p T^{p/\alpha}|\sigma-\wt\sigma|^p.
\]
Since $S=T^{1/\alpha}|\sigma-\wt\sigma|$, this is $\E|Z_1|^pS^p$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, when $\wt\eta=1$, the powers $|x_0-\wt x_0|^{\alpha-1}$, $B^{\alpha-1}$, $A^{\alpha-1}$ and $S^{\alpha-1}$ agree with the exact scaling of the four elementary perturbation mechanisms.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:06:18.018543+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_382303c568fe511544c732b5d8fd113e1f8a90cb13d0f163163a32e614b5c227","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 16 (Airy-time coefficient and the row-column correlation window) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Let $p,q,P,Q$ be positive integers satisfying
\[
 p\leq q,\qquad P\leq Q,\qquad p\leq P,\qquad q\leq Q.
\]
Put
\[
 A=P-p,\qquad B=Q-q,\qquad r_0=q-p,\qquad r=Q-P.
\]
For $0\leq n\leq m$, define
\[
 \varphi_{n,m}(x)
 =
 \sqrt{\frac{n!}{m!}}\,
 \ee^{-x/2}x^{(m-n)/2}L_n^{(m-n)}(x).
\]
For $1\leq\ell\leq p$, define
\[
 c_\ell
 =
 \sqrt{
 \frac{(P-\ell)!(Q-\ell)!}
 {(p-\ell)!(q-\ell)!}
 }.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 &\sum_{\ell=1}^p
 \frac{(P-\ell)!}{(q-\ell)!}
 L_{P-\ell}^{(r)}(x)L_{p-\ell}^{(r_0)}(y)\\
 &\quad=
 \ee^{(x+y)/2}x^{-r/2}y^{-r_0/2}
 \sum_{\ell=1}^p
 c_\ell
 \varphi_{P-\ell,Q-\ell}(x)
 \varphi_{p-\ell,q-\ell}(y).
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
Moreover, with
\[
 c_0=\sqrt{\frac{P!Q!}{p!q!}},
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \frac{c_\ell}{c_0}
 =
 \left\{
 \prod_{h=0}^{\ell-1}
 \frac{(p-h)(q-h)}{(P-h)(Q-h)}
 \right\}^{1/2}.
\end{equation}

Define
\[
 \delta_{p,q}
 =
 \frac{(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)^{2/3}}{(pq)^{1/3}},
 \qquad
 \tau_{p,q;A,B}
 =
 \frac{A/p+B/q}{2\delta_{p,q}}.
\]
Fix $c_{\mathrm{box}}>0$ and $C_{\mathrm{box}}<\infty$. There is a constant $C$ depending only on them such that, whenever
\[
 c_{\mathrm{box}}N\leq p,q\leq C_{\mathrm{box}}N,
 \qquad
 A+B\leq\frac{c_{\mathrm{box}}N}{4},
 \qquad
 1\leq\ell\leq\frac{c_{\mathrm{box}}N}{2},
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \left|
 \log\frac{c_\ell}{c_0}
 +
 \tau_{p,q;A,B}\delta_{p,q}\ell
 \right|
 \leq
 C\frac{(A+B)\ell^2+(A^2+B^2)\ell}{N^2}.
\end{equation}
If $D_N>0$ satisfies
\[
 \frac{\log D_N}{\log N}\to0,
 \qquad
 A+B\leq N^{2/3}D_N,
 \qquad
 \ell\leq N^{1/3}D_N,
\]
then uniformly over these $\ell$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{c_\ell}{c_0}
 =
 \exp(-\tau_{p,q;A,B}\delta_{p,q}\ell)(1+o(1)).
\end{equation}
If
\[
 \frac pN\to a>0,\qquad
 \frac qN\to b>0,\qquad
 \frac A{N^{2/3}}\to\alpha,\qquad
 \frac B{N^{2/3}}\to\beta,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \tau_{p,q;A,B}
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{\alpha/a+\beta/b}{2d_{a,b}},
 \qquad
 d_{a,b}
 =
 \frac{(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^{2/3}}{(ab)^{1/3}}.
\end{equation}
Thus $\tau$ tends to zero when $A+B=o(N^{2/3})$, remains of order one when $A+B$ is of order $N^{2/3}$, and tends to infinity when
\[
 \frac{A+B}{N^{2/3}}\to\infty,
 \qquad
 A+B=o(N).
\]

For the nested rectangles $(M_N,N)$, assume
\[
 \frac{M_N}{N}\to\gamma\in(0,\infty),
 \qquad
 0\leq M_{N+1}-M_N\leq K.
\]
Compare $(M_N,N)$ with $(M_{N+H},N+H)$, where $1\leq H=o(N)$, and sort their dimensions into $(p,q)$ and $(P,Q)$. Then there are constants $0<c<C<\infty$, depending only on $\gamma$ and $K$, such that
\begin{equation}
 c\frac{H}{N^{2/3}}
 \leq
 \tau_{p,q;P-p,Q-q}
 \leq
 C\frac{H}{N^{2/3}}
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $N$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:30:28.836819+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_38627ab69aea12685e95edd74d88bef301af4d1662aa8e92d413e2f4d8eb65d5","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2609.02169, '2609.02169'] Let $S$ be a complex abelian surface.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:28:08.691730+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_38628fa68ff7131990300065a166081a9d3114929b9b09e8ada5a8082342784f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 12 of arXiv:2607.29534, 'Expected signatures via partial integration, coordinate change and symmetrization'] For $w,v\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}}$,
$r,q\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}}$, and
$\blue{i},\blue{j}\in\mathcal{A}^{\prime}$,
\begin{equation}
\left\{\begin{aligned}
r\gammashuffle q
&=
r\shuffle q,
\\
(w\blue{i}r)\gammashuffle q
&=
w\blue{i}(r\shuffle q),
\\
r\gammashuffle(v\blue{j}q)
&=
v\blue{j}(r\shuffle q),
\\
(w\blue{i}r)\gammashuffle(v\blue{j}q)
&=
\bigl((w\blue{i})\gammashuffle v\bigr)
\blue{j}(r\shuffle q)
+
\bigl(w\gammashuffle(v\blue{j})\bigr)
\blue{i}(r\shuffle q).
\end{aligned}\right.
\end{equation}
These identities uniquely determine $\gammashuffle$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:25:06.200908+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3868ed49fdf830327ebcf31c5da52e30f470519cbe34592632474628329eb581","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.22636, 'Q-Learning with Stable Infinite-Dimensional \\Linear Function Approximation'] Fix real numbers $\alpha\ge 1$ and $T>0$, and integers $n\ge0$ and $n_0>0$.  Set $\alpha_k=\alpha/(k+n_0)$,
$\tau(n,m)=\sum_{k=n}^{m-1}\alpha_{k+1}$, and
$\cW(n,T)=\setcond{m\ge n}{\tau(n,m)\le T}$.  Then, for every $m\in\cW(n,T)$,
\begin{equation}
        m+n_0+1
        \le
        e^{T/\alpha}(n+n_0+1).
        
\end{equation}

If $m_\vee=\max\cW(n,T)$ and $\alpha_{n+1}\le T/2$, then the end time satisfies
\begin{equation}
        \frac{T}{2}
        \le
        \tau(n,m_\vee)
        \le
        T.
        
\end{equation}

If either $T=1/4$ and $n+n_0\ge8$, or
$T=1/5$ and $n+n_0\ge10$, then
\begin{equation}
        m+n_0
        \le
        \frac32(n+n_0),
        \quad \forall m\in\cW(n,T).
        
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:57:44.959349+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3871ea0a5b1557d2bd00332b923a17fcdd3bb1a8e672d5f8331dbf563536733e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 22 (Localized continuous centered second-chaos operator) of arXiv:2606.26065, 'Localized Centered Second-Chaos Operators'] Assume the continuous Gaussian setup of Section~\ref{sec:setup}, the order-zero symbol bound~\eqref{eq:m-size}, covariance bounds~\eqref{eq:S-size}, and the time-regularity and cutoff-convergence assumptions in Assumption~\ref{ass:time}.  Assume also the power-law envelope~\eqref{eq:power-envelope}.  Let $\lambda>0$ and let $s,\sigma\in\R$ satisfy the strict window~\eqref{eq:lambda-window}.  Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item For every finite $p\ge2$, the localized centered Galerkin operators
\[
 \cB^\circ_\Lambda:
 \Xspace_T^\sigma
 \longrightarrow
 C_TH^{s-\lambda}\cap L_T^1B^{\sigma-\lambda}_{2,\infty}
\]
are uniformly bounded in $L^p(\Omega)$ and converge in $L^p$ operator norm.  More precisely, after choosing $\eps>0$ below the strict margins in~\eqref{eq:lambda-window},
\[
 \sup_{\Lambda\in\Dyd\cup\{\infty\}}
 \left\|
 \norm{\cB^\circ_\Lambda}_{\Xspace_T^\sigma\to C_TH^{s-\lambda}\cap L_T^1B^{\sigma-\lambda}_{2,\infty}}
 \right\|_{L^p(\Omega)}<\infty,
\]
and
\[
 \cB^\circ_\Lambda\to\cB^\circ
 \quad\text{in }L^p\bigl(\Omega;\cL(\Xspace_T^\sigma,
 C_TH^{s-\lambda}\cap L_T^1B^{\sigma-\lambda}_{2,\infty})\bigr).
\]
\item Under the finite-state Galerkin condition in Assumption~\ref{ass:time}, there is one full-probability event $\Omega_*$ on which the whole Galerkin sequence converges pathwise in the same operator norm.  The same event controls all dyadic blocks simultaneously.
\end{enumerate}
The result applies to independent Gaussian legs and to same-family Wick squares after complete Wick centering and decoupling.  The finite-state hypothesis is used only in item~\textup{(ii)}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.360578+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3886ad8530baeb3a3681c5a268cbb86bf82b63c3a3aa5a6382e8733a6fb1dffa","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Ppn 256 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In both the spherical and Ising settings, there exists $c>0$ and $C = C(\alpha) > 0$ such that the following holds.
    Let $\cA^\circ$ be a $L$-Lipschitz algorithm with $L\ge 1$.
    Let $\chi^\circ \equiv \chi_{\cA^\circ}$ and $q_0 \equiv \chi^\circ(0)$, and suppose $q_0 < 1$.
    Then, there exists an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA$ such that the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item $\chi \equiv \chi_{\cA}$ satisfies $\chi(0) = q_0$ and
    \[
        \chi'(0) \ge  \frac1{L^2}\,.
    \]
In fact, we can take
    \[
        \chi(p) = \bigg(1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg) \chi^\circ(p)+ \frac{q_0 + (1-q_0)p}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \]

\item 
The perturbed algorithm $\cA$ approximates the original algorithm $\cA^\circ$ in the sense that
    \[
        \frac{1}{N} \E\Big[\|\cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) - \cA(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\|^2\Big]
        \le \frac{2}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \]

\end{enumerate}
We remark that the above error should be considered small, since we will prove later in Lemma~\ref{l:sM.Lip.1.trivial} that a sequence of algorithms with $q_0$ tending to one can only achieve the gaussian distribution.

\begin{proof} 
Let $\dot{\bg}$ be a standard gaussian in $\bbR^N$ independent of $\bg^{\aux}$, and
let $\bv$ be a deterministic element of $S_N$ with 
 $(\bv,\bbE \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux})) = 0$. The perturbed algorithm $\cA$ is defined by
    \[\cA(\bG, (\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg} )) 
        = \bigg\{1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}
            \bigg\}^{1/2}
        \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) 
        + \bigg(\frac{q_0}{1-q_0}\bigg)^{1/2} \frac{\bv}{L}
        + \frac{\dot{\bg}}{L} \,.
    \]
Then the gradient of $\cA$ can be bounded as
    \begin{align*}
        \|\nabla\cA
            (\bG,(\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg})) \|^2
        &= \|\nabla_{\bG,\bg^{\aux}}
            \cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg} )) \|^2
        + \|\nabla_{\dot{\bg}} 
            \cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux},\dot{\bg})) \|^2 \\
        &\le \bigg\{1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0) L^2}   \bigg\} L^2 
            + \frac1{L^2}
        \le L^2\,.
    \end{align*}
Since $\bv$ is deterministic and orthogonal to $\bbE \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux})$,
 $\dot{\bg}$ is independent of $(\bG,\bg^{\aux})$, and $\bbE[\|\dot{\bg}\|^2] = N$, we have
    \[\frac{\bbE[
             \|\cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux},\dot{\bg}))\|^2]}{N}
    =\bigg\{ 1-\frac1{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg\}
    	+\frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2}
	+\frac{1}{L^2}
    = 1\,,
    \]
where the last step follows from the trivial inequality $1-q_0\le1\le L^2$.  The above two displays show that $\cA$ is an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}. Moreover, recalling the abbreviations $\chi\equiv\chi_\cA$ and $\chi^\circ\equiv\chi_{\cA^\circ}$, for any $0\le p\le1$ we have
    \[\chi(p) 
    = \bigg(1-\frac1{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg) \chi^\circ(p) + \frac{q_0+(1-q_0)p}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,,
    \]
which implies $\chi(0)=q_0$.
   As noted above, $\chi^\circ$ is nondecreasing, which implies $\chi'(0)\ge 1/L^2$. This proves part~\eqref{it:wlogable.PERTURBED.CHI}. 

Next, since $|a^{1/2}-b^{1/2}| \le |a-b|^{1/2}$ for all $a,b\ge0$, we can bound
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{1}{N} \E\bigg[\Big\|\cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) - \cA(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\Big\|^2\bigg]
        &= \bigg(1 - \bigg(1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg)^{1/2}\bigg)^2
        + \frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{1}{L^2} \\
        &\le \frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{1}{L^2}
        = \frac{2}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \end{align*}
This proves part~\eqref{it:wlogable.PERTURBED.APPX}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:33:17.723457+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_388f8d1138c66622039ba74f2a687fc64be7366cb3c5ed27c0ac7721c10ad963","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 71 (Localization remainder) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $\mathcal R^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,Q,M}(t,s)$ denote the sum over the

For every $2\le p<\infty$, every $A>0$, and every

\begin{align}
 \|\mathcal R^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,Q,M}(t,s)\|_{
 L^p_\omega\mathcal L(L_q^2,L_n^2)}

{"assumptions":["mu satisfies the FKG lattice condition, automatic for independent product measures but requiring verification for dependent Gibbs measures","f, g, or the events A, B, are both increasing, or both decreasing, with respect to the same partial order","the state space is finite or otherwise compactified so that all expectations involved are well defined"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.973188+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_38b7645fc7da6a9d085dab2a80793f9ef28cf412f7ea823995207adfbe1333e1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let mu be a probability measure on a finite distributive lattice satisfying the FKG lattice condition mu(x v y) mu(x ^ y) >= mu(x) mu(y) for all x, y, a condition automatically satisfied by any product measure on {0,1}^E, in which case the conclusion is called the Harris inequality. Then for any two increasing (or two decreasing) functions f, g in L^2(mu), E[fg] >= E[f]E[g]; equivalently, for increasing events A, B, mu(A ^ B) >= mu(A) mu(B), so increasing events are positively correlated. This is the basic monotone-coupling tool throughout percolation and interacting particle systems, lower-bounding joint probabilities of increasing events, such as several disjoint crossings occurring together, by the product of their individual probabilities, and it justifies a wide range of comparison and sprinkling arguments. It does not give any upper bound on the correlation, which requires separate and generally harder tools such as the van den Berg-Kesten inequality for disjoint occurrence; it does not apply to a mix of an increasing and a decreasing event without flipping a sign; and the strength of the positive correlation is not quantified beyond nonnegativity. Typical failure: Applying FKG to a pair of events where one is increasing and the other decreasing without flipping the sign, which reverses the direction of the inequality; or invoking FKG for a non-product Gibbs measure, such as a random-cluster model outside the ferromagnetic regime with cluster weight q<1, without checking the lattice condition, which is known to fail there. {"assumptions":["Ω ⊂ R^n open; derivatives taken in the distributional sense"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:57.492362+00:00","domain":"Sobolev spaces, functional analysis for PDE","id":"claim_38c3cd05223b169021fe1f60a1ce84a3a15d39f588dd388ecea15bbf6fdb3634","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and k ≥ 1 an integer. W^{k,p}(Ω) is the set of u ∈ L^p(Ω) all of whose distributional derivatives D^α u with |α| ≤ k lie in L^p(Ω): for each α there is g_α ∈ L^p(Ω) with ∫_Ω u D^α φ dx = (−1)^{|α|} ∫_Ω g_α φ dx for every φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω); one writes D^α u = g_α (the weak derivative, unique a.e.). The norm is ||u||_{W^{k,p}} = ( Σ_{|α| ≤ k} ||D^α u||_{L^p}^p )^{1/p} (maximum over α for p = ∞). W^{k,p}(Ω) is a Banach space, separable for p < ∞ and reflexive for 1 < p < ∞. H^k(Ω) := W^{k,2}(Ω) is a Hilbert space with ⟨u, v⟩ = Σ_{|α| ≤ k} ∫_Ω D^α u D^α v dx. W^{k,p}_0(Ω) is the closure of C_c^∞(Ω) in W^{k,p}(Ω) (functions 'vanishing on the boundary' together with derivatives of order < k); H^1_0(Ω) := W^{1,2}_0(Ω). The Sobolev conjugate of p < n is p* = np/(n − p), i.e. 1/p* = 1/p − 1/n.\n\nFacts: C^∞(Ω) ∩ W^{k,p}(Ω) is dense in W^{k,p}(Ω) for p < ∞ and any open Ω (Meyers–Serrin); restrictions of C^∞(R^n) functions are dense when Ω is bounded with Lipschitz boundary; W^{k,p}_0(R^n) = W^{k,p}(R^n); for bounded Ω, W^{1,p}_0(Ω) is a proper closed subspace of W^{1,p}(Ω) (nonzero constants are excluded by the Poincaré inequality). On an interval, W^{1,p} functions have absolutely continuous representatives; in dimension n ≥ 2 a W^{1,p} function with p ≤ n can be unbounded and discontinuous. For a bounded Lipschitz domain, W^{1,∞}(Ω) is the space of Lipschitz functions on Ω̄.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T17:09:41.192539+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_38c908d6d617590f98221d7a1608eff9bf05db02ce35b5c55d59b799004eb09e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In computational complexity theory, NP-complete problems are the hardest of the problems to which solutions can be verified quickly. Somewhat more precisely, a problem is NP-complete when:It is a decision problem, meaning that for any input to the problem, the output is either \"yes\" or \"no\". Each input to the problem is associated with a collection of short solutions, which might or might not validly solve the input. The output is \"yes\" when at least one of these solutions is valid, and \"no\" when none of them are. The validity of each solution can be verified quickly, and a brute-force search algorithm can find a valid solution by trying all possible solutions. The problem can be used to simulate every other problem for which we can verify quickly that a solution is valid. Hence, if we could find valid solutions of some NP-complete problem quickly, we could quickly find valid solutions for every other problem in which a given solution can be easily verified.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:07:17.250028+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_38d09da622398d9dd421952ba93b8f74f2e01852e209a0102d833c6c15514e67","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition ARTASS of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let \((\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P}, \theta)\) be a measurable metric dynamical system, and let \(\mathcal{X}\) be a Polish space.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item A random variable \(Y : \Omega \rightarrow (0, \infty)\) is called \emph{tempered} if
		\begin{align*}
			\limsup_{|t| \to \infty,\, t \in \mathbb{T}} \frac{1}{|t|} \log^{+} Y(\theta_t \omega) = 0,
			\quad \text{for } \mathbb{P}\text{-almost every } \omega \in \Omega,
		\end{align*}
		where \(\log^{+} x := \max\{ \log x, 0 \}\).
		
		\item Let \(\mathcal{E}=\{\mathcal{E}(\omega)\}_{\omega \in \Omega}\) be a family of non-empty subsets of \(\mathcal{X}\) such that, for every \(x \in \mathcal{X}\), the function \(\omega \mapsto d(x, \mathcal{E}(\omega))\) is measurable, and with probability one each \(\mathcal{E}(\omega)\) is bounded in \(\mathcal{X}\). We call \(\mathcal{E}\) a {tempered set} if the random variable
		\[
		r(\mathcal{E}(\omega)) := \sup_{x \in \mathcal{E}(\omega)} d(x, x_0)
		\]
		is tempered for some fixed reference point \(x_0 \in \mathcal{X}\). The collection of tempered sets in $\mathcal{X}$ is denoted by $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{X})$.
	\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.362314+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3907ba1bb23285f6271317103cf46cd38c9c1ff8274747604b58e4a04f63bcf6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 3 (Asymptotic validity and power of the test) of arXiv:2608.29465, 'Deciding When to Decide:\\Testing Operational Suboptimality Under Distributional Shift'] Suppose the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:delta_hat_rate} and the local inverse-stability condition in Assumption~\ref{assm:error_bound_P0} hold, and suppose the conditional CLT in Assumption~\ref{ass:eval_clt} holds. \[

\]
denote the preference-estimation error rate. If $\delta_{\rm inv}=0$ and $\sqrt{m''}\,a_n\to0$, then the Wald test in \eqref{eq:T_wald} has asymptotic level $\alpha$:
\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:38:37.420569+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_39087098b6e1681f47b9ce650648a83f4bf1b4beaf147a91fc4fa1a23511ead1","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2605.16733, 'Concentration Inequalities for Sample Cross-Covariances'] Let \((X_i)_{i=1}^N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered Gaussian random
vector \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_X}\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma_X\), and let
\(L\) be a fixed matrix such that $        P:=L\Sigma_XL^\top $ is nonzero. Then
\[
\E \left\|
\bigg( \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N
X_iX_i^\top -\E XX^\top\bigg) L^\top
\right\|
\gtrsim
(\|\Sigma_X\|\|P\|)^{1/2}
\bigg(
\sqrt{\frac{r_X+r_P}{N}}
+
\frac{\sqrt{r_Xr_P}}{N}

\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:23:03.033543+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_39189ad78c197f73292494ba14447706a1b7c8cc2e534c93d9a79bda2361d8c4","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 10 (Decay of the first derivatives of the decoupled flow) of arXiv:2605.03057, 'Uniform-in-time quantitative fluctuations of large scale interacting particle systems'] Assume Assumption~\ref{ass:coeff-level-new}. Fix $ x \in \R^d $, $ \mu \in \Ptwo $, let
$ X_t^{x,\mu} $ be the decoupled flow, and $\omega$ be the constant
defined in \eqref{eq:def-omega-uniform-time}. Then, the following hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For every $ h \in \R^d $, the first spatial derivative
$ \partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] $ exists and solves
\begin{equation}

d\left( \partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] \right)
=
\partial_x b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] dt
+
\partial_x \sigma\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] dB_t,
\end{equation}
with initial condition $\partial_x X_0^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] =
h$. Moreover, for every $ p \in \mathcal P $ and all $t \ge 0$,
\begin{equation}

\E\left(
\abs{\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right]}^p
\right)
\le
e^{-\frac{p\kappa_p}{2} t} \abs{h}^p
\le
e^{-p\omega t} \abs{h}^p.
\end{equation}

\item[(ii)] For every $ v \in \R^d $, the Lions derivative
$ \partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right) $ exists and solves
\begin{align}

d\left( \partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right) \right)
&=
\Bigg(
\partial_x b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right)
+
