{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:51:33.320716+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_392f7fb8b14f0e406f5cc9ff7d53893f29a62a8c49f53c05cd8cb85fddb10ee7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop Spc*-levelwise-tensor of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let ${\mathcal{C}}$ be any $S$-cocomplete $T$-$\infty$-category. Then the levelwise tensor product ${\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}$ is again $S$-cocomplete, the map ${\mathcal{C}}\to{\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}$ induced by $(-)_+\colon\Spc\to\Spc_*$ is $S$-cocontinuous, and it moreover admits the following universal property: for every pointed $S$-cocomplete $T$-$\infty$-category ${\mathcal{D}}$, restriction defines an equivalence
    \[
        \ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}_T({\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}_T({\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}).
    \]
    \begin{proof}
        In light of Proposition~(prop:univ-prop-*-cc-param of the paper), it will be enough to construct an equivalence ${\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\mathcal{C}}_*$ under ${\mathcal{C}}$. For this, we consider the commutative diagram
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                {\Spc}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_{\hphantom{*}}\arrow[d]\arrow[r] & {\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_{\hphantom{*}}\arrow[d]\\
                {\Spc}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_*\arrow[r] & {\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_*
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        with horizontal maps induced by $(-)_+\colon\Spc\to\Spc_*$ and vertical maps induced by $(-)_+\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{C}}_*$. We claim that the right-hand vertical map and the bottom horizontal map are equivalences; this will then complete the proof of the corollary.

        To see that the bottom horizontal map is an equivalence, it suffices to show that ${\Spc}\otimes{\mathcal{D}}\to{\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{D}}$ is invertible for every (non-parametrized) pointed cocomplete ${\mathcal{D}}$, or equivalently that the induced map between corepresented functors on $\CAT_\infty^\text{cc}$ is an equivalence. By the defining property of the tensor product, the latter amounts to saying that we have an equivalence
        \begin{equation}
            {-}\circ(-)_+\colon{\textup{Hom}}(\Spc_*,{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}}))\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\textup{Hom}}(\Spc,{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}}))
        \end{equation}
        for any cocomplete ${\mathcal{E}}$. By [CLL_Global]*{Corollary 4.1.10${}^{\textup{op}}$}, the full subcategory of ${\textup{Fun}}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})$ spanned by the functors preserving the initial object is pointed, whence so is the smaller subcategory ${\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})$ as it still contains the initial object. Thus, applying the Proposition~(prop:univ-prop-*-cc-param of the paper) for $S=T=1$ shows that $((eq:univ-prop-pted of the paper))$ is an equivalence.

        For the vertical map, we similarly compare corepresented functors on fiberwise cocomplete $\infty$-categories. Arguing as above, this reduces us to invertibility of
        \[
            {\textup{Hom}}({\mathcal{C}}_*,{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}(\Spc_*,-)\circ{\mathcal{D}})\to
            {\textup{Hom}}({\mathcal{C}},{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}(\Spc_*,-)\circ{\mathcal{D}}),
        \]
        and applying the above levelwise shows that ${\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}(\Spc_*,-)\circ{\mathcal{D}}$ is pointed. The claim therefore follows from the special case $S=\core T$ of the proposition.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["pointwise form: u ∈ C^2(Ω) (or H^2_loc, a.e.)","integrated form: Ω bounded with Lipschitz boundary, u ∈ C^2 up to the boundary or u ∈ H^2(Ω)","eigenvalue formula: additionally u = 0 on ∂Ω and −Δu = λu in Ω"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:57.492269+00:00","domain":"elliptic PDE, Rellich and Pohozaev identities, Dirichlet eigenvalues","id":"claim_39490348519396f0628002960648e225d47916ef40d2fa4016bd80557364979d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Pointwise identity. Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, x the position vector, and u ∈ C^2(Ω). Then, everywhere in Ω,
   div( (x·∇u) ∇u − (1/2)|∇u|^2 x ) = (x·∇u) Δu − ((n−2)/2) |∇u|^2.
The same holds almost everywhere for u ∈ H^2_loc(Ω) (all terms are then in L^1_loc). Replacing x by x − x_0 for any fixed x_0 gives the same identity (translation invariance).

Integrated form (Rellich). Let Ω be a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary, ν the outward unit normal, dS surface measure, and u ∈ C^2(Ω̄), or u ∈ H^2(Ω) with the boundary integrals read through the L^2(∂Ω) traces of ∇u. Then
   ∫_Ω (x·∇u) Δu dx = ((n−2)/2) ∫_Ω |∇u|^2 dx + ∫_∂Ω [ (x·∇u)(∂_ν u) − (1/2)|∇u|^2 (x·ν) ] dS.

Dirichlet case. If in addition u = 0 on ∂Ω (trace sense), then the tangential gradient vanishes on ∂Ω, ∇u = (∂_ν u) ν there, and the boundary term collapses to (1/2) ∫_∂Ω (x·ν) (∂_ν u)^2 dS. If moreover −Δu = λu in Ω, then
   λ ∫_Ω u^2 dx = (1/2) ∫_∂Ω (x·ν) (∂_ν u)^2 dS,
the Rellich formula expressing a Dirichlet eigenvalue by a boundary integral; equivalently 2λ||u||^2_{L^2(Ω)} = ∫_∂Ω (x·ν)(∂_ν u)^2 dS. For a domain star-shaped with respect to the origin (x·ν ≥ 0 on ∂Ω) the right side is nonnegative term by term. The same computation with −Δu = f(u), u = 0 on ∂Ω, is the Pohozaev identity.

Where it fails / hypotheses that matter. The integrated form needs enough regularity to give ∇u a boundary trace: u ∈ H^2(Ω) (or C^2 up to the boundary). A Dirichlet eigenfunction on a Lipschitz domain that is not convex (a re-entrant corner) need not belong to H^2(Ω), and the identity is then not available in this form without a separate justification. Without u = 0 on ∂Ω the tangential gradient contributes and the simplified boundary term (1/2)∫(x·ν)(∂_ν u)^2 is wrong: the full bracket must be kept. The sign of x·ν is not fixed for a general domain, so conclusions that use x·ν ≥ 0 (star-shapedness, Pohozaev-type nonexistence) fail otherwise. In dimension n = 2 the interior term ((n−2)/2)∫|∇u|^2 vanishes. The identity is for the Laplacian; for a variable-coefficient operator div(A∇u) extra terms involving x·∇A appear.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:58:01.576577+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_397e714e80d89ae6a0e1490bbb818b807c63070c0991d72e6e7ac8f9b75d4cde","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 13 ($\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier) of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Fix $\vartheta\ge1$. Let $N\ge1$, and let
$\Omega\subset\R^N$ be convex and relatively open in its affine hull,
that is, in the smallest affine subspace containing $\Omega$. Set
	\[
	\mathsf V_\Omega
	:=\operatorname{span}\{z-z':z,z'\in\Omega\}.
	\]
	Let $\Psi:\Omega\to\R$ be convex and $C^3$ along line segments in
	$\Omega$. Define the local seminorm
	\[
		\|h\|_{\Psi,z}^2:=\mathrm D^2\Psi(z)[h,h],
		\qquad z\in\Omega,\quad h\in\mathsf V_\Omega.
	\]
	We call such a convex function $\Psi$ a \emph{$\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier} for
	$\Omega$ if $\Psi(z)\to\infty$ as $z$ approaches the relative boundary
	of $\Omega$ and, for every $z\in\Omega$ and $h\in\mathsf V_\Omega$,
	\begin{equation*}
		\tag{SC}
		\bigl|\mathrm D^3\Psi(z)[h,h,h]\bigr|
		\le 2\|h\|_{\Psi,z}^3.
	\end{equation*}
	It must also satisfy the barrier-parameter bound for all $h\in \mathsf V_\Omega$
	\begin{equation*}
		\tag{$\mathrm{BP}_\vartheta$}
		|\mathrm D\Psi(z)[h]|
		\le \sqrt{\vartheta}\,\|h\|_{\Psi,z}.
	\end{equation*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.565204+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3982146e5d653c67e701d5516401f8b16982db4bb5524c5a0741f28e83b513bf","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\\CLE_4$ I:\\\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple...'] We consider the conformal loop ensemble (CLE) with the parameter $\\kappa=4$, the critical value at or below which the loops are simple and do not intersect each other or the domain boundary. This metric was previously constructed in unpublished work of Sheffield, Watson, and Wu. Our approach differs in that we show that the metric arises as the renormalized limit of the graph metric on $\\CLE_\\kappa$ loops as $\\kappa \\downarrow 4$. {"assumptions":["f integrable on the circle","Dini: the integral of |f(x+t)+f(x-t)-2s|/t over (0,1/2) is finite; mere continuity at x is NOT enough","the Holder / two-sided Dini conditions must control t of both signs","symmetric partial sums (the statement is about S_N, not about arbitrary summation orders)"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.263083+00:00","domain":"Fourier series on the circle","id":"claim_39aa62a1130807959488e8d5cf169a363d9a4986f3256659d961d4aa7aea804d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $f\\in L^1(\\mathbb T)$, $x\\in\\mathbb T$ and $s\\in\\mathbb C$.  \nu_S(y,\psi(y))

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:32:38.632345+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_39baeb3eabbb257b7e4aa3ce750ce9b50035b5037c9d49d8733bed029492040e","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2506.17045, '\LARGE{On bivariate Archimax copulas: Level sets, mass distributions and related results}'] Let $I_1,I_2,I_3$ be open sub-intervals of $\mathbb{R}$ and let $\iota \colon I_1 \rightarrow I_2$ be a function whose left-hand derivative $D^-\iota$ exists. Moreover, let $\eta \colon I_2 \rightarrow I_3$ be an arbitrary function. Then the following assertions hold:
      \begin{itemize}
          \item[$(i)$] If $\eta$ is strictly decreasing and convex, then
          $$
          D^-\eta^{-1}(z) = \frac{1}{D^+\eta(\eta^{-1}(z))}
          $$
          holds for every $z \in I_3$, whereby $\eta^{-1}$ denotes the inverse function of $\eta$.
          \item[$(ii)$] If $D^-\eta$ exists and $\iota$ is a non-decreasing function, then
          $$
          D^-(\eta\circ\iota)(t) = D^-\eta(\iota(t)) \cdot D^-\iota(t)
          $$
          holds for every $t \in I_1$.
        \item[$(iii)$] If $D^-\eta$ exists and $\iota$ is a non-increasing function, then
          $$
          D^-(\eta\circ\iota)(t) = D^+\eta(\iota(t)) \cdot D^-\iota(t)
          $$
          holds for every $t \in I_1$.
      \end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

\frac{N}{d}\log N
+\left(\frac{\gamma}{d}+

+
D_d
+

where,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:04:59.433232+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_39be3c07534955c5163b8128720d3b73788c3c3481893d240c3fd2ff56867b28","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:ito-centered-lyapunov-differential of arXiv:2605.20697, 'Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for \\ Second-Order Consensus-Based Optimization'] Let \(p\geqslant2\), and assume the conditions of (assump:centered-decay of the paper).
Let
\[
    L_p(t):=L_p(\mathcal X_t^J,\mathcal V_t^J)
\]
denote the pathwise centered Lyapunov functional defined in
(equation eq:random-Lp-def of the paper) for \(p>2\), and in (equation eq:random-L2-def of the paper) for \(p=2\).

Define the local martingale \(M_{p,t}:=J^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^J M_{p,t}^j\) by
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d M_{p,t}^j
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        \displaystyle
        2\left\langle \hat Z_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle
        +
        \frac5\gamma
        \left\langle Y_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle,
        & p=2,\\[1.2em]
        \displaystyle
        p|\hat Z_t^j|^{p-2}
        \left\langle \hat Z_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle
        +
        \frac m\gamma |Y_t^j|^{p-2}
        \left\langle Y_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle,
        & p>2.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Then there exists a local martingale \(M_{p,t}\) such that, in the sense of semimartingale differentials,
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d L_p(t)
    \leqslant
    -\lambda_p L_p(t)\,\mathrm d t+\mathrm d M_{p,t},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
    \lambda_p
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        \displaystyle
        \frac{\min\{v_1,v_3\}}{c_2^{(2)}},
        & p=2,\\[1.2em]
        \displaystyle
        \frac{p\mu_{\mathrm{gap},p}}{4\gamma},
        & p>2.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Here, for \(p=2\),
\[
    v_1:=\frac1{m\gamma}+\frac3{\gamma^3}-K_\sigma,
    \qquad
    v_3:=\frac{2\gamma}{m}-\frac3\gamma,
\]
and \(c_2^{(2)}\) is the upper norm-equivalence constant associated with \(\psi_2\).

Moreover, when \(p>2\), the stronger componentwise estimate holds:
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d L_p(t)
    \leqslant
    -\widehat\lambda_Y
    \left(\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J |Y_t^j|^p\right)\mathrm d t
    -\widehat\lambda_Z
    \left(\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J |\hat Z_t^j|^p\right)\mathrm d t
    +
    \mathrm d M_{p,t},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{align}
    \widehat\lambda_Y
    &:=
    \frac1\gamma
    \left[
        C_{\mathrm{pos}}
        -
        \gamma\left(\frac2m+\frac1{\gamma^2}\right)
        \left(\frac4\gamma\right)^{p-1}
        +
        \frac{m(p-1)}{\gamma^2}
    \right],
    \\
    \widehat\lambda_Z
    &:=
    p\left(\frac\gamma m+\frac1\gamma\right)
    -
    \left(
        \frac{p-1}{2m}\gamma+\frac{p-1}{4\gamma}
    \right)
    -
    \frac{2m(p-1)}{p\gamma}
    -
    \Lambda_p\sigma^{\frac{2p}{p-2}}\gamma^{\frac2{p-2}}\,,
    
\end{align}
where $C_{\mathrm{pos}} = 1-\frac{3\mu_{\mathrm{gap},p}}{16} - \frac{m(p-1)(p-2)}p$ as defined from (equation eq:Cpos-def of the paper). Under (assump:centered-decay of the paper), these coefficients satisfy
\begin{equation}
    \widehat\lambda_Y
    \geqslant
    \lambda_p
    \left(
        a_p+\frac{m(p-1)}{p\gamma}
    \right),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
    \widehat\lambda_Z
    \geqslant
    \lambda_p
    \left(
        1+\frac{m}{p\gamma}
    \right).
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.162189+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_39ef52ee75249f5f440b1e1246bef6c63616758f5dffa470be1204a3dd78e398","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Cor 17 (\cite{MR51275}; see also \cite{MR317760}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Take $A,b,C,d$ as in Theorem~\ref{t:hoffman} with $(b,d)\in F(A,C)$.
Let $B(M_0)$ denote the ball of radius $M_0$ in $\R^n$, centered at the origin.
\begin{enumerate}[a.]
\item  Suppose $(b',d')\in F(A,C)$, and
suppose further that the (nonempty) sets
$S_{A,C}(b,d)$ and $S_{A,C}(b',d')$ are both contained in $B(M_0)$.
Then
	\[d_H\Big(S_{A,C}(b,d),S_{A,C}(b',d')\Big)
	\le c\left\| \begin{pmatrix}
	b-b'\\d-d'\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2
	\]
where $c$ is a finite constant depending only on $A,C,M_0$.
\item 
Now suppose we have $(A,b,C,d)'$ of the same dimensions,
with $(b',d')\in F(A',C')$. 
Suppose further that the (nonempty) sets
$S\equiv S_{A,C}(b,d)$ and $S'\equiv S_{A',C'}(b',d')$ are both contained in $B(M_0)$.
Then, for any $x'\in S'$ there exists $x\in S$ with
	\[\|x-x'\|_2
	\le c \left\| \begin{pmatrix} A-A'\\ C-C'\\
	b-b'\\d-d'\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2\,,
	\]
where $c$ is a finite constant depending only on $A,C,M_0$, and on the right-hand side we treat $A$ and $C$ as vectors of length $mn$ and $qn$ respectively.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
Suppose $x'\in S'$. Then
	\[
	Ax'-b
	=[A'+(A-A')] x'- [b' + (b-b')]
	\le (A-A')x'-(b-b')\,,
	\]
from which it follows that
	\[
	\|(Ax'-b)_+\|
	\le \| [(A-A')x'-(b-b')]_+\|
	\le \|A-A'\|_\textup{op} M_0 + \|b-b'\|\,.
	\]
Similarly, we can bound
	\[
	\|Cx'-d\|
	\le \|C-C'\|_\textup{op} M_0 + \|d-d'\|\,.
	\]
The operator norm is bounded by the Frobenius norm, so the conclusion of part~\eqref{i:hoffman.semicty} follows.
Part \eqref{i:hoffman.rhs} then follows from part~\eqref{i:hoffman.semicty}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["The standard thirteen-graph cubic distance-regular classification.","The values are reported computations from the campaign record."],"created_at":"2026-10-10T06:51:51.364653+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_39f9c09b53339b708c3cfa454baf0d76df290fd6db9f1e7d7a2a93b62a11785e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14; values computed exactly from the intersection-array identity tau_0 = k sum_{i=1}^d (k_i+...+k_d)/(k_i c_i). That identity was checked against a direct linear-algebra solve on twelve graphs, among them the cubic graphs K_{3,3}, Q_3, Petersen, Heawood, Pappus, Desargues and the dodecahedron, with the complete graph and the cycle as independent controls.] This is the cubic case of Open Problem 7.31 in David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html). For a finite connected simple distance-regular graph G with n vertices, let tau_0 = max_{x,y} E_x[T_y] for simple random walk. By the known classification, there are exactly thirteen cubic (valency-three) distance-regular graphs. Their (n, tau_0) values are: K_4 (4, 3); K_{3,3} (6, 6); cube Q_3 (8, 10); Petersen (10, 12); Heawood (14, 19); Pappus (18, 27); Desargues (20, 65/2); dodecahedron (20, 35); Coxeter (28, 45); Tutte-Coxeter (30, 48); Foster (90, 675/4); Biggs-Smith (102, 195); Tutte 12-cage (126, 234). Hence, given the classification, the maximum of tau_0/(n-1) over all cubic distance-regular graphs is 195/101 (about 1.9307), attained uniquely by the Biggs-Smith graph. This reproduces exactly the value Aldous and Fill attribute to Biggs and settles, for valency three, Biggs's outlined claim that it is the largest. The general O(n) conjecture over non-cycle distance-regular graphs is not settled by this computation. This is an unrefereed campaign result.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:22:48.886360+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3a0128436def76cd30107ff67bf32e1a2854b375166d68c82f3b502c6795500c","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 27 of arXiv:2608.29157, 'Dilator-based analysis of $\KP$'] For each $n\in\bbN$, let $A$ be the leading formula of $[\ttX_n]\vdash \Gamma_n$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:57:59.869570+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3a2208c3223e3a9b72a41a781c8d3f9662256b012cbe5aa3edd387241c9dd104","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theor thm:c4-finite-subgraph of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] There exists a universal constant

Fix an integer $d\ge2$, a real $\rho\in(0,1]$, and positive integers $k,r,n$ with  
 $$2 \le \rho k \le r\le k\le n.$$

\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:38:58.691035+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3a28131608d1c031a978474473c9df7ae0c9464cf41e320d89bb08210526302b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:moment_R_ex1 of arXiv:2510.21186, 'Weingarten Calculus with Virtual Isometries'] Let $m$, $l$, $q$ be nonnegative integers, and consider four sequences:
\[

\]
 of positive integers in $\{1,2,\dots,n\}.$
Then, for each $1 \le s \le n$ the moment
\[
\mathbb{E} \bigl[p_{i_1 j_1} \cdots p_{i_m j_m} \overline{p_{i_1' j_1'} \cdots p_{i_l' j_l'}} r_{ss}^q\bigr]

 vanishes unless $\bm{i} \sqcup \bm{j}'$ is a permutation of $\bm{j} \sqcup \bm{i}'$.

{"assumptions":["Sign convention: L u = -a^{ij} u_{x_i x_j} + b^i u_{x_i} + c u, subsolution means u_t + Lu <= 0","c identically zero for the full maximum principle","c >= 0 for the version with the positive part","bounded c of any sign for the comparison (sign) principle only"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:49.107002+00:00","domain":"parabolic partial differential equations","id":"claim_3a4cafe9e19336aa105a2005fb7c65fd586ea28dc22562c2af3b9b1faed19d02","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"For $u_t+Lu\\le0$ with $Lu=-a^{ij}u_{x_ix_j}+b^iu_{x_i}+cu$, the identity $\\max_{\\overline{U_T}}u=\\max_{\\Gamma_T}u$ requires $c\\equiv0$; with $c\\ge0$ only the weaker $\\max_{\\overline{U_T}}u\\le\\max_{\\Gamma_T}u^+$ survives; with $c$ of arbitrary sign even that fails. (a) $c<0$ destroys everything: on $U=(0,\\pi)$, $u(x,t)=e^t\\sin x$ satisfies $u_t-u_{xx}-2u=0$ (so $c=-2$), has $u=0$ on the lateral sides and $u=\\sin x\\le1$ at $t=0$, hence $\\max_{\\Gamma_T}u=1$, yet $u(\\pi/2,T)=e^T$ is arbitrarily large. (b) $c\\ge0$ genuinely needs the positive part: on $U=(0,\\pi)$ let $u$ solve $u_t-u_{xx}+u=0$ with $u\\equiv-1$ on $\\Gamma_T$ (initial and lateral data $-1$). Then $w=u+1$ solves $w_t-w_{xx}+w=1$ with $w=0$ on $\\Gamma_T$, so $w\\ge0$ by the $c\\ge0$ principle and $w\\not\\equiv0$; hence $\\max_{\\overline{U_T}}u>-1=\\max_{\\Gamma_T}u$, while indeed $\\max u\\le0=\\max_{\\Gamma_T}u^+$. (c) What always survives for bounded $c$ of any sign is the comparison principle: $u_t+Lu\\le0$ and $u\\le0$ on $\\Gamma_T$ imply $u\\le0$, because $v=e^{-\\gamma t}u$ solves an inequality with zeroth-order coefficient $c+\\gamma\\ge0$ for $\\gamma\\ge\\|c^-\\|_\\infty$. Uniqueness for the initial-boundary value problem therefore holds for any bounded $c$; it is only the location of extrema that needs the sign condition. Auditor's check: whenever a proof cites 'the maximum principle' for an equation with a reaction term, ask which of (a), (b), (c) is actually being used, and note that the sign convention depends on whether the operator is written $u_t-\\Delta u+cu$ or $u_t-\\Delta u-cu$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Bernoulli bond percolation on the hypercube {0,1}^d","Critical window width 2^{-d/3}"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T15:09:50+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3a7116d434f2c28df46cdf038009eb62d3472655392fb61aeca9584693ef8aec","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. Heydenreich-van der Hofstad Open Problem 13.4 asks that the second largest cluster at p_c(1 + eps) on {0,1}^d match, to leading order, the largest cluster at p_c(1 - eps), eps >> 2^{-d/3}. G(n,p) has this through the discrete duality principle: after the giant is removed, the rest is close in law to a subcritical G(n', p) with the dual mean (an asymptotic statement, not an exact symmetry); the hypercube has no such principle, so it must come from tails: the subcritical largest cluster is Theta(eps^{-2} log(eps^3 2^d)) once the tail P(|C| >= k) >= c k^{-1/2} exp(-c' eps^2 k) holds with the SHARP rate in eps^2 k (the upper bound is known, the sharp lower bound is the missing half), and the supercritical second-largest needs the same tail for the clusters after removal of the giant, which is the geometric-depletion question of the exploration process. So the duality principle is reduced, heuristically, to two tail statements, one subcritical with a sharp rate and one post-giant; turning tails into the size of the largest cluster also needs control of the number of clusters and of their dependence, so this is not an equivalence.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543633+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3a7f53cc4f4c10093c8e4e07c223f18d52212a9c7d6f98c1196f104f16111a3d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let gamma be the standard Gaussian measure on R^n. The ORNSTEIN-UHLENBECK SEMIGROUP is defined by MEHLER'S FORMULA P_t f(x) = integral f( e^{-t} x + sqrt(1 - e^{-2t}) y ) gamma(dy) for t >= 0. It is a Markov semigroup: P_0 = identity, P_{s+t} = P_s P_t, P_t 1 = 1, P_t preserves nonnegativity, gamma is INVARIANT (integral P_t f dgamma = integral f dgamma), and P_t is SELF-ADJOINT on L^2(gamma). Its generator is L f = Laplacian f - x . grad f, which satisfies the integration-by-parts identity integral (L u) v dgamma = - integral grad u . grad v dgamma. The Hermite polynomials diagonalise it: L He_alpha = - |alpha| He_alpha and P_t He_alpha = e^{-|alpha| t} He_alpha, so the n-th Wiener chaos is the eigenspace of eigenvalue -n. The COMMUTATION RELATION grad P_t f = e^{-t} P_t grad f follows by differentiating Mehler's formula under the integral. Two facts to keep straight: this is the semigroup for the standard Gaussian, and other normalisations of the generator (for example Laplacian/2 minus x . grad/2) rescale time and change the constants in the associated Poincare and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities. As t -> infinity, P_t f -> integral f dgamma, and the exponential rate of that convergence in L^2 is exactly 1, the spectral gap, which is the Gaussian Poincare inequality. [standard; e.g. Bakry, Gentil and Ledoux, Analysis and Geometry of Markov Diffusion Operators, Section 2.7]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:24:25.931193+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3a8d3db00f2f142079d2c70163c5649465d9a8adbbd202ea97f69580cddb30c2","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 13 of arXiv:2506.19123, 'The longest increasing subsequence of Brownian separable permutons'] Let $n \geq 0, k \geq 1$ be integers, let $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k>0$ and $\alpha_0=\sum_{i=1}^k \alpha_i$. 
    \begin{itemize}
    \item 
    The Dirichlet distribution $\Dir \left( \alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k \right)$ is the law on $k$-tuples of non-negative real numbers $(x_1, \dots, x_k)$ which sum up to $1$ given by the probability density function
     \[\frac{\Gamma(\alpha_0)}{\Gamma(\alpha_1)\cdots \Gamma(\alpha_k)} \prod_{i=1}^k x_i^{\alpha_i - 1}.\]

    
    \item The Dirichlet-multinomial distribution $\DirM \left( n; \alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k \right)$ is the law on $k$-tuples of non-negative integers $(n_1, \dots, n_k)$ which sum up to $n$ given by the probability mass function
        \[ \frac{\Gamma(\alpha_0) \Gamma(n+1)}{\Gamma(n+\alpha_0)} \prod_{i=1}^k \frac{\Gamma(n_i+\alpha_i)}{\Gamma(\alpha_i) \Gamma(n_i+1)}. \]
    In other words, a $\DirM \left( n; \alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k \right)$-distributed random variable $\mathbf{N}=\left( N_1, \dots, N_k \right)$ can be obtained as follows: let $\mathbf{D}=(D_1, \dots, D_k)$ follow the Dirichlet distribution $\Dir \left( \alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k \right)$; then, conditionally on $\mathbf{D}$, sample the vector $\mathbf{N}$ as a multinomial vector with parameters $(n;\mathbf{D})$.
    \end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.820761+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3ab938b4d4cb0291e52c58efecec41c9b61657b15af69c0bf3f08bdc1bef47be","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:root-sweep-dictionary of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Let $h\geq1$ and $k\geq2$.  One has the exact difference identity
\begin{equation}
 E_{h,k}-E_{h,k}=h\mathsf R_{k-1}\cap\mathsf A_{k-1}.
\end{equation}
For an ordered real tuple $a=(a_1<\cdots<a_k)$, write
\({\bf1}=(1,\ldots,1)\in\mathbb R^k\) and let
$a^\circ=a-k^{-1}(\sum_i a_i){\bf1}$ be its centered representative.  Let
$F_h(a)$ be the face of $\mathfrak Z_{h,k}$ exposed by $a^\circ$.  The
following data determine one another:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item the total preorder on $E_{h,k}$ induced by $u\mapsto u\cdot a$
      (equivalently, its ordered weak partition into level sets);
\item the complete ordered $h$-addition table of $a$, including ties;
\item the face $F_h(a)$.
\end{enumerate}
The dimension of $F_h(a)$ is the active relation rank $r_h(a)$.  In the
ambient space ${\bf1}^{\perp}$, its normal cone has dimension
$k-1-r_h(a)$, and the relative interior of that cone consists precisely of
the centered weights inducing the same complete table.  Moreover, the same
face determines every ordered addition table in degrees $1\leq j\leq h$.

Fix any field $K$.  If $a\in\mathbb Z^k$, put
$A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ and define
\[
 \varphi_a:K[x_1,\ldots,x_k]\longrightarrow K[u,t,t^{-1}],
 \qquad x_i\longmapsto u t^{a_i},
 \qquad I_a=\ker\varphi_a,
\]
where $\deg u=1$ and $\deg t=0$.  Then the number of blocks in the face
label is the Hilbert value
\begin{equation}
 |hA|=\dim_K\bigl(K[x_1,\ldots,x_k]/I_a\bigr)_h.
\end{equation}
Thus the face records the equality rank and Hilbert/block label, while its
normal cone encodes the normalized shape, realization frequency, and integer
compression developed below.","status":"unverified"}

A bounded operator T: H -> K is Hilbert-Schmidt if sum_{i in I} ||T e_i||^2 < infinity for some orthonormal basis (e_i)_{i in I} of H. Properties: ||T|| <= ||T||_2; ||T*||_2 = ||T||_2; every Hilbert-Schmidt operator is compact (it is the ||.||_2-limit, hence operator-norm limit, of finite-rank operators); the Hilbert-Schmidt operators S_2(H,K) form a Hilbert space under <A,B>_2 = sum_i <A e_i, B e_i> = tr(B*A), independent of the basis; and they form an ideal: ||A T B||_2 <= ||A|| ||T||_2 ||B|| for bounded A, B. Basis independence follows from sum_i ||T e_i||^2 = sum_i sum_j |<T e_i, f_j>|^2 = sum_j ||T* f_j||^2 for any orthonormal basis (f_j) of K.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:29:23.333409+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3ae1e9088eea28fb82b7b70adc673f57b41e5629628fdc56297ef553459190aa","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 2 of arXiv:2512.05466, 'Stochastic Flows and Marked Stable Processes'] \cite[Definition 2.15]{AWYskew}
   Let $\cW$ be a white noise with respect to some filtration $\cF$.  Let $\overline{\delta}$ be a drift function with respect to ${\mathcal F}$.  
   We call a collection of non-negative processes $\cS=(\cS_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)_{r\in \bR,a\ge 0}$ a ${\rm BESQ}(\overline{\delta})$ flow driven by $\cW$ if 
   
    (1) The restriction of $\cS$ to each $A_i$ is a ${\rm BESQ}^{\delta_i}$ flow driven by $\cW$.

    (2) The regularity conditions of Definition \ref{def:BESQflow} hold.

If $E$ is a (possibly random) Borel set, we call $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow killed on $E$ the flow obtained from the $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow by absorbing the flow line $\cS_{r,\cdot}(a)$ at $0$ at time $\inf\{x \in E\cap (r,\infty) \,:\, \cS_{r,x}(a)=0\}$.

 If $E=\bR$, we will simply call it killed  $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow. We call general  $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow a $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow or a  killed $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["translation-invariant (or vertex-transitive) graph structure","the FKG inequality for the measure, which for the random-cluster model restricts to cluster weight q>=1","finite energy, or an analogous positive-conditional-probability condition, for the percolation-type model","existence of the box functional phi_p(S) and the differential inequality relating its p-derivative to itself"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.981266+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3ae2caacde47ce68027ad36384f8328b964b0146b91cb5013ec1471310b791d6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For Bernoulli percolation, and more generally for FKG-satisfying, translation-invariant models with finite energy (including the random-cluster model for cluster weight q>=1), the sharpness-of-phase-transition theorem shows that below the critical point p_c, the probability of connection to distance n decays exponentially in n, proved without duality via a finite-size criterion: a box functional phi_p(S), built from crossing probabilities and a weighted sum over pivotal edges, is shown to satisfy a differential inequality in p that forces it to either stay bounded (subcritical, exponential decay) or blow up past a threshold (supercritical), with the threshold identified as p_c. This unifies and reproves the classical results of Menshikov and of Aizenman-Barsky with a single argument that is robust enough to extend to Z^d for every d, to general transitive graphs, and to the random-cluster model. The theorem does not give the exact value of p_c, does not determine critical behavior exactly at p_c (critical exponents are a separate, generally much harder, question), and the exponential-decay rate produced is not claimed to be sharp or explicit. Typical failure: Assuming the Duminil-Copin-Tassion argument extends automatically to a non-FKG regime, such as random-cluster parameters q<1 or certain long-range or antiferromagnetic models, where positive association fails; the driving differential inequality depends essentially on FKG-type monotonicity and on finite energy, and dropping either hypothesis breaks the exponential-decay conclusion outright rather than merely weakening it. Canonical reference: Duminil-Copin and Tassion, 2016, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Duminil-Copin, Raoufi and Tassion, 2019, Annals of Mathematics.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.495124+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3af301125dec67d5208abf4a3f6300171a5183e5360582f12a11493bfbe8a30c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 31 (Entropy transfer through the random large-gap side) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:random-side-entropy}
For \(n\geq2\), let \(\Gamma_n^X\) and \(\Gamma_n^Y\) be the complete eigenvalue minor
processes of \(X_n\) and \(Y_n\), respectively, and let
\(R_n=\check\lambda_n\).  With the coordinate Lebesgue measures in which
Proposition~\ref{gt-rem}(iv) is volume-preserving, the following assertions
hold.
\begin{enumerate}

\[
\bigl|\ent(R_n)\bigr|=O(n\log n).
\]

\[
\bigl|\ent(L_n\mid\Gamma_n^X)\bigr|=O(n\log n).

\[
\ent(L_n\mid\Gamma_n^X,\Gamma_n^Y)
=
\ent(R_n)
+n\log\left(n^{10}\left(1-\frac1n\right)\right).

\[
\ent(h_n)=\ent(\Gamma_n^X,L_n)
=\ent(\Gamma_n^X)+\ent(L_n\mid\Gamma_n^X)
\]
and
\begin{align*}
&\ent\!\left(h_n^{(1)},h_n^{(2)}
       \hbox{ pasted along }L_n\right)\\
&\qquad=
\ent(\Gamma_n^X,\Gamma_n^Y,L_n)\\
&\qquad=

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:07:17.250191+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3b0f139803eb8776caac82cfa5a1923175451a2e4115400757eed77c49589717","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition SDS of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a Polish space equipped with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra $\sigma(\mathcal{B})$. 
	A quadruple $\left(\mathcal{B}, \{P_t\}_{t \geq 0}, \mathbf{P}, \{\vartheta_t\}_{t \geq 0}\right)$ is called a {stationary noise process} if the following properties hold.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item [(i)] The measure $\mathbf{P}$ is a probability measure on $(\mathcal{B}, \sigma(\mathcal{B}))$. Also, for each $t \geq 0$, the maps 
		$P_t: \mathcal{B} \times \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}$ and 
		$\vartheta_t: \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}$ 
		are measurable, and for every $\omega^- \in \mathcal{B}$, the random variables 
		$P_t(\omega^-, \cdot)$ and $\vartheta_t$ are independent.
		\item [(ii)] The family $\{\vartheta_t\}_{t \geq 0}$ forms a semiflow on $\mathcal{B}$, i.e. 
		$\vartheta_{t+s} = \vartheta_t \circ \vartheta_s$, and preserves $\mathbf{P}$, that is $(\vartheta_t)_{\star}\mathbf{P} = \mathbf{P}$.
		\item [(iii)] For $\omega^- \in \mathcal{B}$ and $t \geq 0$, define
		\[
		\mathcal{P}_t(\omega^-; \cdot) := (P_t(\omega^-, \cdot))_{\star}(\mathbf{P}).
		\]
		The family $\{\mathcal{P}_t\}_{t \geq 0}$ forms a Feller transition semigroup on $\mathcal{B}$.
		Moreover, $\mathbf{P}$ is the unique invariant measure of $\{\mathcal{P}_t\}_{t \geq 0}$.
		\item [(iv)] For all $\omega^-, \omega^+ \in \mathcal{B}$ and $t,s \geq 0$,
		\begin{align*}
			&\vartheta_t \circ P_t(\omega^-, \omega^+) 
			= P_t(\vartheta_t \omega^-, P_t(\omega^+, \omega^-)) = \omega^-,\\
			&P_{t+s}(\omega^-, \omega^+) 
			= P_t(P_s(\omega^-, \omega^+), \vartheta_s \omega^+).
		\end{align*}
	\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:32:35.570269+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3b2db69a81344f521d68dcf0f0f53ce008aa31be20df244a8f056e5f98918c3f","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem.regeneration-toolkit of arXiv:2605.26082, 'Quantitative Einstein relation for reversible diffusions in a random environment'] The coupled regeneration construction of [ballistic2003shen,ballistic2004shen] and [Einstein2012gantert], as recalled in Subsection~(ss.renewal-setup of the paper), has the following properties.
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[\rm(a)] The regeneration times depend only on the path and Bernoulli marks. Under $\widehat{\mathbb P}_0^\lambda$ they are almost surely finite, take values in $\Delta\mathbb{N}$, satisfy $\tau_1\ge2\Delta$, and obey
			\[
				\tau_{k+1}=\tau_k+\tau_1\circ\theta_{\tau_k}\, .
			\]
			\item[\rm(b)] For every $n\ge2$, the first-regeneration slice has an event
			\[
				\Gamma_{1,n}\in\sigma(X^\lambda_s:0\le s\le n\Delta-\Delta)\vee\sigma(Y_0,\ldots,Y_{n-2})
			\]
			such that
			\[
				\{\tau_1=n\Delta\}
				=\Gamma_{1,n}\cap\{Y_{n-1}=1\}\cap\{D\circ\theta_{n\Delta}=\infty\}
			\]
				almost surely, and
				\[
					\Gamma_{1,n}\subseteq
					\left\{\sup_{0\le s\le n\Delta-\Delta}e_1\cdot X^\lambda(s)
					\le e_1\cdot X^\lambda(n\Delta-\Delta)+R\right\}.
				\]
					\item[\rm(c)] At the bridge step ending at $n\Delta$, given the path up to $n\Delta-\Delta$ and the marks through $Y_{n-2}$, the mark $\{Y_{n-1}=1\}$ contributes $p_*$, and the endpoint is averaged uniformly over $B^{X^\lambda(n\Delta-\Delta)}$. Given endpoint $y$, the shifted future path and marks have the coupled law $\widehat P_y^{\lambda,\omega}$.
				\item[\rm(d)] Before the terminal bridge the candidate has advanced at least $2R$ in the $e_1$ direction from the previous regeneration time. The successful bridge satisfies
				\begin{equation}
					X^\lambda(s)\in B_{6R}\bigl(X^\lambda(n\Delta-\Delta)+5Re_1\bigr),\qquad n\Delta-\Delta\le s\le n\Delta .
				\end{equation}
					\item[\rm(e)] The half-space measurability bounds are as follows. For the past factor, if $H_{\rm pre}$ is bounded and measurable in the path on $[0,n\Delta-\Delta]$ and the marks $Y_0,\ldots,Y_{n-2}$, then
					\[
						\omega\mapsto\widehat E_0^{\lambda,\omega}\!\left[
							H_{\rm pre}\,
						\mathbf 1_{\{\sup_{0\le s\le n\Delta-\Delta}e_1\cdot X^\lambda(s)\le y\cdot e_1-7R\}}
					\right]
				\]
				is $\mathcal H_{\mathsf L(y\cdot e_1-4R)}$-measurable. For the future factor, if $\Phi$ is a product of a bounded functional of the shifted future path and shifted marks with a bounded functional of the shifted environment restricted to $\mathsf R_+$, then
				\[
					\omega\mapsto \widehat E_y^{\lambda,\omega}[\Phi(\mathcal Y_0);D=\infty]
					\]
					is $\mathcal H_{\mathsf R(y\cdot e_1-2R)}$-measurable.
				\item[\rm(f)] The coupled kernel is spatially covariant:
				\[
					\widehat P^{\lambda,(\mathbf{a},e^{-2V})}_y
					=\bigl((X^\lambda,Y)\mapsto(y+X^\lambda,Y)\bigr)_{\#}
				\widehat P^{\lambda,T_y(\mathbf{a},e^{-2V})}_0\, .
			\]
		\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.544171+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3b43ec8f5d0fa6d27d0e5752777028d785fae794a67b64a293ba500ca12736e7","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"The GAUSSIAN ORTHOGONAL ENSEMBLE GOE_n is the law of a real symmetric n by n matrix H whose entries are independent up to symmetry with H_{ii} distributed as N(0, 2/n) and H_{ij} distributed as N(0, 1/n) for i < j. Its density with respect to Lebesgue measure on the space of real symmetric matrices is proportional to exp( - (n/4) trace(H^2) ), and the law is invariant under H -> O H O^T for every orthogonal O. The GAUSSIAN UNITARY ENSEMBLE GUE_n is the law of a Hermitian H with H_{ii} distributed as N(0, 1/n) real and, for i < j, H_{ij} = x + i y with x and y independent N(0, 1/(2n)), so that E|H_{ij}|^2 = 1/n; its density is proportional to exp( - (n/2) trace(H^2) ) and it is invariant under H -> U H U^* for every unitary U. With THESE normalisations the empirical spectral distribution of either ensemble converges to the semicircle law on [-2, 2], the largest eigenvalue converges to 2, and the edge fluctuations are of order n^{-2/3} with Tracy-Widom limits (beta = 1 for GOE, beta = 2 for GUE). The DIAGONAL VARIANCE DIFFERS BETWEEN THE TWO ENSEMBLES - 2/n for GOE, 1/n for GUE - and that is what makes both densities come out as the invariant exponential of the trace; getting it wrong changes the density but not the limiting spectral law. Normalisation conventions vary widely across the literature: some authors use unnormalised entries of variance 1 and divide by sqrt(n) afterwards, some put the semicircle on [-1,1] or [-2 sqrt(2), 2 sqrt(2)], and some use exp(-trace(H^2)/2) with n absorbed elsewhere. Any imported constant must be checked against the convention it was derived under. [standard; e.g. Anderson, Guionnet and Zeitouni, An Introduction to Random Matrices, Sections 2.5 and 2.6]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:00:46.819743+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3b587371cf631eb291613b05dab51097d529d27dc0b183b1d5fa8c0a7277305f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 1 of arXiv:2608.13208, 'Universality in dimension $1$ of kinetically constrained lattice gases'] A kinetically constrained lattice gas is a Markov
process on $\Omega=\{0,1\}^{\Z}$ with generator 
\begin{equation}
\cL f(\eta)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{x,y\in\Z}c(x,y,\eta)(f(\eta^{xy})-f(\eta)),
\end{equation}
where $\eta^{xy}$ is the configuration after exchanging $x$ and
$y$. The rates are given by the \emph{constraint function} $c:\Z\times\Z\times\Omega\to[0,\infty]$
satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Nearest-neighbor jumps: $c(x,y,\eta)=0$ if $\left|x-y\right|\neq1$.
By convention $c(x,y,\eta)=c(y,x,\eta)$.
\item Translation invariance: $c(x,y,\eta)=c(x+z,y+z,\tau_{z}\eta)$ for
all $x,y,z$, where $\tau_{z}$ is the translation by $z$.
\item $c(x,y,\eta)$ does not depend on the occupation at $x$ and $y$,
i.e., $c(x,y,\eta)=c(x,y,\eta^{xy})$.
\item Finite range: there exists $r>0$ such that $c(x,y,\eta)$ depends
only on the configuration in $x+[-r,r]$.
\item Monotonicity: if $\eta(x)\le\omega(x)$ for all $x$, then $c(x,y,\eta)\ge c(x,y,\omega)$.
That is, adding vacancies speeds up transitions.
\end{enumerate}
We can also define the process on a finite segment $[a,b]$ of $\Z$
by fixing boundary conditions; in this article we always consider
filled boundary, i.e., for $x,y\in[a,b]$ the constraint in the segment
is given by $c_{[a,b]}(x,y,\eta)=c(x,y,\tilde{\eta})$ where $\tilde{\eta}$
agrees with $\eta$ on $[a,b]$ and equals $1$ outside.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:12:19.505700+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3b5a46b1ddbb7517eecfcc415700139b9100f897dbcf36749ed6aedc54ba4ce1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 37 of arXiv:2608.18075, '2608.18075'] Assume \eqref{eq:q}, put $b=(a-3)/2$, and fix
$b<\beta<a/2-1$.  There is a deterministic time
$t_*>0$, depending only on $(a,\nu,c_Q,C_Q)$, such that the following
assertions hold.

For every $r<\infty$, there are an integer $R_r$, an admissible base weight
\begin{align}
 V_r(w)=
 (1+\|w\|_{H^b}^2)^{R_r}
 \exp(\eta_0\|w\|_2^2),
 
\end{align}
where one sufficiently small $\eta_0>0$ is fixed for the whole hierarchy,
and $C_r<\infty$ such that, uniformly over unit $\mathsf p\in H$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbf E_{w,\mathsf p}\|\mathsf p_{t_*}\|_{H^1}^{2r}
 &\le C_rV_r(w),
 \\
 \mathbf E_w\|w_{t_*}\|_{C^\beta}^r
 &\le C_rV_r(w).
 
\end{align}
The same estimates hold after every almost surely finite stopping time $S$:
\begin{align}
 \mathbf E\left[
  \|\mathsf p_{S+t_*}\|_{H^1}^{2r}\mid\mathcal F_S\right]
 &\le C_rV_r(w_S),
 \\
 \mathbf E\left[
  \|w_{S+t_*}\|_{C^\beta}^{r}\mid\mathcal F_S\right]
 &\le C_rV_r(w_S).
 
\end{align}
The constants do not depend on $S$ or on the value of $\mathsf p_S$.

For every fixed $T\ge t_*$, every $r<\infty$, and every unit
$\mathsf p\in H^1$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbf E_{w,\mathsf p}
 \left(\int_0^T\|\mathsf p_s\|_{H^1}^2\,\dd s\right)^r
 \le C_{r,T}\bigl(V_r(w)+1+\|\mathsf p\|_{H^1}^{R_r}\bigr),
 
\end{align}
where the polynomial orders are independent of $T$.  Finally, all weights
may be chosen from one nested hierarchy.  Given any finite list of moment
orders and polynomial powers, one member $V_*$ dominates every corresponding
right hand side and satisfies
\begin{align}
 P_T^{\rm base}V_*
 \le C_{0,*}e^{-\gamma_*T}V_*+B_*,
 \qquad T\ge0.
 
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:15:54.903423+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3b6077a432a793f0a80f87dc5e6644dd149f2797ff4b881d43f56274b79cacdb","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:block of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] A whitened system $\{(\xi_i,\eta_i)\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ has \emph{orthogonal

under Lemma~(lem:whiten of the paper) has orthogonal circuit-block structure with
dimension vector $r$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["rows iid","S and T are distinct (m-1)-subsets of row indices","the span of the shared rows has full rank almost surely"],"created_at":"2026-09-23T13:16:40.830294+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory","id":"claim_3b6ac9ae92b563a93f51075f27414a262a50f1204b39ef9ae9ea1f99cf7277e6","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $X_1,\\dots,X_m$ be iid random rows in $\\mathbb{R}^m$ and let $S, T$ be two distinct $(m-1)$-subsets of row indices. Put $A = S \\cap T$, $B = S \\setminus T$, $C = T \\setminus S$ and $D = m - |A|$, so that $|B| = |C| = D - 1$. Condition on the rows indexed by $A$, let $E_A = \\operatorname{span}(A)^{\\perp}$, which has dimension $D$ almost surely, and let $Q_A : \\mathbb{R}^D \\to E_A \\subset \\mathbb{R}^m$ be any isometry (an $m \\times D$ matrix with orthonormal columns). Then the unit null normals $u_S, u_T$ of the two $(m-1) \\times m$ row submatrices satisfy $u_S = Q_A v$ and $u_T = Q_A w$, where $v, w \\in S^{D-1}$ are the null directions of the residual matrices $U = B Q_A$ and $V = C Q_A$. Conditionally on $A$ the matrices $U$ and $V$ are independent, each with iid rows of law $Q_A^{\\top} X$, and the pair correlation is preserved exactly: $\\rho_{ST}^2 = \\langle u_S, u_T \\rangle^2 = \\langle v, w \\rangle^2$. Writing $M_A = \\mathbb{E}[v v^{\\top} \\mid A]$ for the conditional second-moment matrix of the residual null line, $\\mathbb{E}[\\langle v,w\\rangle^2 \\mid A] = \\operatorname{tr}(M_A^2)$. {"assumptions":["f integrable on R","the pointwise identity is claimed at a specific point (typically x = 0)"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.264346+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis, common errors","id":"claim_3b718e0037a91db9c64b0a4706cc1000aa0a6e3fe12673010be7f29fee1bf2dc","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypotheses: the periodization $Pf(x)=\\sum_nf(x+n)$ must be continuous at the point where the identity is evaluated, and its Fourier series must converge there (absolute summability of $(\\hat f(k))_k$ is the usual sufficient condition). For a general $f\\in L^1(\\mathbb R)$ all that is true is $\\widehat{Pf}(k)=\\hat f(k)$, i.e. Poisson summation as an identity of Fourier series of an $L^1(\\mathbb T)$ function - which says nothing pointwise. Concrete failure: $f=\\mathbf 1_{[0,1]}$ (with $f(0)=f(1)=1$). Then $\\sum_nf(n)=f(0)+f(1)=2$, while $\\hat f(0)=1$ and $\\hat f(k)=\\int_0^1e^{-2\\pi ikx}dx=0$ for $k\\ne0$, so $\\sum_k\\hat f(k)=1\\ne2$. The periodization equals $1$ off $\\mathbb Z$ and $2$ on $\\mathbb Z$: it is discontinuous exactly where the identity is being evaluated, and the Fourier series converges to the midpoint $1$. Redefining $f(0)=f(1)=1/2$ restores the identity. Second trap: pure decay of $f$ is not enough - one needs decay (or summability) on the transform side as well, since the right-hand series must converge; $f$ continuous and integrable with $\\hat f$ merely tending to zero gives no pointwise statement. When quoting a rate, the clean hypothesis is $|f(x)|\\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\\delta}$ and $|\\hat f(\\xi)|\\le C(1+|\\xi|)^{-1-\\delta}$ with $f$ continuous, or simply $f\\in\\mathcal S$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:22:46.471076+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3b8085876cb651677834928140bd514720eac881bd988ff4b4fafd0a51027fc0","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 96 (Geometric forms and related integrals) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] \hfill
	\begin{itemize}
		\item Recall that $\gnulltori$ is the first fundamental form of the torus $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$.
		We define the canonical area form of $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$ 
		induced by $\gnulltori$
		in the double-null coordinates $(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3)$ by:
		\begin{align} 
			\voldoublenulltori 
			& = \voldoublenulltori(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3) 
			\eqdef 
			\sqrt{\det \gnulltori (\ubar',u',x^2,x^3)} \, \mathrm{d} x^2 \mathrm{d} x^3,
		\end{align}
		where $\det \gnulltori(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3)$ is the determinant of the $2 \times 2$ matrix
		$\left(\gnulltori(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3) \left(\nullgeop{x^A},\nullgeop{x^B}\right) \right)_{A,B=2,3}$
		(see RHS\,\eqref{E:DOUBLENULLTORIFIRSTFUNDRESTRICTEDTODOUBLENULLTORI}).
		\item We define the (non-canonical) area form $\volingoingnullhypersurface$ of $\ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\ubar}{J}$ 
		in the double-null coordinates $(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3)$ by: 
		\begin{align} 
			\volingoingnullhypersurface 
			& = \volingoingnullhypersurface(\ubar,u',x^2,x^3) 
			= \voldoublenulltori(\ubar,u',x^2,x^3) \, \mathrm{d} u'.
		\end{align}
		\item We define the (non-canonical) area form $\voloutgoingnullhypersurface$ on $\outgoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{u}{I}$ 
		in the double-null coordinates $(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3)$ by:  
		\begin{align} 
			\voloutgoingnullhypersurface 
			= 
			\voloutgoingnullhypersurface(\ubar',u,x^2,x^3) 
			& \eqdef \voldoublenulltori(\ubar',u,x^2,x^3) \, \mathrm{d} \ubar'.
		\end{align} 
		\item We define the (non-canonical) volume form $\voldiamond$ of $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{I}{J}$ 
		in the double-null  coordinates $(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3)$ by:
		\begin{align} 
			\voldiamond 
			= \voldiamond(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3) 
			& 
			\eqdef 
			\voldoublenulltori(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3) \, \mathrm{d} u' \, \mathrm{d} \ubar'.
		\end{align}
	\end{itemize}
	
	Unless we explicitly indicate otherwise, 
	all integrals along 
	$\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}, \, \outgoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{u}{I}, \, \ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\ubar}{J}$, and $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{I}{J}$
	are defined with respect to the above forms. 
	Moreover, we will often suppress the variables with respect to which we integrate, 
	e.g., we write:
	\begin{subequations} 
		\begin{align}
			\int_{\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}} 
			f 
			\, \voldoublenulltori 
			& 
			\eqdef 
			\int_{(x^2,x^3) \in \T^2}  
			f(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3) 
			\, \voldoublenulltori(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3),   
			 \\
			\int_{\outgoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{u}{I}} 
			f \, 
			\voloutgoingnullhypersurface 
			& 
			\eqdef \int_{\ubar' \in I}  
			\int_{(x^2,x^3) \in \T^2} 
			f(\ubar',u,x^2,x^3) \, \voldoublenulltori(\ubar',u,x^2,x^3)
			\, \mathrm{d} \ubar', 
			 \\
			\int_{\ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\ubar}{J}} 
			f 
			\, \volingoingnullhypersurface 
			& \eqdef 
			\int_{u' \in J} \int_{(x^2,x^3) \in \T^2} 
			f(\ubar,u',x^2,x^3) 
			\, \voldoublenulltori(\ubar,u',x^2,x^3) \, \mathrm{d} u', 
			 \\
			\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{I}{J}} 
			f 
			\, \voldiamond 
			& 
			\eqdef 
			\int_{\ubar' \in I} 
			\int_{u' \in J} 
			\int_{(x^2,x^3) \in \T^2} 
			f(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3) 
			\, \voldoublenulltori(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3)
			\, 
			\mathrm{d} u' \, \mathrm{d}\ubar'.
			
		\end{align}
	\end{subequations}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:07:17.250084+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3b8212b213c96c4c9090ad77dfe3c58994975574f1d95b2e858786b0a687d11a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let $\Phi$ be an RDS and \( \mathcal{A}=\{\mathcal{A}(\omega)\}_{\omega \in \Omega} \) be a family of non-empty subsets of  $\mathcal{X}$. 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item  [1)] The family \( \mathcal{A} \) is called a random closed set (random compact set) if, with probability one, each \( \mathcal{A}(\omega) \) is closed (compact), and for every \( x \in \mathcal{X} \), the function \( \omega \mapsto d(x, \mathcal{A}(\omega)) \) 
		is \( \mathcal{F} \)-measurable.
		\item [2)] We say that $\mathcal{A}$ is invariant under \( \Phi \) if for all \( t \geq 0 \),
		\[
		\Phi^{t}_{\omega}(\mathcal{A}(\omega)) = \mathcal{A}(\theta_t\omega) 
		\]
		holds for \( \mathbb{P} \)-almost every \( \omega \in \Omega \).
		\item [3)] The set $\mathcal{A}$ is called {random absorbing} if, 
		for every $\mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{X})$, there exists a (random) time 
		$T = T(\mathcal{E}, \omega)$ such that
		\[
		\varphi(t, \theta_{-t}\omega, \mathcal{E}(\theta_{-t}\omega)) \subset \mathcal{A}(\omega),
		\quad \forall\, t \ge T(\mathcal{E}, \omega),
		\]
		for $\mathbb{P}$-almost every $\omega \in \Omega$.
		
	\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:35:05.834577+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3b9f667c7c7f4fa0f7cd39a4865d1d595486c22be3886c48ebff215199950382","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:definetti-identities of arXiv:2606.25976, 'Gaussian rigidity for infinite exchangeable sequences'] Let \((X_i)_{i\ge1}\) be an exchangeable sequence of \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-valued random vectors with de Finetti directing measure \(\eta\). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:08.845010+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3b9f69352fe0f6465568441a559cf112b4609bf6dd09074de6bb2ccd379faebb","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi 9 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $\bs{a} = (a_1,\ldots ,a_d)$ be a $d$-tuple of non-commutative random variables in some $W^\ast$-probability space $(\A,\tau)$. The {\bf $\ast$-distribution} of $\bs{a}$ is the linear functional $\mu_{\bs{a}}\colon\PP_{2d}\to\C$ given by $P \mapsto \tau\left[ P(\bs{a}, \bs{a}^\ast) \right]$.

If $(\A_N,\tau_N)$ is a sequence of $W^\ast$-probability spaces for $N\ge 1$, and $\bs{a}_N \in\A_N$ are $d$-tuples, we say $\bs{a}_N$ {\bf converges in $\ast$-distribution to $\bs{a}$} if the $\ast$-distributions $\mu_{\bs{a}_N}$ converges pointwise to $\mu_{\bs{a}}$; i.e.\ if, for all $P\in\PP_{2d}$
\[ \lim_{N\to\infty} \tau_N[P(\bs{a}_N,\bs{a}_N^\ast)] = \tau[P(\bs{a},\bs{a}^\ast)]. \]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:58:28.466910+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3baa001d444541a9870c76a7e0a370b1a41debad59d8d9f83d48d0246955629a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 7 of arXiv:2606.29132, '\bf Local Well-posedness of General Mean Field Game Master Equations'] Given $\cL_{\xi_1} = \mu_1\in \cP_2(\dbR^{d_1})$ and $x_0\in \dbR^{d_0}$, we say $(\a^*, \bm^*)\in \cA\times \cM$ is a mean field equilibrium (MFE) of MFGM \reff{MFGM-X}-\reff{MFGM-J}-\reff{MFGM-Xxi} at $(0,x_0, \mu_1)$ if

(i) Given $\bm^*$, $\a^{0*}$ is optimal for the major player:
\bea

J_0(\bm^*;  x_0, \a^{0*}) = \inf_{\a^0\in \cA_0} J_0(\bm^*;  x_0, \a^{0}).
\eea

(ii) Given $(\bm^*,\a^{0*})$, $\a^{1*}$ is optimal for the representative minor player:
\bea

J_1(\bm^*;  x_0, x_1, \a^{0*}, \a^{1*}) = \inf_{\a^1\in \cA_1} J_1(\bm^*;  x_0, x_1, \a^{0*}, \a^1),\q \mbox{for $\mu_1$-a.e. $x_1\in \dbR^{d_1}$}.
\eea

(iii) Given $\a^*$, $\bm^*$ is the conditional law of the minor's population:
\bea

\cL_{X^{\bm^*,1, x_0, \xi_1, \a^*}_t|\cF^{X^{\bm^*,0, x_0, \a^{0*}}_t}} = \bm^*_t(X^{\bm^*, 0, x_0, \a^{0*}}),~ 0\le t\le T,~\mbox{ a.s.}
\eea","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.167830+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3bd594c610f4d3fcbc32075d0a439ba6a55b623d7381b74f99a6dadaeddcc669","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:transport-cover-intro of arXiv:2609.00399, 'Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy and a Conjecture of Tao'] For every $0<a<1$ and $0\leq L<\infty$, there is an integer $M=M(a,L)$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:44:17.443501+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3bd81768ce1190f59ddc5618b6a65b1c72f8bb489b07a8c215c873e4fc1da121","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma prop:dyadic-stitching of arXiv:2608.25551, 'Beyond Optimal Rates in Stochastic Optimization: Trajectory-Adaptive Stopping Rules'] Let $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \ge t_0-1}$ be a filtration. Let $\{X_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ be adapted, and let $\{v_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ be nonnegative and predictable. Define
\[
    \bar X_{t_0-1} \coloneqq 0,
    \qquad
    \bar X_t \coloneqq \sum_{s = t_0}^t X_s,
    \qquad
    V_{t_0-1} \coloneqq 0,
    \qquad
    V_t \coloneqq \sum_{s = t_0}^t v_s .
\]
Fix $\gamma \in \mathbb{R}$. Suppose that, for every $\lambda>0$ and every $t \ge t_0$,
\[
    \mathbb{E}\left[
        \exp\left(
            \lambda X_t - 2^\gamma \lambda^2 v_t
        \right)
        \,\middle|\,
        \mathcal{F}_{t-1}
    \right]
    \le 1 .
\]
For $t \ge t_0-1$, let
\[
    V_{t,\mathrm{eff}}\coloneqq\max\{V_t, 1\},
    \qquad
    m_t \coloneqq \left\lceil \log_2 V_{t,\mathrm{eff}}\right\rceil .
\]
Then, for every $\alpha \in (0,1)$,
\[
    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \forall t \ge t_0:\
        \bar X_t
        \le
        2^{(\gamma+3)/2}
        \sqrt{
            V_{t,\mathrm{eff}}
            \left(
                \log\frac{1}{\alpha}
                +
                \log\bigl((m_t+1)(m_t+2)\bigr)
            \right)
        }\,
    \right)
    \ge
    1-\alpha .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T07:57:26.180759+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_3bfec13bd5d64830aa571b1d4a4b378c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In spectral graph theory, the Alon–Boppana bound provides a lower bound on the second-largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of a $d$ -regular graph, meaning a graph in which every vertex has degree $d$. \item For any $n$, $\E[P^{(n)}_{d,kk}] = 0$ and $\E[(P^{(n)}_{d,kk})^2] = \cn'_n$ for some ($N$-independent) constants $\cn'_n$.

\end{itemize}
In addition, we also assume that for any $n=1, 2, 3, 4$, $m=1, 2$, $i<j$ and $k$, $P^{(n)}_{ij}$ and $P^{(m)}_{d,kk}$ are independent.
Fix $\epsilon \in (0, 1/60)$ and let
\[
	\Omega_\caX^\epsilon := \{ \max_{1 \leq k \leq N} |x_k| \leq N^{-1/2 +\epsilon} \} \cap \{ | \| \bsx \| - 1 | \leq N^{-1/5} \}.
\]

{"assumptions":["(X,B,mu) is a probability space and T preserves mu","the partitions P_k are countable, measurable, and increasing: P_{k+1} refines P_k","H_mu(P_k) < infinity for each k","the union of the P_k generates B modulo mu-null sets","h_mu(T) is defined as the supremum of h_mu(T,Q) over countable partitions Q of finite entropy"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.090319+00:00","domain":"ergodic theory, entropy, generators","id":"claim_3c3e128038c699e9bd64175dd57d1489d79b6bc2f84bbdbc616d67a216487a92","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X, B, mu) be a probability space and T : X -> X measure-preserving (invertibility is not assumed). Let P_1 <= P_2 <= ... be an increasing sequence of countable measurable partitions (each P_{k+1} refines P_k) with H_mu(P_k) < infinity for every k, and assume the sequence GENERATES: the sigma-algebra generated by the union of the P_k equals B up to mu-null sets. Then h_mu(T) = lim_k h_mu(T, P_k) = sup_k h_mu(T, P_k), where h_mu(T) is the supremum of h_mu(T,Q) over all finite-entropy partitions Q. The classical generator form is the special case: for an invertible T and a partition P with H_mu(P) < infinity whose two-sided join over all integer translates generates B, take P_k = the join of T^{-n}P over |n| <= k and conclude h_mu(T) = h_mu(T,P); for non-invertible T take the one-sided join over 0 <= n <= k. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) generation is the entire content. If the union of the P_k generates only a proper sub-sigma-algebra, the limit computes the entropy of the corresponding sub-process and can be strictly smaller than h_mu(T); with every P_k trivial the limit is 0 for a system of arbitrarily large entropy. In particular a partition that separates points topologically but only generates a smaller sigma-algebra modulo mu is not enough. (ii) Monotonicity of the sequence (or at least H_mu(Q | P_k) -> 0 for every finite-entropy Q) is used; an arbitrary sequence of partitions that 'converges' in some other sense need not have monotone entropies and the comparison step breaks. (iii) H_mu(P_k) < infinity is needed for the comparison inequality. (iv) Generation is modulo mu-null sets only, and the conclusion says nothing pointwise. (v) For non-invertible T the one-sided generator computes h_mu(T); using the two-sided join for a non-invertible map is meaningless.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:36:16.006042+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3c3ef474dabbe2e0d174050c5e733eec2cda003d3ffa7151a0e802ab8e7a1209","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem Prop_pre_post_inf_dist of arXiv:2606.27573, 'Conditional Path Decomposition at the Infimum and Maximum Drawdowns for Spectrally Negativ'] Conditionally on $I_{T}=a$, the pre-$H_{I}$ and post-$H_{I}$ processes are independent. 
     
i. The law of the pre-$H_I$ process is an $h$-transform of the law of the spectrally negative L\'{e}vy process killed at  $\tau_a\wedge T $ with 
\[
h(x) = \frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)\prime}(x-a) -\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(x-a)
\] 
for $x\ge a$. Moreover, the distribution of the supremum and the maximum drawdown of the pre-infimum process, $S_{H_{I}}$, $M_{0, H_{I}}^{-},$ respectively, when $I_{T}=a$ are given by
	\begin{eqnarray*}
		
        &&\mathbb{P}_0\left\{S_{H_{I}} < b \mid I_{T}=a\right\}=1-\frac{ \frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)\prime}(b-a) -\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(b-a) }{\frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)\prime}(-a) -\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(-a)}\left[\frac{W^{(\gamma)}(-a)}{W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)}\right]
	\end{eqnarray*}
	for  $b\ge 0$, and
    \begin{eqnarray*}
\mathbb{P}\left\{M_{0, H_{I}}^{-}< d \mid I_{T}=a \right\} =1-\frac{ \frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)\prime}(d) -\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(d) }{\frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)\prime}(-a) -\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(-a)}\left[\frac{W^{(\gamma)}(-a)}{W^{(\gamma)}(d)}\right]
\end{eqnarray*}
for $d\ge -a.$

ii. The law of the post-$H_{I}$ process is the $h$-transform of the law of the spectrally negative L\'{e}vy process killed at $T \wedge \tau_{a}^{-}$with	
	$$
	h(x)=1-Z^{(\gamma)}(x-a)+\frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)}(x-a).
	$$	
	Moreover, the distribution of the supremum of the post-infimum process, $S_{H_{I}, T}$, when $I_{T}=a$ is given by

	

\[
\mathbb{P}_{a}\left\{S_{H_{I}, T} \le b \mid I_{T}=a\right\}  = \frac{\Phi(\gamma)({Z^{(\gamma)}}(b-a)-1)}{\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)} 
\]
	for $b>a$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:23:58.630711+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3c4566fd35441bef8f16cb73953085085804d9c9ec05b5967079bb81e6177085","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 244 (ALE coordinates are identical to acoustical geometric coordinates) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $\eta, n, \tau$ be as in \eqref{E:DEFINITIONOFSTEVEFLOWMAP}--\eqref{E:DEFINITIONOFTANGENTVECTORSFORSTEVEOUTGOINGCHAR}, where we recall that equation \eqref{E:DEFINITIONOFSTEVEFLOWMAP} is solved in conjunction with the compressible Euler equations. Let $\mathbf{n}= (n_0,n_1,n_2)$ be the $\mathbf{g}$-null one-form from 
	\eqref{E:OUTGOINGCOCHARCHOICE}, let $\Lunit^{ALE}$ be as in \eqref{E:ALELUNIT}, 
	and let $\Lambda_{ALE}$ be the flow-map of $\Lunit^{ALE}$ as in \eqref{E:FLOWMAPOFALELUNIT}. 
	Then for $C^1$ solutions to the compressible Euler equations, the following hold:
			\begin{enumerate}
				\item \underline{\textbf{The flow of $\Lunit^{ALE}$}}. The flow map $\Lambda_{ALE}$ satisfies $\Lambda_{ALE}^0 = t$ and $\Lambda_{ALE}^i = \eta^i$ for $i = 1,2$.
				\item \underline{\textbf{$\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$ are characteristics in the sense of Def.\,\ref{D:CHARACTERISTICSURFACESCANONICAL}}}. 
				Recall that $\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$ is the surface defined in \eqref{E:CHARACTERISTICS}.
				For any $\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$-tangent vectorfield $W$, we have $\mathbf{n}_\alpha W^\alpha = 0$. Hence, $\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$ is a characteristic surface as in Def.\,\ref{D:CHARACTERISTICSURFACESCANONICAL}.
				\item \underline{\textbf{$\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$ are $\gfour$-null hypersurfaces}}. There exists a $\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$-tangent vectorfield $V$ 
					that is $\gfour$-orthogonal to the tangent space of $\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$. In particular, $\gfour(V,V) = 0$.
				\item \underline{\textbf{The geometric coordinates are identical to ALE coordinates}}. Suppose that $u$ is the solution to the eikonal equation $(\gfour^{-1})^{\alpha\beta}\p_\alpha u \p_\beta u = 0$ with $u \restriction_{t=0} = x^1$ and\footnote{For the proposition to be correct, $\partial_t u < 0$ is the right sign; $\partial_t u > 0$ would correspond to constructing the ingoing characteristics. We point out that  we have $\partial_t u > 0$ in \eqref{E:EIKONALBRANCHINTRO}. The reason is that in the bulk of the paper, we chose the initial data \eqref{E:EIKONALDATAINTRO} to have the opposite sign compared to this proposition.} 
				$\partial_t u \restriction_{t=0} < 0$. 
				Then $x^1_{ALE} = u$. In addition, the vectorfield $\Lunit$ defined by \eqref{E:LUNIT} satisfies $\Lunit = \Lunit^{ALE}$.				
				\item \underline{\textbf{$\Lunit^{ALE}$ is a non-affinely  parametrized geodesic vectorfield}}. {"assumptions":["n ≥ 2"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:51.723666+00:00","domain":"dispersive partial differential equations","id":"claim_3c61dddc2341b2fe03846c34c5f8fd2adaac49c5e5184bddc378dc2b3677df6a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let n ≥ 2. A pair (q,r) is wave-admissible (in the sense of Keel–Tao) if 2 ≤ q ≤ ∞, 2 ≤ r ≤ ∞, 1/q + (n−1)/(2r) ≤ (n−1)/4, and (q,r,n) ≠ (2,∞,3). It is sharp wave-admissible when equality holds, 1/q + (n−1)/(2r) = (n−1)/4. The exponent (n−1)/2 is the dispersive decay rate of frequency-localized waves; the associated regularity s is fixed separately by the scaling relation 1/q + n/r = n/2 − s. Examples in n = 3: (4,4) with s = 1/2, (5,10) and (4,12) with s = 1, and (∞,2) with s = 0, which is the bound ‖u‖_{L^∞_t L²_x} ≲ ‖u0‖_{L²} + ‖u1‖_{Ḣ^{−1}}. Note that the energy bound ‖u‖_{L^∞_t Ḣ¹} + ‖∂_t u‖_{L^∞_t L²} ≲ ‖u0‖_{Ḣ¹} + ‖u1‖_{L²} is not a different admissible pair: it is the pair (∞,2) applied at regularity s = 1, i.e. to |∇|u. The scaling relation always ties s to (q,r), so s = 0 is the only value that goes with (q,r) = (∞,2) in the Lebesgue-norm form of the estimate. Also note that r = ∞ is allowed in this definition but not in the Lebesgue-space wave Strichartz theorem, which requires r < ∞.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:36:31.221997+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3c9dbb84370f01449a45a358af3c4e2180aca4413319da51186af6baec056e3a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (Unique finite-time limit) of arXiv:2609.00501, 'Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow'] Let $F\colon[0,T)\times\Sigma\to\Sph^3$ be a smooth MIWF of a compact
torus, where $T<\infty$, and write $F_t:=F(t,\cdot)$.  Let $A_t^0$
denote the trace-free second fundamental form of $F_t$.  Put
\[
 W(t):=\Will(F_t),\qquad W_0:=W(0),\qquad
 \mu_t:=\mu_{F_t^*g_{\Sph^3}}.
\]
Assume that
for some $c_0>0$,
\[
 \inf_{0<t<T}\min_{x\in\Sigma}|A_t^0(x)|^2\geq c_0.
\]
Let $\Var_t$ denote the multiplicity-counting integral two-varifold in
$\R^4$ induced by $F_t$, and set
$\lambda_t:=\lVert\Var_t\rVert=(F_t)_\#\mu_t$.
Then there exists a unique integral two-varifold
$\Var_T$ in $\R^4$, possibly the zero varifold, such that, with
$\rightharpoonup$ denoting weak varifold convergence,
\begin{equation}
 
 \Var_t\rightharpoonup\Var_T
 \qquad\text{as }t\nearrow T.
\end{equation}
No reparametrizations of $\Sigma$ and no M\"obius transformations of
$\Sph^3$ are required.

More precisely, there are finite nonnegative Radon measures $\mu_T$ on
$\Sigma$ and $\lambda_T=\lVert\Var_T\rVert$ on $\Sph^3$ such that
$\mu_t\to\mu_T$ in total variation and
$\lambda_t\to\lambda_T$ in the bounded-Lipschitz distance
$d_{\BL}$ defined in \eqref{eq:bl-distance}.  Setting
\[
 W_T:=\lim_{t\nearrow T}W(t),
\]
there holds, for every $0<s<T$,
\begin{align}
 
 \lVert\mu_T-\mu_s\rVert_{\TV}
 &\leq \frac{2\sqrt{W_0}}{c_0}
 \sqrt{(T-s)\bigl(W(s)-W_T\bigr)},\\
 
 d_{\BL}(\lambda_T,\lambda_s)
 &\leq \frac{2\sqrt{W_0}}{c_0}
 \sqrt{(T-s)\bigl(W(s)-W_T\bigr)}.
\end{align}
Moreover, $\Var_T$ has generalized Euclidean mean-curvature vector
$H_{\Var_T}^{\R^4}\in L^2(\lVert\Var_T\rVert;\R^4)$ and
\begin{equation}
 
 \frac14\int_{\R^4}|H_{\Var_T}^{\R^4}|^2
 \dd\lVert\Var_T\rVert\leq W_T.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:52:57.717783+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3cce0fcae09e88a01cc7639c3c4a2e2bc94d50206e10e36632982fee8fc99b9f","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 23 (Nesterov look-ahead risk control) of arXiv:2609.02728, 'Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improv'] Assume the stable small-step condition \(\eta\lambda_1\le c_{\rm st}\), where \(c_{\rm st}>0\) is sufficiently small.     \left((1+\rho)e_m(j)-\rho e_{m-1}(j)\right)^2.
\]
Moreover, the deterministic look-ahead risk is comparable to the next deterministic Nesterov risk:
\[
    \frac12\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j

    \eqsim

\]

\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:30:07.958955+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3cda96d871a25672b8dfcdef9984b70a476275b55f06a5c40faca1fa924fae75","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Recursive Terminal Attachment of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Let \(s\) be a square vertex. \begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Base case: \(h_2\)-attachment.}
    The attachment may be a single \(h_2\)-edge from \(s\) to a circle vertex
    \(a\):
    \[
        s \xrightarrow{h_2} a .
    \]

    For any \(t \ge 1\), let \(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_t\) be backbone-dangling

    \[

    \(V_\mathcal{R}\). That is, we add
    \[
        U_\mathcal{R} \xrightarrow{h_1} s \xrightarrow{h_1} V_\mathcal{R} .
    \]
    When \(U_\mathcal{R}=V_\mathcal{R}\), we use the diagonal convention and attach \(s\) to
    this single circle vertex by two parallel \(h_1\)-edges. \anote{I don't think we want to allow this as if $U_\mathcal{R}=V_\mathcal{R}$ then we either don't have a proper concatenation or $t = 0$.}
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:58:38.107123+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3d0643ccb2f2a7fc120a9a1e54b9bb191053e01395201884492ec5577be5547a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] The space of node-edge probability-graphons with node features in \(\mathcal{X}\) and edge weights in
	\(\mathcal{Y}\) is defined as
	\[
		\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{X})\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{Y}) := \mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times[0,1]) \times \mathcal{P}_{\nu\otimes\nu}(\mathcal{Y}\times[0,1]^2).
	\]
	We also define the corresponding subset with node features in a fibered Wasserstein space of order \(p,q\in [1,\infty)\): 
	\[
		\mathcal{N}_{p,q}(\mathcal{X})\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{Y}) := \mathcal{P}_{p,q,\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times[0,1]) \times \mathcal{P}_{\nu\otimes\nu}(\mathcal{Y}\times[0,1]^2).
	\] 
	For any pair \((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})\in \mathcal{N}(\mathcal{X})\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{Y})\), we define the coupled labeled and unlabeled distances as follows: 
	\[
		\begin{aligned}
			d_{(\text{BL},1),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})) &= d_{\text{BL},1}(\mu,\bar{\mu}) + d_{\text{BL},\square}(q,\bar{q}), \\ 
			\delta_{(\text{BL},1),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})) &= \inf_{\varphi \in S_{[0,1]}} d_{(\text{BL},1),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})^{\varphi}),
		\end{aligned}
	\]
	where \((\bar{\mu},\bar{q})^{\varphi}\) denotes the joint rearrangement of the node-edge probability-graphon
	by \(\varphi\), {\it i.e.}, \((\bar{\mu},\bar{q})^{\varphi} = (\bar{\mu}^{\varphi},\bar{q}^{\varphi})\). 
	
	Similarly, for any pair \((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})\in \mathcal{N}_{p,q}(\mathcal{X})\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{Y})\),
	we define the corresponding distances:
	\[
		\begin{aligned}
		d_{(W_p,q),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})) &= d_{W_p,q}(\mu,\bar{\mu}) + d_{\text{BL},\square}(q,\bar{q}), \\ 
		\delta_{(W_p,q),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})) &= \inf_{\varphi \in S_{[0,1]}} d_{(W_p,q),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})^{\varphi}).
		\end{aligned}
	\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["reflection positivity of the Gibbs measure with respect to lattice reflections","translation invariance, typically verified on a torus with periodic boundary conditions","finite-range or sufficiently decaying interaction with a well-defined quadratic energy function E(k)","dimension d>=3 so the infrared integral of 1/E(k) is finite"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.972375+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3d1b7483c816df0af33429f02689b300652fb53dd58b9e9c714fd05827ae29f6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For statistical mechanics models on a torus whose Hamiltonian and lattice satisfy reflection positivity across midplanes between sites, the Gaussian domination (infrared) bound gives an upper bound on the Fourier transform of the two-point function: hat{G}(k) <= C / (beta E(k)), where E(k) is the quadratic energy form of the interaction (e.g. E(k)=sum_i (1-cos k_i) for nearest-neighbor coupling) and C is an explicit constant (often 1/2; exact value depends on normalization and is not always recalled precisely across variants). Combined with a spin-wave/Gaussian domination inequality this yields, for models such as the classical Heisenberg or XY model in dimension d>=3, or the Ising model in sufficiently high dimension, existence of long-range order at low temperature via a second-moment argument applied to the infrared-bounded Fourier integral. It does not give critical exponent values, does not apply in dimension d<=2 where the infrared integral diverges (consistent with the Mermin-Wagner theorem ruling out continuous-symmetry breaking there), and requires the specific reflection-positive algebraic structure; it gives no control for models lacking this symmetry, such as many disordered, frustrated, or non-bipartite systems. Typical failure: Assuming reflection positivity survives a seemingly minor modification of the Hamiltonian, such as adding next-nearest-neighbor terms, a random field, or working on a non-bipartite lattice, without re-checking the checkerboard decomposition; reflection positivity is a delicate algebraic property that most natural perturbations destroy, so the infrared bound and everything built on it, including the Frohlich-Simon-Spencer long-range order conclusion, silently stops applying. Canonical reference: Frohlich, Simon and Spencer, 1976, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Frohlich, Israel, Lieb and Simon, 1978, Communications in Mathematical Physics.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:19:56.667087+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3d2af7624cbbcebe9a407fb02973866e5b018aa9e71fd395f014a55007d94d8a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 9 of arXiv:2608.30859, 'Conservation Laws with Discontinuous Flux:\\ A First Application to Traffic Flow'] A vector field $H : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to have 
    \emph{locally bounded directional variation} if, for every 
    $(t_0,x_0) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, there exist $\delta>0$ and a constant $C>0$
    such that
    \[
    \sum_{i=1}^N 
    \bigl| H(t_i,x_i) - H(t_{i-1},x_{i-1}) \bigr|
    \;\le\; C
    \]
    for every finite sequence $(t_i,x_i)$, $i=0,\ldots,N$, satisfying
    \[
    (t_0,x_0) \prec (t_1,x_1) \prec \cdots \prec (t_N,x_N),
    \qquad t_N < t_0 + \delta .
    \]
    Here $\prec$ denotes the partial order on $\mathbb{R}^2$ induced by the cone
    \begin{equation}
        \Gamma_M := \{ (t,x) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| \le M t\}, 
    \end{equation}
    namely
    \begin{align}
    (t,x) \prec (t',x')
    \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad
    |x - x'| \le M (t - t') .
    \end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.626929+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3d2eccef094bb69e406fac092e701dccd48b74c6119162e597a97768bad97898","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (Omega, F, P) be a probability space with a filtration (F_n)_{n >= 0}, an increasing family of sub-sigma-algebras of F. A sequence (X_n)_{n >= 0} of random variables is a MARTINGALE with respect to (F_n) if (i) X_n is F_n-measurable for every n (adapted), (ii) E|X_n| < infinity for every n (integrable), and (iii) E[X_{n+1} | F_n] = X_n almost surely for every n. It is a SUBMARTINGALE if (iii) is weakened to E[X_{n+1} | F_n] >= X_n almost surely, and a SUPERMARTINGALE if E[X_{n+1} | F_n] <= X_n almost surely. Mnemonic: a supermartingale decreases in expectation, so it is what a gambler faces in an unfair game. All three notions are relative to a specified filtration; a process can be a martingale for its own natural filtration and fail to be one for a larger filtration. Integrability in (ii) is part of the definition, not a consequence: without it the conditional expectation in (iii) need not exist. If (X_n) is a martingale and phi is convex with phi(X_n) integrable for every n, then (phi(X_n)) is a submartingale by conditional Jensen; in particular |X_n| and X_n^2 are submartingales when integrable. [standard; e.g. Williams, Probability with Martingales, Chapter 10]","status":"unverified"}
