{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:01:39.495164+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3d4e1f1ffcd0da3f4de8963e955c2890b562e71ba32bd498f99a80066b27904d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:largeoutdegree of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Assume that $\mu$ is critical and belongs to the domain of

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.685575+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3d503c6327a83a68e621770de7b4c70c36649a0faac6888735187552b9fc9369","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 11 (Exact matrix isospectrality) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $\gamma:[0,T]\to V$ be continuous and of bounded variation, put $g=S(\gamma)$, let $l=\log g=\sum_{n\geq 1}l_n$, and put $v=l_1$.

\[
A_{\Phi}(z)=\sum_{n\geq 1}z^n\Phi^{(n)}(l_n).

\det(\zeta I-A_{\Phi}(z))

 =z^p\tr\bigl(\Phi(v)^p\bigr)

\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:05:57.800872+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3d70a704eb0a27d3b2546851198947036431bfb63eba34b7833c83d50ebbb81b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 20 (Reference measure and asymptotics) of arXiv:2608.30551, 'Critical Discrete Hardy Inequalities in $L^p$'] Let \(p\in(1,\infty)\), \(\sigma\in(0,1/2)\), and
\(\alpha\in(\sigma,1/2)\). Let \(\mu_{p,\sigma,\alpha}\) and
\(w_{p,\sigma,\alpha}\) be defined as in
Proposition~\ref{prop: fractional Hardy weights}. Define \(\gamma_p\) by
\[
    1-2\gamma_p=a_p(1-2\alpha).
\]
Then
\[
    \mu_{p,\sigma,\alpha}(x)\asymp (1+|x|)^{-2\sigma},
    \qquad x\in\Z.
\]
Moreover, as \(|x|\to\infty\),
\[
    w_{p,\sigma,\alpha}(x)
    =
    \frac{\Psi(p,\sigma,\alpha)}{|x|^{2\sigma}}
    +
    O\left(
        \frac{1}
        {|x|^{2\sigma+1-\max\{2\sigma,1-2\alpha\}}}
    \right),
\]
where
\[
    \Psi(p,\sigma,\alpha)
    =
    \frac{1}{a_p+1}
    \frac{\mathcal A_{\gamma_p-\sigma}}{\mathcal A_{\gamma_p}}
    +
    \frac{a_p}{a_p+1}
    \frac{\mathcal A_{\alpha-\sigma}}{\mathcal A_{\alpha}}.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:49.564122+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3d95d69851951d44c43a41a689b8c40f7e78651a7075a3b736fabc4fbeb20a04","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 10 (The two regimes are opposed) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] Fix the total energy $\\sum_k v_k$ over the transformed per-coordinate energy vector $v=(v_k)\\ge0$. (i)~The variable-rate distortion is governed by the geometric mean $\\mathrm{GM}(v)=(\\prod_k v_k)^{1/d}$: exactly proportional to it when every coordinate draws positive rate and the per-coordinate quantizers share one shape constant (as under the Gaussian source of \\Cref{thm:klt}), and bounded below by the water-filling floor of \\Cref{prop:waterfill} when the allocation is not interior; $\\mathrm{GM}$ is symmetric and Schur-concave, hence minimized at the most concentrated (majorizing) $v$; equivalently the coding gain \\eqref{eq:codinggain}$\\,=\\mathrm{AM}(v)/\\mathrm{GM}(v)$ is Schur-convex. (ii)~The uniform-grid fixed-rate distortion is a sum of per-group maxima, $D_{\\mathrm{fr}}=\\sum_g\\max_{k\\in g}v_k$, which by the max-vs-mean bound satisfies $D_{\\mathrm{fr}}\\ge\\frac1G\\sum_k v_k$ with equality iff every group is internally \\emph{uniform}; it is therefore minimized by within-group flattening and driven to its maximum by concentration. As functionals on the energy vector $v$, then, the two surrogate objectives are extremized at opposite ends of the \\emph{within-group} majorization order, at fixed, strictly positive group sums. Because $D_{\\mathrm{fr}}$ depends on the grouping it is not permutation-symmetric, hence not a functional of the global order at all, and the across-group placement of energy is a separate lever, the one the permutation family of \\Cref{sec:tax-permutation} exploits; which energy vectors a given transform can actually realize, and hence whether these extrema are attainable, is the separate question taken up in \\Cref{sec:inversion}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:21:06.854980+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3dd4e2e00dbffc7780fc1c0b58d0423d8eadfa4e8badf857585ab6ead31ff62e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 5 (Local solution) of arXiv:2608.21014, 'The stochastic Cahn--Hilliard equation in critical spaces'] Suppose that Assumption~\ref{Assumption:semilinear:evolution:equation} is satisfied for some $p\in[2,\infty)$ and $\kappa\in[0,p/2-1)\cup\{0\}$. 
     \begin{enumerate}
         \item A pair $(u,\sigma)$ is called an $L^p_\kappa$-\emph{local solution to~\eqref{eq:semilinear-stochastic-evolution}} if $\sigma\colon\Omega\to[a,\infty]$ is a stopping time, $u\colon[a,\sigma)\to X_0$ is a strongly progressively measurable process, there exists an increasing sequence of stopping times $(\sigma_n)_{n\ge 1}$ such that $\lim_{n\to\infty} \sigma_n=\sigma$ a.s., and for all $n\ge 1$ it holds that $(u|_{[a,\sigma_n]},\sigma_n)$ is an $L^p_\kappa$-strong solution to~\eqref{eq:semilinear-stochastic-evolution}. The sequence $(\sigma_n)_{n\ge 1}$ is called \emph{a localising sequence} for $(u,\sigma)$.
         \item An $L^p_\kappa$-local solution $(u,\sigma)$ is called \emph{unique} if for every $L^p_\kappa$-local solution $(v,\tau)$ one has $u=v$ a.s.\ on $[a,\tau\wedge \sigma)$.
         \item An $L^p_\kappa$-local solution $(u,\sigma)$ is called \emph{$L^p_\kappa$-maximal} if for any other unique $L^p_\kappa$-local solution $(v,\tau)$ to~\eqref{eq:semilinear-stochastic-evolution} one has that a.s.\ $\tau\le \sigma$ and $u=v$ on $[a,\tau)$.
         \item An $L^p_\kappa$-local solution $(u,\sigma)$ to~\eqref{eq:semilinear-stochastic-evolution} is called \emph{global} if $\sigma=\infty$ a.s.
     \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

\[
 \mathcal A_L=\{s\in[0,1]: |G(s)|<L<H(s)\}
\]
is central, mixed, or cap, in the following sense.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
\item If $0<L<1$, then either the component is central, opened by $G=L$ and closed by $G=-L$, or it is mixed, opened by $H=L$ and closed by $G=-L$.
\item If $L>1$, then either it is opened by an increasing-branch root of $H=L$ and closed by a decreasing-branch root of $H=L$, or it is opened by $G=L$ and closed by a decreasing-branch root of $H=L$.
\item The cases $L=1$, endpoint roots, and tangencies are limits of the preceding cases.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:19:46.234096+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3e2d31e3bc198f6d34f24b118f4490d0f89d373545b5951f6c3c16244281aa2d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 68 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] Fix $\A$, $\tau$, and $\l$ as above, let $\Delta := \Delta_\tau$, and consider the functionals
\[\phi \mapsto \Delta \phi_{\rm{ac}} \qquad (\phi \in \B(\A,\rmM_k)_+)\]
for each positive integer $k$.  They have the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[a.] They are upper semicontinuous for every $k$.
\item[b.] For every $k$ and $\phi,\psi \in \B(\A,\rmM_k)_+$, they satisfy $\Delta \phi_{\rm{ac}} \le (\tr_k\phi_{\rm{ac}}(1))^k$, and $\Delta \phi_{\rm{ac}} \le \Delta \psi_{\rm{ac}}$ in case $\phi \le \psi$.
\item[c.] They are log-concave:
\[\log \Delta(t\phi_{\rm{ac}} + (1-t)\psi_{\rm{ac}}) \ge t\log \Delta \phi_{\rm{ac}} + (1-t)\log \Delta \psi_{\rm{ac}} \]
whenever $\phi,\psi \in \B(\A,\rmM_k)_+$ and $t\in [0,1]$.
\item[d.] They are multiplicative on diagonal joinings :
\[\Delta (\rm{diag}(\phi,\psi)_{\rm{ac}}) = \Delta \phi_{\rm{ac}} \cdot \Delta \psi_{\rm{ac}}\]
whenever $\phi \in \B(\A,\rmM_k)_+$ and $\psi \in \B(\A,\rmM_\ell)_+$. \qed
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:21:56.726055+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3e382077a8e3267c7aec8426a2ccc3d45c3a67f766318c2182b13accd2e90a2c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:tightness_in_nice_bubble of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] There exists $\zeta > 0$ such that the following is true. Fix $0<r<1$. 
Suppose that $h$ is a GFF on $\mathbf{D}$ with zero boundary conditions. Let $u,v \in B(0,r)$, and let $\eta_u$ be the flow line of $h$ starting from $u$. Given $\eta_u$, let $\eta_{u,v}$ be the flow line of $h$ starting from $v$ and reflected off $\eta_u$ in the opposite direction. Let $x,y \in \eta_{u,v} \cap \eta_u$ be chosen such that the segment of $\eta_{u,v}$ from $v$ to $y$ intersects $\eta_u$ only on the right side of $\eta_u$ with angle difference $0$ (before reflecting off), and $x$ is on the segment between $v$ and $y$. Let $U_{x,y}$ be the region bounded between the segments of $\eta_{u,v}$ and $\eta_u$ from $x$ to $y$. Let $\Gamma_{x,y}$ be the collection of conditionally independent ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}$ naturally coupled with $h$ in each of the components of $U_{x,y}$. Let $\Upsilon_{\Gamma_{x,y}}$ denote the gasket of $\Gamma_{x,y}$. 

Let $E_\delta$ be the event that there exist $u,v,x,y$ as above such that
\begin{itemize}
 \item $U_{x,y} \subseteq B(0,r)$,
 \item $\Upsilon_{\Gamma_{x,y}} \subseteq \Upsilon_\Gamma$,
 \item $\mathrm{diam}(U_{x,y}) \le \delta$,
 \item $D_\epsilon^{\partial U_{x,y}} \ge \delta^\zeta+\epsilon^{a_0}$.
\end{itemize}
Let $\widehat{x}$ be the first point where $\eta_{u,v}$ hits $\eta_u$. Fix $c_1>0$, and let $E^1_\delta$ be the event that $E_\delta$ occurs and additionally the segment of $\eta_u$ from $x$ to $\widehat{x}$ has diameter at least $\delta^{1+c_1}$.
Then
\[ \mathbf{P}[E^1_\delta] = o^\infty(\delta) \quad\text{as } \delta \searrow 0 . \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:03:39.772561+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3e3d98fe4e568c60edff257aef5702b914cac882d59b96ff179d907d7a0454af","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop checking-the-inequalities-new of arXiv:2411.03065, 'Growing conditioned BGW trees with\\ log-concave offspring distributions'] Assume that ${\mathbf{w}}$ is $d$-arithmetic, that ${\mathbf{W}}=(w_0,w_d,w_{2d,\dots})$ is a log-concave sequence, and that $r=r_{d}({\mathbf{w}})$ is finite.
	Then we have
	\begin{align}
	\tfrac{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{d+1}}{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{1}}
	= R_0(0,0)\geq R_0(1,0)\geq\dots\geq R_0\bigl(r-1,0\bigr),
	\end{align}
	and for all $n\geq1$, we have the following long chain of inequalities, where each line continues the preceding one,
	\begin{align*}
	\begin{matrix}
		&	 R_n(0,0)
			&\geq& 	R_n(1,0)
				&\geq&	\dots
					&\geq& 	R_n\bigl(r-1,0\bigr)
								\\

		\geq&  R_n(0,1)
			&\geq& 	R_n(1,1)
				&\geq&	\dots
					&\geq& 	R_n\bigl(r-1,1\bigr)
								\\

		&  \vdots
			&& 	\vdots
				&&	\vdots
					&& 	\vdots
								\\

		\geq&  R_n(0,d-2)
			&\geq& 	R_n(1,d-2)
				&\geq&	\dots
					&\geq& 	R_n\bigl(r-1,d-2\bigr)
								\\

		\geq&  R_n(0,d-1)
			&\geq& 	R_n(1,d-1)
				&\geq&	\dots
					&\geq& 	R_n\bigl(r-1,d-1\bigr).
	\end{matrix}
	\end{align*}
	The first and last term of this chain of inequalities read as follows:
	\begin{align*}
	 R_n(0,0) 
	 	= \frac{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{(n+1)d+1}}{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{nd+1}}
	 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
	 R_n\bigl(r-1,d-1\bigr) 
	 	= \frac{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{nd+1}}{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{(n-1)d+1}}.
	\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:59:58.458182+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3e40d3a9d0e01e833a1e84320cebea234afaa20b4ee62bf25b1244d1b2fb5ef0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem calculus of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] {DRT2019}}]
  Let $(g_n)_{n=0}^\infty$ be a pointwise convergent sequence of differentiable, nondecreasing functions from $[0,p_{\max}]$ to $[0,M]$.
  Let $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$, and suppose that for $n\ge n_0$, the following differential inequality holds$:$
  \[
  \frac d{dp}g_n(p)\ge\Biggl(\frac1n\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}g_j(p)\Biggr)^{-1}g_n(p)\quad\text{for any $p\in(0,p_{\max})$}.
  \]
  Then there exists $\widetilde p\in[0,p_{\max}]$ such that the following statements hold$:$
  \begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] If $p<\widetilde p$, then there exists a constant $c_{p,n_0}>0$ such that
    \[
    g_n(p)\le M\exp(-c_{p,n_0}n)
    \]
    for all $n\ge n_0$$;$
    \item[(ii)] For any $p>\widetilde p$, it holds that $\lim_{n\to\infty}g_n(p)\ge p-\widetilde p$.
  \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.668042+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3e4252501f877713f00253bd4603cd4c86f9b7c92e7acbafd356141a07600dc2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 9 (Time reversal) of arXiv:2607.25685, 'Mimicking diffusion processes with differential equations'] Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:lagrangian} \emph{and, in addition}, the
 one-sided bound
\begin{equation}
  \big[\Div v\big]^+\in L^1\big(0,T;L^\infty(\R^d)\big).

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:35:56.896034+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3e4414d76275d3d3cc8fba37709fdc06c90015d2f9ed197d6a26810fb9886dc8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm th:uniq_im of arXiv:2603.29711, 'Strong Feller property, irreducibility,\\ and uniqueness of the invariant measure\\ for st'] Let $d=1$, $\beta\geq1$, and assume one of the following settings:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $\alpha>2$, $\sigma\in(\sigma_0^1,\frac14)$, 
        and $\delta\in(\frac14+\sigma,\frac12)$,
        \item $\alpha\geq4$, $\sigma\in(\sigma_0^2,\frac12)$, 
        and $\delta\in[\frac12,\frac12+\sigma)
        \cap(\frac14+\sigma,1)$.
    \end{itemize}
    Then,
    there exists a unique probability measure $\mu$
    on $(\mathcal X, \mathscr{B}(\mathcal X))$ that is invariant 
    for $P$. Moreover, $\mu$ is ergodic, strongly mixing,
    and $\mu(\mathcal K_\infty\cap V_{2\sigma+1})=1$.
    Lastly, $\mu$ is equivalent to all transition

{"assumptions":["A and B are linear operators in the same Banach space","D(A) ⊂ D(B)"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.769951+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, perturbation theory of operators","id":"claim_3e4fa40fff097dc9c86af5298ab723946a61639931a25125440e3ee34a2b916e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let A and B be linear operators in a Banach space X. B is relatively bounded with respect to A (A-bounded) if D(A) ⊂ D(B) and there are constants a, b ≥ 0 with ‖Bx‖ ≤ a‖Ax‖ + b‖x‖ for all x ∈ D(A). The infimum of all admissible a is the A-bound (relative bound) of B; the corresponding b usually grows as a approaches the infimum, and the infimum itself need not be attained. In a Hilbert space the condition ‖Bx‖² ≤ a'²‖Ax‖² + b'²‖x‖² defines the same relative bound. Relative bound 0 means: for every ε > 0 there is b_ε with ‖Bx‖ ≤ ε‖Ax‖ + b_ε‖x‖. If A is closed, B is closable, and D(A) ⊂ D(B), then B is automatically A-bounded (closed graph theorem applied to B on the Banach space (D(A), graph norm of A)). The form analogue: for A ≥ 0 self-adjoint with form q_A(x) = ‖A^{1/2}x‖² on Q(A) = D(A^{1/2}), a symmetric form β is A-form-bounded with bound a if Q(A) ⊂ D(β) and |β(x, x)| ≤ a q_A(x) + b‖x‖² for x ∈ Q(A). Operator-boundedness with bound a implies form-boundedness with bound at most a, not conversely.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:54:18.237993+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3e4fc47cee599a676aab3daf2b52b17177ad53fc2494b494e088a32196568848","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:stability_downscaling of arXiv:2608.29448, '\method: Self-Scaled Adaptive Preconditioning for Physics-Informed Learning'] Let $C_t=\mathbb{E}[g_t g_t^{\top}]$ denote the population gradient second-moment matrix at step $t$. For an orthogonal basis $Q \in O(d)$, define the diagonal second-moment operator $\mathcal{D}_Q(C):=\operatorname{diag}\left(Q^{\top} C Q\right)$. Let $V_t=\mathcal{D}_{Q_t}\left(C_t\right)$ and $V_{t+1}^*=\mathcal{D}_{Q_{t+1}}\left(C_{t+1}\right)$,
where $V_t$ is the diagonal second-moment state in the old basis $Q_t$, and $V_{t+1}^*$ is the oracle diagonal second-moment state in the new basis $Q_{t+1}$. Define the basis transition matrix $U=Q_{t+1}^{\top} Q_t$. Consider the scalar soft-reset update $V_{\text {scale }}=\gamma V_t, 0<\gamma \leq 1$. Then
$$
\left\|V_{\text {scale }}-V_{t+1}^*\right\|_F \leq(1-\gamma)\left\|V_t\right\|_F+2\left\|C_t\right\|_2\|I-U\|_F+\left\|C_{t+1}-C_t\right\|_F .
$$
In particular, if the gradient second moment evolves slowly, so that $\left\|C_{t+1}-C_t\right\|_F \leq \Delta_t$, then
$$
\left\|V_{\text {scale }}-V_{t+1}^*\right\|_F \leq(1-\gamma)\left\|V_t\right\|_F+2\left\|C_t\right\|_2\|I-U\|_F+\Delta_t .
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.179244+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3e7c028e15ea54077751c874676a322fafb4f9ef09b31515f5992a62c85933b6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 91 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We have $\sM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0) \subseteq \sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0)$.
\begin{proof} Consider any $\mu \in \cM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$.
    Then, there exists
    \[
        (q_*,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising) \in \Adm^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)
    \]
    such that $\mu^{\sym}(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta) = \mu$.
    Let $\tilde p$ denote the restriction of $p$ to $[q_*,1] \subseteq [q_0,1]$.
    Note that $(b,\sigma,w,\tilde p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$ satisfies the assumptions of
    Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-chaotic} with $q_*$ in place of $q_0$.

    By Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-chaotic}, there exists $\iota = \iota(\epsilon)$ with $\lim_{\epsilon\rightarrow 0} \iota(\epsilon) = 0$ such that for all (sufficiently large) $N$, there exists a $C(L,\epsilon)$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA_N$ with
    \[
        \WERR^\sym(\cA_N,\mu)=
        \max\bigg\{
            \bbW_2\Big(\sym(\mu(\cA_N)), \mu\Big),
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_N), \cP(\{\pm 1\})\Big)
        \bigg\}
        \le \iota\,,

    which furthermore satisfies $\chi_{\cA_N}(0) = 0$ and $\chi_{\cA_N}(1-\iota) \le \iota$.
    This implies
    \[
        \cM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon) \subseteq \cM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0;C(L,\epsilon),\iota(\epsilon))\,.
    \]
    The rest of the proof is identical to that of Lemma~\ref{l:IAMP.in.Lip}.

{"assumptions":["Finite d,q; constant SPD H with spectrum in [m,M]","Adapted states, deterministic u0, v0=0; jointly sampled oracle noise centered conditional on the past","Normal conditional covariance <=sigma^2 H; tangential conditional second moment <=sigma^2 D^2 |v|^2","0<rho<2; 0<eta<=rho/M; sigma,D>=0; F in C_b^2","Unbiased gradient oracle; individual random sample-loss gradient representation not asserted","For the proportional-covariance target subclass require normal covariance equality on v=0; proportionality is on the manifold only"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T19:49:38.596602+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_3eb7dc9fd7523a133f226b8bdae7ac45699057680f6ac8b7e79453b8cfe1178d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Status: proof (unaudited). C006 v1. Novelty unestablished.

Let d,q>=1 be finite, H a constant symmetric positive definite q by q
matrix, and 0<m<=lambda(H)<=M. Fix sigma,D>=0, 0<rho<2 and
0<eta<=rho/M. Let (F_k) be a filtration and (u_k,v_k) adapted, with
deterministic u_0 and v_0=0. At each step let the jointly sampled oracle
noise (xi_k^u,xi_k^v) in R^d x R^q be F_{k+1}-measurable, with

    E[xi_k^u|F_k]=0, E[xi_k^v|F_k]=0,
    E[xi_k^v (xi_k^v)^T|F_k] <= sigma^2 H,
    E[|xi_k^u|^2|F_k] <= sigma^2 D^2 |v_k|^2.           (1)

The matrix inequality is in Loewner order and holds almost surely.
The two noise components may be dependent; their law may depend on the
entire past and on k. No iid, Markov, symmetry or higher-moment hypothesis
is imposed. Consider the unbiased stochastic-gradient oracle recursion
for the population loss L(u,v)=v^T H v/2:

    u_{k+1}=u_k-eta xi_k^u,
    v_{k+1}=B v_k-eta xi_k^v, B=I-eta H.               (2)

Here "oracle" means an unbiased estimator of grad L; this theorem does
not assert that every allowed noise field is the gradient of an individual
random sample loss. The label-gradient models of C005 are included.

For F in C_b^2(R^{d+q}), let f(u)=F(u,0), a(u)=D_v F(u,0), and define

    F_2=sup ||D^2 f||_op,
    F_vv=sup ||D_v^2 F||_op,
    F_uv=sup ||D_u a||_op,
    c=sigma^2 q/(2-rho), gamma=min{m,M(2-rho)/rho}.

Then, for every T>=0,

    sup_{integer 0<=K<=T/eta^2}
      |E F(u_K,v_K)-F(u_0,0)| <= eta C(T),
    C(T)=c[F_vv/2+T sigma^2 D^2 F_2/2+F_uv sigma D/gamma]. (3)

Thus a=1. If, in addition, the normal conditional covariance equals
sigma^2 H on the event v_k=0, then (1) forces xi_k^u=0 there almost
surely. Consequently the full noise covariance on the minimizing
manifold is sigma^2 diag(0,H), proportional to the population Hessian.
That equality is the target-compatible subclass; the estimate itself
uses only domination. No global covariance proportionality is asserted.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X, Y Banach spaces"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:57.492197+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, operator theory","id":"claim_3ecf47d2e1941e3ed3b704c1615dceb455e30d7da6c0085069f13dc22e065c98","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X, Y be Banach spaces. A linear operator K : X → Y is compact if it maps the closed unit ball of X onto a relatively compact subset of Y; equivalently, for every bounded sequence (x_n) in X the sequence (Kx_n) has a norm-convergent subsequence. Compact operators are bounded. They form a norm-closed two-sided ideal in the bounded operators: norm limits of compact operators are compact, and BK and KB are compact whenever K is compact and B is bounded. Every bounded finite-rank operator is compact; in a Hilbert space (and in every Banach space with the approximation property) every compact operator is a norm limit of finite-rank operators. K is compact iff its adjoint K* is compact (Schauder). The identity of an infinite-dimensional space is not compact (Riesz), so on an infinite-dimensional space a compact operator never has a bounded inverse. A compact operator maps weakly convergent sequences to norm-convergent sequences; the converse (complete continuity implies compactness) holds when X is reflexive, e.g. a Hilbert space, but fails in ℓ^1 (Schur property).\n\nExamples: diag(λ_n) on ℓ^2 is compact iff λ_n → 0; integral operators with L^2 kernels (Hilbert–Schmidt operators) are compact; the embedding H^1_0(Ω) → L^2(Ω) for bounded open Ω is compact (Rellich), so the inverse of the Dirichlet Laplacian is a compact self-adjoint operator on L^2(Ω). Non-examples: the shift operators on ℓ^2; multiplication by a function f on L^2[0,1] is compact only when f = 0 a.e.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.591818+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3ef0fba9790a49a2f07e536c3009475e0650fdfc52ad3b559013ef0c83316eaf","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.03589, 'Correlated initialization of deep residual networks'] We study the large-depth behavior of residual networks whose weights are correlated across layers at initialization. Our results confirm and extend a conjecture of \\citet{marionScalingResNetsLargedepth2025}, according to which correlated initializations should interpolate continuously between the Brownian stochastic differential equation arising from independent initialization and the ordinary differential equation arising from perfectly correlated initialization. When the initialization is obtained from the application of a feature function to a stationary Gaussian sequence with regularly varying correlation, we prove that there exists a unique critical scaling such that the infinite-depth limit is the solution of a Young differential equation driven by a Hermite process. Hermite processes reduce to the fractional Brownian motion if the feature function generating the initialization has Hermite rank one, which is the case for the identity function, for example. We show that the critical scaling and asymptotic limit are uniquely determined by the decay of correlations together with the Hermite rank of the feature function. Consequently, the correlation structure and Hermite rank of the initialization represent meaningful hyperparameters in the asymptotic regime. By contrast, under finite-variance iid initialization, the asymptotic driver is universally Brownian up to normalization regardless of the choice of distribution. Our proofs rely on a collection of novel results establishing a robust stability theory for Young differential equations in Banach spaces. \\smallskip \\noindent{\\bf Keywords:} Residual networks, correlated initialization, large-depth limit, Young differential equations, Hermite processes, fractional Brownian motion, long-range dependence, functional limit theorems \\noindent{\\bf AMS Classification:} 60G18, 60G22, 60H10, 60L20, 60L90, 60F17, 68T07.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:28:31.997447+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3f0d172b50e04325020142585660f2ed03b878d25321f5fc4fa6f988d2c6be7f","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2512.02322, 'Ursell functions in lattice gauge theory'] Consider the term $c_{I,\mathfrak{P}}$ from \eqref{eq:defCIp}, where $I \subset [n]$ and $\mathfrak{P} \in \mathfrak{F}_n$.
Then the following holds. \newline 
(a) For any $\mathfrak{P} \in \mathfrak{F}_n$, we have $c_{\emptyset,\mathfrak{P}}=0$. \newline 
(b) If $\mathfrak{P}=\{[n]\}$ and $I \subset [n]$, we have $
c_{I,\mathfrak{P}} = \mathbbm{1}\{|I| ~ \text{odd}\}$. \newline 
(c) For any $\mathfrak{P} \in \mathfrak{F}_n$ and any $i \in [n]$, we have $c_{\{i\},\mathfrak{P}}=1$.
\newline 
(d) For any $\mathfrak{P} \in \mathfrak{F}_n$ and any $I \subset [n]$, we have $
c_{I,\mathfrak{P}} \in \{0,...,n\}$. \newline 
(e) For any $I=\{i,j\} \subset [n], i \neq j$, then we have 
    \begin{equation*}      
        c_{I, \mathfrak{P}} = 2 \cdot \mathbbm{1}\{i,j ~ \text{are in different partitions elements of } \mathfrak{P}\}.
    \end{equation*}
    In particular if $|I|=2$, then $c_{I,\mathfrak{P}} \neq 0$ if and only if $c_{I,\mathfrak{P}} = 2$. \newline 
(f) Let $\mathfrak{P} \in \mathfrak{F}_n \setminus \{[n]\}$. Then there exists $i \in [n-1]$, such that for $I=\{i,i+1\}$ we have $c_{I,\mathfrak{P}} \neq 0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:51:00.241315+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3f10719f875a268d0fdd12b410c21e019ccd67d02e86fb04c3b4d3ebfae1967e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm phase_transition_231 of arXiv:2604.23751, 'Large deviation principles for pattern-avoiding permutations, and limit shapes for constra'] For $\beta >0,$ we let

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:39:41.408089+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3f13c24e3062fafcb5c915f4be647bcee89d9c68b5f4f3705bf65493307de5ed","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2604.06645, '2604.06645'] Let $p$ be large enough such that $\frac{d+2}{p} + \frac{d}{p-2} < 1-\eta$, where $\eta$ is given in Assumption \ref{assump: convolution singularity}, and let $a$ be given by \eqref{eq: alpha}. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:14:37.609841+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3f172d2fe9db4230308a223c82927dc3a74fa77ee6a2b9a66af7422a3a91b640","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theoremen 5 (A refined time-uniform clipped-mean bound) of arXiv:2608.18999, '2608.18999'] Let \(H\) be a separable real Hilbert space, let \(1<p\le2\), let
\((\mathcal F_i)_{i\ge0}\) be a filtration, and let \((X_i)_{i\ge1}\) be
adapted to it.  Suppose that, for some deterministic \(\mu\in H\) and
\(v\in[0,\infty)\), almost surely,
\[
\E[X_i\mid\mathcal F_{i-1}]=\mu,
\qquad
\E[\norm{X_i-\mu}^p\mid\mathcal F_{i-1}]\le v
\quad (i\ge1).
\]
Fix \(k\ge1\), \(\lambda,\rho>0\), and
\(\delta_1,\delta_2\in(0,1)\) with \(\delta_1+\delta_2<1\).  Suppose that
the \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable pilot estimator \(\widehat Z_k\) satisfies
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(
  \norm{\widehat Z_k-\mu}\ge r(\delta_2,k)
\right)\le\delta_2
\]
for a deterministic radius \(r(\delta_2,k)\).  For \(n>k\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_n
=\widehat Z_k+
\frac1{n-k}\sum_{i=k+1}^n
C_{1/\lambda}(X_i-\widehat Z_k).
\]
Then, on an event of probability at least
\(1-\delta_1-\delta_2\), simultaneously for every \(n>k\),
\begin{equation}
\norm{\widehat\mu_n-\mu}
\le
2^{p-1}\kappa_p\!\bigl(\rho h(\rho)\bigr)
\lambda^{p-1}
\bigl(v+r(\delta_2,k)^p\bigr)
+\frac{\log(2/\delta_1)}{\rho\lambda(n-k)}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:01:48.632723+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3f2a27cd682ee0d5c317e0d7af12a3f1c8654de548c0f8a755c4fc28db0c0893","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma l:prior.W.logconcave of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] For $d \ge (1+\epsilon)n$, the prior distribution $W\sim\mathbb{P}_{0}$ conditioned on ${\mathcal{H}}$ in \prettyref{eq:calH}
is $(c_0 d)$-strongly log-concave, where $c_0$ is a positive constant depending on $\epsilon$.

\begin{proof}
Under the prior distribution $\mathbb{P}_{0}$, 
the density of $W$ is given by (see e.g.\ [anderson2003introduction])
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}_0(W) 
&\propto e^{-V(W
)} \mathbf{1}\{ I+W \succ 0\}\,, \\
V(W) &= - \frac{d-n-1}{2}\log \det(I+W)\,.
\end{align*}
Abbreviate ${\widetilde{W}}=I+W$, and denote by 
$\nabla^2$  the Hessian with respect to the lower triangular elements of $W$. Let $H$ be an $n\times n$ symmetric matrix with zero diagonal. Then
    \begin{align*}
    \log\det({\widetilde{W}}+\epsilon H)
    &=\log\det({\widetilde{W}})
    +\log\det(I+\epsilon B)\,,\\
    B &= {\widetilde{W}}^{-1/2}H{\widetilde{W}}^{-1/2}\,.
    \end{align*}
$B$ is a symmetric matrix. Denoting its eigenvalues by $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n$, we have
    \begin{align*}
    \log\det({\widetilde{W}}+\epsilon H)
    &= \log\det({\widetilde{W}})
    +\sum_{i=1}^n\log(1+\epsilon\lambda_i) 
    = \log\det({\widetilde{W}})
    +\epsilon \sum_{i=1}^n \lambda_i
    -\frac{\epsilon^2}{2}
    \sum_{i=1}^n (\lambda_i)^2\\
    &= \log\det({\widetilde{W}})
    +\epsilon \mathop{\rm tr}(B)
    -\frac{\epsilon^2}{2}
    \mathop{\rm tr}(B^2)\,.
    \end{align*}
It follows that
\begin{equation}
-H^\top\nabla^2 \big[\log\det \widetilde{W} \big] H =\mathop{\rm tr}(\widetilde{W}^{-1}H\widetilde{W}^{-1}H)=\|\widetilde{W}^{-1/2}H\widetilde{W}^{-1/2}\|_{\operatorname{F}}^2\ge \frac{\|H\|_{\operatorname{F}}^2}{\|\widetilde{W}\|_{\operatorname{op}}^2}\,,

\end{equation}
that is to say, the log-determinant function is strongly log-concave.\footnote{From  \prettyref{eq:hess-prior} we see that 
as long as $d\geq n+1$,
the prior distribution $\mathbb{P}_{0}$ is always strongly log-concave with constant $\Theta(\frac{d-n-1}{n^2}$); this is tight when all $x_i$'s are aligned. Lemma~(l:prior.W.logconcave of the paper) improves the curvature to $\Theta(d)$ by truncating on the typical behavior of $W$.} Next recall from \prettyref{eq:calH} that 
${\mathcal{H}}=\{\|\widetilde{W}\|_{\operatorname{op}} \leq 4\}$, which is a convex set in $W$. 
For each $W \in {\mathcal{H}}$, the right-hand side of \prettyref{eq:hess-prior} is further lower bounded by $\|H\|^2/16$, and hence
\[
\nabla^2 V(W)\succeq \frac{d-n-1}{16}I_{n(n-1)/2}\succeq c_0 d I_{n(n-1)/2}\,,
\]
for a constant $c_0>0$ depending on $\epsilon$. This proves the claim.
\end{proof}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-10T02:20:17.000000+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_3f8bf7a66fe8f0b6912e3c576538ccfb8d9635fb53551a501252cbeac7436a24","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In the mathematical discipline of group theory, Cayley's theorem, named in honour of Arthur Cayley, states that every group G is isomorphic to a subgroup of a symmetric group. external multibox $q$-components assigned wholly to the fresh root color;

not in $\mathcal P_R$.  Let $\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0)}$ be the sum of

root-only recurrence-dimer subfamily of

 \mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,+)}

Ricci residual component contains an ordinary hard resource in the sense
of (lem:ricci-internal-hard of the paper), and put
\[
 \mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,{\rm soft})}
 :=\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,+)}-
   \mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,{\rm hard})}.

Resolve the internal full-centered hard blocks of this last family as in
(lem:ricci-soft-threshold of the paper).  Route every all-Weyl child and,

termwise estimate after fixing a ribbon, status, Green coefficient, or

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:18:19.412996+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3fa9557ce41f7d66628b425950bee9df09976090f7b79cc209a6941e99d4a167","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:limit_of_difference_operator_intro of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] \begin{enumerate}[$\bullet$]
		\item
			If $(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})$ is above or below $\mathcal{W}$, we have $d(\Delta x)=0$ and $a(\Delta x)=-1$, that is, the
			limiting difference operator is the negative identity $(-Id)$;
		\item If $(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})$ lies on the upper boundary of $\mathcal{W}$,
			then
			\begin{equation*}
				d(\Delta x)=-\kappa^{2} q^{2\Delta x+1/2},
				\qquad
				a(\Delta x)=-1-\kappa^{2}(1+q)q^{2\Delta x+1}.
			\end{equation*}
			On the lower boundary of $\mathcal{W}$, 
			one has to 
			replace the powers of $(q,\kappa)$ with those of
			$(q^{-1},\kappa^{-1})$, while the factor $1+q$ is kept
			the same.
		\item 
			Inside $\mathcal{W}$ but away
			from its center line $\lfloor
			L\hspace{1pt}\mathsf{x}\rfloor=\tfrac12(S+t)$, the
			coefficients in the upper half are
			\begin{equation*}
				d(\Delta x)=-\kappa^{2} q^{2\Delta x+1/2},
				\qquad 
				a(\Delta x)=-\kappa^{2}(1+q)q^{2\Delta x+1}.
			\end{equation*}
			The formulas for the lower part are obtained from these by the same symmetry as in the preceding item.
		\item
			On the center line, we get
			\begin{equation}
				
				d(\Delta x)=\dfrac{-\kappa^2(1 - \kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x})^{-1} q^{2\Delta x+1/2}}{
				\sqrt{(1 - \kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x-1}) (1 - \kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x+1})}}
				,\qquad
				a(\Delta x)=
				\dfrac{-\kappa^2 (1+q) \hspace{1pt} q^{2\Delta x+1}}{(1-\kappa^2 q^{2 \Delta x})(1-\kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x+2})}.
			\end{equation}
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:30:50.719490+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3fd2dd4a134d9d7a33cd7621b45935ae701fb5bff359162f5ef568a8390e10f0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Conjecture Typical AHMS dimension of arXiv:2609.02155, 'Exact Limits of Random Projections for Preserving Geometry:\\ Distance Recovery, Nearest-N'] \label[conjecture]{conj:ordinal-gaussian}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:29:21.937766+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3fdace46589bad5debb6120ca9be17ea43249d6d1744c105bb93b475c04e2bf0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 24 (see \cite{FrGue}) of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $K$ be a compact convex set in $\mathbb R^n$, let
$p\in\mathbb N$, and let
\[
u_j\colon K\to\mathbb R,
\quad j=1,\ldots,p,
\]
be continuous functions. Let $P_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}(K)\ne\emptyset$ be the set of all
log-concave measures $\nu$ supported in $K$ such that
\[
\int_K u_j\,d\nu\ge0,
\quad j=1,\ldots,p.
\]
Let
\[
\Phi\colon P(K)\to\mathbb R
\]
be a convex continuous functional, where $P(K)$ is the space of all Borel
probability measures on $K$, equipped with the weak topology. Then
\[
\sup_{\nu\in P_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}(K)} \Phi(\nu)
\]
is attained at a log-concave measure $\nu\in P_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}(K)$ such that
the affine span $S(\nu)$ of $\operatorname{supp}(\nu)$ satisfies
\[
\dim S(\nu)\le p.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\sup_{\mu\in P_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}(K)} \Phi(\nu)
=
\sup_{\substack{\nu\in P_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}(K)\\ \dim S(\nu)\le p}}
\Phi(\nu).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:26:26.773775+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3fde682e505a7c0edd5ed0500488cd217436017f30313df22d097b5c3d4e2706","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:sc-dual-Darboux of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] Let $K$ be dual dressing compatible with $(\Psi, \Phi)$, with
resolvent $R(u) = (I - zK(u))^{-1}$.  Define the dressed
observable and dressed waves by
\[
\mathcal{M}(u) \vcentcolon= I + z\Phi(u)R(u)\Psi(u),
\]
\[
\widehat\Psi(u) \vcentcolon= R(u)\Psi(u), \qquad
\widehat\Phi(u) \vcentcolon= \Phi(u)R(T^{-1}u).
\]
Then $\mathcal{M}(u)$ is invertible for every
$u \in \mathcal{V}$.  The dressed waves
$\widehat\Psi, \widehat\Phi$ satisfy the dual
linear problem
(equation eq:sc-dual-linear-1 of the paper)--(equation eq:sc-dual-linear-j of the paper) and
dual adjoint problem
(equation eq:sc-dual-adjoint-1 of the paper)--(equation eq:sc-dual-adjoint-j of the paper)
respectively, with data $(\mathcal{M}_k, \Lambda_k)$: for each $j \geq 2$,
\begin{align*}
\partial_1\widehat\Psi(Tu)
  &= \widehat\Psi(Tu)\mathcal{M}_1(u)
     - \widehat\Psi(u)\Lambda_1(u), \\
\widehat\Psi(S_j u)
  &= \widehat\Psi(Tu)\mathcal{M}_j(u)
     - \widehat\Psi(u)\Lambda_j(u),
\shortintertext{and}
\partial_1\widehat\Phi(Tu)
  &= \Lambda_1(Tu)\widehat\Phi(T^2u)
     - \mathcal{M}_1(u)\widehat\Phi(Tu), \\
\widehat\Phi(Tu)
  &= \mathcal{M}_j(u)\widehat\Phi(S_j u)
     - \Lambda_j(Tu)\widehat\Phi(TS_j u),
\end{align*}
where the dressed edge weights are given by
\begin{align}
\mathcal{M}_1(u)
  &\vcentcolon= \mathcal{M}(Tu)^{-1}C_1(u)\mathcal{M}(Tu)
  + \mathcal{M}(Tu)^{-1}\partial_1\mathcal{M}(Tu),
   \\
\mathcal{M}_j(u)
  &\vcentcolon= \mathcal{M}(Tu)^{-1}C_j(u)\mathcal{M}(S_j u),
  
\end{align}
and $\widehat K(u) \vcentcolon= K(u)R(u)$ is dual dressing compatible
with $(\widehat\Psi, \widehat\Phi)$.
Moreover, $(\mathcal{M}_k, \Lambda_k)$ satisfies the dual
diamond equations of
Corollary~(cor:sc-dual-diamonds of the paper).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:04:55.801533+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3fe9562c4925f0ccf9ece0d325ec2bd77ccad2f9bd79ee37ef8bad2a698c9b49","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn d:noise of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] For $d\in\mathbb{N}$, a \emph{$d$-dimensional noise} consists of a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, a collection of sub-$\sigma$-algebras $\{\mathcal{F}_R\}_{R\in\mathcal{R}}$ where $\mathcal{R}$ is the set of open $d$-dimensional rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and a measurable $\mathbb{R}^d$-action $\{\theta_h\}_{h\in\mathbb{R}^d}$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$,
    such that the following properties hold.
    \begin{enumerate}[label={\rm(N\arabic*)},ref={\rm N\arabic*}]
        \item
        \textup{(Exhaustive filtration).} $\mathcal{F} = \bigvee_{R\in\mathcal{R}} \mathcal{F}_R$.
        \item 
        \textup{(Translation covariance).}
        For all $h\in\mathbb{R}^d$, we have $\theta_h(\mathcal{F}_R) = \mathcal{F}_{R+h}$.
        \item 
        \textup{(Independence).}
        For all $R_1,R_2\in\mathcal{R}$ with $R_1\cap R_2=\varnothing$, the $\sigma$-algebras $\mathcal{F}_{R_1}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{R_2}$ are independent.
        \item
        \textup{(Join).}
        For all $R_1,R_2,R_3\in\mathcal{R}$ with $R_1\cap R_2=\varnothing$ and $\overline{R_1\cup R_2}=\overline{R_3}$, we have $\mathcal{F}_{R_1}\vee \mathcal{F}_{R_2} = \mathcal{F}_{R_3}$ up to null sets.
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X is a compact metric space and T is continuous","the metric enters only through the compact topology"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T02:00:35.438163+00:00","domain":"topological dynamics, entropy","id":"claim_3fe95da80d1756dae2bb8c43b479ad29fb9efff8bf12406c39a668547d7335d9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $T: X \\to X$ be a continuous map of a compact metric space $(X, d)$. For $n \\ge 1$ define the dynamical metric $d_n(x, y) = \\max_{0 \\le k < n} d(T^k x, T^k y)$. A set $E \\subset X$ is $(n, \\varepsilon)$-separated if $d_n(x, y) > \\varepsilon$ for all distinct $x, y \\in E$; let $s(n, \\varepsilon)$ be the maximal cardinality of such a set (finite by compactness). A set $F$ is $(n, \\varepsilon)$-spanning if every $x \\in X$ has $d_n(x, y) \\le \\varepsilon$ for some $y \\in F$; let $r(n, \\varepsilon)$ be the minimal cardinality. The topological entropy is\n$$h_{top}(T) = \\lim_{\\varepsilon \\to 0} \\limsup_{n \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{n} \\log s(n, \\varepsilon) = \\lim_{\\varepsilon \\to 0} \\limsup_{n \\to \\infty} \\frac{1}{n} \\log r(n, \\varepsilon) \\in [0, \\infty],$$\nusing $r(n,\\varepsilon) \\le s(n,\\varepsilon) \\le r(n, \\varepsilon/2)$; the limit in $\\varepsilon$ exists by monotonicity, and replacing the $\\limsup$ in $n$ by a $\\liminf$ gives the same value. The value is independent of the compatible metric (this uses compactness) and coincides with the open-cover definition $h_{top}(T) = \\sup_{\\mathcal{U}} \\lim_n \\frac1n \\log N(\\mathcal{U}^n_0)$ where $N$ counts the minimal subcover of the join $\\mathcal{U}^n_0 = \\bigvee_{k<n} T^{-k}\\mathcal{U}$. Basic properties: $h_{top}(T^m) = m\\, h_{top}(T)$ for $m \\ge 1$; $h_{top}(T^{-1}) = h_{top}(T)$ for homeomorphisms; $h_{top}$ is an invariant of topological conjugacy; a Lipschitz map of a compact metric space of finite box dimension has finite entropy, but a continuous map of a compact metric space can have $h_{top} = \\infty$. On a NON-compact space the separated-set quantity depends on the metric, not merely on the topology, and the equalities above can fail.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:52:08.674398+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3ff619da11f26838eeebd63e4e7ab7d17c07daa25e94177b4f2168ecd887ce56","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 42 (Difference equation for two Ricci--DeTurck solutions) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let \(s(t)\) be a Ricci-flow background and let \(v_0(t)\) and \(v_1(t)\)
be two positive definite solutions of the Ricci--DeTurck equation relative to
\(s(t)\) on the same time interval.  Put
\[
        U=v_1-v_0,
        \qquad v_\vartheta=v_0+\vartheta(v_1-v_0),
        \quad 0\leq\vartheta\leq1,
\]
and assume that every \(v_\vartheta\) is positive definite.  With \(\nabla\)
the connection of \(s(t)\), the difference satisfies a homogeneous linear
system
\begin{equation}
        \partial_tU-P^{pq}\nabla_p\nabla_qU
        =B^p\nabla_pU+CU,
\end{equation}
where the second-order part is diagonal in the tensor components: in a fixed
frame, every component \(U^A\) is acted on by the same operator
\(P^{pq}\nabla_p\nabla_q\), and no second derivative of a different component
occurs.  More precisely, for
\[
        \mathcal Q_s(v)=-2\Ric(v)+\Lie_{W(v,s)}v,
\]
one has the structural formula
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
        \mathcal Q_s(v)
        ={}&v^{pq}\nabla_p\nabla_qv
        +v^{-1}*v^{-1}*\nabla v*\nabla v \\
        &\quad+\mathcal R(\Rm(s),v,v^{-1}),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
and the mean-value identity
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
        \partial_tU
        &=\mathcal Q_s(v_1)-\mathcal Q_s(v_0)\\
        &=\int_0^1D\mathcal Q_s|_{v_\vartheta}[U] \,d\vartheta.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Differentiating \eqref{eq:rdt-structural-form} gives
\begin{equation}
        D\mathcal Q_s|_{v_\vartheta}[Z]
        =v_\vartheta^{pq}\nabla_p\nabla_qZ
          +\mathcal B_\vartheta^p\nabla_pZ+\mathcal C_\vartheta Z,
\end{equation}
with
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
        \mathcal B_\vartheta
        &=v_\vartheta^{-1}*v_\vartheta^{-1}*\nabla v_\vartheta,\\
        \mathcal C_\vartheta
        &=v_\vartheta^{-1}*v_\vartheta^{-1}*\nabla^2v_\vartheta
          +v_\vartheta^{-1}*v_\vartheta^{-1}*v_\vartheta^{-1}
             *\nabla v_\vartheta*\nabla v_\vartheta\\
        &\qquad+\mathcal R_1(\Rm(s),v_\vartheta,v_\vartheta^{-1}).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Here \(*\) denotes universal tensor contractions, and \(\mathcal R\) and
\(\mathcal R_1\) are algebraic in the displayed arguments; in particular,
\(\mathcal R_1\) contains no derivatives of \(v_\vartheta\).  The
coefficients in \eqref{eq:rdt-difference-system} are
\[
 P^{pq}=\int_0^1v_\vartheta^{pq}\,d\vartheta,
 \qquad B^p=\int_0^1\mathcal B_\vartheta^p\,d\vartheta,
 \qquad C=\int_0^1\mathcal C_\vartheta\,d\vartheta.
\]
Consequently, uniform metric equivalence and finite-order bounds for
\(v_0,v_1\), and \(s\) give the corresponding ellipticity and H\"older bounds
for \(P,B,C\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:33.537240+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_402cc7a17e09582be87b6b33999c970f349a537eefdc570e9d42f1df8933d920","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2603.28226, '2603.28226'] Let \(f\ge0\) belong to \(L^1(\mathcal F_\infty)\), let \(\lambda>0\), and let
\(\theta\ge0\). Retain the notation of Section~\ref{sec:proof} and
\eqref{eq:s-theta}; thus
\[
r:=\inf\{n\ge1:\ f_n>\lambda\},
\qquad
\varepsilon_n:=d f_n\,\mathbf1_{\{r=n\}},
\qquad
\gamma_n:=d f_n\,\mathbf1_{\{r>n\}},
\]
\[
\Lambda_0:=0,
\qquad
\Lambda_m:=\sum_{k=1}^{m}\mathbb E_k[\varepsilon_{k+1}],
\qquad
s_\theta:=\inf\{m\ge1:\ \Lambda_m>\theta\lambda\},
\qquad
t_\theta:=r\wedge s_\theta.
\]
Also set
\[
r^-:=r-1 \ \text{on }\{r<\infty\},
\qquad
r^-:=\infty \ \text{on }\{r=\infty\}.
\]

Define
\[
g_\theta:=f-f_{t_\theta},
\]
\[
h_{\theta,n}:=
\sum_{j=1}^{n}
\bigl(\varepsilon_j-\mathbb E_{j-1}[\varepsilon_j]\bigr)\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta\ge j\}},
\qquad n\ge1,
\]
\[
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{st}}
:=
\sum_{j=1}^{n}\gamma_j\,\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta\ge j\}},
\qquad
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{pr}}
:=
\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbb E_{j-1}[\varepsilon_j]\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta\ge j\}},
\qquad n\ge1.
\]
Then \(h_{\theta,n}\) converges almost surely and in \(L^1\) to a limit
\(h_\theta\in L^1(\mathcal F_\infty)\), and the sequences
\[
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{st}},
\qquad
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{pr}}
\]
converge almost surely and in \(L^1\) to limits
\[
k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}},
\qquad
k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}
\in L^1(\mathcal F_\infty).
\]
Moreover,
\[
f=g_\theta+h_\theta+k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}+k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}.
\]

\medskip
\noindent\textup{(a)}
\[
\mathbb P\Bigl(\sup_{n\ge1}|\mathbb E_n[g_\theta]|>0\Bigr)
\le \frac{\|f\|_1}{\lambda},
\qquad
\|g_\theta\|_1\le 2\|f\|_1.
\]

\noindent\textup{(b)}
\[
\Bigl\|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}
\bigl|\mathbb E_n[h_\theta]-\mathbb E_{n-1}[h_\theta]\bigr|
\Bigr\|_1
\le 2\|f\|_1.
\]
In particular,
\[
\|h_\theta\|_1\le 2\|f\|_1.
\]

\noindent\textup{(c)}
\[
k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}=f_{s_\theta\wedge r^-},
\qquad
0\le k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\le \lambda
\quad\text{a.s.}
\]

\noindent\textup{(d)}
\[
k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}
=
\Lambda_{s_\theta-1}\,\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta<\infty\}}
+
\Bigl(\sup_{m\ge1}\Lambda_m\Bigr)\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta=\infty\}},
\qquad
0\le k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\le \theta\lambda
\quad\text{a.s.}
\]

\noindent\textup{(e)}
\[
\mathbb E[h_\theta]=\mathbb E[\varepsilon_1],
\]
\[
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\|_1+\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_1
=
\|f\|_1-\mathbb E[\varepsilon_1]
\le \|f\|_1,
\]
\[
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\|_2^2
\le \lambda\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\|_1,
\qquad
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_2^2
\le \theta\lambda\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_1,
\]
and
\[
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}+k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_2^2
\le (1+\theta)\lambda\|f\|_1.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:51.726542+00:00","domain":"dispersive partial differential equations","id":"claim_4035e0f47d8f89385856e3a0fa89ee495b32f2ab6d982252999b8813bc8feedd","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypothesis: finite speed of propagation and the domain-of-dependence cone are properties of the wave equation (and of symmetric hyperbolic systems), proved by a local energy identity on the cone. The Schrödinger equation has no such identity and propagates instantaneously. Concrete counterexample: let f ∈ L¹(R^n) be nonzero and compactly supported and let t ≠ 0. By the kernel formula, e^{itΔ}f(x) = (4πit)^{−n/2} e^{i|x|²/(4t)} · G(x/(2t)) where G is the Fourier transform of the compactly supported integrable function y ↦ e^{i|y|²/(4t)}f(y). By the Paley–Wiener theorem G extends to an entire function on C^n, and it is not identically zero, so its zero set contains no nonempty open set. Hence e^{itΔ}f is nonzero almost everywhere on every open subset of R^n at every t ≠ 0: compactly supported data instantly become globally supported. The same phenomenon rules out any cone-shaped domain of dependence, and the heat equation behaves the same way. What survives for Schrödinger are local smoothing, dispersive decay and (pseudo)locality statements about wave packets moving at velocity ≈ 2ξ, not a finite propagation speed; the wave equation's finite-speed argument must never be transplanted to a dispersive or parabolic equation.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:06:07.078127+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_40499db85848ffefdfdcd5e77731522500404a4250fb26b00f2814cc03ed372c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 9 (Weak stability of positive \(L^2\) Stein kernels) of arXiv:2608.27657, '\bfseries Stein Kernels and Normal Approximation\\ for Log-Concave Bilinear Forms'] Let \(\mu_k\Rightarrow\mu\) weakly on \(\R^n\), where each \(\mu_k\)
is centered and has finite second moments.  Let \(Y_k\sim\mu_k\), and
suppose that \(\mu_k\) admits a symmetric positive-semidefinite Stein
kernel \(\tau_k\) such that
\begin{equation}
  L:=\sup_k\E\|\tau_k(Y_k)\|_{\HS}^2<\infty.
  \tag{4.2}
\end{equation}
Then \(\mu\) is centered, \(\mu_k\to\mu\) in \(W_2\), and \(\mu\)
admits a symmetric positive-semidefinite Stein kernel \(\tau\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
  \E\tau(Y)=\Cov(Y),
  \qquad
  \E\|\tau(Y)\|_{\HS}^2
  \leq
  \liminf_{k\to\infty}\E\|\tau_k(Y_k)\|_{\HS}^2,
  \tag{4.3}
\end{equation}
where \(Y\sim\mu\).  The same kernel may be chosen with the following
additional permanence properties.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
If \(F:\mathsf S_n\to[0,\infty]\) is convex and lower semicontinuous and
\(\sup_k\E F(\tau_k(Y_k))\leq C_F\), then
\[
  \E F(\tau(Y))\leq C_F.
\]

\item
If, for every \(A\in\mathsf S_n\),
\[
  \Var\!\left(\Tr(A\tau_k(Y_k))\right)
  \leq C_{\rm tr}\Tr(A^2),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
  \Var\!\left(\Tr(A\tau(Y))\right)
  \leq C_{\rm tr}\Tr(A^2)
  \qquad(A\in\mathsf S_n).
  \tag{4.4}
\end{equation}

\item
If, for every \(A\in\mathsf S_n\),
\[
  \E\Tr(A\tau_k(Y_k)A\tau_k(Y_k))
  \leq C_{\rm en}\Tr(A^2),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
  \E\Tr(A\tau(Y)A\tau(Y))
  \leq C_{\rm en}\Tr(A^2)
  \qquad(A\in\mathsf S_n).
  \tag{4.5}
\end{equation}

\item
If a constant \(C_{\rm wp}\) satisfies
\[
  \Var_{\mu_k}g
  \leq
  C_{\rm wp}\,
  \E\langle
    \tau_k(Y_k)\nabla g(Y_k),\nabla g(Y_k)
  \rangle
\]
for every \(k\) and every \(g\in C_c^\infty(\R^n)\), then
\begin{equation}
  \Var_\mu g
  \leq
  C_{\rm wp}\,
  \E\langle
    \tau(Y)\nabla g(Y),\nabla g(Y)
  \rangle
  \qquad(g\in C_c^\infty(\R^n)).
  \tag{4.6}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

\begin{equation}

\gamma_1(t-s,y)\,k(t,s)\,

Here,
\begin{equation}
G(t,y)

\gamma_1(\tau,y)

+
\frac{\beta(\psi(y))}{\sigma(y)}
r_1(\tau,y,y),

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:17:42.312267+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_40871787fc45aea8c87bcfc71952dd37f18724345a7ff0c0c4b0ecef144b6d99","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 20 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] For a function $g : X \to Y$, where $X = \T^d$ or $\R^d$ and $Y$ is a Banach space, we define for $s \geq 0$ the (semi)norm space $\mathcal{C}^s$ as follows. For $s=0$, we let
    \[\|g\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(X) Y} := \sup_{x \in X} \|g(x)\|_Y.\]
    For $s \in (0,\infty)$---letting $s = n + r$ where $r \in (0,1]$ and $n \in \N$---we define $\mathcal{C}^s(X)$ as a seminorm on a subspace of $C^n(X)$ by
    \[\|g\|_{\mathcal{C}^s(X) Y} := \sup_{x,x' \in X, x \ne x'} \frac{\|\nabla^n g(x) - \nabla^ng(x')\|_Y}{|x-x'|^r}.\]
    We note in particular that $\mathcal{C}^1$ is the Lipschitz seminorm and that $\mathcal{C}^0$ is the natural norm on the space of bounded functions---rather than $C^1$ and $C^0$ which have additional qualitative regularity hypotheses that we do not want to require, as we will frequently be working with Lipschitz functions that are not $C^1$.

    We also consider for $p \in [1,\infty), s\geq 0$ the fractional Sobolev (semi)norm spaces $W^{s,p}$. For $s \in \N$, we just let $\|g\|_{W^{s,p}(X)Y} := \|\nabla^s g\|_{L^p(X)Y}$, and for $s>0$ and $s \not \in \N$, we again write $s = n+r$ where $r \in (0,1)$ and $n \in \N$ and define
    \[\|g\|_{W^{s,p}(X) Y} := \Big(\int_X \int_X \frac{\|\nabla^n g(x) - \nabla^n g(x')\|^p_Y}{|x-x'|^{d + rp}}\,dx\,dx'\Big)^{1/p}.\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:57:28.721388+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_40ca71dd6ef3c68ffc4d0f55c284dac5dd8311461393016f2d79d105c2651331","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $m,n,\ell\in\Nsf$, let $U\subseteq\Rsf^m$ be an open convex set, and let $\phi:U\to\Rsf^\ell$ be a smooth function. Let $p\in [1,3)$, let $\omega$ be a control function on interval $[S,T]$, and let $X=(X^\tau)$ be an $n$-dimensional branched rough path on interval $[S,T]$ with regularity $p$ and control $\omega$. Let $Y: [S,T]\to U$ be a continuous curve in $U$ and let $f_\tau^i:U\to\Rsf$ (for $\tau\in\Fcal_n^2$ and $i\in\llbracket 1,m \rrbracket$) be smooth functions. Assume that there exists $C\in (0,\infty)$ such that the inequality 
	\begin{equation}
	
		\bigg| 
			Y^i(t) - Y^i(s) 
			- f_{\ta}^i(Y(s)) X^{\ta}(s,t) 
			- \frac{1}{2} f_{\tab}^i(Y(s)) X^{\tab}(s,t) 
			- f_{\tc}^i(Y(s)) X^{\tc}(s,t) 
		\bigg| 
		\leq C \omega(s,t)^\frac{3}{p}
	\end{equation}
holds for every $i\in\llbracket 1,m \rrbracket$ and $(s,t)\in\Delta[S,T]$. Then there is a constant $\widetilde{C}\in (0,\infty)$ such that 
	\[
		\bigg|
			\phi^i(Y(t)) - \phi^i(Y(s)) 
			- g^i_{\ta}(Y(s))X^{\ta}(s,t) 
			- \frac{1}{2} g^i_{\tab}(Y(s)) X^{\tab}(s,t) 
			- g^i_{\tc}(Y(s))X^{\tc}(s,t) 
		\bigg| 
		\leq \widetilde{C}\omega(s,t)^\frac{3}{p},
	\]
where 
	\[
		g^i_{\ta} := \frac{\partial\phi^i}{\partial y^j}f_{\ta}^j, 
			\quad 
		g_{\tab}^i := \frac{\partial\phi^i}{\partial y^j}f_{\tab}^j + \frac{\partial^2 \phi^i}{\partial y^j\partial y^k} f_{\ta}^jf_{\tb}^k, 
			\quad\mbox{and}\quad  
		g_{\tc}^i := \frac{\partial\phi^i}{\partial y^j}f_{\tc}^j,
	\]
holds for every $i\in \llbracket 1,\ell \rrbracket$ and $(s,t)\in\Delta[S,T]$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:25:44.986147+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_40df6458036c9ad2e1b649072df73239baccefc93ec24a82ca372e1787cf05b3","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 7 (Pathwise convergence of threshold-separated jump atoms) of arXiv:2605.11783, 'Stability of Compensated Jump Integrals under Quadratic Variation Convergence'] Let $X$ and $\{X^n\}_{n\ge1}$ be c\`adl\`ag processes on $[0,t]$ such that
\[
[X^n-X]_t \to 0
\qquad \text{a.s.}.
\]

Let \(f_n\) and \(f\) be predictable functions on \(\Omega\times[0,t]\times\mathbb R\). Assume that there exists a set
\(\Omega_0\in\mathcal F\) with \(\mathbb P(\Omega_0)=1\) such that, for every
\(\omega\in\Omega_0\), every \(s\leq t\), and every compact set
\(K\subset\mathbb R\),
\[
        \sup_{x\in K}|f_n(s,x,\omega)-f(s,x,\omega)|\to0 .
\]

Fix \(r>0\), \(k\ge1\), \(a>0\), and let \(s\le t\). Assume moreover that
\[
        f(s,\cdot,\omega)
        \text{ is continuous at }\Delta X_s(\omega)
        \qquad\text{a.s.}
\]

\[
1_{A_k(r)}
\left(
\int_{L(r,k)<|x|\le a} f_{n}(s,x)\,\mu_{n}(\{s\},dx)
-
\int_{L(r,k)<|x|\le a} f_{n}(s,x)\,\mu(\{s\},dx)
\right)
\longrightarrow 0
\]
almost surely on the event
\[
        \{(\Delta X)^*_t<a\}.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Fixed L>0 and eta>0; deterministic square X with operator norm at most L.","Independent standard Gaussian feature-weight vectors; coordinates of the resulting ReLU column need not be independent.","Each symmetric R_j excludes w_j from its measurability and has norm at most 1/eta.","Any auxiliary randomness is independent of all Gaussian feature weights.","Random-input extension requires independence from feature weights and a tight input norm; only convergence in probability is claimed there.","Owner-work proof (unaudited), w737 T385-C13 v1; no independent PASS or novelty claim."],"created_at":"2026-10-21T17:02:46.507882+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory; nonlinear random features; conditional concentration","id":"claim_40f4831c7471e288197440d464ad019ecdc928316db1ec18bf8e195faef67995","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own-work METHOD DRAFT; proof (unaudited), attributed to w737 T385-C13 v1; no independent PASS or novelty claim. Fix L>0 and eta>0. For each n let X be a deterministic real n by n matrix with operator norm at most L, and w_1,...,w_n independent N(0,I_n) vectors. Put h_j=ReLU(Xw_j), mu=E h_j, z_j=h_j-mu, Phi=E[h_j h_j^T], and Sigma=E[z_j z_j^T]. Let R_j be real symmetric, measurable in X and the columns w_k with k!=j (and optionally auxiliary randomness independent of all feature weights), with operator norm at most 1/eta almost surely. The recorded unaudited derivation gives, for each fixed epsilon>0, P(max_j |z_j^T R_j z_j/n-Tr(Sigma R_j)/n|>epsilon)<=C n exp[-c n min(epsilon^2,epsilon)], with C,c depending only on L,eta. The centering step uses the exact identity z^T R z-Tr(Sigma R)=h^T R h-Tr(Phi R)-2 mu^T R(h-mu) for deterministic symmetric R. Louart-Liao-Couillet quadratic-form concentration controls the raw term. Gaussian Lipschitz concentration controls the mean correction. Indeed mu_i=||x_i||/sqrt(2 pi), ||mu||^2<=n L^2/(2 pi), and w->mu^T R ReLU(Xw) is Lipschitz with constant at most sqrt(n/(2 pi))*L^2/eta. Condition on all columns except j before applying those bounds; integrate and take a union bound, without asserting independence between deviation events. Thus the method allows correlations among coordinates within each feature column, but R_j must exclude the tested column. For X=I and eta=1, taking the same-column R=zz^T/||z||^2 makes z^T R z/n tend to kappa=1/2-1/(2 pi)>0 while Tr(Sigma R)/n=kappa/n, illustrating failure if this independence hypothesis is removed. For random X independent of all w_j with tight operator norm, conditioning first on ||X||<=L and then letting L grow gives convergence in probability, rather than a uniform unconditional exponential rate. This is a fixed-positive-ridge concentration ingredient; it supplies neither an edge law nor a justification for a ridge tending to zero. {"assumptions":["A measurable, uniformly parabolic with constants lambda, Lambda (no continuity assumed)","divergence form (the analogous statement for nondivergence form with merely measurable coefficients is a different theory)","s < t; for equations with lower-order terms or on a finite time interval, constants also depend on T and those bounds"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:49.106308+00:00","domain":"parabolic partial differential equations / heat kernel estimates","id":"claim_410506486d1fb1210e085fe9677cd4acaa4ae438a0aa72b12c79fd1a43a41833","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $A(x,t)$ be real measurable on $\\mathbb R^n\\times\\mathbb R$ and uniformly parabolic with constants $0<\\lambda\\le\\Lambda<\\infty$, and consider $\\partial_tu=\\mathrm{div}(A(x,t)\\nabla u)$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:47:22.245900+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_414774552018474bc5ee76321ba5e7b66cb73ff5fb105f49125c1862c38a7ec9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 19 of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] [Liquid and frozen region, arctic boundary]
  Given any open set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, we call a function $F : \overline{\Omega} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ \emph{admissible} if $F$ is $1$-Lipschitz and satisfies $\nabla F (z) \in \overline{\mathcal{T}}$ for Lebesgue almost every $z \in \Omega$. Let $\Adm (\Omega)$ denote the set of admissible functions $F : \overline{\Omega} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ and, for any function $f : \partial \Omega \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, let $\Adm (\Omega; f)$ denote the set of $F \in \Adm (\Omega)$ satisfying $F |_{\partial \Omega} = f$.  Define the \emph{liquid region} $\mathfrak{L}_F \subseteq \Omega$ associated with an admissible height function $F \in \Adm (\Omega)$ by 
         \begin{flalign*}
         	\mathfrak{L}_F = \big\{ z \in \Omega : \nabla F(z) \in \mathcal{T} \big\},
         \end{flalign*}
         where the condition $\nabla F(z) \in \mathcal{T}$ in particular implies that $\nabla F(z)$ exists.

         In particular, we define the liquid region of $\cH_{q;a,b,c}$ as
         \[\mL_{q;a,b,c}:=\mL_{\cH_{q;a,b,c}}.\] The  boundary
        $\mathfrak A_{q;a,b,c}:=\partial\mL_{q;a,b,c}$ is called the
        \emph{arctic boundary} and the interior of
        $\mX_{a,b,c}\setminus\mL_{q;a,b,c}$ is called the \emph{frozen
        region}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:49:02.096739+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_414a97805c7e430b40375305988af74d41a912c17b76a4b851a0137fd760c3b6","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 4 (Uniform subcritical occupancy lower tail) of arXiv:2604.26298, 'The Expiring Coupon Collector\\ Sliding-Window Surjection Flux and Rare-Entry Laws'] Let \(N\ge2\) and \(m\ge N\). \[

Consequently, in any range where \(N\le m\le 2N\log N\) and

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:42:55.304202+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_416178e9b7854cdc3f8b65789b3bda628a0ffef147f9fc83f2ab191519fe9485","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2609.02381, '\bfseries Viscosity Supersolution Barriers to a\\ Non-local Free Boundary Problem'] Let $\nu(dz)$ be a L\'evy measure on $\mathbb{R}_0$ with finite
large-jump intensity
$\lambda:=\nu(\{|z|>1\})<\infty.$
Let for given constant $M>0$ holds
\[
r+\rho<\sqrt{\lambda}\,M,
\;\;
\text{and set}
\;\;
\beta:=\sqrt{\lambda}\,M-(r+\rho)>0.
\]
Fix a uniform linear-growth ceiling constant $C_{\max}>0$. Suppose that
there exist $\tau\in(0,T)$ and $\alpha_*>0$ such that
$\alpha(t)\geq\alpha_*,\;\; t\in[0,\tau].$
Then whenever $\tau$ satisfies
\[
\tau>T_{\mathrm{crit}}
:=
\frac{1}{\beta}
\log\left(\frac{C_{\max}}{\alpha_*}\right),
\]
there exists an admissible jump amplitude $\gamma_*$, with
$L^2(\nu)$-Lipschitz constant $M$, for which there is no
nonnegative lower semicontinuous function
$v^T:\mathbb{R}\times[0,T]\to[0,\infty)$
satisfying the uniform linear-growth bound
\begin{equation}
v^T(g,t)
\leq
C_{\max}(1+|g|),
\qquad
(g,t)\in\mathbb{R}\times[0,T],
\end{equation}
that simultaneously satisfies the obstacle inequality
\begin{equation}
v^T(g,t)-v^T(-g,t)
\geq
\alpha(t)g-c,
\qquad
(g,t)\in\mathbb{R}\times(0,T),
\end{equation}
and the viscosity supersolution inequality for the
integro-differential operator on
$\mathbb{R}\times(0,T)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:09:49.789590+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_416319867a415b3e4440661e19d2a2cd8c3fbb73ef7a3697a7f003d16faa1830","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 16 of arXiv:2609.03061, '2609.03061'] Let $f: [a,b] \rightarrow Sp(2n,\mathbb{R})$ be a smooth symplectic path

$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:51:11.642922+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_41867b6ffc4e606ea6ca570f50de6b669a09e637bf97eaf0aa141f9bcdacef34","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 10 of arXiv:2605.31471, 'Convergence Rates of Continuous-Time Random Walks to Time-Fractional Diffusions with Unbou'] Consider the SDE \eqref{eq:SDE-flow}.  
    Let Assumption~\ref{asm:classical} (items \emph{(1)}–\emph{(2)}) hold.  
    Assume that $\nabla \sigma_j(x)$ is well-defined and (globally) $\alpha$-H\"older continuous for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and all $j = 0, \dots, d$.
    Then the process $\nabla X_t(x)$ is well-defined and is locally $\beta$-H\"older continuous in $x$, almost surely, for any $\beta < \alpha$. Furthermore, it is the unique strong solution of the SDE
    \begin{equation}
        
        \nabla X_t(x)
        =
        e
        + \int_0^t \bigl(\nabla b\bigl(X_s(x)\bigr)\bigr)\,\nabla X_s(x)\,ds
        + \sum_{l=1}^d \int_0^t
            \bigl(\nabla \sigma_l\bigl(X_s(x)\bigr)\bigr)\,\nabla X_s(x)\,dW_s^l,
    \end{equation}
    where $e[u] = u$ is the identity mapping on $X$.  
    Moreover, for every $u \in X$ and $p \ge 2$ we have
    $\nabla X_t(x)[u] \in L^p$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:32:23.740632+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_41918c410806fda3d6ce81068e83f01a2801742dd5d07ae6173c787e38cd6ca1","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:rw_reset of arXiv:2603.24803, 'Critical Spectral Invariants in Random Walks with Geometric Resetting'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ be a probability space. 
Fix $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and $z \in \{1,\dots,a-1\}$. 
Let $\{X_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be a discrete-time stochastic process on 
$\{0,1,\dots,a\}$ with initial condition $X_0=z$.

Let $\{\xi_n\}_{n\ge1}$ be i.i.d.\ random variables, independent of 
everything else, with
\[
\mathbb{P}(\xi_n=+1)=p, 
\qquad 
\mathbb{P}(\xi_n=-1)=q=1-p.
\]

Let $\{\sigma_i\}_{i\ge1}$ be i.i.d.\ geometric random variables with 
parameter $\gamma\in(0,1)$, supported on $\{1,2,\dots\}$:
\[
\mathbb{P}(\sigma_i=k)=\gamma(1-\gamma)^{k-1}, 
\qquad k\ge1,
\]
independent of $\{\xi_n\}$. Define reset times recursively by
\[
\mathbf{t}_0:=0,
\qquad
\mathbf{t}_i := \sum_{j=1}^{i} \sigma_j,
\quad i\ge1.
\]

Then the process evolves according to
\[
X_n =
\begin{cases}
z, & \text{if } n \in \{\mathbf{t}_i\}_{i\ge1}, \\[6pt]
X_{n-1}+\xi_n, & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad n\ge1,
\]
and is absorbed upon first hitting $0$ or $a$. Equivalently, at each 
step the walker resets to $z$ with probability $\gamma$ or performs a 
standard biased step with probability $1-\gamma$, independently of its 
current position.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:58:24.517792+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_41972e9ed8015667e3a3972ce60e41e80c077340540e51900ed17f6025a7f316","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition p:exp.mu.n of arXiv:2601.12677, 'Stable and Fréchet limit theorem for subgraph functionals in the hyperbolic random geometr'] Let $\gamma\in \big(\frac{1}{2\alpha},1\big)$. \\
$(i)$ We have, uniformly for $u \in (0,{\gamma R_n})$, 
$$

where $s_n:= B_\alpha^{-1} n^{-(2\alpha-1)(1-\gamma)} e^{\alpha(d-1)\omega_n}$. \\

$$ 
where $\omega_n :=\log \log R_n$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:24:34.434712+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_41c0ef337c94882e1629039d57e8e6766e72a2c8faf0ac9bcff881bb474e114f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.31164, 'The anisotropic Michael-Simon inequality'] Let $\mu_j, \mu \in \cM( \Omega; \bR^d)$ be vector-valued measures on an open set $\Omega \subset \bR^n$ that converge strictly, $\mu_j \to \mu$, meaning that $\mu_j \xrightharpoonup{*} \mu$ and $|\mu_j|(\Omega) \to |\mu|(\Omega)$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:41:33.837341+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_41c1936c42a7679c8a617b0bee9c08bfc5b11892e62db440d7aa1dc1dd680f66","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 2 of arXiv:2604.11489, '2604.11489'] Assume that the function $g:[0,1] \to \rr$ is differentiable and its derivative $g'$ is $\beta$-H\"{o}lder

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:34:20.780009+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_41cd2300a2a073ce60979588e0272bc6983b0642af310c90e01c3f18e131e145","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi 3 of arXiv:2609.02261, 'Quantization and process'] For each $h>0$,  the space

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:36:23.133324+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_41cd9b2b5f78b947af8b1415d28649431c853fabec721cda6709304fb6731d3b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem AnaLem of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $N\geqslant2$ be a given fixed integer. Suppose
that $S_{n}(a_{1},\cdots,a_{n})=0$ for all $n\leqslant N-1$ and
all non-degenerate sequences $(a_{1},\cdots,a_{n})$ with $a_{j}\in2\pi i\mathbb{Z}$.
Let $(b_{1}^{*},\cdots,b_{N}^{*})$ be a fixed non-degenerate sequence
with $b_{j}\in2\pi i\mathbb{Z}$. Given $w\in\mathbb{C}$, we define
the path development $F_{w}:\mathbb{C}^{2}\rightarrow\mathfrak{sl}_{N+1}(\mathbb{C})$

[A_{w},E_{k,k+1}]=(b_{k}^{*}+w)E_{k,k+1}\ \ \ (k=1,\cdots,N).

Then for any vector $K=(k_{1},\cdots,k_{n})$ satisfying $|K|=N,n\geqslant2$ or $|K|\leqslant N-1,n\geqslant1$ and any $j=1,\cdots,N,$ there exists a meromorphic function $\Psi_{K,j}:\mathbb{C}^{|K|}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$
(i.e. the quotient of two holomorphic functions) in $|K|$ complex variables,
such that 
\[
\hat{F}_{w}(H_{K})=\sum_{j}\Psi_{K,j}(b_{j}^{*}+w,\cdots,b_{j+|K|-1}^{*}+w)E_{j,j+|K|}
\]
and the function $w\mapsto\Psi_{K,j}(b_{j}^{*}+w,\cdots,b_{j+|K|-1}^{*}+w)$
is analytic in a neighbourhood of $w=0$ for all $(K,j)$. Here $\hat{F}_{w}$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:01:39.423732+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_41ec281780e228555015ad321135da7c10041d8812e04a31bc646c231f823757","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:max_lh of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Assume that $\mu$ is critical and belongs to the domain of attraction of a stable law.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]  Assume that $\mu_{1}>0$. There exists a constant $C_{\mu}>0$ such that the following holds. Set
$$k^*_{n} =  \frac{1}{\log(1/\mu_{1})}\log n +  \frac{1}{\log(1/\mu_{1})} \log\bigl((1-\mu_1)C_{\mu}\bigr).$$
Then for every $t \in \mathbb{R}$ we have
\[
\P\bigl(\lambda(\mathcal{T}^n) \leq \lfloor k^*_{n} + t\rfloor\bigr) - \exp\bigl(-\mu_1^{t+1 - \{k^*_{n} + t\}}\bigr) \to 0.
\]
\item[(ii)] Assume that $\mu_{1}=0$. Set $\kappa = \min\{i \geq 2 : \mu_i > 0\}$. There exists a constant $D_{\mu} \in (0,1)$ such that the following holds. Set
$$
k_{n}^{**} \coloneqq  \log_\kappa \log n - \log_\kappa \log(1/D_{\mu}).
$$
 Write $m_n=\lfloor k_n^{**}\rfloor$ and
$\theta_n=\{k_n^{**}\}$, and define
$$
  J_n=
  \begin{cases}
    \{m_n-1,m_n\},&\theta_n\le\tfrac12,\\
    \{m_n,m_n+1\},&\theta_n>\tfrac12.
  \end{cases}
$$
Then $\P(\lambda(\mathcal T^n)\in J_n)\longrightarrow1$. In addition, if $\liminf_n\min(\theta_n,1-\theta_n)>0$, then
$\P(\lambda(\mathcal T^n)=m_n)\to1$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:41:33.837802+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_41f0ac2dc87f9493b558ac938b189efc7b69d3228f3992da9385b68aa984406e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 8 of arXiv:2604.11489, '2604.11489'] \cite{C-S}
 Let $X_1, X_2, \cdots, X_n$ be independent and not necessarily identically distributed random variables with zero means and finite variances. Define $W=\sum_{k=1}^nX_k$ and assume that $Var(W)=1$. Let $F$ be the distribution function of $W$ and $\Phi$ be the standard normal distribution function. Then there exists an absolute constant $C$ such that for every real number $x$,
 $$

 Furthermore, we have

 $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:08.837281+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_41f0e308989b80a243e75480709f0bf7e5e8fba6621915831fc762a3a8377a65","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 ({\cite[Definition~3.3) of arXiv:2511.09930, 'Martingale dimensions for a class of metric measure spaces'] {Hi10}}]
The \emph{AF-martingale dimension} $d_{\mathrm{m}}$ of $\bfM$ or of $(\cE,\cF)$ is the smallest number $d$ such that, there exist $d$ elements $M^{(1)},M^{(2)},\dots,M^{(d)}$ in $\maruM$ such that each $M\in\maruM$ is expressed as
\[
M=\sum_{i=1}^d (\ph^{(i)}\bullet M^{(i)})
\]
for some $\ph^{(i)}\in L^2(K,\mu_{\la M^{(i)}\ra})$, $i=1,2,\dots,d$.
If such a number does not exist, $d_{\mathrm{m}}$ is defined as $\infty$. Moreover, $d_{\mathrm{m}}$ is defined as $0$ if $\maruM=\{0\}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-12T07:22:43.761193+00:00","domain":"graph theory","id":"claim_41f1607fe0ca61747b32e0ca370c278bba715b149e9ab306a7f07d7712059878","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"A graph G = (V, E) is a finite set V of vertices together with a set E of edges, each an unordered pair of vertices; G is simple if it has no loops or repeated edges. A subgraph uses a subset of the vertices and edges. The degree of a vertex is the number of incident edges, and the handshake lemma gives sum of degrees = 2|E|. A walk is a vertex-edge alternation; a path has distinct vertices, a cycle is a closed path, and G is connected if every two vertices are joined by a path. Standard families: the complete graph K_n (all pairs adjacent), a tree (connected and acyclic, with |V|-1 edges), and a bipartite graph (vertices two-colorable so every edge crosses, equivalently no odd cycle). The vertex connectivity kappa(G) and edge connectivity lambda(G) are the least numbers of vertices, respectively edges, whose deletion disconnects G (or reduces it to a single vertex), and kappa(G) <= lambda(G) <= min-degree.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X and Y are Banach spaces","T is linear on a linear subspace D(T) of X"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.769166+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, unbounded operators","id":"claim_41fdcf41b301c72abeac970dc8d13d7e8412473ffc482e2582494edf964e1f49","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X, Y be Banach spaces and T: D(T) ⊂ X → Y a linear operator defined on a linear subspace D(T). Its graph is G(T) = {(x, Tx) : x ∈ D(T)} ⊂ X × Y. T is closed if G(T) is closed in X × Y; equivalently, whenever x_n ∈ D(T), x_n → x in X and Tx_n → y in Y, then x ∈ D(T) and Tx = y. Equivalently, D(T) is complete under the graph norm ‖x‖_T = ‖x‖ + ‖Tx‖. S is an extension of T (written T ⊂ S) if D(T) ⊂ D(S) and Sx = Tx for x ∈ D(T). T is closable if it has a closed extension; equivalently, x_n ∈ D(T), x_n → 0 and Tx_n → y imply y = 0; equivalently, the closure of G(T) is the graph of an operator, called the closure T̄ (the smallest closed extension). If T is closed, a subspace D_0 ⊂ D(T) is a core for T if D_0 is dense in D(T) for the graph norm, i.e. the closure of T restricted to D_0 equals T. A closed operator need not be bounded, and being closed says nothing about D(T) being dense; by the closed graph theorem a closed operator with D(T) = X is bounded.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:05:28.288360+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_420722dc116f181d46e5bc21306e109b458d7c36b99d78c0b5c3070b02f4d9cf","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop boundconditionalmoment of arXiv:2602.08739, '\large \bf MOMENTS OF C$\beta$E FIELD PARTITION FUNCTION, $\mathsf{Sine}_{\beta}$ CORRELAT'] For $p \geq 2$, let $(\theta_m)_{1 \leq m \leq p}\in \mathbb{R}^p$, $(s_m)_{1 \leq m \leq p}\in\mathbb{R}_+^p$,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.234804+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_420a645d67dbdf8ce3464524c57609ebb234e7624abad9039ffdf8e7717b360c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 42 (Coxeter orbit of the monomial physical contour) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] In the adjacent basis of
\cref{cor:monomial-Gaussian-Betti-row}, let \(M_m\) be the positive
Coxeter monodromy of the \(A_{m-1}\) sector fan, fixed by
\[
 M_m\Gamma_0=-\sum_{j=0}^{m-2}\Gamma_j,
 \qquad
 M_m\Gamma_j=\Gamma_{j-1}
 \quad(1\leq j\leq m-2).
\]
Then
\[
 \chi_{M_m}(\lambda)=\frac{\lambda^m-1}{\lambda-1}.
\]
For the physical class
\[
 r_m=[\R]=-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}\Gamma_j,

\]
one has
\begin{equation}

For even \(m\), the missing dimension equals the dimension of the
parity-odd Jacobi sector.  Thus the Betti orbit rank agrees numerically

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.349563+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4227cc72423df9e86220706666cf0c5942ecb93c47543ebc0343a142107821ab","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 171 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let indices $a(q_d),a^\frozen(q_d)$
