{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:17:42.310674+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_46371440f6d526c2e361b3e41113e2f0d6c8a3e2a9f3208cbc2c21f992a0c1fc","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 9 (Hermite Process) of arXiv:2607.23548, '\textbf{A CIR-Type Diffusion Driven by Hermite Processes:\\ Well-Posedness, Positivity and'] Let $q \geq 1$ be an integer and $H \in \bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}, 1\bigr)$.
Set
\[
H_0 := 1 + \frac{H-1}{q} \in \Bigl(1 - \frac{1}{2q},\, 1\Bigr),
\qquad
c(H,q) := \sqrt{\frac{H(2H-1)}{q!\,\beta^q\!\left(H_0 - \tfrac{1}{2},\,
2 - 2H_0\right)}},
\]
where $\beta$ denotes the Beta function.
The \emph{Hermite process of order $q$ and self-similarity parameter $H$}
is the stochastic process $Z^{(q,H)} = \{Z_t^{(q,H)}\}_{t \geq 0}$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:37:51.448057+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4644690746dedca24d0f126ee0abec939bb760d6e2b37cc68e44c74db916ee3b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 4 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] ~
	
	\begin{enumerate}[font=\normalfont,label=(\roman*)]
		\item A $\mathrm{W}^*$-probability space $(\cA,\tau) $ is a unital von Neumann algebra $\cA$ (with operator norm $\norm{\cdot}$) endowed with a faithful, normal, tracial state $\tau \colon \cA \to \C$, i.e., a $\sigma$-WOT--continuous linear map $\tau \colon \cA \to \C$ satisfying $\tau(1_{\cA})=1$, $\tau(ab) = \tau(ba)$ for all $a,b \in \cA$, and $\tau(a^*a)\geq 0$ for all $a\in \cA$, with equality if and only if $a=0$.
        An element of $\cA$ is called a (noncommutative) random variable.
		\item Unital $\ast$-subalgebras $\cA_1,\dots,\cA_n$ of $\cA$ are said to be freely independent, or free for short, if for all $k \in \N$ and all $a_1\in\cA_{j_1},\ldots,a_k \in \cA_{j_k}$ such that $j_1\neq j_2, j_2\neq j_3,\ldots,j_{k-1}\neq j_k$,
		\begin{equation}
			
			\tau\Big( (a_1-\tau(a_1))(a_2-\tau(a_2))\dots (a_k-\tau(a_k)) \Big) = 0.
		\end{equation}
		Families of noncommutative random variables are said to be free if the $\ast$-subalgebras they generate are free. Note, in particular, that if $X$ and $Y$ are free, then
		\begin{equation}
			
			\tau(XY)=\tau(X)\tau(Y).
		\end{equation}

        \item Write $\C \la \cB \ra$ for the free unital $\C$-algebra on the set $\cB$, i.e., the set of noncommutative (complex) polynomials in the indeterminates $X = (X_e)_{e \in \cB}$.
        Two families $x=(x_e)_{e \in \cB} \in \cA^{\cB}$ and $y=(y_e)_{e \in \cB} \in \cA^{\cB}$ of noncommutative random variables are said to have the same noncommutative law or distribution if for all $P \in \C\la \cB \ra$,
        $$ \tau(P(x)) = \tau(P(y)).$$
		
		\item A family $x = (x_e)_{e \in \cB}$ of noncommutative random variables is called 
		a free semicircular system when the noncommutative random variables are free, 
		$x_e$ is self-adjoint (i.e., $x_e=x_e^*$) for all $e \in \cB$, and for all $k \in \N$ and all $e \in \cB$,
        $$
		\tau( x_e^k) = \begin{cases}
		    c_{\frac{k}{2}} & \mbox{if } k \text{ is even}, \\
			0 & \text{otherwise,}
		\end{cases}
		$$
		where $c_n$ is the $n^{\text{th}}$ Catalan number for all $n \in \N$.
        See \cite[Proposition 7.15]{nica_speicher} for a construction of such a system.
	\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

Then

 \|q\|_{C^{k+1+\sigma,(k+1+\sigma)/2}(Q')}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:30:36.772745+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_46a3001bce2720e474498d82a1d9875b18f43e76411057bfc044b296c715704d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 17 of arXiv:2607.10102, 'Dynamical mean-field limit and replica-symmetric free energy for the orthogonally-invarian'] Suppose there exists a (deterministic or random) initial state $\btheta^0$ for
which Assumptions \ref{assump:X} and \ref{assump:dynamics} hold with $f=-U'$.
Suppose that the bound $\alpha>0$ in
\eqref{eq:Uconvexity} satisfies
\begin{equation}
\alpha>\Lambda_{\max},
\qquad \alpha>\sum_{p \geq 1}|\kappa_{p+1}|
\left(\frac{1}{n}\langle \|\btheta\|_2^2 \rangle
-\frac{1}{n}\langle \btheta^\top \btheta' \rangle+\eps\right)^p
\end{equation}
almost surely for all large $n$ and some constant $\eps>0$.
Suppose that Assumption \ref{assump:convergence} holds for this initial state
$\btheta^0$.

For any $v \geq q \geq 0$ such that the R-transform series
\begin{equation}
\cR_\Lambda(x)=\sum_{p \geq 1} \kappa_{p+1}x^p
\end{equation}
is absolutely convergent in a neighborhood of $v-q$ and $q\cR_\Lambda'(v-q) \geq 0$, define
the probability density on $\R$
\begin{equation}
\mu(\theta \mid v,q,\xi)
\propto
\exp\left(-U(\theta)+\frac{1}{2}\cR_\Lambda(v-q)\theta^2+\sqrt{q\cR_\Lambda'(v-q)}\,\xi\theta\right).
\end{equation}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item There exist deterministic almost-sure limits
\begin{equation}
v_*=\lim_{n \to \infty}\frac{1}{n}\langle \|\btheta\|_2^2 \rangle,
\qquad q_*=\lim_{n \to \infty}\frac{1}{n}\langle \btheta^\top \btheta' \rangle
\end{equation}
satisfying the above conditions.
These solve the fixed-point equations
\begin{equation}
v_*=\E_{\xi \sim \cN(0,1)}
\langle \theta^2 \rangle_{v_*,q_*,\xi},
\qquad q_*=\E_{\xi \sim \cN(0,1)} \langle \theta \rangle_{v_*,q_*,\xi}^2
\end{equation}
where $\langle \cdot \rangle_{v,q,\xi}$ denotes the expectation under
$\mu(\cdot \mid v,q,\xi)$. Furthermore, almost surely
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n}\langle \btheta^\top \X\btheta\rangle
=v_*\cR_\Lambda(v_*-q_*)+q_*(v_*-q_*)\cR_\Lambda'(v_*-q_*).
\end{equation}
For any function $f:\R \to \R$ satisfying
$|f(x)-f(y)| \leq C(1+|x|+|y|)|x-y|$ for some $C>0$, almost surely

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:45:27.985329+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_46ae2c73055ca97411583101424ee84abc3f8de58ed19fb1be9294846ccd3cc1","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:admissible_classes of arXiv:2607.04514, 'Boundary-layer asymptotics for Gaussian-smoothed singular measures'] Let \(\ell\in\mathbb N\) and \(\omega>0\). Fix \(A,\sigma_0>0\) and \(R\in(0,\infty]\).

  \begin{enumerate}
    \item A function \(B:\overline{\mathbb B}_A\times \mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\times (0,\sigma_0]\to\mathbb
    R\) belongs to \(\mathfrak B_\ell\) if its pullback \( B(a,\varphi (\theta),\sigma)\) is
    \(C^\ell\) in \((a,\theta, \sigma)\) and, for every \(\gamma\) with \(|\gamma| \leqslant \ell\),
    \begin{equation*}
      \sup_{{\mathcal D}_{A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},\sigma_0}} \bigl| \partial_{a,\theta,\sigma}^{\gamma}
      B(a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma) \bigr|<\infty.
    \end{equation*}

    \item A function \(E:\overline{\mathbb B}_A \times\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\times (0,\sigma_0]\to\mathbb
    R\) belongs to \(\mathfrak E_\ell^\omega\) if its pullback \( E(a, \varphi (\theta),\sigma)\) is
    \(C^\ell\) in \((a, \theta, \sigma)\), and there exists \(c>0\) such that, for every \(\gamma\)
    with \(|\gamma|\leqslant\ell\), there is a constant \(C_\gamma>0\) satisfying
    \begin{equation*}
      \bigl|\partial_{a,\theta,\sigma}^{ \gamma} E(a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma) \bigr|
      \leqslant C_\gamma e^{-c/\sigma^{\omega}},\quad
      \forall (a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma)\in {\mathcal D}_{A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}, \sigma_0}.
    \end{equation*}

    \item A function \(P: \mathcal D_{R, A, \mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}, \sigma_0} \to\mathbb R\) belongs to
    \(\mathfrak P_\ell \) if it is measurable in \(\zeta\) and its pullback
    \(P(\zeta;a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma)\) is \(C^\ell\) in the
    parameter variables \((a,\theta, \sigma)\), for every fixed \(\zeta\), and there exists
    \(n\geqslant 0\) such that
    \begin{equation*}
      \bigl| \partial_{a,\theta,\sigma}^{\gamma} P(\zeta; a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma) \bigr|
      \leqslant C_\gamma \bigl(1 + \|\zeta\|^n\bigr)
    \end{equation*}
    for every \(\gamma\) with \(|\gamma|\leqslant\ell\), uniformly on \(\mathcal D_{R, A,
    \mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}, \sigma_0} \).

    \item A function \(G: \mathcal D_{R, A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}, \sigma_0} \to\mathbb R\) belongs to
    \(\mathfrak G_\ell\) if it is measurable in \(\zeta\) and its pullback
    \(G(\zeta;a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma)\) is \(C^\ell\) in the
    parameter variables \((a,\theta,\sigma) \), for every fixed \(\zeta\), and there exist \(c_0>0,
    n\geqslant 0\) such that
    \begin{equation*}
      \bigl| \partial_{a,\theta,\sigma}^{\gamma} G(\zeta;a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma) \bigr|
      \leqslant C_\gamma\bigl(1+\|\zeta\|^n\bigr)\Gamma_{c_0}(\zeta;a)
    \end{equation*}
    for every \(\gamma\) with \(|\gamma|\leqslant\ell\), uniformly on \({\mathcal
    D}_{R,A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},\sigma_0}\).
  \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:06:55.300741+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_46c9778b2efb1908cf84ed79ba4ae9622858ae4793c8a02dc759c7359d0933e4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:global-drift of arXiv:2602.19192, 'Bakry--\'Emery Curvature of the Fractional Laplacian\\ via Fractional Brownian Covariance'] At $\gamma = 1$, the Hermitianized drift correction satisfies
the scalar identity
\begin{equation}
  \Gamma_{L,2}(f,f)(x) - \Gamma_{1,2}(f,f)(x)
  = \frac{\omega^2}{2}\cos(x)\;\Gamma(f,f)(x)
\end{equation}
for all $f \in \mathcal{T}_N^+$ and all $x \in \mathbb{T}$.
Consequently, the eigenvalues of the curvature operator
$\Gamma^{-1}\Gamma_{L,2}$ on $\mathcal{T}_N^+$ are
\begin{equation}
  \kappa_k(x) = (2k-1) + \frac{\omega^2}{2}\cos x,
  \qquad k = 1,\ldots,N,
\end{equation}
and the global Bakry--\'Emery curvature is
\begin{equation}
  \kappa(1,\omega^2) = 1 - \frac{\omega^2}{2},
\end{equation}
independent of $N$, achieved at $x = \pi$.
Combined with the cross-sign vanishing
(Corollary~(cor:block-diag of the paper)), this extends to all real
trigonometric polynomials.

In particular, $\mathrm{CD}(1-\omega^2/2,\,\infty)$ holds for
$\omega^2 < 2$, with consequences:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Poincar\'e inequality:
  $\mathrm{Var}_\mu(f) \leq \frac{1}{1-\omega^2/2}\,\mathcal{E}_L(f,f)$.
\item Gradient estimate:
  $\Gamma(P_t^L f, P_t^L f)

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.595155+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_46cdc7bc266e3e06f6b15c8be1ef271da4ab8a6d64479f66d9b4287d0091f4c0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.02331, 'Metastability of Interacting Stochastic Systems with Countably Many Metastable States...'] Metastability is typically formulated for systems with finitely many metastable states, most often in positively recurrent settings. In this article, we extend the resolvent framework for metastability to Markov processes with countably many metastable states, thereby encompassing null-recurrent and transient dynamics. For a family of processes on locally compact Polish spaces, we prove, under a mild boundary regularity assumption, that the asymptotic flatness of microscopic resolvent solutions, supplemented by two compactness conditions, is equivalent to convergence in law of the projected trace processes to a limiting Markov chain and to the negligibility of the time spent outside the metastable sets. We apply this framework to two non-compact stochastic systems. First, we study a condensing inclusion process on a countably infinite, uniformly locally finite graph, in a setting where the process may be null recurrent or transient. We prove that the condensate location converges to a weighted random walk on the underlying graph, while the time spent away from the fully condensed configurations is negligible. Second, we study a small-noise one-dimensional Langevin diffusion with countably many stable equilibria, without assuming ergodicity. In the Eyring--Kramers time scale associated with the minimal energy barrier, we establish local equilibration inside each well, convergence of the well-index process to an explicit nearest-neighbor Markov chain on $\\mathbb{Z}$, and negligibility of inter-well excursions. Together, these results broaden the scope of resolvent-based metastability theory beyond finite metastable state spaces and positive recurrence.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:30:08.024516+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_46de119d1f8a743402242ee0461816559d22c35adb700374637705520b5bb0e5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:local-collision-pieces of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Fix a gadget record

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:55:37.821087+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_46fa7dc2594a9df9ad92274d857f68c927c98a5d4deb4f2dbf03c873922f2b89","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defstar of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] The boundary point $\Delta$ is classified as follows:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item \textbf{Entrance} if, when $X$ is started from $\Delta$, it leaves $\Delta$ and never returns almost surely. 
		Equivalently, $\Delta$ is non-absorbing and inaccessible from the interior.
		
		\item \textbf{Exit} if $X$ hits $\Delta$ with positive probability and, once there, remains at $\Delta$ forever. 
		That is, $\Delta$ is accessible and absorbing.
		
		\item \textbf{Regular} if $X$ hits $\Delta$ with positive probability and can subsequently leave it with positive probability; in other words, $\Delta$ is accessible and non-absorbing. Precisely, for any $x\in (0,\infty)$,
		\[
		\mathbb{P}_x\!\left(\exists\, 0 < s < t < \infty : X_s=\Delta \text{ and } X_t \neq \Delta \right) > 0.
		\]
		
		\item \textbf{Natural} if $\Delta$ is inaccessible and absorbing.
	\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:02:17.948678+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_46fbdf27eeeccf6153e3c6bd2c9df4650702a34ec591d5a85c183bee87cc84d5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:standard-couple of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and two distributions $\mathcal{D}$ and~$\mathcal{D}'$ on non-negative integers such that~$\mathcal{D} \gtrsim \mathcal{D}'$.
Let $X$ be the backoff process with 
send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and
birth distribution~$\mathcal{D}$ 
and let $X'$ be the backoff process with send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth distribution~$\mathcal{D}'$.
The \emph{\newsym{standard coupling}{standard coupling of two backoff processes}{\textrm{standard coupling}}} of~$X'$ and~$X$ has the following invariants for every $i\geq 0$ and $t\geq 0$.
\begin{description}  
\item  [Inv-$b_i(t)$:] $\mathbf{b}_i^{X'}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t)$.
\item  [Inv-$B_i(t)$:] $\mathbf{B}_i^{X'}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{B}_i^{X}(t)$.
\item [Inv-$s_i(t)$:] $\mathbf{s}_i^{X'}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{s}_i^{X}(t)$.
\end{description}
The coupling is defined as follows.
For each $i\geq 0$, $\mathbf{b}_i^{X'}(0) = \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(0) = \emptyset$, establishing Inv-$b_i(0)$.
 
For each positive integer~$t$, 
the coupling evolves as follows.
First,
the pair $(n^X(t),n^{X'}(t))$ is chosen from the joint distribution~$C$ from Definition~(def:phi of the paper), so that $n^X(t) \sim \mathcal{D}$, $n^{X'}(t) \sim \mathcal{D}'$ and $n^X(t) \geq n^{X'}(t)$.
Then for each $Z\in\{X',X\}$, the set $\mathbf{n}^Z(t)$
is defined according  to Definition~(def:backoffasgen of the paper). In particular, if
 $n^{Z}(t) = 0$ then $\mathbf{n}^{Z}(t) = \emptyset$. Otherwise, ${\mathbf{n}^Z(t)} = \{\mathcal{B}(t,0,1),\ldots,\mathcal{B}(t,0,n^Z(t))\}$.
For all $i\geq 0$, the sets
$\mathbf{B}^{X'}_i(t)$, $\mathbf{s}^{X'}_i(t)$,  
$\mathbf{e}^{X'}_i(t)$, $\mathbf{b}^{X'}_i(t)$, and $B^X_i(t)$ are chosen according to Definition~(def:backoffasgen of the paper).

Using Inv-$b_0(t-1)$, we get
$\mathbf{B}_0^{X'}(t) = \mathbf{n}^{X'}(t) \cup \mathbf{b}_0^{X'}(t-1) \subseteq
\mathbf{n}^{X}(t) \cup \mathbf{b}_0^{X}(t-1) = \mathbf{B}_0^{X}(t)$, 
establishing Inv-$B_0(t)$.
Also, 
for $i\geq 1$ 
using Inv-$b_i(t-1)$, we get $\mathbf{B}_i^{X'}(t) = \mathbf{b}_i^{X'}(t-1) \subseteq \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t-1) = \mathbf{B}_i^{X}(t)$, establishing Inv-$B_i(t)$

For every   $i\geq 0$, $\mathbf{S}^{X}_i(t)$ is formed by including each ball in 
$\mathbf{B}_i^{X}(t) \setminus \mathbf{B}_i^{X'}(t)$ 
independently with probability~$p_i$.
Then $\mathbf{s}^{X}_i(t) = \mathbf{S}^{X}_i(t) \cup \mathbf{s}^{X'}_i(t)$, establishing Inv-$s_i(t)$.

Finally, for every $i\geq 0$, $\mathbf{e}_i^{X}(t)$ and $\mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t)$ are chosen according to Definition~(def:backoffasgen of the paper).
The invariant Inv-$b_i(t)$ is established for all $i\geq 0$ as follows.  Fix $i$ and consider   a ball $\beta \in \mathbf{b}_i^{X'}(t)$. We wish to show $\beta \in \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t)$.
There are two possibilities.
\begin{itemize}
\item   $\beta \in \mathbf{B}_i^{X'}(t) \setminus \mathbf{s}_i^{X'}(t)$:  
In this case, by Inv-$B_i(t)$, $\beta \in \mathbf{B}_i^{X}(t)$. By construction,   $\beta\notin \mathbf{s}_i^{X}(t)$ so $\beta \in \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t)$.
\item (for $i\geq 1$) $\beta \in \mathbf{s}^{X'}_{i-1}(t) \setminus \mathbf{e}^{X'}_{i-1}(t)$:
From Definition~(def:backoffasgen of the paper), $s^{X'}(t) \geq 2$, By
Inv-$s_{i-1}(t)$, $\beta \in \mathbf{s}^{X}_{i-1}(t)$. By all of the constraints Inv-$s_k(t)$, $s^{X}(t) \geq s^{X'}(t) \geq 2$ so $e^{X}_{i-1}(t) = \emptyset$ and
$\beta \in \mathbf{s}^{X}_{i-1}(t) \setminus \mathbf{e}^{X}_{i-1}(t)$ which implies
$\beta \in \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t)$.
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:04:30.575748+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_470d5703d48475a9500dd597ce7e819e30bdc883d8db03867e70ccd88f5b0857","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn of arXiv:2411.10318, 'Polynomial Mixing of the critical Glauber Dynamics for the Ising Model'] \begin{itemize}
\item 
Let $G$ be a graph on a vertex set $V$. The Ising model on this graph with inverse temperature $\beta$ and external field $h:V\to[-\infty,\infty]$ is the probability measure $\mu$ on $\{-1,1\}^V$ satisfying
$$\mu_{\beta,h}(\sigma)=\dfrac{1}{Z_{G,h}}\exp\left(\beta\sum\limits_{u\sim v}\sigma_u\sigma_v+\sum\limits_{v\in V}h(v)\sigma_v\right).$$
By $\mu_\beta$ we will just denote the Ising model with $h=0$.
\item
For a configuration $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^V$ and for some $i\in[n]$, let $\sigma^i$ be the configuration $\sigma$ in which we have flipped coordinate $i$. For two configurations $\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,1\}^V$, we write $\sigma\sim\tau$ if $\tau=\sigma^i$ for some $i\in[n]$. The Glauber Dynamics on $G$ is a Markov chain with transition probabilities, for $\sigma\neq\tau$, equal to
$$P_\beta(\sigma,\tau)=\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\mu_\beta(\tau)}{\mu_\beta(\sigma)+\mu_\beta(\tau)},\ \ \text{if}\ \ \sigma \sim \tau
\\ \\
0,\ \ \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}$$
\item
On the set of probability measures on $\{-1,1\}^n$, we define the \textbf{Total Variation Distance} between $\mu,\nu$ to be
$$\text{d}_{\text{TV}}(\mu,\nu):=\sup\limits_{A}|\mu(A)-\nu(A)|=\dfrac{1}{2}\sum\limits_{\sigma}|\mu(\sigma)-\nu(\sigma)|.$$
\item 
The mixing time of this Markov Chain is defined to be
$$t_{\beta,\text{mix}}(\varepsilon)=\inf\{t\ge0:\text{d}_{\text{TV}}(P_\beta^t\delta_{\sigma_0},\mu_\beta)\le\varepsilon,\ \forall\sigma_0\in\{-1,1\}^V\},$$
where $\delta_{\sigma_0}$ is the probability measure that gives mass 1 to $\sigma_0$. We set
$t_{\beta,\text{mix}}:=t_{\beta,\text{mix}}\left(1/4\right).$
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:50:44.859094+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_475acc9be61d65a6300e1279115608a88c064fad1862155f8dbf529ff1376318","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 3 (Capacity terminology) of arXiv:2607.16502, 'Asymptotic Behavior of Path Functionals for Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes at High Level'] Let \(E\subset\R\) be non-empty and compact.  A \emph{finite capacity} on
\(E\) (not necessarily normalized) is a set function \(\mu:\mathcal B(E)\to[0,\infty)\) such that
\(\mu(\emptyset)=0\) and \(\mu(A)\le\mu(B)\) whenever \(A\subset B\).  It is
\emph{regular} if, for every Borel set \(A\subset E\),
\[
  \mu(A)
  =\sup\{\mu(K):K\subset A,\ K\text{ compact}\}
  =\inf\{\mu(U):A\subset U,\ U\text{ relatively open in }E\}.
\]
It is \emph{convex} (equivalently, supermodular) if
\[
  \mu(A\cup B)+\mu(A\cap B)\ge\mu(A)+\mu(B),
  \qquad A,B\in\mathcal B(E).
\]
Its support is the closed set
\[
  \supp\mu
  =\{t\in E:\mu(U)>0\text{ for every relatively open neighbourhood }U\ni t\}.
\]
We say that \(\mu\) has the \emph{support-intersection property} if
\[
  \mu(U)>0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  U\cap\supp\mu\ne\emptyset
\]
for every relatively open \(U\subset E\).  This property implies
\(\mu(E\setminus\supp\mu)=0\), but for a non-additive capacity it need not imply
\(\mu(\supp\mu)=\mu(E)\); the latter equality will be called the property that
the support \emph{carries full capacity}.  We say that the capacity has
\emph{full support} if \(\supp\mu=E\).

A capacity \(\nu\) on the Borel subsets of \(\R\), possibly taking the value
\(+\infty\), is \emph{locally finite} if \(\nu(K)<\infty\) for every compact
\(K\subset\R\).  For compact \(E\), its restriction \(\nu|_E\) is the capacity
on \(E\) given by \((\nu|_E)(A)=\nu(A)\), \(A\in\mathcal B(E)\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:38:04.500432+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_477541ad883ef49d43f01aca8c867359074991d8cc85015723916d6fcc2e6901","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:ht.coupling of arXiv:2607.12459, 'Renormalisation of Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] For $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$, let $F_\ell$ be the distribution function of $\hat X_I^{(\ell)}$, and let $F$ be the distribution function of $\sigma_\gamma Y$. Then the following hold:
 \begin{enumerate} 
\item[(i)] 
$F_\ell$ and $F$ are continuous distribution functions. 
\item[(ii)] 
If $U_I$, $I\in[N_{L-\ell}]$, are i.i.d.\ $\mathrm{UNIF}[0,1]$, then 
\[ 
\hat X_I^{(\ell)}=F_\ell^{\leftarrow}(U_I), \qquad \hat Y_I=\sigma_\gamma^{-1}F^{\leftarrow}(U_I), \qquad I\in[N_{L-\ell}], 
\] 
define two coupled families such that $\{\hat X_I^{(\ell)}\}_I$ is i.i.d.\ with the block-sum law above, while $\{\hat Y_I\}_I$ is i.i.d.\ with the standard positive $\gamma$-stable law. Here, 
\[ 
G^{\leftarrow}(u)=\inf\{x\geq0\colon G(x)\geq u\} 
\] 
denotes the generalised inverse, or quantile function, of a distribution function $G$. 
\item[(iii)] For Lebesgue-a.e.\ $u\in(0,1)$, 
\[ 
F_\ell^{\leftarrow}(u)\longrightarrow F^{\leftarrow}(u). 
\] 
Consequently, for every fixed $I$, 
\[ 
\hat X_I^{(\ell)}-\sigma_\gamma\hat Y_I \longrightarrow 0 \qquad\text{a.s.} 
\] 
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:47:12.026082+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_477fe69775d827bdf9284a25e1ee429f748c2cf3379570f192565e37d6a28a7a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Local scales \cite{helfter2025scales} of arXiv:2512.06984, 'Infinite Dimensional Multifractal Analysis of the Wiener measure'] Given a scaling $ \mathsf{scl} $, the upper and lower local scales of a Borel measure $ \mu$ on a metric space $ (X,d) $ are given at a point $x \in X$ by: 
\[ \underline{\mathsf{scl}}_{ \mathrm{loc}} \mu (x )  = \sup \left\{ \alpha > 0 :   \frac{\mu ( B(x, \varepsilon)) }{\mathit{scl}_\alpha( \varepsilon) }  \xrightarrow[\varepsilon \to 0]{}  0  \right\} \]
and \[ \overline{\mathsf{scl}}_{ \mathrm{loc}} \mu (x )  = \inf \left\{ \alpha > 0 :   \frac{\mu ( B(x, \varepsilon)) }{\mathit{scl}_\alpha( \varepsilon) }  \xrightarrow[\varepsilon \to 0]{}  + \infty   \right\}  \; . \] 
Moreover when they coincide, we denote $ \mathsf{scl}_{\mathrm{loc}}  ( x) :=  \underline{\mathsf{scl}}_{ \mathrm{loc}} \mu (x ) = \overline{\mathsf{scl}}_{ \mathrm{loc}} \mu (x ) $ their common value.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:41:28.179324+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_47807b070e35e67c9fc7ec3fdd4b052e624ee084bac7dec340bddd643945b916","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Cor lyapunov-explosive of arXiv:2511.10223, 'Stochastic Reaction Networks Within Interacting Compartments with Content-Dependent Fragme'] Let $X$ be a continuous-time Markov chain on a countable state space $\mathbb S$ with generator $\mathcal L$. Suppose there exists a finite set $K\subset\mathbb S$ and a positive function $V$ on $\mathbb S$ such that
\[
    \mathcal LV(x)\le-1
\]
for all $x\in\mathbb S\setminus K$. Suppose further that $V$ is bounded from above. If there exists $z\in K$ such that $z$ is in a closed, irreducible component of $\mathbb S$, and there exists a $y\in\mathbb S$ reachable from $z$ such that $V(y)<\inf_{x\in K} V(x)$, then $X$ is explosive.
\begin{proof}
    On the one hand, if $X$ was not explosive, every state in a closed, irreducible component of $\mathbb S$ would be positive recurrent by Theorem (thm:lyapunov-stuff of the paper). In particular, the point $z\in K$ given by the statement of the corollary would be positive recurrent for $X$.

    On the other hand, if $X$ was not explosive, then applying Theorem (thm:lyapunov-transience of the paper) to $X$ with function $-V$ would yield that $\mathbb P_{x_0}(\tau_K<\infty)<1$ for any $x_0$ such that $\sup_{x\in K} -V(x)<-V(x_0)$. In particular, taking $x_0$ to be the $y$ given to us by the statement of the corollary, we would have $\mathbb P_y(\tau_K<\infty)<1$. But then when the chain was started from $z$, it would reach $y$ with positive probability by assumption, and then fail to return to $z$ with positive probability.

    Thus Theorems (thm:lyapunov-stuff of the paper) and (thm:lyapunov-transience of the paper), taken together, show that if $X$ were not explosive then the point $z$ given in the statement of this corollary would be both positive recurrent and transient. This is absurd, so $X$ is explosive.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:10:05.828002+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_47868436fe4f0e17b612a2958d78bce7eea94fbe63871a5b656dfe9532a6e2fa","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 34 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\), define
\[
\Sigma_a
:=
\left\{
\theta\in\mathbb{C}:
1+(e^{\theta}-1)r\in(-\infty,0]
\text{ for some } r\in[0,\rho_a]
\right\}.
\]
Then \(\Lambda_a\) extends holomorphically to \(\mathbb{C}\setminus\Sigma_a\). For every integer \(n\geq1\),
\[
\Lambda_a^{(n)}(0)
=
\frac{1}{4\pi(a-1)}
\sum_{m=1}^{n}
(-1)^{m+1}(m-1)!S(n,m)
B\left(\frac{m}{a-1},m+1\right),
\]
where \(S(n,m)\) is the Stirling number of the second kind. The Taylor radius \(R_a\) of \(\Lambda_a\) at \(0\) is
\[
R_a
=
\operatorname{dist}(0,\Sigma_a)

\left(

0

\right)^2

\]
Equivalently,
\[
R_a

\begin{cases}
\pi,

a\geq a_c,\\[2mm]

\]
where \(a_c>1\) is the unique solution of \((a_c-1)a_c^{-a_c/(a_c-1)}=1/2\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.166483+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_478a1bb27d1aaedfc6391e6abf27228a54f343f81889aff4908cd268ecc37ea2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 48 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Suppose $J_+ \neq \emptyset$, and define
    \begin{align}
        
        \Delta_+(\vartheta) 
        &\equiv \vartheta + \gamma_+(z_\star) - \gamma_+(\beta_\star(\gamma_\star + \vartheta))
        \,,\\
        
        \Delta_-(\vartheta) 
        &\equiv \vartheta + \gamma_+(\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta)) - \gamma_+(z_\star)\,.
    \end{align}
These functions are continuous and strictly increasing on the intervals $[0,+\infty)$ and $[0,\vartheta_{-,\max})$ respectively, where in the latter case we define
    \[
        \vartheta_{-,\max} \equiv \sup\lt\{
            \vartheta \ge 0 : \beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta) > z_0
        \rt\}\,.
    \]
    Furthermore, $\Delta_+(0) = \Delta_-(0) = 0$ and 
    \beq
        
        \lim_{\vartheta \uparrow +\infty} \Delta_+(\vartheta)
        = \lim_{\vartheta \uparrow \vartheta_{-,\max}} \Delta_-(\vartheta)
        = +\infty\,.
    \eeq
    In particular, for any $\delta > 0$, there exist (unique) solutions $\vartheta_+ \in (0,+\infty)$, $\vartheta_- \in (0,\vartheta_{-,\max})$ to the equations
    \beq
        
        \Delta_+(\vartheta_+) = \Delta_-(\vartheta_-) = \delta\,.
    \eeq
\begin{proof}
    Since $J_+ \neq \emptyset$, we have $\hv_1 > 0$ and $z_0 = m^{-1}(\alpha / \hv_1)$, and thus case \eqref{i:fp-case2} or \eqref{i:fp-case3} of Remark~\ref{r:fp.cases} holds. In either case, we have $z_\star > z_0$. Note that $\gamma_+$ is strictly decreasing for $z > z_0$. Since $\beta_\star(\gamma_\star) = z_\star$, we have $\Delta_+(0) = \Delta_-(0) = 0$.
Recall that $\beta_\star$ is nondecreasing by Lemma~\ref{l:fp-g2}\eqref{i:fp-beta-incr}; it follows that $\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta) > z_0$ for all $\vartheta \in [0,\vartheta_{-,\max})$. Moreover, $\beta_\star$ is continuous, so $\Delta_+$ and $\Delta_-$ are continuous and strictly increasing on their respective domains. It remains to verify \eqref{e:fp-vartheta-limit}.
Since $\Delta_+(\vartheta)\ge\vartheta$, it is clear the limit involving $\Delta_+$ is $+\infty$.
Similarly, since $\Delta_-(\vartheta)\ge\vartheta$, 
 the limit involving $\Delta_-$ is also clearly $+\infty$ in the case $\vartheta_{-,\max} = +\infty$.
    Otherwise, we must have $\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta) \downarrow z_0$ as $\vartheta \uparrow \vartheta_{-,\max}$, so $\gamma_+(\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta)) \uparrow +\infty$.
    This proves \eqref{e:fp-vartheta-limit}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0093-lace-expansion-for-the-random-cluster-model-with-q-not-in-1-2","No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:26:45.046129+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_47a85609ff5195a4ed60dc8a400ac0a530703241df875e64c92cc8c8ef911c14","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Identify what makes q = 1 and q = 2 expandable and whether a q-analogue of the random-current switching lemma exists. Result: q = 1 is Bernoulli percolation (independence gives the pivotal decomposition); q = 2 is expandable through the random-current representation and the switching lemma (Sakai's lace expansion for the Ising model). For integer q >= 3 the Potts model has a random-current-like representation (the 'random-current representation for Potts' via the Edwards-Sokal coupling with q colours) but the switching lemma fails because currents are Z_q-valued and the pairing structure that gives the switching identity is specific to Z_2. A lace expansion needs a 'pivotal' notion for which the model factorises across the pivotal: in FK with general q the cluster weight q^{k(omega)} couples the two sides of a pivotal edge only through the count of clusters, which changes by one when the pivotal is closed; this suggests an expansion in which each pivotal carries a factor q or 1 depending on whether closing it splits a cluster, i.e. a lace expansion for the two-point function with the cluster count as an extra variable, which is exactly the generating function in the number of clusters, i.e. the Tutte polynomial. So the expansion would be an expansion of the Tutte polynomial's two-point version, which is #P-hard to evaluate in general, suggesting no simple diagrammatic expansion exists for generic q; for the infrared bound one might instead use reflection positivity (available for integer q and for the FK model on Z^d with q >= 1 via the Potts representation), which gives the infrared bound for the Potts spin-spin covariance directly for integer q >= 1 (Frohlich-Simon-Spencer), without a lace expansion. Recorded: for integer q the infrared bound is available by reflection positivity (this is classical), so the source's 'and use it to derive an infrared bound' is partly moot for integer q; the genuinely open content is the expansion itself and the non-integer q infrared bound. Key identity: Reflection positivity gives the infrared bound for integer-q Potts covariances without any expansion; the open part is non-integer q and the expansion. Obstruction: No switching lemma for Z_q currents; the natural expansion variable is a Tutte-polynomial quantity.","status":"unverified"}

\[

 q_u^{r;C}=r^{2\eta}\chi_I(u)C.

Then $\iota_I(B,C)\in\mathsf Z_{\eta;\mathfrak I,1}(H)$ and
\begin{align}
 d_{\eta;\mathfrak I,1}(\iota_I(B,C),0)

 \\
 d_{{\rm op},L}(\iota_I(B,C),0)
 &=\|B\|_{L_A}+\|C\|_{L_Q}.

Thus finite-rank central directions embed the two ideal norms and the two

{"assumptions":["(M,g) complete, without boundary, Ric >= 0 (M = R^n is the model case)","u > 0 everywhere on M x (0,infinity) and smooth","u solves the heat equation u_t = Delta u","in the integrated form: 0 < t_1 < t_2 and d the Riemannian distance"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:49.106567+00:00","domain":"parabolic partial differential equations / geometric analysis","id":"claim_47db85f6916ac54d9a66f428afda4251cde272229adb51598e29f6604b83e38b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $(M,g)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature and without boundary (for instance $M=\\mathbb R^n$), and let $u>0$ be a smooth solution of $u_t=\\Delta u$ on $M\\times(0,\\infty)$. Then the differential Harnack (Li-Yau) inequality holds pointwise: $\\frac{|\\nabla u|^2}{u^2}-\\frac{u_t}{u}\\le\\frac{n}{2t}$, equivalently $-\\Delta\\log u\\le\\frac n{2t}$. Integrating along geodesics gives the classical Harnack form: for $x_1,x_2\\in M$ and $0<t_1<t_2$, $u(x_1,t_1)\\le u(x_2,t_2)\\Big(\\frac{t_2}{t_1}\\Big)^{n/2}\\exp\\Big(\\frac{d(x_1,x_2)^2}{4(t_2-t_1)}\\Big).$ Both are sharp: equality in the differential form holds for the Gaussian $u=\\Phi(x,t)$ on $\\mathbb R^n$. Positivity of $u$ on the whole of $M\\times(0,\\infty)$ and $\\mathrm{Ric}\\ge0$ are both needed; if $\\mathrm{Ric}\\ge-K$ with $K>0$ the estimate degrades to $\\alpha\\frac{|\\nabla u|^2}{u^2}-\\frac{u_t}{u}\\le\\frac{n\\alpha^2}{2t}+\\frac{n\\alpha^2K}{2(\\alpha-1)}$ for any $\\alpha>1$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:33.543793+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_47f004ce49972b96385355d483ae60dbbea7e7dd8169f7703ccea069f0ebcef2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 29 (EFIID implies analyticity \cite{Ott_Analyticity_Ising,Ott_Analyticity_RCM}) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Let $\mu$ be a stationary random field on $S^{\Z^d}$.

 \[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:54:18.241594+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_47f60b1162d7dbf1dc182d6ae6cbcc100219ebf5001622fe4f7853000f968c7b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:persistence pairing-graph of arXiv:2608.29719, 'Persistence Pairing Graphs: Tracking Changes of Selected Homology Bases'] The $q$-th \emph{persistence pairing graph} associated with $\mathfrak F$ is the directed graph
\[
\mathcal G^{(q)}(\mathfrak F) = \bigl(\mathcal V^{(q)},\mathcal E^{(q)}\bigr),
\]
whose vertex set $\mathcal V^{(q)}$ consists of the labeled nonzero $q$-th persistence intervals and whose edge set is
\[
\mathcal E^{(q)} := \left\{(u,v) \ \middle|\ d_u<\infty, b_v<d_u<d_v, \text{ and } w_{uv}\neq 0\right\}.
\]
If the nonzero transition coefficients are retained, we define the edge weight
\[
\omega^{(q)}(u,v) := w_{uv} \in \Bbbk\setminus\{0\}.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:31:57.857955+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_47f790b31574410c8a38bbc7e6ef0b9226d23ef0f0aee1c61a9d6a3f31aadf2a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem th:GW of arXiv:2510.10299, '\Large Sparse graphs and their Benjamini-Schramm limits: a spectral tour'] Let $d >0$, $T$ be a Galton-Watson tree with $\mathrm {Poi}(d)$ distribution  whose root is denoted by $o$, $A$ its adjacency operator and $m_d = \mathbb {E} m_A^{\delta_o}$ its average spectral measure. There exist $1 \leq  d_1 \leq d_2$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
\item (Average spectral measure: atoms) 
$m_d(\{\lambda \}) > 0$ if and only of $\lambda$ is a totally-real algebraic integer.  
\item (Dimension of kernel)  $
m_d (\{0 \}) = q + e^{-dq} + d q e^{-dq} -1
$, where $q \in (0,1)$ is the smallest root to $q = e^{-d e^{-dq}}$.

\item (Average spectral measure: continuous part) 
$m_d$ has a non-trivial continuous part if and only if $d >1$.

\item (Average spectral measure: ac part) 
$m_d$ has a non-trivial ac part for all $d > d_1$ and its total mass goes to $1$ as $d \to \infty$. Moreover, the limit
$
\lim_{t \to 0} m_d([-t,t]\backslash \{0\})/ t 
$
exists and is positive if and only if $d > e$.

\item (Spectral decomposition: atoms)   For all $d> 1$, conditioned on $T$ being infinite, with probability one, there is an $\ell^2$-eigenvector with eigenvalue $\lambda$ for all totally-real algebraic integers.

\item (Spectral decomposition: ac) 
For all $d > d_2$, conditioned on $T$ being infinite, with probability one,  $A$ has non-trivial ac spectrum. Moreover the total mass of the ac part of  $m_A^{\delta_o}$ goes to $1$ in probability as $d \to \infty$.

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:35:04.200053+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_482adf22638afad1a987cec0e2aa1733ef9927d838703bb53eb02bd1872e17c6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] Fix \(r\ge1\).  For each \(\sigma\in\cS_r\), fix a forest
\(\Gamma_\sigma\in\cC_r(\sigma)\).  For a walk \(w\) and an \(r\)-cell
\(\Delta\) that contains neither endpoint of \(w\) and satisfies
\(\Gamma_\Delta(w)\ne\varnothing\), put
\[
  \sigma_\Delta(w)
  =\operatorname{tr}_r\bigl(S_\Delta^{-1}\Gamma_\Delta(w)\bigr).
\]
We call \(\Delta\) \emph{canonical for \(w\)} if
\[
  S_\Delta^{-1}\Gamma_\Delta(w)=\Gamma_{\sigma_\Delta(w)}.
\]
Let \(\mathsf m_r(w)\) be the number of canonical \(r\)-cells of \(w\).
There is a constant \(a>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
  \limsup_{n\to\infty}
  \#\{w\in\cW_{O,n}:\mathsf m_r(w)\le\lfloor an\rfloor\}^{1/n}
  <\mu.
  
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:38:04.499320+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4834c046f0dcc26c8c79dc283b78308eb797952ba932300fa56658182da2494c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lemER of arXiv:2607.12459, 'Renormalisation of Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] {\bf [Invariance property for deterministic weights]}

For every $\delta\in(0,\infty)$, $\eta\in[0,\infty)$ and $w\in(0,\infty)$, the deterministic weight law concentrated at $w$ is invariant under averaging of weights: if $W_1,\ldots,W_m$ are deterministic random variables equal to $w$, then 
\[
m^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^m W_i \stackrel{d}{=}W_1,
\]
where in this case equivalence in distribution coincides with equality in value. Combined with the invariant connection functions $g^{\neq}_\delta(x,y) = \delta xy$ and $g^{=}_\eta(x,x) = \eta x$ identified in Lemma~(leminv of the paper), this gives a two-parameter homogeneous Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph with edge and self-loop  connection probability equal to
\[
p^{\neq} = 1-\mathrm{e}^{-\delta w^2}, \qquad p^{=} = 1-\mathrm{e}^{-\frac12(\delta w^2+\eta w)}.
\]
The above random graph is invariant in distribution under the renormalisation transformation, provided the aggregated weights are rescaled by $m^{-1}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

\[

\begin{equation}

+

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.595230+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4896c8b55d37f829d79b5f233564c7c457174235883befac4f901fc73efbc473","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.02320, 'Analysis of Triggered Packet Streams: A Matrix-Analytic Method for Exponential Triggering...'] In many communication networks, the transmission of a packet may automatically trigger the transmission of a subsequent packet from the same source after a (possibly random) delay, without requiring acknowledgment or feedback. Such behavior arises in multi-stage status updating, proactive protocols, and other applications where users generate causally dependent packet streams. In this paper, in order to analyze these systems, we introduce the $\\mathrm{M^T/G/1}$ queue. In this model, primary customers arrive according to a Poisson process, and each primary customer triggers a secondary customer to join the queue after an independent delay. This arrival mechanism falls outside the scope of classical queueing models with renewal arrival processes. When the triggering delays follow an exponential distribution, we exploit the memoryless property to set up a tractable Markov description. By truncating the number of pending secondary customers, we derive a finite system of linear algebraic equations in the Laplace--Stieltjes transform domain and solve them using matrix-analytic methods. Based on the resulting workload distribution, we compute class-specific performance metrics using PASTA for primary customers and Palm conditioning for secondary customers. Finally, we validate the accuracy of this truncation through numerical experiments.","status":"unverified"}

        $\pi \ll T\circ\nu$. Hence $T\circ\nu \sim \pi$ whenever $\nu \sim \pi$, and,
        for every $x \in \XX$ and every $m \in \N$, each of the relations
        $T^{m}_{x} \ll \pi$, $\pi \ll T^{m}_{x}$ and $T^{m}_{x} \sim \pi$, once it
        holds, holds at every later time $n \ge m$.
  \item \emph{The singular mass is monotone in the measure:} if $\sigma \le \alpha$
        then $\sing(\sigma\mid\pi) \le \sing(\alpha\mid\pi)$.
  \item \emph{It does not increase along the dynamics:}
        $\sing(T\circ\alpha\mid\pi) \le \sing(\alpha\mid\pi)$. Consequently the map
        $\Nz \to [0,1]$, $n \mapsto \sing(T^{n}\circ\mu\mid\pi)$, is non-increasing.
  \item \emph{Nor does the reversed singular mass:}
        $\sing(\pi \mid T\circ\nu) \le \sing(\pi\mid\nu)$. Consequently the map
        $\Nz \to [0,1]$, $n \mapsto \sing(\pi\mid T^{n}_{x})$, is non-increasing, for
        every $x \in \XX$.
\end{enumerate}
Part (i), and the first assertion of (ii), are the vanishing cases of (iv) and (v), by
the last sentence of Proposition \ref{prop:singforms}; they are proved first because
(iv) uses (i).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:48:27.286593+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_48bf9f8fa50bb6298107d1dae6539609d38c60fbbc6c5b43b4f0086aa04dd11b","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 20 (Control of the good event) of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] Fix $\delta\in(0,1)$ and $\rho\in\mathbb N_0$. For $\ell\in\mathbb N$ let
	$
	m_\ell:=\lfloor \delta \ell\rfloor+1
	$
	and define the envelope probabilities
	\begin{equation}
		
		q_-(\ell)
		:=
		\max_{\mu\in S_\alpha}
		\mathbb P(x_\mu=0\mid \eta^{(\alpha)},L_\alpha=\ell),
		\quad\text{and}\quad
		q_+(\ell)
		:=
		\max_{\mu\notin S_\alpha}
		\mathbb P(x_\mu=1\mid \eta^{(\alpha)},L_\alpha=\ell).
	\end{equation}
	
	Then for every $\ell$,
	\[
	\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)^c \mid L_\alpha=\ell\bigr)
	\le
	\binom{\ell}{m_\ell}\,q_-(\ell)^{m_\ell}
	+
	\frac{\bigl((M-\ell)q_+(\ell)\bigr)^{\rho+1}}{(\rho+1)!}.
	\]
	Consequently, if for some window $[\ell_M,u_M]$,
	\begin{equation}
		\max_{\ell\in[\ell_M,u_M]}
		\binom{\ell}{m_\ell}\,q_-(\ell)^{m_\ell}\to0,
	\end{equation}
	and
	\begin{equation}
		\max_{\ell\in[\ell_M,u_M]}
		(M-\ell)q_+(\ell)\to0,
	\end{equation}
	then
	\[
	\max_{\ell\in[\ell_M,u_M]}
	\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)^c \mid L_\alpha=\ell\bigr)\to0.
	\]
	Moreover,
	\[
	\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)^c\bigr)
	\le
	\mathbb P(L_\alpha\notin[\ell_M,u_M])
	+
	\max_{\ell\in[\ell_M,u_M]}
	\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)^c \mid L_\alpha=\ell\bigr).
	\]
	Therefore, $\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)^c\bigr)\to 0$ whenever \eqref{eq:sup1}, \eqref{eq:sup2} and
	\[
	\mathbb P(L_\alpha\notin[\ell_M,u_M])\to 0
	\]
	all hold.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:21:10.894968+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_48e3513c6812a6abfff1a3d257b4b45b978efbf51833adf5c6ebb166d48dfea7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2508.04938, 'Perfect t-embeddings of doubly periodic Aztec diamonds'] Let~$w_0$,~$w_{\ell N-1}$,~$b_0$ and~$b_{\ell N-1}$ be the boundary vertices of the reduced Aztec diamond, and let~$w=w_{\ell x'+i,y'}$ and~$b=b_{\ell x+i,y}$ be vertices in the interior of the reduced Aztec diamond, that is, with~$0<\ell x'+i'<\ell N-1$,~$0\leq y'\leq \ell N-2$,~$1\leq \ell x+i\leq \ell N-1$ and~$0<y<\ell N-1$. Then
\begin{align}
 &K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w_0,b)=\frac{1}{\gamma_1}\prod_{m=1}^\ell\left(-\frac{\alpha_1}{\gamma_1}-\beta_m\right)^{-N}\\
  &\times\frac{1}{2\pi\i}\int_{\Gamma}
  \prod_{m=1}^\ell (\gamma_mz_2+\alpha_m)^N\prod_{m=1}^{i}\frac{\gamma_m+\alpha_m z_2^{-1}}{1-\beta_m z_2^{-1}}\frac{w_2^{x-N}}{z_2^y}\frac{\d z_2}{z_2\left(z_2+\frac{\alpha_1}{\gamma_1}\right)}, \\
& K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w_{\ell N-1},b)=
\prod_{m=1}^\ell(\beta_\ell\gamma_m+\alpha_m)^{-N} \\
  &\times \frac{1}{2\pi\i}\int_{\Gamma} \prod_{m=1}^\ell (\gamma_mz_2+\alpha_m)^N\prod_{m=1}^{i}\frac{\gamma_m+\alpha_m z_2^{-1}}{1-\beta_m z_2^{-1}}\frac{w_2^{x-N}}{z_2^y}\frac{\d z_2}{z_2(z_2-\beta_\ell)}, \\
&  K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w,b_0)
  = -\prod_{m=1}^\ell (-\beta_m)^N \\
  &\times\frac{1}{2\pi\i}\int_{\Gamma}\left(\frac{\prod_{m=1}^{i'+1}(\gamma_m+\alpha_m z_1^{-1})}{\prod_{m=1}^{i'}(1-\beta_m z_1^{-1})}\right)^{-1}\prod_{m=1}^\ell(z_1-\beta_m)^{-N}\frac{z_1^{y'}}{w_1^{x'}}\frac{\d z_1}{z_1},  \\
&  K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w,b_{\ell N-1})
  =\frac{1}{2\pi\i}\int_{\Gamma}\left(\frac{\prod_{m=1}^{i'+1}(\gamma_m+\alpha_m z_1^{-1})}{\prod_{m=1}^{i'}(1-\beta_m z_1^{-1})}\right)^{-1}\prod_{m=1}^\ell(z_1-\beta_m)^{-N}\frac{z_1^{y'}}{w_1^{x'}}\d z_1,

where~$w_1=w(z_1)$,~$w_2=w(z_2)$ and

and~$\Gamma$ is a simple closed curve with~$z=0$ and~$w=\infty$ in its interior and~$z=\infty$ and~$w=0$ in its exterior. Moreover,
\begin{align*}
 &K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w_0,b_{\ell N-1})
 =\frac{1}{\gamma_1}\prod_{m=1}^\ell\left(-\frac{\alpha_1}{\gamma_1}-\beta_m\right)^{-N},\\
 &K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w_{\ell N-1},b_{\ell N-1})
 =\prod_{m=1}^\ell(\beta_\ell\gamma_m+\alpha_m)^{-N}, \\

 &K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w_{\ell N-1},b_0)
 =-\frac{1}{\beta_\ell}\prod_{m=1}^{\ell}(-\beta_m)^N\prod_{m=1}^\ell(\beta_\ell\gamma_m+\alpha_m)^{-N}.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:52:57.718018+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_49055250495c6521bafd2ce7f9d77f5c5d2464941dbba8f046e9f2a2ccccbcd9","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 25 (Exact spectral decomposition and crossover boundary) of arXiv:2609.02728, 'Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improv'] For each coordinate $j$, the characteristic roots of the Nesterov recursion are
\[
    y_{j,\pm}
    =
    \frac{(1+\rho)(1-\eta\lambda_j)\pm\sqrt{\Delta_j^{\nesterov}}}{2},
\]
where
\[
    \Delta_j^{\nesterov}
    :=
    (1+\rho)^2(1-\eta\lambda_j)^2
    -4\rho(1-\eta\lambda_j).
\]
In the stable small-step range $0<\eta\lambda_j<1$, the critical transition $\Delta_j^{\nesterov}=0$ corresponds exactly to
\[
    \eta\lambda_j
    =
    \frac{(1-\rho)^2}{(1+\rho)^2},
\]
which is asymptotically equivalent to $\eta\lambda_j\eqsim(1-\rho)^2$. Thus the individual eigen-directions are classified as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Overdamped Modes} $\bigl(\eta\lambda_j<(1-\rho)^2/(1+\rho)^2\bigr)$: the roots are real.
    \item \textbf{Underdamped Modes} $\bigl(\eta\lambda_j>(1-\rho)^2/(1+\rho)^2\bigr)$: the roots form a complex-conjugate pair.
\end{enumerate}
In the mixed-damping regime, the boundary index $J_{\max}$ separating the underdamped modes from the overdamped modes is defined by the crossover relation $\eta\lambda_{J_{\max}}\eqsim(1-\rho)^2$:
\begin{equation}

    J_{\max}
    \eqsim
    \left(\frac{\eta}{(1-\rho)^2}\right)^{1/\beta}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, based on the maximum eigenvalue $\lambda_{\max}$, Nesterov operates in one of two global regimes:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Fully Overdamped Regime} $\bigl(\eta\lambda_{\max}\lesssim(1-\rho)^2\bigr)$: all spectral modes are overdamped.
    \item \textbf{Mixed-Damping Regime} $\bigl(\eta\lambda_{\max}\gtrsim(1-\rho)^2\bigr)$: the high-curvature modes $j\le J_{\max}$ are underdamped, whereas the flat modes $j>J_{\max}$ are overdamped.
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:38:04.523628+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4906af49534eb410f87cf8d9b9452e38d1c8e472f38dbfbbd919318ebdffdc08","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] \thlabel{prop:giant_determines_c_infty}
    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 1$ and suppose that $J : V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ is a transitive kernel satisfying $J(x,y) = \Omega(d_G(x,y)^{-d \alpha})$ with $\alpha \in (0,2)$.
    
    Let $\beta > \beta_c$.

{"assumptions":["Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0074-scaling-limit-of-random-walk-on-the-high-dimensional-incipient-infinit","No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:26:45.044664+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_49130968f69d04518594feadc86c7254295245afe5504bce42258268d1cce6aa","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Reduce to the scaling limit of the IIC itself (C0077) plus a homogenisation of the walk on the limit tree. Result: If the IIC converges (as a measure-valued process indexed by intrinsic distance) to incipient infinite super-Brownian motion, then the walk on the IIC should converge to the Brownian motion on the associated continuum random tree embedded in R^d, time-changed by the IIC volume measure, i.e. to the 'Brownian motion on the ISE-type tree' with spatial displacement given by the embedding (the Ben Arous-Cabezas-Fribergh limit). The walk on the discrete tree structure of the IIC is a random walk on a graph that is tree-like at all scales in d > 6 (the number of cycles at scale r is bounded), so the spatial position is a Brownian motion time-changed by the intrinsic clock; the intrinsic clock converges by the tree scaling limit; the embedding of the tree in R^d is a branching random walk-type embedding whose limit is the ISE embedding. Each step is known for the branching random walk trace (BCF 2016) and the difficulty for the IIC is the dependence between the tree structure and the embedding (loops, self-intersections). The rigorous reduction: the walk's scaling limit follows from (i) the IIC tree scaling limit with its embedding, (ii) a resistance estimate showing the effective resistance across the IIC at intrinsic distance r is of order r (tree-like), which is known up to constants from Kozma-Nachmias-type estimates. So the problem is subsumed by C0077 plus a resistance-form convergence theorem (Croydon's framework), which needs the convergence of the IIC as a resistance metric space, a stronger statement than the measure-valued convergence in the source. Obstruction: Resistance-metric convergence of the IIC in d > 6 is not established.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.165760+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4997649fea6ac3b1d570818aa0d47cc348dd0bd69b6f01bace7d030ace220912","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 43 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall the function $V_\gamma(\by)$ from \eqref{e:def-V-gamma-y}.
For any $\gamma \ge 0$, any local maximizer of $V_\gamma(\by)$ on the sphere $\{\|\by\|^2=N\}$ is of the form
    \beq
        
        \by =\dbA_\beta\Big(\gamma^{1/2}\dbg+\dbX\by\Big)\,,
    \eeq
    where we recall $\dbA_\beta \equiv (\beta \bI_N - \dbD)^{-1}$. Furthermore, for any such $\by$ we must have $\beta \ge \hw_1$.
\begin{proof}
We apply the method of Lagrange multipliers with the Lagrangian $\Lagr(\by;\beta)$ as defined in \eqref{e:fp-y-lagrangian}. Note that the Lagrangian Hessian (with respect to $\by$) is given by
    \[
        \nabla^2 \Lagr(\by;\beta)
        = -\frac{2}{N} \Big(
            \beta \bI_N - \dbD - \dbX
        \Big)\,.
    \]
At any local maximum, this Hessian must be negative semi-definite. Recall the definitions of $\dbD$ and $\dbX$ from \eqref{e:fp.dbD} and \eqref{e:fp.dbX} respectively. Since $|B_1|\ge\iota N$ by the assumption $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, we can find a non-zero vector $\bv$ that is zero outside the coordinates of $B_1$, and is additionally orthogonal to each of the vectors $\tbmeta^j$ ($1\le j\le r'$) in the definition \eqref{e:fp.dbX} of $\dbX$. It follows that
    \[
    0 \le \bv^\st \Big(\beta -\dbD-\dbX \Big)\bv
    =\bv^\st \Big(\beta -\dbD \Big)\bv
    =(\beta-\hw_1)\|\bv\|^2\,,
    \]
so we conclude $\beta\ge\hw_1$. 
For any local maximizer $\by$ satisfying $\|\by\|^2=N$, stationarity of $\Lagr$ at $\by$ yields the expression~\eqref{e:fp-g-prep2-stationarity}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:32:28.957897+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_49b4d4b35233d9cf508982cda14b600099546ebee5d354d2ae38e6149c975b0b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:path-reduction of arXiv:2608.23545, 'Eulerian walkers on $\Z^2$ have range exponent $2/3$'] Let $G$ be an infinite connected graph of bounded degree with an arbitrary
		rotor mechanism, and let $\mathbb P$ be a law for the initial rotors.

		\begin{equation}

		\end{equation}

			\item If, in addition, $G$ and the rotor mechanism are doubly periodic and the

			exist a deterministic compact convex set $B\subset\mathbb R^2$ containing the origin in its interior

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:04:55.812903+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_49cbe3d73b673b3cc133a2083c4d9abc9b498e668cd584eb91575b9ad4f976c9","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop p:geodesic-deloc of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Fix $L\geqslant 1$ and $\ell>0$ and $t_0\in(0, 1]$ and $\gamma\in(0,\frac13)$.
    There exist $\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_0(L,\ell,\gamma)>0$ and $C=C(L,\gamma)>0$ such that the following holds.

    For all $0 < \varepsilon < \min\{\varepsilon_0, (t_0/4)^{1/\gamma}\}$, all $x,y\in [-L,L]$, and all $r\in[\varepsilon^\gamma, t_0-\varepsilon^\gamma]$, we have
    \begin{multline*}
        \mathbb{P}\left(
            \sup_{|z|\leqslant \ell}
            \bigl[\mathcal{L}(0,x;r,z) + \mathcal{L}(r,z;t_0,y)\bigr]
            \leqslant
            \sup_{|z|\leqslant 2\varepsilon\log^4(1/\varepsilon)}
            \bigl[
                \mathcal{L}(0,x;r,z) + \mathcal{L}(r,z;t_0,y)
            \bigr]
            +
            \varepsilon^{1/2} \log^5(1/\varepsilon)
        \right)\\
        \leqslant 
        C \varepsilon^{1-3\gamma}.
    \end{multline*}
    Note that $[\varepsilon^\gamma, t_0-\varepsilon^\gamma]$ is non-empty, since by hypothesis $\varepsilon^\gamma <  t_0/4$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Fresh mutually independent Gaussian inputs","Noiseless labels","t deterministic, including any finite first expected-risk hit; not a sample-path stopping time","alpha>1 and gamma>alpha+1; fixed eta>0; B positive integer; n positive integer","Independent audit pending; no whole-theorem formal certificate."],"created_at":"2026-10-21T19:58:24.779201+00:00","domain":"stochastic optimization","id":"claim_49faa9192c7b291553081217a714e6fa79ce2dfe68b1cb7571c24cfe0aeea4ee","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"PROOF (UNAUDITED), w741-T422-C05 v1. Not independently checked.
# T422 Target 2: an explicit lower tail bound for instantaneous noise scales

Status: proof (unaudited), C05 v1. This strengthens the positive-probability
scope obstruction C04. It is not an upper tail estimate or a typical-scale
calibration, and it makes no literature-priority claim.

## Statement and all constants

Use the noiseless fresh Gaussian online model of C04. Let alpha>1,
gamma>alpha+1, h_j=j^(-alpha), and deterministic e_0,j satisfy
e_0,j^2=j^(-(gamma-alpha)). Each update averages B independent samples,
B>=1 integer, with a fixed step eta>0. Fix finite integer t>=1, ell in {1,2},
and integer n>=1. Let u_n denote the nth coordinate unit vector, and put

    m=gamma-alpha>1, M=||e_0||=sqrt(zeta(m)), c=M/2,
    y=c u_n, A=<e_0-y,e_0>=M^2-c e_0,n,
    u=(e_0-y)/sqrt(eta A), R=||u||+1,
    r=c h_n^((ell+1)/2)/4,
    T=(1+eta R^2)^t-1,
    rho=min(1, r R/(4 M T)).

Here A>=M^2/2>0, T>0, M,R,r,rho>0. Every division is well defined.
The norm in R is explicit:

    ||u||^2=(M^2-2c e_0,n+c^2)/(eta A).

Choose the following explicit finite truncation:

    N=ceil(max(n,1,
         [16/(eta A (m-1)rho^2)]^(1/(m-1)),
         [32/((alpha-1)rho^2)]^(1/(alpha-1)))).

For a prescribed center w equal to either 0 or u, define

    a=rho/(2 sqrt(N)),
    P_N(w)= (1/2) [rho/sqrt(2 pi N)]^N
             (product_(j=1)^N h_j^(-1/2))
             exp[-(1/2) sum_(j=1)^N (|w_j|+a)^2/h_j].

These are finite explicit strictly positive real numbers, not floating-point
certificates. Put

    pi_event=P_N(0)^(B(t-1)) P_N(u)^B >0,
    L_n=1+(9/25)zeta(ell alpha)n^(ell alpha).

For the conditional single-example instantaneous scale R_ell of C04,

    P(e_t!=0 and R_ell(e_t)>=L_n) >= pi_event.             (Q1)

In particular, for any finite L choose n with L_n>L; the same explicit
pi_event lower-bounds P(e_t!=0 and R_ell(e_t)>L).
The theorem also applies when t is any finite first EXPECTED-risk hitting
index, since that index is deterministic. It does not apply to a realized-risk
stopping time chosen from the samples without an additional stopping argument.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:09:43.679526+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4a2d07af29b3dfae6c47232024d732e640ad255a925174092c7705737164dbda","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem t:multcltmarkedpp of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Consider a stationary marked point process  $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{K}$ with non-null, finite intensity $\rho$, having summable exponential $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations as in Definition~(def.A2 of the paper).  Let $\xi_i : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K} \times \hat\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}} \to \mathbb{R}$,  $i =1,\ldots,{m}$ be translation invariant  score functions. Assume  that the  vector  \(\boldsymbol{\xi} = (\xi_1, \ldots, \xi_{m}) \in \mathbb{R}^{m}\) is jointly fast \textnormal{BL}-localizing on finite windows of $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ in the sense that for all $p \in \mathbb{N} $, condition~(equation Lp-stab of the paper) is satisfied by \(\bk {\boldsymbol{\xi}}1p \in (\mathbb{R}^{m})^p\).

\begin{equation} n^{-1/2}(\mu_n^{\xi_1}(f) - \mathbb {E} \mu_n^{\xi_1}(f),\ldots, \mu_n^{\xi_{m}}(f) - \mathbb {E} \mu_n^{\xi_{m}}(f)) \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} (Z_1,\ldots,Z_{m}),

where $(Z_1,\ldots,Z_{m})$ is a  multivariate normal random vector
(with possibly zero components) having zero mean and covariance 

$$  {\rm{Cov}}(Z_i,Z_j) = \sigma^2_{\Upsilon}[i,j] \int_{W_1}f(x)^2 \mathrm{d} x \in (-\infty, \infty),$$

 where the matrix $(\sigma^2_{\Upsilon}[i,j])_{1 \leq i \leq j \leq {m}}$ involves the vector $\boldsymbol{\Upsilon}_{\0}$ and the matrix  $\boldsymbol{\Upsilon}_{(\0,z)}$ of probability distributions  given in~(equation e.xil-0-multi of the paper) and~(equation e.xil-xy-multi of the paper): 

\begin{align}  
& \sigma^2_{\Upsilon}[i,j]:=
\rho\mathbb {E} \bigl[\Upsilon_{\0}[i] \Upsilon_{\0}[j]\bigr]   \\

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:57:16.068865+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4a2e9cafd45da6c0dd1a914e3ca2acb0a3d760d4a9d628c42e235cdaae6904ed","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:OPRE-model of arXiv:2507.00329, 'Oriented bond-site percolation in random environment and contact processes with periodic r'] Fix some spatial stretches $(\xi_x)_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$, $(\nu_{x,x+1})_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}\subset[0,\infty)$, called the \emph{environment}, and a {\em connection function} $\kappa\colon[0,\infty)\to[0,1]$. Consider the following independent bond-site percolation model on $\mathbb{L}^2$ in the environment $(\xi_x)_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$, $(\nu_{x,x+1})_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$, where 
    \begin{itemize}
    	\item 
    		each vertex $(t,x)\in V$ is open independently with probability \(\kappa(\xi_x)\),
		\item 
			each edge of the form \((t,x)\to(t+1,x+1)\) is open independently with probability \(\kappa(\nu_{x,x+1})\), and
		\item	
			each edge of the form \((t,x)\to(t+1,x-1)\) is open independently with probability \(\kappa(\nu_{x-1,x})\).
    \end{itemize}
    If the graph contains an infinite path consisting of open vertices and open edges only, we say that the model \emph{percolates}. 
    If the environment is given by a realisation of families of random variables, we refer to the associated percolation model as \emph{OPRE}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.362393+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4a3d246eec17c82cac727cddefa9773903da143dca1b224f20cdb79dd8f9d7f3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 10 of arXiv:2604.21669, 'Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts:\\\\ II. order-order interface convergence'] Given a bi-infinite connected set \\(C\\subset\\bbL_\\bullet\\cap  (\\R\\times [-c,c])\\), we say that a subset \\(R\\subset\\R^2\\) is (weakly) \\emph{above} \\(C\\) if it is contained in (the closure of) the connected component of the point~\\((0,c+1)\\) in \\(\\R^2\\setminus C\\), where we identify \\(C\\) with the union of line segments between the endpoints of the edges in \\(\\bbE_C\\). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:47:01.659423+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4a3dcc4c74b47dc5d5ff50d07e00c01ec543c6525547d47adbe155dbdddfa963","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 23 (Bernstein's inequality for sub-exponential variables) of arXiv:2604.23461, 'Scaling limit of Sinkhorn-rescaled Random Matrices \\ via Stability of Static Schrödinger '] Let $Y_1, \dots, Y_n$ be independent centered random variables satisfying the moment bounds
	\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:50:30.563977+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4a45890310264b6f508b33fe9f0f827699aef581ad07c4315ee7d6b9bc160864","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2605.30616, 'Brownian motion: the hyperbolic number setting'] Let $\mu$ be the $\mathbb{H}$-valued probability on a measurable
space $\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right)\right)$.

\noindent $\mathrm{(1)}$ If $A\in\sigma\left(X\right)$, then $\mu\left(A\right)+\mu\left(A^{c}\right)=p$, with $p\in\left\{ 1,e_{+},e_{-}\right\} $.

\noindent $\mathrm{(2)}$ If $\phi$ is the empty set of $\sigma\left(X\right)$
in $X$, then $\mu\left(\phi\right)=0$.

\noindent $\mathrm{(3)}$ If $A\subseteq B$ in $\sigma\left(X\right)$,
then $\mu\left(A\right)\leq\mu\left(B\right)$ in $\mathbb{H}$.

\noindent $\mathrm{(4)}$ If $A,B\in\sigma\left(X\right)$, then 
\[
\mu\left(A\cup B\right)=\mu\left(A\right)+\mu\left(B\right)-\mu\left(A\cap B\right),

and hence,

\mu\left(A\cup B\right)\leq\mu\left(A\right)+\mu\left(B\right),\;\;\;\mathrm{in\;\;\;}\mathbb{H}.

\noindent $\mathrm{(5)}$ If $A_{1}\supseteq A_{2}\supseteq A_{3}\supseteq...,\;\mathrm{\textrm{in}\;}\sigma\left(X\right)$,
and $A=\overset{\infty}{\underset{k=1}{\cap}}A_{k}$ in $X$, then
\[
\underset{k\rightarrow\infty}{\mathrm{lim}}\mu\left(A_{k}\right)=\mu\left(A\right)=\mu\left(\overset{\infty}{\underset{k=1}{\cap}}A_{k}\right).
\]

\noindent $\mathrm{(6)}$ If $A_{1}\subseteq A_{2}\subseteq A_{3}\subseteq...$,
in $\sigma\left(X\right)$, and $A=\overset{\infty}{\underset{k=1}{\cup}}A_{k}$
in $\sigma\left(X\right)$, then 
\[
\underset{k\rightarrow\infty}{\mathrm{lim}}\mu\left(A_{k}\right)=\mu\left(A\right)=\mu\left(\overset{\infty}{\underset{k=1}{\cup}}A_{k}\right).

{"assumptions":["translation invariance, or more generally a transitive amenable group action, of the percolation measure","ergodicity of the measure under the translation group, needed to conclude N is almost surely constant","amenability of the underlying graph, i.e. subexponential boundary-to-volume ratio along a Folner sequence","finite energy or insertion and deletion tolerance for each edge's conditional state"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.981600+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4a75ca0603a5987c8ea2229b5f254b315be024ca14b43e8bb06290ff87223753","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For a translation-invariant, ergodic percolation measure on Z^d, or more generally on an amenable transitive graph, satisfying finite energy (insertion and deletion tolerance for each edge conditionally on the rest of the configuration), the number N of infinite open clusters is almost surely a constant in {0, 1, infinity}, and Burton and Keane's argument rules out 2 <= N < infinity as well as N = infinity: if there were at least two infinite clusters with positive density, a positive density of trifurcation points (local configurations forcing at least three disjoint infinite paths) would be forced, but a discrete isoperimetric counting argument on a large box shows the number of trifurcation points cannot exceed a quantity of the order of the box's boundary, contradicting positive density in the bulk unless N <= 1. It follows that N is almost surely 0 or 1. The argument does not apply to non-amenable graphs, where coexistence of infinitely many infinite clusters is a genuine, well-studied phenomenon rather than a proof artifact, and constancy of N itself (ruling out a mixture over the value of N) is a separate ergodic-theory step, not part of the trifurcation-counting argument. Typical failure: Applying Burton-Keane uniqueness to a non-amenable graph, such as a regular tree or a graph with exponential volume growth, and expecting a unique infinite cluster; the trifurcation-point isoperimetric argument fundamentally requires amenability, and on non-amenable graphs the coexistence of infinitely many infinite clusters, studied by Haggstrom, Peres and others, is a real phenomenon that this theorem simply does not rule out. Canonical reference: Burton and Keane, 1989, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Gandolfi, Keane and Newman, 1992, Probability Theory and Related Fields.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:58:01.577720+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4a7e5afb5dcd6eb054453ba06d81f5651e5471d79dd88213cbebee1aeff7db25","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $\mathcal D\subset\R^N$ be nonempty, bounded, convex, and

	$\mathcal B:\mathcal D\to\R$ be a $\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier

	$c,c_0,\rho_0>0$ and $C>0$ such that, for every

		\[
			\|u\|_{\mathcal B,\theta}\le\rho_0,

		\[

		\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:29:35.081011+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4a9d5d82c8b3d30ad304d0a94bd48ce3acf49c853d808038ed2ee96bf8c59f2a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2609.03803, 'List-distance consistent vertices in trees are confined to a path'] Let $G=SP(w;\ell_1,\dots,\ell_k)$ with $k\ge3$. Then
\[
  \sigma_i=
  \begin{cases}
    1, & \text{if } k\ge4,\\
    \infty, & \text{if } k=3 \text{ and } \ell_{i'}=1 \text{ for some } i'\ne i,\\
    2, & \text{if } k=3 \text{ and } \ell_{i'}\ge2 \text{ for both } i'\ne i .
  \end{cases}
\]
Moreover
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] for $1\le j\le\ell_i$ one has $v_{i,j}\in S_{c_i}(G)$ if and
only if $j\ge\bigl\lceil(\ell_i-\sigma_i)/2\bigr\rceil$, so that
\[
  \bigl|S_{c_i}(G)\cap\{v_{i,1},\dots,v_{i,\ell_i}\}\bigr|
  =\min\Bigl\{\ell_i,\ \bigl\lfloor(\ell_i+\sigma_i)/2\bigr\rfloor+1\Bigr\};
\]
\item[\textup{(ii)}] $w\in S_{c_i}(G)$ if and only if $\ell_i\le\sigma_i$;
\item[\textup{(iii)}] consequently
\[
  \bigl|S_{c_i}(G)\cap\bigl(\{w\}\cup\{v_{i,1},\dots,v_{i,\ell_i}\}\bigr)\bigr|=
  \begin{cases}
    \lceil \ell_i/2\rceil+1, & \text{if } \sigma_i=1,\\
    \lfloor \ell_i/2\rfloor+2, & \text{if } \sigma_i=2,\\
    \ell_i+1, & \text{if } \sigma_i=\infty .
  \end{cases}
\]
\end{enumerate}
Here the conventions for $\sigma_i=\infty$ are that the condition in
\textup{(i)} holds for every $j$, that the count in \textup{(i)} equals
$\ell_i$, and that the inequality in \textup{(ii)} holds.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:57:28.228397+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4ad62140468ebb8bbab6129a8630c718c54d71548ce60b7e2aaabeb2fee419de","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 ({\cite[Definition 10.1) of arXiv:2607.18104, '2607.18104'] {DOV:DirectedLandscape}}]
We denote by $\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}(x,s;y,t)$ the \textbf{(full-space) directed landscape}, a four parameter random function in $\mathcal{C}(\R^{4}_{\uparrow},\R)$. It satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] The marginals laws are given by the Airy sheet, i.e., for any $t,s>0$, the increment over the time interval $[t,t+s^3)$
\begin{equation}
(x,y) \mapsto \mathcal{L}(x,t;y,t+s^3)
\end{equation} is an Airy sheet $\mathcal{S}^{(s)}$ of scale $s$.
\item[(ii)] The metric composition law
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{L}(x,s;y,t) = \sup_{z \in \R} \big(\mathcal{L}(x,s;z,r) + \mathcal{L}(z,r;y,t) \big)
\end{equation} holds almost surely for any $s< r < t$ and $x,y \in \R$. The supremum in \eqref{eq:InvTriangleSup} is attained. 

\item[(iii)] For all $(t_i)_{i\in \lbr \ell \rbr}$ and $(s_i)_{i \in \lbr \ell \rbr}$ with $\ell \in \N$ such that $(t_i,s_i)_{i \in \lbr \ell \rbr}$ are disjoint intervals, the random functions $
\mathcal{L}(\cdot,t_i;\cdot,s_i)
$ are independent. 
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:40:59.393836+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4ad6e27bca2e519fa49d69caf569fbd26ab7a1bddf2cfbee2c86bf96e2688670","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.03976, '2609.03976'] Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{D}_{Y}$ module. A V-filtration along $X \times \{0\} \subset X \times \mathbb{C}$ on $\mathcal{M}$ is a decreasing filtration $V^{\bullet}\mathcal{M}$ indexed by rational numbers satisfying the following conditions.
	
	$(1)$ It is exhaustive, i.e. $\bigcup_{\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}}V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}=\mathcal{M}$,
	
	$(2)$ It is discrete and left continuous. This means that there exists a positive integer $N$ large enough such that for every $i \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $\alpha \in (\frac{i}{N},\frac{i+1}{N})$, $V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}$ is constant.
	
	$(3)$ For every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z}$, we have $V^{i}\mathcal{D}_{Y} \cdot V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M} \subset V^{i+\alpha}\mathcal{M}$.
	
	$(4)$ For every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$, the operator $s+\alpha$ is nilpotent on $\mathrm{Gr}_{V}^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}:=V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}/\bigcup_{\beta>\alpha}V^{\beta}\mathcal{M}$.
	
	$(5)$ For every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$, $V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}$ is finitely generated over $V^{0}\mathcal{D}_{Y}$.
	
	$(6)$ We have $t \cdot V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}=V^{\alpha+1}\mathcal{M}$ for $\alpha>0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:54:18.290494+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4adab735ee0d4a79c868d0502fcac2097d60167078ecd3b7646f44b8724eb25d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:DeltaF of arXiv:2608.30166, 'Square Functions and Rectifiability\\ under Monotone Transformations of the Density'] Let $F\colon(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a Borel function. For $x\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu)$ and $r>0$ set
\[
\Delta^F_\mu(x,r):=F\bigl(D_\mu(x,r)\bigr)-F\bigl(D_\mu(x,2r)\bigr).
\]
For $x\notin\operatorname{supp}(\mu)$ we set $\Delta^F_\mu(x,r):=0$; since
$\mu(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\operatorname{supp}(\mu))=0$, this convention does not affect any of the integrals
below. Given a compact interval $J\subset(0,\infty)$ and $\lambda\ge 1$, we say $F$ is
\emph{bi-Lipschitz on $J$ with constant $\lambda$} if
\[
\lambda^{-1}|s-t|\;\le\;|F(s)-F(t)|\;\le\;\lambda|s-t|
\qquad\text{for all } s,t\in J.
\]
We do not assume that $F$ is monotone; see Remark~(rem:scope of the paper).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:16:46.131481+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4adabcc59320ad5f87cc7a9ba0cf46e7b8341893255de754d222d8fffb11bc53","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:Laplacian of arXiv:2605.01444, 'From second moments to pairwise negative correlation: \\applications to minimal and unifor'] Let $G$ be a finite graph and let $L_G$ be the associated Laplacian matrix. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:44:12.651239+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4add96ec7da75fbde6768616880e59ef9fdc09d1d3a8fcba72acdeefc14971eb","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:sos-certify of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Let $P$ be an $s$-sub-Gaussian distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with mean $\mu$, and let $m\in 2\mathbb{N}$.

$v=(v_i)_{i=1}^d$ such that $\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}[\|v\|_2^{m}]>0$.

\[

       {\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}[\|v\|_2^{m}]}
\right]
\;\le\; (C\, s \sqrt{m})^{\,m},
\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:02:11.326267+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4ae3674107401d3778bce4455f479f5cffaab5ef0c7467f6d2cc75593dac3e40","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem lem-kmsw-bdy of arXiv:2510.26123, 'Directed distances in bipolar-oriented triangulations:\\ exact exponents and scaling limit'] Let $\mathfrak{Z}=(\mathfrak{L},\mathfrak{R}) : [0,n]\cap\mathbbm Z \to \mathbbm Z^2$ be a walk with increments in $\{(1,-1), (-1,0) , (0,1)\}$ and started at $\mathfrak{Z}(0) = (0,0)$ and let $\mathfrak{m}$ be its associated map via the KMSW procedure as in Definition~(def-kmsw of the paper). 
Define the four boundary segments of $\mathfrak{m}$ as done in Definition~(defn:bound-edges of the paper). 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),ref=(\roman*)]
    \item  The time $\min\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\{ m \in \mathbbm N : \mathfrak L (m) = -k \aftergroup\egroup\originalright\}$, is the time when the $k$th lower-left (missing) boundary edge of $\mathfrak{m}$ (counting starting from the initial vertex of $\lambda_0$ and moving along the lower-left boundary)  is added to $\mathfrak{m}$ by the KMSW procedure. Moreover, this is the first time that the west vertex of this new edge is the initial vertex of an active edge (and all the other times the same fact happens are the times $m$ such that $\mathfrak L (m)= -k$ and $\mathfrak L (j) \geq  -k$ for all $j\leq m$).
 
    \item  The time $\min\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\{ m \in \mathbbm N : \mathfrak R (m) = -k \aftergroup\egroup\originalright\}$,  is the time when the $k+1$th (counting respecting the orientation) lower-right boundary edge of $\mathfrak{m}$ is added to $\mathfrak{m}$ by the KMSW procedure. Moreover, this is the first time that the terminal vertex of this new edge is the terminal vertex of an active edge (and all the other times the same fact happens are the times $m$ such that $\mathfrak R (m)= -k$ and $\mathfrak R (j) \geq  -k$ for all $j\leq m$).
    
    \item  The $k$th smallest $m\in\mathbbm N$ such that ${\mathfrak L} (j) \geq {\mathfrak L} (m)+1$ for all $j\in [m+1,n]\cap\mathbbm Z$ is the time when the $k$th (counting respecting the orientation)  upper-left boundary edge of $\mathfrak{m}$ is added to $\mathfrak{m}$ by the KMSW procedure. Moreover, for every time $m'\leq m$ such that ${\mathfrak L} (m')={\mathfrak L} (m)$ and ${\mathfrak L} (j) \geq {\mathfrak L} (m')$ for all $j\in [m', m]\cap\mathbbm Z$, the corresponding active edge $\lambda_{m'}$ has the same initial vertex as the upper-left boundary edge $\lambda_{m}$. 
    
    \item  The $k$th smallest $m\in\mathbbm N$ such that ${\mathfrak R} (j) \geq {\mathfrak R} (m-1)+1$ for all $j\in [m,n]\cap\mathbbm Z$ is the time when the $k$th upper-right (missing) boundary edge of $\mathfrak{m}$ (counting starting from the terminal vertex of the lower-right boundary and moving along the upper-right boundary) is added to $\mathfrak{m}$ by the KMSW procedure.  
\end{enumerate}
In particular, denoting the set of edges on the upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, and lower-right boundary segments by $\overline\partial_L \mathfrak{m}$, $\overline\partial_R \mathfrak{m}$, $\underline\partial_L \mathfrak{m}$, and $\underline\partial_R \mathfrak{m}$, respectively, we have that
\allb 
\# \overline \partial_L \mathfrak{m} &= \mathfrak{L}(n) - \min_{j\in [0,n]\cap\mathbbm Z} \mathfrak{L}(j)+ 1  ,\quad \qquad
\# \overline \partial_R \mathfrak{m} = \mathfrak{R}(n) - \min_{j\in [0,n]\cap\mathbbm Z} \mathfrak{R}(j) ,\notag\\ 
\# \underline \partial_L \mathfrak{m} &=   - \min_{j\in [0,n]\cap\mathbbm Z} \mathfrak{L}(j) , \quad 
\qquad\qquad\qquad\# \underline \partial_R \mathfrak{m} =   - \min_{j\in [0,n]\cap\mathbbm Z} \mathfrak{R}(j) + 1 .
\alle","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:02:28.628934+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4aed24bb3ac7ade3260a8d89466183084be6b3ec75ae4bba52bfe1c9ac2eb732","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.01362, '{Double cluster swapping for spin models: \\Pfaffian relations and sharpness}'] Let $\P_{G,\beta,h}$ be the probability measure on $\R^V \times \R^V \times \left\{ 0,1 \right\}^{ \overline{E}} \times \left\{ 0,1 \right\}^E$ defining the law of $(\vpp,\vpm,\w^+,\w^-)$ in the following construction.
