{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:01:15.318084+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4b2a3686bc36ac714e873171661a8e6deeca0e899582a724b6bb529b0d57306d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 6 of arXiv:2608.30246, '2608.30246'] Let $X$ be a Polish space, let $\cC$ be a Borel concept
class on $X$, and let $L=(L_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a learning rule for $\cC$.
The rule $L$ is \emph{probably approximately correct (PAC)} for $\cC$ if, for every
$\varepsilon,\delta>0$, there exists $N\geq 1$ such that, for every $n\geq N$,
every $C\in\cC$, and every Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $X$,
\[
 (\mu^{\otimes n})^*\left(B_{C,\mu,n}(\varepsilon)\right)\leq\delta,
\]
where $(\mu^{\otimes n})^*$ denotes the outer measure induced by $\mu^{\otimes n}$.

We say that $\cC$ is \emph{PAC learnable} if there exists a PAC learning rule for $\cC$.

We say that $\cC$ is \emph{consistently PAC learnable} if every consistent learning rule for $\cC$ is PAC.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the underlying space is a Lebesgue probability space (the unit interval with Lebesgue measure, after normalisation)","the construction uses three cuts and exactly one spacer above the middle subcolumn at every stage, with h_0 = 1 and h_{n+1} = 3h_n + 1","T is the induced a.e.-defined invertible measure-preserving map"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:07:38.814795+00:00","domain":"ergodic theory, mixing and rank-one constructions","id":"claim_4b4d539c3f629ff9022575793ca66b8a2b15d3199dbed5c40bec97bddfa73324","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Chacon's transformation is the invertible, rank-one, measure-preserving transformation T of a Lebesgue probability space produced by the following cutting-and-stacking construction. Start with the column C_0 consisting of the single interval [0,1), of height h_0 = 1. Given the column C_n, a stack of h_n disjoint intervals ('levels') of equal width w_n, cut it vertically into three subcolumns of equal width w_n/3, place one new 'spacer' interval of width w_n/3, taken from the not-yet-used part of the line, on top of the MIDDLE subcolumn, and stack the three pieces in order: subcolumn 1 at the bottom, then subcolumn 2 with its spacer on top of it, then subcolumn 3. The result is the column C_{n+1} of height h_{n+1} = 3 h_n + 1. The map T sends each point of a level to the point directly above it in the current column; the columns exhaust the space in the limit, T is defined almost everywhere, is invertible, and preserves Lebesgue measure normalised to a probability measure. The same system appears symbolically as the subshift generated by the blocks B_0 = 0, B_{n+1} = B_n B_n 1 B_n, whose lengths satisfy the same recursion. STANDARD FACTS about this system: it is ergodic; it has rank one, hence simple spectrum and ZERO entropy; it is WEAKLY MIXING but NOT strongly mixing; del Junco, Rahe and Swanson proved that it has minimal self-joinings, from which it follows that it is prime (its only factors are the trivial ones) and that its centraliser consists of the powers of T alone. WHY MIXING FAILS, in one line one can check: let I be a level of C_n and let I_1, I_2, I_3 be the three pieces into which the cut splits I inside C_{n+1}, each of measure mu(I)/3. By construction T^{h_n} carries I_1 onto I_2, and I_2 is a subset of I; hence I_1 is contained in I ∩ T^{-h_n} I, so mu(I ∩ T^{-h_n} I) >= (1/3) mu(I). The same argument applied at every later stage m >= n gives mu(A ∩ T^{-h_m} A) >= (1/3) mu(A) for every A which is a union of levels of C_n and every m >= n. Mixing would force these correlations to converge to mu(A)^2, which is smaller than (1/3) mu(A) as soon as mu(A) < 1/3. SHARP EDGES. (a) This is THE standard witness that weak mixing does not imply strong mixing; do not use it as an example of a mixing system, and do not expect quantitative decay of correlations from it - along the tower heights h_n the correlations do not decay at all. (b) Its zero entropy and simple spectrum show that weak mixing carries no entropy or spectral-multiplicity information whatsoever. (c) Rank one and minimal self-joinings are properties of this specific construction, not of cutting-and-stacking systems in general; changing the number of cuts or the spacer pattern changes the mixing behaviour (some cutting-and-stacking constructions are mixing).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["P and Q are probability measures on one measurable space"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T07:39:17.917728+00:00","domain":"total variation, Kullback-Leibler divergence and two-point lower bounds","id":"claim_4b7b88b0a274034c33250c07a3aedbb06cfa837fecc4c43b4b9429a74ecd76ec","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For probability measures P and Q on one space, TV(P, Q) = sup_A |P(A) - Q(A)| and D = D(P || Q) is the Kullback-Leibler divergence in nats (+infinity unless P << Q). For every event A, P(A^c) + Q(A) >= 1 - TV(P, Q), with equality for A = {p >= q}. So the smallest average error of a test between P and Q under equal priors is R* = (1 - TV)/2, and by the Bretagnolle-Huber inequality R* >= (1 - sqrt(1 - exp(-D)))/2 >= (1/4) exp(-D).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:44:17.444165+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4b8d956252286d08bb7c3d0ecee83571a6880cb144acdd59d7104d2e32bb4a77","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:variable-range-eb of arXiv:2608.25551, 'Beyond Optimal Rates in Stochastic Optimization: Trajectory-Adaptive Stopping Rules'] Fix a deterministic integer $t_0 \ge 1$. Let $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \ge t_0-1}$ be a filtration. Let $\{H_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ be a real-valued integrable adapted process, and let $\{c_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ be an almost surely finite,\footnote{No uniform upper bound on the process $\{c_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ is assumed.} nonnegative predictable process such that
\[
    |H_t|
    \le
    c_t
    \qquad
    \text{almost surely for every } t \ge t_0.
\]
Define
\[
    \overline H_{t_0-1}
    \coloneqq
    0,
    \qquad
    \overline H_t
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{s = t_0}^t
    \left(
        H_s - \mathbb{E}[H_s \mid \mathcal{F}_{s-1}]
    \right),
\]
and
\[
    W_{t_0-1}
    \coloneqq
    0,
    \qquad
    W_t
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{s = t_0}^t H_s^2,
    \qquad
    C_t
    \coloneqq
    \max_{t_0 \le s \le t} c_s,
    \qquad
    t \ge t_0.
\]
Then, for every $\alpha \in (0,1)$,
\begin{equation}

    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \forall t \ge t_0:\
        \overline H_t
        \le
        \mathfrak B_\alpha(W_t, C_t)
    \right)
    \ge
    1-\alpha.
\end{equation}
Moreover, the map $(v, b) \mapsto \mathfrak B_\alpha(v, b)$ is nondecreasing in each argument. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:13:18.505546+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4b9123247713378b8558488734fb1bf861f944969c4f7845ce04589a7418ded1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 6 (Compatibility with separable tensor products) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Let $d_1,d_2\ge 1$ and $m\ge 1$.
Let $f,r\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_1},\mathbb{R}^m)$ and $g,u\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_2},\mathbb{R}^m)$.
Define $h,k\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_1+d_2},\mathbb{R}^m)$ by
\[
h(x,y):= f(x)\odot g(y),\qquad
k(x,y):= r(x)\odot u(y),
\]
where $\odot$ denotes the componentwise product: $(a\odot b)_i:=a_i b_i$.
This compatibility will be used later in our separable construction of multivariate vector-valued wavelets.
Then

\[
\langle h,k\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}
=
\langle f,r\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\ \odot\ \langle g,u\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})},
\]
where on the right-hand side $\odot$ denotes the Hadamard (entrywise) product of matrices:
$(A\odot B)_{ij}:=A_{ij}B_{ij}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:39:41.406778+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4ba1f82d003e4715574eb820ed685785d76a70d480e6e3a802da95d76780569c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 3 (Main result; see \Cref{thm:main}) of arXiv:2604.06532, 'Random permutations from $q$-Demazure products'] Fix $q \in (0,1)$ and $p \in (0,1)$.

with deletion probability $1-p$ applied to the standard reduced decomposition of~$w_0$.

  to a deterministic permuton $\mu_{p,q}$.

  \]
  \item The explicit height function of $\mu_{p,q}$ is given in \cref{eq:h_refl,eq:height_rescaling}.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

For f(theta,x)=m^-1 sum_j a_j phi(w_j dot x), width m>=1, centered C1 activation phi(0)=0, c=phi'(0)>0 and beta-Lipschitz derivative beta>=0, let P be the orthogonal projection onto the per-neuron spans of (1,e), and Q=I-P. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:42:55.344468+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4bdd5c67b1900810f440f7cfe4af6c615488f6e40ca304714e653740fc1bda1a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 41 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Assume $q\equiv c>0$ and $a\in C([-L,L])$. For compactly supported $J$, the functions $M$ and $\cH$ are analytic near the origin and $\cH(v)=\sum_{k\ge1}h_{2k}v^{2k}$,
where, writing $D_j=D_j(J)=\int_{\mathbb R}z^jJ(z)\,dz$,
\[
h_2=\frac1{2D_2},\qquad
h_4=-\frac{D_4}{24D_2^4},\qquad
h_6=\frac{D_4^2}{72D_2^7}-\frac{D_6}{720D_2^6}.
\]
For every integer $K\ge1$ and every fixed $1<m<2$,
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})
=\sum_{k=1}^{K}h_{2k}c^{2k}\sigma^{(2k-1)m-2k}
-\max a
+O\!\left(\sigma^{(2K+1)m-(2K+2)}\right)+o(1).
\]
More intrinsically, define $N(m)=\max\{k\ge1:(2k-1)m-2k\le0\}$.
Then the expansion through every nonvanishing order is
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})
=\sum_{k=1}^{N(m)}h_{2k}c^{2k}\sigma^{(2k-1)m-2k}
-\max a+o(1).
\]
The $k$th correction becomes order one at $m=2k/(2k-1)$; the successive thresholds are $4/3,6/5,8/7,\ldots$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["gamma the standard Gaussian measure on R^n","f locally Lipschitz with f and grad f in L^2(gamma)","the generator normalisation L = Laplacian minus x . gradient, which fixes the constant 2"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.628082+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4bdeb13cc86ab526b0013e02b6024d3dede00f91d34eca4a10273fa64375e52c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let gamma be the standard Gaussian measure on R^n. For every locally Lipschitz f with f and grad f in L^2(gamma), Ent_gamma(f^2) <= 2 E_gamma[ |grad f|^2 ], where Ent(g) = E[g log g] - E[g] log E[g] for g >= 0. The constant 2 is sharp, with near-equality for exponentials f = e^{a . x / 2}. As with the Poincare inequality the constant is DIMENSION-FREE, obtained from the one-dimensional case by tensorization of entropy. Gross's theorem states that this inequality is EQUIVALENT to Nelson's hypercontractivity for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup, and it implies the Gaussian Poincare inequality by linearisation. Combined with the Herbst argument it yields Gaussian concentration for Lipschitz functions with the sharp sub-Gaussian variance proxy equal to the square of the Lipschitz constant. Care with normalisation: the inequality is often written as Ent(f) <= 2 E[ |grad sqrt(f)|^2 ] for f >= 0, which is the same statement after substituting f -> f^2, and some sources carry a factor 1/2 from using a different generator normalisation; the version stated here is the one matching the standard Gaussian and the generator L = Laplacian minus x . gradient. [Gross (1975); see Bakry, Gentil and Ledoux, Analysis and Geometry of Markov Diffusion Operators, Chapter 5]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:30:36.754536+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4bfae1048e09d9f51cabc0ff101cf28990f5b6dc711cd87a6c787c074ea9e4fe","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.09246, 'Scaling limit of 1+1 dimensional directed polymer with power-law tail and spatial correlat'] Assume that conditions \textbf{(A)} and \textbf{(B)} hold. Let the tail exponent satisfy $\alpha > \frac{6}{3-2r}$. For a sequence of inverse temperatures $\beta_N$,  the log-partition function $\ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega)$ exhibits the following two limit behaviors:

\noindent
\textbf{(a)} 
If $\beta_N N^{H/2} \to \beta \in (0, \infty)$ as $N \to \infty$, then the log-partition function centered by its multi-order polynomial drift converges in distribution to the logarithm of the continuous Wiener chaos:
$$
    \ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega) - N \sum_{j=2}^{\lfloor 2/H \rfloor} \frac{\beta_N^j}{j!} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\bar{\xi}^j] \sum_{y=-\infty}^{\infty} \psi_y^j \stackrel{D}{\Longrightarrow} \ln Z_{\sqrt{2}\beta}(1, \cdot),
$$
where $Z_{\sqrt{2}\beta}(t, \cdot)$ is the unique solution to the following stochastic heat equation (SHE)
$$
    \partial_t u = \frac{1}{2} \Delta u + \sqrt{2}\beta u \dot{W}, \quad u(0,x) = \delta_0(x),
$$
driven by a centered Gaussian space-time noise $\dot{W}$ with covariance structure
$$
    \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\dot{W}(t,x) \dot{W}(s,y)] = H(2H-1)\delta(t-s) |x-y|^{2H-2}.
$$

\noindent
\textbf{(b)} 
Let $\beta_N N^{H/2} \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$, and there exists a constant $a$ with $0 < a < A_{*}(\alpha, H)$, which is defined in \eqref{A_alpha_H}, such that 
\[
\beta_N N^{H/2} \gg N^{-a}.
\]
Then the normalized fluctuation converges to a Gaussian distribution:
$$
    \frac{1}{\beta_N N^{H/2}} \left( \ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega) - N \sum_{j=2}^{p'} \frac{\beta_N^j}{j!} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\bar{\xi}^j] \sum_{y=-\infty}^{\infty} \psi_y^j \right) \stackrel{D}{\longrightarrow} \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_H^2),
$$
where $p'=\left\lfloor\frac2H\right\rfloor$. \(\text{More generally, \(p'\) can be replaced by any integer }
p\le \lfloor2/H\rfloor
\text{ such that }
\frac{N\beta_N^{p+1}}{\beta_NN^{H/2}}\to0.\) The variance is given by
$$
    \sigma_H^2 = 2H(2H-1) \int_0^1 \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \rho(t,x)\rho(t,y)|x-y|^{2H-2} \,dx \,dy \,dt,
$$
with $\rho(t,x)$ being the standard heat kernel. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-02T01:20:52.931336+00:00","domain":"harvested statement (arXiv 2605.24611, 2026): owner_math","id":"claim_4bfb4312751e7b4b65a99c25a8bda6a321b048b42ff129e2faf2efae009dfffa","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 2 (Limit cycle and basin of attraction) of arXiv:2605.24611, 'Beyond Fixed Points: Superpolynomial Capacity of Asymmetric Hopfield Networks'] A limit cycle of period P ≥1 is a set of distinct states C = {x(0), x(1), . . . , x(P −1)} such that, for the synchronous update map F : {−1, 1}n → {−1, 1}n, we have F(x(i)) = x(i+1) for i = 0, . . . , P −2 and F(x(P −1)) = x(0). The special case P = 1 is a fixed point. The basin of attraction of C is B(C) = {y ∈{−1, +1}n : ∃T ≥ 0 such that F T (y) ∈C}. Clearly, C ⊆B(C); we call C a limit-cycle attractor if C ⊊B(C).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0042-ballisticity-under-the-ellipticity-moment-condition","No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T15:09:50+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4c0573eeb68875a288bad32602cde50741903f8641dcc5a9f41678c4602b28d3","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.168074+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4c11f58e2f57c5e388ed07546352b3dfb6ffc72cfcc09faff48ef8fb92de90ce","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:countable-KL of arXiv:2609.00399, 'Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy and a Conjecture of Tao'] For $s,t\in[0,1]$, define
\[
 \Phi_{\rm rel}(s,t)=
 \begin{cases}
 s\log(s/t)-s+t,&s>0,\ t>0,\\

Equivalently, (1/2π)∫_0^{2π} log|f(Re^{iθ})| dθ - log|f(0)| = Σ_k log(R/|a_k|) = ∫_0^R n(t) dt/t, where n(t) is the number of zeros of f in |z| ≤ t counted with multiplicity. The formula remains valid if f has zeros on the circle |z| = R, the boundary integral still converging absolutely; if f(0) = 0 of order m one applies the formula to f(z)/z^m and adds m log R. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:48:25.142700+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4c46c6a1dbe7ddf1cd9704d0a1a1e438449cf0a0452e6aa8850046fbeeae9192","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:three-causes of arXiv:2607.04620, 'The Exact Ville Identity\\ \large From the Absorbing Case to the General Law\\ with an App'] For a nonnegative supermartingale $(M_n)$ with $M_0=1$ crossing the level $b>1$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The martingale-versus-supermartingale gap governs $D_b$. If $(M_n)$ is a martingale then $\delta_n\equiv0$ and $D_b=0$; the loss term is nonzero precisely to the extent that the process is a strict supermartingale, that is, sheds predictable mass before crossing.
\item Bounded overshoot governs $O_b$. If the conditional landing value satisfies $\mathbb{E}[M_{T_b}\mid \mathcal{F}_{T_b-1},T_b=n]\le b+\omega$ a.s. for a constant $\omega$, then $O_b\le\omega$ ((sec:overshoot of the paper)); on a lattice that includes $b$, $O_b=0$. The overshoot is nonzero precisely to the extent that the increments can carry the process strictly past the boundary.
\item Wobbling governs $R_b$. If, in the martingale case, conditions (i)--(ii) of (thm:wobbling of the paper) hold (sufficient wobbling and bounded overshoot), then $\mathbb{P}(T_b<\infty)=1$, so the survival event is null and $R_b=0$. The residual is nonzero precisely to the extent that wobbling fails -- that is, to the extent that paths can settle and survive forever without crossing.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:35:04.197884+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4c63e8b305c62e41b425da64218ae3cbde2f819431e38f13b4a00ad4ef070029","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] \phantomsection

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If the nested fractal graph is \(h\)-flexible,
then
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+h}}{c_n}=\mu^h.
  
\end{equation}
In particular, \(1\)-flexibility implies
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+1}}{c_n}=\mu.
\]
\item For the regular polygonal \(N\)-gasket with \(N\ge3\) and
\(4\nmid N\), write
\[
  N=4k_N+\ell_N,\qquad
  \ell_N\in\{1,2,3\},\qquad
  s_N=k_N+1,
\]
and put
\[
  h_N
  =
  \gcd\bigl(N-2s_N,\,2s_N-(N-2s_N)\bigr).
\]
Then \(h_N\) is the smallest flexibility step.  In fact, the graph is
\(h_N\)-flexible at scale \(2\), and
\[
  h_N=
  \begin{cases}
    2,&N\equiv2\pmod4,\\
    3,&N\equiv9\pmod{12},\\
    1,&\text{otherwise}.
  \end{cases}
\]
Consequently,
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+h_N}}{c_n}=\mu_N^{h_N}.
\]
\item The standard Vicsek graph is not \(h\)-flexible for any
\(h\ge1\).  Its connective constant is
\(\mu=\sqrt2\), but, for every \(k\ge2\),
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  c_{3^k-2}&=2^{(3^k+1)/2},\\
  c_{3^k-1}&=3\cdot2^{(3^k-3)/2},\\
  c_{3^k}&=3\cdot2^{(3^k-1)/2}.
  \end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
  \frac{c_{3^k-1}}{c_{3^k-2}}=\frac34,
  \qquad
  \frac{c_{3^k}}{c_{3^k-1}}=2,
\]
and the successive ratios do not converge.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:04:06.977065+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4c63f191ae758b090890f63554b58ac65dab68e8c167ac819e61e8dbbb4ddb95","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Function $K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}$ of arXiv:2607.24528, 'On Feige's conjecture'] For \(x,y\geq 0\), let \(a=\min(x,y)\) and \(b=\max(x,y)\). When \(0\leq a<1<b\), let \(\tau(a,b)\) be the larger root of
\[
t^2-b(1+a)t+ab=0.
\]
Define \(K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}\colon[0,\infty)^2\to[0,1]\) by
\[
K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}(a,b)
=
\begin{cases}
1,
& b\leq 1,\\
\frac{2}{\tau(a,b)}-\frac{1}{\tau(a,b)^2},
& 0\leq a<1<b,\\
\frac{1}{ab},
& 1\leq a.
\end{cases}
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:15:55.137874+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4c6523ffb15699853f69977561b606c07a11beb5d5af7460cc8bbf35a33e60a7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:all-is-fair of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, W_\bot, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ be a CK-model. Then $x \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$ for every $x \in W_\bot$ and $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$.
  \begin{proof}
    We use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$.

    It is trivial when $\varphi = \bot$ or $\varphi = p$ for some $p \in \mathord{\mathrm{PropVar}}$.

    Suppose $\varphi = \psi_1 \circledcirc \psi_2$, for $\circledcirc \in \set{\land, \lor}$, then it is easily proven with the induction hypothesis.

    Suppose $\varphi = \psi_1 \to \psi_2$. Take any $x'$ such that $x \leq x' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1$, then $x' \in W_\bot$ by $W_\bot$ being upward closed with respect to $\leq$,
    then $x' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi_2$ by the induction hypothesis. Therefore, $x \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \to \psi_2$ holds.

    Suppose $\varphi = \Box \psi$. Take any $x', y'$ such that $x \leq x' \sqsubset y'$, then $x', y' \in W_\bot$ by $W_\bot$ being upward closed with respect to $\leq$ and $\sqsubset$,
    then $y' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis. Therefore, $x \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$.

    Suppose $\varphi = \Diamond \psi$. Take any $x'$ such that $x \leq x'$, then $x' \in W_\bot$ by $W_\bot$ being upward closed with respect to $\leq$.
    By $W_\bot$ being $\sqsubset$-serial, there is $y'$ such that $x' \sqsubset y'$,
    then $y' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis. Therefore, $x \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:31:20.615284+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4c6c543f211775f81e17258e84be6b56ba7c5c724d2ea53c655e440161959d78","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 20 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $(S,\mathcal{E})$ and $(T,\mathcal{F})$ be coarse spaces.
A map $f : S \rightarrow T$ is called: 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \emph{controlled} (cf.~\cite{BunkeEngel2020}) if, for each $E\in \mathcal{E}$, 
    \[
    \Ad_f(E) = \{ (f(x_1),f(x_2)) \mid (x_1,x_2) \in E \} \subset T \times T
    \]
    is an entourage on $T$, 
    \item  \emph{coarsely proper} (cf.~\cite{LeitnerVigolo2023}) if the set $f^\dagger[D]=f^{-1}(D)$ is bounded in $S$ for any bounded subset $D$ of $T$,  
    \item \emph{coarse} (cf.~\cite{Roe2003LectureCoarse}) if it is controlled and coarsely proper,
    \item  \emph{effectively proper} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZavaCatCoarseGp2020}) if, for any $F\in \mathcal{F}$, the relation 
    \[
    \Ad_{f^\dagger}F = \{ (p,q) \mid (f(p),f(q)) \in F \} \subset S \times S
    \]
    is also an entourage on $S$,
    \item   \emph{a coarse embedding} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZavaCatCoarseGp2020}) if $f$ is controlled and effectively proper,
    \item  \emph{coarsely surjective} (cf.~\cite{LeitnerVigolo2023}) if there exists $F\in \mathcal{F}$ such that $F[f(S)] = T$,
    \item  \emph{a coarse equivalence} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZava2017}) if $f$ is controlled and there exists a controlled map $h: T\to S$ such that $h\circ f\sim \id_S$ and $f\circ h\sim \id_T$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-11-02T23:15:00.816415+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_4cae3f5b9a178a11d166813d4d0e53156585a8a6fbc243f863103d73a4b978a7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Publication record. Y. Shmalo, A Brownian piece in front of a process absolutely continuous with respect to Brownian motion (2026). Burdzy and Scheutzow (Forward Brownian motion, Probab. Theory Related Fields 160 (2014), Problem 7.5) asked whether, for every process X whose law is equivalent to Wiener measure, a random piece of path can be put in front of X so that the new process is a Brownian motion. The paper proves that absolute continuity with respect to Wiener measure is enough: on an extension of the probability space there are a standard Brownian motion B and an almost surely finite random integer N >= 0 with X_t = B_{N+t} - B_N for all t >= 0; N cannot in general be a stopping time for B. More generally, for an invertible measure-preserving map theta of (E, P) and a target law fP, a forward shift theta^N with N built from a P-distributed point and independent uniforms carries P to fP if and only if E[f | I] = 1, I the invariant sigma-field; without the auxiliary uniforms only integer-valued densities can be reached. The construction is Rost's filling scheme (Chacon-Ornstein, Rost 1971) for the unit shift of two-sided Brownian motion. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/brownian-prefix-filling (commit eb410953a445). Not refereed.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:40:59.391506+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4cb461c1c49dcf36134e64f5c27365305ab7868e87a109860bf9648853490ce2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 17 (Phases of the burglars) of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian burg'] The burglar $X$ behaves in the following way depending on the parameter $\nu$ :

- For $\nu \geq 1 $, $X$ does not hit full local time anywhere else than its target, i.e.\ $L_X(T(X),x)<\lambda_0(x)$ for all $x\in I\setminus\{x_0\}$ almost surely.

- For $\nu \in (0,1)$, for any deterministic $x\in I\setminus\{x_0\}$, $L_X(T(X),x)<\lambda_0(x)$ almost surely, but there almost surely exists exceptional $x\in I\setminus\{x_0\}$ such that $L_X(T(X),x)=\lambda_0(x)$. 

- For $\nu \leq  0$, $X$ is ``local-time-filling", i.e.\ for all $x\in I$, $L_X(T(X),x)=\lambda_0(x)$ almost surely.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:53:10.207864+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4cd786f90401a1fa66a664ea5f8dc03669df306bc70c61300bf3f74e7013f574","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi Def:W-homotopy-Equiv of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] Let $(X,\lambda)$ and $(X',\lambda')$ be 
    weighted polyhedra of the same type and
       $f, g: (X,\lambda)\rightarrow (X',\lambda')$ be two  
     W-continuous maps. A \emph{W-homotopy} from $f$ to $g$ relative
to $A\subseteq X$ is a W-continuous map
$$H : (X \times [0, 1],\lambda\times \mathbf{1}) \rightarrow (X',\lambda')$$ which satisfies:
 \begin{itemize}
   \item $H(x, 0) =f(x)$ and $H(x,1)=g(x)$ for all $x\in X$;\vskip 0.1cm
   \item $H(a,t)=f(a)=g(a)$ for all $a\in A$ and 
   $t\in [0,1]$.\vskip 0.1cm
   \end{itemize}
   
   Here $([0,1],\mathbf{1})$ is considered as a weighted polyhedron, and $(X\times [0,1],\lambda\times \mathbf{1})$ is the product $(X,\lambda)$ with
   $([0,1],\mathbf{1})$.
   \vskip 0.1cm
   If there exists a W-homotopy from $f$ to $g$,
   we say that $f$ is \emph{W-homotopic to} $g$.
   If moreover $H$ is weight-preserving, we say
   that $f$ is \emph{strongly W-homotopic to} $g$ (a priori $f$ and $g$ must be both weight-preserving).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:58:53.192689+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4cd9dd1ade8eea879b530c4cc2d3db734d279b76fb3c9c03bc426ad2deeb77e3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 12 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] Let $U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ be a nonempty index set with $|U|=m$ and let
$\pi_U:\mathbb{N}^d\to\mathbb{N}^m$ be the coordinate projection.
Define the projected increments $X_n^{[U]}:=\pi_U(X_n)$.
Then $(X_n^{[U]})_{n\ge 1}$ is an i.i.d.\ sequence on $\mathbb{N}^m$ with pmf

\begin{equation}
f^{[U]}(k_U):=\mathbb{P}(X_1^{[U]}=k_U),
\qquad k_U\in\mathbb{N}^m.
\end{equation}

Assume $f^{[U]}(0_m)<1$ (non-degeneracy in the projected coordinates), and define the
projected renewal chain and counting process by

\begin{equation}
S_0^{[U]}=0_m,
\qquad
S_n^{[U]}=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^{[U]},
\qquad n\ge 1,
\end{equation}

and

\begin{equation}
N^{[U]}(k_U):=\sup\{n\in\mathbb{N}: S_n^{[U]}\le_m k_U\},
\qquad k_U\in\mathbb{N}^m,
\end{equation}

where $\le_m$ denotes componentwise order in $\mathbb{N}^m$.
Its renewal function is

\begin{equation*}
M^{[U]}(k_U):=\mathbb{E}[N^{[U]}(k_U)].
\end{equation*}

\smallskip
\noindent
In particular, for $U=\{u\}$ one recovers the univariate marginal renewal process
$S_n^{[u]}=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^{[u]}$ and the marginal counting process

$N^{[u]}(k_u)=\sup\{n:S_n^{[u]}\le k_u\}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["G finite, p prime with p dividing |G|"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:31:12.478772+00:00","domain":"group theory","id":"claim_4d35593daa64c444cac9ce0985344a1fd51aea56f0ba9d34f01bd81800978194","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let G be a finite group and p a prime dividing the order |G|. Then G contains an element of order exactly p, hence a subgroup of order p. More precisely (McKay), the number of solutions to x^p = e in G is a multiple of p, and since x = e is one of them, there are at least p - 1 elements of order p; in fact the number of elements of order p is congruent to -1 modulo p. Cauchy's theorem is the p^1 case of Sylow's first theorem (a subgroup of order p^a exists whenever p^a divides |G|) and is the converse of Lagrange's theorem for prime orders; the converse of Lagrange fails in general (A_4 has order 12 and no subgroup of order 6).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:07:15.726839+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d3cf72c243ca43f0092b4a117da076edc55df97128ced7bcf0a7570584c3ed8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:vector-valued of arXiv:2608.01279, 'Stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate Hölder diffusion coefficient: uniqueness below'] Let \(d\geq1\), \(\beta\in(2/3,1)\), and let
\[
    G:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times d}
\]
be a measurable mapping that satisfies the following two conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For some constant \(c_G>0\),
\[
    G(z)G(z)^{*}\geq c_G^2 I_d,
    \qquad z\in\mathbb R^d,
\]
\item    For some constant \([G]_{C^\beta}<\infty\),
\begin{equation}
    \|G(z)-G(z')\|_{\mathrm{HS}}
       \leq [G]_{C^\beta}\|z-z'\|^\beta,
    \qquad \forall z,z'\in\mathbb R^d.
    
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

Consider the following vector-valued stochastic heat equation
$$
    \partial_t U
      =\Delta U+G(U)\dot W,
      \qquad
      U(0)=u_0\in L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb R^d),
$$
where \(W=(W^1,\ldots,W^d)\) is a \(d\)-dimensional
space--time white noise.

Then weak uniqueness holds for the above equation in
$
    C\bigl([0,T];L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb R^d)\bigr)
$
for every \(T>0\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.097652+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d4bc2c914255102e0b0fa0df3fd56d972fe9eab9b698b26f4419da6aace4953","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:singleton-renewal of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] For a Kac plane $i$, let
\[
 W_i^\circ=\Pi_{\mathcal W}(\mathsf P_i-N^{-1}I_W)
\]
be its pure-Weyl coefficient.  On the common star space, with an arbitrary
passive ancillary Hilbert space $E$, put
\[
 (\mathsf M h)(i,\theta)=(W_i^\circ\otimes I_E)h(i,\theta),
 \qquad \mathsf J=\mathscr E^*\mathscr E,
 \qquad \mathsf Q=I-\mathsf J.
\]
Relative to $\operatorname{ran}\mathsf J\oplus
\operatorname{ran}\mathsf Q$, write
\[
 \mathsf M=
 \begin{pmatrix}0&\mathsf S^-\\ \mathsf S^+&\mathsf V\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{3.2.10n}
\]
We call $0,\mathsf S^-,\mathsf S^+,\mathsf V$ the four
\emph{star statuses} of a passive singleton; a status record chooses one
of these four blocks for every singleton after equal-time fusion.  These
statuses are distinct from the derivative-placement coefficients

Then
\[
 \|\mathsf S^-\|=\|\mathsf S^+\|
 \le\sqrt{\frac{n-3}{N(n-1)}}\le N^{-1/2},
 \qquad \|\mathsf V\|\le2,
\tag{3.2.10o}
\]
and the one-sided utilized-step maps factor through the innovation:
\[
 \mathscr E\mathsf M\mathscr T=\mathscr E\mathsf M\mathscr G,
 \qquad
 \mathscr T^*\mathsf M\mathscr E^*
 =\mathscr G^*\mathsf M\mathscr E^*.
\tag{3.2.10p}
\]
Consequently a passive singleton isolated between invariant separators is
zero.  A run of $s\ge2$ passive singletons with $s-1$ prescribed finite
Green gates has norm at most
\[
 \frac{2^{2s-3}}N.
\tag{3.2.10q}
\]
Thus its two endpoints create one $N^{-1}$ resource and every interior

    \[ \frac{\partial}{\partial v}\mathrm{I}(X_t^i\ ;\,X_v^{-i}) = \bE_{x_t^i, x_v^{-i}} \left[\left(Q^{-i}_v \log \Pr(X_t^i = x_t^i \mid \cdot\ )\right)(x_v^{-i})\right]; \]

    \item for $i \in [d]$, we have
    \[ \frac{\partial}{\partial t}\mathrm{I}(X_t^i\ ;\,X_v^{-i}) = \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \mathcal{H}(X_t^i) + \bE_{x_t^i, x_v^{-i}} \left[\left(Q^{i}_t \log \Pr(\,\cdot \mid X_v^{-i} = x_v^{-i}\,)\right)(x_t^i)\right]; \]

    \item 
    \begin{align*}
        \sum_{i \in [d]} \frac{\partial}{\partial v} \mathrm{I}(X_t^i\ ;\, X_v^{-i}) \bigg\rvert_{t = v} &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} v} \mathrm{DTC}(X_v), \qquad \text{and} \qquad
        \sum_{i \in [d]} \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \mathrm{I}(X_t^i\ ;\, X_v^{-i}) \bigg\rvert_{v = t} = \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} \mathrm{TC}(X_t);
    \end{align*}

    \item for fixed $x_v^{-i}$, $j$, and $b$, let us define  
    \[ r(a) = \frac{\Pr(X_t^i = a \mid X_v^{-i} = x_v^{-i})}{\Pr(X_t^i = a \mid X_v^{-i} = x_v^{-i} \odot_j b)}.\]
    It then obeys
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\partial^2}{\partial t \partial v} \mathrm{I}(X_t^i\ ;\, X_v^{-i}) 
        &= \bE_{x_v^{-i}} \sum_{j \neq i} \sum_{a, b, c}\cQ_v(x_v^j, b) \cQ_t(a, c)\Pr(X_t^i = a \mid x_v^{-i} \odot_j b) \times \left[r(a) \log \frac{r(a)}{r(c)} + r(c) - r(a) \right].
    \end{align*}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["phi_i 1-Lipschitz with phi_i(0) = 0","eps_i independent Rademacher signs","T bounded so the suprema are finite; constant 1 WITHOUT absolute values, 2 WITH them"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.628629+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d71e82701baa0652e97a3150c16f319f1bfdeca9e4a8d8cfae7f2157af90f94","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let T be a bounded subset of R^n, let eps_1, ..., eps_n be independent Rademacher signs, and let phi_i : R -> R be 1-Lipschitz with phi_i(0) = 0 for every i. Then E sup_{t in T} sum_{i=1}^n eps_i phi_i(t_i) <= E sup_{t in T} sum_{i=1}^n eps_i t_i. With ABSOLUTE VALUES inside the supremum the same statement holds with a factor 2: E sup_{t in T} | sum_i eps_i phi_i(t_i) | <= 2 E sup_{t in T} | sum_i eps_i t_i |. The distinction between the constants 1 and 2 is a standard source of misquotation; the constant 1 belongs to the version WITHOUT absolute values. The hypothesis phi_i(0) = 0 is needed for the version without absolute values and can be arranged by subtracting a constant, which is harmless for a symmetric process. In statistical learning the principle is what lets one strip a Lipschitz loss off a function class without changing the Rademacher complexity by more than a constant. [Ledoux and Talagrand, Probability in Banach Spaces, Theorem 4.12]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["F entire on C (or C^d)","claims of band limitation require the growth bound off the real axis","L^2 version needs square integrability on R; distributions need the polynomial-growth version"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.264631+00:00","domain":"complex and harmonic analysis, common errors","id":"claim_4d88e0d15b6e8881d2eb18cd54107f75b8c1834afa521c13029e34cc2e348e2d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypotheses: (1) the growth bound $|F(z)|\\le Ce^{A|z|}$ must hold for all complex $z$, not merely on $\\mathbb R$; (2) $F$ must be square integrable on $\\mathbb R$ (for the $L^2$ version) or have controlled polynomial growth (for the distributional version). Failure of (1): $F(z)=e^{-z^2}$ is entire and its restriction to $\\mathbb R$ is in $L^2$, yet $|F(iy)|=e^{y^2}$, so $F$ is of order 2, not of exponential type; its Fourier transform is a Gaussian, supported everywhere - no band limitation. Failure of (2): $F(z)=\\cos(Az)$ is entire of exponential type exactly $A$ and bounded on $\\mathbb R$, but not in $L^2(\\mathbb R)$; it is not $\\int_{-A}^A\\varphi(t)e^{itz}dt$ for any $\\varphi\\in L^2$, only for the measure $\\frac12(\\delta_A+\\delta_{-A})$ - the correct statement in that regime is the Paley-Wiener-Schwartz theorem for compactly supported distributions, with a polynomial factor $(1+|\\zeta|)^N$ allowed. Similarly $F(z)=e^{Az}$ has type $A$ but grows on the real axis. Two further traps: the exponential factor in Paley-Wiener-Schwartz measures the support of the transform only through the supporting function of its convex hull, so the theorem detects $\\operatorname{ch}(\\operatorname{supp}u)$, not the support itself; and no such function can have both itself and its transform compactly supported, since a nonzero entire function cannot vanish on an open set (see Benedicks' theorem for the measure-theoretic strengthening).","status":"unverified"}

\in \sqcup_{m=1}^{\infty} \SRm $ such that $

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:32:35.572375+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d8dd37cc870c042d2c739c5c64707ff5d28cdf721b491d658978013ec700ff6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:matrix.normal.Wishart.operator.connection of arXiv:2606.04859, 'Stein's method for the Wishart distribution'] Let $\nu\in [d, \infty)\cap \mathbb{N}$, $\Sigma\in \mathcal{S}_{++}^d$, and let $f:\mathcal{S}_{++}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be smooth. Set
\[
\mathcal{R}_{\nu,d} \vcentcolon= \{X\in \mathbb{R}^{\nu\times d}: \mathrm{rank}(X)=d\}.
\]
The set $\mathcal{R}_{\nu,d}$ is open, and its complement has Lebesgue measure zero. For $X\in \mathcal{R}_{\nu,d}$, define $g_f(X) = f(X^{\top}X)$. Then, pointwise on $\mathcal{R}_{\nu,d}$,
\begin{equation}
\left(\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{OU}}g_f\right)(X) = \left(\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{W}}_{\nu, \Sigma} \, f\right)(X^{\top}X), \qquad X\in \mathcal{R}_{\nu,d},
\end{equation}
where $\nabla f$ denotes the symmetric gradient in the variable $S$ and
\[
\left(\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{W}}_{\nu, \Sigma} \, f\right)(S) = 2 \, \mathrm{tr}\{(\nu\Sigma - S)\nabla f(S)\} + 4 \, \mathrm{tr}\{S \nabla \Sigma \nabla f(S)\}, \qquad S\in \mathcal{S}_{++}^d.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X_1, ..., X_n independent","Z = f(X) nonnegative with E[Z log Z] finite"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.627951+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4dc336ffe1859932768872cd898d8a70b2b6935d4bd7b90c575ded181869d08f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent random variables and let Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n) be a nonnegative random variable with E[Z log Z] finite. Write Ent(Z) = E[Z log Z] - E[Z] log E[Z] and let Ent^{(i)}(Z) denote the same functional computed with respect to X_i alone, with the other coordinates held fixed. Then Ent(Z) <= sum_{i=1}^n E[ Ent^{(i)}(Z) ]. The same statement with variance in place of entropy is the Efron-Stein inequality, and the two are the p = 2 and p = 1 members of a family of phi-entropies that all tensorize. Tensorization is what converts a ONE-DIMENSIONAL functional inequality into an n-dimensional one with no loss of constant: if each coordinate's law satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant C, then the product law satisfies it with the SAME constant C, independent of n. That dimension-free feature is the whole reason the entropy method produces concentration bounds that do not degrade as n grows. Independence of the coordinates is essential. [standard; e.g. Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities, Theorem 4.10 and Section 4.1]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:41:11.635894+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4dc3f1bcec7db304a707ed1904c1873b2db694de992292bd0c81d99a5696c2e8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma terms_in_signature_first of arXiv:2411.13707, 'High-degree cubature on Wiener space \\ through unshuffle expansions'] \[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:49.842905+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4dc98dd7c31a684b85e53b3e98a5154dab9b984bd93f17570fe8ea405a2d33d8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2506.13913, '2506.13913'] {Existence and uniqueness theorem for SDEs}{existence-uniqueness}
Let \((\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \geq 0}, \mathbb{P})\) be a filtered probability space, and let \(\{W_t\}_{t \geq 0}\) be a standard \(m\)-dimensional Brownian motion adapted to the filtration \(\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \geq 0}\). Consider the SDE in \(\mathbb{R}^d\)
\[
\mathrm{d}X_t = \mu(t, X_t) \, \mathrm{d}t + \sigma(t, X_t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t, \quad X_0=Z,
\]
where \(Z\) is a random variable, \(\mathcal{F}_0\)-measurable, with \(\mathbb{E}[\|X_0\|^2] < \infty\). Furthermore, assume the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
    \item {Lipschitz continuity:} There exist constants \(L_{\mu}, L_\sigma > 0\) such that for all \(t \in [0, T]\) and \(x, y \in \mathbb{R}^d\)
    \[
    \|\mu(t, x) - \mu(t, y)\| \leq L_{\mu} \|x - y\|, \quad
    \|\sigma(t, x) - \sigma(t, y)\|_F \leq L_\sigma \|x - y\|,
    \]
    where \(\|\cdot\|_F\) denotes the Frobenius norm.
    
    \item {Linear growth:} There exist constants \(K_{\mu}, K_\sigma > 0\) such that for all \(t \in [0, T]\) and \(x \in \mathbb{R}^d\)
    \[
    \|\mu(t, x)\| \leq K_{\mu}(1 + \|x\|), \quad \|\sigma(t, x)\|_F \leq K_\sigma(1 + \|x\|).
    \]
\end{itemize}

Then, there exists a unique stochastic process \(\{X_t\}_{t \geq 0}\) satisfying the SDE such that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Existence:} The solution \(X_t\) exists, is adapted to \(\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \geq 0}\), and satisfies
    \[
    \mathbb{E} \left[ \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \|X_t\|^2 \right] < \infty.
    \]
    \item \textbf{Uniqueness:} If \(\{X_t\}\) and \(\{Y_t\}\) are two solutions with the same initial condition \(Z\), then
    \[
    \mathbb{P} \left( X_t = Y_t, \, \forall t \in [0, T] \right) = 1.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

	where

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:11:11.695099+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4e2841da640a398408c72f98a4c00ba304f3a51379b2beecfbd04e38294d3c1f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:whole-plane-persistence of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Fix $\kappa,M,R>0$.  Then there exists $C=C(\kappa,M,R)>0$ such that the following
holds.  For $\varepsilon>0$, let
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \omega_{\varepsilon,0}\geq0,\qquad
  \int_{\mathbb R^2}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=\kappa,
  \qquad
  \|\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty\leq M\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R\varepsilon}(\mathbf0).
\end{equation}
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding Yudovich
solution of the two-dimensional Euler equation in $\mathbb R^2$.  Then
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})^2
  \leq C\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0}).
\end{equation}
If, in addition,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})\leq\frac{\kappa^2}{C},
\end{equation}
then, with
\[
  \mathbf X_\varepsilon
  :=\frac1\kappa\int_{\mathbb R^2}\mathbf x
  \omega_{\varepsilon,0}(\mathbf x)\,\mathrm d\mathbf x,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf X_\varepsilon|
  \leq (1+\sqrt2)R\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  |\mathbf b|
  \leq(2+\sqrt2)R\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
In particular, for any family of initial data satisfying
(equation eq:whole-plane-initial-data of the paper) with the same $\kappa,M,R$, if
$\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})\to0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, then
\[
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})\longrightarrow0,
  \qquad
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in
  \mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}|\mathbf b|\longrightarrow0.
\]","status":"unverified"}

The integral form: for f and g both monotone in the same direction on [0,1], the integral of f g is at least the product of the integrals. {"assumptions":["Y = sum_{k>=0} B_k (2/3)^k with i.i.d. digits B_k, P(B_k=1)=p (the biased-coin Bernoulli convolution at contraction ratio lambda=2/3, equivalently the same non-Pisot ratio 3/2 used elsewhere in this campaign)","elementary dimension bound only: Hochman's theorem is NOT used; only the entropy-over-Lyapunov upper bound on dimension and the fact that a measure on R of dimension below 1 cannot be absolutely continuous"],"created_at":"2026-09-24T23:46:59.956588+00:00","domain":"probability/Bernoulli convolutions","id":"claim_4e3f794ecd634c87b21e676f1227583d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For the biased Bernoulli convolution at ratio 2/3 - the law of sum_k B_k (2/3)^k with B_k i.i.d., P(B_k = 1) = p - the measure is singular for every p < p* = 0.140277, where p* solves H(p) = log(3/2) in natural logarithms (H(p)/log(3/2) = 0.4896, 0.8018, 1.2341, 1.7095 at p = 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 1/2). Proof: the dimension of the measure is at most the entropy-over-Lyapunov ratio H(p)/log(3/2), and a measure on the line of dimension below one is not absolutely continuous; Hochman's theorem is needed only for the matching lower bound dim = min(1, H(p)/log(3/2)), which this does not use. Two further thresholds govern the Fourier criterion at this ratio. The biased factor |(1-p) + p e^{i phi}|^2 = 1 - 2p(1-p)(1 - cos phi) has arithmetic mean 1 - 2p(1-p) over the phase, which gives the annealed (main-term) exponent alpha(p) = 1 + log(1 - 2p(1-p))/log(3/2), zero at p(1-p) = 1/6, i.e. p = (1 - 3^{-1/2})/2 = 0.211325; and log-mean 2 log(1-p), which gives the quenched (typical) threshold (3/2)(1-p)^2 = 1 at p = 0.183503. As a calibration control for statistics on the unbiased Bernoulli convolution at 2/3 (the same ratio, frequencies and arithmetic, only the weights changed): below p* the measure is singular and a detection is expected; above 0.2113 the main term decays and a pass is expected; between 0.1403 and 0.2113 the measure has dimension one while the main term already diverges, so a reading there means nothing - controls belong at p <= 0.12 and p >= 0.35. Unlike the Pisot control lambda = 1/phi, where one localised cell forces the reading a priori, the absence of such a cell at ratio 3/2 is Mahler's open problem on ||(3/2)^m xi||, so the control's genuineness rests on an empirical extensiveness test: a flat per-step rate means one cell forces the reading, a wobbling rate means a real measurement (flat to 0.0005 at 1/phi from K = 8; wobbling by 0.028 at the unbiased 2/3).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:59:45.010899+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4e515b945cd1cebba6e1622ec02ad7403e8e8f394a8fe204d807fde695330790","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem small-frequency-abelian-estimates of arXiv:2605.13004, 'Orientation in Poisson Cluster Processes via Imaginary Bispectra'] Let $\overline H(x):=\int_x^\infty h(u)\,du\sim x^{-\alpha}L(x)$ with $0<\alpha\le2$, where $L$ is slowly varying. Write $L_t:=L(1/t)$,
\[
U(t):=\int_0^\infty \cos(tu)h(u)\,du,
\qquad
V(t):=\int_0^\infty \sin(tu)h(u)\,du.
\]
Then, as $t\downarrow0$, the following estimates hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $0<\alpha<1$, then
\[
1-U(t)\sim S(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t,
\qquad
V(t)\sim C(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t,
\]
where
\[
S(\alpha)=\frac{\pi/2}{\Gamma(\alpha)\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},
\qquad
C(\alpha)=\frac{\pi/2}{\Gamma(\alpha)\cos(\pi\alpha/2)}.
\]
\item If $\alpha=1$, then
\[
1-U(t)\sim \frac{\pi}{2}tL_t,
\qquad
2V(t)-V(2t)\sim 2(\log2)tL_t.
\]
More explicitly, with $J(x):=\int_1^x u^{-1}L(u)\,du$, the potentially larger slowly varying contribution to $V(t)$ is of order $tJ(1/t)$, and it cancels in $2V(t)-V(2t)$ because
\[
J(1/t)-J(1/(2t))\sim (\log2)L_t.
\]
\item If $1<\alpha<2$, then $\mu_1:=\int_0^\infty u h(u)\,du<\infty$, and
\[
1-U(t)\sim S(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t,
\qquad
V(t)-\mu_1t\sim C(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t.
\]
\item If $\alpha=2$, then $\mu_1:=\int_0^\infty u h(u)\,du<\infty$,
\[
V(t)-\mu_1t\sim -\frac{\pi}{2}t^2L_t,
\qquad
2V(t)-V(2t)\sim \pi t^2L_t.
\]
Moreover, if $R_2(x):=1+\int_1^x u^{-1}L(u)\,du$, then
\[
1-U(t)=O(t^2R_2(1/t)),
\qquad
 tR_2(1/t)=o(L_t).
\]
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

  \mu\left(A\mid B\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\frac{\left(\mu_{1}+\mu_{2}\right)\left(A\cap B\right)}{\left(\mu_{1}+\mu_{2}\right)\left(B\right)}e_{+}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:57:28.723939+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4e92ce6e9b8fc59cb1d4748bc8c36496d4a69b015f697587300eb89a24e12c0a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $f:\Rsf^m\to\Rsf$ be a smooth, compactly supported function and let $\varepsilon, \tilde{\varepsilon}, \delta, \zeta\in [0,\infty)$ and $a,b, \tilde{a},\tilde{b}\in\Rsf^m$ be such that 
	\[
		|b-a|\leq \varepsilon, 
			\quad 
		|\tilde{b}-\tilde{a}|\leq \tilde{\varepsilon}, 
			\quad 
		|\tilde{a}-a|\leq \delta, 
			\quad\mbox{and}\quad 
		|\tilde{b}-\tilde{a} - (b-a)| \leq \zeta.
	\]
Let also $T_0,T_1: \Rsf^m\times\Rsf^m\to\Rsf$ be defined by 
	\begin{align*}
		& T_0(x,y):= f(y)-f(x),\\
		& T_1(x,y):= f(y)-f(x)- \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^j}(x)(y^j-x^j)
	\end{align*}
for $x,y\in\Rsf^m$. Then
	\[
		\left|T_0(a,b)\right|  \lesssim \varepsilon 
		\quad\mbox{and}\quad
		|T_0(\tilde{a},\tilde{b})-T_0(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon(\delta + \zeta) + \zeta,
	\]
and
	\[
		 |T_1(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon^2
		 \quad \mbox{and}\quad 
		 |T_1(\tilde{a},\tilde{b})-T_1(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon^2(\delta + \zeta) + (\varepsilon + \tilde{\varepsilon})\zeta
	\]
where the constants are non-decreasing functions of $C^1$, $C^2$, $C^2$, and $C^3$ norm of $f$, respectively. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

\[
 f_\varepsilon=(\omega+\varepsilon)^\alpha,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.222512+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4ec5ac7206a02ee269e114086078147bb6c150f5945dff018a8b030b50638a48","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 29 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Let $B$ be a ball in $\R^d.$
Suppose that $U$ is an open subset of $B$. A Borel function $u$ on
$B$ is said to be:
\begin{itemize}
\item harmonic in $U$ with respect to $X^{b, B}$ if
\begin{equation}
u(x) = \E_x[u(X^{b, B}_{\tau^b_{V}})],\qquad
x\in V,
\end{equation}
for every bounded open set $V$ with $\overline{V}\subset U$;

\item excessive with respective to $X^{b, B}$ if $u$ is
nonnegative and for every $t > 0$ and $x\in B$
\[
u(x) \geq \E_x[u(X^{b, B}_{t})]
\quad\mbox{and}\quad u(x) = \lim_{t \downarrow0}
\E_x[u(X^{b, B}_t)];
\]

\item a potential with respect to $X^{b, B}$ if it is excessive
with respect to $X^{b, B}$ and for every sequence $\{U_n\}_{n \ge1}$
of open sets with
$\overline{U}_n \subset U_{n+1}$ and $\bigcup_n U_n = B$,
\[
\lim_{n \to\infty}
\E_x[u(X^{b, B}_{\tau^b_{U_n}})] = 0,\qquad
\xi_B\mbox{-a.e. } x\in B;
\]

\item a pure potential with respect to $X^{b, B}$ if
it is a potential with respect to $X^{b, B}$ and

\[
\lim_{t \to\infty} \E_x[u(X^{b, B}_t)] = 0,\qquad
\xi_B \mbox{-a.e. } x\in B.
\]

\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:24:20.645892+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4ec873d06ff22a2b37214214c7389d6627ae122b760d7d702368898982b7647c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:main1 of arXiv:2608.11084, 'Sharp Frobenius-Norm Concentration for Sample Moment Tensors'] Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered sub-Gaussian random
vector \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and
sub-Gaussian constant \(K\). Let \(p\ge 2\) be an integer. Then, for every
\(q\ge1\),
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(
\mathbbm{E}
\bigg\|
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}
-
\mathbbm{E} X^{\otimes p}
\bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q
\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)^{1/q}
\lesssim_p
K^p
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(
\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N}
+
\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}
+
\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}
\aftergroup\egroup\originalright),
\]
where
\[
\rho_p(\Sigma)
:=
\begin{cases}
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2},
& p \text{ even},\\[3pt]
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2},
& p \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\]
Moreover, if $X$ is Gaussian, then
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathbbm{E} \bigg\|
\frac{1}{N}
\sum_{i=1}^N
X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbbm{E} X^{\otimes p}
\bigg\|_{\mathsf{F}}^q\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)^{1/q}
\asymp_p
\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt{N}}
+
\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q}{N}}
+
\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N},
\]
where
\[
\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)
:=
\begin{cases}
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt]
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["entries independent up to symmetry with mean 0 and variance 1 before scaling by 1/sqrt n","moments bounded uniformly in n (finite fourth moment suffices for the semicircle limit of the empirical spectral distribution; the diagonal entries may have a different variance)","the moment method identifies the limit because the semicircle law is determined by its moments (compact support)"],"created_at":"2026-09-02T07:51:33.049288+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory (hand-authored statement with hypotheses, 2026-09-02)","id":"claim_4f1567c38734286426940b4f4f52f264db38c2264b6a25725643dc91aea4918c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"For the semicircle density (1/(2 pi)) sqrt(4 - x^2) on [-2, 2] (mean 0, variance 1), all odd moments vanish and the 2k-th moment equals the Catalan number C_k = (1/(k+1)) binom(2k, k): 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, 132, ... . A semicircle of radius R has 2k-th moment C_k (R/2)^{2k}. In the moment method for a Wigner matrix W = X / sqrt n, where X is real symmetric with independent entries above the diagonal, mean 0 and variance 1, the normalized traces satisfy E tr(W^{2k}) / n -> C_k: expanding the trace as a sum over closed walks of length 2k on the index set, only walks whose edges are each traversed exactly twice and whose underlying graph is a tree survive as n grows, and such walks are counted by C_k; the Catalan numbers determine the semicircle law uniquely because it has compact support. Wigner's theorem then follows from convergence of moments plus a variance bound (or a concentration bound on the trace) giving weak convergence of the empirical spectral distribution in probability.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f holomorphic on a punctured disc around a, a an isolated essential singularity","the conclusion is density, not surjectivity: Picard's great theorem is the stronger, deeper statement"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:05:27.626465+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_4f2a0d209f59418cfbe6a3e636baf86d6aab06cd28c72428263a3b5173a5e488","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f be holomorphic on a punctured disc D' = { 0 < |z - a| < r } and suppose a is an essential singularity of f (neither removable nor a pole; equivalently the Laurent series at a has infinitely many negative-power terms). Then for every 0 < rho < r the image f({ 0 < |z - a| < rho }) is dense in C: for every w in C and every eps > 0 there are points z arbitrarily close to a with |f(z) - w| < eps. Equivalently, every complex number is a limit of f along some sequence z_n -> a. The three singularity types are thereby characterised by the behaviour of |f| near a: bounded (removable, Riemann), tending to infinity (pole), neither (essential). Picard's great theorem sharpens density to: f takes every complex value with at most one exception infinitely often in every punctured neighbourhood of a (exp(1/z) omits 0).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:08.844621+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4f3a76af7669e71634cef341c091b25d6e3fca816ad2d4eac83135014d29ad47","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi 4 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $(\A,\tau)$ be a $W^\ast$-probability space, and let $a\in\A$ (just $L^2(\A,\tau)$ suffices).  Then $a^\ast a = |a|^2$ is selfadjoint, and so has a spectral measure $\mu_{|a|^2}$: the unique compactly-supported probability distribution on $\R_+$ whose moments are given by $\int x^k \mu_{|a|^2}(dx) = \tau[(a^\ast a)^k]$ (see \eqref{eq.spectral.meas}).  Denote by $\nu_a$ the push-forward of $\mu_{|a|^2}$ under $x\mapsto\sqrt{x}$; in other words, $\nu_a$ is the spectral measure of $|a|:=\sqrt{a^\ast a}$.

For $z\in\C$, define the {\bf log potential} $U_a\colon\C\to\R\cup\{-\infty\}$ by
\[ U_a(z):= \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^\infty \log(x)\,\nu_{a-z}(dx). \]
It is a subharmonic function, and so its (weak) Laplacian is a positive Radon measure.  In this case it is a probability measure: the {\bf Brown measure of $a$}
\[ \mu_a:= \Delta U_a \quad \text{i.e.} \quad
\int_{\C} \psi\,d\mu_a = \int_{\C} \Delta\psi(z)\, U_a(z)\,dz \qquad \forall\,\psi\in C^\infty(\C). \]
The Brown measure is then also uniquely defined by 
\[ \int_{\C} \log |\lambda-z|\,\mu_a(d\lambda) = U_a(z). \]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:42.499458+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_4f46b2de22e7549670bcc1dce7b0f972c96bfd2b3336d5d4426cf06f59a598fa","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"The Weierstrass convergence theorem (a locally uniform limit of holomorphic functions is holomorphic and derivatives converge locally uniformly) has no real-variable analogue and does not upgrade to uniform convergence on the whole domain. (1) Real failure: f_n(x) = sin(n^2 x)/n converges to 0 uniformly on R, but the derivatives f_n'(x) = n cos(n^2 x) do not converge to the derivative of the limit — at x = 0, f_n'(0) = n → ∞ — so uniform convergence of real functions carries no information about derivatives. More dramatically, by the Weierstrass approximation theorem every continuous nowhere differentiable function on [0,1] is a uniform limit of polynomials, so uniform limits of real-analytic functions need not be differentiable anywhere. The complex proof uses the Cauchy estimates, which need holomorphy on a two-dimensional neighborhood: a bound on |g| on a disk controls all derivatives at the center. (2) Only locally uniform: f_n(z) = z^n/n converges to 0 uniformly on all of D, yet f_n'(z) = z^{n-1} has supremum 1 on D for every n and does not converge uniformly on D. So the derivative statement must be quoted with 'uniformly on compact subsets'; deducing a uniform derivative bound up to the boundary from a uniform bound on the functions is a genuine error, and controlling it requires extra input (a larger domain of holomorphy, or boundary regularity). (3) The hypothesis is convergence on compact subsets of the open set, not convergence on the closed set: a sequence converging uniformly on the closed unit disk still gives derivative convergence only on |z| ≤ r < 1 unless the functions are holomorphic on a larger disk.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:25:39.116617+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4f52df7591d276d237c39a099ff651be4172081a5ae7f970158d4c820b49a008","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def: partition procedure in sle of arXiv:2606.13147, 'Scaling limits of the single-curve interface and outermost loops in the planar random fiel'] Fix a sufficiently small constant $\iota>0$, and set
$M=\iota r^{3\kappa}N.$
For a box $\mathsf{B}$, write
$S_\gamma(\mathsf{B}):=\sum_{x\in\mathsf{B}}{\operatorname{dist}}(x,\gamma)^{-1/4}.$
We define the following recursive partition procedure. We first partition $\Lambda_N$ into boxes of side length $M$. Given a current box $\mathsf{B}$, we proceed as follows.

If
$
S_\gamma(\mathsf{B})<M^{7/4},
$
we leave $\mathsf{B}$ unchanged.
If
$
S_\gamma(\mathsf{B})\ge M^{7/4},
$
we divide $\mathsf{B}$ into two sub-boxes according to the following rule. Suppose, after translation and rotation if necessary, that
$
\mathsf{B}=[1,a]\times[1,b],
1\le a\le b.
$
For \(0\le c\le b\), let
$
\mathsf{C}_1(c)=[1,a]\times[1,c],
\mathsf{C}_2(c)=[1,a]\times[c+1,b],
$
with the convention that empty boxes are omitted. We choose \(c\) so that
$
\big|S_\gamma(\mathsf{C}_1(c))-S_\gamma(\mathsf{C}_2(c))\big|
$
is minimized, and replace \(\mathsf{B}\) by the two boxes \(\mathsf{C}_1(c)\) and \(\mathsf{C}_2(c)\).

We repeat this procedure until every current box \(\mathsf{B}\) satisfies
$
S_\gamma(\mathsf{B})<M^{7/4}.
$
The resulting collection of boxes is denoted by
$
\mathsf{B}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{B}_n.
$
Finally, we set
$
\mathsf{B}_i^+=\mathsf{B}_i\cap\Lambda^+,
\mathsf{B}_i^-=\mathsf{B}_i\cap\Lambda^-.
$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:57:44.953885+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4f5dff5fb5481dde234608b4ce64fde970eac83c8839ed1da5bbada7612e03d7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 3 of arXiv:2606.25494, 'A functional central limit theorem for kernel gradient flow and infinitesimal gradient boo'] \begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] Suppose that
    \[
    (X_{0,n}, G_n) \xrightarrow{a.s.} (x_0, g)

{"assumptions":["f is entire","M(r) denotes the maximum modulus on the circle of radius r"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:42.483753+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_4f9f621425ba3aa6639c052588aacad670196f81a185514037630e2dd0e75a91","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f be a nonconstant entire function and M(r) = max_{|z| = r} |f(z)|. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:30:50.720061+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4fa9790dd3e01aed38d65fabc6a8058bf2f13dcffb837f07fdfa5ccc041832c2","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def-sect of arXiv:2609.02769, 'Divergence-Free Approximation in Sobolev and Lebesgue Spaces on general unbounded domains '] Let $\omega\in[0,\pi)$. We define the closed sector of angle $\omega$ in the complex plane by
	$$
	\Sigma_\omega
	:=
	\{0\neq z\in\mathbb{C}:|\arg z|\leq\omega\}\cup\{0\}=
	\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\{

	\aftergroup\egroup\originalright\}.
	$$
	A linear operator $\mathcal{T}$ on a
	Banach space $\mathbb{X}$, with dense domain and range, is said to be \emph{sectorial
		of type $\omega$} if its spectrum contained in $\Sigma_{\omega}$, that is, 
	$$

Moreover, for every $\theta\in(\omega,\pi)$, the resolvent operators satisfy the uniform bound
\begin{align*}
	\sup\limits_{\lambda\notin\Sigma_{\theta}}\|\lambda(\lambda\mathrm{I}-\mathcal{T})^{-1}\|_{\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{X})}<\infty.
\end{align*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:27:14.894452+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4fc2974bc3b1c341456cddc85e347396fc20c1b7a3a5d234cac51a04c7c4db3f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.23960, 'Learning from Uncertainty-dependent Missing Labels for Semi-supervised Classification'] Let \(\theta_0\) denote the true parameter of the augmented complete-data model
\(p_{\theta_0}(Y,Z,M)\), where \(M\) is the mechanism-generated missingness
indicator. Let
\[
  S_{\rm aug}(Y,Z,M;\theta_0)
  =
  \nabla_\theta \log p_\theta(Y,Z,M)\big|_{\theta=\theta_0}
\]
be the corresponding augmented complete-data score, and define
\[
  \mathcal I_{\rm aug}(\theta_0)
  =
  \operatorname{Var}\{S_{\rm aug}(Y,Z,M;\theta_0)\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal G\) be any observed sigma-field obtained by coarsening the
augmented data, for example
\[
  \mathcal G=\sigma(Y,M,Z^{\rm obs},R),
\]
where \(R\) denotes any design randomization. Define the design information
\[
  \mathcal I_{\rm des}(\theta_0)
  =
  \operatorname{Var}\!\left[
    E\{S_{\rm aug}(Y,Z,M;\theta_0)\mid \mathcal G\}
  \right].
\]
Then
\[
  \mathcal I_{\rm des}(\theta_0)
  \preceq
  \mathcal I_{\rm aug}(\theta_0).
\]
Consequently, no regular estimator based on the coarsened observed experiment
can have asymptotic variance below the information bound for the augmented full
experiment, whenever the relevant information matrices are nonsingular. Equality
can occur only when the augmented complete-data score is
\(\mathcal G\)-measurable almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:46:36.094693+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4fe7d6a4fc47d555d7442b06471ec12b1d6bd49bb673a0819417ff13efd5687e","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:uniform-approximate-Goh of arXiv:2609.02710, 'Asymptotic Mean Value Laplacian\\ on equiregular sub-Riemannian manifolds'] Let $X^\lambda=(X_1^\lambda,\ldots,X_k^\lambda)$ be a jointly smooth
family of vector fields on $\mathbb R^n$, all supported in one fixed compact set,
with $\lambda\in\Theta$.  Let $\mathcal A\subset\Theta\times
L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^k)$ be compact for the strong $L^2$ topology, and assume
that every $(\lambda,u)\in\mathcal A$ is energy minimizing between its
endpoints and that
\[
 \sup\{\|u\|_{L^\infty}:(\lambda,u)\in\mathcal A\}<\infty.
\]
Write $E_\lambda$ for the endpoint map from $0$, set
\[
 J(u):=\frac12\|u\|_{L^2}^2,\qquad F_\lambda:=(E_\lambda,J),
\]
and let $\operatorname{ind}_{-}(Q)$ denote the maximal dimension of a
subspace on which a quadratic form $Q$ is negative definite.  For every
$\kappa>0$ and integer $N\ge1$, there is $\Lambda>0$ with the following

\begin{equation}
 \bar pD_uE_\lambda=\bar p_0D_uJ,\qquad
 |\bar p|\ge\Lambda|\bar p_0|,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{ind}_{-}\!\left(
  \left.(\bar p,-\bar p_0)\cdot D_u^2F_\lambda
  \right|_{\ker D_uF_\lambda}\right)<N,
\end{equation}
then the adjoint covector $p(t)$ with terminal value $p(1)=\bar p$
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \left|p(t)[X_i^\lambda,X_j^\lambda](\gamma_{0,u}^\lambda(t))\right|
 \le\kappa|\bar p|
 \qquad(0\le t\le1, 1\le i,j\le k).
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:18:13.294453+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4fe9be5b3a390b33f23aad5959c861507b8ab26e18ed2db78f7a203c0c015431","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:disconnect_interior of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] {amy-cle-resampling}}]

Suppose that $\Gamma$ is a nested ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa}${} in a simply connected domain $D$, and let $\Upsilon_\Gamma$ be its gasket. For each $a\in(0,1)$, $b>0$ there exists $p > 0$ such that the following holds. 

Let $z\in D$ and $j_0\in\mathbf{Z}$ be such that $B(z,2^{-j_0})\subseteq D$. There exists a resampling $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ of $\Gamma$ within $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$ for each $j>j_0$ with the following property. Let $G^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ be the event that $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ has a loop $\widetilde\mathcal {L}$ that
\begin{itemize}
 \item disconnects every point in $\Upsilon_{\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}} \cap B(z,2^{-j})$ from $\partial B(z,2^{-j+1})$,
 \item the gasket and the collection of loops of $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ remain the same in each connected component of $\mathbf{C} \setminus \widetilde\mathcal {L}$ that intersects $B(z,2^{-j})$.
\end{itemize}
For $k\in\mathbf{N}$, let $\widetilde G_{z,j_0,k}$ be the event that the number of $j=j_0+1,\ldots,j_0+k$ so that
\[ \mathbf{P}[ G^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j} \,|\, \Gamma ] \geq p\]
is at least $(1-a)k$.  Then
\[ \mathbf{P}[(\widetilde G_{z,j_0,k})^c] = O(e^{-b k}) \]
where the implicit constant does not depend on $z,j_0,k$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

$$\Vert \Phi\Vert_\infty:=\max_{x\in K}|\Phi(x)|,\quad [\Phi]_\alpha:=\sup_{\substack{x,y\in K\\x\neq y}}\frac{|\Phi(x)-\Phi(y)|}{(d_\mathcal{X}(x,y))^\alpha},\quad \Phi\in C(\mathcal{K},\mathbb{R}^d).$$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:21:45.257586+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_501f11904a0b7f4b19a9f466e31a41d8bb9e2209475262404cfe0108edca0b2e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 7 of arXiv:2607.26894, 'Stability in stochastic hypergraph matching II: weights, batch arrivals, and continuous ti'] \hfill
	\begin{itemize}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:48:17.126971+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_502ad83e7404b19f631ece643f03381dc34a5c721250602dcb68a2876455d6ab","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 15 ({\cite[p.\ 110) of arXiv:2605.27974, 'Discrete approximation of semi-Dirichlet forms with non-symmetric perturbations of resista'] {FOT}}]
    Let $(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$ be a Dirichlet form on $L^2(X, \mu)$ and assume that 
    $\mathcal{F} \subset C(X)$ and that $\mathcal{F}$ is dense in 
    $(C(X),\norm{\cdot}_{\infty})$. Then, for any $f \in \mathcal{F}$, 
    there exists a unique finite Borel measure $\nu_{f}$ on $X$ which satisfies 
    \begin{align}
        \int_{X}g\,d\nu_{f}=2\mathcal{E}(fg,f)-\mathcal{E}(g,f^{2}), 
        \quad g \in \mathcal{F}.
    \end{align}
     The measure $\nu_{f}$ is called the energy measure of $f$. Also, for any 
     $f,g \in \mathcal{F}$, we define a signed measure $\nu_{f,g}$ by 
    \begin{equation}
        \nu_{f,g} \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}(\nu_{f+g}-\nu_{f}-\nu_{g}).
    \end{equation}
    $\nu_{f,g}$ is called the mutual energy measure of $f$ and $g$. Then, we have 
    $\abs{\nu_{f,g}(B)} \leq \nu_{f}(B)^{1/2}\nu_{g}(B)^{1/2}$
    for any Borel set $B$ of $X$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f ∈ C^1","u is a weak solution which is piecewise C^1 with C^1 shock curves and one-sided traces (the equivalence as stated is for this piecewise-smooth class; Kruzhkov's definition is what governs general L^∞ solutions)","the chord condition must hold at EVERY point of EVERY discontinuity curve","Rankine-Hugoniot alone is not sufficient: it fixes σ but permits inadmissible jumps"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T10:04:12.417666+00:00","domain":"partial differential equations: hyperbolic conservation laws","id":"claim_502c4a8cf7e11bf1fd64197cea9e23277293f004895262e4972b802ea4718867","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f ∈ C^1(R) and let u ∈ L^∞(R × (0,∞)) be a weak solution of u_t + f(u)_x = 0 that is piecewise C^1: away from finitely many disjoint C^1 curves x = s_i(t) it is C^1, and it has C^1 one-sided traces u_-(t) (from x < s_i(t)) and u_+(t) (from x > s_i(t)) on each curve. Each curve then satisfies Rankine-Hugoniot, σ := s_i'(t) = ( f(u_-) - f(u_+) ) / ( u_- - u_+ ) when u_- ≠ u_+. Such a u is a Kruzhkov entropy solution if and only if at every point of every discontinuity curve the chord condition holds: for every k strictly between u_- and u_+, ( f(k) - f(u_-) ) / ( k - u_- ) ≥ σ ≥ ( f(k) - f(u_+) ) / ( k - u_+ ). Equivalently: if u_+ < u_-, the graph of f on [u_+,u_-] lies on or below the chord joining (u_+,f(u_+)) to (u_-,f(u_-)); if u_- < u_+, the graph of f on [u_-,u_+] lies on or above that chord. If f is strictly convex, this is equivalent to the Lax shock inequalities f'(u_-) ≥ σ ≥ f'(u_+), i.e. to u_- > u_+: a strictly convex flux admits only downward jumps.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:33.543870+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_503a791b1755d53c7385e64d56512fef661f8ac68a58a89821ec3caef72ecfb3","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 30 (Coordinate representation) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Let $G$ be a finite graph and $\beta\in[0,\infty)$.
    Define $\mu_{G,\beta}'$ as the probability measure on
    \[
        \tau:=(\alpha,\omega,\eta)\in [0,\tfrac\pi2]^V\times\{0,1\}^E\times\{0,1\}^E:=\Pi_G
    \]
    with density
    \begin{align}
        &
        \diff\mu_{G,\beta}'(\tau)
        \propto
        \textstyle
        \left(\prod_{u\in V}\diff\alpha_u\right)
        \\
        &
        \qquad\qquad
        \textstyle
        \cdot
        2^{k(\omega)}
        \left(
            \prod_{uv\in \omega}
                (1-\e^{-2\beta(\cos\alpha_u)(\cos\alpha_v)})
            \middle)\middle(
            \prod_{uv\not\in\omega}
                e^{-2\beta(\cos\alpha_u)(\cos\alpha_v)}
            \right)
            \\&
            \qquad\qquad
            \textstyle
            \cdot
            2^{k(\eta)}
            \left(
                \prod_{uv\in \eta}
                     (1-\e^{-2\beta(\sin\alpha_u)(\sin\alpha_v)})
                \middle)\middle(
                \prod_{uv\not\in\eta}
                    e^{-2\beta(\sin\alpha_u)(\sin\alpha_v)}
                \right).
    \end{align}
    Here $k(\rho)$ denotes the number of connected components of $(V,\rho)$.

    Now obtain a sample $\sigma\in(\S^1)^V$ as follows:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item Sample $\tau\sim\mu_{G,\beta}'$,
        \item Sample $\xi\in\{-1,+1\}^V$ by flipping a fair coin for each connected component of $\omega$,
        \item Sample $\zeta\in\{-1,+1\}^V$ by flipping a fair coin for each connected component of $\eta$,
        \item Set $\sigma_u:=\xi_u\cos\alpha_u + i\cdot \zeta_u\sin\alpha_u$ for each $u\in V$.
    \end{itemize}
    Then $\sigma\sim\mu_{G,\beta}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["bond percolation on the square lattice Z^2","the Harris half as sketched uses Burton-Keane uniqueness, self-duality, the square-root trick and a planar topological argument","the Kesten half is stated but not proved in this node"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543220+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_5050896df8f7fb9dbfa990fc0b0cefbd0928a39e58de37c123d446e63228d84e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For bond percolation on the square lattice Z^2, p_c = 1/2, and moreover theta(1/2) = 0: there is no infinite open cluster AT the critical point. The two halves have separate histories and separate proofs. HARRIS (1960) proved theta(1/2) = 0, which gives p_c >= 1/2. KESTEN (1980) proved that theta(p) > 0 for every p > 1/2, giving p_c <= 1/2. The self-duality of Z^2 bond percolation at p = 1/2 - the dual of the open configuration at parameter p is a configuration at parameter 1 - p on an isomorphic lattice - makes 1/2 the ONLY candidate but does not by itself decide the critical behaviour, which is why the theorem is hard. The corresponding value for SITE percolation on Z^2 is not known; for site percolation on the triangular lattice the answer is 1/2 by the same duality mechanism, and that is the case where conformal invariance at criticality is proved. [Harris (1960); Kesten (1980), Comm. Math. Phys. 74; see Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Chapter 11, or Bollobas-Riordan, Percolation]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:18:54.364463+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_5050ebeed2cb4fc8fbc23adfd61dee8c3fb8d114cf7445e4c9d7c8a005157a83","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] A function $f:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R^M$ is continuously differentiable,
$$f(x+t)\simeq f(x)+f'(x)t$$
with $f'(x)$ linear, and $x\to f'(x)$ continuous, precisely when it has partial derivatives,
$$\frac{df_i}{dx_j}(x)=\lim_{t\to 0}\frac{f_i(x+te_j)-f_i(x)}{t}$$
which depend continuously on $x$. In this case the derivative is
$$f'(x)=\left(\frac{df_i}{dx_j}(x)\right)_{ij}\in M_{M\times N}(\mathbb R)$$ 
acting on the vectors $t\in\mathbb R^N$ by usual multiplication.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T01:54:57.544734+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_505cff961fe29adc78b740b001ea81ac013720965efddfef7f16a6e13715fb7e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:conv-immig of arXiv:2412.03325, 'Functional limit theorem for branching processes \\ in nearly degenerate varying environme'] Assume that the BPVEI $(Y_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ defined in (equation eq:Y of the paper) satisfies the conditions (C1)--(C3) and (C4) or (C4') holds. Then, for any $0<\varepsilon \leq 1$,
\[
\mathcal{L} ((Y_{A(nt)})_{t \geq  \varepsilon}) 
\stackrel{\mathcal{D}}{\longrightarrow} \mathcal{L} ((W(\log t))_{t \geq \varepsilon}),
\]
as $n\to \infty$, 
where $(W(u))_{u\geq \log \varepsilon}$ is a continuous time branching 
process with immigration with initial distribution having g.f.,
\[
\log f_Y(s) 
= 
\begin{cases}
-\sum_{k=1}^{\kappa} 
\frac{2^k\lambda_k}{\nu^k} \left( \log\left( 
1+\frac{\nu}{2}(1-s)\right) +
\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{\nu^i}{i2^i}
(s-1)^i\right), & \nu > 0, \\
\sum_{k=1}^{\kappa} \frac{\lambda_k}{k} (s-1)^k, & \nu = 0,
\end{cases}
\]
with parameters $\alpha = 1+\nu$, $\beta = \sum_{k=1}^{\kappa}(-1)^{k+1}\lambda_k$,
and
\[
\begin{split}
f(s) & = (1+\nu)^{-1} \left(1+\frac{\nu}{2} + \frac{\nu}{2}s^2\right), \\
h(s) & = 1 + \beta^{-1} \sum_{k=1}^{\kappa} \lambda_k (s-1)^k,
\end{split}
\]
offspring and immigration g.f.'s, where $\kappa=K-1$ or $\kappa=\infty$ depending on whether condition (C4) or (C4') holds. The transition generating function of $W$ is given by
\begin{equation*} 
G_y(s, t) = \mathbf{E} \left[ s^{W(t + u)} | W(u) = y \right] = 
\frac{f_Y(s)}{f_Y(h_{e^{-t}}(s))} \left( h_{e^{-t}}(s) \right)^y.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:53:30.651266+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_50652d2136ddb08dcb7ce5e74196e731756b45ad795be53c5b0a7bbeb1e83aec","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] Let $j \in \{1,\ldots,n\}$ and suppose $\mathcal{Z}$ is a positive solution to the system of PDEs, such that the limit

\]
exists and is nonzero for all fixed $\{x_k\}_{k \neq j, j\pm1}$ and $\xi$ in a suitable interval.
